children.translated_text: // <s>Saddharmalaṅkāvatārasūtram</s> (The Sūtra of the Entrance of the True Dharma into Laṅkā) //

children.text: om namo ratnatrayāya / om namaḥ sarvabuddhabodhisattvebhyaḥ //
children.translated_text: Oṃ, homage to the Triple Gem! Oṃ, homage to all <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>!

body.text: START Parivarta 1
body.translated_text: START Chapter 1

body.text: rāvaṇādhyeṣaṇāparivartaḥ prathamaḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Rāvaṇādhyeṣaṇāparivartaḥ</s> (The Chapter on <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s Invitation), the first.

body.text: evaṃ mayā śrutam / ekasmin samaye bhagavāṃllaṅkāpure samudramalayaśikhare viharati sma nānāratnagotrapuṣpapratimaṇḍite mahatā bhikṣusaṃghena sārdhaṃ mahatā ca bodhisattvagaṇena nānābuddhakṣetrasaṃnipatitairbodhisattvairmahāsattvaiḥ anekasamādhivaśitābalābhijñāvikrīḍitairmahāmatibodhisattvapūrvaṃgamaiḥ sarvabuddhapāṇyabhiṣekābhiṣiktaiḥ svacittadṛśyagocaraparijñānārthakuśalairnānāsattvacittacaritrarūpanayavinayadhāribhiḥ pañcadharmasvabhāvavijñānanairātmyādvayagatiṃgataiḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus have I heard. At one time, <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling in the city of <s>Laṅkā</s>, on the peak of <s>Malaya</s> by the ocean, adorned with various jewel-veined flowers, together with a great assembly of monks and a great company of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> — <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas</s> who had assembled from various <s>Buddha-kṣetras</s> (Buddha-fields), who sported in manifold <s>samādhi</s>, <s>vaśitā</s> (mastery), powers, and <s>abhijñā</s> (superknowledges), led by the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s>, all consecrated by the hand-anointing of all <s>Buddhas</s>, skilled in comprehending that the domain of experience is merely one's own mind, upholding the methods of discipline suited to the forms, conduct, and minds of various beings, and having attained the path of the twofold <s>nairātmya</s> (selflessness) of the five <s>dharmas</s>, the self-natures, and the <s>vijñānas</s> (consciousnesses).

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayena bhagavān sāgaranāgarājabhavanāt saptāhenottīrṇa 'bhūt / anekaśakrabrahmanāgakanyākoṭibhiḥ pratyudgamyamāno laṅkāmalayamavalokya smitamakarot - pūrvakairapi tathāgatairarhadbhiḥ samyaksaṃbuddhairasmiṃllaṅkāpurīmalayaśikhare svapratyātmāryajñānatarkadṛṣṭitīrthyaśrāvakapratyekabuddhāryaviṣaye tadbhāvito dharmo deśitaḥ / yannvahamapi atraiva rāvaṇaṃ yakṣādhipatimadhikṛtya etadevodbhāvayan dharmaṃ deśayeyam //
body.translated_text: Now at that time, <s>Bhagavān</s> had emerged after seven days from the palace of <s>Sāgara</s>, the <s>Nāga</s> king. Being welcomed by myriads of <s>Śakra</s>s, <s>Brahmā</s>s, <s>Nāga</s> maidens, and others, he looked upon <s>Laṅkā</s> and Mount <s>Malaya</s> and smiled — "By former <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Enlightened Ones, on this very peak of <s>Malaya</s> in the city of <s>Laṅkā</s>, the <s>Dharma</s> was taught, cultivated in that manner, in the domain of the noble realization of one's own <s>pratyātma</s> (self-realized) knowledge, beyond the speculations and views of <s>tīrthyas</s> (heretics), <s>Śrāvakas</s>, and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>. Let me too, right here, teach this very <s>Dharma</s>, manifesting it for <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of the <s>Yakṣas</s>."

body.text: aśrauṣīdrāvaṇo rākṣasādhipatistathāgatādhiṣṭhānāt - bhagavān kila sāgaranāgarājabhavanāduttīrya anekaśakrabrahmanāgakanyākoṭibhiḥ parivṛtaḥ puraskṛtaḥ samudrataraṃgānavalokya ālayavijñānodadhipravṛttivijñānapavanaviṣaye preritāṃstebhyaḥ saṃnipatitebhyaścittānyavalokya tasminneva sthitaḥ udānamudānayati sma - yannvahaṃ gatvā bhagavantamadhyeṣya laṅkāṃ praveśayeyam / tanme syāddīrgharātramarthāya hitāya sukhāya devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca //
body.translated_text: <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of the <s>Rākṣasas</s>, heard through the power of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s blessing — "<s>Bhagavān</s>, it is said, having emerged from the palace of <s>Sāgara</s> the <s>Nāga</s> king, surrounded and attended by myriads of <s>Śakra</s>s, <s>Brahmā</s>s, and <s>Nāga</s> maidens, gazing upon the ocean waves, in the domain of the winds of <s>pravṛttivijñāna</s> (active consciousness) upon the ocean of <s>ālayavijñāna</s> (store-consciousness), observing the minds of those who had gathered, driven by those winds, standing right there, he utters an inspired utterance." — "Let me go and invite <s>Bhagavān</s> to enter <s>Laṅkā</s>. May that be for my long-lasting benefit, welfare, and happiness, for gods and humans alike."

body.text:
atha rāvaṇo rākṣasādhipatiḥ saparivāraḥ pauṣpakaṃ vimānamadhiruhya yena bhagavāṃstenopajagāma / upetya vimānādavatīrya saparivāro bhagavantaṃ triṣkṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya tūryatālāvacaraiḥ pravādyadbhirindranīlamayena
daṇḍena vaiḍūryamusāra(galva)pratyuptāṃ vīṇāṃ priyaṅgupāṇḍunā anardhyeṇa vastreṇa pārśvāvalambitāṃ kṛtvā ṣaḍjarṣabhagāndhāradhaivataniṣādamadhyamakaiśikagītasvaragrāmamūrchanādiyuktenānusārya salīlaṃ vīṇāmanupraviśya gāthābhigītairanugāyati sma -
body.translated_text: Then <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of the <s>Rākṣasas</s>, together with his retinue, ascended the <s>Puṣpaka</s> aerial chariot and approached <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having arrived and descended from the chariot, he and his retinue circumambulated <s>Bhagavān</s> three times. Then, with musicians playing drums and cymbals, he took up a <s>vīṇā</s> made of sapphire, inlaid with <s>vaiḍūrya</s> and coral, slung at his side with a priceless cloth pale as millet, and following the musical system of the scale-notes — <s>ṣaḍja</s>, <s>ṛṣabha</s>, <s>gāndhāra</s>, <s>dhaivata</s>, <s>niṣāda</s>, <s>madhyama</s>, and <s>kaiśika</s> — with their song-modes, scales, and modulations, he gracefully entered into playing the <s>vīṇā</s> and sang in verse-songs:

children.translated_text: The method of the <s>Dharma</s> that is the nature of mind, <s>nairātmya</s> (selflessness), free from views, stainless —

children.text: pratyātmavedyagatisūcanakaṃ deśehi nāyaka iha dharmanayam // Lank_1.1 //
children.translated_text: Teach here, O Leader, this <s>Dharma</s>-method that indicates the path of <s>pratyātma</s> (self-realization). // Laṅk. 1.1 //
The <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One) whose body is an accumulation of excellent <s>dharmas</s>, who displays emanations created by <s>nirmāṇa</s> (magical creation) —

children.text: pratyātmavedyagatidharmarataṃ laṅkāṃ hi gantu samayo 'dya mune // Lank_1.2 //
children.translated_text: Delighting in the <s>Dharma</s> of the path of <s>pratyātma</s> (self-realization), now is the time, O Sage, to come to <s>Laṅkā</s>. // Laṅk. 1.2 //
This <s>Laṅkā</s>, inhabited by former <s>Jinas</s> (Conquerors) and their sons who bore many forms —

children.text: deśehi nātha iha dharmavaraṃ śroṣyanti yakṣa bahurūpadharāḥ // Lank_1.3 //
children.translated_text: Teach here, O Lord, the supreme <s>Dharma</s>; the <s>Yakṣas</s> who bear many forms shall listen. // Laṅk. 1.3 //

body.text: atha rāvaṇo laṅkādhipatiḥ toṭakavṛttenānugāyya punarapi gāthābhigītenānugāyati sma -
body.translated_text: Then <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>, having sung in the <s>toṭaka</s> metre, again sang in verse-song:

children.translated_text: After seven nights, <s>Bhagavān</s>, from the ocean, abode of sea-creatures,

children.text: sāgarendrasya bhavanāt samuttīrya taṭe sthitaḥ // Lank_1.4 //
children.translated_text: Having emerged from the palace of the lord of the ocean, stood upon the shore. // Laṅk. 1.4 //
As soon as the <s>Buddha</s> stood there, <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, together with <s>Apsarases</s>,
And various <s>Yakṣas</s> of many kinds, with <s>Śuka</s> and <s>Sāraṇa</s>, the learned ones, // Laṅk. 1.5 //

children.text: ṛddhyā gatvā tamadhvānaṃ yatra tiṣṭhati nāyakaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having gone by supernatural power along that path to where the Leader stood,
Descending from the <s>Puṣpaka</s> vehicle, saluting and worshipping the <s>Tathāgata</s>,
Announcing his name to him, empowered by the Lord of Conquerors — // Laṅk. 1.6 //
"I am <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, the ten-necked one, lord of <s>Rākṣasas</s>, come here.

children.text: anugṛhṇāhi me laṅkāṃ ye cāsmin puravāsinaḥ // Lank_1.7 //
children.translated_text: Graciously bless my <s>Laṅkā</s> and those who dwell in this city. // Laṅk. 1.7 //
By former Fully Awakened Ones too, the domain of <s>pratyātma</s> (self-realization),
On this jewel-studded peak, in the midst of the city, was illuminated. // Laṅk. 1.8 //
May <s>Bhagavān</s> too, on that very jewel-adorned peak,
Teach the stainless <s>Dharma</s>, surrounded by the sons of the <s>Jinas</s> —

children.text: śrotukāmā vayaṃ cādya ye ca laṅkānivāsinaḥ // Lank_1.9 //
children.translated_text: We and the inhabitants of <s>Laṅkā</s> wish to hear it today. // Laṅk. 1.9 //
Free from the constructs of doctrinal exposition, the domain of <s>pratyātma</s> (self-realization) —
The <s>Laṅkāvatāra Sūtra</s>, praised by former <s>Buddhas</s>. // Laṅk. 1.10 //
I remember that by former <s>Buddhas</s>, attended by the sons of the <s>Jinas</s>,
This sūtra was proclaimed — may <s>Bhagavān</s> also speak it! // Laṅk. 1.11 //
In the future age, the <s>Buddhas</s> and sons of <s>Buddhas</s> who shall arise,
This very divine method, on the jewel-adorned peak,
The Leaders shall teach, out of compassion for the <s>Yakṣas</s>. // Laṅk. 1.12 //
The delightful divine city of <s>Laṅkā</s>, adorned with various jewels,
With cool, charming balconies and canopies of jewel-nets — // Laṅk. 1.13 //
Free from passion and hatred, contemplating the path of <s>pratyātma</s> (self-realization),
There are here, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s> whose aims were fulfilled by former <s>Buddhas</s>,
Devoted to the <s>Mahāyāna</s> method, connecting with one another in faith. // Laṅk. 1.14 //
<s>Yakṣiṇīs</s>, sons of <s>Yakṣas</s>, eager to learn the <s>Mahāyāna</s> —
May <s>Bhagavān</s>, the Teacher, come to <s>Laṅkā</s> and Mount <s>Malaya</s>! // Laṅk. 1.15 //
The <s>Rākṣasas</s>, dwellers of the city, led by <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>,
Shall hear the path of <s>pratyātma</s> (self-realization), devoted to the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. // Laṅk. 1.16 //
They have performed meritorious deeds toward the <s>Buddhas</s> and shall do so now as well.

children.text: anukampārthaṃ mahyaṃ vai yāhi laṅkāṃ sutaiḥ saha // Lank_1.17 //
children.translated_text: Out of compassion for me, go to <s>Laṅkā</s> together with your sons! // Laṅk. 1.17 //
My palaces, companies of <s>Apsarases</s>, and various necklaces,
And the delightful <s>Aśoka</s> grove — accept them, O Great Sage! // Laṅk. 1.18 //

children.text: ājñākaro 'haṃ buddhānāṃ ye ca teṣāṃ jinātmajāḥ /
children.translated_text: I am a servant of the <s>Buddhas</s> and of their sons, the <s>Jinātmajas</s> —

children.text: nāsti tadyanna deyaṃ me anukampa mahāmune // Lank_1.19 //
children.translated_text: There is nothing that I would not give; have compassion, O Great Sage! // Laṅk. 1.19 //
Having heard his words, the Lord of the Three Worlds spoke:
"By past Leaders too, O lord of <s>Yakṣas</s>, on this jewel mountain, // Laṅk. 1.20 //
The <s>Dharma</s> of <s>pratyātma</s> (self-realization) was taught, and you too were shown compassion.
And those of the future shall also teach on this jewel-adorned mountain. // Laṅk. 1.21 //
For this is the abode of <s>yogins</s> who dwell in the directly realized <s>Dharma</s>.

children.text: anukampyo 'si yakṣendra sugatānāṃ mamāpi ca // Lank_1.22 //
children.translated_text: You are worthy of compassion, O lord of <s>Yakṣas</s>, from the <s>Sugatas</s> and from me as well." // Laṅk. 1.22 //
Having consented, <s>Bhagavān</s> remained in silence, established in tranquil wisdom,
And mounted the <s>Puṣpaka</s> vehicle offered by <s>Rāvaṇa</s>. // Laṅk. 1.23 //
There, <s>Rāvaṇa</s> and the other confident sons of the <s>Jinas</s>,
Honored by <s>Apsarases</s> with laughter, dance, and the like, proceeded to the city. // Laṅk. 1.24 //

children.text: tatra gatvā purīṃ ramyāṃ punaḥ pūjāṃ pralabdhavān /
children.translated_text: Having gone to that delightful city, he again received worship —
Honored by <s>Rāvaṇa</s> and other groups of <s>Yakṣas</s>, and by <s>Yakṣiṇīs</s>,
And honored by <s>Yakṣa</s> sons and <s>Yakṣa</s> maidens with jewel-nets. // Laṅk. 1.25 //
By <s>Rāvaṇa</s> too, jewel-adorned necklaces for the <s>Buddha</s>
Were placed upon the heads of the <s>Jina</s> and the sons of the <s>Jina</s>. // Laṅk. 1.26 //
Having accepted the worship, <s>Bhagavān</s>, together with the learned sons of the <s>Jina</s>,
Illuminated the <s>Dharma</s>, the domain of <s>pratyātma</s> (self-realization). // Laṅk. 1.27 //
<s>Rāvaṇa</s> and the <s>Yakṣa</s> hosts, having worshipped the best of speakers,
Honor <s>Mahāmati</s> and invite him again and again:
"You are the questioner of all <s>Buddhas</s> regarding the domain of <s>pratyātma</s> (self-realization). // Laṅk. 1.28 //

children.text: ahaṃ hi śrotā yakṣāśca jinaputrāśca sanniha /
children.translated_text: I am the listener, and the <s>Yakṣas</s>, and the sons of the <s>Jinas</s> present here.

children.text: adhyeṣayāmi tvāṃ yakṣā jinaputrāśca paṇḍitāḥ // Lank_1.29 //
children.translated_text: I and the <s>Yakṣas</s> and the learned sons of the <s>Jina</s> invite you: // Laṅk. 1.29 //
You are the great debater among debaters, the vehicle of <s>yoga</s> among <s>yogins</s> —

children.text: adhyeṣayāmi tvāṃ bhaktyā nayaṃ pṛccha viśārada // Lank_1.30 //
children.translated_text: I invite you with devotion; ask about the method, O skilled one! // Laṅk. 1.30 //
Free from the faults of <s>tīrthyas</s> (heretics), and from <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> and <s>Śrāvakas</s>,
Pure in the <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature) of <s>pratyātma</s> (self-realization), illuminating the stage of <s>Buddhahood</s>. // Laṅk. 1.31 //
<s>Bhagavān</s> then magically created there jewel-adorned peaks,
And other divine ones as well, ornamented with crores of jewel-diadems. // Laṅk. 1.32 //
On each and every great mountain, displaying his own form,

children.text: tatraiva rāvaṇo yakṣa ekaikasmin vyavasthitaḥ // Lank_1.33 //
children.translated_text: And there <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, the <s>Yakṣa</s>, was established on each one. // Laṅk. 1.33 //

children.text: atra tāḥ parṣadaḥ sarvā ekaikasmin hi dṛśyate /
children.translated_text: All those assemblies were visible on each one,

children.text: sarvakṣetrāṇi tatraiva ye ca teṣu vināyakāḥ // Lank_1.34 //
children.translated_text: And all the <s>Buddha-kṣetras</s> (Buddha-fields) were there, and the Guides within them. // Laṅk. 1.34 //
The lord of <s>Rākṣasas</s> was also there, and the inhabitants of <s>Laṅkā</s>,
And a <s>Laṅkā</s> rivaling the original was created by the <s>Jina</s>,
And other <s>Aśoka</s> groves and forest splendors were there as well. // Laṅk. 1.35 //
On each mountain, the Lord, prompted by <s>Mahāmati</s>,
Taught the <s>Dharma</s> to the <s>Yakṣa</s>, indicating the path of <s>pratyātma</s> (self-realization),

children.text: dideśa nikhilaṃ sūtraṃ śatasāhasrikaṃ girau // Lank_1.36 //
children.translated_text: And taught the entire sūtra of one hundred thousand verses on the mountain. // Laṅk. 1.36 //
The Teacher and the sons of the <s>Jina</s> then vanished from that very place.

children.text: adrākṣīdrāvaṇo yakṣa ātmabhāvaṃ gṛhe sthitam // Lank_1.37 //
children.translated_text: <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, the <s>Yakṣa</s>, saw himself standing in his own palace. // Laṅk. 1.37 //

children.text: cinteti kimidaṃ ko 'yaṃ deśitaṃ kena vā śrutam /
children.translated_text: He reflected: "What was this? Who was that? What was taught? By whom was it heard?

children.text: kiṃ dṛṣṭaṃ kena vā dṛṣṭaṃ nagaro vā kva saugataḥ // Lank_1.38 //
children.translated_text: What was seen? By whom was it seen? Where is the city? Where is the <s>Sugata</s>? // Laṅk. 1.38 //

children.text: tāni kṣetrāṇi te buddhā ratnaśobhāḥ kva saugatāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those fields, those <s>Buddhas</s>, those jewel-splendors — where are the <s>Sugatas</s>?

children.text: svapno 'yamatha vā māyā nagaraṃ gandharvaśabditam // Lank_1.39 //
children.translated_text: Was this a dream, or an illusion, or a city called 'of the <s>Gandharvas</s>'? // Laṅk. 1.39 //
A cataract of the eye, or a mirage, or a dream, or the child of a barren woman,
Or the smoke of a whirling firebrand — is this what I have seen here? // Laṅk. 1.40 //

children.text: atha vā dharmatā hyeṣā dharmāṇāṃ cittagocare /
children.translated_text: Or rather, this is the very <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature) of all <s>dharmas</s> in the domain of mind,

children.text: na ca bālāvabudhyante mohitā viśvakalpanaiḥ // Lank_1.41 //
children.translated_text: But the foolish do not understand, deluded by manifold <s>vikalpas</s> (conceptual constructions). // Laṅk. 1.41 //

children.text: na draṣṭā na ca draṣṭavyaṃ na vācyo nāpi vācakaḥ /
children.translated_text: There is no seer, nor anything to be seen, no speaker, nor anything spoken.
This <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual construction) is something other than the form and abiding of the <s>Buddha-Dharma</s>.

children.text: ye paśyanti yathādṛṣṭaṃ na te paśyanti nāyakam // Lank_1.42 //
children.translated_text: Those who see as they have [conventionally] seen do not see the Leader. // Laṅk. 1.42 //
When one whose <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual construction) has ceased does not see the <s>Buddha</s>,

children.text: apravṛttibhave buddhaḥ saṃbuddho yadi paśyati // Lank_1.43 //
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s> is truly awakened in the cessation of arising — if one sees thus. // Laṅk. 1.43 //

body.text:
samanantaraprativibuddhe parāvṛttāśraye svacittadṛśyamātrādhigame 'vikalpapracārasthitasya laṅkādhipateḥ pūrvakuśalamūlasaṃcoditasya sarvaśāstravidagdhabuddheryathātathyadarśanasya aparapraṇeyasya svabuddhivicālanakuśalasya tarkadṛṣṭivyapetadarśanasya aparapraṇeyasya mahāyogayogino mahāviśvarūpadhāriṇaḥ upāyakauśalyagatiṃgatasya sarvabhūmyuttarottarasvalakṣaṇādhigamanakuśalasya cittamagomanovijñānasvabhāvavivekaratasya trisaṃtativyavacchinnadarśanasya sarvakāraṇatīrthyavyapetabuddheḥ tathāgatagarbhabuddhabhūmyadhyātmasamāpannasya sthitabuddhabuddhergaganādadhyātmavedyaśabdamaśrauṣīt - sādhu sādhu laṅkādhipate, sādhu khalu punastvaṃ laṅkādhipate / evaṃ śikṣitavyaṃ yoginā yathā tvaṃ śikṣase / evaṃ ca tathāgatā draṣṭavyāḥ dharmāśca, yathā tvayā dṛṣṭāḥ / anyathā dṛśyamāne ucchedamāśrayaḥ / cittamanomanovijñānavigatena tvayā sarvadharmā vibhāvayitavyāḥ / antaścāriṇā na bāhyārthadṛṣṭyabhiniviṣṭena / na ca tvayā śrāvakapratyekabuddhatīrthādhigamapadārthagocarapatitadṛṣṭisamādhinā bhavitavyam / nākhyāyiketihāsaratena bhavitavyam / na svabhāvadṛṣṭinā, na rājādhipatyamadapatitena, ṣaḍdhyānādidhyāyinā / eṣa laṅkādhipate abhisamayo mahāyogināṃ parapravādamathanānāmakuśaladṛṣṭidālanānāmātmadṛṣṭivyāvartanakuśalānāṃ sūkṣmamabhivijñānaparāvṛttikuśalānāṃ jinaputrāṇāṃ mahāyānacaritānām / tathāgatasvapratyātmabhūmipraveśādhigamāya tvayā yogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ / evaṃ kriyamāṇe bhūyo 'pyuttarottaraviśodhako 'yaṃ laṅkādhipate mārgo yastvayā parigṛhītaḥ samādhikauśalasamāpattyā / na ca śrāvakapratyekabuddhatīrthyānupraveśasukhagocaro yathā bālatīrthayogayogibhiḥ kalpyate ātmagrāhadṛśyalakṣaṇābhiniviṣṭairbhūtaguṇadravyānucāribhiravidyāpratyayadṛṣṭyabhiniveśābhiniviṣṭaiḥ śūnyatotpādavikṣiptairvikalpābhiniviṣṭairlakṣyalakṣaṇapatitāśayaiḥ / viśvarūpagatiprāpako 'yaṃ laṅkādhipate svapratyātmagatibodhako 'yaṃ mahāyānādhigamaḥ / viśeṣabhavopapattipratilambhāya ca pravartate / paṭalakośavividhavijñānataraṃgavyāvartako
'yaṃ laṅkādhipate mahāyānayogapraveśo na tīrthyayogāśrayapatanam / tīrthyayogo hi laṅkādhipate tīrthyānāmātmābhiniveśātpravartate / vijñānasvabhāvadvayārthānāmabhiniveśadarśanādasaumyayogastīrthakarāṇām / tatsādhu laṅkādhipate etamevārthamanuvicintayeḥ / yathā vicintitavāṃstathāgatadarśanāt / etadeva tathāgatadarśanam //
body.translated_text: Immediately upon awakening, when the transformation of the basis (<s>parāvṛttāśraya</s>) had occurred, upon the realization that [all is] mere appearance of one's own mind (<s>svacittadṛśyamātra</s>), the lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>, who abided in the realm of non-conceptual activity, who was impelled by roots of merit from previous [lives], whose intellect was skilled in all treatises, who saw things as they truly are, who was not led by others, who was skilled in examining through his own intellect, whose vision was free from the views of logical speculation, who was not guided by others, who was a great practitioner of <s>yoga</s> (<s>mahāyogayogin</s>), who bore the great universal form (<s>viśvarūpa</s>), who had attained the course of skillful means (<s>upāyakauśalya</s>), who was skilled in attaining the own-characteristics of each successively higher stage (<s>bhūmi</s>), who delighted in discriminating the nature of mind (<s>citta</s>), mentation (<s>manas</s>), and consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>), whose vision had transcended the three continuities, whose intellect was free from all causal heretical [views], who had internally attained the <s>Tathāgatagarbha</s> and the Buddha-stages (<s>buddhabhūmi</s>), whose intellect was established — heard a voice from the sky, inwardly perceived: 'Well done, well done, O lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>! Well done indeed, O lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>! Thus should a <s>yogin</s> train, just as you train. And thus should <s>Tathāgatas</s> and <s>dharmas</s> be seen, just as you have seen them. When seen otherwise, one takes refuge in annihilationism (<s>uccheda</s>). By you, who are free from mind, mentation, and consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>), all <s>dharmas</s> should be contemplated. [You should be] one who moves inwardly, not one attached to the view of external objects. Nor should you abide in the concentration that falls into the domain of <s>Śrāvaka</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, and heretical attainments. You should not delight in legends and histories. You should not hold the view of inherent nature (<s>svabhāvadṛṣṭi</s>), nor should you fall into the intoxication of royal sovereignty, [but should be] one who meditates on the six <s>dhyānas</s>. This, O lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>, is the realization (<s>abhisamaya</s>) of the great <s>yogins</s> — those who crush the doctrines of others, who shatter unwholesome views, who are skilled in turning away from the view of self (<s>ātmadṛṣṭi</s>), who are skilled in the subtle transformation of consciousness (<s>vijñānaparāvṛtti</s>) — of the sons of the <s>Jina</s> who practice the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. For the attainment of entry into the <s>Tathāgata's</s> own inner stage, you should practice <s>yoga</s>. When practiced thus, this path that you have undertaken, O lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>, through the skill of concentration-attainment, purifies further and further. And it is not the domain of comfort of entry into <s>Śrāvaka</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, and heretical [paths], as is imagined by foolish heretical <s>yogins</s> who are attached to the characteristics of the view grasping a self, who follow the elements, qualities, and substances, who are attached to views conditioned by ignorance, who are distracted by emptiness and arising, who are attached to conceptual construction, who have dispositions fallen into the [confusion of] the characterized and the characteristic. This, O lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>, leads to the attainment of the universal form; this <s>Mahāyāna</s> realization awakens one to one's own inner course. And it proceeds toward the attainment of birth in special existences. This entry into <s>Mahāyāna</s> <s>yoga</s>, O lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>, turns back the waves of manifold consciousness [arising like] sheaths and coverings — it is not a falling into the refuge of heretical <s>yoga</s>. For heretical <s>yoga</s>, O lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>, proceeds from the heretics' attachment to self. The disagreeable <s>yoga</s> of the <s>Tīrthakaras</s> [arises] from the view of attachment to the dual objects of the nature of consciousness. Therefore, well done, O lord of <s>Laṅkā</s> — contemplate this very meaning. As you have contemplated, so [have you gained] the vision of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. This itself is the vision of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.'

body.text: atha tasminnantare rāvaṇasyaitadabhavat - yannvahaṃ punarapi bhagavantaṃ sarvayogavaśavartinaṃ tīrthyayogavyāvartakaṃ pratyātmagatigocarodbhāvakaṃ nairmitanairmāṇikavyapetamadhigamabuddhiryadyogināṃ yogābhisamayakāle samādhimukhe samāptānāmadhigamo bhavati / tasya ca adhigamādyogināṃ yogaśabdo nipātyate adhigamaneneti / tadahaṃ kāruṇikaṃ kleśendhanavikalpakṣayakaraṃ taṃ jinaputraiḥ parivṛtaṃ sarvasattvacittāśayānupraviṣṭaṃ sarvagataṃ sarvajñaṃ kriyālakṣaṇavinivṛttaṃ tayaivamṛddhyā
body.translated_text: Then at that time, this [thought] occurred to <s>Rāvaṇa</s>: 'What if I again [approach] the Blessed One, who is master of all <s>yogas</s>, who turns back heretical <s>yoga</s>, who manifests the domain of one's own inner course, who is free from the [distinction of] emanation and emanator, whose realization-intellect [knows] what realization arises for <s>yogins</s> at the time of <s>yoga</s>-realization, at the gateway of <s>samādhi</s>, when they have completed [their practice]. And from that realization, the word "<s>yoga</s>" is applied to <s>yogins</s> — because of realization. Therefore, let me see that Compassionate One, who destroys the fuel of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) and conceptual proliferation, who is surrounded by the sons of the <s>Jina</s>, who has entered into the mental dispositions of all beings, who is omnipresent, omniscient, free from the characteristics of [conditioned] action — let me see him with that very supernatural power

body.text: paśyeyam, taddarśanānnādhigatamadhigaccheyam, adhigataṃ ca me nirvikalpācāraḥ sukhasamādhisamāpattivihārastathāgatagatibhūmiprāpako vivṛddhiṃ yāyāt //
body.translated_text: and from seeing him, may I realize what has not yet been realized; and may what I have realized — [namely] the dwelling in the comfort of the <s>samādhi</s>-attainment of non-conceptual conduct, which leads to the attainment of the <s>Tathāgata's</s> course and stage — increase!'

body.text: atha bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāṃ laṅkādhipateranutpattikadharmakṣāntyadhigataṃ viditvā tayaiva śobhayā daśagrīvasyānukampayā punarapyātmānaṃ śikhare subahuratnakhacite ratnajālavitate darśayati sma / adrākṣīddaśagrīvo laṅkādhipatiḥ punarapi dṛṣṭānubhūtāṃ śobhāṃ śikhare tathāgatamarhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ dvātriṃśadvaralakṣaṇavibhūṣitatanum / svātmabhāvaṃ caikekasmin girau tathāgatānāṃ purataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ mahāmatinā sārdhaṃ tathāgatapratyātmagatigocarakathāṃ prakurvantaṃ yakṣaiḥ parivṛtaṃ tāṃ deśanāpāṭhakathāṃ kathayantam / te ca kṣetrāḥ sanāyakāḥ //
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, at that time, knowing that the lord of <s>Laṅkā</s> had attained the patient acceptance of the non-arising of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>anutpattikadharmakṣānti</s>), out of compassion for the ten-headed one (<s>Daśagrīva</s>), with that very splendor, again displayed himself on the peak adorned abundantly with jewels and covered with jewel-nets. The ten-headed lord of <s>Laṅkā</s> saw again the previously seen and experienced splendor — on the peak, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, his body adorned with the thirty-two excellent marks. And [he saw] his own form on each mountain, before the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the Perfectly Awakened Ones, engaged in discourse on the domain of the <s>Tathāgata's</s> own inner course together with <s>Mahāmati</s>, surrounded by <s>yakṣas</s>, speaking that teaching-recitation-discourse. And those realms had their leaders.

body.text: atha bhagavān punarapi tasyāṃ velāyāṃ parṣadamavalokya buddhyā na māṃsacakṣuṣā siṃharājavadvijṛmbhya mahāhāsamahasat / ūrṇākośācca raśmiṃ niścāryamāṇaḥ pārśvorukaṭikāyācca śrīvatsātsarvaromakūpebhyo yugāntāgniriva dīpyamānaḥ tejasendradhanurudayabhāskaropamena prabhāmaṇḍalena dedīpyamānaḥ śakrabrahmalokapālairgaganatale nirīkṣyamāṇaḥ sumeruśṛṅgapratispardhini śikhare niṣaṇṇo mahāhāsamahasat / atha tasyā bodhisattvaparṣadaḥ teṣāṃ ca śakrabrahmādīnāmetadabhavat - ko nu khalvatra hetuḥ, ka ḥ pratyayo yadbhagavān sarvadharmavaśavartī mahāhāsaṃ smitapūrvakaṃ hasati? raśmīṃśca svavigrahebhyo niścārayati? niścārya tūṣṇīmabhavat svapratyātmāryajñānagocarasamādhimukhe patitāśayo 'vismitaḥ siṃhāvalokanatayā diśo 'valokya rāvaṇasyaiva yogagatipracāramanuvicintayamānaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, again at that time, surveying the assembly with his Buddha[-eye] and not with the fleshly eye, like a lion-king, yawning, laughed a great laugh. And from the tuft of hair between his brows (<s>ūrṇākośa</s>), emitting rays, and from his sides, thighs, hips, and from the <s>Śrīvatsa</s> [mark], from all the pores of his body, blazing like the fire at the end of an age, resplendent with an aureole resembling a rainbow and a rising sun, beheld in the sky by <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and the world-guardians, seated on a peak rivaling the summit of <s>Sumeru</s>, he laughed a great laugh. Then this [thought] occurred to that assembly of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> and to <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and the others: 'What indeed is the cause here, what is the condition, that the Blessed One, who is master of all <s>dharmas</s>, laughs a great laugh preceded by a smile? And emits rays from his own body? And having emitted them, became silent, his mind fallen into the gateway of <s>samādhi</s> [which is] the domain of one's own noble knowledge (<s>āryajñāna</s>), undisturbed, looking at the directions in the manner of a lion's gaze, contemplating the course of <s>Rāvaṇa's</s> <s>yoga</s>-practice?'

body.text: atha khalu mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ pūrvamevādhyeṣito rāvaṇasyānukampāmupādāya tasyā bodhisattvaparṣadaścittāśayavicāramājñāya anāgatāṃ janatāṃ cāvalokya deśanāpāṭhābhiratānāṃ sattvānāṃ cittavibhramo bhaviṣyatīti yathārutārthābhiniviṣṭānāṃ sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhatīrthyayogabalābhiniviṣṭānāṃ tathāgatā api bhagavanto vinivṛttavijñānaviṣayā mahāhāsaṃ hasanti / teṣāṃ kautūhalavinivṛttyarthaṃ bhagavantaṃ paripṛcchati sma - kaḥ khalvatra hetuḥ, kaḥ pratyayaḥ smitasya pravṛttaye? bhagavānāha - sādhu sādhu mahāmate, sādhu khalu punastvaṃ mahāmate, lokasvabhāvamavalokya kudṛṣṭipatitānāṃ ca lokānāṃ traikālyacittāvabodhāya māṃ praṣṭumārabdhaḥ / evaṃ paṇḍitaiḥ paripṛcchanajātīyairbhavitavyaṃ svaparobhayārtham / eṣa mahāmate rāvaṇo laṅkādhipatiḥ pūrvakānapi tathāgatānarhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhān praśnadvayaṃ pṛṣṭavān / māmapyetarhi praṣṭukāmo yadanālīḍhaṃ sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhatīrthyayogayogināṃ praśnadvayaprabhedagatilakṣaṇaṃ vibhāvayitum / ya eṣa praṣṭukāmo daśagrīvo 'nāgatānapi jinān prakṣyati //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s>, who had been previously requested, out of compassion for <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, knowing the investigation of the mental dispositions of that <s>Bodhisattva</s> assembly, and surveying future generations [thinking], 'Beings who delight in the teaching-recitation will have mental confusion' — [thinking] of those who are attached to the literal meaning, of those who are attached to the power of <s>Śrāvaka</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, and heretical <s>yoga</s>-practice — [thinking] that even the Blessed <s>Tathāgatas</s>, whose domain of consciousness has ceased, laugh a great laugh — for the purpose of dispelling their curiosity, asked the Blessed One: 'What indeed is the cause here, what is the condition for the arising of the smile?' The Blessed One said: 'Well done, well done, <s>Mahāmati</s>! Well done indeed, <s>Mahāmati</s>! You have begun to ask me, having observed the nature of the world, for the understanding of the minds of beings in the three times who have fallen into wrong views. Thus should the wise who are of the questioning nature be — for the benefit of self, others, and both. This, <s>Mahāmati</s>, is <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>, who has asked the pair of questions of previous <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones as well. And now he wishes to ask me the same, in order to illuminate the characteristics of the course and the classification of the pair of questions that have not been tasted by all <s>Śrāvaka</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, and heretical <s>yoga</s>-practitioners. This ten-headed one who wishes to ask will ask future <s>Jinas</s> as well.'

body.text: jānanneva bhagavāṃllaṅkādhiupatimetadavocat - pṛccha tvaṃ laṅkādhipate / kṛtaste tathāgatenāvakāśaḥ / mā vilamba pracalitamaulin / yadyadevākāṅkṣasi, ahaṃ te tasta tasyaiva praśnasyavyākaraṇena cittamārādhayiṣyāmi / yathā tvaṃ parāvṛttavikalpāśraye bhūmivipakṣakauśalena pravicayabuddhyā vicārayamāṇaḥ pratyātmanayalakṣaṇasamādhisukhavihāraṃ samādhibuddhaiḥ parigṛhītaḥ
body.translated_text: The Blessed One, knowing [this], said this to the lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>: 'Ask, O lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>! The <s>Tathāgata</s> has granted you the opportunity. Do not delay, O you whose crown trembles! Whatever you desire, I shall delight your mind with the answer to each and every question. Just as you, with the basis of conceptual construction transformed, examining with discriminating intellect through skill in the opposites of the stages,

body.text: śamathasukhavyavasthitaḥ śrāvakapratyekabuddhasamādhipakṣānatikramya acalāsādhumatīdharmameghābhūmivyavasthito dharmanairātmyayathātathākuśalo mahāratnapadmavimāne samādhijinābhiṣekatāṃ pratilapsyase / tadanurūpaiḥ padmaiḥ svakāyavicitrādhiṣṭhānādhiṣṭhitaistaiḥ padmaiḥ svakāyaṃ niṣaṇṇaṃ drakṣyasi, anyonyavakramukhanirīkṣaṇaṃ ca kariṣyasi / evamacintyo 'sau viṣayaḥ yadekenābhinirhārakauśalenābhinirhṛtaścaryābhūmau sthitaḥ / upāyakauśalaparigrahābhinirhārābhinirhṛte tamacintyaviṣayamanuprāpsyasi, bahurūpavikāratāṃ ca tathāgatabhūmim / yadadṛṣṭapūrvaṃ śrāvakapratyekabuddhatīrthyabrahmendropendrādibhistaṃ prāpsyasi //
body.translated_text: established in the comfort of tranquility (<s>śamatha</s>), having transcended the side of <s>Śrāvaka</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> <s>samādhi</s>, established in the Immovable, the Good-Intellect, and the <s>Dharmameghā</s> stages, skilled in the selflessness of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmanairātmya</s>) as it truly is — in the great jewel-lotus palace you shall obtain the <s>samādhi</s>-<s>Jina</s>-consecration. With lotuses corresponding to that, with those lotuses established in the marvelous supernatural transformation of your own body, you will see your own body seated, and you will gaze face to face with each other. Thus inconceivable is that domain which has been brought forth by a single power of bringing-forth, established in the stage of wonder. Through the bringing-forth brought about by the embrace of skillful means, you will attain that inconceivable domain, and the <s>Tathāgata</s>-stage of manifold transformation. That which has never been seen before by <s>Śrāvakas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, heretics, <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Upendra</s>, and others — that you will attain.'

body.text: atha khalu laṅkādhipatirbhagavatā kṛtāvakāśa utthāya tasmādraśmivimalaprabhādratnapadmasadṛśādratnaśikharāt sāpsarogaṇaparivṛto vividhairanekavidhairnānāprakāraiḥ puṣpamālyagandhadhūpavilepanacchatradhvajapatākāhārārdhahārakirīṭamukuṭairanyaiśca adṛṣṭaśrutapūrvairābharaṇaviśeṣairviśiṣṭaistūryatālāvacarairdevanāgayakṣarākṣasagandharvakinnaramahoragamanuṣyātikrāntaiḥ sarvakāmadhātuparyāpannān vādyabhāṇḍānabhinirmāya ye cānyeṣu buddhakṣetreṣu tūryaviśeṣā dṛṣṭāḥ, tānabhinirmāya bhagavantaṃ bodhisattvāṃśca ratnajālenāvaṣṭabhya nānāvastrocchritapatākaṃ kṛtvā sapta tālān gagane 'bhyudgamya mahāpūjāmeghānabhipravṛṣya tūryatālāvacarāṇi nirnādya tasmādgaganādavatīrya sūryavidyutprabhe dvitīye mahāratnapadmālaṃkṛtau ratnaśikhare niṣasāda / niṣadya upacārātsmitapūrvaṃ bhagavatā kṛtāvakāśo bhagavanta praśnadvayaṃ pṛcchati sma - pṛṣṭā mayā pūrvakāstathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ / taiścāpi visarjitam / bhagavantamapyetarhi pṛcchāmi / deśanāpāṭhe cāyaṃ buddhaistvayā cāvaśyamanuvarṇitaṃ bhaviṣyati / nirmitanirmāṇabhāṣitamidaṃ bhagavan dharmadvayam / na maunaistathāgatairbhāṣitam / maunā hi bhagavaṃstathāgatāḥ samādhisukhagocaramevodbhāvayanti / na ca gocaraṃ vikalpayanti / taṃ deśayanti / tatsādhu me bhagavān svayameva dharmavaśavartī dharmadvayaṃ tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho deśayatu / śroṣyantīme jinaputrā ahaṃ ca //
body.translated_text: Then the lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>, having been granted the opportunity by the Blessed One, rising from that jewel-peak resembling a jewel-lotus of radiant, stainless light, surrounded by hosts of <s>Apsarases</s>, with manifold, diverse, and various flowers, garlands, fragrances, incense, unguents, parasols, banners, flags, necklaces, half-necklaces, crowns, diadems, and with other ornaments of extraordinary kinds never before seen or heard, with musical instruments, cymbals, and accompaniments surpassing those of <s>Devas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Rākṣasas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, <s>Mahoragas</s>, and humans, having magically created all musical instruments belonging to the desire realm, and having also created the special musical instruments seen in other Buddha-fields, covering the Blessed One and the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> with a jewel-net, making banners raised on various cloths, ascending seven palm-tree [heights] into the sky, raining down great clouds of offerings, sounding the musical instruments, cymbals, and accompaniments, descending from that sky, he sat down on a second jewel-peak adorned with great jewel-lotuses, [brilliant] like the sun and lightning. Having sat down, with a smile of homage, having been granted the opportunity by the Blessed One, he asked the Blessed One the pair of questions: 'I have asked the previous <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, and they too have answered. I now ask the Blessed One as well. In the teaching-recitation, this <s>dharma</s>-pair will necessarily have been described by the Buddhas and by you. This, O Blessed One, is the pair of <s>dharmas</s> spoken by the emanated-emanation. It is not spoken by the silent <s>Tathāgatas</s>. For the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, O Blessed One, are silent — they manifest only the domain of <s>samādhi</s>-comfort. And they do not conceptualize the domain; they teach it. Therefore, may the Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, who is himself master of <s>Dharma</s>, kindly teach the pair of <s>dharmas</s>. These sons of the <s>Jina</s> will listen, and I also.'

body.text: bhagavānāha - brūhi laṅkādhipate dharmadvayam / rākṣasendra āha - kirīṭāṅgadahāravajrasūtrāvabaddhābharaṇanuśobhāśobhita, dharmā eva prahātavyāḥ prāgevādharmāḥ / tatkathaṃ bhagavan dharmadvayaṃ prahāṇaṃ bhavati? ke cādharmā dharmāḥ? kathaṃ sati dvitvaṃ prahāṇadharmāṇāṃ vikalpalakṣaṇapatitānāṃ vikalpasvabhāvābhāvānāmabhautikabhautikānāmālayavijñānāparijñānādaviśeṣalakṣaṇānāṃ keśoṇḍukasvabhāvāvasthitānāmaśuddhakṣayajñānaviṣayiṇām / tatkathaṃ teṣāṃ prahāṇamevaṃbhāvinām?
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) said: Speak, O Lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>, of the twofold <s>dharma</s>. The <s>Rākṣasa</s> king said: O one adorned and made radiant by ornaments bound with crown, armlets, necklace, and diamond cord — <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) alone are to be abandoned, let alone <s>adharmas</s> (non-phenomena)! Then how, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, does the abandonment of the twofold <s>dharma</s> take place? And what are <s>adharmas</s> and <s>dharmas</s>? How can there be duality in phenomena subject to abandonment, which have fallen into the character of conceptual discrimination (<s>vikalpa</s>), whose nature as conceptual discrimination is non-existent, which are both material and immaterial, whose distinguishing characteristics are unknown due to non-comprehension of <s>ālayavijñāna</s> (store-consciousness), which abide in the nature of a ball of hair, and which are objects of impure exhaustion-knowledge? How then is there abandonment of those that are of such nature?

body.text: bhagavānāha - nanu laṅkādhipate, dṛṣṭo ghaṭādīnāṃ bhedanātmakānāṃ vināśadharmiṇāṃ bālavikalpagocaraiḥ prativibhāgaḥ / evamihāpi kiṃ na gṛhyate? asti dharmādharmayoḥ prativibhāgo bālaprativikalpamupādāya, na tvāryajñānādhigamaṃ prati darśanena / tiṣṭhantu tāvallaṅkādhipate ghaṭādayo bhāvā vicitralakṣaṇapatitā bālānāṃ na tvāryāṇām / ekasvābhāvikānāmekajvālodbhavaprajvālitānāṃ
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: Is it not so, O Lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>, that a distinction is observed among pots and such things, which are of the nature of breaking and subject to destruction, through the conceptual range of the childish? Thus here also, why is it not grasped? There is a distinction between <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> based on the conceptual discrimination of the childish, but not through the vision of noble (<s>ārya</s>) knowledge-attainment. Let us set aside for now, O Lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>, pots and other entities that have fallen into variegated characteristics — they belong to the childish, not to the noble ones. Among those of a single essential nature, kindled from a single flame,

body.text: gṛhabhavanodyānaprāsādapratiṣṭhāpitānāṃ dṛṣṭaḥ prativibhāgaḥ indhanavaśāddīrghahrasvaprabhālpamahāviśeṣāśca / evamihāpi kiṃ na gṛhyate? asti dharmādharmayoḥ prativibhāgaḥ / na kevalamagnijvālāyā ekasaṃtānapatitāyā dṛṣṭo 'rciṣaśca prativibhāgaḥ / ekabījaprasūtānāṃ yatsaṃtānānāmapi laṅkādhipate nālāṅkuragaṇḍaparvapatrapalāśapuṣpaphalaśākhāviśeṣāḥ / evaṃ sarvadharmaprarohadharmiṇāṃ bāhyānāmādhyātmikānāmapyavidyāniryātānāṃ skandhadhātvāyatanopagānāṃ sarvadharmāṇāṃ traidhātukopapannānāṃ dṛṣṭasukhasaṃsthānāmabhilāpyagativiśeṣāḥ / vijñānānāmekalakṣaṇānāṃ viṣayābhigrahaṇapravṛttānāṃ dṛṣṭo hīnotkṛṣṭamadhyamaviśeṣo vyavadānāvyavadānataśca kuśalākuśalataśca / na kevalameṣāṃ laṅkādhipate dharmāṇāṃ prativibhāgaviśeṣaḥ, yogināmapi yogamabhyasyatāṃ yogamārge pratyātmagatilakṣaṇaviśeṣo dṛṣṭaḥ / kimaṅga punardharmādharmayoḥ prativikalpapravṛttayorviśeṣo na bhavati? bhavatyeva //
body.translated_text: established in houses, dwellings, gardens, and palaces — a distinction is observed, and due to the fuel, [there are] differences of long, short, bright, small, and great. Thus here also, why is it not grasped? There is a distinction between <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>. Not only is a distinction observed in the flames and sparks of fire that have fallen into a single continuum, but also, O Lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>, among the shoots born from a single seed, there are distinctions of stalk, sprout, stem, joint, leaf, petal, flower, fruit, and branch in their continuum. Thus, of all phenomena that have the nature of sprouting — both external and internal — proceeding from <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), comprising the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), and <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases), of all phenomena arising in the three realms, having the appearance of visible happiness, there are distinctions of designation and destiny. Among the <s>vijñānas</s> (consciousnesses) of a single character, operating through the apprehension of sense-objects, a distinction of inferior, superior, and middling is observed — both in terms of purification and non-purification, and in terms of wholesome and unwholesome. Not only is there a distinctive difference among these phenomena, O Lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>, but even among <s>yogins</s> practicing <s>yoga</s>, on the path of <s>yoga</s>, a distinctive difference of inner realization and characteristic is observed. How much more so — would there not be a distinction between <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> operating through conceptual discrimination? There certainly is.

body.text: asti laṅkādhipate dharmādharmayoḥ prativibhāgo vikalpalakṣaṇatvāt / tatra laṅkādhipate dharmāḥ katame? yaduta ete tīrthyaśrāvakapratyekabuddhabālavikalpakalpitāḥ / kāraṇato guṇadravyapūrvakā dharmā ityupadiśyante, te prahātavyāḥ / na lakṣaṇataḥ prativikalpayitavyāḥ / svacittadṛśyadharmatābhiniveśānna santi ghaṭādayo dharmā bālaparikalpitā alabdhaśarīrāḥ / evaṃ vidarśanayā prativipaśyataḥ prahīṇā bhavanti //
body.translated_text: There is, O Lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>, a distinction between <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, because they have the character of conceptual discrimination. Therein, O Lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>, what are the <s>dharmas</s>? Namely, those fabricated by the conceptual discrimination of non-Buddhist teachers (<s>tīrthya</s>), <s>śrāvakas</s>, <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>, and the childish. Those that are taught as <s>dharmas</s> based on cause, quality, and substance — those are to be abandoned. They should not be conceptually discriminated by their characteristics. Due to attachment to the nature of one's own mind as the seen, there are no such phenomena as pots fabricated by the childish, which have not obtained a [real] body. Through such insight, for one who sees clearly, they become abandoned.

body.text: tatra adharmāḥ katame? ye 'labdhātmakā lakṣaṇavikalpāpracārā dharmā ahetukāḥ teṣāmapravṛttirdṛṣṭā bhūtābhūtataḥ / atha dharmasya prahāṇaṃ bhavati / punarapyalabdhātmakā dharmāḥ katame? yaduta śaśakharoṣṭravājiviṣāṇavandhyāputraprabhṛtayo dharmāḥ / alabdhātmakatvānna lakṣaṇataḥ kalpyāḥ / te 'nyatra saṃvyavahārārthā abhidhīyante, nābhiniveśato yathā ghaṭādayaḥ / yathā te praheyā agrahaṇato vijñānena, tathā vikalpabhāvā api praheyāḥ / ato dharmādharmayoḥ prahāṇaṃ bhavati / yaduktavānasi laṅkādhipate dharmādharmāḥ kathaṃ praheyā iti, tadetaduktam //
body.translated_text: Therein, what are the <s>adharmas</s>? Those phenomena that have not obtained a self, where the operation of characteristic-discrimination does not occur, that are without cause — their non-operation is observed in terms of both the real and unreal. Then there is abandonment of <s>dharma</s>. Furthermore, what are the phenomena that have not obtained a self? Namely, phenomena such as the horn of a hare, the horn of a camel, the horn of a horse, the son of a barren woman, and the like. Because they have not obtained a self, they cannot be conceptually constructed by their characteristics. They are spoken of elsewhere only for the purpose of conventional usage, not out of attachment, like pots etc. Just as those are to be abandoned through the non-grasping by consciousness, so too the states of conceptual discrimination are to be abandoned. Thus there is abandonment of both <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>. What you have said, O Lord of <s>Laṅkā</s> — 'how are <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> to be abandoned?' — that has been answered.

body.text: yadapyuktavānasi laṅkādhipate - pūrvakā api tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā mayā pṛṣṭāḥ, taiśca visarjitaṃ pūrvam / iti laṅkādhipate vikalpasyaitadadhivacanam / atīto 'pyevaṃ vikalpyate atītaḥ / evamanāgato 'dhunāpi dharmatayā / nirvikalpāstathāgatāḥ sarvavikalpaprapañcātītāḥ / na yathā rūpasvabhāvo vikalpyate / anyatrājñānādhigamataḥ sukhārthaṃ vibhāvyate / prajñayā animittacāriṇaḥ / ato jñānātmakāstathāgatā jñānaśarīrāḥ / na kalpante na kalpyante / kena na kalpante? manasā ātmato jīvataḥ pudgalataḥ / kathaṃ na vikalpante? manovijñānena viṣayārthahetukena yathā rūpalakṣaṇasaṃsthānākārataśca / ato vikalpāvikalpāgatena bhavitavyam //
body.translated_text: As for what you have also said, O Lord of <s>Laṅkā</s> — 'the previous <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly awakened ones were also asked by me, and they too previously gave answers' — O Lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>, this is an expression of conceptual discrimination. The past too is thus conceptually discriminated as past. Similarly the future and the present, by the nature of phenomena (<s>dharmatā</s>). The <s>Tathāgatas</s> are free from conceptual discrimination, having transcended all conceptual elaboration (<s>prapañca</s>). They are not conceptually discriminated as having the nature of form. Apart from the attainment of knowledge of ignorance, [their nature] is illuminated for the purpose of happiness. They move in the signless (<s>animitta</s>) through <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom). Therefore the <s>Tathāgatas</s> are of the nature of knowledge, having knowledge-bodies. They neither construct nor are constructed. By what are they not constructed? By the mind, in terms of self, soul (<s>jīva</s>), or person (<s>pudgala</s>). How are they not conceptually discriminated? By <s>manovijñāna</s> (mind-consciousness) operating through sense-object causes, and in terms of form, characteristic, shape, and appearance. Therefore, one should abide in that which is beyond both conceptual discrimination and non-discrimination.

body.text: api ca laṅkādhipate bhittikhacitavigrahasamaḥ sattvapracāraḥ / niśceṣṭo laṅkādhipate lokasaṃniveśaḥ karmakriyārahito 'sattvātsarvadharmāṇām / na cātra kaścicchṛṇoti śrūyate vā / nirmitapratimo hi laṅkādhipate lokasaṃniveśaḥ / na ca tīrthyabālayogino vibhāvayanti / ya evaṃ paśyati laṅkādhipate, sa samyakpaśyati / anyathā paśyanto vikalpe carantīti / svavikalpā dvidhā gṛhṇanti / tadyathā darpaṇāntargataṃ svabimbapratibimbaṃ jale vā svāṅgacchāyā vā jyotsnādīpapradīpite vā gṛhe vā aṅgacchāyā pratiśrutkāni / atha svavikalpagrahaṇaṃ pratigṛhya dharmādharmaṃ prativikalpayanti / na ca dharmādharmayoḥ prahāṇena caranti / vikalpayanti puṣṇanti, na praśamaṃ pratilabhante / ekāgrasyaitadadhivacanam - tathāgatagarbhasvapratyātmāryajñānagocarasyaitatpraveśo yatsamādhiḥ paramo jāyata iti //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O Lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>, the activity of beings is like figures carved on a wall. Motionless, O Lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>, is the world's arrangement, devoid of the action of <s>karma</s>, due to the non-existence of all phenomena. And here no one hears or is heard. For the world's arrangement, O Lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>, is like a constructed image. But the non-Buddhist teachers and childish <s>yogins</s> do not discern this. One who sees thus, O Lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>, sees rightly. Those who see otherwise move in conceptual discrimination. Their own conceptual discriminations grasp in a twofold manner — just as one's own reflection-image within a mirror, or the shadow of one's body in water, or the shadow of one's limbs in a house illuminated by moonlight or lamplight, or echoes. Then, having grasped their own conceptual grasping, they conceptually discriminate <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>. But they do not conduct themselves through the abandonment of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>. They discriminate and nourish [discrimination], and do not attain quiescence. This is the expression of the one-pointed [mind]: the entry into the domain of the noble self-realized knowledge of the <s>Tathāgatagarbha</s> (womb of the <s>Tathāgata</s>) — [is that state] in which the supreme <s>samādhi</s> (meditation) is born.

body.text: rāvaṇādhyeṣaṇāparivarto nāma prathamaḥ //
body.translated_text: [Thus ends] the first chapter, named 'The Entreaty of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.'

body.text: START Parivarta 2
body.translated_text: START Chapter 2

body.text: ṣaṭtriṃśatsāhasrasarvadharmasamuccayo nāma dvitīyaḥ parivartaḥ /
body.translated_text: The second chapter, named 'The Collection of All Dharmas in Thirty-Six Thousand.'

body.text: atha khalu mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvo mahāmatibodhisattvasahitaḥ sarvabuddhakṣetrānucārī buddhānubhāvena utthāyāsanādekāṃsamuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena bhagavāṃstenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantaṃ gāthābhirabhyaṣṭāvīt - utpādabhaṅgarahito lokaḥ khapuṣpasaṃnibhaḥ /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s>, accompanied by other <s>Bodhisattva Mahāmatis</s>, wanderer through all <s>Buddha</s>-fields, by the power of the <s>Buddha</s>, rising from his seat, arranging his upper robe over one shoulder, placing his right knee on the ground, and joining his palms toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>, praised the <s>Bhagavān</s> with verses: The world is free from arising and cessation, resembling a flower in the sky;

body.text: sadasannopalabdhaste prajñayā kṛpayā ca te // Lank_2.1 //
body.translated_text: neither existent nor non-existent are things obtained by you, through <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) and <s>kṛpā</s> (compassion). || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.1 ||

children.translated_text: All <s>dharmas</s> are like illusions, free from mind and consciousness;

children.text: sadasannopalabdhāste prajñayā kṛpayā ca te // Lank_2.2 //
children.translated_text: neither existent nor non-existent are they obtained by you, through wisdom and compassion. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.2 ||
The world, free from the eternal and the annihilationist [views], is always like a dream;

children.text: sadasannopalabdhaste prajñayā kṛpayā ca te // Lank_2.3 //
children.translated_text: neither existent nor non-existent are things obtained by you, through wisdom and compassion. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.3 ||
What praise can there be for the <s>Dharmakāya</s> (truth-body), whose nature is that of illusion and dream?

children.text: bhāvānāṃ niḥsvabhāvānāṃ yo 'nutpādaḥ sa saṃbhavaḥ // Lank_2.4 //
children.translated_text: Of entities that have no inherent nature — their non-arising is their arising. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.4 ||
Whose vision is unseen, disconnected from sense-faculties and objects —

children.text: praśaṃsā yadi vā nindā tasyocyeta kathaṃ mune // Lank_2.5 //
children.translated_text: how could praise or blame be spoken of that one, O <s>Muni</s> (Sage)? || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.5 ||
The selflessness (<s>nairātmya</s>) of <s>dharma</s> and <s>pudgala</s> (person), and the afflictive (<s>kleśa</s>) and cognitive (<s>jñeya</s>) [obscurations] — always for you

children.text: viśuddhamānimittena prajñayā kṛpayā ca te // Lank_2.6 //
children.translated_text: purified through the signless, through wisdom and compassion. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.6 ||

children.text: na nirvāsi nirvāṇena nirvāṇaṃ tvayi saṃsthitam /
children.translated_text: You have not entered <s>nirvāṇa</s> through [mere] extinction; <s>nirvāṇa</s> abides in you,
free from <s>Buddha</s> and what-is-to-be-awakened-to, beyond the sides of existence and non-existence. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.7 ||
Those who see the <s>Muni</s> as peaceful, thus free from arising —

children.text: te bhonti nirupādānā ihāmutra nirañjanāḥ // Lank_2.8 //
children.translated_text: they become free from clinging (<s>upādāna</s>), unstained in this world and the next. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.8 ||

body.text: atha khalu mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantamābhiḥ sārūpyābhirgāthābhirabhiṣṭutya svanāmagotraṃ bhagavate saṃśrāvayati sma -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s>, having praised the <s>Bhagavān</s> with these befitting verses, announced his own name and lineage to the <s>Bhagavān</s>:

children.translated_text: I am <s>Mahāmati</s>, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, one who has entered the path of the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle);

children.text: aṣṭottaraṃ praśnaśataṃ pṛcchāmi vadatāṃ varam // Lank_2.9 //
children.translated_text: I ask one hundred and eight questions of you, the best of speakers. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.9 ||

children.text: tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā buddho lokavidāṃ varaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having heard those words of his, the <s>Buddha</s>, best among world-knowers,
surveying the entire assembly, [spoke] to the pure son of the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One): || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.10 ||

children.text: pṛcchantu māṃ jinasutāstvaṃ ca pṛccha mahāmate /
children.translated_text: Let the sons of the <s>Jina</s> (Conqueror) ask me, and you too ask, O <s>Mahāmati</s>;
I shall teach you the domain of inner self-realization. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.11 ||

body.text: atha khalu mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavatā kṛtāvakāśo bhagavataścaraṇayornipatya bhagavantaṃ praśnaṃ paripṛcchati sma -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s>, having been given opportunity by the <s>Bhagavān</s>, falling at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, asked the <s>Bhagavān</s> questions:

children.text: kathaṃ hi śudhyate tarkaḥ kasmāttarkaḥ pravartate /
children.translated_text: How is reasoning purified, and from what does reasoning arise?

children.text: kathaṃ hi dṛśyate bhrāntiḥ kasmādbhrāntiḥ pravartate // Lank_2.12 //
children.translated_text: How is delusion perceived, and from what does delusion arise? || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.12 ||
Why are there [Buddha-]fields and emanations, and what are the characteristics and the non-Buddhist teachers?

children.text: nirābhāsaḥ kramaḥ kena jinaputrāśca te kutaḥ // Lank_2.13 //
children.translated_text: What is appearance-free? By what is there gradual progression? And whence are the sons of the <s>Jina</s>? || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.13 ||

children.text: muktasya gamanaṃ kutra baddhaḥ kaḥ kena mucyate /
children.translated_text: Where does the liberated one go? Who is bound and by what is one freed?

children.text: dhyāyināṃ viṣayaḥ ko 'sau kathaṃ yānatrayaṃ bhavet // Lank_2.14 //
children.translated_text: What is the domain of meditators, and how do the three vehicles (<s>yānas</s>) come to be? || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.14 ||

children.text: pratyate jāyate kiṃ tatkāryaṃ kiṃ kāraṇaṃ ca kim /
children.translated_text: From what condition does [something] arise? What is an effect and what is a cause?

children.text: ubhayāntakathā kena kathaṃ vā saṃpravartate // Lank_2.15 //
children.translated_text: By whom is the discourse on both extremes, and how does it proceed? || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.15 ||
How does the formless (<s>ārūpya</s>) attainment come about, and [how does] cessation?

children.text: saṃjñānirodhaśca kathaṃ kathaṃ kasmāddhi mucyate // Lank_2.16 //
children.translated_text: And how does the cessation of perception [come about]? How and from what is one liberated? || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.16 ||
By what does action arise? What is the movement of embodied beings?

children.text: kathaṃ dṛśyaṃ vibhāvo kathaṃ kathaṃ bhūmiṣu vartate // Lank_2.17 //
children.translated_text: How is the visible [perceived]? How is dissolution? How does one progress through the [<s>Bodhisattva</s>] stages (<s>bhūmis</s>)? || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.17 ||

children.text: nirbhidyentribhavaṃ ko 'sau kiṃ sthānaṃ kā tanurbhavet /
children.translated_text: Who is the one who breaks through the three realms of existence? What is the station? What body would there be?

children.text: sthitaḥ pravartate kutra jinaputraḥ kathaṃ bhavet // Lank_2.18 //
children.translated_text: Established where does [a being] proceed? How does one become a son of the <s>Jina</s>? || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.18 ||
By what are the superknowledges (<s>abhijñās</s>) obtained, and the masteries (<s>vaśitās</s>) and <s>samādhis</s> (meditative absorptions)?

children.text: samādhyate kathaṃ cittaṃ brūhi me jinapuṃgava // Lank_2.19 //
children.translated_text: How is the mind collected in <s>samādhi</s>? Tell me, O best of Conquerors. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.19 ||
How and why is there the <s>ālaya</s> (store-consciousness), and also <s>manovijñāna</s> (mind-consciousness)?

children.text: kathaṃ pravartate dṛśyaṃ kathaṃ dṛśyānnivartate // Lank_2.20 //
children.translated_text: How does the visible arise? How does one turn away from the visible? || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.20 ||
How and by what are there lineage (<s>gotra</s>) and non-lineage? How does mind-only (<s>cittamātra</s>) come about?

children.text: lakṣaṇasya vyavasthānaṃ nairātmyaṃ ca kathaṃ bhavet // Lank_2.21 //
children.translated_text: How is the establishment of characteristics? And how does selflessness (<s>nairātmya</s>) come about? || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.21 ||

children.text: kathaṃ na vidyate sattvaḥ saṃvṛtyā deśanā katham /
children.translated_text: How is it that beings do not [truly] exist? How is there teaching through conventional truth (<s>saṃvṛti</s>)?
How do the views of eternalism and annihilationism not arise? || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.22 ||

children.text: kathaṃ hi tīrthikāstvaṃ ca lakṣaṇairna virudhyase /
children.translated_text: How is it that you and the non-Buddhist teachers are not contradicted by [your respective] characteristics?

children.text: naiyāyikāḥ kathaṃ brūhi bhaviṣyanti anāgate // Lank_2.23 //
children.translated_text: Tell [me], how will the logicians (<s>naiyāyikas</s>) be in the future? || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.23 ||

children.text: śūnyatā ca kathaṃ kena kṣaṇabhaṅgaśca te katham /
children.translated_text: How and by what is <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness)? And how is momentary destruction for you?

children.text: kathaṃ pravartate garbhaḥ kathaṃ loko nirīhikaḥ // Lank_2.24 //
children.translated_text: How does the [<s>Tathāgata</s>-]embryo (<s>garbha</s>) operate? How is the world without agent? || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.24 ||
By what is [the world] like an illusion and a dream? How is it like a <s>gandharva</s> [city]?

children.text: marīcidakacandrābhaḥ kena loko bravīhi me // Lank_2.25 //
children.translated_text: Like a mirage, like water, like the moon [reflected] — by what is the world [thus]? Tell me. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.25 ||
How and by what are the factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅgas</s>)? Whence do the wings of awakening (<s>bodhipakṣas</s>) arise?

children.text: marāśca deśasaṃkṣobho bhavadṛṣṭiḥ kathaṃ bhavet // Lank_2.26 //
children.translated_text: What are <s>Māra</s> and the disturbance of the land? How does the view of becoming arise? || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.26 ||
How is [the world] unborn and unceasing, resembling a flower in the sky?

children.text: kathaṃ ca budhyase lokaṃ kathaṃ brūṣe nirakṣaram // Lank_2.27 //
children.translated_text: And how do you awaken to the world? How do you teach [it as] without syllables? || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.27 ||
By what would one become free from conceptual discrimination? And how are [the <s>Tathāgatas</s>] like space?

children.text: tathatā bhavetkatividhā cittaṃ pāramitāḥ kati // Lank_2.28 //
children.translated_text: How many kinds of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) would there be? How many are the minds and <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections)? || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.28 ||
How does the progression through the stages (<s>bhūmis</s>) come about? And what is the course of appearance-free [realization]?

children.text: nairātmyaṃ ca dvidhā kena kathaṃ jñeyaṃ viśudhyati // Lank_2.29 //
children.translated_text: And how is selflessness (<s>nairātmya</s>) twofold? How is the knowable (<s>jñeya</s>) purified? || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.29 ||

children.text: jñānaṃ katividhaṃ nātha śīlaṃ sattvākarāṇi ca /
children.translated_text: How many kinds of knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>) are there, O Lord? And [how many kinds of] moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>) and types of beings?
By whom were the lineages of gold, gems, and pearls set in motion? [Laṅk 2.30]
By whom is speech the knower of the diversity of beings and states?
And how and by whom are the fields of knowledge and arts illuminated? [Laṅk 2.31]
How many kinds of verses (<s>gāthā</s>) are there? How do prose and poetry arise?

children.text: kathaṃ yuktiḥ katividhā vyākhyānaṃ ca kathaṃvidham // Lank_2.32 //
children.translated_text: How many kinds of reasoning are there, and what kinds of exposition? [Laṅk 2.32]

children.text: annapānaṃ ca vaicitryaṃ maithunaṃ jāyate katham /
children.translated_text: How does diversity of food and drink arise, and how does sexual union [arise]?

children.text: rājā ca cakravartī ca maṇḍalī ca kathaṃ bhavet // Lank_2.33 //
children.translated_text: How does a king, a <s>cakravartin</s> (universal monarch), and a ruler of a circle [of kingdoms] come to be? [Laṅk 2.33]
How is a kingdom to be protected? What kinds are the hosts of <s>devas</s> (gods)?
By whom are the hosts of stars and earth-[bound beings]? How are the moon and sun [established]? [Laṅk 2.34]

children.text: vidyāsthānaṃ bhavetkiṃ ca mokṣo yogī katividhaḥ /
children.translated_text: What are the fields of knowledge? How many kinds are liberation and yogins?
How many kinds of disciples are there, and how does a teacher come to be? [Laṅk 2.35]
How many kinds of <s>Buddhas</s> are there, and what kinds are the <s>Jātakas</s> (birth-stories)?
How many kinds of <s>Māras</s> are there, and how many kinds of heretics? [Laṅk 2.36]
How many kinds are their inherent natures, and how many kinds does mind (<s>citta</s>) have?

children.text: prajñaptimātraṃ ca kathaṃ brūhi me vadatāṃvara // Lank_2.37 //
children.translated_text: And how is [everything] mere designation (<s>prajñaptimātra</s>)? Tell me, O best of speakers! [Laṅk 2.37]

children.text: ghanāḥ khe pavanaṃ kena smṛtirmegho kathaṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: By what [cause] are clouds in the sky, wind, memory? How does a cloud come to be?

children.text: taruvallyaḥ kathaṃ kena brūhi me tribhaveśvara // Lank_2.38 //
children.translated_text: How and by whom are trees and creepers? Tell me, O Lord of the three realms! [Laṅk 2.38]

children.text: hayā gajā mṛgāḥ kena grahaṇaṃ yānti bāliśāḥ /
children.translated_text: By what [cause] are horses, elephants, and deer? How do foolish ones become captive?

children.text: uhoḍimā narāḥ kena brūhi me cittasārathe // Lank_2.39 //
children.translated_text: By what [cause] are humans [like] waves? Tell me, O charioteer of the mind! [Laṅk 2.39]
By what [cause] is the apprehension of the six seasons? How does an <s>icchantika</s> (spiritually incorrigible one) come to be?

children.text: strīpuṃnapuṃsakānāṃ ca kathaṃ janma vadāhi me // Lank_2.40 //
children.translated_text: And how is the birth of women, men, and neuters? Tell me! [Laṅk 2.40]
How does one turn away from yoga, and how does yoga proceed?

children.text: kathaṃ caivaṃvidhā yoge narāḥ sthāpyā vadāhi me // Lank_2.41 //
children.translated_text: How are people of such kinds established in yoga? Tell me! [Laṅk 2.41]

children.text: gatyāgatānāṃ sattvānāṃ kiṃ liṅgaṃ kiṃ ca lakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: Of beings who go and come, what is the mark and what is the characteristic?

children.text: dhaneśvaro kathaṃ kena brūhi me gaganopama // Lank_2.42 //
children.translated_text: How and by whom is a lord of wealth [produced]? Tell me, O one like space! [Laṅk 2.42]
How and by whom is the <s>Śākya</s> lineage? How is [one] born in the <s>Ikṣvāku</s> [dynasty]?

children.text: ṛṣirdīrghapatāḥ kena kathaṃ tena prabhāvitam // Lank_2.43 //
children.translated_text: By whom is the sage <s>Dīrghatapas</s> (Long-Austerity)? How was [the world] illumined by him? [Laṅk 2.43]
Why are you yourself seen everywhere, in all buddha-fields,
surrounded by sons of the <s>Jina</s> (Conqueror) with various names and forms? [Laṅk 2.44]

children.text: abhakṣyaṃ hi kathaṃ māṃsaṃ kathaṃ māṃsaṃ niṣidhyate /
children.translated_text: How is flesh not to be eaten? How is meat prohibited?

children.text: kravyādagotrasaṃbhūtā māsaṃ bhakṣyanti kena vai // Lank_2.45 //
children.translated_text: Why indeed do those born in lineages of flesh-eaters eat meat? [Laṅk 2.45]
How are [buddha-fields] shaped like the moon and sun, resembling <s>Meru</s> and lotuses?

children.text: śrīvatsasiṃhasaṃsthānāḥ kṣetrāḥ kena vadāhi me // Lank_2.46 //
children.translated_text: How are [there] fields with <s>Śrīvatsa</s> and lion-configurations? Tell me, by whom! [Laṅk 2.46]
How are [fields] inverted, with heads downward, resembling a magician's illusion?

children.text: sarvaratnamayā kṣetrāḥ kathaṃ kena vadāhi me // Lank_2.47 //
children.translated_text: How are fields made entirely of jewels, and by whom? Tell me! [Laṅk 2.47]
Shaped like lutes and drums, resembling various flowers and fruits,

children.text: ādityacandravirajāḥ kathaṃ kena vadāhi me // Lank_2.48 //
children.translated_text: shining like the sun and moon — how and by whom? Tell me! [Laṅk 2.48]

children.text: kena nirmāṇikā buddhāḥ kena buddhā vipākajāḥ /
children.translated_text: By whom are the <s>Nirmāṇika</s> (transformation) <s>Buddhas</s>? By whom are the <s>Vipākaja</s> (karma-result) <s>Buddhas</s>?

children.text: tathatā jñānabuddhā vai kathaṃ kena vadāhi me // Lank_2.49 //
children.translated_text: And the <s>Tathatā-jñāna</s> (suchness-wisdom) <s>Buddhas</s> — how and by whom? Tell me! [Laṅk 2.49]

children.text: kāmadhātau kathaṃ kena na vibuddho vadāhi me /
children.translated_text: How and why is there no awakening in the <s>Kāmadhātu</s> (desire-realm)? Tell me!

children.text: akaniṣṭhe kimarthaṃ tu vītarāgeṣu budhyase // Lank_2.50 //
children.translated_text: Why then do you awaken in <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> (highest heaven), among the passionless ones? [Laṅk 2.50]
When the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One) has passed into <s>nirvāṇa</s>, who will uphold the teaching?

children.text: kiyatsthāyī bhavecchāstā kiyantaṃ sthāsyate nayaḥ // Lank_2.51 //
children.translated_text: How long will the Teacher endure, and how long will the doctrine last? [Laṅk 2.51]
How many kinds is your <s>siddhānta</s> (established doctrine), and what kinds are the views?

children.text: vinayo bhikṣubhāvaśca kathaṃ kena vadāhi me // Lank_2.52 //
children.translated_text: What of the <s>vinaya</s> (discipline) and the state of a <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk)? How and by whom? Tell me! [Laṅk 2.52]
By whom is the state of <s>parāvṛtti</s> (turning-about)? How is the state of <s>nirābhāsa</s> (imagelessness) [attained]?
Of <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary awakened ones), sons of the <s>Jina</s>, and <s>Śrāvakas</s> (hearers) — tell me! [Laṅk 2.53]
By whom are the worldly <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges)? How do supramundane ones arise?

children.text: cittaṃ hi bhūmayaḥ sapta kathaṃ kena vadāhi me // Lank_2.54 //
children.translated_text: How are mind and the seven stages (<s>bhūmis</s>), and by whom? Tell me! [Laṅk 2.54]
How many kinds would your <s>saṃgha</s> (community) be? How does schism in the <s>saṃgha</s> occur?

children.text: cikitsāśāstraṃ sattvānāṃ kathaṃ kena vadāhi me // Lank_2.55 //
children.translated_text: How is the science of healing for beings, and by whom? Tell me! [Laṅk 2.55]
<s>Kāśyapa</s>, <s>Krakucchanda</s>, <s>Konākamuni</s>, and I [<s>Śākyamuni</s>] —
you speak of [these] to the sons of the <s>Jina</s>; tell [me] why, O great sage! [Laṅk 2.56]
By whom is the doctrine of the unreal self? How is the doctrine of permanence and destruction?

children.text: kasmāttattvaṃ na sarvatra cittamātraṃ prabhāṣase // Lank_2.57 //
children.translated_text: Why do you not everywhere proclaim the truth as mind-only (<s>cittamātra</s>)? [Laṅk 2.57]
By whom are forests of men and women? How are forests of myrobalan and gooseberry?
How are <s>Kailāsa</s> and <s>Cakravāla</s>? How are [bodies of] adamantine composition? [Laṅk 2.58]
Who are the mountains in between, adorned with various jewels,

children.text: ṛṣigandharvasaṃkīrṇāḥ kathaṃ kena vadāhi me // Lank_2.59 //
children.translated_text: inhabited by sages and <s>Gandharvas</s> — how and by whom? Tell me! [Laṅk 2.59]

children.text: idaṃ śrutvā mahāvīro buddho lokavidāṃ varaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having heard this, the great hero, the <s>Buddha</s>, best of world-knowers,

children.text: mahāyānamayaṃ cittaṃ buddhānāṃ hṛdayaṃ balam // Lank_2.60 //
children.translated_text: [spoke] the mind of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, the heart-force of the <s>Buddhas</s>: [Laṅk 2.60]
'Well done, well done, O greatly wise <s>Mahāmati</s>, you understand!
I shall speak in due order regarding what you have asked. [Laṅk 2.61]
Arising and non-arising, <s>nirvāṇa</s>, the characteristic of emptiness (<s>śūnya</s>),
transmigration, lack of inherent nature, <s>Buddhas</s>, sons of the <s>Pāramitās</s> (perfections); [Laṅk 2.62]
<s>Śrāvakas</s>, sons of the <s>Jina</s>, heretics, and those who dwell in the formless [realms];

children.text: merusamudrā hyacalā dvīpā kṣetrāṇi medinī // Lank_2.63 //
children.translated_text: <s>Meru</s>, oceans, mountains, islands, fields, and the earth; [Laṅk 2.63]
stars, the sun, the moon, heretics, <s>Devas</s> and <s>Asuras</s> likewise;

children.text: vimokṣā vaśitābhijñā balā dhyānā samādhayaḥ // Lank_2.64 //
children.translated_text: liberations, masteries (<s>vaśitā</s>), superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>), powers (<s>bala</s>), <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations), and <s>samādhis</s> (concentrations); [Laṅk 2.64]

children.text: nirodhā ṛddhipādāśca bodhyaṅgā mārga eva ca /
children.translated_text: cessations (<s>nirodha</s>), bases of spiritual power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>), factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>), and the path itself;

children.text: dhyānāni cāpramāṇāni skandhā gatyāgatāni ca // Lank_2.65 //
children.translated_text: meditations and the immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>), aggregates (<s>skandha</s>), goings and comings; [Laṅk 2.65]
attainments (<s>samāpatti</s>), cessations, emergence, and the teaching of mind;

children.text: cittaṃ manaśca vijñānaṃ nairātmyaṃ dharmapañcakam // Lank_2.66 //
children.translated_text: mind (<s>citta</s>), <s>manas</s>, and consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>), selflessness (<s>nairātmya</s>), and the five dharmas; [Laṅk 2.66]

children.text: svabhāvaḥ kalpanā kalpyaṃ dṛśyaṃ dṛṣṭidvayaṃ katham /
children.translated_text: inherent nature (<s>svabhāva</s>), conceptualization, the conceptualized, the perceived, and the two views — how?
vehicles, forms, lineages, and those born of gold, gems, and pearls; [Laṅk 2.67]
<s>Icchantikas</s>, great elements, bees, and the one-<s>Buddha</s>-nature;

children.text: jñānaṃ jñeyo gamaṃ prāptiḥ sattvānāṃ ca bhavābhavam // Lank_2.68 //
children.translated_text: knowledge, the knowable, going, attainment, and the becoming and non-becoming of beings; [Laṅk 2.68]

children.text: hayā gajā mṛgāḥ kena grahaṇaṃ brūhi me katham /
children.translated_text: by whom are horses, elephants, and deer? How does captivity [occur]? Tell me!
How are [doctrines] connected with examples and reasons? How is the established teaching? [Laṅk 2.69]

children.text: kāryaṃ ca kāraṇaṃ kena nānābhrāntistathā nayam /
children.translated_text: By whom are effect and cause, the various delusions, and the method?

children.text: cittamātraṃ na dṛśyo 'sti bhūmīnāṃ nāsti vai kramaḥ // Lank_2.70 //
children.translated_text: There is mind-only (<s>cittamātra</s>), nothing perceived exists; there is no gradation of the stages (<s>bhūmis</s>). [Laṅk 2.70]
By whom is the hundred[-fold] <s>nirābhāsa-parāvṛtti</s> (imageless turning-about)? Tell me!
The science of healing, crafts, arts, knowledge, and scripture; [Laṅk 2.71]

children.text: acalānāṃ tathā meroḥ pramāṇaṃ hi kṣiteḥ katham /
children.translated_text: what is the measure of the mountains and of <s>Meru</s>? And how [great] is the earth?

children.text: udadheścandrasūryāṇāṃ pramāṇaṃ brūhi me katham // Lank_2.72 //
children.translated_text: What is the measure of the ocean, the moon, and the sun? Tell me! [Laṅk 2.72]
How many atoms are in the body of a being — inferior, superior, and middling?

children.text: kṣetre kṣetre rajāḥ kṛtto dhanvo dhanve bhavetkati // Lank_2.73 //
children.translated_text: How many atoms in each field? How many in each league (<s>dhanvan</s>)? [Laṅk 2.73]
In a hand[-span], a bow[-length], a <s>krośa</s>, a <s>yojana</s>, and a half-<s>yojana</s>?

children.text: śaśavātāyanaṃ likṣā eḍakaṃ hi yavāḥ kati // Lank_2.74 //
children.translated_text: A rabbit-[hair-tip], a mote, a louse-egg, a sheep[-hair], and how many barley-grains? [Laṅk 2.74]

children.text: prasthe hi syādyavāḥ kyantaḥ prasthārdhe ca yavāḥ kati /
children.translated_text: How many barley-grains in a <s>prastha</s> (measure)? And how many barley-grains in a half-<s>prastha</s>?

children.text: droṇe khāryāṃ tathā lakṣāḥ koṭyo vai biṃbarāḥ kati // Lank_2.75 //
children.translated_text: In a <s>droṇa</s>, a <s>khārī</s>, how many <s>lakṣas</s>, <s>koṭis</s>, and <s>bimbaras</s>? [Laṅk 2.75]

children.text: sarṣape hyaṇavaḥ kyanto rakṣikā sarṣapāḥ kati /
children.translated_text: How many atoms in a mustard seed? How many mustard seeds in a <s>rakṣikā</s>?

children.text: katirakṣiko bhavenmāṣo dharaṇaṃ māṣakāḥ kati // Lank_2.76 //
children.translated_text: How many <s>rakṣikās</s> make a <s>māṣa</s>? How many <s>māṣas</s> in a <s>dharaṇa</s>? [Laṅk 2.76]

children.text: karṣo hi dharaṇāḥ kyantaḥ palaṃ vai kati kārṣikā /
children.translated_text: How many <s>dharaṇas</s> in a <s>karṣa</s>? How many <s>karṣas</s> in a <s>pala</s>?
By this method of calculation, how many <s>palas</s> would <s>Meru</s> be?

children.text: evaṃ hi pṛccha māṃ putra anyathā kiṃ nu pṛcchasi // Lank_2.77 //
children.translated_text: Thus ask me, O son! Why do you ask otherwise? [Laṅk 2.77]
Of <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, <s>Śrāvakas</s>, <s>Buddhas</s>, and true sons of the <s>Jina</s> —

children.text: katyaṇuko bhavetkāyaḥ kiṃ nu evaṃ na pṛcchasi // Lank_2.78 //
children.translated_text: how many atoms would [each] body be? Why do you not ask thus? [Laṅk 2.78]

children.text: vahneḥ śikhā katyaṇukā pavane hyaṇavaḥ kati /
children.translated_text: How many atoms in a flame of fire? How many atoms in the wind?

children.text: indriye indriye kyanto romakūpe bhruvoḥ kati // Lank_2.79 //
children.translated_text: How many in each sense-organ? How many in a hair-pore and in the eyebrows? [Laṅk 2.79]
By what [cause] are lords of wealth, men, kings, and <s>cakravartins</s> (universal monarchs)?

children.text: rājyaṃ ca taiḥ kathaṃ rakṣyaṃ mokṣaścaiṣāṃ kathaṃ bhavet // Lank_2.80 //
children.translated_text: How is a kingdom to be protected by them, and how is their liberation attained? [Laṅk 2.80]

children.text: gadyaṃ padyaṃ kathaṃ brūṣe maithunaṃ lokaviśrutā /
children.translated_text: How do you speak of prose and poetry? [How is] sexual union famous in the world?
How is the diversity of food and drink? How are forests of men and women? [Laṅk 2.81]

children.text: vajrasaṃhananāḥ kena hyacalā brūhi me katham /
children.translated_text: By whom are [bodies] of adamantine composition? How are the mountains? Tell me!
By whom are [things] resembling illusion and dreams? How are [things] like a mirage? [Laṅk 2.82]

children.text: ghanānāṃ saṃbhavaḥ kutra ṛtūnāṃ ca kuto bhavet /
children.translated_text: Whence is the arising of clouds? And whence do the seasons come?
Whence is the flavor-nature of flavors? Whence are female, male, and neuter? [Laṅk 2.83]

children.text: śobhāśca jinaputrāśca kutra me pṛccha māṃ suta /
children.translated_text: And splendors and sons of the <s>Jina</s> — where? Ask me, O son!

children.text: kathaṃ hi acalā divyā ṛṣigandharvamaṇḍitāḥ // Lank_2.84 //
children.translated_text: How are the divine mountains adorned by sages and <s>Gandharvas</s>? [Laṅk 2.84]

children.text: muktasya gamanaṃ kutra baddhaḥ kaḥ kena mucyate /
children.translated_text: Where does the liberated one go? Who is bound, and by whom is one freed?

children.text: dhyāyināṃ viṣayaḥ ko 'sau nirmāṇastīrthakāni ca // Lank_2.85 //
children.translated_text: What is the domain of meditators? [What of] the <s>Nirmāṇa</s> (emanation) and heretical [views]? [Laṅk 2.85]
By whom are the unreal, the real, and non-action? How does the perceived cease?

children.text: kathaṃ hi śudhyate tarkaḥ kena tarkaḥ pravartate // Lank_2.86 //
children.translated_text: How is reasoning purified? By whom does reasoning proceed? [Laṅk 2.86]

children.text: kriyā pravartate kena gamanaṃ brūhi me katham /
children.translated_text: By whom does action proceed? How does going [occur]? Tell me!

children.text: saṃjñāyāśchedanaṃ kena samādhiḥ kena cocyate // Lank_2.87 //
children.translated_text: By whom is the cutting of perception? And by whom is <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) spoken of? [Laṅk 2.87]

children.text: vidārtha tribhavaṃ ko 'sau kiṃ sthānaṃ kā tanurbhavet /
children.translated_text: Who is that knower of the three realms? What is the abode? What body would there be?

children.text: asatyātmakathā kena saṃvṛtyā deśanā katham // Lank_2.88 //
children.translated_text: By whom is the doctrine of the unreal self? How is teaching by conventional [truth]? [Laṅk 2.88]

children.text: lakṣaṇaṃ pṛcchase kena nairātmyaṃ pṛcchase katham /
children.translated_text: Why do you ask about characteristics? Why do you ask about selflessness (<s>nairātmya</s>)?

children.text: garbhā naiyāyikāḥ kena pṛcchase māṃ jinaurasāḥ // Lank_2.89 //
children.translated_text: By whom are the womb-[doctrines] and the logicians? You ask me, O sons of the <s>Jina</s>! [Laṅk 2.89]
By whom are the views of eternalism and annihilation? How is the mind afflicted?

children.text: abhilāpastathā jñānaṃ śīlaṃ gotraṃ jinaurasāḥ // Lank_2.90 //
