children.translated_text: And speech, knowledge, conduct, and lineage, O sons of the <s>Jina</s>! [Laṅk 2.90]
Reasoning, exposition, teacher and disciple — how is the diversity of beings?

children.text: annapānaṃ nabho meghā mārāḥ prajñaptimātrakam // Lank_2.91 //
children.translated_text: Food and drink, sky, clouds, <s>Māras</s>, mere designation (<s>prajñaptimātra</s>); [Laṅk 2.91]

children.text: taruvallyaḥ kathaṃ kena pṛcchase māṃ jinaurasa /
children.translated_text: how and by whom are trees and creepers? You ask me, O son of the <s>Jina</s>!
By whom is the diversity of fields? And the sage <s>Dīrghatapas</s>? [Laṅk 2.92]

children.text: vaṃśaḥ kaste guruḥ kena pṛcchase māṃ jinaurasa /
children.translated_text: What is your lineage, and who is [your] teacher, and by whom? You ask me, O son of the <s>Jina</s>!

children.text: uhoḍimā narā yoge kāmadhātau na budhyase // Lank_2.93 //
children.translated_text: Humans [like] waves in yoga — [why] do you not awaken in the <s>Kāmadhātu</s>? [Laṅk 2.93]

children.text: siddhānto hyakaniṣṭheṣu yuktiṃ pṛcchasi me katham /
children.translated_text: The established doctrine [is revealed] in <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> — how do you ask me about reasoning?

children.text: abhijñāṃ laukikāṃ kena kathaṃ bhikṣutvameva ca // Lank_2.94 //
children.translated_text: By whom are the worldly superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>)? How is monkhood itself? [Laṅk 2.94]

children.text: nairmāṇikān vipākasthān buddhān pṛcchasi me katham /
children.translated_text: How do you ask me about the <s>Nirmāṇika</s> (transformation) and <s>Vipākastha</s> (karma-result) <s>Buddhas</s>?

children.text: tathatājñānabuddhā vai saṃghāścaiva kathaṃ bhavet // Lank_2.95 //
children.translated_text: And the <s>Tathatā-jñāna</s> (suchness-wisdom) <s>Buddhas</s> — and how would the <s>Saṃghas</s> be? [Laṅk 2.95]
Fields resembling lutes, drums, and flowers, devoid of [ordinary] worlds;

children.text: cittaṃ hi bhūmayaḥ sapta pṛcchase māṃ jinaurasa /
children.translated_text: mind and the seven stages — you ask me, O son of the <s>Jina</s>!

children.text: etāṃścānyāṃśca subahūn praśnān pṛcchasi māṃ suta // Lank_2.96 //
children.translated_text: These and many other questions you ask me, O son! [Laṅk 2.96]
Each one endowed with [proper] characteristics, free from the fault of [wrong] views —

children.text: siddhāntaṃ deśanāṃ vakṣye sahasā tvaṃ śṛṇohi me // Lank_2.97 //
children.translated_text: I shall teach the established doctrine and the teaching; listen to me at once! [Laṅk 2.97]

children.text: upanyāsaṃ kariṣyāmi padānāṃ śṛṇu me suta /
children.translated_text: I shall make an exposition of the terms; listen, O son!
One hundred and eight terms, as described by the <s>Buddhas</s>: [Laṅk 2.98]

body.text: atha khalu mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantametadavocat - katamadbhagavan aṣṭottarapadaśatam? bhagavānāha - utpādapadam anutpādapadam, nityapadam anityapadam, lakṣaṇapadam alakṣaṇapadam, sthityanyathātvapadam asthityanyathātvapadam, kṣaṇikapadam akṣaṇikapadam, svabhāvapadam asvabhāvapadam, śūnyatāpadam aśūnyatāpadam, ucchedapadam anucchedapadam, cittapadam acittapadam, madhyamapadam amadhyamapadam, śāśvatapadam aśāśvatapadam,
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'What, Blessed One, are the one hundred and eight terms?' The Blessed One said: 'The term arising, the term non-arising; the term permanent, the term impermanent; the term characteristic, the term non-characteristic; the term persistence-and-change, the term non-persistence-and-change; the term momentary, the term non-momentary; the term inherent nature, the term non-inherent-nature; the term emptiness, the term non-emptiness; the term annihilation, the term non-annihilation; the term mind, the term non-mind; the term middle, the term non-middle; the term eternal, the term non-eternal;'

body.text: atha khalu mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ punarapi bhagavantametadavocat - katividho bhagavan vijñānānāmutpādasthitinirodho bhavati? bhagavānāha - dvividho mahāmate vijñānānāmutpattisthitinirodho bhavati, na ca tārkikā avabudhyante yaduta prabandhanirodho lakṣaṇanirodhaśca / dvividha utpādo vijñānānām, prabandhotpado lakṣaṇotpādaśca / dvividhā sthitiḥ prabandhasthitirlakṣaṇasthitiśca / trividhaṃ vijñānaṃ pravṛttilakṣaṇaṃ karmalakṣaṇaṃ jātilakṣaṇaṃ ca / dvividhaṃ mahāmate vijñānaṃ saṃkṣepeṇa aṣṭalakṣaṇoktaṃ khyātivijñānaṃ vastuprativikalpavijñānaṃ ca / yathā mahāmate darpaṇasya rūpagrahaṇam, evaṃ khyātivijñānasyākhyāsyati / khyātivijñānaṃ ca mahāmate vastuprativikalpavijñānaṃ ca / dve 'pyete 'bhinnalakṣaṇe 'nyonyahetuke / tatra khyātivijñānaṃ mahāmate acintyavāsanāpariṇāmahetukam / vastuprativikalpavijñānaṃ ca mahāmate viṣayavikalpahetukamanādikālaprapañcavāsanāhetukaṃ ca //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s> again addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s> thus: Of how many kinds, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, is the arising, abiding, and cessation of the <s>vijñānas</s> (consciousnesses)? The <s>Bhagavān</s> replied: Of two kinds, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the arising, abiding, and cessation of the <s>vijñānas</s>, and the logicians do not comprehend [this] — namely, cessation of the continuum (<s>prabandhanirodha</s>) and cessation of characteristics (<s>lakṣaṇanirodha</s>). Of two kinds is the arising of the <s>vijñānas</s>: arising of the continuum (<s>prabandhotpāda</s>) and arising of characteristics (<s>lakṣaṇotpāda</s>). Of two kinds is the abiding: abiding of the continuum (<s>prabandhasthiti</s>) and abiding of characteristics (<s>lakṣaṇasthiti</s>). Of three kinds is <s>vijñāna</s> with respect to its characteristics: the characteristic of activity (<s>pravṛttilakṣaṇa</s>), the characteristic of action (<s>karmalakṣaṇa</s>), and the characteristic of birth (<s>jātilakṣaṇa</s>). Of two kinds, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, in brief, is <s>vijñāna</s> as stated with eight characteristics: the <s>vijñāna</s> of manifestation (<s>khyātivijñāna</s>) and the <s>vijñāna</s> of discriminating objects (<s>vastuprativikalpavijñāna</s>). Just as, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, a mirror grasps forms, so does the <s>vijñāna</s> of manifestation manifest. The <s>vijñāna</s> of manifestation and the <s>vijñāna</s> of discriminating objects, O <s>Mahāmati</s> — these two, though of inseparable characteristics, are mutually causative. Therein, the <s>vijñāna</s> of manifestation, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, has as its cause the transformation of inconceivable impressions (<s>acintyavāsanāpariṇāma</s>). The <s>vijñāna</s> of discriminating objects, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, has as its cause the discrimination of objects (<s>viṣayavikalpa</s>) and the impressions of beginningless proliferation (<s>anādikālaprapañcavāsanā</s>).

body.text: tatra sarvendriyavijñānanirodho mahāmate yaduta ālayavijñānasya abhūtaparikalpavāsanāvaicitryanirodhaḥ / eṣa hi mahāmate lakṣaṇanirodhaḥ / prabandhanirodhaḥ punarmahāmate yasmācca pravartate / yasmāditi mahāmate yadāśrayeṇa yadālambanena ca / tatra yadāśrayamanādikālaprapañcadauṣṭhulyavāsanā yadālambanaṃ svacittadṛśyavijñānaviṣaye vikalpāḥ / tadyathā mahāmate mṛtparamāṇubhyo mṛtpiṇḍaḥ, na cānyo nānanyaḥ, tathā suvarṇaṃ bhūṣaṇāt / yadi ca mahāmate mṛtpiṇḍo mṛtparamāṇubhyo 'nyaḥ syāt, tairnārabdhaḥ syāt / sa cārabdhastairmṛtparamāṇubhiḥ, tasmānnānyaḥ / athānanyaḥ syāt, mṛtpiṇḍaparamāṇvoḥ pratibhāgo na syāt / evameva mahāmate pravṛttivijñānānyālayavijñānajātilakṣaṇādanyāni syuḥ, anālayavijñānahetukāni syuḥ / athānanyāni pravṛttivijñānanirodhe ālayavijñānavirodhaḥ syāt, sa ca na bhavati svajātilakṣaṇanirodhaḥ / tasmānmahāmate na svajātilakṣaṇanirodho vijñānānāṃ kiṃ tu karmalakṣaṇanirodhaḥ / svajātilakṣaṇe punarnirudhyamāne ālayavijñānanirodhaḥ syāt / ālayavijñāne punarnirudhyamāne nirviśiṣṭastīrthakarocchedavādenāyaṃ vādaḥ syāt / tīrthakarāṇāṃ mahāmate ayaṃ vādo yaduta viṣayagrahaṇoparamādvijñānaprabandhoparamo bhavati / vijñānaprabandhoparamādanādikālaprabandhavyucchittiḥ syāt / kāraṇataśca mahāmate tīrthakarāḥ prabandhapravṛttiṃ varṇayanti / na cakṣurvijñānasya rūpālokasamudayata utpattiṃ varṇayanti anyatra kāraṇataḥ / kāraṇaṃ punarmahāmate pradhānapuruṣeśvarakālāṇupravādāḥ //
body.translated_text: Therein, the cessation of all sense-consciousnesses, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the cessation of the variety of impressions of false imagination (<s>abhūtaparikalpavāsanāvaicitrya</s>) in the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> (store-consciousness). This indeed, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the cessation of characteristics. The cessation of the continuum, moreover, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, [concerns] that from which [consciousness] proceeds. "That from which," O <s>Mahāmati</s>, means: by which support (<s>āśraya</s>) and by which object (<s>ālambana</s>). Therein, the support is the impressions of the depravity of beginningless proliferation; the object is the discriminations (<s>vikalpa</s>) regarding the domain of consciousness that appears as one's own mind. Just as, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, a lump of clay [arises] from clay-atoms, being neither different nor non-different [from them], and similarly gold from ornaments. If, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the lump of clay were different from the clay-atoms, it would not be produced from them; but it is produced from those clay-atoms, therefore it is not different. If it were non-different, there would be no distinction between lump and atoms. Even so, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the active consciousnesses (<s>pravṛttivijñāna</s>) would be different from the <s>ālayavijñāna</s>'s birth-characteristic, and would have no <s>ālayavijñāna</s> as their cause. But if they were non-different, then with the cessation of the active consciousnesses there would be cessation of the <s>ālayavijñāna</s>; and that does not occur — the cessation of its own birth-characteristic. Therefore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, there is no cessation of the <s>vijñānas</s>'own birth-characteristic, but rather cessation of the action-characteristic (<s>karmalakṣaṇa</s>). If the own birth-characteristic were to cease, there would be cessation of the <s>ālayavijñāna</s>. If the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> were to cease, this doctrine would be indistinguishable from the annihilationist doctrine of the heretical teachers (<s>tīrthakara</s>). The heretical teachers, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, hold the doctrine that from the cessation of the grasping of objects, there follows the cessation of the continuum of consciousness; from the cessation of the continuum of consciousness, there would be the extinction of the beginningless continuum. The heretical teachers, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, describe the activity of the continuum from [the standpoint of] causation; they describe the arising of eye-consciousness from the conjunction of form and light, not otherwise than from causation. And causation, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, [for them] consists of the doctrines of <s>Pradhāna</s> (primal matter), <s>Puruṣa</s> (spirit), <s>Īśvara</s> (lord), time (<s>kāla</s>), and atoms (<s>aṇu</s>).

body.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate saptavidho bhāvasvabhāvo bhavati yaduta samudayasvabhāvo bhāvasvabhāvo lakṣaṇasvabhāvo mahābhūtasvabhāvo hetusvabhāvaḥ pratyayasvabhāvo niṣpattisvabhāvaśca saptamaḥ //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the inherent nature of entities (<s>bhāvasvabhāva</s>) is of seven kinds, namely: the inherent nature of origination (<s>samudayasvabhāva</s>), the inherent nature of entity (<s>bhāvasvabhāva</s>), the inherent nature of characteristics (<s>lakṣaṇasvabhāva</s>), the inherent nature of great elements (<s>mahābhūtasvabhāva</s>), the inherent nature of cause (<s>hetusvabhāva</s>), the inherent nature of conditions (<s>pratyayasvabhāva</s>), and the inherent nature of accomplishment (<s>niṣpattisvabhāva</s>) as the seventh.

body.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate saptavidhaḥ paramārtho yaduta cittagocaro jñānagocaraḥ prajñāgocaro dṛṣṭidvayagocaro dṛṣṭidvayātikrāntagocaraḥ sutabhūmyanukramaṇagocarastathāgatasya pratyātmagatigocaraḥ //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the supreme truth (<s>paramārtha</s>) is of seven kinds, namely: the domain of mind (<s>cittagocara</s>), the domain of knowledge (<s>jñānagocara</s>), the domain of wisdom (<s>prajñāgocara</s>), the domain of the two views (<s>dṛṣṭidvayagocara</s>), the domain transcending the two views (<s>dṛṣṭidvayātikrāntagocara</s>), the domain of progressive traversal of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> stages (<s>sutabhūmyanukramaṇagocara</s>), and the domain of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s inner realization (<s>pratyātmagati</s>).

body.text: etanmahāmate atītānāgatapratyutpannānāṃ tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ bhāvasvabhāvaparamārthahṛdayaṃ yena samanvāgatāstathāgatā laukikalokottaratamān dharmānāryeṇa prajñācakṣuṣā svasāmānyalakṣaṇapatitān vyavasthāpayanti / tathā ca vyavasthāpayanti yathā tīrthakaravādakudṛṣṭisādhāraṇā na bhavanti / kathaṃ ca mahāmate tīrthakaravādakudṛṣṭisādhāraṇā bhavanti? yaduta svacittaviṣayavikalpadṛṣṭyanavabodhanādvijñānānām / svacittadṛśyamātrānavatāreṇa mahāmate bālapṛthagjanā bhāvābhāvasvabhāvaparamārthadṛṣṭidvayavādino bhavanti //
body.translated_text: This, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the essence of the inherent nature of entities and the supreme truth of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly enlightened <s>Buddhas</s> of the past, future, and present. Endowed with this, the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, with the noble eye of wisdom, establish the mundane and supramundane <s>dharmas</s> as falling under specific and general characteristics. And they establish [them] in such a way that [these teachings] do not become common with the wrong views of heretical doctrines. And how, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, do [teachings] become common with the wrong views of heretical doctrines? Through the non-realization that the <s>vijñānas</s> [arise from] the discrimination of the appearances of one's own mind. Through not entering into [the realization that all is] mere appearance of one's own mind (<s>svacittadṛśyamātra</s>), O <s>Mahāmati</s>, foolish ordinary beings become proponents of the dual view (<s>dṛṣṭidvaya</s>) regarding the inherent nature of entities and non-entities and the supreme truth.

body.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate vikalpabhavatrayaduḥkhavinivartanamajñānatṛṣṇākarmapratyayavinivṛttiṃ svacittadṛśyamāyāviṣayānudarśanaṃ bhāṣiṣye / ye kecinmahāmate śramaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā abhūtvā śraddhāhetuphalābhivyaktidravyaṃ ca kālāvasthitaṃ pratyayeṣu ca skandhadhātvāyatanānāmutpādasthitiṃ cecchanti, bhūtvā ca vyayam, te mahāmate saṃtatikriyotpādabhaṅgabhavanirvāṇamārgakarmaphalasatyavināśocchedavādino bhavanti / tatkasya hetoḥ? yadidaṃ pratyakṣānupalabdherādyadarśanābhāvāt / tadyathā mahāmate ghaṭakapālābhāvo ghaṭakṛtyaṃ na karoti, nāpi dagdhabījamaṅkurakṛtyaṃ karoti, evameva mahāmate ye skandhadhātvāyatanabhāvā niruddhā nirudhyante nirotsyante, svacittadṛśyavikalpadarśanāhetutvānnāsti nairantaryapravṛttiḥ //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, I shall teach the turning away from the suffering of the three realms of existence through discrimination, the cessation of the conditions of ignorance, craving, and action, and the contemplation of the magical illusion-like nature of the objects appearing as one's own mind. Whatever ascetics (<s>śramaṇa</s>) or brahmins (<s>brāhmaṇa</s>), O <s>Mahāmati</s>, wish for the arising and abiding of the aggregates (<s>skandha</s>), elements (<s>dhātu</s>), and sense-bases (<s>āyatana</s>) in conditions — [taking them as] substance endowed with the manifestation of faith, cause, and effect, established in time, not having existed [before] — and [wish for their] destruction after having existed, they, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, become proponents of annihilation (<s>uccheda</s>) with regard to the continuum, activity, arising, breaking apart, existence, <s>nirvāṇa</s>, path, action, fruit, truth, and destruction. For what reason? Because of the non-apprehension of direct perception, and the absence of the vision of the origin. Just as, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the absence of a pot-sherd does not perform the function of a pot, nor does a burnt seed perform the function of a sprout, even so, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, for those entities of aggregates, elements, and sense-bases that have ceased, are ceasing, or will cease, because they are not the cause of the vision of discrimination that [everything is] the appearance of one's own mind — there is no uninterrupted activity.

body.text: yadi punarmahāmate abhūtvā śraddhāvijñānānāṃ trisaṃgatipratyayakriyāyogenotpattirabhaviṣyat, asatāmapi mahāmate kūrmaromnāmutpattirabhaviṣyat, sikatābhyo vā tailasya / pratijñāhānirniyamanirodhaśca mahāmate prasajyate, kriyākarmakaraṇavaiyarthyaṃ ca sadasato bruvataḥ / teṣāmapi mahāmate trisaṃgatipratyayakriyāyogenopadeśo vidyate hetuphalasvalakṣaṇatayā atītānāgatapratyutpannāsatsallakṣaṇāstitāṃ yuktyāgamaistarkabhūmau vartamānāḥ svadṛṣṭidoṣavāsanatayā nirdekṣyanti / evameva mahāmate bālapṛthagjanāḥ kudṛṣṭidaṣṭā viṣamamatayo 'jñaiḥ praṇītaṃ sarvapraṇītamiti vakṣyanti //
body.translated_text: If, however, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, there were to be an arising of the <s>vijñānas</s> through faith, [arising] from what did not exist before, through the functional connection of conditions in the three destinies, then, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, there would also be the arising of tortoise hairs or oil from sand. A loss of the thesis and the negation of the restriction would follow, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, as well as the purposelessness of action, deed, and instrument, for one who speaks of existent and non-existent. For them too, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, there is instruction through the functional connection of conditions in the three destinies, by way of the specific characteristics of cause and effect; [yet] those who dwell on the ground of logic, by the force of their own wrong-view impressions, will declare the characteristics of existent and non-existent, of past, future, and present, by reasoning and scripture. Even so, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, foolish ordinary beings, bitten by wrong views, with uneven minds, will declare that what is propounded by the ignorant is the best of all propounded [teachings].

body.text: ye punaranye mahāmate śramaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā niḥsvabhāvaghanālātacakragandharvanagarānutpādamāyāmarīcyudakacandrasvapnasvabhāvabāhyacittadṛśyavikalpānādikālaprapañcadarśanena svacittavikalpapratyayavinivṛttirahitāḥ parikalpitābhidhānalakṣyalakṣaṇābhidheyarahitā dehabhogapratiṣṭhāsamālayavijñānaviṣayagrāhyagrāhakavisaṃyuktaṃ nirābhāsagocaramutpādasthitibhaṅgavarjyaṃ svacittotpādānugataṃ vibhāvayiṣyanti, nacirātte mahāmate bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ saṃsāranirvāṇasamatāprāptā bhaviṣyanti / mahākaruṇopāyakauśalyānābhogagatena mahāmate prayogena sarvasattvamāyāpratibimbasamatayā anārabdhapratyayatayā adhyātmabāhyaviṣayavimuktatayā cittabāhyādarśanatayā animittādhiṣṭhānānugatā anupūrveṇa bhūmikramasamādhiviṣayānugamanatayā traidhātukasvacittatayā adhimuktitaḥ prativibhāvayamānā māyopamasamādhiṃ pratilabhante / svacittanirābhāsamātrāvatāreṇa prajñāpāramitāvihārānuprāptā utpādakriyāyogavirahitāḥ samādhivajrabimbopamaṃ tathāgatakāyānugataṃ tathatānirmāṇānugataṃ balābhijñāvaśitākṛpākaruṇopāyamaṇḍitaṃ sarvabuddhakṣetratīrthyāyatanopagataṃ cittamanomanovijñānarahitaṃ parāvṛttyānuśrayānupūrvakaṃ tathāgatakāyaṃ mahāmate te bodhisattvāḥ
body.translated_text: But those other <s>śramaṇas</s> or <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, who — through seeing that external appearances of mind (<s>cittadṛśya</s>) are like essenceless masses, firebrand-circles, <s>gandharva</s>-cities, non-arising, illusion, mirages, water-moons, and dreams from beginningless time's proliferation — are free from the cessation of conditions arising from the conceptualization of one's own mind, free from the imagined designations and the characteristics of what is designated and what designates, [and who] will contemplate the domain of the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> (store-consciousness) of body, enjoyment, and abode as disconnected from the grasped and the grasper, having the appearance-free as its domain, free from arising, abiding, and ceasing, following the arising of one's own mind — before long, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, those <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> will attain the equality of <s>saṃsāra</s> and <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Through effortless practice (<s>anābhogagati</s>), O <s>Mahāmati</s>, by means of great compassion and skillful means, through the equality of all beings as illusion-like reflections, through the non-initiation of conditions, through freedom from internal and external objects, through not seeing [anything] external to mind, following the establishment of the signless, by progressively entering the domain of the <s>samādhis</s> of the stages in sequence, by understanding the three realms as one's own mind, through conviction — they attain the illusion-like <s>samādhi</s>. By entering the mere appearance-free nature of one's own mind, having reached the dwelling in the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>), free from the yoga of arising and action, [they attain] the <s>Tathāgata</s>-body — like a diamond reflection of <s>samādhi</s>, following the <s>Tathāgata</s>-body, following the emanation of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), adorned with powers, superknowledges, masteries, loving-kindness, compassion, and skillful means, having reached all Buddha-fields and heretical abodes, free from mind, mentation, and consciousness — O <s>Mahāmati</s>, those <s>Bodhisattvas</s>

body.text: pratilapsyante / tasmāttarhi mahāmate bodhisattvairmahāsattvaistathāgatakāyānugamena pratilābhinā skandhadhātvāyatanacittahetupratyayakriyāyogotpādasthitibhaṅgavikalpaprapañcarahitairbhavitavyaṃ cittamātrānusāribhiḥ //
body.translated_text: will attain [that body] through the progressive transformation of the basis (<s>parāvṛtti</s>). Therefore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> should be free from the conceptual proliferation of aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>), elements (<s>dhātus</s>), sense-bases (<s>āyatanas</s>), mind, causes, conditions, action, yoga, arising, abiding, and ceasing — following mind-only (<s>cittamātra</s>) — in order to attain the <s>Tathāgata</s>-body.

body.text: anādikālāprapañcadauṣṭhulyavikalpavāsanahetukaṃ tribhavaṃ paśyato nirābhāsabuddhabhūmyanutpādasmaraṇatayā pratyātmāryadharmagatiṃgataḥ svacittavaśavartī anābhogacaryāgatiṃgato viśvarūpamaṇisadṛśaḥ sūkṣmaiḥ sattvacittānupraveśakairnirmāṇavigrahaiścittamātrāvadhāraṇatayā bhūmikramānusaṃghau pratiṣṭhāpayati / tasmāttarhi mahāmate bodhisattvena mahāsattvena svasiddhāntakuśalena bhavitavyam //
body.translated_text: For one who sees the three realms of existence as caused by the seeds (<s>vāsanā</s>) of the conceptualization of the depravity of beginningless proliferation, by recollecting the non-arising of the appearance-free Buddha-stage, having entered the course of the noble <s>dharma</s> of inner self-realization, master of one's own mind, having entered the course of effortless practice, like a wish-fulfilling jewel of universal form, through subtle emanation-bodies that enter the minds of beings, by establishing the stages in sequence through the ascertainment of mind-only — therefore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> should be skilled in his own doctrine.

body.text: punarapi mahāmatirāha - deśayatu me bhagavān cittamanomanovijñānapañcadharmasvabhāvalakṣaṇakusumadharmaparyāyaṃ buddhabodhisattvānuyātaṃ svacittadṛśyagocaravisaṃyojanaṃ sarvabhāṣyayuktitattvalakṣaṇavidāraṇaṃ sarvabuddhapravacanahṛdayaṃ laṅkāpurigirimalaye nivāsino bodhisattvānārabhyodadhitaraṃgālayavijñānagocaraṃ dharmakāyaṃ tathāgatānugītaṃ prabhāṣasva //
body.translated_text: Again <s>Mahāmati</s> said: 'May the Blessed One teach me the <s>dharma</s>-discourse called the Flower of mind, mentation, consciousness (<s>manovijñāna</s>), the five <s>dharmas</s>, and the characteristics of [their] natures — [the discourse] followed by Buddhas and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, [which is] the disjunction from the domain of what is seen by one's own mind, the splitting open of the characteristics of the truth of all logical discourse, the heart of all Buddha-teachings. Proclaim, for the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> dwelling on Mount <s>Malaya</s> in the city of <s>Laṅkā</s>, beginning [with them], the <s>Dharmakāya</s> (Dharma-body), the domain of the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> (store-consciousness) like ocean-waves, as sung by the <s>Tathāgatas</s>!'

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān punareva mahāmatiṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvametadavocat - caturbhirmahāmate kāraṇaiścakṣurvijñānaṃ pravartate / katamaiścaturbhiḥ? yaduta svacittadṛśyagrahaṇānavabodhato 'nādikālaprapañcadauṣṭhulyarūpavāsanābhiniveśato vijñānaprakṛtisvabhāvato vicitrarūpalakṣaṇakautūhalataḥ / ebhirmahāmate caturbhiḥ kāraṇairoghāntarajalasthānīyādālayavijñānātpravṛttivijñānataraṃgautpadyate / yathā mahāmate cakṣurvijñāne, evaṃ sarvandriyaparamāṇuromakūpeṣu yugapatpravṛttikramaviṣayādarśabimbadarśanavat udadheḥ pavanāhatā iva mahāmate viṣayapavanacittodadhitaraṃgā avyucchinnahetukriyālakṣaṇā anyonyavinirmuktāḥ karmajātilakṣaṇasuvinibaddharūpasvabhāvānavadhāriṇo mahāmate pañca vijñānakāyāḥ pravartante / saha taireva mahāmate pañcabhirvijñānakāyairhetuviṣayaparicchedalakṣaṇāvadhārakaṃ nāma manovijñānaṃ taddhetujaśarīraṃ pravartate / na ca teṣāṃ tasya caivaṃ bhavati - vayamatrānyonyahetukāḥ svacittadṛśyavikalpābhiniveśapravṛttā iti //
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One again said this to the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s>: 'O <s>Mahāmati</s>, eye-consciousness operates due to four causes. Which four? Namely: due to not understanding the grasping of what is seen by one's own mind; due to attachment to the seeds of the depravity of beginningless proliferation of form; due to the inherent nature of consciousness; and due to curiosity about the characteristics of various forms. Through these four causes, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, from the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> (store-consciousness) — which is like the water within a flood — the waves of the active consciousnesses (<s>pravṛttivijñāna</s>) arise. Just as with eye-consciousness, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, so in all sense-organs, atoms, and pores, [the consciousnesses] function simultaneously and sequentially, like seeing reflections in a mirror. Like waves on the ocean struck by wind, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the waves of the mind-ocean [arise] impelled by the wind of objects — with unbroken characteristics of cause and action, mutually distinct, yet bound to the characteristics of birth and type, unable to ascertain the nature of form — O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the five consciousness-groups operate. Together with those very five consciousness-groups, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, what is called <s>manovijñāna</s> (mind-consciousness) — whose characteristic is the ascertainment of the discrimination of causal objects, whose body is born from that [ālaya] cause — operates. And it is not the case that they or it have this [thought]: "We here are mutually caused, operating through attachment to the conceptualization of what is seen by our own mind."

body.text: atha ca anyonyābhinnalakṣaṇasahitāḥ pravartante vijñaptiviṣayaparicchede / tathā ca pravartamānāḥ pravartante yathā samāpannasyāpi yoginaḥ sūkṣmagativāsanāpravṛttā na prajñāyante / yogināṃ caivaṃ bhavati - nirodhya vijñānāni samāpatsyāmahe iti / te cāniruddhaireva vijñānaiḥ samāpadyante vāsanābījānirodhādaniruddhāḥ, viṣayapravṛttagrahaṇavaikalyānniruddhāḥ / evaṃ sūkṣmo mahāmate ālayavijñānagatipracāro yattathāgataṃ sthāpayitvā bhūmipratiṣṭhitāṃśca bodhisattvān, na sukaramanyaiḥ śrāvakapratyekabuddhatīrthyayogayogibhiradhigantuṃ samādhiprajñābalādhānato 'pi vā paricchettum / anyatra bhūmilakṣaṇaprajñājñānakauśalapadaprabhedaviniścayajinānantakuśalamūlopacayasvacittadṛśyavikalpaprapañcavirahitairvanagahanaguhālayāntargatairmahāmate hīnotkṛṣṭamadhyamayogayogibhirna śakyaṃ svacittavikalpadṛśyadhārādraṣṭranantakṣetrajinābhiṣekavaśitābalābhijñāsamādhayaḥ
body.translated_text: And yet they operate together with mutually undifferentiated characteristics in the discrimination of the object of cognition. And operating thus, they operate [so subtly] that even for a <s>yogin</s> who has attained [absorption], the activity of the seeds of subtle movement is not perceived. And <s>yogins</s> think thus: 'We shall attain [cessation] by ceasing the consciousnesses.' But they attain [absorption] with consciousnesses that have not in fact ceased — uncased because the seeds have not ceased, [appearing] ceased because of the deficiency of grasping the activity of objects. Thus subtle, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the course of the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> (store-consciousness), such that — except for the <s>Tathāgata</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> established in the stages — it is not easy for other <s>Śrāvaka</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, and heretical <s>yoga</s>-practitioners to realize, nor even to discriminate through the power of <s>samādhi</s> and wisdom. Except by those, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, who are free from the conceptual proliferation of what is seen by their own mind, who have the skill of the characteristics of the stages and the ascertainment of the classifications of the categories of wisdom-knowledge, who have accumulated infinite roots of merit of the <s>Jinas</s>, who dwell in caves, forests, and thickets — by <s>yoga</s>-practitioners of inferior, superior, and middling [capacity], it is not possible to attain the <s>samādhis</s> of the flow of seeing what is conceptualized by one's own mind, the consecrations of the <s>Jinas</s> of infinite realms, and the masteries, powers, and superknowledges

body.text: prāptum / kalyāṇamitrajinapuraskṛtairmahāmate śakyaṃ cittamanovijñānaṃ svacittadṛśyasvabhāvagocaravikalpasaṃsārabhavodadhiṃ karmatṛṣṇājñānahetukaṃ tartum / ata etasmātkāraṇānmahāmate yoginā kalyāṇamitrajinayoge yogaḥ prārabdhavyaḥ //
body.translated_text: [without guidance]. But O <s>Mahāmati</s>, those who are accompanied by spiritual friends (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>) and <s>Jinas</s> are able to cross the ocean of becoming in <s>saṃsāra</s> — [the ocean of] mind, mentation, and consciousness, the domain of the nature of what is seen by one's own mind, caused by <s>karma</s>, craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>), and ignorance. Therefore, for this reason, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, a <s>yogin</s> should commence <s>yoga</s> in the <s>yoga</s> of spiritual friends and <s>Jinas</s>.

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, at that time, spoke these verses:

children.translated_text: Just as waves of the ocean,

children.text: nṛtyamānāḥ pravartante vyucchedaśca na vidyate // Lank_2.99 //
children.translated_text: set in motion by the condition of wind, dance forth and there is no cessation, || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.99 ||
so the flood of the <s>ālaya</s> (store-consciousness), constantly stirred by the wind of objects,
dances forth with the varied consciousness-waves. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.100 ||

children.text: nīle rakte 'tha lavaṇe śaṅkhe kṣīre ca śārkare /
children.translated_text: In blue, in red, in salt, in conch-shell, in milk, and in sugar —

children.text: kaṣāyaiḥ phalapuṣpādyaiḥ kiraṇā yatha bhāskare // Lank_2.101 //
children.translated_text: with astringent fruits, flowers, and the rest — like the rays in the sun. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.101 ||

children.text: na cānyena ca nānanyena taraṃgā hyudadhermatāḥ /
children.translated_text: The waves of the ocean are considered neither different nor non-different [from it];

children.text: vijñānāni tathā sapta cittena saha saṃyutāḥ // Lank_2.102 //
children.translated_text: likewise the seven consciousnesses are conjoined with <s>citta</s> (mind). || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.102 ||
That transformation of the ocean is the variety of the waves;

children.text: ālayaṃ hi tathā citraṃ vijñānākhyaṃ pravartate // Lank_2.103 //
children.translated_text: likewise the <s>ālaya</s>, in its manifoldness, operates under the name 'consciousness.' || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.103 ||
<s>Citta</s> (mind), <s>manas</s> (mentation), and <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) are conceptualized for the purpose of [indicating] characteristics;

children.text: abhinnalakṣaṇā hyaṣṭau na lakṣyā na ca lakṣaṇam // Lank_2.104 //
children.translated_text: the eight are of undifferentiated characteristic — neither characterized nor characteristic. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.104 ||
Just as there is no distinction between the ocean and the waves,

children.text: vijñānānāṃ tathā cittaiḥ pariṇāmo na labhyate // Lank_2.105 //
children.translated_text: so the transformation of the consciousnesses in [relation to] <s>citta</s> is not found. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.105 ||

children.text: cittena cīyate karma manasā ca vicīyate /
children.translated_text: By <s>citta</s> (mind), <s>karma</s> (action) is accumulated; by <s>manas</s> (mentation), it is examined;

children.text: vijñānena vijānāti dṛśyaṃ kalpeti pañcabhiḥ // Lank_2.106 //
children.translated_text: by <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness), one cognizes; the visible is imagined by the five [sense-consciousnesses]. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.106 ||
Consciousness appears to people as being of the nature of blue, red, and so forth;
tell me, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, why is there a similarity between waves and <s>citta</s>? || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.107 ||
The nature of blue, red, and so forth is not found in the waves;

children.text: vṛttiśca varṇyate cittaṃ lakṣaṇārthaṃ hi bāliśān // Lank_2.108 //
children.translated_text: activity is predicated of <s>citta</s> for the purpose of [indicating] characteristics to the childish. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.108 ||

children.text: na tasya vidyate vṛttiḥ svacittaṃ grāhyavarjitam /
children.translated_text: There is no [such] activity in it; one's own <s>citta</s> is free from the grasped;

children.text: grāhye sati hi vai grāhastaraṃgaiḥ saha sādhyate // Lank_2.109 //
children.translated_text: when there is a grasped, there is indeed a grasper — [this] is demonstrated together with the waves. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.109 ||
Consciousness appears to people as the establishment of body, enjoyment, and abode;

children.text: tenāsya dṛśyate vṛttistaraṃgaiḥ saha sādṛśā // Lank_2.110 //
children.translated_text: thereby its activity is seen to be similar to the waves. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.110 ||
The ocean is perceived as dancing in the form of waves;

children.text: ālayasya tathā vṛttiḥ kasmādbuddhyā na gamyate // Lank_2.111 //
children.translated_text: why is the activity of the <s>ālaya</s> likewise not understood by the intellect? || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.111 ||
Because of the deficiency of intellect of the childish, the <s>ālaya</s> — like the ocean —
is brought near by the analogy of similarity to the activity of waves. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.112 ||
Just as the sun rises upon the equal, the inferior, and the superior <s>Jina</s>,

children.text: tathā tvaṃ lokapradyota tattvaṃ deśesi bāliśān // Lank_2.113 //
children.translated_text: so you, O illuminator of the world, teach the truth to the childish. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.113 ||
Having established a position regarding <s>dharmas</s>, why do you not speak the truth?

children.text: bhāṣase yadi vā tattvaṃ citte tattvaṃ na vidyate // Lank_2.114 //
children.translated_text: If indeed you speak the truth, the truth is not found in <s>citta</s>. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.114 ||

children.text: udadheryathā taraṃgā hi darpaṇe supine yathā /
children.translated_text: Just as waves of the ocean, as in a mirror, as in a dream,

children.text: dṛśyanti yugapatkāle tathā cittaṃ svagocare // Lank_2.115 //
children.translated_text: are seen simultaneously — so is <s>citta</s> in its own domain. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.115 ||
Due to the deficiency of [simultaneous perception of] objects, [consciousness] operates sequentially;

children.text: vijñānena vijānāti manasā manyate punaḥ // Lank_2.116 //
children.translated_text: by <s>vijñāna</s> one cognizes; by <s>manas</s> one deliberates. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.116 ||

children.text: pañcānāṃ khyāyate dṛśyaṃ kramo nāsti samāhite /
children.translated_text: The visible appears for the five [sense-consciousnesses]; there is no sequence for the concentrated [mind].
Just as some master painter or a painting apprentice

children.text: citrārthe nāmayedraṅgān deśayāmi tathā hyaham // Lank_2.117 //
children.translated_text: applies pigments to the subject of a painting, so indeed do I teach. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.117 ||

children.text: raṅge na vidyate citraṃ na bhūmau na ca bhājane /
children.translated_text: The painting is not found in the pigments, nor on the ground, nor in the vessel;
for the purpose of attracting beings, a painting is imagined with pigments —

children.text: deśanā vyabhicāraṃ ca tattvaṃ hyakṣaravarjitam // Lank_2.118 //
children.translated_text: the teaching is variable, but the truth is free from syllables. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.118 ||
Having established a position regarding <s>dharmas</s>, I teach the truth to <s>yogins</s>;
the truth is of the nature of inner self-realization, free from the imaginable and the unimaginable.

children.text: deśemi jinaputrāṇāṃ neyaṃ bālāna deśanā // Lank_2.119 //
children.translated_text: I teach the sons of the <s>Jina</s>; this teaching is not for the childish. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.119 ||

children.text: vicitrā hi yathā māyā dṛśyate na ca vidyate /
children.translated_text: Just as illusion, though manifold, is seen yet does not exist,
so too the teaching, though variegated, is taught without deviation;
for a teaching that belongs to one is no teaching for another. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.120 ||
Just as a physician gives medicine to each and every patient,

children.text: buddhā hi tadvatsattvānāṃ cittamātraṃ vadanti vai // Lank_2.121 //
children.translated_text: so too the Buddhas declare mind-only (<s>cittamātra</s>) to beings. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.121 ||
Beyond the domain of logicians and not that of <s>Śrāvakas</s> either —

children.text: yaṃ deśayanti vai nāthāḥ pratyātmagatigocaram // Lank_2.122 //
children.translated_text: [that is] what the Lords teach: the domain of inner self-realization. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.122 ||

body.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate bodhisattvena svacittadṛśyagrāhyagrāhakavikalpagocaraṃ parijñātukāmena saṃgaṇikāasaṃsargamiddhanivaraṇavigatena bhavitavyam / prathamamadhyamapaścādrātrajāgarikāyoganuyuktena bhavitavyam / kutīrthyaśāstrākhyāyikāśrāvakapratyekabuddhayānalakṣaṇavirahitena ca bhavitavyam / svacittadṛśyavikalpalakṣaṇagatiṃgatena ca bhavitavyaṃ bodhisattvena mahāsattvena //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who wishes to fully understand the domain of the conceptualization of the grasped and grasper [as] what is seen by one's own mind, should be free from the hindrance of association with crowds. He should be engaged in the <s>yoga</s> of wakefulness in the first, middle, and last watches of the night. He should be free from the characteristics of heretical treatises, legends, and the <s>Śrāvaka</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> vehicles. The <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> should be one who has entered the course of the characteristics of the conceptualization of what is seen by his own mind.

body.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate bodhisattvena mahāsattvena cittavijñānaprajñālakṣaṇavyavasthāyāṃ sthitvā upariṣṭādāryajñānalakṣaṇatrayayogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ / tatropariṣṭādāryajñānalakṣaṇatrayaṃ mahāmate katamat? yaduta nirābhāsalakṣaṇaṃ sarvabuddhasvapraṇidhānādhiṣṭhānalakṣaṇaṃ pratyātmāryajñānagatilakṣaṇaṃ
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, having established himself in the determination of the characteristics of mind, consciousness, and wisdom, should practice above the <s>yoga</s> of the three characteristics of noble knowledge (<s>āryajñāna</s>). What, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the triad of characteristics of noble knowledge above? Namely: the characteristic of appearance-free [realization], the characteristic of the sustaining power of the personal vows of all Buddhas, and the characteristic of the course of one's own inner noble knowledge

body.text: ca / yānyadhigamya yogī khañjagardabha iva cittaprajñājñānalakṣaṇaṃ hitvā jinasutāṣṭamīṃ prāpya bhūmiṃ taduttare lakṣaṇatraye yogamāpadyate //
body.translated_text: — having realized which, the <s>yogin</s>, like a lame donkey, abandoning the characteristics of mind, wisdom, and knowledge, having attained the eighth stage (<s>bhūmi</s>) as a son of the <s>Jina</s>, engages in the <s>yoga</s> of the three characteristics above that.

body.text: tatra nirābhāsalakṣaṇaṃ punarmahāmate sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhatīrthalakṣaṇaparicayātpravartate / adhiṣṭhānalakṣaṇaṃ punarmahāmate pūrvabuddhasvapraṇidhānādhiṣṭhānataḥ pravartate / pratyātmāryajñānagatilakṣaṇaṃ punarmahāmate sarvadharmalakṣaṇānabhiniveśato māyopamasamādhikāyapratilambhādbuddhabhūmigatigamanapracārāt pravartate / etanmahāmate āryāṇāṃ lakṣaṇatrayaṃ yenāryeṇa lakṣatrayeṇa samanvāgatā āryāḥ svapratyātmāryajñānagatigocaramadhigacchanti / tasmāttarhi mahāmate āryajñānalakṣaṇatrayayogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Therein, the characteristic of imagelessness (<s>nirābhāsa</s>), O <s>Mahāmati</s>, arises from familiarity with the characteristics of all <s>Śrāvakas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and heretics. The characteristic of empowerment (<s>adhiṣṭhāna</s>), O <s>Mahāmati</s>, arises from the empowerment of former <s>Buddhas</s>' own vows (<s>praṇidhāna</s>). The characteristic of the noble knowledge of one's own inner realization (<s>pratyātmāryajñānagati</s>), O <s>Mahāmati</s>, arises from non-attachment to the characteristics of all <s>dharmas</s>, from the attainment of the illusion-like <s>samādhi</s>-body, and from the progress of advancing to the <s>Buddha</s>-stages. This, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the threefold characteristic of the noble ones. Endowed with this noble threefold characteristic, the noble ones realize the domain of the noble knowledge of their own inner realization. Therefore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the practice of the threefold characteristic of noble knowledge should be undertaken.

body.text: atha khalu mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ punareva tasyā bodhisattvaparṣadaścittāśayavicāramājñāya āryajñānavastupravicayaṃ nāma dharmaparyāyaṃ sarvabuddhādhiṣṭhānādhiṣṭhito bhagavantaṃ paripṛcchati sma - deśayatu me bhagavānāryajñānavastupravicayaṃ nāma dharmaparyāyamaṣṭottarapadaśataprabhedāśrayam, yamāśritya tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ svasāmānyalakṣaṇapatitānāṃ parikalpitasvabhāvagatiprabhedaṃ deśayanti, yena parikalpitasvabhāvagatiprabhedena suprativibhāgaviddhena pudgaladharmanairātmyapracāraṃ prativiśodhya bhūmiṣu kṛtavidyāḥ sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhatīrthakaradhyānasamādhisamāpattisukhamatikramya tathāgatācintyaviṣayapracāragatipracāraṃ pañcadharmasvabhāvagativinivṛttaṃ tathāgataṃ dharmakāyaṃ prajñājñānasunibaddhadharmaṃ māyāviṣayābhinivṛttaṃ sarvabuddhakṣetratuṣitabhavanākaniṣṭhālayopagaṃ tathāgatakāyaṃ pratilabheran //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s>, again discerning the mental dispositions of that assembly of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, empowered by the empowerment of all <s>Buddhas</s>, questioned the Blessed One regarding the <s>dharmaparyāya</s> (discourse) called 'Investigation of the Objects of Noble Knowledge' (<s>Āryajñānavastupravicaya</s>): 'May the Blessed One teach me the <s>dharmaparyāya</s> called "Investigation of the Objects of Noble Knowledge," based on the analysis of the one hundred and eight terms, relying upon which the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly enlightened <s>Buddhas</s> teach <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas</s> — who fall under specific and general characteristics — the differentiation of the course of the imagined inherent nature (<s>parikalpitasvabhāva</s>), so that, pierced by that well-differentiated understanding of the course of the imagined inherent nature, having purified the practice of the selflessness of persons and dharmas (<s>pudgaladharmanairātmya</s>), accomplished in the stages (<s>bhūmis</s>), having transcended the happiness of the meditations, concentrations, and attainments of all <s>Śrāvakas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and heretical teachers, they may attain the <s>Tathāgata</s>-body — [which is] the inconceivable domain and course and progress of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, freed from the course of the five dharmas and the inherent natures, the <s>Dharmakāya</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, having its dharma well-bound by wisdom-knowledge (<s>prajñājñāna</s>), turned away from attachment to the domain of illusion (<s>māyā</s>), approaching the abodes of all <s>Buddha</s>-fields, <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven, and <s>Akaniṣṭha</s>.'

body.text: bhagavānāha - iha mahāmate eke tīrthyātīrthyadṛṣṭayo nāstitvābhiniviṣṭā vikalpabuddhihetukṣayasvabhāvābhāvānnāsti śaśasya viṣāṇaṃ vikalpayanti / yathā śaśaviṣāṇaṃ nāsti, evaṃ sarvadharmāḥ / anye punarmahāmate bhūtaguṇāṇudravyasaṃsthānasaṃniveśaviśeṣaṃ dṛṣṭvā nāstiśaśaśṛṅgābhiniveśābhiniviṣṭā asti gośṛṅgamiti kalpayanti / te mahāmate antadvayadṛṣṭipatitāścittamātrānavadhāritamatayaḥ / svacittadhātuvikalpena te puṣṇanti / dehabhogapratiṣṭhāgativikalpamātre mahāmate śaśaśṛṅgaṃ nāstyastivinivṛttaṃ na kalpayettathā mahāmate sarvabhāvānāṃ nāstyastivinivṛttaṃ na kalpayitavyam //
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: Here, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, certain heretics, attached to heretical views and to the notion of non-existence, because of the absence of inherent nature due to the destruction of the cause of discriminating intellect, conceptualize: 'The horn of a hare does not exist.' Just as a hare's horn does not exist, so all <s>dharmas</s> [do not exist, they say]. Others again, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, seeing the distinctive configuration of the qualities, atoms, and substance of the material elements, attached to the notion of non-existence like [the non-existence of] a hare's horn, conceptualize: 'A cow's horn exists.' They, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, have fallen into the dual view and have not ascertained that [all is] mind-only (<s>cittamātra</s>). Through the discrimination of the elements of their own minds, they are nourished. Regarding the mere discrimination of body, enjoyment, place, and destiny, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, one should not conceptualize a hare's horn as freed from existence and non-existence. Similarly, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the being freed from existence and non-existence of all entities should not be conceptualized.

body.text: ye punarmahāmate nāstyastivinivṛttā nāsti śaśaśṛṅgaṃ na kalpayanti, tairanyonyāpekṣahetutvānnāsti śaśaviṣāṇamiti na kalpayitavyam / āparamāṇupravicayādvastvanupalabdhabhāvānmahāmate āryajñānagocaravinivṛttamasti gośṛṅgamiti na kalpayitavyam //
body.translated_text: Those again, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, who are freed from existence and non-existence and do not conceptualize 'a hare's horn does not exist' — by them, since [things are] mutually dependent causes, it should not be conceptualized that 'a hare's horn does not exist.' Since, upon analysis down to atoms, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, substance is not apprehended — being freed from the domain of noble knowledge — it should not be conceptualized that 'a cow's horn exists.'

body.text: atha khalu mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantametadavocat - nanu bhagavan vikalpasyāpravṛttilakṣaṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā anumimīmahe vikalpāpravṛttyapekṣaṃ tasya nāstitvam / bhagavānāha - na hi mahāmate vikalpāpravṛttyapekṣaṃ tasya nāstitvam / tatkasya hetoḥ? vikalpasya tatpravṛttihetutvāt / tadviṣāṇāśrayapravṛtto hi mahāmate vikalpaḥ / yasmādviṣāṇāśrayapravṛtto mahāmate vikalpaḥ, tasmādāśrayahetutvādanyānanyavivarjitatvānna hi tadapekṣaṃ nāstitvaṃ śaśaviṣāṇasya /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'Is it not, Blessed One, that seeing the non-arising characteristic of discrimination, we infer its non-existence dependent on the non-arising of discrimination?' The Blessed One said: 'Not so, O <s>Mahāmati</s> — its non-existence is not dependent on the non-arising of discrimination. For what reason? Because discrimination has that [horn] as the cause of its arising. For discrimination, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, arises depending on the support of that horn. Since discrimination, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, arises depending on the support of the horn, therefore — because the support is the cause, and because [the horn] is free from both sameness and difference — the non-existence of the hare's horn is not dependent on that [discrimination].'

body.text: yadi punarmahāmate vikalpo 'nyaḥ syācchaśaviṣāṇādaviṣāṇahetukaḥ syāt / athānanyaḥ syāt, taddhetukatvādāparamāṇupravicayānupalabdherviṣāṇādananyatvāttadabhāvaḥ syāt / tadubhayabhāvābhāvātkasya kimapekṣya nāstitvaṃ bhavati? atha na bhavati mahāmate apekṣya nāstitvaṃ śaśaviṣāṇasya astitvamapekṣya nāstitvaṃ śaśaviṣāṇaṃ na kalpayitavyaṃ viṣamahetutvānmahāmate nāstyastitvam siddhirna bhavati nāstyastitvavādinām / anye punarmahāmate tīrthakaradṛṣṭayo rūpakāraṇasaṃsthānābhiniveśābhiniviṣṭā ākāśabhāvāparicchedakuśalā rūpamākāśabhāvavigataṃ paricchedaṃ dṛṣṭvā vikalpayanti / ākāśameva ca mahāmate rūpam / rūpabhūtānupraveśānmahāmate rūpamevākāśam / ādheyādhāravyayasthānabhāvena mahāmate rūpākāśakāraṇayoḥ pravibhāgaḥ pratyetavyaḥ / bhūtāni mahāmate pravartamānāni parasparasvalakṣaṇabhedabhinnāni ākāśe cāpratiṣṭhitāni / na ca teṣvākāśaṃ nāsti / evameva śaśasya viṣāṇaṃ mahāmate goviṣāṇamapekṣya bhavati / goviṣāṇaṃ punarmahāmate aṇuśo vibhajyamānaṃ punarapyaṇavo vibhajyamānā aṇutvalakṣaṇe nāvatiṣṭhante / tasya kimapekṣya nāstitvaṃ bhavati? athānyadapekṣya vastu, tadapyevaṃdharmi //
body.translated_text: 'If again, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, discrimination were different from the hare's horn, it would not have the horn as its cause. But if it were non-different, then — because it would be caused by that, and because upon atomic analysis the horn is not apprehended, and because of non-difference from the horn — there would be its non-existence. Since both states of difference and non-difference are absent, with respect to what does one speak of the non-existence [of something]? Thus, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, if the non-existence of the hare's horn is not established by dependence — one should not conceptualize the non-existence of the hare's horn dependent on existence. Because of an unequal cause, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, there is no establishment of non-existence or existence for those who speak of non-existence and existence. Others again, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, holding heretical views, attached to the notion of the configuration and form of material causation, unskilled in the non-delimitation of the nature of space, seeing form as delimited and separate from the nature of space, conceptualize. Space itself, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is form. Because of the penetration of form into the elements, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, form itself is space. The distinction between form and space as cause should be understood, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, by way of the container, the contained, and the place of change. The elements, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, while in activity, distinguished by their mutual own-characteristics, are also not established in space; yet space is not absent from them. Just so, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the horn of a hare exists in dependence on the horn of a cow. But the cow's horn, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, when analyzed atomically — and the atoms [themselves] when further analyzed — do not remain in the characteristic of atomicity. With respect to what does its non-existence hold? If with respect to some other entity — that too has the same nature.'

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān punarapi mahāmatiṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvametadavocat - śaśagośṛṅgākāśarūpapadṛṣṭivikalpavigatena mahāmate bhavitavyam, tadanyaiśca bodhisattvaiḥ / svacittadṛśyavikalpānugamamanasā ca mahāmate bhavitavyam / sarvajinasutakṣetramaṇḍale ca tvayā svacittadṛśyayogopadeśaḥ karaṇīyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One again spoke thus to the <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s>: 'You must be free, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, from discriminating views about hare's horn, cow's horn, space, form, and term — and so must other <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. And you must be, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, of a mind that follows the discrimination of the appearances of your own mind. And in all the <s>maṇḍala</s>-assemblies of the sons of the <s>Jina</s>-fields, you should impart the instruction on the yoga of the appearances of one's own mind.'

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, at that time, uttered these verses:

children.text: dṛśyaṃ na vidyate cittaṃ cittaṃ dṛśyātpravartate /
children.translated_text: The perceived does not exist [apart from] mind; mind arises from the perceived.
The abode of divine enjoyments is manifested to humans. [Laṅk 2.123]
Mind (<s>citta</s>), <s>manas</s>, and consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>), inherent nature, and the five dharmas;

children.text: nairātmyaṃ dvitayaṃ śuddhaṃ prabhāṣante vināyakāḥ // Lank_2.124 //
children.translated_text: the twofold selflessness (<s>nairātmya</s>), pure — the guides (<s>vināyaka</s>) proclaim. [Laṅk 2.124]
The connection of long, short, etc. arises from mutual [dependence];
there is nothing that establishes existence; what exists does not establish non-existence. [Laṅk 2.125]

children.text: aṇuśo bhajyamānaṃ hi naiva rūpaṃ vikalpayet /
children.translated_text: When analyzed atomically, one should not at all conceptualize form;

children.text: cittamātraṃ vyavasthānaṃ kudṛṣṭyā na prasīdati // Lank_2.126 //
children.translated_text: the establishment of mind-only (<s>cittamātra</s>) is not approved by those of wrong views. [Laṅk 2.126]
It is beyond the domain of logicians, and indeed not of <s>Śrāvakas</s> [either] —

children.text: yaṃ deśayanti vai nāthāḥ pratyātmagatigocaram // Lank_2.127 //
children.translated_text: what the Protectors teach [is] the domain of one's own inner realization. [Laṅk 2.127]

body.text: atha khalu mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ punarapi svacittadṛśyadhārāviśuddhyarthaṃ bhagavantamadhyeṣate sma - kathaṃ bhagavan svacittadṛśyadhārā viśudhyati yugapatkramavṛttyā vā? bhagavānāha - kramavṛttyā mahāmate svacittadṛśyadhārā viśudhyati na yugapat / tadyathā mahāmate āmraphalāni kramaśaḥ pacyante na yugapat, evameva mahāmate svacittadṛśyadhārā sattvānāṃ kramaśo viśudhyati
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s> again entreated the Blessed One for the purpose of purifying the stream of the appearances of one's own mind: 'How, Blessed One, is the stream of the appearances of one's own mind purified — simultaneously or by gradual progression?' The Blessed One said: 'By gradual progression, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the stream of the appearances of one's own mind purified, not simultaneously. Just as, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, mango fruits ripen gradually, not simultaneously, even so, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the stream of the appearances of one's own mind of beings is purified gradually,

body.text: na yugapat / tadyathā mahāmate kumbhakāraḥ kramaśo bhāṇḍāni kurute na yugapat, evameva mahāmate tathāgataḥ sattvānāṃ svacittadṛśyadhārāṃ kramaśo viśodhayati na yugapat / tadyathā mahāmate pṛthivyāṃ tṛṇagulmauṣadhivanaspatayaḥ kramavṛttyā virohanti na yugapat, evameva mahāmate sattvānāṃ tathāgataḥ kramaśaḥ svacittadṛśyadhārāṃ viśodhayati na yugapat / tadyathā mahāmate hāsyalāsyagītavāditravīṇālekhyayogyāḥ kramaśaḥ pravartante na yugapat, evemeva mahāmate tathāgataḥ sarvasattvānāṃ kramaśaḥ svacittadṛśyadhārāṃ viśodhayati na yugapat / tadyathā mahāmate darpaṇāntargatāḥ sarvarūpāvabhāsāḥ saṃdṛśyante nirvikalpā yugapat, evameva mahāmate svacittadṛśyadhārāṃ yugapattathāgataḥ sarvasattvānāṃ viśodhayati nirvikalpāṃ nirābhāsagocarām / tadyathā mahāmate somādityamaṇḍalaṃ yugapatsarvarūpāvabhāsān kiraṇaiḥ prakāśayati, evameva mahāmate tathāgataḥ svacittadṛśyadauṣṭhulyavāsanāvigatānāṃ sattvānāṃ yugapadacintyajñānajinagocaraviṣayaṃ saṃdarśayati / tadyathā mahāmate ālayavijñānaṃ svacittadṛśyadehapratiṣṭhābhogaviṣayaṃ yugapadvibhāvayati, evameva mahāmate niṣyandabuddho yugapatsattvagocaraṃ paripācya ākaniṣṭhabhavanavimānālayayogaṃ yogināmarpayati / tadyathā mahāmate dharmatābuddho yugapanniṣyandanirmāṇakiraṇairvirājate, evameva mahāmate pratyātmāryagatidharmalakṣaṇaṃ bhāvābhāvakudṛṣṭivinivartanatayā yugapadvirājate //
body.translated_text: not simultaneously. Just as, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, a potter makes vessels gradually, not simultaneously, even so, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> purifies the stream of the appearances of one's own mind of beings gradually, not simultaneously. Just as, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, grasses, shrubs, herbs, and forest trees grow by gradual progression on the earth, not simultaneously, even so, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> purifies the stream of the appearances of one's own mind of beings gradually, not simultaneously. Just as, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, proficiency in dance, music, song, instrumental music, lute-playing, and painting develops gradually, not simultaneously, even so, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> purifies the stream of the appearances of one's own mind of all beings gradually, not simultaneously. Just as, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, all reflections of forms within a mirror are seen non-discriminatively and simultaneously, even so, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> purifies simultaneously the stream of the appearances of one's own mind of all beings — non-discriminative, with imagelessness as its domain. Just as, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the orb of the moon and sun simultaneously illuminates all reflections of forms with its rays, even so, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> simultaneously reveals the inconceivable wisdom-domain of the <s>Jina</s> to beings who are free from the depravity-impressions of the appearances of one's own mind. Just as, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> (store-consciousness) simultaneously manifests the domain of body, establishment, enjoyment, and perception as the appearances of one's own mind, even so, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the <s>Niṣyanda-Buddha</s> (outflow-Buddha), having simultaneously ripened the domain of beings, bestows upon yogins the yoga of the palace-abode of the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> heaven. Just as, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the <s>Dharmatā-Buddha</s> (nature-Buddha) simultaneously shines forth with the rays of outflow and emanation, even so, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the characteristic of the <s>dharma</s> of one's own inner noble realization shines forth simultaneously through the turning away from wrong views of existence and non-existence.

body.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate dharmatāniṣyandabuddhaḥ svasāmānyalakṣaṇapatitātsarvadharmātsvacittadṛśyavāsanāhetulakṣaṇopanibaddhātparikalpitasvabhāvābhiniveśahetukānatadātmakavividhamāyāraṅgapuruṣavaicitryābhiniveśānupalabdhito mahāmate deśayati / punaraparaṃ mahāmate parikalpitasvabhāvavṛttilakṣaṇaṃ paratantrasvabhāvābhiniveśataḥ pravartate / tadyathā tṛṇakāṣṭhagulmalatāśrayānmāyāvidyāpuruṣasaṃyogātsarvasattvarūpadhāriṇaṃ māyāpuruṣavigrahamabhiniṣpannaikasattvaśarīraṃ vividhakalpavikalpitaṃ khyāyate, tathā khyāyannapi mahāmate tadātmako na bhavati, evameva mahāmate paratantrasvabhāve parikalpitasvabhāve vividhavikalpacittavicitralakṣaṇaṃ khyāyate / vastuparikalpalakṣaṇābhiniveśavāsanātparikalpayan mahāmate parikalpitasvabhāvalakṣaṇaṃ bhavati / eṣā mahāmate niṣyandabuddhadeśanā / dharmatābuddhaḥ punarmahāmate cittasvabhāvalakṣaṇavisaṃyuktāṃ pratyātmāryagatigocaravyavasthāṃ karoti / nirmitanirmāṇabuddhaḥ punarmahāmate dānaśīladhyānasamādhicitraprajñājñānaskandhadhātvāyatanavimokṣavijñānagatilakṣaṇaprabhedapracāraṃ vyavasthāpayati / tīrthyadṛṣṭyā ca rūpyasamatikramaṇalakṣaṇaṃ deśayati / dharmatābuddhaḥ punarmahāmate nirālambaḥ / ālambavigataṃ sarvakriyendriyapramāṇalakṣaṇavinivṛttamaviṣayaṃ bālaśrāvakapratyekabuddhatīrthakarātmakalakṣaṇābhiniveśābhiniviṣṭānām / tasmāttarhi mahāmate pratyātmāryagativiśeṣalakṣaṇe yogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ / svacittalakṣaṇadṛśyavinivṛttidṛṣṭinā ca te bhavitavyam //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the <s>Dharmatā-Niṣyanda-Buddha</s> teaches from [the standpoint of] all <s>dharmas</s> falling under specific and general characteristics, bound to the characteristic of the cause of the impressions of the appearances of one's own mind, through the non-apprehension of attachment to the variety of illusory stage-figures caused by attachment to the imagined inherent nature (<s>parikalpitasvabhāva</s>), which is not [truly] of that nature. Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the characteristic of the activity of the imagined inherent nature arises from attachment to the dependent inherent nature (<s>paratantrasvabhāva</s>). Just as, from the conjunction of a magician (<s>māyāvidyāpuruṣa</s>) with supports such as grass, wood, shrubs, and creepers, an illusory figure bearing the forms of all beings appears — a body that is a single accomplished being, imagined by various conceptualizations — yet even while appearing, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, it is not of that nature; even so, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, in the dependent inherent nature, the imagined inherent nature appears with characteristics diversified by the various discriminations of the mind. Through the impressions of attachment to the characteristic of the imagination of things, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the one who imagines produces the characteristic of the imagined inherent nature. This, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the teaching of the <s>Niṣyanda-Buddha</s>. The <s>Dharmatā-Buddha</s>, moreover, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, establishes the domain of one's own inner noble realization, dissociated from the characteristics of the inherent nature of mind. The emanated <s>Nirmāṇa-Buddha</s> (transformation-Buddha), moreover, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, establishes the differentiated course of the characteristics of giving (<s>dāna</s>), morality (<s>śīla</s>), meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>), concentration (<s>samādhi</s>), varied wisdom-knowledge (<s>prajñājñāna</s>), aggregates (<s>skandha</s>), elements (<s>dhātu</s>), sense-bases (<s>āyatana</s>), liberations (<s>vimokṣa</s>), and the course of consciousness. And he teaches the characteristic of transcending the equalizing of form according to heretical views. The <s>Dharmatā-Buddha</s>, moreover, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is without support (<s>nirālamba</s>) — free from all activity, senses, means of knowledge, and characteristics of support — beyond the domain of those attached to the characteristic of self in foolish persons, <s>Śrāvakas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and heretical teachers. Therefore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the practice of the distinctive characteristic of one's own inner noble realization should be undertaken. And you must have the view that turns away from the perception of the characteristics of one's own mind.

body.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate dvividhaṃ śrāvakayānanayaprabhedalakṣaṇaṃ yaduta pratyātmāryādhigamaviśeṣalakṣaṇaṃ ca bhāvavikalpasvabhāvābhiniveśalakṣaṇaṃ ca / tatra mahāmate pratyātmāryādhigamaviśeṣalakṣaṇaṃ śrāvakāṇāṃ katamat? yaduta śūnyatānātmaduḥkhānityaviṣayasatyavairāgyopaśamātskandhadhātvāyatanasvasāmānyalakṣaṇabāhyārthavināśalakṣaṇādyathābhūtaparijñānāccittaṃ
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the distinguishing characteristic of the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> (hearers' vehicle) method is twofold: namely, the characteristic of the distinction of inner noble self-realization, and the characteristic of attachment to the inherent nature of conceptual discrimination of entities. Therein, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, what is the characteristic of the distinction of inner noble self-realization for the <s>śrāvakas</s>? Namely, from the pacification and dispassion regarding the domains of emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>), non-self (<s>anātma</s>), suffering (<s>duḥkha</s>), impermanence (<s>anitya</s>), and truth (<s>satya</s>), from the true comprehension of the specific and general characteristics of the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), and <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases), and from the characteristic of the destruction of external objects, the mind

body.text: samādhīyate / svacittaṃ samādhāya dhyānavimokṣasamādhimārgaphalasamāpattivimuktivāsanācintyapariṇaticyutivigataṃ pratyātmāryagatilakṣaṇasukhavihāraṃ mahāmate adhigacchanti śrāvakāḥ / etanmahāmate śrāvakāṇāṃ pratyātmāryagatilakṣaṇam / etaddhi mahāmate śrāvakāṇāṃ pratyātmāryādhigamavihārasukhamadhigamya bodhisattvena mahāsattvena nirodhasukhaṃ samāpattisukhaṃ ca sattvakriyāpekṣayā pūrvasvapraṇidhānābhinirhṛtatayā ca na sākṣātkaraṇīyam / etanmahāmate śrāvakāṇāṃ pratyātmāryagatilakṣaṇasukhaṃ yatra bodhisattvena mahāsattvena pratyātmāryagatilakṣaṇasukhe na śikṣitavyam / bhāvavikalpasvabhāvābhiniveśaḥ punarmahāmate śrāvakāṇāṃ katamaḥ? yaduta nīlapītoṣṇadravacalakaṭhināni mahābhūtānyakriyāpravṛttāni svasāmānyalakṣaṇayuktyāgamapramāṇasuvinibaddhāni dṛṣṭvā tatsvabhāvābhiniveśavikalpaḥ pravartate / etanmahāmate bodhisattvenādhigamya vyāvartayitavyam / dharmanairātmyalakṣaṇānupraveśatayā pudgalanairātmyalakṣaṇadṛṣṭiṃ nivārya bhūmikramānusaṃghau pratiṣṭhāpayitavyam / etanmahāmate śrāvakāṇāṃ bhāvavikalpasvabhāvābhiniveśalakṣaṇaṃ yaduktam, idaṃ tatpratyuktam //
body.translated_text: is concentrated. Having concentrated their own minds, free from the inconceivable transformation and falling away of the impressions of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), liberation, <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), path, fruit, and attainment, the <s>śrāvakas</s>, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, attain the blissful abode characterized by the inner noble course. This, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the characteristic of the inner noble course of the <s>śrāvakas</s>. Indeed, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, having attained this blissful abode of inner noble self-realization of the <s>śrāvakas</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> should not directly realize the bliss of cessation or the bliss of attainment, out of concern for the welfare of beings and because of the force of their own previous vows. This, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the bliss of the inner noble course characteristic of the <s>śrāvakas</s>, in which a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> should not train. What, furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the <s>śrāvakas</s>' attachment to the inherent nature of conceptual discrimination of entities? Namely, having observed the great elements — blue, yellow, hot, fluid, moving, hard — as operating without agency, well-connected with specific and general characteristics through logic and scripture as authoritative means, the conceptual discrimination of attachment to their inherent nature arises. This, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, having been understood by the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, should be turned away from. By entering into the characteristic of selflessness of phenomena (<s>dharmanairātmya</s>), having removed the view of the characteristic of selflessness of persons (<s>pudgalanairātmya</s>), one should be established in the progressive traversal of the stages. This, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the characteristic of the <s>śrāvakas</s>' attachment to the inherent nature of conceptual discrimination of entities that was asked about; this has been answered.

body.text: atha khalu mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantametadavocat - nityamacintyaṃ ca bhagavatā pratyātmāryagatigocaraṃ paramārthagocaraṃ ca prabhāṣitam / nanu bhagavaṃstīrthakarā api nityācintyavādinaḥ kāraṇānām? bhagavānāha - na mahāmate tīrthakarāṇāṃ kāraṇasya nityācintyatāṃ prāpnoti / tatkasya hetoḥ? tīrthakarāṇāṃ mahāmate nityācintyaṃ na hetusvalakṣaṇayuktam / yasya mahāmate nityācintyaṃ na hetusvalakṣaṇayuktam, tatkathaṃ kenābhivyajyate nityamacintyamiti? nityācintyavādaḥ punarmahāmate yadi hetusvalakṣaṇayuktaḥ syāt, nityaṃ kāraṇādhīnahetulakṣaṇatvānnityamacintyaṃ na bhavati / mama tu mahāmate paramārthanityācintyaṃ paramārthalakṣaṇahetuyuktaṃ bhāvābhāvavigataṃ pratyātmāryādhigamalakṣaṇatvāllakṣaṇavatparamārthajñānahetutvācca hetumadbhāvābhāvavigatatvādakṛtakākāśanirvāṇanirodhadṛṣṭāntasādharmyānnityam / ata etanmahāmate tīrthakaranityācintyavādatulyaṃ na bhavati / nityācintyataiveyaṃ mahāmate tathāgatānāṃ pratyātmāryajñānādhigamatathatā / tasmāttarhi mahāmate bodhisattvena mahāsattvena nityācintyapratyātmāryajñānādhigamāya yogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'The <s>Bhagavān</s> has spoken of the eternal and the inconceivable as the domain of inner noble self-realization and the domain of the supreme truth. Is it not so, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, that the non-Buddhist teachers (<s>tīrthakara</s>) also speak of causes as eternal and inconceivable?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: No, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the eternality and inconceivability of causes as held by the non-Buddhist teachers does not hold. For what reason? The eternal and inconceivable of the non-Buddhist teachers, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is not connected with the own-characteristic of a cause. That whose eternality and inconceivability, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is not connected with the own-characteristic of a cause — how and by whom is it manifested as eternal and inconceivable? Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, if the doctrine of the eternal-inconceivable were connected with the own-characteristic of a cause, [then] because the eternal would have the characteristic of a cause dependent on conditions, the eternal-inconceivable would not be [truly] eternal. My eternal-inconceivable, however, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the eternal-inconceivable of the supreme truth, connected with the cause that is the characteristic of the supreme truth, free from existent and non-existent, because it has the characteristic of inner noble self-realization, because it has the cause of ultimate knowledge endowed with characteristics, because it is free from the states of existent and non-existent [while] being possessed of cause, and because it is analogous to the uncreated, space, <s>nirvāṇa</s>, and cessation — [therefore] it is eternal. Hence, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, this is not equal to the doctrine of the eternal-inconceivable of the non-Buddhist teachers. This eternal-inconceivability, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>' inner noble knowledge-realization. Therefore then, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> should practice <s>yoga</s> for the attainment of the eternal-inconceivable inner noble knowledge-realization.

body.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate nityācintyatā tīrthakarāṇāmanityabhāvavilakṣaṇahetutvāt / na svakṛtahetulakṣaṇaprabhāvitatvānnityam / yadi punarmahāmate tīrthakarāṇāṃ nityācintyatā kṛtakabhāvābhāvādanityatāṃ dṛṣṭvā anumānabuddhyā nityaṃ samāpyate, tenaiva hetunā mamāpi mahāmate kṛtakabhāvābhāvādanityatāṃ dṛṣṭvā nityamahetūpadeśāt //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the eternality-inconceivability of the non-Buddhist teachers, because of having causes characterized by impermanent and different natures, is not eternal, since it is not made manifest by self-made causal characteristics. If, furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the eternality-inconceivability of the non-Buddhist teachers, having observed the impermanence arising from the existence and non-existence of created things, arrives at eternality through inferential reasoning, then by that same reason, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, for me too, having observed the impermanence arising from the existence and non-existence of created things, eternality would be [established] without a causal teaching.

body.text: yadi punarmahāmate hetulakṣaṇasaṃyuktaṃ nityācintyatā, tīrthakarāṇāṃ hetubhāvasvalakṣaṇabhāvābhāvācchaśaviṣāṇatulyā mahāmate nityācintyatā, vāgvikalpamātrā ca mahāmate tīrthakarāṇāṃ prasajyate / tatkasya hetoḥ? yaduta vāgvikalpamātraṃ hi mahāmate śaśaviṣāṇaṃ svahetulakṣaṇābhāvāt / mama tu mahāmate nityācintyatā pratyātmāryādhigamalakṣaṇahetutvātkṛtakabhāvābhāvavarjitatvānnityam,
body.translated_text: If, furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the eternality-inconceivability is connected with causal characteristics, then, because the causal state of the non-Buddhist teachers has the own-characteristic of existence and non-existence, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the eternality-inconceivability [of the non-Buddhist teachers] is comparable to a hare's horn, and it follows, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, that it is merely verbal and conceptual for the non-Buddhist teachers. For what reason? Because, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, a hare's horn is merely verbal and conceptual, due to the absence of its own causal characteristic. But my eternality-inconceivability, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, because it has as its cause the characteristic of inner noble self-realization, and because it is free from the [states of] existence and non-existence of created things, is eternal;

body.text: na bāhyabhāvābhāvanityānityānupramāṇānnityam / yasya punarmahāmate bāhyābhāvānnityānumānānnityācintyatvānnityam, tasyā nityācintyatāyāḥ svahetulakṣaṇaṃ na jānīte / pratyātmādhigamāryajñānagocaralakṣaṇaṃ bahirdhā te mahāmate asaṃkathyāḥ //
body.translated_text: not eternal [merely] from the inference of the permanence or impermanence of external existence and non-existence. He, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, whose eternality-inconceivability [derives] from the inference of eternality from external non-existence — of that eternality-inconceivability, the own causal characteristic is not known. Those who have the domain of the inner noble self-realization knowledge-characteristic, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, are beyond discussion with externalists.

body.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate saṃsāravikalpaduḥkhabhayabhītā nirvāṇamanveṣante / saṃsāranirvāṇayoraviśeṣajñāḥ sarvabhāvavikalpābhāvādindriyāṇāmanāgataviṣayoparamācca mahāmate nirvāṇaṃ vikalpayanti na pratyātmagativijñānālayaṃ parāvṛttipūrvakaṃ mahāmate / ataste mahāmate mohapuruṣā yānatrayavādino bhavanti, na cittamātragatinirābhāasavādinaḥ / ataste mahāmate atītānāgatapratyutpannānāṃ tathāgatānāṃ svacittadṛśyagocarānabhijñā bāhyacittadṛśyagocarābhiniviṣṭāḥ / te saṃsāragaticakre punarmahāmate caṃkramyante //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, those who are frightened by the fear of the suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence) through conceptual discrimination seek <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Not knowing the non-difference between <s>saṃsāra</s> and <s>nirvāṇa</s>, and due to the absence of conceptual discrimination of all entities and the cessation of the future domain of the sense-faculties, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, they conceptually discriminate <s>nirvāṇa</s> — not [through] the turning-back (<s>parāvṛtti</s>) of the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> (store-consciousness), which is the inner course of consciousness, O <s>Mahāmati</s>. Therefore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, those deluded persons become proponents of the three vehicles, not proponents of the appearance-free course of mind-only (<s>cittamātra</s>). Therefore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, not knowing the domain of appearances of their own mind with respect to the <s>Tathāgatas</s> of the past, future, and present, [being] attached to the domain of external mental appearances — they wander again, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, in the wheel of <s>saṃsāric</s> existence.

body.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate anutpannān sarvadharmānatītānāgatapratyutpannāstathāgatā bhāṣante / tatkasya hetoḥ? yaduta svacittadṛśyabhāvābhāvātsadasatorutpattivirahitatvānmahāmate anutpannāḥ sarvabhāvāḥ / śaśahayakharoṣṭraviṣāṇatulyā mahāmate sarvadharmāḥ / bālapṛthagjanābhūtaparikalpitasvabhāvavikalpitatvānmahāmate anutpannāḥ sarvabhāvāḥ / pratyātmāryajñānagatigocaro hi mahāmate sarvabhāvasvabhāvalakṣaṇotpādaḥ, na bālapṛthagjanavikalpadvayagocarasvabhāvaḥ / dehabhogapratiṣṭhāgatisvabhāvalakṣaṇaṃ mahāmate ālayavijñānaṃ grāhyagrāhakalakṣaṇena pravartamānaṃ bālā utpādasthitibhaṅgadṛṣṭidvayapatitāśayā utpādaṃ sarvabhāvānāṃ sadasatorvikalpayanti / atra te mahāmate yogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the <s>Tathāgatas</s> of the past, future, and present declare all phenomena to be unborn. For what reason? Because, since the existence and non-existence of appearances of one's own mind [are recognized], and since arising from both the existent and the non-existent is absent, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, all entities are unborn. All phenomena, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, are comparable to the horn of a hare, horse, or camel. Because they are conceptually discriminated through the inherent nature fabricated by foolish ordinary beings, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, all entities are unborn. The arising of the inherent nature and characteristics of all entities, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is indeed the domain of inner noble knowledge-course, not the inherent nature of the dual domain of conceptual discrimination by foolish ordinary beings. The <s>ālayavijñāna</s> (store-consciousness), O <s>Mahāmati</s>, which has the characteristic of the inherent nature of the establishment of body, enjoyment, and destiny, operating through the characteristic of grasper and grasped — the childish, having fallen into the disposition of the dual view of arising, abiding, and cessation, conceptually discriminate the arising of all entities from the existent and non-existent. Here, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, <s>yoga</s> should be practiced.

body.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate pañcābhisamayagotrāṇi / katamāni pañca? yaduta śrāvakayānābhisamayagotraṃ pratyekabuddhayānābhisamayagotraṃ tathāgatayānābhisamayagotram aniyataikataragotram agotraṃ ca pañcamam / kathaṃ punarmahāmate śrāvakayānābhisamayagotraṃ pratyetavyam? yaḥ skandhadhātvāyatanasvasāmānyalakṣaṇaparijñānādhigame deśyamāne romāñcitatanurbhavati / lakṣaṇaparicayajñāne cāsya buddhiḥ praskandati, na pratītyasamutpādāvinirbhāgalakṣaṇaparicaye / idaṃ mahāmate śrāvakayānābhisamayagotram / yaḥ śrāvakayānābhisamayaṃ dṛṣṭvā ṣaṭpañcamyāṃ bhūmau paryutthānakleśaprahīṇo vāsanakleśāprahīṇo 'cintyācyutigataḥ samyaksiṃhanādaṃ nadati - kṣīṇā me jātiḥ, uṣitaṃ brahmacaryam, ityevamādi nigadya pudgalanairātmyaparicayādyāvannirvāṇabuddhirbhavati //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, there are five lineage-types (<s>gotra</s>) of awakening-realization. What five? Namely, the lineage of <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> (hearers' vehicle) awakening-realization, the lineage of <s>Pratyekabuddhayāna</s> (solitary-awakeners' vehicle) awakening-realization, the lineage of <s>Tathāgatayāna</s> awakening-realization, the indeterminate (<s>aniyata</s>) single-vehicle lineage, and the fifth [which is] non-lineage (<s>agotra</s>). How then, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the lineage of <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> awakening-realization to be known? When instruction is given regarding the comprehension of the specific and general characteristics of the <s>skandhas</s>, <s>dhātus</s>, and <s>āyatanas</s>, one whose body-hairs stand on end — and whose intellect rushes toward the knowledge of familiarity with characteristics, but not toward familiarity with the inseparable characteristic of dependent co-arising (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>) — this, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> awakening-realization lineage. One who, having seen the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> awakening-realization, at the fifth or sixth stage has abandoned the manifest afflictions (<s>paryutthānakleśa</s>) but not the latent afflictions (<s>vāsanakleśa</s>), having entered the inconceivable falling-away, correctly roars the lion's roar: 'My births are exhausted, the holy life has been lived' — and having proclaimed thus and so forth, through familiarity with the selflessness of persons, [remains] in the understanding of <s>nirvāṇa</s>.

body.text: anye punarmahāmate ātmasattvajīvapoṣapuruṣapudgalasattvāvabodhānnirvāṇamanveṣante / anye punarmahāmate kāraṇādhīnān sarvadharmān dṛṣṭvā nirvāṇagatibuddhayo bhavanti / dharmanairātmyadarśanābhāvānnāsti mokṣo mahāmate / eṣā mahāmate śrāvakayānābhisamayagotrakasyāniryāṇaniryāṇabuddhiḥ / atra te mahāmate kudṛṣṭivyāvṛttyarthaṃ yogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Others, moreover, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, seek <s>nirvāṇa</s> through the understanding of self, being, soul (<s>jīva</s>), nourisher (<s>poṣa</s>), person (<s>puruṣa</s>), and individual (<s>pudgala</s>). Yet others, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, seeing all phenomena as dependent on causes, arrive at the understanding of the <s>nirvāṇa</s>-course.
