Due to the absence of the vision of the selflessness of phenomena (<s>dharmanairātmya</s>), there is no liberation, O <s>Mahāmati</s>. This, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the understanding of the exit and non-exit of one of the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> awakening-realization lineage. Here, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, <s>yoga</s> should be practiced for the purpose of turning away from wrong views.

body.text: tatra mahāmate pratyekabuddhayānābhisamayagotrakaḥ, yaḥ pratyekābhisamaye deśyamāne aśruhṛṣṭaromāñcitatanurbhavati / asaṃsargapratyayādbhāvābhiniveśabahuvividhasvakāyavaicitryarddhivyastayamakaprātihāryadarśane nirdiśyamāne 'nunīyate, sa pratyekabuddhayānābhisamayagotraka iti viditvā pratyekabuddhayānābhisamayānurūpā kathā karaṇīyā / etanmahāmate pratyekabuddhayānābhisamayagotrakasya lakṣaṇam //
body.translated_text: Therein, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, one of the <s>Pratyekabuddhayāna</s> awakening-realization lineage is one who, when instruction on solitary awakening-realization is given, becomes tearful, with body-hairs standing on end. When shown the wondrous display of the variety of his own body, the miraculous feat of the pairs, and the <s>prātihārya</s> (miracle), [arising] from the condition of non-association — he is won over. He should be known as one of the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> awakening-realization lineage, and teaching appropriate to the <s>Pratyekabuddhayāna</s> awakening-realization should be given. This, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the characteristic of one of the <s>Pratyekabuddhayāna</s> awakening-realization lineage.

body.text: tatra mahāmate tathāgatayānābhisamayagotraṃ trividham - yaduta svabhāvaniḥsvabhāvadharmābhisamayagotram, adhigamasvapratyātmāryābhisamayagotram, bāhyabuddhakṣetraudāryābhisamayagotraṃ ca / yadā punarmahāmate trayāṇāmapyeṣāmanyatame deśyamāne svacittadṛśyadehālabhogapratiṣṭhācintyaviṣaye deśyamāne notrasati na saṃtrasati na saṃtrāsamāpadyate, veditavyamayaṃ tathāgatayānābhisamayagotraka iti / etanmahāmate tathāgatayānābhisamayagotrakasya lakṣaṇam //
body.translated_text: Therein, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the <s>Tathāgatayāna</s> awakening-realization lineage is threefold — namely, the lineage of awakening-realization regarding the inherent nature and non-inherent-nature of phenomena, the lineage of awakening-realization regarding the inner noble self-realization, and the lineage of awakening-realization regarding the magnificence of external <s>Buddha</s>-fields. When, moreover, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, instruction is given on any one of these three — regarding the inconceivable domain of the body, non-body, enjoyment, and establishment as appearances of one's own mind — one who is not terrified, does not become frightened, does not fall into fright, should be known as one of the <s>Tathāgatayāna</s> awakening-realization lineage. This, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the characteristic of one of the <s>Tathāgatayāna</s> awakening-realization lineage.

body.text: aniyatagotrakaḥ punarmahāmate triṣvapyeteṣu deśyamāneṣu yatrānunīyate tatrānuyojyaḥ syāt / parikarmabhūmiriyaṃ mahāmate gotravyavasthā / nirābhāsabhūmyavakramaṇatayā vyavasthā kriyate / pratyātmālaye tu svakleśavāsanāśuddhasya dharmanairātmyadarśanātsamādhisukhavihāraṃ prāpya śrāvako jinakāyatāṃ pratilapsyate //
body.translated_text: One of the indeterminate (<s>aniyata</s>) lineage, moreover, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, when these three are being taught, should be directed to whichever [teaching] wins him over. This stage of lineage-determination, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the preparatory ground. The determination is made through the entry into the stage of appearance-free [realization]. However, for one whose own affliction-impressions in the inner <s>ālaya</s> (store-consciousness) are purified, through the vision of the selflessness of phenomena, having attained the blissful abode of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), the <s>śrāvaka</s> will attain the state of a <s>Jina</s>-body (Conqueror's body).

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣat -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, at that time, spoke these verses:

children.translated_text: The fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotāpatti</s>), and likewise that of once-returning (<s>sakṛdāgāmi</s>),
the fruit of non-returning (<s>anāgāmi</s>), and <s>arhatship</s> (<s>arhattvam</s>) — [these are] delusions of the mind. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.128 ||
Three vehicles, one vehicle, and no vehicle — I declare [them all];
for the childish of dull intellect, and for the noble ones, solitude. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.129 ||
The gateway to the supreme truth is cognition (<s>vijñapti</s>) free from duality;
where there is establishment in the appearance-free, whence could there be a three-vehicle arrangement? || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.130 ||
The <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations), the immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>), the formless [attainments], and the <s>samādhis</s>,

children.text: saṃjñānirodho nikhilaṃ cittamātre na vidyate // Lank_2.131 //
children.translated_text: the cessation of perception — all these do not exist in mind-only (<s>cittamātra</s>). || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.131 ||

body.text: tatrecchantikānāṃ punarmahāmate anicchantikatāmokṣaṃ kena pravartate? yaduta sarvakuśalamūlotsargataśca sattvānādikālapraṇidhānataśca / tatra sarvakuśalamūlotsargaḥ katamaḥ? yaduta bodhisattvapiṭakanikṣepo 'bhyākhyānaṃ ca naite sūtrāntā vinayamokṣānukūlā iti bruvataḥ sarvakuśalamūlotsargatvānna nirvāyate / dvitīyaḥ punarmahāmate bodhisattvo mahāsattva evaṃ bhavapraṇidhānopāyapūrvakatvānnāparinirvṛtaiḥ sarvasattvaiḥ parinirvāsyāmīti tato na parinirvāti / etanmahāmate aparinirvāṇadharmakāṇāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ yenecchantikagatiṃ samādhigacchanti //
body.translated_text: Therein, moreover, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, by what does the liberation from <s>icchantika</s>-hood (the state of those devoid of aspiration) of the <s>icchantikas</s> proceed? Namely, through the abandonment of all wholesome roots and through the vows of beings [made] since beginningless time. Therein, what is the abandonment of all wholesome roots? Namely, the rejection of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-collection [of scriptures] and the false accusation: 'These <s>sūtrāntas</s> are not conducive to the <s>Vinaya</s> and liberation.' Due to the abandonment of all wholesome roots, one does not attain <s>nirvāṇa</s>. The second [type], moreover, O <s>Mahāmati</s>: a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>, because of being preceded by vows and skillful means directed toward [continued] existence, [declares]: 'I shall not attain final <s>nirvāṇa</s> as long as all beings have not attained final <s>nirvāṇa</s>' — therefore does not attain final <s>nirvāṇa</s>. This, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the characteristic of those whose nature is non-<s>parinirvāṇa</s>, by which they enter the <s>icchantika</s> course.

body.text: punarapi mahāmatirāha - katamo 'tra bhagavan atyantato na parinirvāti? bhagavānāha - bodhisattvecchantiko 'tra mahāmate ādiparinirvṛtān sarvadharmān viditvā atyantato na parinirvāti /
body.translated_text: <s>Mahāmati</s> again asked: Which one, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, absolutely does not attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s> (final cessation)? The <s>Bhagavān</s> replied: The <s>bodhisattva-icchantika</s>, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, having understood that all <s>dharmas</s> are from the beginning in <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, absolutely does not attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s>.

body.text: na punaḥ sarvakuśalamūlotsargecchantikaḥ / sarvakuśalamūlotsargecchantiko hi mahāmate punarapi tathāgatādhiṣṭhānātkadācitkarhicitkuśalamūlān vyutthāpayati / tatkasya hetoḥ? yaduta aparityaktā hi mahāmate tathāgatānāṃ sarvasattvāḥ / ata etasmātkāraṇānmahāmate bodhisattvecchantiko na parinirvātīti //
body.translated_text: But not the <s>icchantika</s> who has abandoned all wholesome roots (<s>kuśalamūla</s>). For the <s>icchantika</s> who has abandoned all wholesome roots, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, by the empowerment (<s>adhiṣṭhāna</s>) of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, at some time or another produces wholesome roots again. For what reason? Because, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the <s>Tathāgatas</s> have not abandoned any beings. For this very reason, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the <s>bodhisattva-icchantika</s> does not attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s>.

body.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate bodhisattvena mahāsattvena svabhāvalakṣaṇatrayakuśalena bhavitavyam / tatra mahāmate parikalpitasvabhāvo nimittātpravartate / kathaṃ punarmahāmate parikalpitasvabhāvo nimittātpravartate? tatra mahāmate paratantrasvabhāvo vastunimittalakṣaṇākāraḥ khyāyate / tatra mahāmate vastunimittalakṣaṇābhiniveśaḥ punardviprakāraḥ / parikalpitasvabhāvaṃ vyavasthāpayanti tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā nāmābhiniveśalakṣaṇena ca nāmavastunimittābhiniveśalakṣaṇena ca / tatra vastunimittābhiniveśalakṣaṇaṃ punarmahāmate yaduta adhyātmabāhyadharmābhiniveśaḥ / nimittalakṣaṇābhiniveśaḥ punaryaduta teṣveva ādhyātmikabāhyeṣu dharmeṣu svasāmānyalakṣaṇaparijñānāvabodhaḥ / etanmahāmate dviprakāraṃ parikalpitasvabhāvasya lakṣaṇam / yadāśrayālambanātpravartate tatparatantram / tatra mahāmate pariniṣpannasvabhāvaḥ katamaḥ? yaduta nimittanāmavastulakṣaṇavikalpavirahitaṃ tathatāryajñānagatimanapratyātmāryajñānagatigocaraḥ / eṣa mahāmate pariniṣpannasvabhāvastathāgatagarbhahṛdayam //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> should be skilled in the three characteristics of inherent nature (<s>svabhāvalakṣaṇatraya</s>). Therein, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the imagined inherent nature (<s>parikalpitasvabhāva</s>) proceeds from signs (<s>nimitta</s>). How then, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, does the imagined inherent nature proceed from signs? Therein, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the dependent inherent nature (<s>paratantrasvabhāva</s>) is manifested as having the appearance of object-sign-characteristics. Therein, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the attachment to object-sign-characteristics is of two kinds. The <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly enlightened <s>Buddhas</s> establish the imagined inherent nature through the characteristic of attachment to names and through the characteristic of attachment to name-object-signs. Therein, the characteristic of attachment to object-signs, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the attachment to internal and external <s>dharmas</s>. The attachment to sign-characteristics is the full understanding and awakening to the specific and general characteristics (<s>svasāmānyalakṣaṇa</s>) of those very internal and external <s>dharmas</s>. This, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the twofold characteristic of the imagined inherent nature. That which proceeds from the support and object is the dependent (<s>paratantra</s>). Therein, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, what is the perfected inherent nature (<s>pariniṣpannasvabhāva</s>)? That which is devoid of the discrimination of sign-name-object-characteristics, the domain of the noble knowledge of <s>Suchness</s> (<s>tathatā</s>), the domain of one's own inner noble knowledge (<s>pratyātmāryajñāna</s>). This, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the perfected inherent nature — the essence of the <s>Tathāgatagarbha</s> (womb of the <s>Tathāgata</s>).

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimāṃ gāthāmabhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, at that time, spoke this verse:

children.translated_text: Signs, names, and mental construction are the characteristics of the two [imagined and dependent] inherent natures;
Right knowledge, which is <s>Suchness</s> (<s>tathatā</s>), is the characteristic of the perfected [inherent nature]. [Laṅk 2.132]

body.text: eṣa mahāmate pañcadharmasvabhāvalakṣaṇapravicayo nāma dharmaparyāyaḥ pratyātmāryajñānagatigocaraḥ, yatra tvayā anyaiśca bodhisattvaiḥ śikṣitavyam //
body.translated_text: This, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the <s>dharmaparyāya</s> (discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>) called the investigation of the five <s>dharmas</s> and the characteristics of inherent nature, the domain of one's own inner noble knowledge, in which you and other <s>Bodhisattvas</s> should train.

body.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate bodhisattvena mahāsattvena nairātmyadvayalakṣaṇapravicayakuśalena bhavitavyam / tatra mahāmate katamannairātmyadvayalakṣaṇam? yaduta ātmātmīyarahitaskandhadhātvāyatanakadambamajñānakarmatṛṣṇāprabhavaṃ cakṣuṣā rūpādigrahaṇābhiniveśātpravartamānaṃ vijñānaṃ sarvendriyaiḥ svacittadṛśyabhājanadehālayasvacittavikalpavikalpitaṃ vijñāpayati / nadībījadīpavāyumeghasadṛśakṣaṇaparaṃparābhedabhinnaṃ capalaṃ vānaramakṣikāsadṛśamacaukṣamacaukṣaviṣayacāryanātho 'nala ivātṛptamanādikālaprapañcaviṣayavāsanārahitamaraghaṭṭacakrayantracakravatsaṃsārabhavagaticakre vicitradeharūpadhārimāyāvetālayantrapratimaṃ pravartamānaṃ pravartate / yadatra mahāmate lakṣaṇakauśalajñānam, idamucyate pudgalanairātmyajñānam //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> should be skilled in the investigation of the characteristics of the twofold selflessness (<s>nairātmya</s>). What, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the characteristic of twofold selflessness? It is the mass of aggregates (<s>skandha</s>), elements (<s>dhātu</s>), and sense-bases (<s>āyatana</s>), devoid of self and what belongs to self, arising from ignorance, action, and craving — consciousness that proceeds from the attachment to grasping forms etc. by the eye and other [senses], manifesting through all the sense-faculties the appearances of one's own mind as vessel[-world], body, and store(<s>ālaya</s>), discriminated by the discriminations of one's own mind. [This consciousness is] like a river, a seed, a lamp, wind, or a cloud — differentiated by the undivided succession of momentary [instances]; fickle, like a monkey or a fly; impure, roaming in impure objects; insatiable like fire; bearing the impressions of beginningless proliferative objects — like a water-wheel or an automaton, revolving on the wheel of the courses of <s>saṃsāric</s> (cyclic) existence, wearing diverse body-forms like a magical zombie-puppet. That which is skill in the knowledge of characteristics herein, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is called the knowledge of the selflessness of the person (<s>pudgalanairātmya</s>).

body.text: tatra mahāmate dharmanairātmyajñānaṃ katamat? yaduta skandhadhātvāyatanānāṃ parikalpitalakṣaṇasvabhāvāvabodhaḥ / yathā mahāmate skandhadhātvāyatanānyātmavirahitāni skandhasamūhamātraṃ hetukarmatṛṣṇāsūtropanibaddhamanyonyapratyayatayā pravartate nirīham, tathā skandhā api mahāmate svasāmānyalakṣaṇavirahitā abhūtaparikalpalakṣaṇavicitraprabhāvitā bālairvikalpyante na tvāryaiḥ /
body.translated_text: What, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the knowledge of the selflessness of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmanairātmya</s>)? It is the awakening to the imagined characteristic-inherent-nature of the aggregates, elements, and sense-bases. Just as, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the aggregates, elements, and sense-bases, being devoid of self, are merely a collection of aggregates, bound together by the thread of cause, action, and craving, proceeding through mutual conditionality without any [independent] agent; so too the aggregates themselves, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, devoid of specific and general characteristics, produced by the variety of the characteristics of false imagination (<s>abhūtaparikalpa</s>), are discriminated by the foolish, not by the noble ones.

body.text: cittamanomanovijñānapañcadharmasvabhāvarahitān mahāmate sarvadharmān vibhāvayan bodhisattvo mahāsattvo dharmanairātmyakuśalo bhavati / dharmanairātmyakuśalaḥ punarmahāmate bodhisattvo mahāsattvo nacirātprathamāṃ bodhisattvabhūmiṃ nirābhāsapravicayāṃ pratilabhate / bhūmilakṣaṇapravicayāvabodhātpramuditānantaramanupūrvaṃ navasu bhūmiṣu kṛtavidyo mahādharmameghā pratilabhate / sa tasyāṃ pratiṣṭhito 'nekaratnamuktopaśobhite mahāpadmarāje padmakṛtau mahāratnavimāne māyāsvabhāvagocaraparicayābhinirvṛtte niṣaṇṇaḥ tadanurūpairjinaputraiḥ parivṛtaḥ sarvabuddhakṣetrāgatairbuddhapāṇyabhiṣekaiścakravartiputravadabhiṣicyate / buddhasutabhūmimatikramya pratyātmāryadharmagatigamanatvāttathāgato dharmakāyavaśavartī bhaviṣyati dharmanairātmyadarśanāt / etanmahāmate sarvadharmanairātmyalakṣaṇam / atra te mahāmate śikṣitavyam, anyaiśca bodhisattvairmahāsattvaiḥ //
body.translated_text: Discerning all <s>dharmas</s> as devoid of mind, <s>manas</s> (thought), <s>manovijñāna</s> (mind-consciousness), the five <s>dharmas</s>, and inherent nature, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> becomes skilled in the selflessness of <s>dharmas</s>. Being skilled in the selflessness of <s>dharmas</s>, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> before long attains the first <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage (<s>bhūmi</s>), which is the investigation of non-appearance (<s>nirābhāsa</s>). Through the awakening to the investigation of stage-characteristics, [the <s>Bodhisattva</s>], immediately after the Joyful (<s>Pramuditā</s>) [stage], progressively, having become accomplished in the nine stages, attains the Great <s>Dharma</s>-Cloud [stage]. Established therein, seated in a great jeweled lotus-mansion, adorned with many jewels and pearls, in a lotus-throne produced by the practice of the domain of illusion-like inherent nature, surrounded by sons of the <s>Jina</s> of like form, coming from all <s>Buddha</s>-fields, he is anointed by the <s>Buddhas</s> with the anointing of their hands, like the son of a <s>Cakravartin</s> (universal monarch). Having transcended the stage of a son of the <s>Buddha</s>, because of proceeding to the course of one's own inner noble <s>Dharma</s>, he will become a <s>Tathāgata</s>, master of the <s>Dharmakāya</s> (truth-body), through the vision of the selflessness of <s>dharmas</s>. This, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the characteristic of the selflessness of all <s>dharmas</s>. Herein you, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, and other <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas</s>, should train.

body.text: atha khalu mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ punarapi bhagavantametadavocat - samāropāpavādalakṣaṇaṃ me bhagavān deśayatu yathāhaṃ ca anye ca bodhisattvāḥ samāropāpavādakudṛṣṭivarjitamatayaḥ kṣipramanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeran / abhisaṃbudhya śāśvatasamāropāpavādocchedadṛṣṭivivarjitāstava buddhanetrīṃ nāpavadiṣyante //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s> again addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s> thus: May the <s>Bhagavān</s> teach me the characteristics of superimposition (<s>samāropa</s>) and denial (<s>apavāda</s>), so that I and other <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, with minds free from the wrong views of superimposition and denial, may quickly attain unsurpassed perfect enlightenment (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). Having attained enlightenment, freed from the views of eternalist superimposition, annihilationist denial, and permanence, they will not disparage your <s>Buddha</s>-guidance.

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān punarapi mahāmaterbodhisattvasya mahāsattvasyādhyeṣaṇāṃ viditvā imāṃ gāthāmabhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having understood the request of the <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s>, spoke this verse:

children.translated_text: Superimposition and denial do not exist in mind-only (<s>cittamātra</s>);
Those who do not understand the mind as the appearance of body, enjoyment, and abode,
those unwise ones wander in superimposition and denial. [Laṅk 2.133]

body.text: atha khalu bhagavānetameva gāthārthamuddyotayan punarapyetadavocat - caturvidho mahāmate asatsamāropaḥ / katamaścaturvidhaḥ? yaduta asallakṣaṇasamāropo 'saddṛṣṭisamāropo 'taddhetusamāropo 'sadbhāvasamāropaḥ / eṣa hi mahāmate caturvidhaḥ samāropaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, illuminating the meaning of this very verse, spoke again thus: Of four kinds, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is false superimposition (<s>asatsamāropa</s>). Of which four kinds? Namely: superimposition of unreal characteristics (<s>asallakṣaṇasamāropa</s>), superimposition of unreal views (<s>asaddṛṣṭisamāropa</s>), superimposition of wrong causes (<s>ataddhetusamāropa</s>), and superimposition of unreal existence (<s>asadbhāvasamāropa</s>). This, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the fourfold superimposition.

body.text: apavādaḥ punarmahāmate katamaḥ? yaduta asyaiva kudṛṣṭisamāropasyānupalabdhipravicayābhāvādapavādo bhavati / etaddhi mahāmate samāropāpavādasya lakṣaṇam //
body.translated_text: What then, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is denial (<s>apavāda</s>)? It is the denial that arises from the absence of the investigation of non-apprehension of this very false superimposition of wrong views. This, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the characteristic of superimposition and denial.

body.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate asallakṣaṇasamāropasya lakṣaṇaṃ katamat? yaduta skandhadhātvāyatanānāmasatsvasāmānyalakṣaṇābhiniveśaḥ - idamevamidaṃ nānyatheti / etaddhi mahāmate asallakṣaṇasamāropasya lakṣaṇam / eṣa hi mahāmate asallakṣaṇasamāropavikalpo 'nādikālaprapañcadauṣṭhulyavicitravāsanābhiniveśātpravartate / etaddhi mahāmate asallakṣaṇasamāropasya lakṣaṇam //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, what is the characteristic of the superimposition of unreal characteristics? It is the attachment to unreal specific and general characteristics of the aggregates, elements, and sense-bases — "this is just so, this is not otherwise." This, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the characteristic of the superimposition of unreal characteristics. This, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the discrimination of superimposition of unreal characteristics, which proceeds from the attachment to the impressions of the varied depravity of beginningless proliferation. This, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the characteristic of the superimposition of unreal characteristics.

body.text: asaddṛṣṭisamāropaḥ punarmahāmate yasteṣveva skandhadhātvāyataneṣvātmasattvajīvajantupoṣapuruṣapudgaladṛṣṭisamāropaḥ / ayamucyate mahāmate asaddṛṣṭisamāropaḥ //
body.translated_text: The superimposition of unreal views, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the superimposition of views of self, being, life, individual, nourisher, person, and <s>pudgala</s> (person) upon those very aggregates, elements, and sense-bases. This is called, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the superimposition of unreal views.

body.text: asaddhetusamāropaḥ punarmahāmate yaduta ahetusamutpannaṃ prāgvijñānaṃ paścādabhūtvā māyāvadanutpannaṃ pūrvaṃ cakṣūrūpālokasmṛtipūrvakaṃ pravartate / pravṛtya bhūtvā ca punarvinaśyati / eṣa mahāmate asaddhetusamāropaḥ //
body.translated_text: The superimposition of wrong causes, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is when the prior consciousness, having arisen without a cause, not having existed before, and being unarisen like an illusion, then proceeds preceded by eye, form, light, and memory. Having proceeded and existed, it again perishes. This, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the superimposition of wrong causes.

body.text: asaddhāvasamāropaḥ punarmahāmate yaduta ākāśanirodhanirvāṇākṛtakabhāvābhiniveśasamāropaḥ / ete ca mahāmate bhāvābhāvavinivṛttāḥ / śaśahayakharoṣṭraviṣāṇakeśoṇḍukaprakhyā mahāmate sarvadharmāḥ sadasatpakṣavigatāḥ / samāropāpavādāśca / bālairvikalpyante svacittadṛśyamātrānavadhāritamatibhirna tvāryaiḥ / etanmahāmate asadbhāvavikalpasamāropāpavādasya lakṣaṇam / tasmāttarhi mahāmate samāropāpavādadṛṣṭivigatena bhavitavyam //
body.translated_text: The superimposition of unreal existence, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the superimposition of attachment to the uncreated entities of space, cessation, and <s>nirvāṇa</s>. These entities, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, are free from existence and non-existence. All <s>dharmas</s>, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, are like the horns of a hare, horse, camel, or the hair of a tortoise — departed from the theses of existent and non-existent. [So too are] superimposition and denial. They are discriminated by the foolish, whose minds do not ascertain [that all is] mere appearance of one's own mind (<s>svacittadṛśyamātra</s>), not by the noble ones. This, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the characteristic of the discrimination of the superimposition of unreal existence, and of denial. Therefore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, one should be free from the views of superimposition and denial.

body.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate bodhisattvāścittamanomanovijñānapañcadharmasvabhāvanairātmyalakṣaṇadvayagatiṃgatvā parahitahetoranekarūpaveśadhāriṇo bhavanti / parikalpitasvabhāvā iva paratantrāśayā viśvarūpacintāmaṇisadṛśāḥ sarvabuddhakṣetraparṣanmaṇḍalagatā māyāsvapnapratibhāsapratibimbodakacandragatisamānutpādabhaṅgaśāśvatocchedarahitān sarvadharmān saṃmukhaṃ sarvatathāgatebhyaḥ sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhayānavirahān dharmadeśanāṃ śṛṇvanti, samādhimukhaśatasahasrāṇi ca pratilabhante / yāvadanekāni samādhikoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇi pratilabhyaḥ taiḥ samādhibhiḥ kṣetrātkṣetraṃ saṃkrāmanti / buddhapūjābhiyuktāśca sarvopapattidevabhavanālayeṣu ratnatrayamupadeśya buddharūpamāsthāya śrāvakagaṇabodhisattvagaṇaparivṛtāḥ svacittadṛśyamātrāvatāraṇatayā bāhyabhāvābhāvopadeśaṃ kurvanti sadasatpakṣavinivṛttyartham //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, having entered the course of the twofold characteristics of mind, <s>manas</s>, <s>manovijñāna</s>, the five <s>dharmas</s>, inherent nature, and selflessness (<s>nairātmya</s>), for the benefit of others, assume diverse forms. Like the imagined inherent nature [which depends on] the dependent [nature], resembling a wish-fulfilling jewel (<s>cintāmaṇi</s>) of universal form, having gone to the assemblies and <s>maṇḍalas</s> of all <s>Buddha</s>-fields, they hear the <s>Dharma</s>-teaching from all the <s>Tathāgatas</s> face to face — [teachings about] all <s>dharmas</s> as devoid of the vehicles of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, [dharmas that are] like illusion, dreams, reflected images, mirror-reflections, and the moon in water, free from arising and destruction, eternalism and annihilation. And they attain hundreds of thousands of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) doors, and even many tens of millions of hundreds of thousands of <s>samādhis</s>. Having attained those <s>samādhis</s>, they pass from field to field. Devoted to the worship of the <s>Buddhas</s>, in all the divine abode-palaces of [re]birth, having taught the Triple Jewel (<s>Ratnatraya</s>) and having assumed the form of a <s>Buddha</s>, surrounded by hosts of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and hosts of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, they teach [beings] about external existence and non-existence through the entry into [the realization that all is] mere appearance of one's own mind (<s>svacittadṛśyamātra</s>), for the purpose of turning away from the theses of existent and non-existent.

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimāṃ gāthāmabhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, at that time, spoke this verse:

children.translated_text: When the sons of the <s>Jina</s> see that the world is mind-only (<s>cittamātra</s>),
then they obtain a transformation body (<s>nairmāṇika kāya</s>), free from the constructions of activity,

children.text: labhante te balābhijñāvaśitaiḥ saha saṃyutam // Lank_2.134 //
children.translated_text: endowed with powers (<s>bala</s>), superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>), and mastery (<s>vaśitā</s>). [Laṅk 2.134]

body.text: atha khalu mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ punarapi bhagavantamadhyeṣate sma - deśayatu bhagavān śūnyatānutpādādvayaniḥsvabhāvalakṣaṇaṃ sarvadharmāṇām, yena śūnyatānutpādādvayaniḥsvabhāvalakṣaṇāvabodhena ahaṃ ca anye ca bodhisattvā mahāsattvā nāstyastivikalpavarjitāḥ kṣipramanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeran //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s> again entreated the <s>Bhagavān</s>: May the <s>Bhagavān</s> teach the characteristics of emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>), non-arising (<s>anutpāda</s>), non-duality (<s>advaya</s>), and non-inherent-nature (<s>niḥsvabhāva</s>) of all <s>dharmas</s>, so that I and other <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas</s>, through the awakening to the characteristics of emptiness, non-arising, non-duality, and non-inherent-nature, freed from the discrimination of "it does not exist" and "it exists," may quickly attain unsurpassed perfect enlightenment.

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān mahāmatiṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvametadavocat - tena hi mahāmate śṛṇu, tatsādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuru / bhāṣiṣye 'haṃ te / sādhu bhagavanniti mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavataḥ pratyaśrauṣīt / bhagavānetadavocat - śūnyatā śūnyateti mahāmate parikalpitasvabhāvapadametat / parikalpitasvabhāvābhiniveśena punarmahāmate śūnyatānutpādābhāvādvayaniḥsvabhāvabhāvavādino bhavanti / tatra mahāmate saṃkṣepeṇa saptavidhā śūnyatā / yaduta lakṣaṇaśūnyatā bhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā apracaritaśūnyatā pracaritaśūnyatā sarvadharmanirabhilāpyaśūnyatā paramārthāryajñānamahāśūnyatā itaretaraśūnyatā ca saptamī //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s> thus: Then, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, listen, and attend well and thoroughly. I shall teach you. "Very well, <s>Bhagavān</s>," the <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s> assented to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said this: "Emptiness, emptiness" (<s>śūnyatā</s>), O <s>Mahāmati</s> — this is a term of the imagined inherent nature. By attachment to the imagined inherent nature, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, one becomes a proponent of [the existence of] emptiness, non-arising, non-existence, non-duality, and non-inherent-nature. Therein, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, emptiness is of seven kinds in brief: namely, emptiness of characteristics (<s>lakṣaṇaśūnyatā</s>), emptiness of the inherent nature of entities (<s>bhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā</s>), non-proceeding emptiness (<s>apracaritaśūnyatā</s>), proceeding emptiness (<s>pracaritaśūnyatā</s>), the emptiness of all <s>dharmas</s> as inexpressible (<s>sarvadharmanirabhilāpyaśūnyatā</s>), the great emptiness of supreme noble knowledge (<s>paramārthāryajñānamahāśūnyatā</s>), and mutual emptiness (<s>itaretaraśūnyatā</s>) as the seventh.

body.text: tatra mahāmate lakṣaṇaśūnyatā katamā? yaduta svasāmānyalakṣaṇaśūnyāḥ sarvabhāvāḥ / parasparasamūhāpekṣitatvātpravicayavibhāgābhāvānmahāmate svasāmānyalakṣaṇasyāpravṛttiḥ / svaparobhayābhāvācca mahāmate lakṣaṇaṃ nāvatiṣṭhate / atastaducyate svalakṣaṇaśūnyāḥ sarvabhāvā iti //
body.translated_text: Now, <s>Mahāmati</s>, what is <s>lakṣaṇa-śūnyatā</s> (emptiness of characteristics)? That is, all <s>dharmas</s> are empty of their own and general characteristics. Because they are mutually dependent upon aggregations, <s>Mahāmati</s>, there is no occurrence of analysis and distinction of own and general characteristics, due to the absence of discernment and differentiation. And because of the non-existence of self, other, or both, <s>Mahāmati</s>, characteristics do not persist. Therefore it is said that all <s>dharmas</s> are empty of their own characteristics.

body.text: bhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā punarmahāmate katamā? yaduta svayaṃ svabhāvābhāvotpattito mahāmate bhāvasvabhāvaśūnyatā bhavati sarvadharmāṇām / tenocyate bhāvasvabhāvaśūnyateti //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Mahāmati</s>, what is <s>bhāvasvabhāva-śūnyatā</s> (emptiness of the intrinsic nature of entities)? That is, <s>Mahāmati</s>, from the standpoint of the non-arising of intrinsic nature by itself, there is <s>bhāvasvabhāva-śūnyatā</s> of all <s>dharmas</s>. Therefore it is called <s>bhāvasvabhāva-śūnyatā</s>.

body.text: apracaritaśūnyatā punarmahāmate katamā? yaduta apracaritapūrvaṃ nirvāṇaṃ skandheṣu / tenocyate apracaritaśūnyateti //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Mahāmati</s>, what is <s>apracarita-śūnyatā</s> (emptiness of the unmanifested)? That is, <s>Nirvāṇa</s> has never been manifested among the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates). Therefore it is called <s>apracarita-śūnyatā</s>.

body.text: pracaritaśūnyatā punarmahāmate katamā? yaduta skandhā ātmātmīyarahitā hetuyuktikriyākarmayogaiḥ pravartamānāḥ pravartante / tenocyate pracaritaśūnyateti //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Mahāmati</s>, what is <s>pracarita-śūnyatā</s> (emptiness of the manifested)? That is, the <s>skandhas</s>, devoid of self and what belongs to self, operate and continue to operate through the conjunction of causes, reasoning, action, and <s>karma</s>. Therefore it is called <s>pracarita-śūnyatā</s>.

body.text: sarvadharmanirabhilāpyaśūnyatā punarmahāmate katamā? yaduta parikalpitasvabhāvānabhilāpyatvānnirabhilāpyaśūnyāḥ sarvadharmāḥ / tenocyate nirabhilāpyaśūnyateti //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Mahāmati</s>, what is <s>sarvadharma-nirabhilāpya-śūnyatā</s> (emptiness of the inexpressibility of all dharmas)? That is, because the <s>parikalpita-svabhāva</s> (imagined nature) is inexpressible, all <s>dharmas</s> are empty of expressibility. Therefore it is called <s>nirabhilāpya-śūnyatā</s>.

body.text: paramārthāryajñānamahāśūnyatā punarmahāmate katamā? yaduta svapratyātmāryajñānādhigamaḥ sarvadṛṣṭidoṣavāsanābhiḥ śūnyaḥ / tenocyate paramārthāryajñānamahāśūnyateti //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Mahāmati</s>, what is <s>paramārtha-āryajñāna-mahā-śūnyatā</s> (great emptiness of the noble wisdom of ultimate reality)? That is, the realization of one's own noble wisdom of inner experience is empty of all the <s>vāsanās</s> (habitual tendencies) of the faults of all views. Therefore it is called <s>paramārtha-āryajñāna-mahā-śūnyatā</s>.

body.text: itaretaraśūnyatā punarmahāmate katamā? yaduta yadyatra nāsti tattena śūnyamityucyate / tadyathā mahāmate śṛgālamātuḥ prāsāde hastigavaiḍakādyā na santi / aśūnyaṃ ca bhikṣubhiriti bhāṣitaṃ mayā / sa ca taiḥ śūnya ityucyate / na ca punarmahāmate prāsādaḥ prāsādabhāvato nāsti, bhikṣavaśca bhikṣubhāvato na santi / na ca te 'nyatra hastigavaiḍakādyā bhāvā nāvatiṣṭhante / idaṃ mahāmate svasāmānyalakṣaṇaṃ sarvadharmāṇām / itaretaraṃ tu na saṃvidyate / tenocyate itaretaraśūnyateti / eṣā mahāmate saptavidhā śūnyatā / eṣā ca mahāmate itaretaraśūnyatā sarvajaghanyā / sā ca tvayā parivarjayitavyā //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Mahāmati</s>, what is <s>itaretara-śūnyatā</s> (mutual emptiness)? That is, when something is absent somewhere, that place is said to be empty of it. For example, <s>Mahāmati</s>, in the hall of <s>Śṛgālamātā</s> (Mṛgāramātā), there are no elephants, cattle, donkeys, and so forth; and I have said that it is not empty of monks — yet it is said to be empty of those. But, <s>Mahāmati</s>, the hall does not not-exist as a hall, nor do the monks not-exist as monks; nor do the elephants, cattle, donkeys, and other entities not-exist elsewhere. <s>Mahāmati</s>, this is the own and general characteristic of all <s>dharmas</s>; but in relation to one another, they are not found. Therefore it is called <s>itaretara-śūnyatā</s>. This, <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the sevenfold <s>śūnyatā</s>. And this <s>itaretara-śūnyatā</s>, <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the most inferior of all. It should be abandoned by you.

body.text: na svayamutpadyate, na ca punarmahāmate te notpadyante anyatra samādhyavasthāyām / tenocyante anutpannā niḥsvabhāvāḥ / anutpattiṃ saṃghāya mahāmate niḥsvabhāvāḥ sarvabhāvāḥ / kṣaṇasaṃtatiprabandhābhāvācca anyathābhāvadarśanānmahāmate niḥsvabhāvāḥ sarvabhāvāḥ / tenocyate niḥsvabhāvāḥ sarvabhāvā iti //
body.translated_text: Nothing arises by itself, and yet, <s>Mahāmati</s>, they are not non-arising except in the state of <s>samādhi</s>. Therefore they are called unborn and without intrinsic nature (<s>niḥsvabhāva</s>). By virtue of their non-arising, <s>Mahāmati</s>, all <s>dharmas</s> are <s>niḥsvabhāva</s>. And because of the absence of a continuous succession of moments and because one sees their becoming-otherwise, <s>Mahāmati</s>, all <s>dharmas</s> are <s>niḥsvabhāva</s>. Therefore it is said that all <s>dharmas</s> are without intrinsic nature.

body.text: advayalakṣaṇaṃ punarmahāmate katamat? yaduta cchāyātapavaddīrghahrasvakṛṣṇaśuklavanmahāmate dvayaprabhāviatā na pṛthakpṛthak / evaṃ saṃsāranirvāṇavanmahāmate sarvadharmā advayāḥ / na yatra mahāmate nirvāṇaṃ tatra saṃsāraḥ / na ca yatra saṃsārastatra nirvāṇam, vilakṣaṇahetusadbhāvāt / tenocyate advayā saṃsāraparinirvāṇavatsarvadharmā iti / tasmāttarhi mahāmate śūnyatānutpādādvayaniḥsvabhāvalakṣaṇe yogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Mahāmati</s>, what is the characteristic of non-duality (<s>advaya</s>)? That is, just as shadow and sunlight, long and short, black and white, <s>Mahāmati</s>, arise from the manifestation of duality and are not separate from each other, so too, <s>Mahāmati</s>, like <s>saṃsāra</s> and <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, all <s>dharmas</s> are non-dual. Where there is <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, <s>Mahāmati</s>, there is no <s>saṃsāra</s>; and where there is <s>saṃsāra</s>, there is no <s>Nirvāṇa</s> — because of the existence of mutually distinct characteristics and causes. Therefore it is said that all <s>dharmas</s> are non-dual, like <s>saṃsāra</s> and <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. Therefore, <s>Mahāmati</s>, you should practice yoga with respect to the characteristics of <s>śūnyatā</s>, non-arising, non-duality, and essencelessness.

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmime gāthe abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then at that time, the <s>Bhagavān</s> spoke these verses:

children.translated_text: I teach <s>śūnyatā</s> always, free from eternalism and annihilationism,

children.text: saṃsāraṃ svapnamāyākhyaṃ na ca karma vinaśyati // Lank_2.135 //
children.translated_text: <s>Saṃsāra</s> is proclaimed as like a dream and illusion, yet <s>karma</s> does not perish. [Laṅk. 2.135]
Space, and <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, and cessation, and duality —
The ignorant imagine them as uncreated; the noble ones are free from existence and non-existence. [Laṅk. 2.136]

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān punarapi mahāmatiṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvametadavocat - etaddhi mahāmate śūnyatānutpādādvayaniḥsvabhāvalakṣaṇaṃ sarvabuddhānāṃ sarvasūtrāntagatam / yatra kvacitsūtrānte 'yamevārtho vibhāvayitavyaḥ / eṣa hi mahāmate sūtrāntaḥ sarvasattvāśayadeśanārthavyabhicāraṇī, na sā tattvapratyavasthānakathā / tadyathā mahāmate mṛgatṛṣṇikā mṛgollāpinī udakabhāvābhiniveśenābhiniveśyate, tasyāṃ codakaṃ nāsti, evameva mahāmate sarvasūtrāntadeśanā dharmā bālānāṃ svavikalpasaṃtoṣaṇam, na tu sā tattvāryajñānavyavasthānakathā / tasmāttarhi mahāmate arthānusāriṇā bhavitavyaṃ na deśanābhilāpābhiniviṣṭena //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> again spoke to the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s> thus: Indeed, <s>Mahāmati</s>, these characteristics of <s>śūnyatā</s>, non-arising, non-duality, and essencelessness are found throughout all the <s>sūtras</s> of all the <s>Buddhas</s>. In whatever <s>sūtra</s> they appear, this very meaning should be discerned. For, <s>Mahāmati</s>, the <s>sūtra</s> discourse is adapted to the dispositions of all beings in its teaching and meaning — it is not a statement establishing ultimate truth. Just as, <s>Mahāmati</s>, a mirage entices deer with the appearance of water, though there is no water in it, so too, <s>Mahāmati</s>, all <s>sūtra</s> teachings are for the satisfaction of the self-projections (<s>vikalpa</s>) of the ignorant, and are not statements establishing the noble wisdom of reality. Therefore, <s>Mahāmati</s>, one should follow the meaning, not be attached to the letter of the teaching.

body.text: atha khalu mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantametadavocat - tathāgatagarbhaḥ punarbhagavatā sūtrāntapāṭhe 'nuvarṇitaḥ / sa ca kila tvayā prakṛtiprabhāsvaraviśuddhyādiviśuddha eva varṇyate dvātriṃśallakṣaṇadharaḥ sarvasattvadehāntargataḥ / mahārghamūlyaratnaṃ malinavastupariveṣṭitamiva skandhadhātvāyatanavastuveṣṭito rāgadveṣamohābhūtaparikalpamalamalino nityo dhruvaḥ śivaḥ śāśvataśca bhagavatā varṇitaḥ / tatkathamayaṃ bhagavaṃstīrthakarātmavādatulyastathāgatagarbhavādo na bhavati? tīrthakarā api bhagavan nityaḥ kartā nirguṇo vibhuravyaya ityātmavādopadeśaṃ kurvanti //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s> said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: The <s>Tathāgatagarbha</s> (Buddha-nature) has been praised by the <s>Bhagavān</s> in the <s>sūtra</s> discourses. And it is described by you as inherently luminous and pure from the beginning, endowed with the thirty-two marks, dwelling within the bodies of all sentient beings — like a precious gem of great value wrapped in a soiled cloth, it is enveloped by the <s>skandhas</s>, <s>dhātus</s>, and <s>āyatanas</s>, stained by the defilements of <s>rāga</s> (passion), <s>dveṣa</s> (hatred), and <s>moha</s> (delusion) and false imagination, and yet is described by the <s>Bhagavān</s> as permanent, stable, blissful, and eternal. How then, <s>Bhagavān</s>, does this <s>Tathāgatagarbha</s> doctrine not become equivalent to the <s>ātmavāda</s> (self-doctrine) of the non-Buddhist teachers? For the non-Buddhist teachers too, <s>Bhagavān</s>, teach the doctrine of a self that is permanent, a creator, without qualities, all-pervading, and imperishable.

body.text: bhagavānāha - na hi mahāmate tīrthakarātmavādatulyo mama tathāgatagarbhopadeśaḥ / kiṃ tu mahāmate tathāgatāḥ śūnyatābhūtakoṭinirvāṇānutpādānimittāpraṇihitādyānāṃ mahāmate padārthānāṃ tathāgatagarbhopadeśaṃ kṛtvā tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā bālānāṃ nairātmyasaṃtrāsapadavivarjanārthaṃ nirvikalpanirābhāsagocaraṃ tathāgatagarbhamukhopadeśena deśayanti / na cātra mahāmate anāgatapratyutpannaiḥ bodhisattvairmahāsattvairātmābhiniveśaḥ kartavyaḥ / tadyathā mahāmate kumbhakāra ekasmānmṛtparamāṇurāśervividhāni bhāṇḍāni karoti hastaśilpadaṇḍodakasūtraprayatnayogāt, evameva mahāmate tathāgatāstadeva dharmanairātmyaṃ sarvavikalpalakṣaṇavinivṛttaṃ vividhaiḥ prajñopāyakauśalyayogairgarbhopadeśena vā nairātmyopadeśena vā kumbhakāravaccitraiḥ padavyañjanaparyāyairdeśayante / etasmātkāraṇānmahāmate tīrthakarātmavādopadeśatulyastathāgatagarbhopadeśo na bhavati / evaṃ hi mahāmate tathāgatagarbhopadeśamātmavādābhiniviṣṭānāṃ tīrthakarāṇāmākarṣaṇārthaṃ tathāgatagarbhopadeśena nirdiśanti - kathaṃ bata abhūtātmavikalpadṛṣṭipatitāśayā vimokṣatrayagocarapatitāśayopetāḥ kṣipramanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeranniti / etadarthaṃ mahāmate tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāstathāgatagarbhopadeśaṃ kurvanti / ata etanna bhavati tīrthakarātmavādatulyam / tasmāttarhi mahāmate tīrthakaradṛṣṭivinivṛttyarthaṃ tathāgatanairātmyagarbhānusāriṇā ca te bhavitavyam //
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: No indeed, <s>Mahāmati</s>, my <s>Tathāgatagarbha</s> teaching is not equivalent to the <s>ātmavāda</s> of the non-Buddhist teachers. Rather, <s>Mahāmati</s>, the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, having taught the <s>Tathāgatagarbha</s> through such terms as <s>śūnyatā</s>, <s>bhūtakoṭi</s> (reality-limit), <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, non-arising, signlessness, wishlessness, and other such meanings, <s>Mahāmati</s> — the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, <s>Samyaksaṃbuddhas</s> teach the <s>Tathāgatagarbha</s> through this introductory device in order to eliminate the fear of <s>nairātmya</s> (selflessness) among the ignorant, teaching through the door of <s>Tathāgatagarbha</s> a domain free from conceptual discrimination and without appearances. And herein, <s>Mahāmati</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s> and <s>Mahāsattvas</s> of the future and present should not cling to a notion of self. Just as, <s>Mahāmati</s>, a potter makes various vessels from a single mass of clay particles through the application of hands, skill, rod, water, string, and effort, so too, <s>Mahāmati</s>, the <s>Tathāgatas</s> teach that very <s>dharma-nairātmya</s> (selflessness of dharmas), free from the characteristics of all <s>vikalpas</s> (conceptual constructions), through various skillful means of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) and <s>upāya</s> (method) — whether through the teaching of <s>garbha</s> (embryo/matrix) or the teaching of <s>nairātmya</s> — like a potter, with variegated expressions, words, and synonyms. For this reason, <s>Mahāmati</s>, the <s>Tathāgatagarbha</s> teaching is not equivalent to the <s>ātmavāda</s> teaching of the non-Buddhist teachers. Thus indeed, <s>Mahāmati</s>, the <s>Tathāgatas</s> set forth the <s>Tathāgatagarbha</s> teaching in order to attract non-Buddhist teachers who are attached to the doctrine of self — thinking: "How might those whose dispositions have fallen into the view of false self-imagination, endowed with dispositions fallen into the domain of the three gates of liberation, quickly realize unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>)?" For this purpose, <s>Mahāmati</s>, the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, <s>Samyaksaṃbuddhas</s> teach the <s>Tathāgatagarbha</s>. Therefore it is not equivalent to the <s>ātmavāda</s> of the non-Buddhist teachers. Therefore, <s>Mahāmati</s>, in order to abandon the views of the non-Buddhist teachers, you should follow the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>nairātmya-garbha</s> (selflessness-womb).

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimāṃ gāthāmabhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then at that time, the <s>Bhagavān</s> spoke this verse:

children.translated_text: <s>Pudgala</s> (person), continuity, <s>skandhas</s>, conditions, atoms,
<s>Pradhāna</s> (primal matter), <s>Īśvara</s> (Lord), creator — these are merely <s>cittamātra</s> (mind-only) imagined by <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual construction). [Laṅk. 2.137]

body.text: atha khalu mahāmatirbodhisattvo 'nāgatāṃ janatāṃ samālokya punarapi bhagavantamadhyeṣate sma - deśayatu me bhagavān yogābhisamayaṃ yathā bodhisattvā mahāsattvā mahāyogayogino bhavanti / bhagavānāha - caturbhirmahāmate dharmaiḥ samanvāgatā bodhisattvā mahāyogayogino bhavanti / katamaiścaturbhiḥ? yaduta svacittadṛśyavibhāvanatayā ca utpādasthitibhaṅgadṛṣṭivivarjanatayā ca bāhyabhāvābhāvopalakṣaṇatayā ca svapratyātmāryajñānādhigamābhilakṣaṇatayā ca / ebhirmahāmate caturbhirdharmaiḥ samanvāgatā bodhisattvā mahāsattvā mahāyogayogino bhavanti //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s>, looking toward future generations, again requested the <s>Bhagavān</s>: May the <s>Bhagavān</s> teach me the yogic realization by which <s>Bodhisattvas</s> and <s>Mahāsattvas</s> become practitioners of the great yoga. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: <s>Mahāmati</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s> endowed with four <s>dharmas</s> become practitioners of the great yoga. Which four? Namely: by discerning that all is the appearance of one's own mind (<s>svacittadṛśya-vibhāvanā</s>), by abandoning the view of arising, abiding, and ceasing (<s>utpāda-sthiti-bhaṅga-dṛṣṭi-vivarjana</s>), by recognizing the non-existence of external entities (<s>bāhyabhāvābhāva-upalakṣaṇa</s>), and by aspiring to the realization of one's own noble inner wisdom (<s>svapratyātma-āryajñāna-adhigama</s>). Endowed with these four <s>dharmas</s>, <s>Mahāmati</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s> and <s>Mahāsattvas</s> become practitioners of the great yoga.

body.text: tatra kathaṃ mahāmate bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ svacittadṛśyavibhāvanākuśalo bhavati? yaduta sa evaṃ pratyavekṣate - svacittamātramidaṃ traidhātukamātmātmīyarahitaṃ nirīhamāyūhaniyūhavigatamanādikālaprapañcadauṣṭhulyavāsanābhiniveśavāsitaṃ traidhātukavicitrarūpopacāropanibaddhaṃ dehabhogapratiṣṭhāgativikalpānugataṃ vikalpyate khyāyate ca / evaṃ hi mahāmate bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ svacittadṛśyavibhāvanākuśalo bhavati //
body.translated_text: Now how, <s>Mahāmati</s>, does a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> become skilled in discerning the appearance of one's own mind? That is, one reflects thus: this triple world is nothing but one's own mind (<s>svacittamātra</s>), devoid of self and what belongs to self, free from effort, striving, and contriving, pervaded by the habitual tendencies (<s>vāsanā</s>) of attachment to the defilements of beginningless proliferation, bound to the varied forms and activities of the triple world, following the conceptual constructions of body, enjoyment, abode, and destiny — it is imagined and appears thus. In this way, <s>Mahāmati</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> becomes skilled in discerning the appearance of one's own mind.

body.text: kathaṃ punarmahāmate bodhisattvo mahāsattva utpādasthitibhaṅgadṛṣṭivivarjito bhavati? yaduta māyāsvapnarūpajanmasadṛśāḥ sarvabhāvāḥ svaparobhayābhāvānnotpadyante / svacittamātrānusāritvādbāhyabhāvābhāvadarśanādvijñānānāmapravṛttiṃ dṛṣṭvā pratyayānāmakūṭarāśitvaṃ ca vikalpapratyayodbhavaṃ traidhātukaṃ paśyanto 'dhyātmabāhyasarvadharmānupalabdhibhirniḥsvabhāvadarśanādutpādadṛṣṭivinivṛttau māyādidharmasvabhāvānugamādanutpattikadharmakṣāntiṃ pratilabhante / aṣṭamyāṃ bhūmau sthitāḥ cittamanomanovijñānapañcadharmasvabhāvanairātmyadvayagatiparāvṛttyadhigamānmanomayakāyaṃ pratilabhante //
body.translated_text: How then, <s>Mahāmati</s>, does a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> abandon the view of arising, abiding, and ceasing? That is, all <s>dharmas</s> are like illusion, dream, and form-born appearances — because of the non-existence of self, other, or both, they do not arise. Seeing the non-operation of the <s>vijñānas</s> (consciousnesses) because one follows mind-only and sees the non-existence of external entities, and seeing that conditions are not a false heap and that the triple world originates from conceptual conditions, through the non-apprehension of all internal and external <s>dharmas</s> and the seeing of essencelessness — one turns away from the view of arising, and through following the nature of <s>dharmas</s> such as illusion and so forth, one attains <s>anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti</s> (patient acceptance of the non-arising of dharmas). Established on the eighth <s>bhūmi</s>, through the turning-about (<s>parāvṛtti</s>) of the realization of <s>citta</s> (mind), <s>manas</s> (mentation), <s>manovijñāna</s> (mental consciousness), the five <s>dharmas</s>, the three <s>svabhāvas</s> (natures), and the twofold <s>nairātmya</s> (selflessness), one attains the <s>manomayakāya</s> (mind-made body).

body.text: mahāmatirāha - manomayakāya iti bhagavan kena kāraṇena? bhagavānāha - manomaya iti mahāmate manovadapratihataśīghragābhitvānmanomaya ityucyate / tadyathā mahāmate mano 'pratihataṃ girikuḍyanadīvṛkṣādiṣvanekāni yojanaśatasahasrāṇi pūrvadṛṣṭānubhūtān viṣayānanusmaran svacittaprabandhāvicchinnaśarīramapratihatagati pravartate, evameva mahāmate manomayakāyasahapratilambhena māyopamasamena samādhinā balavaśitābhijñānalakṣaṇakusumitamāryagatinikāyasahajo mana iva pravartate 'pratihatagatiḥ pūrvapraṇidhānaviṣayānanusmaran sattvaparipākārtham / evaṃ hi mahāmate bodhisattvo mahāsattva utpādasthitibhaṅgadṛṣṭivivarjito bhavati //
body.translated_text: <s>Mahāmati</s> said: <s>Bhagavān</s>, why is it called <s>manomayakāya</s>? The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: It is called <s>manomaya</s> (mind-made), <s>Mahāmati</s>, because like the mind it moves swiftly and without obstruction — therefore it is called <s>manomaya</s>. Just as, <s>Mahāmati</s>, the mind moves unobstructedly across mountains, walls, rivers, trees, and other things, recollecting objects previously seen and experienced over many hundreds of thousands of <s>yojanas</s>, with an uninterrupted body of its own mental continuum and an unobstructed course — so too, <s>Mahāmati</s>, with the attainment of the <s>manomayakāya</s>, through a <s>samādhi</s> like an illusion, adorned with the marks of the powers (<s>bala</s>), sovereign masteries (<s>vaśitā</s>), and superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>), born together with the noble destiny, one moves like the mind itself with an unobstructed course, recollecting the objects of former vows for the sake of maturing sentient beings. Thus indeed, <s>Mahāmati</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> abandons the view of arising, abiding, and ceasing.

body.text: tatra kathaṃ mahāmate bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bāhyabhāvābhāvopalakṣaṇakuśalo bhavati? yaduta marīcisvapnakeśoṇḍukaprakhyā mahāmate sarvabhāvāḥ / anādikālaprapañcadauṣṭhulyavicitravipākavikalpavāsanābhiniveśahetukāḥ sarvabhāvasvabhāvā iti saṃpaśyan pratyātmāryajñānagativiṣayamabhilaṣate / ebhirmahāmate caturbhirdharmaiḥ samanvāgatā bodhisattvā mahāsattvā mahāyogayogino bhavanti / atra te mahāmate yogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Now how, <s>Mahāmati</s>, does a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> become skilled in recognizing the non-existence of external entities? That is, <s>Mahāmati</s>, all <s>dharmas</s> are like mirages, dreams, and hair-circles. Seeing that the intrinsic natures of all entities arise from causes of attachment to the habitual tendencies of varied karmic fruition from the defilements of beginningless proliferation, one aspires toward the domain of one's own noble inner wisdom. Endowed with these four <s>dharmas</s>, <s>Mahāmati</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s> and <s>Mahāsattvas</s> become practitioners of the great yoga. Herein, <s>Mahāmati</s>, you should practice yoga.

body.text: atha khalu mahāmatirbodhisattvaḥ punarapi bhagavantamadhyeṣate sma - deśayatu me bhagavān hetupratyayalakṣaṇaṃ sarvadharmāṇām, yena hetupratyayalakṣaṇāvabodhena ahaṃ ca anye ca bodhisattvā mahāsattvā sadasaddṛṣṭivikalparahitāḥ sarvabhāvanākramaṃ yugapadutpattiṃ na kalpayeyuḥ //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s> again entreated the Blessed One: 'May the Blessed One teach me the characteristics of the causes and conditions of all <s>dharmas</s>, so that through understanding the characteristics of causes and conditions, I and other <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s>, free from the conceptualization of the views of existence and non-existence, may not imagine all stages of becoming as arising simultaneously.'

body.text: bhagavānāha - dviprakāraṃ mahāmate pratītyasamutpādahetulakṣaṇaṃ sarvadharmāṇāṃ yaduta bāhyaṃ ca ādhyātmikaṃ ca / tatra bāhyapratītyasamutpādo mahāmate / mṛtpiṇḍadaṇḍacakrasūtrodakapuruṣaprayatnādipratyayairmahāmate ghaṭa utpadyate / yathā ca mahāmate ghaṭo mṛtpiṇḍādeva, tantubhyaḥ paṭāḥ, vīraṇebhyaḥ kaṭāḥ, bījādaṅkuraḥ, manthādipuruṣaprayatnayogāddadhno navanīta utpadyate, evameva mahāmate bāhyaḥ pratītyasamutpādaḥ pūrvottarottaro draṣṭavyam //
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'The characteristic of the cause of dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>) of all <s>dharmas</s> is of two kinds, O <s>Mahāmati</s> — namely, external and internal. Therein, external dependent origination, O <s>Mahāmati</s>: a pot arises, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, from conditions such as a lump of clay, a stick, a wheel, a string, water, a person's effort, and so forth. Just as, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, a pot [arises] from a lump of clay itself, cloth from threads, mats from grass, a sprout from a seed, butter from curd through the effort-yoga of churning and a person's labor — even so, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, external dependent origination should be seen as successive and progressive.'

body.text: tatra ādhyātmikaḥ pratītyasamutpādo yaduta avidyā tṛṣā karmetyevamādyā mahāmate dharmāḥ pratītyasamutpādasaṃjñāṃ pratilabhante / ebhya utpannā mahāmate skandhadhātvāyatanākhyā dharmāḥ pratītyasamutpādasaṃjñāṃ pratilabhante / te cāviśiṣṭāḥ, kalpyante ca bālaiḥ //
body.translated_text: Therein, internal dependent origination is as follows: <s>dharmas</s> such as ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>), and <s>karma</s> (action), O <s>Mahāmati</s>, obtain the designation 'dependent origination.' The <s>dharmas</s> called aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>), elements (<s>dhātus</s>), and sense-bases (<s>āyatanas</s>), arising from these, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, obtain the designation 'dependent origination.' And they are undifferentiated, though they are conceptualized by the childish.

body.text: tatra heturmahāmate ṣaḍūvidhaḥ / yaduta bhaviṣyaddhetuḥ saṃbandhaheturlakṣaṇahetuḥ kāraṇaheturvyañjanaheturupekṣāheturmahāmate ṣaṣṭhaḥ / tatra bhaviṣyaddheturmahāmate hetukṛtyaṃ karotyadhyātmabāhyotpattau dharmāṇām / saṃbandhahetuḥ punarmahāmate ālambanakṛtyaṃ karotyadhyātmikabāhyotpattau skandhabījādīnām / lakṣaṇahetuḥ punaraparaṃ mahāmate anantarakriyālakṣaṇoparibaddhaṃ janayati / kāraṇahetuḥ punarmahāmate ādhipatyādhikārakṛtyaṃ karoti cakravartinṛpavat / vyañjanahetuḥ punarmahāmate utpannasya vikalpasya bhāvasya lakṣaṇoddyotanakṛtyaṃ karoti pradīpavadrūpādīnām / upekṣāhetuḥ punarmahāmate vinivṛttikāle prabandhakriyāvyucchittiṃ karotyavikalpotpattau //
body.translated_text: Therein, cause, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is sixfold. Namely: the future cause (<s>bhaviṣyaddhetu</s>), the connective cause (<s>saṃbandhahetu</s>), the characteristic cause (<s>lakṣaṇahetu</s>), the causal cause (<s>kāraṇahetu</s>), the expressive cause (<s>vyañjanahetu</s>), and the indifference cause (<s>upekṣāhetu</s>), O <s>Mahāmati</s>, as the sixth. Therein, the future cause, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, performs the function of a cause in the internal and external arising of <s>dharmas</s>. The connective cause, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, performs the function of a support in the internal and external arising of aggregate-seeds and the like. The characteristic cause, moreover, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, produces [an effect] bound to the characteristic of immediate action above. The causal cause, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, performs the function of sovereign authority, like a universal emperor. The expressive cause, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, performs the function of illuminating the characteristics of an arisen, conceptualized entity — like a lamp [illuminating] form and the like. The indifference cause, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, at the time of cessation, produces the discontinuation of the activity of the series, in the arising of the non-conceptual.

body.text: ete hi mahāmate svavikalpakalpitā bālapṛthagjanairna kramavṛttyā na yugapatpravartante / tatkasya hetoḥ? yadi punarmahāmate yugapatpravarteran, kāryakāraṇavibhāgo na syādapratilabdhahetulakṣaṇatvāt / atha kramavṛttyā pravarteran, alabdhasya lakṣaṇātmakatvātkramavṛttyā na pravartate / ajātaputrapitṛśabdavanmahāmate kramavṛttisaṃbandhayogā na ghaṭante / tārkikāṇāṃ hetvārambaṇanirantarādhipatipratyayādibhirjanyajanakatvānmahāmate kramavṛttyā notpadyante / parikalpitasvabhāvābhiniveśalakṣaṇānmahāmate yugapannotpadyante / svacittadṛśyadehabhogapraviṣṭhānatvātsvasāmānyalakṣaṇabāhyabhāvābhāvānmahāmate krameṇa yugapadvā notpadyante / anyatra svacittadṛśyavikalpavikalpitatvādvijñānaṃ pravartate / tasmāttarhi mahāmate hetupratyayakriyāyogalakṣaṇakramayugapaddṛṣṭivigatena te bhavitavyam //
body.translated_text: These, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, being imagined by the conceptualization of childish ordinary persons, do not operate by sequential progression nor simultaneously. For what reason? If, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, they were to operate simultaneously, there would be no distinction between effect and cause, since the characteristic of cause would not be obtained. But if they were to operate by sequential progression — since what has not been obtained has the nature of a characteristic — it does not operate by sequential progression. Just as, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the connection of sequential progression does not apply to the terms 'father' and 'son' when the son is unborn, [so too] for the logicians, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, [causes] do not arise sequentially, because of the producer-produced relationship among their cause-conditions, object-conditions, immediately-preceding conditions, and dominant conditions. Due to attachment to the characteristic of the imagined inherent nature (<s>parikalpitasvabhāva</s>), O <s>Mahāmati</s>, they do not arise simultaneously. Because body, enjoyment, and establishment are entered as appearances of one's own mind, and because external entities of own-characteristic and general-characteristic are absent, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, they do not arise either sequentially or simultaneously. Apart from being conceptualized by the conceptualization of the appearances of one's own mind, consciousness does not operate. Therefore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, you should be free from views of sequential and simultaneous [arising] with regard to the characteristics of the yoga of causal activity.

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: On this, it is said:

children.translated_text: Nothing whatsoever arises here from conditions, nor does it cease;

children.text: utpadyante nirudhyante pratyayā eva kalpitāḥ // Lank_2.138 //
children.translated_text: [both] arising and ceasing — the conditions themselves are imagined. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.138 ||
The defilement of ceasing and arising of conditions is not denied;

children.text: yatra bālā vikalpanti pratyayaiḥ sa nivāryate // Lank_2.139 //
children.translated_text: where the childish conceptualize through conditions, that is denied. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.139 ||
Since there is no arising of <s>dharmas</s> from conditions that are non-existent,
and since the mind, deluded by impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>), appears in the three realms of existence —
nothing arises from non-being, nor is it destroyed by conditions. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.140 ||
When [people] perceive the conditioned as a barren woman's son or a flower in the sky,

children.text: tadā grāhaśca grāhyaṃ ca bhrāntiṃ dṛṣṭvā nivartate // Lank_2.141 //
children.translated_text: then both the grasper and the grasped, having seen [their] delusion, cease. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.141 ||

children.text: na cotpādyaṃ na cotpannaḥ pratyayo 'pi na kiṃcana /
children.translated_text: There is nothing to be produced, nor is there any producer; a condition too is nothing whatsoever —
nothing exists anywhere; but conventional usage is spoken of. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.142 ||

body.text: atha khalu mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ punarapi bhagavantametadavocat - deśayatu me bhagavān vāgvikalpalakṣaṇahṛdayaṃ nāma dharmaparyāyaṃ yena vāgvikalpalakṣaṇahṛdayena bhagavan suprativibhāgavinibaddhena ahaṃ ca anye ca bodhisattvā mahāsattvā abhilāpābhilāpyārthadvayagatiṃgatāḥ kṣipramanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhya abhilāpābhilāpyārthadvayagatiṃ sarvasattvānāṃ viśodhayeyuḥ / bhagavānāha - tena hi mahāmate śṛṇu, sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasikuru / bhāṣiṣye 'haṃ te / sādhu bhagavan iti mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavataḥ pratyaśrauṣīt / bhagavānasyaitadavocat - caturvidhaṃ mahāmate vāgvikalpalakṣaṇaṃ bhavati / yaduta lakṣaṇavāk svapnavāk dauṣṭhulyavikalpābhiniveśavāk anādivikalpavāk //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s> again said this to the Blessed One: 'May the Blessed One teach me the <s>dharma</s>-discourse called the Heart of the Characteristics of Speech-Conceptualization, so that, O Blessed One, through that Heart of the Characteristics of Speech-Conceptualization, well-differentiated and well-established, I and other <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s>, having entered the course of the duality of expression and what is expressed, may quickly realize unsurpassed, perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>) and purify the course of the duality of expression and what is expressed for all beings.' The Blessed One said: 'Then, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, listen, and attend well and thoroughly. I shall speak to you.' 'Very well, Blessed One!' — the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s> gave assent to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this to him: 'The characteristics of speech-conceptualization, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, are of four kinds. Namely: characteristic-speech, dream-speech, depravity-conceptualization-attachment-speech, and beginningless-conceptualization-speech.'

body.text: tatra mahāmate lakṣaṇavāk svavikalparūpanimittābhiniveśātpravartate / svapnavāk punarmahāmate pūrvānubhūtaviṣayānusmaraṇātprativibuddhaviṣayābhāvācca pravartate / dauṣṭhulyavikalpābhiniveśavāk punarmahāmate śatrupūrvakṛtakarmānusmaraṇātpravartate / anādikālavikalpavāk punarmahāmate anādikālaprapañcābhiniveśadauṣṭhulyasvabījavāsanātaḥ pravartate / etaddhi mahāmate caturvidhaṃ vāgvikalpalakṣaṇamiti me yaduktam, idaṃ tatpratyuktam //
body.translated_text: Therein, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, characteristic-speech operates from attachment to the appearance of the form of one's own conceptualization. Dream-speech, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, operates from the recollection of previously experienced objects and from the absence of objects upon awakening. Depravity-conceptualization-attachment-speech, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, operates from the recollection of enmity and deeds done previously. Beginningless-conceptualization-speech, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, operates from the seeds of one's own impressions of the depravity of attachment to beginningless proliferation. This, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the fourfold characteristic of speech-conceptualization that I have stated; this is the reply to that.

body.text: atha khalu mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ punarapi bhagavantametamevārthamadhyeṣate sma - deśayatu me bhagavān punarapi vāgvikalpābhivyaktigocaram / kutra kasmāt kathaṃ kena bhagavan nṛṇāṃ vāgvijñaptivikalpaḥ pravartate? bhagavānāha - śirauronāsākaṇṭhatālvoṣṭhajihvādantasamavāyānmahāmate vāk pravartamānā pravartate / mahāmatirāha - kiṃ punarbhagavan vāg vikalpādanyā uta ananyā? bhagavānāha - na hi mahāmate vāg vikalpādanyā nānanyā / tatkasya hetoḥ? yaduta taddhetūtpattilakṣaṇatvānmahāmate vāgvikalpaḥ pravartate / yadi punarmahāmate vāg vikalpādanyā syāt, avikalpahetukī syāt / athānanyā syāt, arthābhivyaktitvādvāg na kuryāt / sā ca kurute / tasmānnānyā nānanyā //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s> again entreated the Blessed One on this very matter: 'May the Blessed One teach me further the domain of the manifestation of speech-conceptualization. Where, from what, how, and by what, O Blessed One, does the conceptualization of speech-cognition operate in people?' The Blessed One said: 'From the conjunction of head, chest, nose, throat, palate, lips, tongue, and teeth, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, speech operates as it operates.' <s>Mahāmati</s> said: 'Is speech, O Blessed One, other than conceptualization, or not other?' The Blessed One said: 'Speech, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is neither other than conceptualization nor non-other. For what reason? Because speech-conceptualization operates, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, having the characteristic of arising from that cause. If, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, speech were other than conceptualization, it would not have conceptualization as its cause. But if it were non-other, speech would not produce the manifestation of meaning. Yet it does produce [it]. Therefore it is neither other nor non-other.'

body.text: punarapi mahāmatirāha - kiṃ punarbhagavan vacanameva paramārthaḥ, uta yadvacanenābhilapyate sa paramārthaḥ? bhagavānāha - na mahāmate vacanaṃ paramārthaḥ, na ca yadvacanenābhilapyate sa paramārthaḥ / tatkasya hetoḥ? yaduta paramārthāryasukhābhilāpapraveśitvātparamārthasya vacanaṃ na paramārthaḥ / paramārthasyu mahāmate āryajñānapratyātmagatigamyo na vāgvikalpabuddhigocaraḥ / tena vikalpo nodbhāvayati paramārtham / vacanaṃ punarmahāmate utpannapradhvaṃsi capalaṃ parasparapratyayahetusamutpannam / yacca mahāmate parasparapratyayahetusamutpannaṃ tatparamārthaṃ nodbhāvayati / svaparalakṣaṇābhāvānmahāmate bāhyalakṣaṇaṃ nodbhāvayati //
body.translated_text: Again <s>Mahāmati</s> said: 'Is speech itself, O Blessed One, the ultimate reality (<s>paramārtha</s>), or is what is expressed by speech the ultimate reality?' The Blessed One said: 'Speech, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is not the ultimate reality, nor is what is expressed by speech the ultimate reality. For what reason? Because the ultimate reality enters through the noble bliss that is beyond expression, therefore speech is not the ultimate reality. The ultimate reality, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is reached by one's own inner noble knowledge (<s>āryajñāna</s>), not by the domain of the intellect of speech-conceptualization. Therefore conceptualization does not manifest the ultimate reality. Speech, moreover, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is produced and destroyed, unstable, arisen from mutually conditioning causes. And that which, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, arises from mutually conditioning causes does not manifest the ultimate reality. Because of the absence of own- and other-characteristics, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, it does not manifest the external characteristic.'

body.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate svacittadṛśyamātrānusāritvādvividhavicitralakṣaṇabāhyabhāvābhāvādvāgvikalpaḥ paramārthaṃ na vikalpayati / tasmāttarhi mahāmate vāgvicitravikalparahitena te bhavitavyam //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, because [things] follow merely the appearances of one's own mind, and because of the absence of external entities with manifold and varied characteristics, speech-conceptualization does not conceptualize the ultimate reality. Therefore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, you should be free from the manifold conceptualization of speech.

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: On this, it is said:

children.translated_text: All entities are without inherent nature; speech likewise, though [seemingly] real, is unreal;
the childish one, not seeing the meaning of emptiness and non-emptiness, runs about. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.143 ||
The inherent natures of all entities, and speech of people too —
that conceptualization also does not exist; <s>nirvāṇa</s> is like a dream.

children.text: bhavaṃ parīkṣeta na saṃsāre nāpi nirvāyāt // Lank_2.144 //
children.translated_text: One should examine existence — [there is] neither <s>saṃsāra</s> nor would one pass into <s>nirvāṇa</s>. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.144 ||
Just as a king or a merchant, having enticed [his] children with various clay animals

children.text: pralobhya krīḍayitvā ca bhūtān dadyāttato mṛgān // Lank_2.145 //
children.translated_text: and having let them play, would then give them real animals, || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.145 ||
so do I, with the variegated reflections of the characteristics of <s>dharmas</s>,
speak to [my] children of the limit of reality (<s>bhūtakoṭi</s>), [which is] to be realized by oneself. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.146 ||

body.text: atha khalu mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ punarapi bhagavantametadavocat - deśayatu me bhagavān nāstyastitvaikatvānyatvobhayanobhayanaivāstinanāstinityānityavarjitaṃ sarvatīrthyāgatipracāramāryapratyātmajñānagatigamyaṃ parikalpitasvasāmānyalakṣaṇavinivṛttaṃ paramārthatattvāvatāraṃ bhūmyanusaṃdhikramottarottaraviśuddhilakṣaṇaṃ tathāgatabhūmyanupraveśalakṣaṇamanābhogapūrvapraṇidhānaviśvarūpamaṇisadṛśaviṣayānantalakṣaṇapracāraṃ svacittadṛśyagocaragativibhāgalakṣaṇaṃ sarvadharmāṇām / yathā ca ahaṃ ca anye ca bodhisattvā mahāsattvā evamādiṣu parikalpitasvabhāvasvasāmānya lakṣaṇavinivṛttadṛṣṭayaḥ kṣipramanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhya sarvasattvānāṃ sarvaguṇasaṃpattīḥ paripūrayema //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s> again said this to the Blessed One: 'May the Blessed One teach me the entry into the truth of the ultimate reality — free from the [views of] non-existence, existence, oneness, otherness, both, neither, neither-existence-nor-non-existence, and permanence-and-impermanence — beyond the course of all heretics, reached by one's own inner noble knowledge, freed from the imagined own- and general-characteristics, having the characteristic of progressive purification through the stages in sequence, having the characteristic of entry into the <s>Tathāgata</s>-stage, having the course of the infinite characteristics of the domain resembling a wish-fulfilling jewel of universal form through effortless former vows, and having the characteristic of the differentiation of the course of the domain of what is seen by one's own mind — [the entry into the truth of the ultimate reality] of all <s>dharmas</s>. So that I and other <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s>, with views freed from the imagined inherent nature and own- and general-characteristics in such [matters], may quickly realize unsurpassed, perfect awakening and fulfill all the excellent qualities for all beings.'

body.text: bhagavānāha - sādhu sādhu mahāmate, sādhu khalu punastvaṃ mahāmate, yattvametamarthamadhyeṣitavyaṃ manyase / bahujanahitāya tvaṃ mahāmate pratipanno bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāyai mahato janakāyasyārthāya hitāya sukhāya devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca / tena hi mahāmate śṛṇu, sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuru / bhāviṣye 'haṃ te / sādhu bhagavanniti mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavataḥ
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'Well done, well done, <s>Mahāmati</s>! Well done indeed, <s>Mahāmati</s>, that you consider this matter worthy of requesting. You, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, have set forth for the benefit of many, for the happiness of many, out of compassion for the world, for the welfare, benefit, and happiness of the great multitude of beings, of <s>devas</s> and humans. Then, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, listen, and attend well and thoroughly. I shall speak to you.' 'Very well, Blessed One!' — the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s>

body.text:
pratyaśrauṣīt / bhagavāṃstasyaitadavocat - svacittadṛśyamātrānavabodhānmahāmate bālapṛthagjanā bāhyavicitrabhāvābhiniveśena ca nāstyastitvaikatvānyatvobhayanaivāstinanāstinityānityasvabhāvavāsanāhetuvikalpābhiniveśena vikalpayanti / tadyathā mahāmate mṛgatṛṣṇodakaṃ mṛgā udakabhāvena vikalpya grīṣmābhitaptāḥ pātukāmatayā pradhāvanti, svacittadṛṣṭibhrāntyanavabodhānna prajānantinātrodakamiti, evameva mahāmate bālapṛthagjanā anādikālavividhaprapañcavikalpavāsitamatayo rāgadveṣamohāgnitāpitamanaso vicitrarūpaviṣayābhilāṣiṇaḥ utpādabhaṅgasthitidṛṣṭyāśayā ādhyātmikabāhyabhāvābhāvākuśalāḥ / te ekatvānyatvanāstyastitvagrāhe prapatanti / tadyathā mahāmate gandharvanagare 'viduṣāmanagare nagarasaṃjñā bhavati / sā ca nagarākṛtiranādikālanagarabījavāsanābhiniveśātkhyāti / tacca nagaraṃ nānagaraṃ na nagaram / evameva mahāmate anādikālatīrthyapraprañcavādavāsanābhiniviṣṭāḥ ekatvānyatvāstitvanāstitvavādānabhiniviśante svacittadṛśyamātrānavadhāritamatayaḥ / tadyathā mahāmate kaścideva puruṣaḥ śayitaḥ svapnāntare strīpuruṣahastyaśvarathapadātigrāmanagaranigamagomahiṣavanodyānavividhagirinadītaḍāgopaśobhitaṃ janapadamantaḥpuraṃ praviśya prativibudhyeta / sa prativibuddhaḥ saṃstadeva janapadamantaḥpuraṃ samanusmaret / tatkiṃ manyase mahāmate - api nu sa puruṣaḥ paṇḍitajātīyo bhavet, yastadabhūtaṃ svapnavaicitryamanusmaret? āha - no hīdaṃ bhagavan / bhagavānāha - evameva mahāmate bālapṛthagjanāḥ kudṛṣṭidaṣṭāstīrthyamatayaḥ svapnatulyātsvacittadṛśyabhāvānna prativijānante, ekatvānyatvanāstyastitvadṛṣṭiṃ samāśrayante / tadyathā
mahāmate citrakarakṛtapradeśā animnonnatāḥ santo nimnonnatā bālaiḥ kalpyante, evameva mahāmate bhaviṣyantyanāgate 'dhvani tīrthyadṛṣṭivāsanāśayaprativikalpapuṣṭāḥ / te ekatvānyatvobhayānubhayavādābhiniviṣṭāḥ svayaṃ naṣṭā anyānapi sadasatpakṣaviviktānutpādavādino nāstikā iti vakṣyanti / ete hetuphalāpavādino durdarśanonmūlitahetukuśalaśuklapakṣāḥ / ete śreyorthibhirdūrataḥ parivarjyāṃ iti vakṣyante / te ca svaparobhayadṛṣṭipatitāśayā nāstyastitvavikalpasamāropāpavādakudṛṣṭipatitāśayā narakaparāyaṇā bhaviṣyanti / tadyathā mahāmate taimirikāḥ keśoṇḍukaṃ dṛṣṭvā parasparamācakṣate - iadaṃ citramidaṃ citramiti paśyantu bho mārṣāḥ / tacca keśoṇḍukamubhayānutpannatayā na bhāvo nābhāvo darśanādarśanataḥ / evameva mahāmate tīrthyakudṛṣṭivikalpāśayābhiniviṣṭāḥ sadasatpakṣaikatvānyatvobhayānubhayatvavādābhiniviṣṭāḥ saddharmāpavādakā ātmānaṃ parāṃśca vinipātayiṣyanti / tadyathā mahāmate acakramalātacakraṃ bālaiścakrabhāvena parikalpyate na paṇḍitaiḥ, evameva mahāmate kudṛṣṭitīrthyāśayapatitā ekatvānyatvobhayānubhayatvaṃ parikalpayiṣyanti sarvabhāvotpattau / tadyathā mahāmate deve pravarṣati jalabudbudakāḥ sphaṭikamaṇisadṛśāḥ khyāyante / tatra ca bālāḥ sphaṭikamaṇibhāvamabhiniveśya pradhāvanti / te ca mahāmate udakabudbudakā na maṇayo nāmaṇayo grahaṇāgrahaṇataḥ / evameva mahāmate tīrthyadṛṣṭivikalpāśayavāsanāvāsitā asataścotpādaṃ varṇayiṣyanti pratyayaiḥ, sataśca vināśam //
body.translated_text: He assented. The Blessed One said this to him: Because of non-awakening to [the fact that all is] merely the appearance of one's own mind (<s>svacittadṛśyamātra</s>), O <s>Mahāmati</s>, foolish ordinary beings, through attachment to external diverse entities and through attachment to the discrimination of impressions of the inherent nature of non-existence, existence, oneness, otherness, both, neither-existence-nor-non-existence, permanence, and impermanence, conceptually discriminate. Just as, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, deer, scorched by summer heat, conceptualizing mirage-water as having the nature of water, rush [toward it] with the desire to drink, not knowing — because of non-awakening to the confusion of the vision of their own minds — that 'there is no water here'; even so, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, foolish ordinary beings, whose minds are perfumed by the impressions of beginningless diverse proliferative discrimination, whose minds are scorched by the fires of passion, hatred, and delusion, who crave diverse form-objects, who hold the views of arising, breaking apart, and abiding, who are unskilled in the existence and non-existence of internal and external entities — they fall into the grasping of oneness, otherness, non-existence, and existence. Just as, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, in a <s>Gandharva</s>-city (mirage-city), the ignorant have the notion of 'city' where there is no city; and that city-appearance is manifested from attachment to the impressions of beginningless city-seeds; and that city is neither a non-city nor a city; even so, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, those attached to the impressions of the beginningless proliferative speech of heretics embrace doctrines of oneness, otherness, existence, and non-existence, with minds that do not ascertain [that all is] merely the appearance of one's own mind. Just as, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, a certain man, asleep, in a dream enters a country with its inner quarters adorned with women, men, elephants, horses, chariots, foot-soldiers, villages, cities, market-towns, cows, buffaloes, forests, gardens, various mountains, rivers, and ponds — and then awakens. He, upon awakening, would still remember that country with its inner quarters. What do you think, O <s>Mahāmati</s> — would that man be of wise nature, who remembers that unreal dream-diversity? He said: 'No indeed, Blessed One.' The Blessed One said: Even so, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, foolish ordinary beings, bitten by wrong views, holding heretical views, do not discern that entities are mere appearances of one's own mind, like a dream, and take recourse to views of oneness, otherness, non-existence, and existence. Just as, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, painted surfaces, though not depressed or elevated, are conceptualized by the childish as depressed and elevated; even so, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, in the future time there will be those nourished by the discriminations rooted in the impressions of heretical views. They, attached to doctrines of oneness, otherness, both, and neither, ruined themselves, will declare others also — those who teach the non-arising [doctrine], free from the theses of existent and non-existent — to be nihilists. These are deniers of cause and effect, whose wholesome element of right vision has been uprooted by wrong vision. 'These are to be avoided from afar by those who seek welfare' — so it will be said. And they, fallen into the disposition of views of self, other, and both, fallen into the disposition of wrong views of superimposition and denial through discrimination of non-existence and existence, will go to hell. Just as, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, those with diseased eyes (<s>taimirika</s>), seeing a mass of floating hairs, tell each other: 'Look, sirs, how marvelous, how marvelous!' — and that mass of floating hairs, because of its non-arising from both [external reality and mere nothing], is neither an entity nor a non-entity, from the standpoint of seeing and not-seeing; even so, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, those attached to the dispositions of heretical wrong-view discriminations, attached to doctrines of oneness, otherness, both, and neither from the standpoint of the theses of existent and non-existent, will disparage the true <s>Dharma</s> and cause themselves and others to fall. Just as, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the circle of a whirling firebrand is conceptualized by the childish as having the nature of a [real] circle, but not by the wise; even so, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, those fallen into the disposition of heretical wrong views will conceptualize oneness, otherness, both, and neither regarding the arising of all entities.
