Just as, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, when it rains, water-bubbles appear resembling crystal gems — and therein the childish, projecting the notion of crystal gems, run [toward them]; and those water-bubbles, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, are neither gems nor non-gems, from the standpoint of grasping and non-grasping; even so, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, those perfumed by the impressions of heretical-view discriminations will describe the arising of the non-existent through conditions, and the destruction of the existent.

body.text:
punaraparaṃ mahāmate pramāṇatrayāvayavapratyavasthānaṃ kṛtvā āryajñānapratyātmādhigamyaṃ svabhāvadvayavinirmuktaṃ vastu svabhāvato vidyata iti vikalpayiṣyanti / na ca mahāmate cittamano manovijñānacittaparāvṛttyāśrayāṇāṃ svacittadṛśyagrāhyagrāhakavikalpaprahīṇānāṃ tathāgatabhūmipratyātmāryajñānagatānāṃ yogināṃ bhāvābhāvasaṃjñā pravartate / yadi punarmahāmate yogināmevaṃgativiṣayāṇāṃ bhāvābhāvagrāhaḥ pravartate, sa evaiṣāmātmagrāhaḥ poṣagrāhaḥ puruṣagrāhaḥ pudgalagrāhaḥ syāt / yā punarevaṃ mahāmate bhāvasvabhāvasvasāmānyalakṣaṇadeśanā, eṣā mahāmate nairmāṇikabuddhadeśanāḥ na dharmatābuddhadeśanā / deśanā punarmahāmate bālaśayagatadṛṣṭipravṛttā, na ca pratyavasthānagatisvabhāvadharmāryajñānapratyātmādhigamasamādhisukhavihāramudbhāvayati / tadyathā mahāmate jalāntargatā vṛkṣacchāyā khyāyate / sā ca na cchāyā nācchāyā vṛkṣasaṃsthānāsaṃsthānataḥ, evameva mahāmate tīrthyadṛṣṭivāsanāvāsitavikalpā ekatvānyatvobhayatvānubhayatvanāstyastitvaṃ vikalpayiṣyanti svacittadṛśyamātrānavadhāritamatayaḥ / tadyathā mahāmate darpaṇāntargatāni sarvarūpapratibimbakāni khyāyante yathāpratyayataḥ svavikalpanācca, na tāni bimbāni nābimbāni bimbābimbadarśanataḥ / atha ca te mahāmate svacittadṛśyavikalpāḥ khyāyante bālānāṃ bimbākṛtayaḥ / evameva mahāmate svacittapratibimbāni khyāyante ekatvānyatvobhayānubhayadṛṣṭyākāreṇa / tadyathā mahāmate pratiśrutkā puruṣanadīpavanasaṃyogātpravartamānā anuśrūyate / sā ca na bhāvā nābhāvā ghoṣāghoṣaśravaṇataḥ, evameva mahāmate nāstyastitvaikatvānyatvobhayanobhayadṛṣṭisvacittavāsanāvikalpāḥ khyāyante / tadyathā mahāmate nistṛṇagulmalatāvanāyāṃ medinyāmādityasaṃyogānmṛgatṛṣṇikāstaraṃgavatsyandante / te ca na bhāvā nābhāvā lobhyālobhyataḥ / evameva mahāmate bālānāmanādikālaprapañcadauṣṭhulyavāsanāvāsitaṃ vikalpavijñānamutpādasthitibhaṅgaikatvānyatvobhayānubhayanāstyastyāryapratyātmajñānavastumukhena mṛgatṛṣṇikāvattaraṃgāyate
/ tadyathā mahāmate vetālayantrapuruṣau niḥsattvau piśācayuktigātspandanakriyāṃ kurvāte / tatra ca asadvikalpe bālā abhiniviśante gamanāgamanataḥ / evameva mahāmate bālapṛthagjanāḥ kudṛṣṭitīrthyāśayapatitā ekatvānyatvavādānabhiniviśante / sa ca asadbhūtasamāropaḥ / tasmāttarhi mahāmate utpādasthitibhaṅgaikatvānyatvobhayānubhayanāstyastyāryapratyātmavastvadhigamavikalparahitena bhavitavyam //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, taking their stand on the three means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇatraya</s>) and their components, they will conceptualize: 'That reality which is free from the duality of inherent nature and is the domain of inner noble knowledge — it exists by its own nature.' But, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, for yogins who have reached the <s>Tathāgata</s>-stage through the inner noble knowledge of one's own realization, whose supports of mind, <s>manas</s>, <s>manovijñāna</s>, and the turning-about of the mind (<s>cittaparāvṛtti</s>) [have been transformed], who have abandoned the discrimination of grasper and grasped in the appearances of their own mind — for them no notion of existence or non-existence operates. If, however, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, for yogins of such course and domain, a grasping of existence and non-existence were to operate, that very grasping would be their grasping of self, grasping of nourisher, grasping of spirit (<s>puruṣa</s>), grasping of individual (<s>pudgala</s>). That teaching, moreover, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, which teaches the inherent nature and the specific and general characteristics of entities — this, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the teaching of the <s>Nairmāṇika-Buddha</s> (transformation-Buddha), not of the <s>Dharmatā-Buddha</s> (nature-Buddha). Teaching, moreover, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, operates in accordance with the dispositions and views of the childish, and does not bring forth the blissful abode of the <s>samādhi</s> of the inner noble-knowledge-realization regarding the inherent nature of the <s>dharma</s> of the course of establishment. Just as, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the reflection of a tree appears inside water — it is neither a reflection nor a non-reflection, from the standpoint of the configuration and non-configuration of the tree; even so, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, those perfumed by the discriminative impressions of heretical views since beginningless time will conceptualize oneness, otherness, both, neither, non-existence, and existence, with minds that do not ascertain [that all is] merely the appearance of one's own mind. Just as, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, reflections of all forms within a mirror appear according to conditions and one's own discrimination — and those reflections are neither images nor non-images, from the standpoint of seeing images and non-images; and yet, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, those discriminations of the appearances of one's own mind appear to the childish as having the form of images; even so, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the reflections of one's own mind appear in the aspect of views of oneness, otherness, both, and neither. Just as, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, an echo, proceeding from the conjunction of a person, a river, and wind, is heard — and it is neither an entity nor a non-entity, from the standpoint of hearing sound and non-sound; even so, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the discriminations of impressions of one's own mind with views of non-existence, existence, oneness, otherness, both, and neither appear. Just as, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, on ground devoid of grass, shrubs, creepers, and trees, from conjunction with the sun, mirages stream like waves — and they are neither entities nor non-entities, from the standpoint of being desirable and undesirable; even so, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the discriminating consciousness of the childish, perfumed by the depravity-impressions of beginningless proliferation, undulates like the waves of a mirage through [the discriminations of] arising, abiding, breaking apart, oneness, otherness, both, and neither, non-existence and existence — [all being merely] the gateway of noble inner knowledge of one's own realization. Just as, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, a zombie-puppet automaton, being soulless, performs movements and actions through the device of a <s>piśāca</s> (demon) — and therein the childish attach themselves to the unreal discrimination based on its going and coming; even so, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, foolish ordinary beings, fallen into the disposition of heretical wrong views, attach themselves to doctrines of oneness and otherness. And that is the superimposition of the unreal. Therefore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, one must be free from the discrimination of arising, abiding, and breaking apart — oneness, otherness, both, neither, non-existence and existence — [which constitutes] the realization of noble inner truth.

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Therein this is said:

children.translated_text: Like the reflection of a tree in water, the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) with consciousness as the fifth;
like illusion and dream — through cognition (<s>vijñapti</s>), do not conceptually discriminate! [Laṅk 2.147]
This [world] resembles a mass of floating hairs, confused like mirage-water;
the three realms, called dream and illusion — contemplating thus, one is liberated. [Laṅk 2.148]
Just as a mirage in summer shimmers, deluding the mind,

children.text: mṛgā gṛhṇanti pānīyaṃ na cāsyāṃ vastu vidyate // Lank_2.149 //
children.translated_text: deer grasp it as water, yet nothing real exists therein. [Laṅk 2.149]
So too the seed of consciousness shimmers in the domain of views;

children.text: bālā gṛhṇanti jāyantaṃ timiraṃ taimirā yathā // Lank_2.150 //
children.translated_text: the childish grasp what arises, like those with cataracts [grasp] floaters. [Laṅk 2.150]
In the beginningless course of <s>saṃsāra</s>, embraced by the grasping of entities,

children.text: bālaḥ kīle yathā kīlaṃ pralobhya vinivartayet // Lank_2.151 //
children.translated_text: the fool, like one [driving out] a peg with a peg, enticingly turns away. [Laṅk 2.151]
Resembling illusion, zombie-puppets, dreams, lightning, and clouds — always
cut off by the three continuities — seeing the world [thus], one is liberated. [Laṅk 2.152]
For there is no cognition (<s>vijñapti</s>) here at all, like mirages in the sky;

children.text: evaṃ dharmān vijānanto na kiṃcitpratijānate // Lank_2.153 //
children.translated_text: knowing <s>dharmas</s> thus, one asserts nothing. [Laṅk 2.153]
This cognition is name-only; it does not exist by [its own] characteristics;

children.text: skandhāḥ keśoṇḍukākārā yatra cāsau vikalpyate // Lank_2.154 //
children.translated_text: the <s>skandhas</s> have the form of floating hairs — where that [cognition too] is conceptually discriminated. [Laṅk 2.154]

children.text: cittaṃ keśoṇḍukaṃ māyāṃ svapna gandharvameva ca /
children.translated_text: Mind is [like] floating hairs, illusion, dream, <s>Gandharva</s>[-city],

children.text: alātaṃ mṛgatṛṣṇā ca asantaḥ khyāti vai nṛṇām // Lank_2.155 //
children.translated_text: firebrand-[circle], and mirage — non-existent, yet appearing to humans. [Laṅk 2.155]
Permanent and impermanent, likewise oneness, both, and neither —
bound by beginningless faults, the deluded childish conceptualize. [Laṅk 2.156]

children.text: darpaṇe udake netre bhāṇḍeṣu ca maṇīṣu ca /
children.translated_text: In a mirror, in water, in the eye, in vessels, and in gems,

children.text: bimbaṃ hi dṛśyate teṣu bimbaṃ nāsti ca kutracid // Lank_2.157 //
children.translated_text: a reflection is indeed seen in them, yet the reflection does not exist anywhere [in them]. [Laṅk 2.157]

children.text: bhāvābhāsaṃ tathā cittaṃ mṛgatṛṣṇā yathā nabhe /
children.translated_text: So too mind [merely] reflects entities, like a mirage in the sky;

children.text: dṛśyate citrarūpeṇa svapne vandhyauraso yathā // Lank_2.158 //
children.translated_text: it is seen with diverse forms, like the son of a barren woman in a dream. [Laṅk 2.158]

body.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate catuṣṭayavinirmuktā tathāgatānāṃ dharmadeśanā, yaduta ekatvānyatvobhayānubhayapakṣavivarjitā nāstyastisamāropāpavādavinirmuktā / asatyapratītyasamutpādanirodhamārgavimokṣapravṛttipūrvakā mahāmate tathāgatānāṃ dharmadeśanā / na prakṛtīśvarahetuyadṛcchāṇukālasvabhāvopanibaddhā mahāmate tathāgatānāṃ dharmadeśanā //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>-teaching of the <s>Tathāgatas</s> is free from the fourfold [proposition] — namely, free from the theses of oneness, otherness, both, and neither, free from the superimposition and denial of non-existence and existence. The <s>Dharma</s>-teaching of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is preceded by the operation of the unreal dependent co-arising (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>), cessation, path, and liberation. The <s>Dharma</s>-teaching of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is not bound to [doctrines of] primal matter (<s>Prakṛti</s>), God (<s>Īśvara</s>), causation, chance, atoms (<s>aṇu</s>), time (<s>kāla</s>), or inherent nature (<s>svabhāva</s>).

body.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate kleśajñeyāvaraṇadvayaviśuddhyarthaṃ sārthavāhavadānupūrvyā aṣṭottare nirābhāsapadaśate pratiṣṭhāpayanti yānabhūmyaṅgasuvibhāgalakṣaṇe ca //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, for the purpose of purification from the two obscurations — the obscuration of afflictions (<s>kleśāvaraṇa</s>) and the obscuration of the knowable (<s>jñeyāvaraṇa</s>) — [the <s>Tathāgatas</s>], like caravan-leaders, gradually establish [beings] in the one hundred and eight imageless terms, and in the well-differentiated characteristics of vehicles, stages, and factors.

body.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate caturvidhaṃ dhyānam / katamaccaturvidham? yaduta bālopacārikaṃ dhyānam, arthapravicayaṃ dhyānam, tathatālambanaṃ dhyānam, tāthāgataṃ caturthaṃ dhyānam / tatra mahāmate bālopacārikaṃ dhyānaṃ katamat? yaduta śrāvakapratyekabuddhayogayogināṃ pudgalanairātmyabhāvasvasāmānyabimbasaṃkalānityaduḥkhāśubhalakṣaṇābhiniveśapūrvakam, evamidaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ nānyatheti
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) is of four kinds. Of which four kinds? Namely: the <s>dhyāna</s> practiced by the childish (<s>bālopacārika</s>), the <s>dhyāna</s> of investigation of meaning (<s>arthapravicaya</s>), the <s>dhyāna</s> with <s>Suchness</s> as its object (<s>tathatālambana</s>), and the fourth — the <s>Tathāgata</s>-<s>dhyāna</s>. Therein, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, what is the <s>dhyāna</s> practiced by the childish? Namely, that of the yogins of the <s>Śrāvaka</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> vehicles, preceded by attachment to the characteristics of the selflessness of the person, the specific and general image of entity, and impermanence, suffering, and impurity — [thinking] 'This is just the characteristic, not otherwise,'

body.text: paśyataḥ pūrvottarottarata ā saṃjñānirodhādbālopacārikaṃ bhavati / tatra arthapravicayadhyānaṃ punarmahāmate katamat? yaduta pudgalanairātmyasvasāmānyalakṣaṇabāhyatīrthakarasvaparobhayābhāvaṃ kṛtvā dharmanairātmyabhūmilakṣaṇārthaṃ pravicayānupūrvakamarthapravicayadhyānaṃ bhavati / tatra tathatālambanaṃ dhyānaṃ mahāmate katamat? yaduta parikalpitanairātmyadvayavikalpayathābhūtāvasthānādapravṛttervikalpasya tathatālambanamiti vadāmi / tāthāgataṃ punarmahāmate dhyānaṃ katamat? yaduta tāthāgatabhūmyākārapraveśaṃ pratyātmāryajñānalakṣaṇatrayasukhavihārācintyasattvakṛtyakaraṇatayā tāthāgataṃ dhyānamiti vadāmi //
body.translated_text: seeing thus, progressively from the earlier to later [stages], up to the cessation of perception (<s>saṃjñānirodha</s>) — this is the [<s>dhyāna</s>] practiced by the childish. Therein, what is the <s>dhyāna</s> of investigation of meaning, O <s>Mahāmati</s>? Namely, having established the absence of self and other, and both, regarding the specific and general characteristics of the selflessness of the person and [the absence of] external heretical teachers, [one proceeds] through progressive investigation of the meaning of the characteristics of the stages of the selflessness of <s>dharmas</s> — this is the <s>dhyāna</s> of investigation of meaning. Therein, what is the <s>dhyāna</s> with <s>Suchness</s> as its object, O <s>Mahāmati</s>? Namely, since through the true realization of the twofold selflessness that is imagined, discrimination does not operate, I call [this] 'having <s>Suchness</s> (<s>tathatā</s>) as its object.' The <s>Tathāgata</s>-<s>dhyāna</s>, moreover, O <s>Mahāmati</s> — what is it? Namely, having entered the form of the <s>Tathāgata</s>-stage, through the blissful abode of the threefold characteristic of inner noble knowledge of one's own realization, and through the accomplishing of inconceivable deeds for beings — I call [this] the <s>Tathāgata</s>-<s>dhyāna</s>.

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Therein this is said:

children.translated_text: The <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) of investigation of meaning; the <s>dhyāna</s> practiced by the childish;

children.text: tathatālambanaṃ dhyānaṃ dhyānaṃ tāthāgataṃ śubham // Lank_2.159 //
children.translated_text: the <s>dhyāna</s> with <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) as its object; the auspicious <s>Tathāgata</s>-<s>dhyāna</s>. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.159 ||
Having the form of the moon and sun, resembling a lotus and the netherworld,
resembling space, fire, and a painting — the <s>yogin</s>, while practicing, sees [these]. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.160 ||

children.text: nimittāni ca citrāṇi tīrthamārgaṃ nayanti te /
children.translated_text: And these varied signs lead to the path of the non-Buddhist teachers;
they cause one to fall into the state of a <s>Śrāvaka</s>, into the domain of the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.161 ||
Having dispelled all these, when one becomes appearance-free (<s>nirābhāsa</s>),
then the <s>Buddha</s>-sun-like ones from all fields arrive,

children.text: śiro hi tasya mārjanti nimittaṃ tathatānugam // Lank_2.162 //
children.translated_text: and they anoint his head with the sign that accords with <s>Suchness</s> (<s>tathatā</s>). || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.162 ||

body.text: atha khalu mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ punarapi bhagavantametadavocat - nirvāṇaṃ nirvāṇamiti bhagavannucyate / kasyaitadbhagavannadhivacanaṃ yaduta nirvāṇamiti ? bhagavānāha - sarvavijñānasvabhāvavāsanālayamanomanovijñānadṛṣṭivāsanāparāvṛttirnirvāṇamityucyate sarvabuddhairmayā ca nirvāṇagatisvabhāvaśūnyatāvastugocaram //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s> again said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: '<s>Nirvāṇa</s>, <s>nirvāṇa</s>' — thus, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, it is spoken of. Of what, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, is this a designation — namely '<s>nirvāṇa</s>'? The <s>Bhagavān</s> replied: The turning-back (<s>parāvṛtti</s>) of the impressions of the view of mind (<s>manas</s>) and <s>manovijñāna</s> (mind-consciousness) [stored] in the <s>ālaya</s> (store[-consciousness]) of the impressions of the inherent nature of all <s>vijñānas</s> — that is called <s>nirvāṇa</s> by all <s>Buddhas</s> and by me, having emptiness of inherent nature as its domain and <s>nirvāṇa</s>-course as its object.

body.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate nirvāṇamāryajñānapratyātmagatigocaraṃ śāśvatocchedavikalpabhāvābhāvavivarjitam / kathaṃ na śāśvatam? yaduta svasāmānyalakṣaṇavikalpaprahīṇam, ato na śāśvatam / tatrānucchedo yaduta sarvārthā atītānāgatapratyutpannāḥ pratyātmamapi gacchanti, ato nocchedaḥ //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, <s>nirvāṇa</s> has the domain of inner noble knowledge-realization (<s>āryajñānapratyātmagati</s>), and is free from the conceptual discrimination of eternalism and annihilationism, existence and non-existence. How is it not eternal? Because the conceptual discrimination of specific and general characteristics has been abandoned — therefore it is not eternal. Therein, [how is there] non-annihilation? Because all objects — past, future, and present — also proceed to the inner self — therefore there is no annihilation.

body.text: punarmahāmate mahāparinirvāṇaṃ na nāśo na maraṇam / yadi punarmahāmate mahāparinirvāṇaṃ maraṇaṃ syāt, punarapi janmaprabandhaḥ syāt / atha vināśaḥ syāt, saṃskṛtalakṣaṇapatitaṃ syāt / ata etasmātkāraṇānmahāmate mahāparinirvāṇaṃ na nāśaṃ na maraṇam / cyutivigataṃ maraṇamadhigacchanti yoginaḥ / punaraparaṃ mahāmate mahāparinirvāṇamaprahīṇāsaṃprāptito 'nucchedāśāśvatato naikārthato nānārthato nirvāṇamityucyate //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, <s>mahāparinirvāṇa</s> (great final cessation) is neither destruction nor death. If, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, <s>mahāparinirvāṇa</s> were death, there would again be the continuum of birth. If it were destruction, it would fall into the characteristic of the conditioned (<s>saṃskṛta</s>). Therefore, for this reason, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, <s>mahāparinirvāṇa</s> is neither destruction nor death. <s>Yogins</s> attain death that is free from falling away (<s>cyuti</s>). Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, <s>mahāparinirvāṇa</s> is called <s>nirvāṇa</s> because it is neither abandoned nor attained, neither annihilation nor eternity, neither one meaning nor different meanings.

body.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate śrāvakapratyekabuddhānāṃ nirvāṇaṃ svasāmānyalakṣaṇāvabodhādasaṃsargataḥ / viṣayāviparyāsadarśanādvikalpo na pravartate / tatasteṣāṃ tatra nirvāṇabuddhirbhavati //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the <s>nirvāṇa</s> of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> arises from the awakening to specific and general characteristics, and from non-association. Because they see the objects without distortion, conceptual discrimination does not operate. From that, their understanding of <s>nirvāṇa</s> arises therein.

body.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate dviprakāraṃ svabhāvadvayalakṣaṇaṃ bhavati / katamat dviprakāram? yaduta abhilāpasvabhāvābhiniveśataśca vastusvabhāvābhiniveśataśca / tatra mahāmate abhilāpasvabhāvābhiniveśo 'nādikālavākprapañcavāsanābhiniveśātpravartate / tatra vastusvabhāvābhiniveśaḥ punarmahāmate svacittadṛśyamātrānavabodhātpravartate //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the characteristic of the twofold inherent nature is of two kinds. What two kinds? Namely, from the attachment to the inherent nature of designation (<s>abhilāpa</s>), and from the attachment to the inherent nature of objects (<s>vastu</s>). Therein, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the attachment to the inherent nature of designation proceeds from the attachment to the impressions of beginningless verbal proliferation (<s>vākprapañca</s>). Therein, the attachment to the inherent nature of objects, moreover, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, proceeds from the non-awakening to [the truth that all is] merely the appearance of one's own mind.

body.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate adhiṣṭhānadvayādhiṣṭhitā bodhisattvāstathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ caraṇayornipatya praśnān paripṛcchanti / katamenādhiṣṭhānadvayenādhiṣṭhitāḥ? yaduta samādhisamāpattyadhiṣṭhānena sarvakāyamukhapāṇyabhiṣekādhiṣṭhānena ca / tatra mahāmate bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ prathamāyāṃ bhūmau buddhādhiṣṭhānādhiṣṭhitā mahāyānaprabhāsaṃ nāma bodhisattvasamādhiṃ samāpadyante / samanantarasamāpannānāṃ ca teṣāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ mahāyānaprabhāsaṃ bodhisattvasamādhim, atha daśadiglokadhātuvyavasthitāstathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā mukhānyupadarśya sarvakāyamukhavācāsaṃdarśanenādhiṣṭhānaṃ kurvanti / yathā mahāmate vajragarbhasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya anyeṣāṃ ca tādṛglakṣaṇaguṇasamanvāgatānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānām, evaṃ mahāmate prathamāyāṃ bhūmau bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ samādhisamāpattyadhiṣṭhānaṃ pratilabhante / kalpaśatasahasraṃ saṃcitaiḥ kuśalamūlairanupūrveṇa bhūmipakṣavipakṣalakṣaṇagatiṃgatāṃ dharmameghāyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau mahāpadmavimānāsanasthasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya tadanurūpairbodhisattvairmahāsattvaiḥ parivṛtasya sarvaratnābharaṇavibhūṣitakirīṭasya haritālakanakacampakacandrāṃśumayūkhapadmasadṛśā daśadiglokadhātvāgatā jinakarāstasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya padmavimānāsanasthasya mūrdhanyabhiṣiñcanti vaśavarticakravartīndrarājavatsarvakāyamukhapāṇyabhiṣekena / sa ca bodhisattvaste ca bodhisattvāḥ pāṇyabhiṣekādhiṣṭhānādhiṣṭhitā ityucyante / etanmahāmate bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāmadhiṣṭhānadvayam, yenādhiṣṭhānadvayenādhiṣṭhitā bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ sarvabuddhamukhānyavalokayanti / anyatrāvyavalokyāstathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s> empowered by the twofold empowerment (<s>adhiṣṭhāna</s>) of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly awakened ones, fall at their feet and ask questions. By which twofold empowerment are they empowered? Namely, by the empowerment of <s>samādhi</s>-attainment, and by the empowerment of the anointing of the entire body, face, and hands. Therein, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas</s>, at the first stage (<s>bhūmi</s>), empowered by the empowerment of the <s>Buddhas</s>, enter the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhi</s> called 'Radiance of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>.' Immediately upon those <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas</s> entering the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>samādhi</s> 'Radiance of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>,' the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly awakened ones, established throughout the world-realms of the ten directions, showing their faces, perform the empowerment by the display of the entire body, face, and speech. Just as, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, [it was] for the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Vajragarbha</s> and for other <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas</s> endowed with similar characteristics and qualities — thus, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, at the first stage, <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas</s> obtain the empowerment of <s>samādhi</s>-attainment. Having accumulated wholesome roots over hundreds of thousands of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons), having progressively entered the course of the characteristics of the favorable and unfavorable [factors] of the stages, at the <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage of the <s>Dharma</s>-Cloud (<s>Dharmameghā</s>), the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>, seated on a great lotus-mansion, surrounded by similar <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas</s>, adorned with crowns of all jeweled ornaments — the hands of the <s>Jinas</s> (Conquerors), arriving from the world-realms of the ten directions, resembling <s>Harītāla</s>-gold-<s>Campaka</s>-moonbeam rays and lotuses, anoint the head of that <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> seated on the lotus-mansion, with the anointing of the entire body, face, and hands, like a sovereign emperor (<s>Cakravartin</s>) king of kings. That <s>Bodhisattva</s> and those [anointing] <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are said to be empowered by the empowerment of hand-anointing. This, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the twofold empowerment of <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas</s>, by which twofold empowerment, being empowered, <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas</s> behold the faces of all <s>Buddhas</s>. Otherwise, the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly awakened ones, are not to be beheld.

body.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate yatkiṃcidbodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ pratibhāti samādhyṛddhideśanākāreṇa, tatsarvabuddhādhiṣṭhānadvayādhiṣṭhitānām / yadi punarmahāmate bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāmadhiṣṭhānamantareṇa pratibhānaṃ pratibhāyāt, bālapṛthagjanānāmapi mahāmate pratibhānaṃ pratibhāyāt / tatkasya hetoḥ? yaduta adhiṣṭhānānadhiṣṭhitatvāt / tṛṇagulmavṛkṣaparvatā api mahāmate vividhāni ca vādyabhāṇḍāni nagarabhavanagṛhavimānāsanasthānāni tathāgatapraveśādhiṣṭhānena pravādyante / kiṃ punarmahāmate sacetanā mūkāndhabadhirā api mahāmate svadoṣebhyo vimucyante / evaṃ mahāguṇaviśeṣaṃ mahāmate tathāgatādhiṣṭhānam //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, whatever appears to <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas</s> in the form of <s>samādhi</s>, miraculous power, and teaching — all that belongs to those empowered by the twofold empowerment of all <s>Buddhas</s>. If, moreover, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the inspiration of <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas</s> were to arise without empowerment, then, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the inspiration of foolish ordinary beings would also arise. For what reason? Because of not being empowered by empowerment. Even grasses, shrubs, trees, and mountains, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, and various musical instruments, city-dwellings, house-mansions, and seats — through the empowerment of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s entry, [they all] resound. How much more, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, sentient beings! Even the mute, blind, and deaf, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, are freed from their own defects. Such, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s empowerment of great quality and distinction.

body.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmatirāha - kiṃ punarbhagavaṃstathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ samādhisamāpattyavasthānakāle viśeṣabhūmau ca abhiṣekādhiṣṭhānaṃ prakurvanti?
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Mahāmati</s> asked: Why, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, do the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly awakened ones, perform the empowerment of anointing for <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas</s> at the time of their abiding in <s>samādhi</s>-attainment and at the special stages?

body.text: bhagavānāha - mārakarmakleśaviyuktārthaṃ śrāvakadhyānabhūmyaprapatanatayā ca tathāgatabhūmipratyātmādhigamanatayā ca prāptadharmādhigamavivṛddhaye ca / etena mahāmate kāraṇena tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāmadhiṣṭhānairadhitiṣṭhanti / anadhiṣṭhitāśca mahāmate bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ kutīrthyaśrāvakamārāśayapatitā nānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeran / atastena kāraṇena bodhisattvā mahāsattvāstathāgatairarhadbhiḥ samyaksaṃbuddhairanugṛhyante //
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: For the purpose of freedom from the work of <s>Māra</s> and afflictions, for the sake of not falling into the stage of <s>Śrāvaka</s> <s>dhyāna</s>, for the attainment of inner <s>Tathāgata</s>-stage realization, and for the growth of the attained <s>Dharma</s>-realization. For this reason, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly awakened ones, empower <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas</s> with their empowerments. And <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas</s> without empowerment, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, having fallen into the disposition of non-Buddhist teachers, <s>Śrāvakas</s>, and <s>Māra</s>, would not awaken to unsurpassed perfect enlightenment. For this reason, <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas</s> are favored by the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly awakened ones.

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Therein it is said:

children.translated_text: The empowerment of the lords of men, purified by [their] vows,
the anointing, <s>samādhi</s>, and so forth — from the first [stage] through the tenth. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.163 ||

body.text: atha khalu mahāmatirbodhisattvaḥ punarapi bhagavantametadavocat - pratītyasamutpādaṃ punarbhagavatā deśayatā kāraṇavyapadeśa eva kṛto na svanayaprakṛtyavasthānakathā / tīrthakarā api bhagavan kāraṇata utpattiṃ varṇayanti, yaduta pradhāneśvarapuruṣakālāṇupratyayebhyo bhāvānāmutpattayaḥ / kiṃ tu bhagavatā pratyayaparyāyāntareṇotpattirvarṇyate bhāvānām / na ca siddhāntaviśeṣāntaram / sadasato hi bhagavaṃstīrthakarā apyutpattiṃ varṇayanti, bhūtvā ca vināśaṃ pratyayairbhāvānām / yadapyuktaṃ bhagavatā - avidyāpratyayāḥ saṃskārā yāvajjarāmaraṇamiti, ahetuvādavyapadeśa eṣa bhagavatānuvarṇitaḥ, na sa hetuvādaḥ / yugapadvayavasthitānāṃ bhagavannetadbhavati - asmin satīdaṃ bhavatīti, na kramavṛttyapekṣāvasthitānām / kiṃ tu tīrthakaravyapadeśa eva bhagavan viśiṣyate na tvadīyam / tatkasya hetoḥ? tīrthakarāṇāṃ hiṃ bhagavan kāraṇamapratītyasamutpannaṃ kāryamabhinirvartayati / tava tu bhagavan kāraṇamapi kāryāpekṣaṃ kāryamapi kāraṇāpekṣam / hetupratyayasaṃkaraśca evamanyonyānavasthā prasajyate / ahetutvaṃ ca bhagavan lokasya - asmin satīdaṃ bruvataḥ / bhagavānāha - na mahāmate mamāhetukakāraṇavādo hetupratyayasaṃkaraśca prasajyate - asmin satīdaṃ bruvataḥ, grāhyagrāhakābhāvāt, svacittadṛśyamātrāvabodhāt / ye tu mahāmate grāhyagrāhakābhiniviṣṭāḥ svacittadṛśyamātraṃ nāvabudhyante bāhyasvaviṣayabhāvābhāvatvena, teṣāṃ mahāmate eṣa doṣaḥ prasajyate , na tu mama pratītyakāraṇavyapadeśaṃ kurvataḥ //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s> again said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: In teaching dependent co-arising (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>), the <s>Bhagavān</s> has made merely a designation of causation, not a discourse on the abiding in the essential nature of one's own doctrine. The non-Buddhist teachers too, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, describe arising from causes — namely, the arising of entities from <s>Pradhāna</s> (primal matter), <s>Īśvara</s> (lord), <s>Puruṣa</s> (spirit), time, atoms, and conditions. But you, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, describe the arising of entities merely by a different expression for conditions. There is no doctrinal difference. For, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, the non-Buddhist teachers too describe the arising of entities from the existent and non-existent, and their destruction by conditions after having existed. What the <s>Bhagavān</s> has also stated — 'conditioned by ignorance are the formations (<s>saṃskāras</s>), up to old age and death' — this is a designation of non-causation described by the <s>Bhagavān</s>, not a doctrine of causation. For those established simultaneously, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, this does not apply — 'when this exists, that comes to be' — it does not apply to those established in sequential occurrence. Rather, the designation of the non-Buddhist teachers, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, is superior, not yours. For what reason? Because, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, for the non-Buddhist teachers the cause produces the effect without being dependently arisen. But for you, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, the cause too depends on the effect, and the effect depends on the cause. And thus a confusion of cause and condition, and mutual infinite regress, would follow. And it would be [a doctrine of] causelessness for the world, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, for one who says 'when this exists, that [comes to be].' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: No, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, for one who says 'when this exists, that [comes to be],' neither a doctrine of causelessness nor a confusion of cause and condition follows — because of the absence of grasper and grasped, and because of the awakening to [the truth that all is] merely the appearance of one's own mind. Those, however, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, who are attached to grasper and grasped and do not awaken to [the truth of] the mere appearance of one's own mind, [taking things] as external objects existing or not existing — for them, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, this fault follows; not for me, who makes the designation of dependent causation.

body.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmatirāha - nanu bhagavan abhilāpasadbhāvātsanti sarvabhāvāḥ / yadi punarbhagavan bhāvā na syuḥ, abhilāpo na pravartate / pravartate ca / tasmādabhilāpasadbhāvādbhagavan santi sarvabhāvāḥ / bhagavānāha - asatāmapi mahāmate bhāvānāmabhilāpaḥ kriyate / yaduta śaśaviṣāṇakūrmaromavandhyāputrādīnāṃ loke dṛṣṭo 'bhilāpaḥ / te ca mahāmate na bhāvā nābhāvāḥ, abhilapyante ca / tadyadavocastvaṃ mahāmate - abhilāpasadbhāvātsanti sarvabhāvā iti, sa hi vādaḥ prahīṇaḥ / na ca mahāmate sarvabuddhakṣetreṣu prasiddho 'bhilāpaḥ / abhilāpo mahāmate kṛtakaḥ / kvacinmahāmate buddhakṣetre 'nimiṣaprekṣayā dharmo deśyate, kvacidiṅgitaiḥ, kvacidbhūvikṣepeṇa, kvacinnetrasaṃcāreṇa, kvacidāsyena, kvacidvijṛmbhitena, kvacidutkāsanaśabdena,
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Mahāmati</s> said: Is it not so, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, that because of the real existence of designation (<s>abhilāpa</s>), all entities exist? For if, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, entities did not exist, designation would not operate. But it does operate. Therefore, because of the real existence of designation, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, all entities exist. The <s>Bhagavān</s> replied: Even of non-existent entities, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, designation is made — namely, of a hare's horn, a tortoise's hair, a barren woman's son, and the like — designation is observed in the world. And those, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, are neither entities nor non-entities, yet they are designated. Therefore, your assertion, O <s>Mahāmati</s> — 'because of the real existence of designation, all entities exist' — that argument is refuted. And, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, designation is not established in all <s>Buddha</s>-fields. Designation, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is constructed. In some <s>Buddha</s>-fields, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the <s>Dharma</s> is taught by unblinking gaze; in some by gestures; in some by frowning; in some by movement of the eyes; in some by the mouth; in some by yawning; in some by the sound of clearing the throat;

body.text: kvacitkṣetrasmṛtyā, kvacitspanditena / yathā mahāmate animiṣāyāṃ gandhasugandhāyāṃ ca lokadhātau samantabhadrasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya buddhakṣetre animiṣairnetraiḥ prekṣamāṇāste bodhisattvā mahāsattvā anutpattikadharmakṣāntiṃ pratilabhante anyāṃśca samādhiviśeṣān, ata evāsmātkāraṇānmahāmate nābhilāpasadbhāvātsanti sarvabhāvāḥ / dṛṣṭaṃ caitanmahāmate / iha loke kṛmimakṣikaivamādyāḥ sattvaviśeṣā anabhilāpenaiva svakṛtyaṃ kurvanti //
body.translated_text: in some by the memory of a field; in some by trembling. Just as, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, in the world-realm of <s>Animiṣā</s> (<s>Unblinking</s>) and <s>Gandhasugandha</s> (<s>Fragrant Perfume</s>), in the <s>Buddha</s>-field of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Arhat</s> perfectly awakened <s>Samantabhadra</s>, those <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas</s>, gazing with unblinking eyes, attain the acceptance of the non-arising of phenomena (<s>anutpattikadharmakṣānti</s>), and other special <s>samādhis</s>. For this very reason, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, it is not the case that because of the real existence of designation, all entities exist. Consider also this, O <s>Mahāmati</s>: in this world, certain kinds of beings such as worms and flies perform their activities without any designation at all.

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Therein it is said:

children.text: ākāśaṃ śaśaśṛṅgaṃ ca vandhyāyāḥ putra eva ca /
children.translated_text: Space, and a hare's horn, and the son of a barren woman —

children.text: asanto hyabhilapyante tathā bhāveṣu kalpanā // Lank_2.164 //
children.translated_text: non-existent things are designated; similarly is the conceptual construction regarding entities. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.164 ||
In the assemblage of causes and conditions, the childish construct arising;
not knowing this method, they wander in the abode of the three existences. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.165 ||

body.text: atha khalu mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ punarapi bhagavantametadavocat - nityaśabdaḥ punarbhagavan kvabhihitaḥ? bhagavānāha - bhrāntau mahāmate / yasmādiyaṃ bhrāntirāryāṇāmapi khyāyate viparyāsataḥ / tadyathā mahāmate mṛgatṛṣṇālātacakrakeśoṇḍukagandharvanagaramāyāsvapnapratibimbākṣapuruṣā loke 'vidvadbhirviparyasyante, na tu vidvadbhiḥ / na ca punarna khyāyante / sā punarbhrāntirmahāmate anekaprakārā khyāyāt / na bhrānteraśāśvatatāṃ kurute / tatkasya hetoḥ? yaduta bhāvābhāvavivarjitatvāt / kathaṃ punarmahāmate bhāvābhāvavivarjitā bhrāntiḥ? yaduta sarvabālavicitragocaratvātsamudrataraṃgagaṅgodakavatpretānāṃ darśanādarśanataḥ / ata etasmātkāraṇānmahāmate bhrāntibhāvo na bhavati / yasmācca tadudakamanyeṣāṃ khyāyate, ato hyabhāvo na bhavati / evaṃ bhrāntirāryāṇāṃ viparyāsāviparyāsavarjitā / ataśca mahāmate asmātkāraṇācchāśvatā bhrāntiryaduta nimittalakṣaṇābhedatvāt / na hi mahāmate bhrāntirvividhavicitranimittavikalpena vikalpyamānā bhedamupayāti / ata etasmātkāraṇānmahāmate bhrāntiḥ śāśvatā //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s> again addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s> thus: Where, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, is the word "permanent" (<s>nitya</s>) spoken? The <s>Bhagavān</s> replied: With reference to error (<s>bhrānti</s>), O <s>Mahāmati</s>. Because this error appears even to the noble ones, through inversion (<s>viparyāsa</s>). Just as, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, mirages, fire-brands, hair-tufts, <s>Gandharva</s>-cities, illusions, dreams, reflections, and wooden puppets are inverted [i.e. misconceived] by the unwise in the world, but not by the wise — and yet they do not cease to appear. That error, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, manifests in many ways, [yet] error does not make itself impermanent. For what reason? Because it is devoid of [both] existence and non-existence. How then, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is error devoid of existence and non-existence? Because it is the diverse domain of all the foolish — like ocean-waves or <s>Gaṅgā</s>-water, which hungry ghosts (<s>pretas</s>) see and do not see. For this very reason, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the existence of error does not exist [as an entity]. And since that water appears to others, therefore its non-existence does not exist either. Thus error, for the noble ones, is free from both inversion and non-inversion. And for this reason, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, error is permanent — namely, because of the non-differentiation of sign-characteristics. For indeed, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, error, though being discriminated by the discrimination of diverse and varied signs, does not undergo differentiation. For this very reason, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, error is permanent.

body.text: kathaṃ punarmahāmate bhrāntistattvaṃ bhavati? yena punaḥ kāraṇena mahāmate āryāṇāmasyāṃ bhrāntau viparyāsabuddhirna pravartate, nāviparyāsabuddhiḥ / nānyatra mahāmate āryā asyāṃ bhrāntau yakiṃcitsaṃjñino bhavanti nāryajñānavastusaṃjñinaḥ / yatkiṃciditi mahāmate bālapralāpa eṣa nāryapralāpaḥ / sā punarbhrāntirviparyāsāviparyāsena vikalpyamānā gotradvayāvahā bhavati yaduta āryagotrasya vā bālapṛthagjanagotrasya vā / āryagotraṃ punarmahāmate triprakāramupayāti yaduta śrāvakapratyekabuddhabuddhaprabhedataḥ / tatra kathaṃ punarmahāmate bālairbhrāntirvikalpyamānā śrāvakayānagotraṃ janayati? yaduta mahāmate svasāmānyalakṣaṇābhiniveśenābhiniviśyamānā śrāvakayānagotrāya saṃvartate / evaṃ mahāmate sā bhrāntiḥ śrāvakayānagotrāvahā bhavati / tatra kathaṃ punarmahāmate saiva bhrāntirvikalpyamānā pratyekabuddhayānagotrāvahā bhavati? yaduta tasyā eva mahāmate bhrānteḥ svasāmānyalakṣaṇābhiniveśāsaṃsargataḥ pratyekabuddhayānagotrāvahā bhavati / tatra kathaṃ
body.translated_text: How then, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, does error become reality (<s>tattva</s>)? By the reason, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, that in the noble ones, with regard to this error, neither the cognition of inversion nor the cognition of non-inversion proceeds. The noble ones, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, have no perception of anything whatsoever in this error, nor do they have the perception of the object of noble knowledge. "Anything whatsoever," O <s>Mahāmati</s> — this is idle talk of the foolish, not the discourse of the noble. That error, moreover, when discriminated through inversion and non-inversion, leads to two lineages (<s>gotra</s>) — namely, the lineage of the noble and the lineage of the foolish ordinary person. The noble lineage, moreover, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is of three kinds — namely, by the division into <s>Śrāvaka</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, and <s>Buddha</s>. Therein, how then, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, does error, when discriminated by the foolish, give rise to the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> lineage? When, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, one is attached through the attachment to specific and general characteristics, it conduces to the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> lineage. Thus, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, that error leads to the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> lineage. Therein, how then, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, does that very error, when discriminated, lead to the <s>Pratyekabuddhayāna</s> lineage? When, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, through the non-association with the attachment to the specific and general characteristics of that very error, it leads to the <s>Pratyekabuddhayāna</s> lineage. Therein, how then

body.text: punarmahāmate paṇḍitaiḥ saiva bhrāntirvikalpyamānā buddhayānagotrāvahā bhavati? yaduta mahāmate svacittadṛśyamātrāvabodhādbāhyabhāvābhāvavikalpanatayā vikalpyamānā buddhayānagotrāavahā bhavati / ata eva mahāmate gotram / eṣa gotrārthaḥ / vicitravastubhāvanā punarmahāmate bālairbhrāntirvikalpyamānā saṃsārayānagotrāvahā bhavati, evamidaṃ nānyatheti / ata etasmātkāraṇānmahāmate bhrāntirvicitravastutvena kalpyate bālaiḥ / sā ca na vastu, nāvastu / saiva mahāmate bhrāntiravikalpyamānā āryāṇāṃ cittamanomanovijñānadauṣṭhulyavāsanāsvabhāvadharmaparāvṛttibhāvādbhrāntirāryāṇāṃ tathatetyucyate / ata etaduktaṃ bhavati mahāmate - tathatāpi cittavinirmukteti / asyaiva mahāmate padasyābhidyotanārthamidamuktaṃ mayā - kalpanaiśca vivarjitaṃ sarvakalpanāvirahitamiti yāvaduktaṃ bhavati //
body.translated_text: , O <s>Mahāmati</s>, does that very error, when discriminated by the wise, lead to the <s>Buddhayāna</s> lineage? When, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, through the awakening that [all is] mere appearance of one's own mind (<s>svacittadṛśyamātra</s>), it is discriminated through the non-discrimination of external existence and non-existence — [then] it leads to the <s>Buddhayāna</s> lineage. This indeed, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the lineage; this is the meaning of lineage. The contemplation of diverse objects, moreover, O <s>Mahāmati</s> — error discriminated by the foolish leads to the <s>saṃsāra</s>-vehicle lineage, [thinking] "this is just so, not otherwise." For this very reason, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, error is conceived by the foolish as a diversity of objects. And it is neither an object nor a non-object. That very error, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, when not discriminated [by the noble ones], because of the reversal of the inherent nature of the depravity-impressions of mind, <s>manas</s>, and <s>manovijñāna</s>, the error of the noble ones is called <s>Suchness</s> (<s>tathatā</s>). Hence this is stated, O <s>Mahāmati</s>: "<s>Suchness</s> too is released from mind." For the purpose of illuminating this very term, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, this was said by me: "devoid of conceptual construction" — "free from all conceptual construction" — and so forth.

body.text: mahāmatirāha - bhrāntirbhagavan vidyate neti? bhagavānāha - māyāvanmahāmate na lakṣaṇābhiniveśato bhrāntirvidyate / yadi punarmahāmate bhrāntirlakṣaṇābhiniveśena vidyate, avyāvṛtta eva mahāmate bhāvābhiniveśaḥ syāt / pratītyasamutpādavattīrthakarakāraṇotpādavadetatsyānmahāmate / mahāmatirāha - yadi bhagavan māyāprakhyā bhrāntiḥ, tenānyasyā bhrānteḥ kāraṇībhaviṣyati / bhagavānāha - na mahāmate māyā bhrāntikāraṇam / adauṣṭhulyadoṣāvahatvānna hi mahāmate māyā dauṣṭhulyadoṣamāvahati / avikalpyamānā māyā punarmahāmate parapuruṣavidyādhiṣṭhānātpravartate, na svavikalpadauṣṭhulyavāsanādhiṣṭhānataḥ / sā na doṣāvahā bhavati / cittadṛṣṭimohamātrametanmahāmate bālānāṃ yatkiṃcidabhiniveśato na tvāryāṇām //
body.translated_text: <s>Mahāmati</s> asked: Does error exist or not, O <s>Bhagavān</s>? The <s>Bhagavān</s> replied: Like an illusion (<s>māyā</s>), O <s>Mahāmati</s> — error does not exist through attachment to characteristics. If, moreover, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, error were to exist through attachment to characteristics, then the attachment to [the existence of] entities would be ineliminable, O <s>Mahāmati</s>. It would be like dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>), like the arising-from-cause of the heretical teachers — this would be the case, O <s>Mahāmati</s>. <s>Mahāmati</s> asked: If, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, error is like an illusion, then it will be the cause of another error. The <s>Bhagavān</s> replied: No, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, illusion is not the cause of error, because illusion does not bring about the fault of depravity. For indeed, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, illusion does not bring about the fault of depravity. Illusion, moreover, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, when not discriminated, proceeds through the empowerment of another person's knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>), not through the empowerment of one's own discriminative depravity-impressions. Therefore it does not bring about faults. This is merely a delusion of the vision of the mind, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, [occurring] among the foolish through some attachment — not among the noble ones.

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Therein this is said:

children.text: āryo na paśyati bhrāntiṃ nāpi tattvaṃ tadantare /
children.translated_text: The noble one sees neither error nor reality therein;
error itself would become reality, since reality is therein. [Laṅk 2.166]

children.text: bhrāntiṃ vidhūya sarvāṃ hi nimittaṃ jāyate yadi /
children.translated_text: If, having dispelled all error, a sign were to arise,

children.text: saiva tasya bhavedbhrāntiraśuddhaṃ timiraṃ yathā // Lank_2.167 //
children.translated_text: that very [sign] would be his error, like the impure [vision caused by] an eye-disease. [Laṅk 2.167]

body.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate na māyā nāsti / sādharmyadarśanātsarvadharmāṇāṃ māyopamatvaṃ bhavati / mahāmatirāha - kiṃ punarbhagavan vicitramāyābhiniveśalakṣaṇena sarvadharmāṇāṃ māyopamatvaṃ bhavati, atha vitathābhiniveśalakṣaṇena? tadyadi bhagavan vicitramāyābhiniveśalakṣaṇena sarvadharmāṇāṃ māyopamatvaṃ bhavati, hanta bhagavan na bhāvā māyopamāḥ / tatkasya hetoḥ? yaduta rūpasya vicitralakṣaṇāhetudarśanāt / na hi bhagavan kaściddheturasti yena rūpaṃ vicitralakṣaṇākāraṃ khyāyate māyāvat / ata etasmātkāraṇādbhagavan na vicitramāyālakṣaṇābhiniveśasādharmyādbhāvā māyopamāḥ //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, illusion (<s>māyā</s>) does not not exist [i.e. illusion is not utterly nonexistent]. It is by seeing the similarity [between illusion and dharmas] that all <s>dharmas</s> are said to be illusion-like. <s>Mahāmati</s> asked: Is it, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, through the characteristic of attachment to the diversity of illusion that all <s>dharmas</s> are illusion-like, or through the characteristic of attachment to the false? If, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, it is through the characteristic of attachment to the diversity of illusion that all <s>dharmas</s> are illusion-like — well then, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, entities are not illusion-like. For what reason? Because of the perception that there is no cause for the diverse appearance of form. For indeed, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, there is no cause by which form appears in diverse characteristic-appearances like an illusion. For this very reason, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, entities are not illusion-like through the similarity of attachment to the characteristic of diverse illusion.

body.text: bhagavānāha - na mahāmate vicitramāyālakṣaṇābhiniveśasādharmyātsarvadharmā māyopamāḥ, kiṃ tarhi mahāmate vitathāśuvidyutsadṛśasādharmyeṇa sarvadharmā māyopamāḥ / tadyathā mahāmate
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> replied: No, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, it is not through the similarity of attachment to the characteristic of diverse illusion that all <s>dharmas</s> are illusion-like. Rather, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, it is through the similarity with false and swift lightning that all <s>dharmas</s> are illusion-like. Just as, O <s>Mahāmati</s>,

body.text: vidyullatā kṣaṇabhaṅgadṛṣṭanaṣṭadarśanaṃ punarbālānāṃ khyāyate, evameva mahāmate sarvabhāvāḥ svavikalpasāmānyalakṣaṇāḥ pravicayābhāvānna khyāyante rūpalakṣaṇābhiniveśataḥ //
body.translated_text: a flash of lightning, momentarily arising and perishing, appears to the foolish as seen-and-lost, even so, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, all entities, [having] the specific and general characteristics of one's own discrimination, do not appear through the attachment to form-characteristics because of the absence of investigation.

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Therein this is said:

children.translated_text: Not that illusion does not exist — by similarity, the existence of entities is proclaimed;
they are like the false and swift lightning — therefore they are said to be illusion-like. [Laṅk 2.168]

body.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmatirāha - yatpunaretaduktaṃ bhagavatā - anutpannāḥ sarvabhāvā māyopamāśceti / nanu te bhagavan evaṃ bruvataḥ pūrvottaravacanavyāghātadoṣaḥ prasajyate, anutpādaṃ bhāvānāṃ māyopamatvenābhilapataḥ / bhagavānāha - na mahāmate mamānutpādaṃ bhāvānāṃ māyopamatvenābhilapataḥ pūrvottaravacanavyāghātadoṣo bhavati / tatkasya hetoḥ? yaduta utpādānutpādasvacittadṛśyamātrāvabodhātsadasatorbāhyabhāvābhāvānutpattidarśanānna mahāmate pūrvottaravacanavyāghātadoṣaḥ prasajyate / kiṃ tu mahāmate tīrthakarakāraṇakṣotpattivyudāsārthamidamucyate - māyāvadanutpannāḥ sarvabhāvāḥ / tīrthakaramohavargā hi mahāmate sadasatorbhāvānāmutpattimicchanti na svavikalpavicitrābhiniveśapratyayataḥ / mama tu mahāmate na saṃtrāsamutpadyate / ata etasmātkāraṇānmahāmate anutpādābhidhānamevābhidhīyate / bhāvopadeśaḥ punarmahāmate saṃsāraparigrahārthaṃ ca nāstītyucchedanivāraṇārthaṃ ca / macchiṣyāṇāṃ vicitrakarmopapattyāyatanaparigrahārthaṃ bhāvaśabdaparigraheṇa saṃsāraparigrahaḥ kriyate / māyābhāvasvabhāvalakṣaṇanirdeśena mahāmate bhāvasvabhāvalakṣaṇavyāvṛttyarthaṃ bālapṛthagjanānāṃ kṛdṛṣṭilakṣaṇapatitāśayānāṃ svacittadṛśyamātrānavadhāriṇāṃ hetupratyayakriyotpattilakṣaṇābhiniviṣṭhānāṃ nivāraṇārthaṃ māyāsvapnasvabhāvalakṣaṇān sarvadharmān deśayāmi / ete bālapṛthagjanāḥ kudṛṣṭilakṣaṇāśayābhiniviṣṭā ātmānaṃ paraṃ ca sarvadharmā yathābhūtāvasthānadarśanādvisaṃvādayiṣyanti / tatra yathābhūtāvasthānadarśanaṃ mahāmate sarvadharmāṇāṃ yaduta svacittadṛśyamātrāvatāraḥ //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Mahāmati</s> asked: As for this statement made by the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "All entities are unborn and illusion-like" — does it not follow, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, that there is the fault of contradiction between the earlier and later statements, in proclaiming the non-arising of entities through their being illusion-like? The <s>Bhagavān</s> replied: No, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, for me, proclaiming the non-arising of entities through their being illusion-like, there is no fault of contradiction between earlier and later statements. For what reason? Because, through the awakening that arising and non-arising are mere appearance of one's own mind (<s>svacittadṛśyamātra</s>), and through seeing the non-arising of external existence and non-existence of the existent and non-existent — there is no fault of contradiction between earlier and later statements, O <s>Mahāmati</s>. Rather, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, for the purpose of removing the origination from cause [posited by] the heretical teachers, this is said: "All entities are unborn, like an illusion." For the deluded followers of heretical teachers, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, wish for the arising of entities from the existent and non-existent, [but] not from the condition of the attachment to diverse discriminations of one's own [mind]. For me, however, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, no alarm arises. For this very reason, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the designation of "non-arising" (<s>anutpāda</s>) is indeed designated. The teaching of "entity" (<s>bhāva</s>), moreover, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is for the purpose of embracing <s>saṃsāra</s> and for the purpose of preventing the annihilation [view that] "it does not exist." For the purpose of my disciples' embracing the domains of rebirth through diverse actions, the embrace of <s>saṃsāra</s> is made through the embrace of the word "entity." By the indication of the characteristics of the inherent nature of illusion, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, for the purpose of turning away from the characteristics of the inherent nature of entities — for the purpose of preventing those foolish ordinary beings who have fallen into the disposition of the characteristics of wrong views, who do not ascertain [that all is] mere appearance of one's own mind, who are attached to the characteristics of arising from cause-condition-activity — I teach all <s>dharmas</s> as having the characteristics of the inherent nature of illusion and dream. These foolish ordinary beings, attached to the disposition of the characteristics of wrong views, will deceive themselves and others by [failing to see] the vision of all <s>dharmas</s> as they truly are. Therein, the vision of all <s>dharmas</s> as they truly are, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the entry into [the realization that all is] mere appearance of one's own mind (<s>svacittadṛśyamātra</s>).

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Therein this is said:

children.translated_text: In non-arising, the absence of cause; in entity, the embrace of <s>saṃsāra</s>;
one should see [all] as similar to illusion etc. — one should not discriminate characteristics. [Laṅk 2.169]

body.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate nāmapadavyañjanakāyānāṃ lakṣaṇamuddekṣyāmaḥ, yairnāmapadavyañjanakāyaiḥ sūpalakṣitairbodhisattvā mahāsattvā arthapadavyañjanānusāriṇaḥ kṣipramanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhya tathaiva sarvasattvānavabodhayiṣyanti / tatra mahāmate kāyo nāma yaduta yadvastvāśritya nāma kriyate, sa kāyo vastu / kāyaḥ śarīramityanarthāntaram / eṣa mahāmate nāmakāyaḥ / padakāyaḥ punarmahāmate yaduta padārthakāyasadbhāvo niścayaḥ / niṣṭhā upalabdhirityanarthāntaram / eṣa mahāmate padakāyopadeśaḥ kṛto māyā / vyañjanakāyaḥ punarmahāmate yaduta yena nāmapadayorabhivyaktirbhavati / vyañjanaṃ liṅgaṃ lakṣaṇamupalabdhiḥ prajñaptirityanarthāntaram //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, we shall point out the characteristics of the bodies of names (<s>nāmakāya</s>), words (<s>padakāya</s>), and syllables (<s>vyañjanakāya</s>). When the <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas</s> have well-discerned the bodies of names, words, and syllables, they will, following the meanings, words, and syllables, quickly attain unsurpassed perfect enlightenment and will likewise awaken all beings. Therein, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the "body" [of names] is that entity dependent on which a name is made; that body is the entity. "Body" and "substance" are synonymous. This, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the name-body. The word-body (<s>padakāya</s>), moreover, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the ascertainment of the real existence of the meaning-body of the word. "Conclusion," "apprehension" — these are synonymous. This, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the instruction on the word-body — [but it is like] an illusion. The syllable-body (<s>vyañjanakāya</s>), moreover, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is that by which the manifestation of name and word occurs. "Syllable," "sign," "mark," "apprehension," "designation" — these are synonymous.

body.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate padakāyo yaduta padakāryaniṣṭhā / nāma punarmahāmate yaduta akṣarāṇāṃ ca nāmasvabhāvabhedo 'kārādyāvaddhakāraḥ / tatra vyañjanaṃ punarmahāmate yaduta hrasvadīrghaplutavyañjanāni / tatra padakāyāḥ punarmahāmate ye padavīthīgāmino hastyaśvanaramṛgapaśugomahiṣājaiḍakādyāḥ padakāyasaṃjñāṃ labhante / nāma ca vyañjanaṃ ca punarmahāmate catvāra arūpiṇaḥ skandhāḥ / nāmnābhilapyanta iti kṛtvā nāma, svalakṣaṇena vyajyate iti kṛtvā vyañjanam / etanmahāmate nāmapadavyañjanakāyānāṃ nāmapadābhidhānalakṣaṇam / atra te paricayaḥ karaṇīyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the word-body is the completion of the function of words. Name, moreover, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the differentiation of the inherent nature of names among syllables, from the letter "a" up to the letter "ha." Therein, syllables, moreover, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, are the short, long, and protracted syllable-signs. Therein, word-bodies, moreover, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, are those that traverse the path of tracks — elephants, horses, men, deer, cattle, buffalo, goats, sheep, and the like — [these] obtain the designation of "word-body" (<s>padakāya</s>). Name and syllable, moreover, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, are the four formless aggregates. They are called "name" because they are expressed by name; they are called "syllable" because they are manifested by their own characteristics. This, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the characteristic of the designation of the bodies of names, words, and syllables. Herein you should become familiar.

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Therein this is said:

children.text: vyañjane padakāye ca nāmni cāpi viśeṣataḥ /
children.translated_text: In syllables, word-bodies, and especially in names,

children.text: bālāḥ sajjanti durmedhā mahāpaṅke yathā gajāḥ // Lank_2.170 //
children.translated_text: the foolish become stuck, like elephants in great mud. [Laṅk 2.170]

body.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate yuktihetubuddhivaikalyātkutārkikā durvidagdhamatayo 'nāgate 'dhvani pṛṣṭā vidvadbhirekatvānyatvobhayānubhayadṛṣṭilakṣaṇavinirmuktamantadvayavidhiṃ pṛcchadbhirevaṃ vakṣyanti - apraśnamidaṃ nedaṃ yoniśa iti, yaduta rūpādibhyo 'nityatā anyā ananyeti / evaṃ nirvāṇaṃ saṃskārebhyo lakṣaṇāllakṣaṇaṃ guṇebhyo guṇī bhūtebhyo bhautikaṃ dṛśyāddarśanaṃ pāṃśubhyo 'ṇavo jñānādyoginaḥ, evamādyenottarottarakramalakṣaṇavidhinā avyākṛtāni pṛṣṭāḥ sthāpanīyaṃ bhagavatā avyākṛtamiti vakṣyanti / na tu te mohapuruṣā evaṃ jñāsyanti yathā śrotṝṇāṃ buddhivaikalyāt tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā utrāsapadavivarjanārthaṃ sattvānāṃ na vyākurvanti / avyākṛtānyapi ca mahāmate tīrthakaradṛṣṭivādavyudāsārthaṃ nopadiśyante tathāgataiḥ / tīrthakarā hi mahāmate evaṃvādinaḥ - yaduta sa jīvastaccharīram, anyo jīvo 'nyaccharīram, ityevamādye 'vyākṛtavādaḥ / tīrthakarāṇāṃ hi mahāmate kāraṇavisaṃmūḍhānāmavyākṛtaṃ na tu matpravacane / matpravacane tu mahāmate grāhyagrāhakavisaṃyukte vikalpo na pravartate / teṣāṃ kathaṃ sthāpyaṃ bhavet? ye tu mahāmate grāhyagrāhakābhiniviṣṭāḥ svacittadṛśyamātrānavadhāritamatayasteṣāṃ sthāpyaṃ bhavati / caturvidhapadapraśnavyākaraṇena mahāmate tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ sattvebhyo dharmaṃ deśayanti / sthāpanīyamiti mahāmate kālāntaradeśanaiṣā mayā kṛtā aparipakvendriyāṇām / na tu paripakvendriyāṇāṃ sthāpyaṃ bhavati //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, due to the deficiency of the intellect of reasoned causes, sophists of debased intellect, in the future time, when asked by the wise who inquire about the method of the two extremes — free from the characteristics of the views of oneness, otherness, both, and neither — will say thus: 'This is a non-question; this is not [to be answered] thoroughly' — namely, whether impermanence is other than or not other than form and so forth. Likewise [they will say] regarding <s>nirvāṇa</s> [and] conditioned things, characteristic [and] what is characterized, qualities [and] what possesses qualities, elements [and] the elemental, the seen [and] seeing, dust-particles [and] atoms, knowledge [and] the <s>yogin</s> — by this and similar progressive method of characteristics, [they will say that] being asked about the undeclared [questions], 'the Blessed One left it undeclared.' But those deluded persons will not understand that it is because of the deficiency of the listeners' intellect that the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, do not make declarations for beings — for the purpose of avoiding grounds for fear. And the undeclared [questions], O <s>Mahāmati</s>, are also not taught by the <s>Tathāgatas</s> for the purpose of removing the views and doctrines of the heretics. For the heretics, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, speak thus: 'The soul is the same as the body; the soul is one thing, the body another' — the undeclared doctrine concerns such [questions]. For the heretics, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, who are confused about causation, [these are] undeclared — but not in my teaching. In my teaching, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, when [all is] dissociated from the grasped and the grasper, conceptualization does not operate. How could there be anything to be set aside for them? But for those, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, who are attached to the grasped and grasper, whose minds have not ascertained [that all is] mere appearance of one's own mind — for them there is something to be set aside. By the fourfold method of answering questions, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones teach the <s>dharma</s> to beings. 'To be set aside' — O <s>Mahāmati</s>, this is a teaching I have given for another time, for those whose faculties are not yet ripened. But for those whose faculties are ripened, nothing is to be set aside.

body.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate kriyākārakarahitāḥ sarvadharmā notpadyante 'kārakatvāt / tenocyate 'nuptannāḥ sarvadharmāḥ / niḥsvabhāvāḥ punarmahāmate sarvabhāvāḥ kena kāraṇenaḥ? yasmānmahāmate svabuddhyā vicāryamāṇānāṃ svasāmānyalakṣaṇābhāvā nāvadhāryante, tenocyante niḥsvabhāvāḥ sarvadharmā iti / tatra anāyūhāniryūhāḥ punarmahāmate sarvadharmāḥ kena kāraṇena? yasmānmahāmate svasāmānyalakṣaṇamāyūhyamānaṃ nāyuhyate, niryūhyamānaṃ na niryūhyate / ata etasmātkāraṇānmahāmate sarvadharmā āyūhaniryūhavigatāḥ / aniruddhāḥ punarmahāmate sarvadharmāḥ kena kāraṇena? yaduta bhāvasvabhāvalakṣaṇāsattvātsarvadharmā nopalabhyante / tenocyante 'niruddhāḥ sarvadharmā iti / tatra
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, all <s>dharmas</s>, being free from action and agent, do not arise — because they are without agent. Therefore it is said: 'All <s>dharmas</s> are unborn.' All entities, moreover, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, are without inherent nature — for what reason? Because, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, when examined by one's own intellect, they are not ascertained [to have] own-characteristics or general-characteristics — therefore it is said: 'All <s>dharmas</s> are without inherent nature.' Therein, all <s>dharmas</s> are without production or withdrawal, O <s>Mahāmati</s> — for what reason? Because, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, when own- and general-characteristics are being produced, they are not produced; when being withdrawn, they are not withdrawn. For this reason, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, all <s>dharmas</s> are free from production and withdrawal. All <s>dharmas</s> are unceased, O <s>Mahāmati</s> — for what reason? Because all <s>dharmas</s> are not apprehended, due to the non-existence of the characteristic of the inherent nature of entities. Therefore it is said: 'All <s>dharmas</s> are unceased.' Therein

body.text: anityāḥ punarmahāmate sarvadharmāḥ kena kāraṇenocyante? yaduta lakṣaṇotpattyanityabhāvāt / tenocyante anityāḥ sarvadharmā iti / tatra nityāḥ punarmahāmate sarvadharmāḥ kena kāraṇena? yaduta lakṣaṇotpannānutpannābhāvādanityatayā nityāḥ / tenocyante mahāmate nityāḥ sarvadharmā iti //
body.translated_text: all <s>dharmas</s> are said to be impermanent, O <s>Mahāmati</s> — for what reason? Because of the impermanent nature of the arising of characteristics. Therefore it is said: 'All <s>dharmas</s> are impermanent.' Therein, all <s>dharmas</s> are permanent, O <s>Mahāmati</s> — for what reason? Because the arisen and unarisen of characteristics are absent, they are permanent by way of impermanence. Therefore it is said, O <s>Mahāmati</s>: 'All <s>dharmas</s> are permanent.'

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: On this, it is said:

children.translated_text: The fourfold declaration: definite answer, interrogation,
analytical [answer], and setting aside — [these] ward off the doctrines of the heretics. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.171 ||
The non-arising of the existent and the non-existent is held by the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s> and <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s>;

children.text: avyākṛtāni sarvāṇi taireva hi prakāśitā // Lank_2.172 //
children.translated_text: all [their questions are] undeclared — they have been clarified by them alone. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.172 ||
When examined by the intellect, the inherent nature [of things] is not ascertained;
therefore they are taught as inexpressible and without inherent nature. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.173 ||

body.text: atha khalu mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ punarapi bhagavantametadavocat - deśayatu me bhagavān srotaāpannānāṃ srotaāpattigatiprabhedanayalakṣaṇam / yena srotaāpattigatiprabhedanayalakṣaṇena ahaṃ ca anye ca bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ srotaāpannānāṃ srotaāpattigatiprabhedanayalakṣaṇakuśalā uttarottarasakṛdāgāmyanāgāmyarhattvopāyalakṣaṇavidhijñāstathā sattvebhyo dharmaṃ deśayeyuḥ, yathā nairātmyalakṣaṇadvayamāvaraṇadvayaṃ ca prativiśodhya bhūmerbhūmilakṣaṇātikramagatiṃgatāstathāgatācintyagativiṣayagocaraṃ pratilabhya viśvarūpamaṇisadṛśāḥ sarvasattvopajīvyatāmadhigaccheyuḥ, sarvadharmaviṣayagatikāyopabhogyatopajīvyāḥ syuḥ //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s> again said this to the Blessed One: 'May the Blessed One teach me the characteristic of the method and classification of the course of the stream-enterer's (<s>srotaāpanna</s>) stream-entry, so that I and other <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s>, skilled in the characteristic of the method and classification of the course of the stream-enterer's stream-entry, knowing the method of the characteristics of the means for [attaining] the successively higher [stages of] once-returner (<s>sakṛdāgāmin</s>), non-returner (<s>anāgāmin</s>), and <s>arhat</s>ship, may teach the <s>dharma</s> to beings accordingly, so that, having purified the twofold characteristics of selflessness (<s>nairātmya</s>) and the twofold obscurations, having entered the course that transcends the characteristics of the stages from stage to stage, having attained the domain of the inconceivable course of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, like wish-fulfilling jewels of universal form, they may become the sustenance of all beings, and be sustained by the enjoyment of the body of the course of the domain of all <s>dharmas</s>.'

body.text: bhagavānāha - tena hi mahāmate śṛṇu, sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasikuru / bhāṣiṣye 'haṃ te / sādhu bhagavanniti mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavataḥ pratyaśrauṣīt / bhagavāṃstasyaitadavocat - traya ime mahāmate srotaāpannānāṃ srotaāpattiphalaprabhedāḥ / katame trayaḥ? yaduta hīnamadhyaviśiṣṭāḥ tatra mahāmate hīnaḥ saptajanmabhavaparamaḥ / madhyaḥ punarmahāmate tripañcabhavaparinirvāyī bhavati / uttamaḥ punarmahāmate tajjanmaparinirvāyī bhavati / eṣāṃ tu mahāmate trayāṇāṃ trīṇi saṃyojanāni mṛdumadhyādhimātrāṇyeva bhavanti / tatra mahāmate katamāni trīṇi saṃyojanāni? yaduta satkāyadṛṣṭirvicikitsā śīlavrataparāmarśaśca / etāni mahāmate trīṇi saṃyojanāni viśeṣottarottareṇa arhatāmarhatphalībhavanti / tatra mahāmate satkāyadṛṣṭirdvividhā yaduta sahajā ca parikalpitā ca, paratantraparikalpitasvabhāvavat / tadyathā mahāmate paratantrasvabhāvāśrayādvicitraparikalpitasvabhāvābhiniveśaḥ pravartate / sa ca tatra na sannāsanna sadasan, abhūtaparikalpalakṣaṇatvāt / atha ca bālairvikalpyate vicitrasvabhāvalakṣaṇābhiniveśena mṛgatṛṣṇikeva mṛgaiḥ / iyaṃ mahāmate srotaāpannasya parikalpitā satkāyadṛṣṭirajñānāccirakālābhiniveśasaṃcitā / sā ca tasya pudgalanairātmyagrahābhāvataḥ prahīṇā / sahajā punarmahāmate srotaāpannasya satkāyadṛṣṭiḥ svaparakāyasamatayā catuḥskandharūpalakṣaṇatvādrūpasyotpattibhūtabhautikatvātparasparahetulakṣaṇatvādbhūtānāṃ
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'Then, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, listen, and attend well and thoroughly. I shall speak to you.' 'Very well, Blessed One!' — the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s> gave assent to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this to him: 'There are, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, three classifications of the fruit of stream-entry for stream-enterers. Which three? Namely: inferior, middling, and superior. Therein, the inferior, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, has at most seven births. The middling, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, attains final <s>nirvāṇa</s> after three to five existences. The superior, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, attains final <s>nirvāṇa</s> in that very birth. Of these three, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the three fetters (<s>saṃyojana</s>) are mild, moderate, and intense respectively. What, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, are the three fetters? Namely: the view of the self-existing body (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>), doubt (<s>vicikitsā</s>), and attachment to rules and observances (<s>śīlavrataparāmarśa</s>). These, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, three fetters, through progressively superior [practice], become the fruit of the <s>arhat</s> for <s>arhats</s>. Therein, the view of the self-existing body, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is twofold — namely, innate (<s>sahajā</s>) and imagined (<s>parikalpitā</s>), like the dependent and imagined inherent natures. Just as, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, from the basis of the dependent inherent nature, the attachment to the varied imagined inherent nature operates — and that is therein neither existent nor non-existent, nor both existent and non-existent, because of the characteristic of unreal imagination — yet it is conceptualized by the childish through attachment to the characteristics of varied inherent natures, like a mirage [conceptualized] by deer — this, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the stream-enterer's imagined view of the self-existing body, accumulated through long-standing attachment in ignorance. And that is abandoned through the absence of grasping at personal selflessness (<s>pudgalanairātmya</s>). The innate view of the self-existing body of the stream-enterer, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, through the equality of one's own and others' bodies, because the four aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>) have the characteristic of form, because form arises from elements and elementals, and because of the mutual cause-characteristic of elements

body.text: rūpasyāsamudaya iti kṛtvā srotaāpannasya sadasatpakṣadṛṣṭidarśanātsatkāyadṛṣṭiḥ prahīṇā bhavati / ata eva satkāyadṛṣṭiprahīṇasya rāgo na pravartate / etanmahāmate satkāyadṛṣṭilakṣaṇam //
body.translated_text: — taking it that form does not [truly] arise — the view of the self-existing body is abandoned for the stream-enterer through seeing the views of the positions of existent and non-existent. Therefore, for one whose view of the self-existing body is abandoned, passion does not operate. This, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the characteristic of the view of the self-existing body.

body.text: vicikitsālakṣaṇaṃ punarmahāmate yaduta prāptidharmādhigamasudṛṣṭilakṣaṇatvātpūrvaṃ satkāyadṛṣṭidvayavikalpaprahīṇatvācca vicikitsā dharmeṣu na bhavati / na cāsya anyā śāstṛdṛṣṭirbhavati śuddhāśuddhitaḥ / etanmahāmate vicikitsālakṣaṇaṃ srotaāpannasya //
body.translated_text: The characteristic of doubt (<s>vicikitsā</s>), O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is as follows: because of the characteristic of correct seeing of the <s>dharma</s> and its attainment, and because the twofold conceptualization of the view of the self-existing body has been previously abandoned, doubt regarding <s>dharmas</s> does not exist. Nor does he have any other view of a teacher as [being] pure or impure. This, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the characteristic of the stream-enterer's [abandonment of] doubt.

body.text: śīlaṃ punarmahāmate kathaṃ na parāmṛśati srotaāpannaḥ? yaduta duḥkhopapattyāyatanalakṣaṇasaṃdṛṣṭatvānna parāmṛśati / parāmṛṣṭiḥ punarmahāmate yaduta śīlavratataponiyamairbālapṛthagjanā bhogasukhābhilāṣiṇo bhavotpattiṃ prārthayante, na ca parāmṛśanti / evamanyatra svapratyātmādhigamaviśeṣagāmitāyāṃ pariṇāmayanti / nirvikalpānāsravadharmalakṣaṇākāreṇa prasajyante śīlāṅgaiḥ / etanmahāmate srotaāpannasya śīlavrataparāmarśalakṣaṇaṃ bhavati / na tu mahāmate srotaāpannasya trisaṃyojanaprahīṇasya rāgadveṣamohāḥ pravartante //
body.translated_text: How, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, does the stream-enterer not cling to moral rules? Because he has seen the characteristic of the sense-bases as the ground of painful rebirth, he does not cling. Clinging, moreover, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is when childish ordinary persons, desirous of the pleasure of enjoyments, through rules, observances, and ascetic restraints, aspire for rebirth in [higher] existence — yet they do not [truly] cling. Rather, apart from [this], they transform [their practice] in the direction of the distinctive course of one's own inner realization. They engage with the limbs of moral conduct in the form of non-conceptual, outflow-free (<s>anāsrava</s>) <s>dharma</s>-characteristics. This, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the characteristic of the stream-enterer's [abandonment of] attachment to rules and observances. But for the stream-enterer, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, who has abandoned the three fetters, passion, aversion, and delusion do not operate.

body.text: mahāmatirāha - rāgaḥ punarbhagavatā bahuprakāra upadiṣṭaḥ / tatkatamastasyātra rāgaḥ prahīṇo bhavati? bhagavānāha - viṣayakāmendriyaḥ strīsaṃyogarāgaḥ pratyutpannasukhaḥ āyatyāṃ duḥkhajanmahetukaḥ khaṭacapeṭaliṅgitacumbitapariṣvaktāghrātakaṭākṣekṣitaiḥ / tasya mahāmate rāgo na pravartate / tatkasya hetoḥ? yaduta samādhisukhavihāralābhitvāt / ata eṣa prahīṇo bhavati, na nirvāṇādhigamarāgaḥ //
body.translated_text: <s>Mahāmati</s> said: 'The Blessed One has taught that passion is of many kinds. Which passion of his is abandoned here?' The Blessed One said: 'The passion for the enjoyment of objects and senses, the passion of union with women — [which brings] present pleasure [but is] the cause of painful birth in the future — [manifesting] through scratching, slapping, embracing, kissing, hugging, smelling, sidelong glances, and gazes. That passion, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, does not operate [for the stream-enterer]. For what reason? Because of obtaining the dwelling in the bliss of <s>samādhi</s>. Therefore this [passion] is abandoned — not the passion for the attainment of <s>nirvāṇa</s>.'

body.text: sakṛdāgāmiphalalakṣaṇaṃ punarmahāmate katamat? yaduta sakṛdrūpalakṣaṇābhāsavikalpaḥ pravartate / nimittadṛṣṭilakṣyalakṣaṇābhāvāddhyānagatilakṣaṇasudṛṣṭatvātsakṛdetaṃ lokamāgamya duḥkhasyāntakriyāyai parinirvāsyati / tenocyate sakṛdāgāmīti / tatra anāgāmīti mahāmate kathaṃ bhavati? yaduta atītānāgatapratyutpannasya rūpalakṣaṇabhāvābhāvapravṛtterdṛṣṭidoṣānuśayavikalpasya anāgāmitvādanāgāmirūpaprahīṇatvācca saṃyojanānāmanāgāmītyucyate / arhan punarmahāmate dhyānadhyeyasamādhivimokṣabalābhijñākleśaduḥkhavikalpābhāvādarhannityucyate //
body.translated_text: What, moreover, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the characteristic of the fruit of the once-returner (<s>sakṛdāgāmin</s>)? When the conceptualization of the appearance of the characteristic of form operates just once — because of the absence of signs, viewed [objects], the characterized, and characteristics, and because of correct seeing of the characteristic of the course of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) — having come once to this world, he will attain final <s>nirvāṇa</s> for the complete ending of suffering. Therefore he is called a 'once-returner.' Therein, how does one become a non-returner (<s>anāgāmin</s>), O <s>Mahāmati</s>? Because the conceptualization of the latent tendencies of the view-fault regarding the existence and non-existence of the characteristic of form in past, future, and present does not return (<s>anāgāmin</s>) — because of the non-returning of form-abandonment and of the fetters — he is called a 'non-returner.' An <s>arhat</s>, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is called an <s>arhat</s> because of the absence of meditation, meditated [object], the object of meditation, <s>samādhi</s>, liberation, powers, superknowledges, affliction, suffering, and conceptualization.

body.text: mahāmatirāha - trayaḥ punarbhagavatā arhanto 'bhihitāḥ / tatkatamasyāyaṃ bhagavannarhacchabdo nipātyate? kiṃ bhagavan śamaikāyanamārgapratilambhikasya, uta bodhipraṇidhānābhyastakuśalamūlasaṃmūḍhasya, uta nirmitanairmāṇikasya? bhagavānāha - śamaikāyanamārgapratilambhikasya mahāmate śrāvakasya, na tvanyeṣām / anye punarmahāmate bodhisattvacaryācaritāvino buddhanirmitanairmāṇikāśca upāyakuśalamūlapraṇidhānapūrvakatvātparṣanmaṇḍaleṣūpapattiṃ darśayanti buddhaparṣanmaṇḍalopaśobhanārtham / vikalpagatisaṃsthānāntaravicitropadeśo 'yaṃ mahāmate yaduta phalādhigamadhyānadhyātṛdhyeyaviviktatvātsvacittadṛśyopagamātphalaprāptilakṣaṇamupadiśyate / punaraparaṃ mahāmate yadi
body.translated_text: <s>Mahāmati</s> said: 'The Blessed One has spoken of three kinds of <s>arhats</s>. To which of these, O Blessed One, does the term "<s>arhat</s>" apply? Is it, O Blessed One, to one who has attained the path of tranquility as the sole course? Or to one confused by roots of merit practiced through the vow of awakening (<s>bodhipraṇidhāna</s>)? Or to one who is an emanation?' The Blessed One said: 'To the <s>Śrāvaka</s> who has attained the path of tranquility as the sole course, O <s>Mahāmati</s> — not to the others. The others, moreover, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, are those who have practiced the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct, and Buddha-emanations, who — because of their prior skillful-means-rooted vows — display their appearance in the <s>maṇḍala</s>-assemblies for the purpose of adorning the Buddha-<s>maṇḍala</s>-assemblies. This, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is a varied teaching through the distinctions of different configurations of the course of conceptualization — namely, the characteristic of fruit-attainment is taught because of the isolation of fruit-attainment, meditation, meditator, and meditated [object] from the approach to what is seen by one's own mind. Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, if

body.text: srotaāpannasyaitadabhaviṣyat - imāni saṃyojanāni, ahamebhirna saṃyukta iti, taddvitvaprasaṅga ātmadṛṣṭipatitaḥ syādaprahīṇasaṃyojanaśca //
body.translated_text: the stream-enterer were to have this [thought]: 'These are the fetters, and I am not conjoined with them' — that would lead to the fault of duality; he would have fallen into the view of self, and the fetters would not have been abandoned.

body.text:
punaraparaṃ mahāmate dhyānāpramāṇārūpyadhātusamatikramāya svacittadṛśyalakṣaṇavyāvṛttiḥ karaṇīyā / saṃjñāveditanirodhasamāpattiśca mahāmate
svacittadṛśyagativyatikramastasya na yujyate cittamātratvāt //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, for the purpose of transcending the <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations), immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>), and formless realm (<s>ārūpyadhātu</s>), the turning away from the characteristics of what is seen by one's own mind should be practiced. And for the stream-enterer, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling (<s>saṃjñāveditanirodhasamāpatti</s>) — the transcendence of the course of what is seen by one's own mind — is not appropriate, because [all is] mind-only (<s>cittamātra</s>).

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: On this, it is said:

children.translated_text: The <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations), the immeasurables, and the formless <s>samādhis</s>,
