and the complete cessation of perception — [all these] are not found in mind-only. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.174 ||
The fruit of stream-entry, and likewise of the once-returner,
the fruit of the non-returner, and <s>arhat</s>ship — [these are] a confusion of mind. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.175 ||

children.text: dhyātā dhyānaṃ ca dhyeyaṃ ca prahāṇaṃ satyadarśanam /
children.translated_text: The meditator, the meditation, and the meditated, the abandonment and the seeing of truth —

children.text: kalpanāmātramevedaṃ yo budhyati sa mucyate // Lank_2.176 //
children.translated_text: all this is mere conceptualization; whoever awakens to this is liberated. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.176 ||

body.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate dviprakārā buddhiḥ pravicayabuddhiśca vikalpalakṣaṇagrāhābhiniveśapratiṣṭhāpikā ca / tatra mahāmate pravicayabuddhirnāma yaduta yayā buddhyā bhāvasvabhāvalakṣaṇaṃ pravicīyamānaṃ catuṣkoṭikārahitaṃ nopalabhyate, sā pravicayabuddhiḥ / tatra mahāmate catuṣkoṭikā yaduta ekatvānyatvobhayanobhayāstināstinityānityarahitāṃ catuṣkoṭikāmiti vadāmi / etayā catuṣkoṭikayā mahāmate rahitāḥ sarvadharmā ityucyate / iyaṃ mahāmate catuṣkoṭikā sarvadharmaparīkṣāyāṃ prayoktavyā / tatra mahāmate vikalpalakṣaṇagrāhābhiniveśapratiṣṭhāpikā buddhiḥ katamā? yaduta yena mahāmate cittavikalpalakṣaṇagrāhābhiniveśena uṣṇadravacalakaṭhinānabhūtaparikalpalakṣaṇān mahābhūtān pratijñāhetulakṣaṇadṛṣṭāntābhiniveśādasadbhūtasamāropeṇa samāropayati, sā vikalpalakṣaṇagrāhābhiniveśapratiṣṭhāpikā buddhiḥ / etanmahāmate buddhidvayasya lakṣaṇaṃ yena buddhidvayalakṣaṇena samanvāgatā bodhisattvā dharmapudgalanairātmyalakṣaṇagatiṃgatā nirābhāsabuddhipravicayacaryābhūmikuśalāḥ prathamāṃ bhūmiṃ pratilabhante, samādhiśataṃ ca samāpadyante / buddhabodhisattvaśataṃ ca samādhiviśeṣapratilambhena paśyanti, kalpaśataṃ ca pūrvāntāparāntato 'nupraviśanti, kṣetraśataṃ cāvabhāsayanti / kṣetraśataṃ cāvabhāsya uttarottarabhūmilakṣaṇavidhijñāḥ praṇidhānavaiśeṣikatayā vikrīḍanto dharmameghābhiṣekābhiṣiktāstathāgatapratyātmabhūmimadhigamya daśaniṣṭhāpadasunibaddhadharmāṇaḥ sattvaparipākāya vicitrairnirmāṇakiraṇairvirājante pratyātmagatisukhasamāhitāḥ //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, intelligence (<s>buddhi</s>) is of two kinds: the intelligence of investigation (<s>pravicayabuddhi</s>) and the intelligence that establishes attachment to the grasping of discriminative characteristics (<s>vikalpalakṣaṇagrāhābhiniveśapratiṣṭhāpikā</s>). Therein, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, what is called the intelligence of investigation? Namely, that intelligence by which, when the inherent-nature-characteristic of entities is investigated, [it] is not apprehended as free from the fourfold [proposition] — that is the intelligence of investigation. Therein, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the fourfold proposition (<s>catuṣkoṭikā</s>) is what I call [that which is] free from oneness, otherness, both, neither, existence, non-existence, permanence, and impermanence. All <s>dharmas</s>, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, are said to be free from this fourfold proposition. This fourfold proposition, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, should be applied in the examination of all <s>dharmas</s>. Therein, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, what is the intelligence that establishes attachment to the grasping of discriminative characteristics? Namely, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, that by which, through the attachment to the grasping of discriminative characteristics of the mind, one superimposes upon the great elements — whose characteristics of heat, fluidity, motion, and solidity are falsely imagined — through the attachment to the characteristics of thesis, reason, and example, by the superimposition of the unreal — that is the intelligence that establishes attachment to the grasping of discriminative characteristics. This, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the characteristic of the twofold intelligence, endowed with which <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, having entered the course of the characteristics of the selflessness of <s>dharmas</s> and persons, skilled in the stages of the practice of investigation through imageless intelligence, attain the first stage (<s>bhūmi</s>), enter a hundred <s>samādhis</s>, see a hundred <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> through the special attainment of <s>samādhi</s>, enter a hundred <s>kalpas</s> (aeons) past and future, and illuminate a hundred fields. Having illuminated a hundred fields, knowing the rules of the characteristics of progressively higher stages, sporting through the distinction of vows, anointed with the anointing of the <s>Dharmamegha</s> (Cloud of <s>Dharma</s> [stage]), having reached the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s inner stage, with <s>dharmas</s> well-bound to the ten ground-positions, they shine with diverse emanation-rays for the maturation of beings, concentrated in the bliss of their own inner realization.

body.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate bodhisattvena mahāsattvena mahābhūtabhautikakuśalena bhavitavyam / kathaṃ ca mahāmate bodhisattvo mahābhūtabhautikakuśalo bhavati? tatra mahāmate bodhisattvo mahāsattva itaḥ pratisaṃśikṣate tatsatyaṃ yatra mahābhūtānāmasaṃbhavo 'saṃbhūtāni cemāni mahāmate bhūtānīti prativipaśyati / evaṃ prativipaśyan nāma vikalpamātraṃ svacittadṛśyamātrāvabodhādbāhyabhāvābhāvānnāma cittadṛśyavikalpamātramidaṃ yaduta traidhātukaṃ mahābhūtabhautikarahitaṃ prativipaśyati cātuṣkoṭikanayaviśuddhimātmātmīyarahitaṃ yathābhūtasvalakṣaṇāvasthānāvasthitamanutpādasvalakṣaṇasiddham /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> should be skilled in the great elements (<s>mahābhūta</s>) and their derivatives (<s>bhautika</s>). And how, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, does a <s>Bodhisattva</s> become skilled in the great elements and their derivatives? Therein, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> trains himself thus, reflecting: 'It is true that the great elements do not arise,' and he contemplates: 'These elements, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, are unarisen.' Contemplating thus — [seeing that] name is mere discrimination, that from the awakening to [the fact that all is] merely the appearance of one's own mind, and from the non-existence of external entities, name is merely the discrimination of the appearances of the mind — namely, that the three realms are free from great elements and their derivatives — he contemplates the purity of the fourfold method, free from self and what belongs to self, established in the realization of the true own-characteristic, accomplished in the own-characteristic of non-arising.

body.text: tatra mahāmate mahābhūteṣu kathaṃ bhautikaṃ bhavati? yaduta snehavikalpamahābhūtaṃ mahāmate abdhātuṃ niṣpādayatyadhyātmabāhyam / utsāhavikalpamahābhūtaṃ mahāmate tejodhātuṃ niṣpādayatyadhyātmabāhyam / samudīraṇavikalpamahābhūtaṃ mahāmate vāyudhātuṃ niṣpādayatyadhyātmabāhyam / rūpaparicchedavikalpamahābhūtaṃ punarmahāmate pṛthivīdhātuṃ janayatyākāśasahitamadhyātmabāhyam / mithyāsatyābhiniveśātpañcaskandhakadambakaṃ mahābhūtabhautikaṃ pravartate / vijñānaṃ punarmahāmate vicitrapadaviṣayābhiniveśābhilāṣahetutvādvijñānaṃ pravartate 'nyagatisaṃdhau / pṛthivībhūtabhautikānāṃ mahāmate kāraṇamasti mahābhūtāni, na tu mahābhūtānām / tatkasya hetoḥ? yaduta bhāvaliṅgalakṣaṇagrahaṇasaṃsthānakriyāyogavatāṃ mahāmate kriyāsaṃyogotpattirbhavati nāliṅgavatām / tasmādetanmahāmate mahābhūtabhautikalakṣaṇaṃ tīrthakarairvikalpyate na tu mayā //
body.translated_text: Therein, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, how do the derivatives come to be among the great elements? Namely, the great element of the discrimination of moisture (<s>sneha</s>), O <s>Mahāmati</s>, produces the water-element (<s>abdhātu</s>), internal and external. The great element of the discrimination of energy (<s>utsāha</s>), O <s>Mahāmati</s>, produces the fire-element (<s>tejodhātu</s>), internal and external. The great element of the discrimination of movement (<s>samudīraṇa</s>), O <s>Mahāmati</s>, produces the wind-element (<s>vāyudhātu</s>), internal and external. The great element of the discrimination of form-delimitation (<s>rūpapariccheda</s>), moreover, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, produces the earth-element (<s>pṛthivīdhātu</s>) together with space, internal and external. Through attachment to the false and the real, the cluster of the five aggregates (<s>skandha</s>) operates as the great elements and their derivatives. Consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>), moreover, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, because of being the cause of craving for objects of diverse terms, operates at the juncture of other destinies. For the derivatives of the earth-element, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the great elements are the cause; but not for the great elements [themselves]. For what reason? Because, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, for those possessing the conjunction of activity with signs, characteristics, grasping, configuration, and function, there is arising from the conjunction of activity — not for those without signs. Therefore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, this characteristic of great elements and derivatives is conceptualized by heretical teachers, not by me.

body.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate skandhānāṃ skandhasvabhāvalakṣaṇaṃ nirdekṣyāmaḥ / tatra mahāmate pañca skandhāḥ / katame? yaduta rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānāni / tatra mahāmate catvāraḥ skandhā arūpiṇo vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārāṃ vijñānaṃ ca / rūpaṃ mahāmate cāturmahābhautikam, bhūtāni ca parasparavilakṣaṇāni / na ca mahāmate arūpiṇāṃ catuṣkasaṃkhyā bhavatyākāśavat / tadyathā mahāmate ākāśaṃ saṃkhyālakṣaṇātītam, atha ca vikalpyate evamākāśamiti, evameva mahāmate skandhāḥ saṃkhyālakṣaṇagaṇanātītā bhāvābhāvavivarjitāścātuṣkoṭikarahitāḥ saṃkhyāgaṇanānirdeśena nirdiśyante bālairna tvāryaiḥ //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, we shall explain the inherent-nature-characteristic of the aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>). Therein, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, there are five aggregates. Which? Namely, form (<s>rūpa</s>), feeling (<s>vedanā</s>), perception (<s>saṃjñā</s>), formations (<s>saṃskāra</s>), and consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>). Therein, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the four aggregates are formless — feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness. Form, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, consists of the four great elements, and the elements are mutually distinct in characteristics. But, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the enumeration 'four' does not apply to the formless [aggregates], like space. Just as, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, space transcends the characteristic of enumeration, yet is conceptualized as 'thus is space'; even so, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the aggregates transcend the characteristic and calculation of enumeration, are free from existence and non-existence, free from the fourfold proposition, and are described by the childish through enumeration, calculation, and description — not by the noble ones.

body.text: āryaiḥ punarmahāmate māyāvicitrarūpākṛtivadanyānanyavarjitāḥ prajñāpyante svapnabimbapuruṣavat / āśrayānanyatvādāryajñānagatisaṃmohānmahāmate skandhavikalpaḥ khyāyate / etanmahāmate skandhānāṃ skandhasvabhāvalakṣaṇam / sa ca vikalpastvayā vyāvartanīyaḥ, vyāvṛtya viviktadharmopadeśaḥ karaṇīyaḥ / sarvabuddhaparṣanmaṇḍaleṣu tīrthyadṛṣṭinivāraṇāya viviktadharmopadeśena mahāmate kriyamāṇena dharmanairātmyadarśanaṃ viśudhyate, dūraṃgamābhūmipraveśaśca bhavati / sa dūraṃgamāṃ mahābhūmimanupraviśya anekasamādhivaśavartī bhavati / manomayakāyapratilambhācca samādhiṃ māyopamaṃ pratilabhate / balābhijñāvaśitāgatiṃgataḥ sarvasattvopajīvyo bhavati pṛthivīvat / yathā mahāmate mahāpṛthivī sarvasattvopajīvyā bhavati, evameva mahāmate bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ sarvasattvopajīvyo bhavati //
body.translated_text: By the noble ones, moreover, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, [the aggregates] are designated as free from sameness and difference, like the diverse forms fashioned by a magician, like a man seen in a dream or reflection. Because of non-difference from the support, and because of the confusion of the course of noble knowledge, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the discrimination of aggregates appears. This, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the inherent-nature-characteristic of the aggregates. And that discrimination is to be abandoned by you; having abandoned it, the teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> of solitude should be given. In all the <s>maṇḍala</s>-assemblies of the <s>Buddhas</s>, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, by giving the teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> of solitude for the purpose of averting heretical views, the vision of the selflessness of <s>dharmas</s> is purified, and entry into the Far-Reaching (<s>Dūraṃgamā</s>) stage occurs. Having entered that great Far-Reaching stage, one becomes master of many <s>samādhis</s>. And from the attainment of the mind-made body (<s>manomayakāya</s>), one attains the illusion-like <s>samādhi</s>. Having entered the course of powers (<s>bala</s>), superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>), and masteries (<s>vaśitā</s>), one becomes the support of all beings, like the earth. Just as, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the great earth is the support of all beings, even so, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> becomes the support of all beings.

body.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate caturvidhaṃ nirvāṇam / katamaccaturvidham? yaduta bhāvasvabhāvābhāvanirvāṇaṃ lakṣaṇavicitrabhāvābhāvanirvāṇaṃ svalakṣaṇabhāvābhāvāvabodhanirvāṇaṃ skandhānāṃ svasāmānyalakṣaṇasaṃtatiprabandhavyucchedanirvāṇam / etanmahāmate caturvidhaṃ tīrthakarāṇāṃ nirvāṇaṃ na tu matpravacane / matpravacane punarmahāmate vikalpakasya manovijñānasya vyāvṛttirnirvāṇamityucyate //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, <s>nirvāṇa</s> is of four kinds. Of which four kinds? Namely: the <s>nirvāṇa</s> of the non-existence of the inherent nature of entities (<s>bhāvasvabhāvābhāvanirvāṇa</s>), the <s>nirvāṇa</s> of the non-existence of the diverse entities of characteristics (<s>lakṣaṇavicitrabhāvābhāvanirvāṇa</s>), the <s>nirvāṇa</s> of the awakening to the non-existence of one's own characteristic-entity (<s>svalakṣaṇabhāvābhāvāvabodhanirvāṇa</s>), and the <s>nirvāṇa</s> of the cutting off of the continuum-series of the specific and general characteristics of the aggregates (<s>skandhānāṃ svasāmānyalakṣaṇasaṃtatiprabandhavyucchedanirvāṇa</s>). This, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the fourfold <s>nirvāṇa</s> of heretical teachers — not in my teaching. In my teaching, moreover, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the turning-away (<s>vyāvṛtti</s>) of the discriminating <s>manovijñāna</s> (mind-consciousness) is called <s>nirvāṇa</s>.

body.text: mahāmatirāha - nanu bhagavatā aṣṭau vijñānāni vyavasthāpitāni? bhagavānāha - vyavasthāpitāni mahāmate / mahāmatirāha - tadyadi bhagavan vyavasthāpitāni, tatkathaṃ manovijñānasyaiva
body.translated_text: <s>Mahāmati</s> said: 'Has the Blessed One not established eight <s>vijñānas</s> (consciousnesses)?' The Blessed One said: 'They have been established, O <s>Mahāmati</s>.' <s>Mahāmati</s> said: 'If, Blessed One, they have been established, then how is it the turning-away of the <s>manovijñāna</s> alone,

body.text: vyāvṛttirbhavati na tu saptānāṃ vijñānānām? bhagavānāha - taddhetvālambanatvānmahāmate saptānāṃ vijñānānāṃ pravṛttirbhavati / manovijñānaṃ punarmahāmate viṣayaparicchedābhiniveśena pravartamānaṃ vāsanābhirālayavijñānaṃ prapuṣṇāti / manaḥ sahitamātmātmīyagrāhābhiniveśamanyanākāreṇānupravartate / abhinnaśarīralakṣaṇamālayavijñānahetvālambanaṃ svacittadṛśyaviṣayābhiniveśāccittakalāpaḥ pravartate 'nyonyahetukaḥ / udadhitaraṃgā iva mahāmate svacittadṛśyaviṣayapavaneritāḥ pravartante nivartante ca / atastena mahāmate manovijñānena vyāvṛttena saptānāṃ vijñānānāṃ vyāvṛttirbhavati //
body.translated_text: and not of the seven [other] <s>vijñānas</s>?' The Blessed One said: 'Because it is their cause and object, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the activity of the seven <s>vijñānas</s> occurs. The <s>manovijñāna</s>, moreover, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, operating through attachment to the delimitation of objects, nourishes the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> (store-consciousness) with impressions. Accompanied by <s>manas</s>, [it] follows along with the grasping of self and what belongs to self in a different mode. The cluster of consciousness operates, with undivided body-characteristics, having the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> as its cause and object, through attachment to the objects appearing as one's own mind — mutually causative. Just as ocean waves, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, stirred by the wind of the objects appearing as one's own mind, arise and cease; so, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, when that <s>manovijñāna</s> has turned away, the turning-away of the seven <s>vijñānas</s> occurs.'

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Therein this is said:

children.text: nāhaṃ nirvāmi bhāvena kriyayā lakṣaṇena ca /
children.translated_text: I do not attain <s>nirvāṇa</s> by entity, action, or characteristic;
when the <s>vijñāna</s> that is the cause of discrimination ceases, I indeed am in <s>nirvāṇa</s>. [Laṅk 2.177]
Caused by that [manovijñāna], resting on that as object, dependent on the course of <s>manas</s>,

children.text: hetuṃ dadāti cittasya vijñānaṃ ca samāśritam // Lank_2.178 //
children.translated_text: it provides the cause for the mind, and consciousness too is dependent [on it]. [Laṅk 2.178]
Just as when a great ocean dries up, there is no arising of waves,

children.text: tathā vijñānavaicitryaṃ niruddhaṃ na pravartate // Lank_2.179 //
children.translated_text: so too the variety of <s>vijñānas</s>, having ceased, does not operate. [Laṅk 2.179]

body.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate parikalpitasvabhāvaprabhedanayalakṣaṇamupadekṣyāmo yena parikalpitasvabhāvaprabhedanayalakṣaṇena suprativibhāgaviddhena tvaṃ ca anye ca bodhisattvā mahāsattvā vikalpakalparahitāḥ pratyātmāryasvagatitīrthyanayagatisudṛṣṭabuddhayo grāhyagrāhakavikalpaprahīṇāḥ paratantravividhavicitralakṣaṇaṃ parikalpitasvabhāvākāraṃ na prativikalpayiṣyanti / tatra mahāmate katamatparikalpitasvabhāvaprabhedanayalakṣaṇam? yaduta abhilāpavikalpo 'vidheyavikalpo lakṣaṇavikalpo 'rthavikalpaḥ svabhāvavikalpo hetuvikalpo dṛṣṭivikalpo yuktivikalpa utpādavikalpo 'nutpādavikalpaḥ saṃbandhavikalpo bandhābandhavikalpaḥ / etanmahāmate parikalpitasvabhāvaprabhedanayalakṣaṇam //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, we shall teach the characteristic of the method of differentiation of the imagined inherent nature (<s>parikalpitasvabhāvaprabhedanayalakṣaṇa</s>), by which characteristic of the method of differentiation of the imagined inherent nature — being pierced by [this] well-differentiated [understanding] — you and other <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas</s>, free from conceptual discrimination, with intelligence that has well-seen the course of the inner noble realization [as distinct from] the course of heretical methods, having abandoned the discrimination of grasper and grasped, will not conceptually discriminate the imagined-inherent-nature-form of the diverse and varied characteristics of the dependent [nature]. Therein, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, what is the characteristic of the method of differentiation of the imagined inherent nature? Namely: the discrimination of speech (<s>abhilāpavikalpa</s>), the discrimination of the expressible (<s>abhidheyavikalpa</s>), the discrimination of characteristics (<s>lakṣaṇavikalpa</s>), the discrimination of meaning (<s>arthavikalpa</s>), the discrimination of inherent nature (<s>svabhāvavikalpa</s>), the discrimination of cause (<s>hetuvikalpa</s>), the discrimination of views (<s>dṛṣṭivikalpa</s>), the discrimination of reasoning (<s>yuktivikalpa</s>), the discrimination of arising (<s>utpādavikalpa</s>), the discrimination of non-arising (<s>anutpādavikalpa</s>), the discrimination of connection (<s>saṃbandhavikalpa</s>), and the discrimination of bondage and non-bondage (<s>bandhābandhavikalpa</s>). This, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the characteristic of the method of differentiation of the imagined inherent nature.

body.text: tatra mahāmate abhilāpavikalpaḥ katamaḥ? yaduta vicitrasvaragītamādhuryābhiniveśaḥ / eṣa mahāmate abhilāpavikalpaḥ / tatra mahāmate abhidheyavikalpaḥ katamaḥ? yaduta asti tatkiṃcidabhidheyavastu svabhāvakamāryajñānagatigamyaṃ yadāśrityābhilāpaḥ pravartate iti vikalpayati / tatra lakṣaṇavikalpaḥ katamaḥ? yaduta tasminnevābhidheye mṛgatṛṣṇākhye lakṣaṇavaicitryābhiniveśenābhiniveśate yaduta uṣṇadravacalakaṭhinalakṣaṇātsarvabhāvān vikalpayati / tatra arthavikalpaḥ katamaḥ? yaduta suvarṇarūpyavividharatnārthaviṣayābhilāpaḥ / tatra svabhāvavikalpaḥ katamaḥ? yaduta bhāvasvabhāvāvadhāraṇamidamevamidaṃ nānyatheti tīrthyavikalpadṛṣṭyā vikalpayanti / tatra hetuvikalpaḥ katamaḥ? yaduta yadyena hetupratyayena sadasatorvibhajyate hetulakṣaṇotpattitaḥ sa hetuvikalpaḥ / tatra dṛṣṭivikalpaḥ katamaḥ? yaduta nāstyastitvaikatvānyatvobhayānubhayakudṛṣṭitīrthyavikalpābhiniveśaḥ /
body.translated_text: Therein, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, what is the discrimination of speech? Namely, the attachment to the sweetness of diverse voices and songs. This, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the discrimination of speech. Therein, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, what is the discrimination of the expressible? Namely, one conceptualizes: 'There is some expressible reality having its own nature, accessible to the course of noble knowledge, depending on which speech operates.' Therein, what is the discrimination of characteristics? Namely, when in that very expressible — which is called a 'mirage' — one becomes attached through attachment to the variety of characteristics: namely, one conceptualizes all entities from the characteristics of heat, fluidity, motion, and solidity. Therein, what is the discrimination of meaning? Namely, the speech regarding objects of gold, silver, and various jewels as meaning. Therein, what is the discrimination of inherent nature? Namely, the ascertainment of the inherent nature of entities — 'this is just so, this is not otherwise' — conceptualizing with the discriminative view of heretics. Therein, what is the discrimination of cause? Namely, that which distinguishes between the existent and non-existent by whatever cause and condition, through the arising of the characteristic of cause — that is the discrimination of cause. Therein, what is the discrimination of views? Namely, the attachment to heretical discriminative wrong views of non-existence, existence, oneness, otherness, both, and neither.

body.text: tatra yuktivikalpaḥ katamaḥ? yaduta ātmātmīyalakṣaṇayuktivigrahopadeśaḥ / tatra utpādavikalpaḥ katamaḥ? yaduta pratyayaiḥ sadasatorbhāvasyotpādābhiniveśaḥ / tatra anutpādavikalpaḥ katamaḥ? yaduta anutpannapūrvāḥ sarvabhāvā abhūtvā pratyayairbhavantyahetuśarīrāḥ / tatra saṃbandhavikalpaḥ katamaḥ? yaduta saha saṃbadhyate suvarṇatantuvat / tatra bandhābandhavikalpaḥ katamaḥ? yaduta bandhahetubandhyābhiniveśavat / yathā puruṣaḥ pāśasaṃyogādrajjugranthiḥ kriyate mucyate ca / evaṃ mahāmate parikalpitasvabhāvaprabhedanayalakṣaṇam, yasmin parikalpitasvabhāvaprabhedanayalakṣaṇe sarvabālapṛthagjanā abhiniviśante / sadasataḥ paratantrābhiniveśābhiniviṣṭā mahāmate parikalpitasvabhāvavaicitryamabhiniviśante / māyāśrayavaicitryadarśanavadanyamāyādarśanabuddhyā bālairvikalpyante / māyā ca mahāmate vaicitryānnānyā nānanyā / yadyanyā syāt, vaicitryaṃ māyāhetukaṃ na syāt / athānanyā syāt, vaicitryānmāyāvaicitryayorvibhāgo na syāt / sa ca dṛṣṭo vibhāgaḥ / tasmānnānyā nānanyā / ata etasmātkāraṇānmahāmate tvayā anyaiśca bodhisattvairmahāsattvairmāyā nāstyastitvena nābhiniveṣṭavyā //
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the discrimination of reasoning (<s>yuktivikalpa</s>)? Namely, the teaching of the debate regarding the characteristic of self and what belongs to self, based on reasoning. Therein, what is the discrimination of arising (<s>utpādavikalpa</s>)? Namely, the attachment to the arising of an entity from the existent and non-existent through conditions. Therein, what is the discrimination of non-arising (<s>anutpādavikalpa</s>)? Namely, [the notion that] all entities, not having arisen before, not having existed, come into being through conditions and have causeless bodies. Therein, what is the discrimination of connection (<s>saṃbandhavikalpa</s>)? Namely, that [things] are connected together, like gold and thread. Therein, what is the discrimination of bondage and non-bondage (<s>bandhābandhavikalpa</s>)? Namely, like the attachment to a cause of bondage and a binder — just as a person, through contact with a snare, has a rope-knot made and is also freed. Thus, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the characteristic of the method of differentiation of the imagined inherent nature (<s>parikalpitasvabhāva</s>), in which all foolish ordinary beings become attached. Attached to the attachment of the dependent (<s>paratantra</s>) to the existent and non-existent, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, they become attached to the variety of the imagined inherent nature. They are conceptually discriminated by the childish with the understanding that an illusion is something other than the vision of the variety of the illusion's basis. But illusion, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is neither different from nor non-different from its variety. If it were different, the variety would not have illusion as its cause. If it were non-different, there would be no distinction between illusion and its variety. But that distinction is observed. Therefore, [illusion] is neither different nor non-different. For this very reason, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, neither you nor other <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas</s> should be attached to illusion as existent or non-existent.

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Therein it is said:

children.translated_text: Mind, connected with objects — knowledge operates in reasoning;

children.text: nirābhāse viśeṣe ca prajñā vai saṃpravartate // Lank_2.180 //
children.translated_text: but in the appearance-free and the distinctive, wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) indeed operates. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.180 ||
The imagined inherent nature does not exist in the dependent;

children.text: kalpitaṃ gṛhyate bhrāntyā paratantraṃ na kalpyate // Lank_2.181 //
children.translated_text: the imagined is grasped through delusion; the dependent is not [merely] imagined. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.181 ||
Just as illusion is not established through the production of varied limbs,

children.text: nimittaṃ hi tathā citraṃ kalpyamānaṃ na sidhyati // Lank_2.182 //
children.translated_text: so too a sign, however varied, when conceptually constructed, is not established. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.182 ||
The sign consists of depravity; bondage arises from mind;
the imagined, through ignorance, is conceptually discriminated by the dependent. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.183 ||
That which is this imagined entity — that is indeed the dependent;

children.text: kalpitaṃ hi vicitrābhaṃ paratantre vikalpyate // Lank_2.184 //
children.translated_text: the imagined, with its varied appearances, is conceptually discriminated in the dependent. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.184 ||
The conventional (<s>saṃvṛti</s>) and the ultimate (<s>paramārtha</s>), and a third — the causeless;
the imagined is aptly called the conventional; from cutting that — the domain of the noble. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.185 ||

children.text: yathā hi yogināṃ vastu citramekaṃ virājate /
children.translated_text: Just as for <s>yogins</s>, a single varied object shines forth,

children.text: na hyasti citratā tatra tathā kalpitalakṣaṇam // Lank_2.186 //
children.translated_text: yet there is no variety therein — so too the characteristic of the imagined. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.186 ||
Just as those with cataracts (<s>timira</s>) conceptually construct the varied perception of forms,

children.text: timiraṃ na rūpaṃ nārūpaṃ paratantraṃ tathābudhaiḥ // Lank_2.187 //
children.translated_text: the cataract is neither form nor non-form — so is the dependent for the unwise. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.187 ||

children.text: haimaṃ syāttu yathā śuddhaṃ jalaṃ kaluṣavarjitam /
children.translated_text: Just as gold would be pure, water free from turbidity,

children.text: gaganaṃ hi ghanābhāvāttathā śuddhaṃ vikalpitam // Lank_2.188 //
children.translated_text: and space [pure] due to the absence of clouds — so is the pure, [but] conceptually discriminated. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.188 ||

children.text: nāsti vai kalpito bhāvaḥ paratantraśca vidyate /
children.translated_text: The imagined entity does not [truly] exist, yet the dependent is found;
those who discriminate through superimposition and denial perish. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.189 ||
If the imagined were non-existent by the inherent nature of the dependent,

children.text: vinā bhāvena vai bhāvo bhāvaścābhāvasaṃbhavaḥ // Lank_2.190 //
children.translated_text: then existence without existence, and existence arising from non-existence [would follow]. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.190 ||
Depending on the imagined, the dependent is apprehended;
from the connection of sign and name, the imagined arises. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.191 ||
Absolutely unaccomplished, the imagined is not produced from another;

children.text: tadā prajñāyate śuddhaṃ svabhāvaṃ pāramārthikam // Lank_2.192 //
children.translated_text: then the pure ultimate inherent nature becomes evident. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.192 ||
The imagined is of ten kinds; the dependent is of six kinds;
inner <s>Suchness</s> (<s>tathatā</s>) is to be known — hence there is no [further] qualification. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.193 ||

children.text: pañca dharmā bhavettattvaṃ svabhāvā hi trayastathā /
children.translated_text: The five <s>dharmas</s> would be the reality, and the three inherent natures likewise;
the <s>yogin</s> who illuminates these does not transgress <s>Suchness</s>. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.194 ||
The sign is indeed the dependent; what is named is the imagined;
but the imagined sign proceeds from the dependent. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.195 ||

children.text: buddhyā vivecyamānaṃ tu na tantraṃ nāpi kalpitam /
children.translated_text: When discriminated by wisdom, it is neither the dependent nor the imagined;

children.text: niṣpanno nāsti vai bhāvaḥ kathaṃ buddhyā vikalpyate // Lank_2.196 //
children.translated_text: the perfected entity does not exist [as conceptualized] — how could it be discriminated by intellect? || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.196 ||
The perfected entity exists, free from existence and non-existence;

children.text: bhāvābhāvavinirmukto dvau svabhāvau kathaṃ nu tau // Lank_2.197 //
children.translated_text: freed from existence and non-existence — how then are those two inherent natures? || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.197 ||
In the imagined inherent nature, the two inherent natures are established;

children.text: kalpitaṃ dṛśyate citraṃ viśuddhaṃ cāryagocaram // Lank_2.198 //
children.translated_text: the imagined is seen as varied; the pure is the domain of the noble. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.198 ||
The imagined, with varied appearances, is conceptually discriminated by the dependent;

children.text: anyathā kalpyamānaṃ hi tīrthyavādaṃ samāśrayet // Lank_2.199 //
children.translated_text: if conceptually constructed otherwise, it would resort to the doctrine of the non-Buddhist teachers. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.199 ||
Conceptual construction is called 'the imagined,' from seeing and from the arising of a cause;
freed from the twofold conceptual discrimination — that indeed is the perfected (<s>niṣpanna</s>). || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.200 ||

body.text: punarapi mahāmatirāha - deśayatu me bhagavān pratyātmāryajñānagatilakṣaṇamekayānaṃ ca, yena bhagavan pratyātmaikayānagatilakṣaṇena ahaṃ ca anye ca bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ pratyātmāryajñānaikayānakuśalā aparapraṇeyā bhaviṣyanti buddhadharmeṣu //
body.translated_text: <s>Mahāmati</s> again said: May the <s>Bhagavān</s> teach me the characteristic of the course of inner noble knowledge, and the one vehicle (<s>ekayāna</s>), so that by the characteristic of the inner course of the one vehicle, I and other <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas</s>, being skilled in the one vehicle of inner noble knowledge, may become free from being led by others in the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: bhagavānāha - tena hi mahāmate śṛṇu, sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasikuru / bhāṣiṣye 'haṃ te / sādhu bhagavanniti mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavataḥ pratyaśrauṣīt / bhagavāṃstasyaitadavocat - pramāṇāptopadeśavikalpābhāvānmahāmate bodhisattvo mahāsattva ekākī rahogataḥ svapratyātmabuddhyā vicārayatyaparapraṇeyo dṛṣṭivikalpavivarjita uttarottaratathāgatabhūmipraveśanatayā vyāyamate / etanmahāmate svapratyātmāryajñānagatilakṣaṇam / tatra ekayānagatilakṣaṇaṃ katamat?
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: Then, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, listen, and attend well and thoroughly. I shall teach you. 'Very well, O <s>Bhagavān</s>,' the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s> assented to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said this to him: Due to the absence of conceptual discrimination regarding authoritative instruction (<s>pramāṇāptopadeśa</s>), O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>, alone and in seclusion, investigates through his own inner wisdom, not led by others, free from the conceptual discrimination of views, and strives through progressive entry into the <s>Tathāgata</s>-stages. This, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the characteristic of the course of one's own inner noble knowledge. Therein, what is the characteristic of the one-vehicle course?

body.text: yaduta ekayānamārgādhigamāvabodhādekayānamiti vadāmi / ekayānamārgādhigamāvabodhaḥ katamaḥ? yaduta grāhyagrāhakavikalpayathābhūtāvasthānādapravṛttervikalpasya ekayānāvabodhaḥ kṛto bhavati / eṣa ekayānāvabodho mahāmate nānyatīrthyaśrāvakapratyekabuddhabrahmādibhiḥ prāptapūrvo 'nyatra mayā / ata etasmātkāraṇānmahāmate ekayānamityucyate //
body.translated_text: Namely, because of the awakening to the attainment of the one-vehicle path, I call it 'the one vehicle.' What is the awakening to the attainment of the one-vehicle path? Namely, from the abiding in the true state of the conceptual discrimination of grasper and grasped, and from the non-operation of conceptual discrimination — the awakening to the one vehicle is accomplished. This is the awakening to the one vehicle, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, not attained before by any non-Buddhist teachers, <s>Śrāvakas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, or others — except by me. For this very reason, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, it is called the one vehicle.

body.text: mahāmatirāha - kiṃ kāraṇaṃ bhagavatā yānatrayamupadiṣṭam, ekayānaṃ nopadiśyate? bhagavānāha - svayamaparinirvāṇadharmatvānmahāmate sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhānāmekayānaṃ na vadāmi / yasmānmahāmate sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhāstathāgatavinayavivekayogopadeśena vimucyante na svayam //
body.translated_text: <s>Mahāmati</s> asked: For what reason has the <s>Bhagavān</s> taught the three vehicles and not the one vehicle? The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: Because all <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> are by nature incapable of their own <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, I do not speak of one vehicle for them. Since, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, all <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> are liberated by the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s instruction in discipline, solitude, and <s>yoga</s> — not by themselves.

body.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate jñeyāvaraṇakarmavāsanāprahīṇatvātsarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhānāṃ naikayānam / dharmanairātmyānavabodhācca acintyapariṇāmacyuteraprāptivācca yānatrayaṃ deśayāmi śrāvakāṇām / yadā teṣāṃ mahāmate sarvadoṣavāsanāḥ prahīṇā bhavanti dharmanairātmyāvabodhāt, tadā te vāsanādoṣasamādhimadābhāvādanāsravadhātau prativibudhyante / punarapi lokottarānāsravadhātuparyāpannān saṃbhārān paripūrya acintyadharmakāyavaśavartitāṃ pratilapsyante //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, because all <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> have not abandoned the <s>karma</s>-impressions of the obscuration of the knowable (<s>jñeyāvaraṇa</s>), and because of the non-awakening to the selflessness of <s>dharmas</s>, and the non-attainment of the inconceivable transformation and falling-away, I teach the three vehicles for <s>Śrāvakas</s>. When, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, all their fault-impressions have been abandoned through the awakening to the selflessness of <s>dharmas</s>, then they awaken in the undefiled realm (<s>anāsravadhātu</s>), free from the intoxication of the <s>samādhi</s> of impressional faults. And furthermore, having fulfilled the requisites belonging to the supramundane undefiled realm, they will attain mastery over the inconceivable <s>Dharmakāya</s> (truth-body).

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Therein it is said:

children.translated_text: The vehicle of the gods, the vehicle of <s>Brahmā</s>, the <s>Śrāvaka</s> [vehicle] likewise,

children.text: tāthāgataṃ ca pratyekaṃ yānānetān vadāmyaham // Lank_2.201 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Tathāgata</s>[-vehicle] and the <s>Pratyeka</s>[-vehicle] — these vehicles I declare. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.201 ||

children.text: yānānāṃ nāsti vai niṣṭhā yāvaccittaṃ pravartate /
children.translated_text: There is no finality of vehicles as long as mind operates;

children.text: citte tu vai parāvṛtte na yānaṃ na ca yāninaḥ // Lank_2.202 //
children.translated_text: but when the mind is turned back (<s>parāvṛtta</s>), there is neither vehicle nor traveler. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.202 ||
There is no establishment of vehicles; I speak of vehicle-differentiation
for the purpose of drawing along the childish — [thus] I speak of vehicle-differentiation. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.203 ||
The three liberations likewise, and the selflessness of <s>dharmas</s> —
called equality-knowledge and affliction, they are free from those [categories of] liberation. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.204 ||
Just as a piece of wood on the ocean is carried away by waves,

children.text: tathā hi śrāvako mūḍho lakṣaṇena pravāhyate // Lank_2.205 //
children.translated_text: so the deluded <s>Śrāvaka</s> is carried away by [attachment to] characteristics. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.205 ||
Bound by the afflictions of impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>), freed from manifest afflictions (<s>paryutthāna</s>),
intoxicated by the intoxication of <s>samādhi</s>, they abide in the undefiled realm. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.206 ||

children.text: niṣṭhāgatirna tasyāsti na ca bhūyo nivartate /
children.translated_text: There is no final course for him, nor does he return again;

children.text: samādhikāyaṃ saṃprāpya ā kalpānna prabudhyate // Lank_2.207 //
children.translated_text: having attained the <s>samādhi</s>-body, he does not awaken for an [entire] <s>kalpa</s> (aeon). || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.207 ||
Just as an intoxicated man awakens when the liquor is gone,

children.text: tathā te buddhadharmākhyaṃ kāyaṃ prāpsyanti māmakam // Lank_2.208 //
children.translated_text: so they will attain my body called the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharma</s>. || <s>Laṅk</s> 2.208 ||

body.text: iti laṅkāvatāre ṣaṭtriṃśatsāhasrasarvadharmasamuccayo nāma dvitīyaḥ parivartaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Laṅkāvatāra</s>, [ends] the second chapter named 'The Collection of All Dharmas in Thirty-Six Thousand.'

body.text: START Parivarta 3
body.translated_text: START Chapter 3

body.text: Anityatāparivarto nāma tṛtīyaḥ /
body.translated_text: The third chapter, named 'The Chapter on Impermanence.'

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān punarapi mahāmatiṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvametadavocat - manomayakāyagatiprabhedanayalakṣaṇaṃ mahāmate upadekṣyāmi / tacchṛṇu, sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasikuru / bhāṣiṣye 'haṃ te / sādhu bhagavanniti mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavataḥ pratyaśrauṣīt / bhagavāṃstasyaitadavocat - triprakāro mahāmate kāyo manomayaḥ / katamastriprakāraḥ? yaduta samādhisukhasamāpattimanomayo dharmasvabhāvāvabodhamanomayo nikāyasahajasaṃskārakriyāmanomayaśca / prathamottarottarabhūmilakṣaṇaparijñānādadhigacchanti yoginaḥ / tatra katamo mahāmate samādhisukhasamāpattimanomayaḥ kāyaḥ? yaduta tricaturthapañcamyāṃ bhūmau svacittavividhavivekavihāreṇacittodadhipravṛttitaraṃgavijñānalakṣaṇasukhasamāpattimanaso 'pravṛttiḥ svacittadṛśyaviṣayābhāvābhāvaparijñānānmanaso manomayaḥ kāya ityucyate / tatra dharmasvabhāvāvabodhamanomayaḥ kāyaḥ katamaḥ? yaduta aṣṭamyāṃ bhūmau māyādidharmanirābhāsapravicayāvabodhena cittāśrayaparāvṛttasya māyopamasamādhipratilambhādanyeṣāṃ ca samādhimukhānāṃ pratilambhādanekalakṣaṇavaśitābhijñākusumitaṃ manojavasadṛśaṃ māyāsvapnabimbaprakhyamabhautikaṃ bhūtabhautikasadṛśaṃ sarvarūpaviciatrāṅgasamuditaṃ sarvabuddhakṣetraparṣanmaṇḍalānugataṃ kāyaṃ dharmasvabhāvagatiṃgatatvānmanomaya ityucyate / tatra nikāyasahajasaṃskārakriyāmanomayaḥ kāyaḥ katamaḥ? yaduta sarvabuddhadharmapratyātmādhigamasukhalakṣaṇāvabodhānnikāyasahajasaṃskārakriyāmanomaya ityucyate / atra te mahāmate kāyatrayalakṣaṇapravicayāvabodhe yogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> again said this to the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s>: I shall teach you, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the characteristic of the method of the differentiation of the course of the mind-made body (<s>manomayakāya</s>). Listen to that, and attend well and thoroughly. I shall teach you. 'Very well, O <s>Bhagavān</s>,' the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s> assented to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said this to him: The mind-made body, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is of three kinds. Of which three kinds? Namely, the mind-made [body] of the blissful attainment of <s>samādhi</s>, the mind-made [body] of the awakening to the inherent nature of <s>dharmas</s>, and the mind-made [body] of the natural activity of the formations of the type [of being]. <s>Yogins</s> attain [these] through the comprehension of the characteristics of the progressively higher stages. Therein, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, what is the mind-made body of the blissful attainment of <s>samādhi</s>? Namely, at the third, fourth, and fifth stages, through the varied solitary abiding of one's own mind, the non-operation of the mind in the blissful attainment characterized by the wave-consciousness arising in the ocean of mind, and through the comprehension of the existence and non-existence of the objects appearing as one's own mind — this is called the mind-made body, born from the mind. Therein, what is the mind-made body of the awakening to the inherent nature of <s>dharmas</s>? Namely, at the eighth stage, through the awakening to the investigation of the appearance-free nature of phenomena such as illusion, from the attainment of the illusion-like <s>samādhi</s> and other <s>samādhi</s>-gateways by one whose mind-basis has been turned back, [the <s>Bodhisattva</s> obtains] a body that blossoms with various mastery-characteristics and superknowledges, swift as thought, resembling illusion, dream, and reflection, immaterial yet resembling material elements, endowed with all varied forms and limbs, traversing all <s>Buddha</s>-field assemblies and <s>maṇḍalas</s>. Because it has entered the course of the inherent nature of <s>dharmas</s>, it is called mind-made. Therein, what is the mind-made body of the natural activity of the formations of the type [of being]? Namely, from the awakening to the characteristic of the bliss of inner self-realization of all <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, it is called the mind-made [body] of the natural activity of the formations of the type. Here, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, <s>yoga</s> should be practiced for the awakening to the investigation of the characteristic of the three bodies.

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Therein it is said:

children.text: na me yānaṃ mahāyānaṃ na ghoṣo na ca akṣarāḥ /
children.translated_text: For me, the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle) is not a vehicle, nor [mere] sound, nor syllables,

children.text: na satyā na vimokṣā vai na nirābhāsagocaram // Lank_3.1 //
children.translated_text: nor truths, nor liberations, nor the domain of the appearance-free. || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.1 ||
Rather, the <s>Mahāyāna</s> vehicle is the mastery of <s>samādhi</s>,
the varied mind-made body, adorned with the flowers of mastery. || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.2 ||

body.text: atha khalu mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ punarapi bhagavantametadavocat - pañcānantaryāṇi bhagavatā nirdiṣṭāni / katamāni tāni bhagavan pañcānantaryāṇi yānyadhyāpadya kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā avīciko bhavati? bhagavānāha - tena hi mahāmate śṛṇu, sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasikuru / bhāṣiṣye 'haṃ te / sādhu bhagavanniti mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavataḥ pratyaśrauṣīt / bhagavānetadavocat - tatra mahāmate pañcānantaryāṇi katamāni? yaduta mātṛpitrarhadvadhasaṃghabhedāstathāgatakāye duṣṭacittarudhirotpādaśca //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s> again addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s> thus: The five heinous acts (<s>ānantarya</s>) have been indicated by the <s>Bhagavān</s>. What, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, are those five heinous acts, having committed which a son or daughter of good family goes to <s>Avīci</s> [hell]? The <s>Bhagavān</s> replied: Then, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, listen, and attend well and thoroughly. I shall teach you. "Very well, <s>Bhagavān</s>," the <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s> assented to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said this: Therein, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, what are the five heinous acts? Namely, the killing of mother, the killing of father, the killing of an <s>Arhat</s>, the splitting of the <s>Saṅgha</s>, and the malicious drawing of blood from the body of a <s>Tathāgata</s>.

body.text: tatra mahāmate mātā katamā sattvānām? yaduta tṛṣṇā paunarbhavikī nandīrāgasahagatā mātṛtvenottiṣṭhate / avidyā pitṛtvenāyatanagrāmasyotpattaye / anayorubhayormātāpitroratyantamūlopacchedānmātṛpitṛvadho
body.translated_text: Therein, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, who is the mother of beings? It is craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>), which leads to renewed existence, accompanied by delight and passion — [this] arises in the role of mother. Ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) [arises] in the role of father, for the arising of the aggregate of sense-bases. From the complete uprooting of both these — mother and father — the killing of mother and father

body.text: bhavati / tatra anuśayānāmariprakhyāṇāṃ mūṣikāviṣavatprakopadharmiṇāmatyantasamuddhātādarhadvadho bhavati / tatra saṃdhabhedaḥ katamaḥ? yaduta bhinnānyonyalakṣaṇasya skandhasaṃghātasyātyantamūlopaghātātsaṃghabheda ityucyate / svasāmānyabāhyasvacittadṛśyamātrāvabodhakānāṃ mahāmate aṣṭānāṃ vijñānakāyānāṃ vimokṣatrayānāsravaduṣṭavikalpenātyantopaghātādvijñānabuddhasya duṣṭacittarudhirotpādanādānantaryakārītyucyate / etāni mahāmate ādhyātmikāni pañcānantaryāṇi yānyadhyāpadya kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā ānantaryakārī bhavatyabhisamitadharmaḥ //
body.translated_text: occurs. Therein, from the complete eradication of the latent tendencies (<s>anuśaya</s>), which are like enemies, having the nature of flaring up like rat-poison, the killing of an <s>Arhat</s> occurs. Therein, what is the splitting of the <s>Saṅgha</s>? From the complete destruction at the root of the aggregate-combination of aggregates (<s>skandha</s>) with mutually different characteristics, it is called the splitting of the <s>Saṅgha</s>. The eight bodies of consciousness (<s>vijñānakāya</s>), O <s>Mahāmati</s>, which awaken [one] to the mere appearance of one's own mind (<s>svacittadṛśyamātra</s>) through specific, general, and external [characteristics] — from the complete destruction [of these] by the impure discrimination of the three liberations and the outflow-free [states], one is called a perpetrator of the heinous act of maliciously drawing blood from the <s>Buddha</s> of consciousness. These, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, are the five internal heinous acts, having committed which a son or daughter of good family becomes a perpetrator of heinous acts, one who has realized the <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate bāhyāni te ānantaryāṇyupadekṣyāmi, yairupadiṣṭaistvaṃ ca anye ca bodhisattvā anāgate 'dhvani saṃmohaṃ na gamiṣyanti / tatra katamāni tāni? yaduta yāni deśanāpāṭhe 'nusaṃvarṇitānyānantaryāṇi, yānyadhyāpadya tisṝṇāṃ vimuktīnāmanyatarānyatarasyāṃ nābhisametā bhavanti anyatra nirmitādhiṣṭhānābhisamayāt / nirmitādhiṣṭhānaśrāvako hi mahāmate bodhisattvādhiṣṭhānena vā tathāgatādhiṣṭhānena vā / yasya kasyacidanyasyānantaryakāriṇaḥ kaukṛtyaṃ tasya kaukṛtyadṛṣṭivinivartanārthaṃ nikṣiptadhurasya kaukṛtyadṛṣṭyabhāvārtham / punarapi protsāhanāṃ kariṣyata iti kṛtvā nirmitādhiṣṭhānābhisamayaḥ pradarśyate mayā / nāstyekāntena mahāmate ānantaryakāriṇo 'bhisamayaḥ anyatra svacittadṛśyabhāvanāmātratāvabodhāddehabhogapratiṣṭhāgativikalpātmātmīyagrāhaviviktadarśanātkadā - citkarhicitkalyāṇamitramāsādya anyagatisaṃdhau svavikalpadoṣairvimucyate //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, I shall point out to you the external heinous acts, instructed by which you and other <s>Bodhisattvas</s> in the future time will not fall into confusion. Therein, what are they? Namely, the heinous acts that are described in the teaching-recitation, having committed which one does not achieve any of the three liberations — except through the realization of empowerment by a manifest being (<s>nirmita</s>). For the <s>Śrāvaka</s> empowered by a manifest being, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, [acts] through <s>Bodhisattva</s>-empowerment or <s>Tathāgata</s>-empowerment. For any other perpetrator of heinous acts, for the purpose of turning away his view of remorse, for the purpose of the absence of the view of remorse in one who has laid down the burden — and [thinking] "he will again exert effort" — the realization through the empowerment of a manifest being is demonstrated by me. There is absolutely no realization, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, for a perpetrator of heinous acts, except through the awakening that [all is] merely the cultivation of the appearance of one's own mind (<s>svacittadṛśya</s>), and from the vision of freedom from the grasping of self and what belongs to self through the discrimination of body, enjoyment, abode, and destiny — [such a one] at some time or another, encountering a spiritual friend (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>), at the juncture between existences, is freed from the faults of his own discriminations.

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Therein this is said:

children.text: tṛṣṇā hi mātā ityuktā avidyā ca pitā tathā /
children.translated_text: Craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>) is said to be the mother, and ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) likewise the father;
the consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>) that awakens from the objects is taught to be the <s>Buddha</s>. [Laṅk 3.3]
The <s>Arhats</s> are the five latent tendencies (<s>anuśaya</s>); the <s>Saṅgha</s> is the mass of aggregates (<s>skandha</s>);
from the uninterrupted cutting of the interval of action, the heinous [act] occurs. [Laṅk 3.4]

body.text: punarapi mahāmatirāha - deśayatu me bhagavān buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ kathaṃ bhagavan buddhānāṃ buddhatā bhavati? bhagavānāha - dharmapudgalanairātmyāvabodhānmahāmate āvaraṇadvayaparijñānāvabodhācca cyutidvayādhigamātkleśadvayaprahāṇācca mahāmate buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ buddhatā bhavati / eteṣāmeva mahāmate dharmāṇāmadhigamācchrāvakapratyekabuddhasaṃbuddhatā bhavati / ata etasmānmahāmate ekayānaṃ deśayāmi //
body.translated_text: <s>Mahāmati</s> again asked: May the <s>Bhagavān</s> teach me — how, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, does the <s>Buddhahood</s> of the <s>Buddhas</s> <s>Bhagavāns</s> come about? The <s>Bhagavān</s> replied: From the awakening to the selflessness of <s>dharmas</s> and persons (<s>dharma-pudgala-nairātmya</s>), O <s>Mahāmati</s>, from the awakening to the comprehension of the twofold obscuration (<s>āvaraṇadvaya</s>), from the attainment of the twofold falling-away (<s>cyutidvaya</s>), and from the abandonment of the twofold affliction (<s>kleśadvaya</s>), O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the <s>Buddhahood</s> of the <s>Buddhas</s> <s>Bhagavāns</s> comes about. From the attainment of these very <s>dharmas</s>, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the awakening of <s>Śrāvakas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and perfectly awakened <s>Buddhas</s> comes about. For this very reason, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, I teach the one vehicle (<s>ekayāna</s>).

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Therein this is said:

children.translated_text: The twofold selflessness, the afflictions, and likewise the twofold obscuration;
from the attainment of the falling-away of the inconceivable transformation, [one becomes] a <s>Tathāgata</s>. [Laṅk 3.5]

body.text: atha khalu mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ punarapi bhagavantametadavocat - kiṃ saṃdhāya bhagavatā parṣanmadhyagatena vāgbhāṣitā - ahameva sarvabuddhā ye 'tītā jātakopapattivaicitryaṃ ca / ahameva ca tena kālena tena samayena rājā māṃdhātā / gajaḥ śuka indro vyāsaḥ sunetraḥ,
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s> again addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s> thus: With what intention did the <s>Bhagavān</s>, in the midst of the assembly, utter these words: "I indeed am all the <s>Buddhas</s> of the past, and the diversity of <s>Jātaka</s> rebirths — and I at that time, at that moment, was King <s>Māṃdhātā</s>, the elephant, the parrot, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Vyāsa</s>, <s>Sunetra</s>,"

body.text: ityevamādyāni bhagavatā jātakaśatasahasrāṇyupadiṣṭāni? bhagavānāha - caturvidhāṃ samatāṃ saṃghāya mahāmate tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ parṣanmadhyagatā vācaṃ niścārayanti yaduta ahameva tena kālena tena samayena krakucchandaḥ kanakamuniḥ kāśyapaścābhavam / katamāṃ caturvidhasamatāṃ saṃdhāya? yaduta akṣarasamatāṃ vāksamatāṃ dharmasamatāṃ kāyasamatāṃ ca / imāṃ mahāmate caturvidhāṃ samatāṃ saṃghāya tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ parṣanmadhyagatā vācaṃ niścārayanti / tatra mahāmate katamā akṣarasamatā? yaduta yairakṣarairmama nāma buddha iti, tairevākṣaraisteṣāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ tānyakṣarāṇi mahāmate nirviśiṣṭānyakṣarāṇyakṣarasvabhāvatvena / iyaṃ mahāmate akṣarasamatā / tatra mahāmate katamā vāksamatā tathāgatānāmarhatā samyaksaṃbuddhānām? yaduta mamāpi catuṣṣaṣṭyākāro brahmasvararutaghoṣavāgvikalpaḥ pravartate, teṣāmapi mahāmate tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāmevameva catuṣṣaṣṭyākāro brahmasvararutaghoṣo vāgvikalpaḥ pravartate 'nūnānadhikā nirviśiṣṭāḥ kalaviṅkabrahmasvararutaghoṣasvabhāvena / tatra katamā kāyasamatā? yaduta ahaṃ ca te ca tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā dharmakāyena ca rūpalakṣaṇānuvyañjanakāyena ca samā nirviśiṣṭā anyatra vaineyavaśamupādāya / tatra tatra sattvagativiśeṣeṇa tathāgatā rūpavaicitryamādarśayanti / tatra dharmasamatā mahāmate katamā? yaduta te ca ahaṃ ca saptatriṃśatāṃ bodhipakṣyāṇāṃ dharmāṇāmadhigantāraḥ / imāṃ mahāmate caturvidhāṃ samatāṃ saṃdhāya tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ parṣanmadhyagatā vācaṃ niścārayanti //
body.translated_text: and so on — thus have hundreds of thousands of <s>Jātakas</s> been taught by the <s>Bhagavān</s>? The <s>Bhagavān</s> replied: With reference to the fourfold equality (<s>samatā</s>), O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly awakened <s>Buddhas</s>, in the midst of the assembly, utter the words: "I indeed at that time, at that moment, was <s>Krakucchanda</s>, <s>Kanakamuni</s>, and <s>Kāśyapa</s>." With reference to which fourfold equality? Namely, the equality of syllables (<s>akṣarasamatā</s>), the equality of speech (<s>vāksamatā</s>), the equality of <s>Dharma</s> (<s>dharmasamatā</s>), and the equality of body (<s>kāyasamatā</s>). With reference to this fourfold equality, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly awakened <s>Buddhas</s>, in the midst of the assembly, utter [those] words. Therein, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, what is the equality of syllables? Those syllables by which my name is "<s>Buddha</s>" — by those very syllables, the syllables of those <s>Buddhas</s> <s>Bhagavāns</s>, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, are indistinguishable, because of the nature of syllables as syllables. This, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the equality of syllables. Therein, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, what is the equality of speech of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly awakened <s>Buddhas</s>? For me too, the speech-discrimination of the sixty-four kinds of <s>Brahma</s>-voice-sound-tone proceeds; for those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly awakened <s>Buddhas</s> too, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the speech-discrimination of the sixty-four kinds of <s>Brahma</s>-voice-sound-tone proceeds in just the same way — neither less nor more, indistinguishable, in the nature of the <s>Kalaviṅka</s>-<s>Brahma</s>-voice-sound-tone. Therein, what is the equality of body? I and those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly awakened <s>Buddhas</s> are equal and indistinguishable in the <s>Dharmakāya</s> (truth-body) and in the body of form-characteristics and minor marks — except [for differences] depending on [the needs of] those to be trained. In this and that special destiny of beings, the <s>Tathāgatas</s> display the diversity of form. Therein, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, what is the equality of <s>Dharma</s>? They and I are attainers of the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment (<s>bodhipakṣya dharma</s>). With reference to this fourfold equality, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly awakened <s>Buddhas</s>, in the midst of the assembly, utter [those] words.

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Therein this is said:

children.translated_text: <s>Kāśyapa</s>, <s>Krakucchanda</s>, and <s>Konākamuni</s> — that too am I;
I speak to the sons of the <s>Jina</s>, arisen in equality. [Laṅk 3.6]

body.text: punarapi mahāmatirāha - yadidamuktaṃ bhagavatā - yāṃ ca rātriṃ tathāgato 'bhisaṃbuddho yāṃ ca rātriṃ parinirvāsyati, atrāntare ekamapyakṣaraṃ tathāgatena nodāhṛtam, na pravyāhariṣyati, avacanaṃ buddhavacanamiti, tatkimidaṃ saṃdhāyoktaṃ tathāgatenārhatā samyaksaṃbuddhena avacanaṃ buddhavacanamiti? bhagavānāha - dharmadvayaṃ mahāmate saṃdhāya mayaitaduktam / katamaddharmadvayam? yaduta pratyātmadharmatāṃ ca saṃdhāya paurāṇasthitidharmatāṃ ca / idaṃ mahāmate dharmadvayaṃ saṃdhāyedamuktaṃ mayā / tatra svapratyātmadharmatānusaṃdhiḥ katamaḥ? yattaistathāgatairadhigataṃ tanmayāpyadhigatamanūnamanadhikaṃ svapratyātmagatigocaraṃ vāgvikalparahitamakṣaragatidvayavinirmuktam / tatra paurāṇasthitidharmatā katamā? yaduta paurāṇamidaṃ mahāmate dharmatāvanme hiraṇyarajatamuktākaravanmahāmate dharmadhātusthititā - utpādādvā tathāgatānāmanutpādādvā tathāgatānāṃ sthitaivaiṣāṃ dharmāṇāṃ dharmatā dharmasthititā dharmaniyāmatā / paurāṇanagarapathavanmahāmate / tadyathā mahāmate kaścideva puruṣo 'ṭavyāṃ paryaṭan paurāṇaṃ nagaramanupaśyedavikalapathapraveśam / sa taṃ nagaramanupraviśet / tatra praviśya pratiniviśya
body.translated_text: <s>Mahāmati</s> again asked: As for this statement made by the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "From the night the <s>Tathāgata</s> attained perfect awakening to the night he will attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, in this interval not even a single syllable has been uttered by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, nor will be uttered — the word of the <s>Buddha</s> is wordless" — with what intention was this said by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, perfectly awakened <s>Buddha</s>: "the word of the <s>Buddha</s> is wordless"? The <s>Bhagavān</s> replied: With reference to two <s>dharmas</s>, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, this was said by me. Which two <s>dharmas</s>? Namely, with reference to the <s>dharma</s>-nature of inner self-realization (<s>pratyātmadharmatā</s>) and with reference to the <s>dharma</s>-nature of ancient abiding (<s>paurāṇasthitidharmatā</s>). This, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the twofold <s>dharma</s> with reference to which this was said by me. Therein, what is the connection with the <s>dharma</s>-nature of inner self-realization? What was attained by those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, that was also attained by me — neither less nor more — the domain of inner self-realization, free from speech-discrimination, released from the duality of syllable-courses. Therein, what is the <s>dharma</s>-nature of ancient abiding? This is ancient, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, my <s>dharma</s>-nature — like a [deposit of] gold, silver, and pearls, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, [is] the abiding-nature of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of <s>dharmas</s>): whether <s>Tathāgatas</s> arise or <s>Tathāgatas</s> do not arise, this <s>dharma</s>-nature of these <s>dharmas</s> abides — the <s>dharma</s>-abiding, the <s>dharma</s>-determination. It is like an ancient city-path, O <s>Mahāmati</s>. Just as, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, some man, wandering in the wilderness, perceives an ancient city with an undamaged entrance-path, and enters that city; having entered and settled

body.text: nagaraṃ nagarakriyāsukhamanubhavet / tatkiṃ manyase mahāmate api nu tena puruṣeṇa sa panthā utpādito yena pathā taṃ nagaramanupraviṣṭo nagaravaicitryaṃ ca (anubhūtam)? āha - no bhagavan / bhagavānāha - evameva mahāmate yanmayā taiśca tathāgatairadhigatam - sthitaivaiṣā dharmatā dharmasthititā dharmaniyāmatā tathatā bhūtatā satyatā / ata etasmātkāraṇānmahāmate mayedamuktam - yāṃ ca rātriṃ tathāgato 'bhisaṃbuddho yāṃ ca rātriṃ parinirvāsyati, atrāntare ekamapyakṣaraṃ tathāgatena nodāhṛtaṃ nodāhariṣyati //
body.translated_text: in the city, he experiences the happiness of the city's activities. What do you think, O <s>Mahāmati</s> — was that path created by that man, by which path he entered that city and experienced the variety of the city? He replied: No, <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: Even so, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, what was attained by me and by those <s>Tathāgatas</s> — this <s>dharma</s>-nature abides — the <s>dharma</s>-abiding, the <s>dharma</s>-determination, the <s>Suchness</s> (<s>tathatā</s>), the reality (<s>bhūtatā</s>), the truth (<s>satyatā</s>). For this very reason, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, this was said by me: "From the night the <s>Tathāgata</s> attained perfect awakening to the night he will attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, in this interval not even a single syllable has been uttered by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, nor will be uttered."

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Therein this is said:

children.text: yasyāṃ ca rātryāṃ dhigamo yasyāṃ ca parinirvṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: On the night of attainment and on the [night] of <s>parinirvāṇa</s>,
in this interval, nothing has been proclaimed by me. [Laṅk 3.7]
With reference to the <s>dharma</s>-nature of inner self-realization and abiding, this was spoken by me;

children.text: taiśca buddhairmayā caiva na ca kiṃcidviśeṣitam // Lank_3.8 //
children.translated_text: between those <s>Buddhas</s> and me, nothing whatsoever has been distinguished. [Laṅk 3.8]

body.text:
atha khalu mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ punarapi bhagavantamadhyeṣate sma - deśayatu me bhagavānnāstyastitvalakṣaṇaṃ sarvadharmāṇāṃ yathā ahaṃ ca anye ca bodhisattvā mahāsattvā nāstyastitvavarjitāḥ kṣipramanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeran / bhagavānāha - tena hi mahāmate śṛṇu, sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuru / bhāṣiṣye 'haṃ te / sādhu bhagavanniti mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavataḥ pratyaśrauṣīt / bhagavānetadavocat - dvayaniśrito 'yaṃ mahāmate loko yaduta astitvaniśritaśca nāstitvaniśritaśca / bhāvābhāvacchandadṛṣṭipatitaśca aniḥśaraṇe niḥśaraṇabuddhiḥ / tatra mahāmate kathamastitvaniśrito lokaḥ? yaduta vidyamānairhetupratyayairloka utpadyate nāvidyamānaiḥ, vidyamānaṃ cotpadyamānamutpadyate nāvidyamānam / sa caivaṃ bruvan mahāmate bhāvānāmastitvahetupratyayānāṃ lokasya ca hetvastivādī bhavati / tatra mahāmate kathaṃ nāstitvaniśrito bhavati? yaduta rāgadveṣamohābhyupagamaṃ kṛtvā punarapi rāgadveṣamohabhāvābhāvaṃ vikalpayati / yaśca mahāmate bhāvānāmastitvaṃ nābhyupaiti bhāvalakṣaṇaviviktatvāt, yaśca buddhaśrāvakapratyekabuddhānāṃ rāgadveṣamohānnābhyupaiti bhāvalakṣaṇavinirmuktatvādvidyante neti / katamo 'tra mahāmate vaināśiko bhavati? mahāmatirāha - ya eṣa bhagavan abhyupagamya rāgadveṣamohān na punarabhyupaiti / bhagavānāha - sādhu sādhu mahāmate, sādhu khalu punastvaṃ mahāmate, yastvamevaṃ prabhāṣitaḥ / kevalaṃ mahāmate na rāgadveṣamohabhāvābhāvādvaināśiko bhavati / buddhaśrāvakapratyekabuddhavaināśiko 'pi bhavati / tatkasya hetoḥ? yaduta adhyātmabahirdhānupalabdhitvācca kleśānām / na hi mahāmate rāgadveṣamohā adhyātmabahirdhopalabhyante 'śarīratvāt / anabhyupagamatvācca mahāmate rāgadveṣamohābhāvānāṃ buddhaśrāvakapratyekabuddhavaināśiko bhavati / prakṛtivimuktāste buddhaśrāvakapratyekabuddhā bandhyabandhahetvabhāvāt / bandhye sati mahāmate bandho bhavati bandhahetuśca / evamapi bruvan mahāmate vaināśiko bhavati / idaṃ mahāmate nāstyastitvasya lakṣaṇam / idaṃ ca mahāmate saṃdhāyoktaṃ mayā - varaṃ khalu sumerumātrā
pudgaladṛṣṭirna tveva nāstyastitvābhimānikasya śūnyatādṛṣṭiḥ / nāstyastitvābhimāniko hi mahāmate vaināśiko
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s> again entreated the Blessed One: 'May the Blessed One teach me the characteristics of non-existence and existence of all <s>dharmas</s>, so that I and other <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s>, free from non-existence and existence, may quickly realize unsurpassed, perfect awakening.' The Blessed One said: 'Then, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, listen, and attend well and thoroughly. I shall speak to you.' 'Very well, Blessed One!' — the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s> gave assent to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said: 'This world, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, relies on a duality — namely, reliance on existence and reliance on non-existence. Fallen into the views of desire for being and non-being, it has the conviction of escape in what offers no escape. Therein, how, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, does the world rely on existence? Namely: the world arises from existent causes and conditions, not from non-existent ones; and what arises, arises as existent, not as non-existent. He who speaks thus, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, becomes an advocate of the existence of causes and conditions of entities, and of the existence of causes of the world. Therein, how, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, does one come to rely on non-existence? Namely: having accepted passion, aversion, and delusion, one then again conceptualizes the existence and non-existence of passion, aversion, and delusion. And whoever, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, does not accept the existence of entities — because of their isolation from the characteristics of entities — and whoever does not accept the passion, aversion, and delusion of Buddhas, <s>Śrāvakas</s>, and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> — because they are liberated from the characteristics of entities — [saying] "they do not exist" — who here, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, becomes an annihilationist?' <s>Mahāmati</s> said: 'He, O Blessed One, who having accepted passion, aversion, and delusion, does not accept them again.' The Blessed One said: 'Well done, well done, <s>Mahāmati</s>! Well done indeed, <s>Mahāmati</s>, that you have spoken thus. But, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, it is not merely through the existence or non-existence of passion, aversion, and delusion that one becomes an annihilationist. One also becomes an annihilationist regarding Buddhas, <s>Śrāvakas</s>, and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>. For what reason? Because afflictions are unobtainable either internally or externally. For passion, aversion, and delusion, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, are not found internally or externally, because they are bodiless. And because, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, one does not accept the non-existence of passion, aversion, and delusion, one becomes an annihilationist regarding Buddhas, <s>Śrāvakas</s>, and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>. Those Buddhas, <s>Śrāvakas</s>, and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> are naturally liberated, because of the absence of a cause of bondage in what is to be bound. When there is something to be bound, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, there is bondage and a cause of bondage. Even speaking thus, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, one becomes an annihilationist. This, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the characteristic of non-existence and existence. And with this in view, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, I have said: "Better indeed a view of self as great as Mount <s>Sumeru</s> than the view of emptiness of one who is conceited about non-existence and existence." For one conceited about non-existence and existence, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is an annihilationist

body.text: bhavati / svasāmānyalakṣaṇadṛṣṭipatitāśayaḥ svacittadṛśyamātrābhāvānna pratijānan, apratijñānādbāhyabhāvānnityadarśanātkṣaṇaparaṃparābhedabhinnāni skandhadhātvāyatanāni saṃtatiprabandhena vinivṛtya vinivartanta iti kalpākṣararahitāni prativikalpayan punarapi vaināśiko bhavati //
body.translated_text: — one whose disposition has fallen into the views of own- and general-characteristics, who does not acknowledge [that all is] merely the appearance of one's own mind; through non-acknowledgment, from the view of permanence regarding external entities, conceptualizing the aggregates, elements, and sense-bases — undivided in the division of the continuity of momentary succession — as being extinguished, as turning away through the series of continuity, as free from syllables of time — he becomes an annihilationist again.

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: On this, it is said:

children.translated_text: Existence and non-existence — these are both extremes, as long as they are the domain of mind;
when the domain ceases, the mind is rightly ceased. || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.9 ||

children.text: viṣaye grahaṇābhāvānnirodho na ca nāsti ca /
children.translated_text: In the absence of grasping at objects, there is cessation — yet it is neither non-existent nor existent;

children.text: vidyate tathatāvastu āryāṇāṃ gocaro yathā // Lank_3.10 //
children.translated_text: the reality of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) exists — as it is the domain of the noble ones. || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.10 ||

children.text: abhūtvā yasya utpādo bhūtvā vāpi vinaśyati /
children.translated_text: That which, not having existed, arises, or, having existed, perishes,

children.text: pratyayaiḥ sadasaccāpi na te me śāsane sthitāḥ // Lank_3.11 //
children.translated_text: and [is imagined] through conditions as both existent and non-existent — those are not established in my teaching. || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.11 ||

children.text: na tīrthakairna buddhaiśca na mayā na ca kenacit /
children.translated_text: Not by heretics, not by Buddhas, not by me, not by anyone —

children.text: pratyayaiḥ sādhyate 'stitvaṃ kathaṃ nāsti bhaviṣyati // Lank_3.12 //
children.translated_text: is existence established through conditions; how then could non-existence come to be? || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.12 ||
By whom is existence established through conditions, of which there is non-existence?
Through the wrong view of the doctrine of arising, 'it does not exist' and 'it exists' are conceptualized. || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.13 ||
For one for whom nothing whatsoever arises and nothing whatsoever ceases,

children.text: tasyāstināsti nopaiti viviktaṃ paśyato jagat // Lank_3.14 //
children.translated_text: existence and non-existence do not apply — seeing the world as isolated [from both]. || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.14 ||

body.text: atha khalu mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ punarapi bhagavantamadhyeṣate - deśayatu me bhagavān, deśayatu me sugataḥ, deśayatu me tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho vadatāṃ variṣṭhaḥ siddhāntanayalakṣaṇam, yena siddhāntanayalakṣaṇena suprativibhāgaviddhena ahaṃ ca anye ca bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ siddhāntanayalakṣaṇagatiṃgatāḥ kṣipramanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyante, aparapraṇeyāśca bhaviṣyanti sarvatārkikatīrthakarāṇām / bhagavānāha - tena hi mahāmate śṛṇu, sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasikuru / bhāṣiṣye 'haṃ te / sādhu bhagavanniti mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavataḥ pratyaśrauṣīt / bhagavāṃstasyaitadavocat - dvividhaṃ mahāmate siddhāntanayalakṣaṇaṃ sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhabodhisattvānāṃ yaduta siddhāntanayaśca deśanānayaśca / tatra siddhāntanayo mahāmate yaduta pratyātmādhigamaviśeṣalakṣaṇaṃ vāgvikalpākṣararahitamanāsravadhātugatiprāpakaṃ pratyātmagatibhūmigatisvalakṣaṇaṃ sarvatarkatīrthyamāravarjitam / vinihatya ca tāṃstīrthyamārān pratyātmagatirvirājate / etanmahāmate siddhāntanayalakṣaṇam / tatra deśanānayaḥ katamaḥ? yaduta navāṅgaśāsanavicitropadeśo 'nyānanyasadasatpakṣavarjitaḥ upāyakuśalavidhipūrvakaḥ sattveṣu darśanāvatāraḥ / yadyenādhimucyate tattasya deśayet / etanmahāmate deśanānayalakṣaṇam / atra mahāmate tvayā anyaiśca bodhisattvairmahāsattvairyogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s> again entreated the Blessed One: 'May the Blessed One teach me, may the <s>Sugata</s> teach me, may the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, best of speakers, teach me the characteristic of the method and established doctrine (<s>siddhāntanaya</s>), so that I and other <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s>, having entered the course of the characteristic of the method and established doctrine, well-pierced with discrimination, may quickly realize unsurpassed, perfect awakening, and may become unled by all logicians and heretics.' The Blessed One said: 'Then, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, listen, and attend well and thoroughly. I shall speak to you.' 'Very well, Blessed One!' — the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s> gave assent to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this to him: 'The characteristic of the method and established doctrine for all <s>Śrāvakas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> is twofold, O <s>Mahāmati</s> — namely, the established doctrine-method and the teaching-method. Therein, the established doctrine-method, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the characteristic of the distinctive realization of one's own inner attainment, free from verbal conceptualization and syllables, leading to the course of the outflow-free realm, having the own-characteristic of the course of the stages of inner self-realization, free from all logicians, heretics, and <s>Māra</s>. And having destroyed those heretics and <s>Māras</s>, the inner self-realization shines forth. This, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the characteristic of the established doctrine-method. Therein, what is the teaching-method? Namely: the varied teaching of the nine divisions of scripture, free from the positions of other and non-other, existent and non-existent, preceded by the method of skillful means, [being] an entry of insight into beings. Whatever [a being] has conviction in, that should be taught to him. This, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the characteristic of the teaching-method. Herein, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, you and other <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> should practice <s>yoga</s>.'

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: On this, it is said:

children.translated_text: Established doctrine and method, and indeed the teaching of inner self[-realization] —

children.text: ye paśyanti vibhāgajñā na te tarkavaśaṃ gatāḥ // Lank_3.15 //
children.translated_text: those who see these, knowers of distinctions, have not fallen under the sway of logic. || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.15 ||

children.text: na bhāvo vidyate satyaṃ yathā bālairvikalpyate /
children.translated_text: Entities do not exist in truth as conceptualized by the childish;

children.text: abhāvena tu vai mokṣaṃ kathaṃ necchanti tārkikāḥ // Lank_3.16 //
children.translated_text: why then do the logicians not seek liberation through non-existence? || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.16 ||
For those who perceive the conditioned as bound to arising and ceasing,

children.text: dṛṣṭidvayaṃ prapuṣṇanti na paśyanti viparyayāt // Lank_3.17 //
children.translated_text: they nourish the dual view — they do not see [reality], due to inversion. || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.17 ||
Only one thing would be true — <s>nirvāṇa</s>, free from mentation;
one should see the world as imagined — like a plantain-trunk or an illusion. || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.18 ||

children.text: rāgo na vidyate dveṣo mohaścāpi na pudgalaḥ /
children.translated_text: Passion does not exist, nor aversion, nor delusion, nor a person (<s>pudgala</s>);

children.text: tṛṣṇāyā hyuditāḥ skandhā vidyante svapnasādṛśāḥ // Lank_3.19 //
children.translated_text: the aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>), arisen from craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>), exist like a dream. || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.19 ||

body.text:
atha khalu mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ punarapi bhagavantamadhyeṣate sma - deśayatu me bhagavān, deśayatu me sugataḥ abhūtaparikalpasya lakṣaṇam / kathaṃ kiṃ kena kasya bhagavan abhūtaparikalpaḥ pravartamānaḥ pravartate? abhūtaparikalpo 'bhūtaparikalpa iti bhagavannucyate / katamasyaitadbhagavan dharmasyādhivacanaṃ yaduta abhūtaparikalpa iti? kiṃ vā prativikalpayan abhūtaparikalpo bhavati? bhagavānāha - sādhu sādhu mahāmate / sādhu khalu punastvaṃ mahāmate, yattvametamarthamadhyeṣitavyaṃ manyase / bahujanahitāya tvaṃ mahāmate pratipanno bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāyai mahato janakāyasyārthāya hitāya sukhāya devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca / tena hi mahāmate śṛṇu, sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasikuru / bhāṣiṣye 'haṃ te / sādhu bhagavanniti mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavataḥ pratyaśrauṣīt / bhagavāṃstasyaitadavocat - arthavividhavaicitryābhūtaparikalpābhiniveśānmahāmate vikalpaḥ pravartamānaḥ pravartate / nṛṇāṃ grāhyagrāhakābhiniveśābhiniviṣṭānāṃ ca mahāmate svacittadṛśyamātrānavadhāritamatīnāṃ ca sadasaddṛṣṭipakṣapatitānāṃ ca mahāmate tīrthakaradṛṣṭiprativikalpavāsanāpratipuṣṭānāṃ bāhyavicitrārthopalambhābhiniveśāccittacaittakalāpo vikalpasaṃśabditaḥ pravartamānaḥ pravartate ātmātmīyābhiniveśāt / mahāmatirāhatadyadi bhagavannarthavividhavaicitryābhūtaparikalpābhiniveśānnṛṇāṃ vikalpaḥ pravartamānaḥ pravartate sadasaddṛṣṭipakṣapatitānāṃ grāhyagrāhakatīrthakaradṛṣṭiprativikalpapuṣṭānāṃ bāhyavicitrārthopalambhābhiniveśāccittacaittakalāpo vikalpasaṃśabditaḥ svacittadṛśyamātrānavabodhātsantāsantavicitrabhāvābhiniveśātpravartamānaḥ pravartate / tadyathaiva bhagavan bāhyārthavicitralakṣaṇaḥ sadasatpakṣapatitalakṣaṇo bhāvābhāvavivikto dṛṣṭilakṣaṇavinivṛttaḥ, tathaiva bhagavan paramārthapramāṇendriyāvayavadṛṣṭāntahetulakṣaṇavinivṛttaḥ / tatkathaṃ bhagavannekatra vicitravikalpo 'bhūtārthavicitrabhāvābhiniveśaṃ prativikalpayan pravartate, na punaḥ paramārthalakṣaṇābhiniveśaṃ prativikalpayan pravartate vikalpaḥ? nanu bhagavan viṣamahetuvādastava
prasajyate ekatra pravartate ekatra neti bruvataḥ, sadasatpakṣāśrayābhiniveśaśca abhūtaprativikalpadṛṣṭipravṛttiṃ bruvato vividhamāyāṅgapuruṣavaicitryānniṣpannaikarūpavatprativikalpayan vikalpena lakṣaṇavaicitryabhāvābhāvaṃ ca vikalpasya vinivṛtterlokāyatikadṛṣṭyāśayapatitaśca /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s> again entreated the Blessed One: 'May the Blessed One teach me, may the <s>Sugata</s> teach me, the characteristic of unreal imagination (<s>abhūtaparikalpa</s>). How, what, by what, and for whom, O Blessed One, does unreal imagination operate as it operates? "Unreal imagination, unreal imagination" — thus it is said, O Blessed One. To which <s>dharma</s>, O Blessed One, is this a designation — namely, "unreal imagination"? Or what does one conceptualize in order to become an unreal imaginer?' The Blessed One said: 'Well done, well done, <s>Mahāmati</s>! Well done indeed, <s>Mahāmati</s>, that you consider this matter worthy of requesting. You, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, have set forth for the benefit of many, for the happiness of many, out of compassion for the world, for the welfare, benefit, and happiness of the great multitude of beings, of <s>devas</s> and humans. Then, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, listen, and attend well and thoroughly. I shall speak to you.' 'Very well, Blessed One!' — the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s> gave assent to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this to him: 'From attachment to unreal imagination of the variety and diversity of objects, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, conceptualization operates as it operates.
