For people who are attached to the grasped and the grasper, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, whose minds have not ascertained [that all is] merely the appearance of one's own mind, who have fallen into the positions of the views of existent and non-existent, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, who are nourished by the impressions of counter-conceptualization of heretical views, from the attachment to the apprehension of varied external objects — the aggregate of mind and mental factors, termed "conceptualization," operates as it operates, from attachment to self and what belongs to self.' <s>Mahāmati</s> said: 'If, O Blessed One, conceptualization operates from attachment to unreal imagination of the variety and diversity of objects, for people who have fallen into the positions of the views of existent and non-existent, who are nourished by counter-conceptualization of the views of the grasped, the grasper, and the heretics, [and operates] from attachment to the apprehension of varied external objects — [since] the aggregate of mind and mental factors, termed "conceptualization," operates from not understanding [that all is] merely the appearance of one's own mind, from attachment to the varied entities of existent and non-existent — then, just as, O Blessed One, external objects of varied characteristics, having the characteristic of falling into the positions of existent and non-existent, are isolated from being and non-being and freed from the characteristics of views, so too, O Blessed One, [they should be] freed from the characteristics of ultimate reality, valid means of knowledge, sense-organs, parts, examples, and logical reasons. Then how, O Blessed One, does the varied conceptualization in one case operate by counter-imagining the attachment to unreal and varied entities, but in the other case does conceptualization not operate by counter-imagining the attachment to the characteristics of ultimate reality? Does it not follow, O Blessed One, that you propound an unequal cause — saying that it operates in one case but not in the other? And would not there be attachment to the position of existent and non-existent, and [would you not be] stating the operation of the view of unreal counter-imagination, conceptualizing like the variety of the limbs of a manifold illusory figure as having a single accomplished form, and [asserting] the cessation of conceptualization [along with] the existence and non-existence of the variety of characteristics — and [thereby] having a disposition fallen into the <s>Lokāyatika</s> (materialist) view?

body.text: bhagavānāha - na hi mahāmate vikalpaḥ pravartate nivartate vā / tatkasya hetoḥ? yaduta sadasato vikalpasyāpravṛttitvādbāhyadṛśyabhāvābhāvātsvacittadṛśyamātrāvabodhānmahāmate vikalpo na pravartate na nivartate / anyatra mahāmate bālānāṃ svacittavaicitryavikalpakalpitatvāt / kriyāpravṛttipūrvako vikalpo vaicitryabhāvalakṣaṇābhiniveśātpravartata iti vadāmi / kathaṃ khalu mahāmate bālapṛthagjanāḥ svavikalpacittamātrāvabodhādātmātmīyābhivinivṛttadṛṣṭayaḥ kāryakāraṇapratyayavinivṛttadoṣāḥ svacittamātrāvabodhātparāvṛttacittāśrayāḥ sarvāsu bhūmiṣu kṛtavidyāstathāgatasvapratyātmagatigocaraṃ pañcadharmasvabhāvavastudṛṣṭivikalpavinivṛttiṃ pratilabheran? ata etasmātkāraṇānmahāmate idamucyate mayā - vikalpo 'bhūtārthavaicitryādabhiniveśātpravartate, svavikalpavaicitryārthayathābhūtārthaparijñānādvimucyata iti //
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'Conceptualization, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, neither operates nor ceases to operate. For what reason? Because conceptualization does not operate regarding the existent and non-existent; because of the existence and non-existence of external visible entities; because, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, through the understanding of [all as] merely the appearance of one's own mind, conceptualization neither operates nor ceases. Except, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, for the childish, because [things are] imagined by the conceptualization of the variety of their own minds. I say that conceptualization operates from attachment to the characteristics of the variety of entities, preceded by the operation of action. How then, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, could childish ordinary persons — through understanding [that all is] merely their own conceptual mind, with views freed from attachment to self and what belongs to self, with the faults of cause-effect-condition freed, with the basis of mind transformed through understanding mind-only, accomplished in all stages — attain the domain of the <s>Tathāgata's</s> own inner self-realization, the cessation of the views and conceptualization of the five <s>dharmas</s>, inherent natures, and entities? For this reason, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, I say: "Conceptualization operates from attachment to the variety of unreal objects; through the true knowledge of the meaning of the variety of one's own conceptualization, one is liberated."'

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: On this, it is said:

children.translated_text: Those for whom the world proceeds by causes and conditions,

children.text: cātuṣkoṭikayā yuktā na te mannayakovidāḥ // Lank_3.20 //
children.translated_text: connected with the fourfold [proposition] — they are not skilled in my method. [Laṅk 3.20]

children.text: asanna jāyate loko na sanna sadasan kvacit /
children.translated_text: The world does not arise from the non-existent, nor from the existent, nor from the existent-and-non-existent, ever;
yet through conditions and causes it is conceptualized by the childish. [Laṅk 3.21]
When one sees the world as neither existent nor non-existent nor both,

children.text: tadā vyāvartate cittaṃ nairātmyaṃ cādhigacchati // Lank_3.22 //
children.translated_text: then the mind turns away and realizes selflessness (<s>nairātmya</s>). [Laṅk 3.22]
All entities are unborn, since they arise from conditions;

children.text: kāryaṃ hi pratyayāḥ sarve na kāryājjāyate bhavaḥ // Lank_3.23 //
children.translated_text: conditions are all effects — existence does not arise from an effect. [Laṅk 3.23]

children.text: kāryānna jāyate kāryaṃ dvitvaṃ kārye prasajyate /
children.translated_text: An effect does not arise from an effect; [if so,] duality in the effect would follow;
and by the implication of duality, no entity is apprehended from an effect. [Laṅk 3.24]
When one sees the conditioned as free from object and subject,

children.text: niścitaṃ cittamātraṃ hi cittamātraṃ vadāmyaham // Lank_3.25 //
children.translated_text: one is certain of mind-only (<s>cittamātra</s>) — indeed, I declare mind-only. [Laṅk 3.25]
The 'only' (<s>mātrā</s>) is the establishment of inherent nature, free from entities [produced] by conditions;

children.text: niṣṭhābhāvaḥ paraṃ brahma etāṃ mātrāṃ vadāmyaham // Lank_3.26 //
children.translated_text: the ultimate non-existence, the supreme <s>Brahman</s> — this 'only' I declare. [Laṅk 3.26]
The self exists by the truth of designation (<s>prajñapti</s>); it does not exist as substance;

children.text: skandhānāṃ skandhatā tadvatprajñaptyā na tu dravyataḥ // Lank_3.27 //
children.translated_text: the aggregate-nature of the aggregates is likewise [only] by designation, not by substance. [Laṅk 3.27]
Equality (<s>samatā</s>) is of four kinds: [that] of characteristics, [that] born from causes and entities,
the equality of selflessness, and the fourth — [that] of the yogins of yoga. [Laṅk 3.28]
The turning-away from all views, free from the imagined and imagining,
non-apprehension and non-arising — [this] I call mind-only. [Laṅk 3.29]
Neither entity nor non-entity, free from entity and non-entity,
<s>Suchness</s> (<s>tathatā</s>), freed from mind — [this] I call mind-only. [Laṅk 3.30]
<s>Suchness</s>, emptiness, the limit (<s>koṭi</s>), <s>nirvāṇa</s>, the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of <s>dharma</s>),

children.text: kāyaṃ manomayaṃ citraṃ cittamātraṃ vadāmyaham // Lank_3.31 //
children.translated_text: the diverse mind-made body — [all this] I call mind-only. [Laṅk 3.31]
Bound by the impressions of discrimination, diverse, arising from mind,

children.text: bahirākhyāyate nṛṇāṃ cittamātraṃ hi laukikam // Lank_3.32 //
children.translated_text: it is proclaimed externally to humans — worldly mind-only indeed. [Laṅk 3.32]

children.text: dṛśyaṃ na vidyate bāhyaṃ cittaṃ citraṃ hi dṛśyate /
children.translated_text: The external perceived does not exist; mind is seen diversely;
body, enjoyment, and place of establishment — [this] I call mind-only. [Laṅk 3.33]

body.text: atha khalu mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantametadavocat - yatpunaretaduktaṃ bhagavatā - yathārutārthagrahaṇaṃ na kartavyaṃ bodhisattvena mahāsattvena anyaiśceti / kathaṃ na bhagavan bodhisattvo mahāsattvo yathārutārthagrāhī na bhavati? kiṃ ca rutam? ko 'rthaḥ? bhagavānāha - tena hi mahāmate śṛṇu, sādhu ca suṣṭhu na ca manasi kuru / bhāṣiṣye 'haṃ te / sādhu bhagavanniti mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavataḥ pratyaśrauṣīt / bhagavāṃstasyaitadavocat - tatra rutaṃ mahāmate katamat? yaduta vāgakṣarasaṃyogavikalpo dantahanutālujihvauṣṭhapuṭaviniḥsṛtaparasparajalpo vikalpavāsanāhetuko rutamityucyate / tatra arthaḥ punarmahāmate katamaḥ? yaduta śrutacintābhāvanāmayyā prajñayā eko rahogato nirvāṇapuragāmimārgaḥ svabuddhyā vāsanāśrayaparāvṛttipūrvakaḥ svapratyātmagatigocarabhūmisthānāntaraviśeṣārthalakṣaṇagatiṃ pravicārayan bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'rthakuśalo bhavati //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'Regarding what was said by the Blessed One — that a <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> and others should not grasp the meaning according to the letter (<s>yathāruta</s>) — how is it, Blessed One, that a <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> does not become one who grasps the meaning according to the letter? And what is the letter (<s>ruta</s>)? What is the meaning (<s>artha</s>)?' The Blessed One said: 'Then, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, listen well and thoroughly, and attend. I shall speak to you.' 'Very well, Blessed One,' the <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s> assented to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this to him: 'Therein, what is the letter, O <s>Mahāmati</s>? Namely, the discrimination of the conjunction of speech, syllables — the mutual talk issuing from the cavities of teeth, jaw, palate, tongue, and lips, caused by the impressions of discrimination — this is called the letter. Therein, what is the meaning, O <s>Mahāmati</s>? Namely, through the wisdom born of hearing, thinking, and meditation (<s>śrutacintābhāvanāmayī prajñā</s>), alone in solitude, on the path leading to the city of <s>nirvāṇa</s>, preceded by the turning-about of the support of impressions by one's own intellect — a <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> who investigates the course of the characteristics of the meaning of the distinctions among the various positions of the stages and domains of one's own inner noble realization becomes skilled in meaning.'

body.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate rūtārthakuśalo bodhisattvo mahāsattvo rutamarthādanyannānyaditi samanupaśyati, arthaṃ ca rutāt / yadi ca punarmahāmate artho rutādanyaḥ syāt, arutārthābhivyaktihetukaḥ syāt / sa cārtho rutenānupraviśyate pradīpeneva dhanam / tadyathā mahāmate kaścideva puruṣaḥ pradīpaṃ gṛhītvā dhanamavalokayet - idaṃ me dhanamevaṃvidhamasmin pradeśe iti / evameva mahāmate vāgvikalparutapradīpena bodhisattvā mahāsattvā vāgvikalparahitāḥ svapratyātmāryagatimanupraviśanti //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> skilled in the letter and meaning sees that the letter is not other than, and not the same as, the meaning — and the meaning [is not other than or the same as] the letter. If, moreover, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the meaning were other than the letter, the letter would not be the cause of expressing the meaning. But the meaning is entered through the letter, like wealth by a lamp. Just as, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, a certain man, taking a lamp, would examine his wealth — 'This is my wealth, of such a kind, in this place' — even so, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas</s>, by the lamp of the letter of speech-discrimination, free from speech-discrimination, enter their own inner noble realization.

body.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate aniruddhā anutpannāḥ prakṛtiparinirvṛtāstriyānamekayānaṃ ca pañcacittasvabhāvādiṣu yathārutārthābhiniveśaṃ pratītya abhiniveśataḥ samāropāpavādadṛṣṭipatito bhavati / anyathā vyavasthitānanyathā prativikalpayan māyāvaicitryadarśanavikalpanavat / tadyathā mahāmate anyathā hi māyāvaicitryaṃ draṣṭavyamanyathā pratikalpyate bālairna tvāryaiḥ //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, regarding the unceased, the unborn, those in <s>nirvāṇa</s> by nature, the three vehicles, the one vehicle, and the five natures of mind etc. — depending on the attachment to the literal meaning (<s>yathārutārtha</s>), one falls into the views of superimposition and denial from attachment, conceptualizing what is established one way as being another way — like the discrimination of seeing the variety of an illusion. Just as, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the variety of an illusion is to be seen one way, yet is conceptualized another way by the childish — not by the noble ones.

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Therein this is said:

children.translated_text: Having conceptualized according to the letter, they superimpose upon the nature of <s>dharma</s> (<s>dharmatā</s>);

children.text: te ca vai tatsamāropātpatanti narakālaye // Lank_3.34 //
children.translated_text: and from that very superimposition, they fall into the abode of hell. [Laṅk 3.34]

children.text: na hyātmā vidyate skandhaiḥ skandhāścaiva hi nātmani /
children.translated_text: For the self does not exist through the aggregates, nor are the aggregates in the self;

children.text: na te yathā vikalpyante na ca te vai na santi ca // Lank_3.35 //
children.translated_text: they do not exist as they are conceptualized, yet it is not that they do not exist at all. [Laṅk 3.35]
The existence of all entities, as conceptualized by the childish —

children.text: yadi te bhavedyathādṛṣṭāḥ sarve syustattvadarśinaḥ // Lank_3.36 //
children.translated_text: if they existed as seen, all would be seers of truth. [Laṅk 3.36]
Because of the non-existence of all <s>dharmas</s>, there is neither defilement nor purification;

children.text: na te tathā yathā dṛṣṭā na ca te vai na santi ca // Lank_3.37 //
children.translated_text: they do not exist as they are seen, yet it is not that they do not exist at all. [Laṅk 3.37]

body.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate jñānavijñānalakṣaṇaṃ te upadekṣyāmi, yena jñānavijñānalakṣaṇena suprativibhāgaviddhena tvaṃ ca anye ca bodhisattvā mahāsattvā jñānavijñānalakṣaṇagatiṃgatāḥ kṣipramanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyante / tatra mahāmate triprakāraṃ jñānaṃ laukikaṃ lokottaraṃ ca lokottaratamaṃ ca / tatrotpannapradhvaṃsi vijñānam / anutpannapradhvaṃsi jñānam / punaraparaṃ mahāmate nimittānimittapatitaṃ vijñānaṃ nāstyastivaicitryalakṣaṇahetukaṃ ca / nimittānimittavyatikrāntalakṣaṇaṃ jñānam / punaraparaṃ mahāmate upacayalakṣaṇaṃ vijñānam / apacayalakṣaṇaṃ jñānam / tatra trividhaṃ jñānaṃ svasāmānyalakṣaṇāvadhārakaṃ ca utpādavyayāvadhārakaṃ ca anutpādānirodhāvadhārakaṃ ca / tatra laukikaṃ jñānaṃ sadasatpakṣābhiniviṣṭānāṃ sarvatīrthakarabālapṛthagjanānāṃ ca / tatra lokottaraṃ jñānaṃ sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhānāṃ ca svasāmānyalakṣaṇapatitāśayābhiniviṣṭānām / tatra lokottaratamaṃ jñānaṃ buddhabodhisattvānāṃ nirābhāsadharmapravicayādanirodhānutpādadarśanātsadasatpakṣavigataṃ tathāgatabhūminairātmyādhigamātpravartate //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, I shall teach you the characteristic of knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>) and consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>), by which characteristic of knowledge and consciousness — being pierced by [this] well-differentiated [understanding] — you and other <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas</s>, having entered the course of the characteristic of knowledge and consciousness, will quickly attain unsurpassed perfect enlightenment. Therein, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, knowledge is of three kinds: worldly (<s>laukika</s>), supramundane (<s>lokottara</s>), and most supramundane (<s>lokottaratama</s>). Therein, consciousness arises and perishes. Knowledge neither arises nor perishes. Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, consciousness falls under sign and non-sign, and is caused by the characteristics of the variety of existence and non-existence. Knowledge has the characteristic of transcending sign and non-sign. Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, consciousness has the characteristic of accumulation. Knowledge has the characteristic of diminishment. Therein, the threefold knowledge ascertains specific and general characteristics, ascertains arising and ceasing, and ascertains non-arising and non-ceasing. Therein, worldly knowledge [belongs to] all heretical teachers and foolish ordinary beings who are attached to the theses of existent and non-existent. Therein, supramundane knowledge [belongs to] all <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> who are attached to the dispositions falling under specific and general characteristics. Therein, the most supramundane knowledge of <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> arises from the investigation of imageless <s>dharmas</s>, from the vision of non-ceasing and non-arising, free from the theses of existent and non-existent, through the realization of the selflessness of the <s>Tathāgata</s>-stage.

body.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate asaṅgalakṣaṇaṃ jñānam, viṣayavaicitryasaṅgalakṣaṇaṃ ca vijñānam / punaraparaṃ mahāmate trisaṅgakṣayotpādayogalakṣaṇaṃ vijñānamasaṅgasvabhāvalakṣaṇaṃ jñānam / punaraparaṃ mahāmate aprāptilakṣaṇaṃ jñānaṃ svapratyātmāryajñānagatigocaramapraveśānirgamatvādudakacandravajjale //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, knowledge has the characteristic of non-attachment; consciousness has the characteristic of attachment to the variety of objects. Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, consciousness has the characteristic of the yoga of arising through the destruction of the three attachments; knowledge has the characteristic of the inherent nature of non-attachment. Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, knowledge has the characteristic of non-attainment, because there is no entering or exiting the domain of one's own inner noble knowledge-realization — like the moon in water.

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Therein this is said:

children.text: cittena cīyate karma jñānena ca vidhīyate /
children.translated_text: <s>Karma</s> (action) is accumulated by mind (<s>citta</s>); by knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>) it is regulated;

children.text: prajñayā ca nirābhāsaṃ prabhāvaṃ cādhigacchati // Lank_3.38 //
children.translated_text: and by wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), [one attains] imagelessness and realizes the [supreme] power. [Laṅk 3.38]
Mind is connected with objects; knowledge operates in reasoning;

children.text: nirābhāse viśeṣe ca prajñā vai saṃpravartate // Lank_3.39 //
children.translated_text: in imagelessness and distinction, wisdom indeed operates. [Laṅk 3.39]
Mind, <s>manas</s>, and consciousness, perception — free from discrimination [only in name];

children.text: vikalpadharmatāṃ prāptāḥ śrāvakā na jinātmajāḥ // Lank_3.40 //
children.translated_text: [those who have] attained the nature of discrimination are <s>Śrāvakas</s>, not sons of the <s>Jina</s>. [Laṅk 3.40]

children.text: śānte kṣāntiviśeṣe vai jñānaṃ tāthāgataṃ śubham /
children.translated_text: In the peaceful, in the distinction of patience (<s>kṣānti</s>), the auspicious <s>Tathāgata</s>-knowledge
arises for the purpose of distinction, free from manifest activity. [Laṅk 3.41]

children.text: prajñā hi trividhā mahyaṃ āryā yena prabhāvitā /
children.translated_text: Wisdom is threefold for me — the noble, by which [one is] illumined,

children.text: lakṣaṇaṃ kalpyate yena yaśca bhāvān vṛṇoti ca // Lank_3.42 //
children.translated_text: that by which characteristics are conceptualized, and that which conceals entities. [Laṅk 3.42]
Dissociated from the two vehicles, wisdom free from non-existence —
through attachment to existence, it operates for <s>Śrāvakas</s>;
through entry into mind-only, wisdom is considered that of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. [Laṅk 3.43]

body.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate navavidhā pariṇāmavādināṃ tīrthakarāṇāṃ pariṇāmadṛṣṭirbhavati yaduta saṃsthānapariṇāmo lakṣaṇapariṇāmo hetupariṇāmo yuktipariṇāmo dṛṣṭipariṇāma utpādapariṇāmo bhāvapariṇāmaḥ pratyayābhivyaktipariṇāmaḥ kriyābhivyaktipariṇāmaḥ / etā mahāmate nava pariṇāmadṛṣṭayaḥ, yāḥ saṃdhāya sarvatīrthakarāḥ sadasatpakṣotpādapariṇāmavādino bhavanti //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the heretical teachers who are proponents of transformation (<s>pariṇāmavādin</s>) have nine kinds of views of transformation: namely, transformation of configuration (<s>saṃsthānapariṇāma</s>), transformation of characteristics (<s>lakṣaṇapariṇāma</s>), transformation of cause (<s>hetupariṇāma</s>), transformation of reasoning (<s>yuktipariṇāma</s>), transformation of views (<s>dṛṣṭipariṇāma</s>), transformation of arising (<s>utpādapariṇāma</s>), transformation of entity (<s>bhāvapariṇāma</s>), transformation of the manifestation of conditions (<s>pratyayābhivyaktipariṇāma</s>), and transformation of the manifestation of action (<s>kriyābhivyaktipariṇāma</s>). These, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, are the nine views of transformation, with reference to which all heretical teachers become proponents of transformation through the arising of the theses of existent and non-existent.

body.text: tatra mahāmate saṃsthānapariṇāmo yaduta saṃsthānasyānyathābhāvadarśanāt, suvarṇasya bhūṣaṇavikṛtivaicitryadarśanavat / tadyathā mahāmate suvarṇaṃ kaṭakarucakasvastyādipariṇāmena pariṇāmyamānaṃ vicitrasaṃsthānapariṇataṃ dṛśyate / na suvarṇaṃ bhāvataḥ pariṇamati / evameva mahāmate sarvabhāvānāṃ pariṇāmaḥ kaiścittīrthakarairvikalpyate anyaiśca kāraṇataḥ / na ca te tathā, na cānyathā parikalpamupādāya / evaṃ sarvapariṇāmabhedo draṣṭavyo dadhikṣīramadyaphalapākavat / tadyathā mahāmate evaṃ dadhikṣīramadyaphalādīnāmekaikasya pariṇāmo vikalpasya pariṇāmo vikalpyate tīrthakaraiḥ, na cātra kaścitpariṇamati sadasatoḥ svacittadṛśyabāhyabhāvābhāvāt, evameva mahāmate bālapṛthagjanānāṃ svacittavikalpabhāvanāpravṛttirdraṣṭavyā / nātra mahāmate kaściddharmaḥ pravartate vā nivartate vā, māyāsvapnapravṛttarūpadarśanavat / tadyathā mahāmate svapne pravṛttinivṛttī upalabhyete vandhyāputramṛtajanmavat //
body.translated_text: Therein, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the transformation of configuration is seeing the becoming-otherwise of configuration — like seeing the variety of modifications of gold into ornaments. Just as, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, gold, being modified by transformation into bangles, rings, <s>svastika</s>-patterns, and such, is seen as transformed into diverse configurations — yet gold does not transform in reality; even so, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the transformation of all entities is conceptualized by some heretical teachers, and by others from [the standpoint of] causation. And they are not like that, nor otherwise — depending on imagination. Thus should all differentiation of transformation be seen — like the ripening of curds, milk, wine, and fruit. Just as, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the transformation of each one of curds, milk, wine, fruit, etc. is conceptualized as transformation of a conceptualization by heretical teachers — and nothing here transforms from the existent or non-existent, because of the non-existence of external entities [which are merely] appearances of one's own mind; even so, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, should the operation of the cultivation of the discriminations of one's own mind of foolish ordinary beings be seen. No <s>dharma</s> here, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, operates or ceases — like seeing forms operating in illusion and dream. Just as, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, operating and ceasing are apprehended in a dream — like the birth of a dead child from a barren woman.

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Therein this is said:

children.translated_text: Transformation in time, configuration, elements, entities, and sense-faculties;

children.text: antarābhavasaṃgrāhyo ye kalpenti na te budhāḥ // Lank_3.44 //
children.translated_text: that which is grasped as an intermediate state — those who conceptualize thus are not the wise. [Laṅk 3.44]

children.text: na pratītyasamutpannaṃ lokaṃ kalpenti vai jināḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>Jinas</s> (Conquerors) do not conceptualize the world as dependently co-arisen;

children.text: kiṃ tu pratyaya evedaṃ lokaṃ gandharvasaṃnibham // Lank_3.45 //
children.translated_text: rather, this condition [alone] — the world resembling a <s>Gandharva</s>[-city]. [Laṅk 3.45]

body.text: atha khalu mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ punarapi bhagavantaṃ sarvadharmasaṃdhyarthaparimocanārthamadhyeṣate sma - deśayatu me bhagavān, deśayatu me tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ sarvadharmāṇāṃ saṃdhyasaṃdhilakṣaṇam, yena saṃdhyasaṃdhilakṣaṇena suprativibhāgābhividdhena ahaṃ ca anye ca bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ sarvasaṃdhyasaṃdhyupāyakuśalā yathārutārthābhiniveśasaṃdhau na prapateyuḥ / sarvadharmāṇāṃ saṃdhyasaṃdhikauśalena vāgakṣaraprativikalpanaṃ ca vinihatya buddhyā sarvabuddhakṣetraparṣaccāriṇo balavaśitābhijñādhāraṇīmudrāsumudritā vicitrairnirmāṇakiraṇairdaśaniṣṭhāpāde
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s> again entreated the Blessed One for the purpose of liberating the meaning of the intended purport (<s>saṃdhi</s>) of all <s>dharmas</s>: 'May the Blessed One teach me, may the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, perfectly enlightened <s>Buddha</s>, teach the characteristic of the intended purport and its connection (<s>saṃdhyasaṃdhilakṣaṇa</s>) of all <s>dharmas</s>, so that I and other <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas</s>, pierced by [this] well-differentiated [understanding], skilled in the means of all intended purports and their connections, may not fall into the intended purport of attachment to the literal meaning. Through skill in the intended purport and connection of all <s>dharmas</s>, having destroyed the conceptual discrimination of speech-syllables by wisdom, traversing all <s>Buddha</s>-field assemblies, well-sealed with the seals of powers, masteries, superknowledges, and <s>dhāraṇīs</s>, with diverse emanation-rays, [established] in the ten ground-positions—'

body.text: sunibaddhabuddhayo 'nābhogacandrasūryamaṇimahābhūtacaryāgatisamāḥ sarvabhūmiṣu svavikalpalakṣaṇavinivṛttadṛṣṭayaḥ svapnamāyādisarvadharmānudarśanādbuddhabhūmyāśrayānupraviṣṭāḥ sarvasattvadhātuṃ yathārhattvadharmadeśanayā
body.translated_text: Those whose minds are firmly bound, whose conduct is comparable to the effortless activity of the moon, sun, gems, and great elements, who on all <s>bhūmis</s> (stages) have turned away from the views characterized by their own <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual discrimination), who through perceiving all <s>dharmas</s> as dream, illusion and the like have entered into the support of the <s>Buddha-bhūmi</s> (Buddha-stage), drawing in all beings in the realm of sentient beings through teaching the <s>Dharma</s> as is appropriate

body.text: ākṛṣya svapnamāyādisarvadharmasadasatpakṣavarjite bhaṅgotpādavikalparahite rutānyathāparyāyavṛttyāśrayatayā pratiṣṭhāpayeyuḥ / bhagavānāha - sādhu sādhu mahāmate / tena hi mahāmate śṛṇu, sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasikuru / bhāṣiṣye 'haṃ te / sādhu bhagavanniti mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavataḥ pratyaśrauṣīt / bhagavāṃstasyaitadavocat - aparimito mahāmate sarvadharmāṇāṃ yathārutārthābhiniveśasaṃdhiḥ, lakṣaṇābhiniveśasaṃdhiḥ, pratyayābhiniveśasaṃdhiḥ, bhāvābhāvābhiniveśasaṃdhiḥ, utpādānutpādavikalpābhiniveśasaṃdhiḥ, nirodhānirodhābhiniveśaprativikalpasaṃdhiḥ, yānāyānābhiniveśaprativikalpasaṃdhiḥ, saṃskṛtāsaṃskṛtaprativikalpābhiniveśasaṃdhiḥ, bhūmyabhūmisvalakṣaṇavikalpābhiniveśasaṃdhiḥ, svavikalpābhisamayavikalpasaṃdhiḥ, sadasatpakṣatīrthyāśrayaprativikalpasaṃdhiḥ, triyānaikayānābhisamayavikalpasaṃdhiḥ / ete cānye ca mahāmate bālapṛthagjanānāṃ svavikalpasaṃdhayaḥ, yāṃ saṃdhiṃ saṃdhāya bālapṛthagjanāḥ prativikalpayamānāḥ kauśeyakrimaya iva svavikalpadṛṣṭisaṃdhisūtreṇa ātmānaṃ parāṃśca svavikalpadṛṣṭisaṃdhisūtrarocanatayā pariveṣṭayanti bhāvābhāvasaṃdhilakṣaṇābhiniveśābhiniviṣṭāḥ / na cātra mahāmate kaścitsaṃdhirna saṃdhilakṣaṇaṃ viviktadarśanātsarvadharmāṇām / vikalpasyāpravṛttatvānmahāmate bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ sarvadharmeṣu viviktadarśī viharati //
body.translated_text: would establish them in a support characterized by the turning of meaning into alternative expressions and sounds, free from the sides of existent and non-existent regarding all <s>dharmas</s> as dream, illusion and the like, devoid of <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual discrimination) of arising and destruction. The Blessed One said: Well done, well done, <s>Mahāmati</s>! Therefore, <s>Mahāmati</s>, listen and attend well and thoroughly. I shall speak to you. "Very well, Blessed One" — thus the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s> assented to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said to him: Limitless, <s>Mahāmati</s>, are the nexuses of attachment to meaning as literally expressed regarding all <s>dharmas</s>: the nexus of attachment to characteristics, the nexus of attachment to conditions, the nexus of attachment to existence and non-existence, the nexus of attachment through <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual discrimination) of production and non-production, the nexus of counter-discrimination through attachment to cessation and non-cessation, the nexus of counter-discrimination through attachment to vehicle and non-vehicle, the nexus of attachment through counter-discrimination of the conditioned and unconditioned, the nexus of attachment through <s>vikalpa</s> of the own-characteristics of stages and non-stages, the nexus of <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual discrimination) regarding realization of one's own <s>vikalpa</s>, the nexus of counter-discrimination regarding the support of <s>tīrthyas</s> (heretics) in the sides of existent and non-existent, the nexus of <s>vikalpa</s> regarding the realization of three vehicles and one vehicle. These and others, <s>Mahāmati</s>, are the nexuses of the own <s>vikalpa</s> of childish ordinary beings. Bound by these nexuses, childish ordinary beings, discriminating and counter-discriminating, like silkworms, wrap themselves and others with the thread of the nexus of their own <s>vikalpa</s>-views, delighting in the thread of the nexus of their own <s>vikalpa</s>-views, attached to attachment to the characteristics of the nexus of existence and non-existence. But here, <s>Mahāmati</s>, there is no nexus whatsoever, nor any nexus-characteristic, because all <s>dharmas</s> are seen as solitary. Because <s>vikalpa</s> does not operate, <s>Mahāmati</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> abides seeing all <s>dharmas</s> as solitary.

body.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate bāhyabhāvābhāvasvacittadṛśyalakṣaṇāvabodhānnirābhāsacittamātrānusāritvātsadasatoḥ sarvabhāvavikalpasaṃdhiviviktadarśanānna saṃdhirnāsaṃdhilakṣaṇaṃ sarvadharmāṇām / nātra kaścinmahāmate badhyate na ca mucyate, anyatra vitathapatitayā buddhyā bandhamokṣau prajñāyete / tatkasya hetoḥ? yaduta sadasatoḥ saṃdhyanupalabdhitvātsarvadharmāṇām //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Mahāmati</s>, through understanding the characteristic that external existence and non-existence are mere appearances of one's own mind, through following mind-only that is free from appearances, through seeing the solitude of the nexus of <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual discrimination) of all entities as existent and non-existent — there is no nexus nor any nexus-characteristic of all <s>dharmas</s>. Here, <s>Mahāmati</s>, no one is bound and no one is liberated; it is only through a falsely fallen cognition that bondage and liberation are perceived. For what reason? Because the nexus is unapprehended in all <s>dharmas</s> as either existent or non-existent.

body.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate trayaḥ saṃdhayo bālānāṃ pṛthagjanānāṃ yaduta rāgo dveṣo mohaśca / tṛṣṇā ca paunarbhavikī nandīrāgasahagatā yāṃ saṃdhāya gatisaṃdhayaḥ prajāyante / tatra saṃdhisaṃdhānaṃ sattvānāṃ gatipañcakaṃ saṃdhervyucchedānmahāmate nasaṃdhirnāsaṃdhilakṣaṇaṃ prajñāyate / punaraparaṃ mahāmate trisaṃgatipratyayakriyāyogābhiniveśāya saṃdhiḥ / vijñānānāṃ nairantaryātpravṛttiyogenābhiniveśato bhavasaṃdhirbhavati / trisaṃgatipratyayavyāvṛttervijñānānāṃ vimokṣatrayānudarśanātsarvasaṃdhayo na pravartante //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Mahāmati</s>, there are three nexuses of childish ordinary beings, namely: <s>rāga</s> (passion), <s>dveṣa</s> (hatred), and <s>moha</s> (delusion). And the craving for re-becoming, accompanied by delight and passion — by binding through that nexus, the nexuses of the destinies arise. Therein, through the nexus-binding of beings, there is the fivefold destiny. Through the cutting off of the nexus, <s>Mahāmati</s>, neither nexus nor nexus-characteristic is perceived. Furthermore, <s>Mahāmati</s>, the nexus serves attachment to the conjunction of conditions and the application of the three convergences. Through the uninterrupted operation of the <s>vijñānas</s> (consciousnesses), through attachment by the application of activity, the nexus of becoming arises. Through the turning away from the conditions of the three convergences, through perceiving the three liberations of the <s>vijñānas</s>, all nexuses cease to operate.

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Here it is said:

children.translated_text: <s>Abhūtaparikalpa</s> (unreal conceptual construction) is indeed declared to be the characteristic of the nexus;
Through the true knowledge of that, the net of nexuses becomes clear. (Laṅk. 3.46)
Just as silkworms, through grasping at the sounds of knowledge of entities,
The childish, who are ignorant of the nexus, are bound by their own <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual discrimination). (Laṅk. 3.47)

body.text: punarapi mahāmatirāha - yatpunaretaduktaṃ bhagavatā - yena yena vikalpena ye ye bhāvā vikalpyante, na hi sa teṣāṃ svabhāvo bhavati / parikalpita evāsau / tadyadi bhagavan parikalpita
body.translated_text: Again <s>Mahāmati</s> said: As for what was said by the Blessed One — "By whatever <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual discrimination) whatever entities are discriminated, that is not their own-nature; it is merely imagined" — if, Blessed One, it is merely imagined

body.text: evāsau na bhāvasvabhāvalakṣaṇāvadhāraṇam, nanu te bhagavan evaṃ bruvataḥ saṃkleśavyavadānābhāvaḥ prasajyate parikalpitasvabhāvabhāvitatvātsarvadharmāṇām / bhagavānāha - evametanmahāmate yathā vadasi / na mahāmate yathā bālapṛthagjanairbhāvasvabhāvo vikalpyate, tathā bhavati / parikalpita evāsau mahāmate, na bhāvasvabhāvalakṣaṇāvadhāraṇam / kiṃ tu yathā mahāmate āryairbhāvasvabhāvo 'vadhāryate āryeṇa jñānena āryeṇa darśanena āryeṇa prajñāacakṣuṣā tathā bhāvasvabhāvo bhavati //
body.translated_text: and there is no ascertainment of the own-nature-characteristic of entities, then, Blessed One, for one who speaks thus, would not the absence of defilement and purification follow, since all <s>dharmas</s> have the nature of <s>parikalpita-svabhāva</s> (imagined own-nature)? The Blessed One said: It is just so, <s>Mahāmati</s>, as you say. <s>Mahāmati</s>, the own-nature of entities does not exist as it is discriminated by childish ordinary beings. It is merely imagined, <s>Mahāmati</s>, not an ascertainment of the own-nature-characteristic of entities. However, <s>Mahāmati</s>, as the own-nature of entities is ascertained by the Noble Ones through noble knowledge, through noble vision, through the noble eye of wisdom — so the own-nature of entities exists.

body.text: mahāmatirāha - tadyadi bhagavan yathā āryairāryeṇa jñānena āryeṇa darśanena āryeṇa prajñācakṣuṣā na divyamāṃsacakṣuṣā bhāvasvabhāvo 'vadhāryate tathā bhavati, na tu yathā bālapṛthagjanairvikalpyate bhāvasvabhāvaḥ, tatkathaṃ bhagavan bālapṛthagjanānāṃ vikalpavyāvṛttirbhaviṣyati āryabhāvavastvanavabodhāt? na ca te bhagavan viparyastāḥ nāviparyastāḥ / tatkasya hetoḥ? yaduta āryavastusvabhāvānavabodhātsadasatorlakṣaṇasya vṛttidarśanāt / āryairapi bhagavan yathā vastu vikalpyate, na tathā bhavati svalakṣaṇaviṣayāgocaratvāt / sa teṣāmapi bhagavan bhāvasvabhāvalakṣaṇaḥ parikalpitasvabhāva eva khyāyate hetvahetuvyapadeśāt / yaduta bhāvasvalakṣaṇadṛṣṭipatitatvādanyeṣāṃ gocaro bhavati na yathā teṣām / ityevamanavasthā prasajyate bhagavan bhāvasvabhāvalakṣaṇānavabodhāt / na ca bhagavan parikalpitasvabhāvahetuko bhāvasvabhāvalakṣaṇaḥ / sa ca kathaṃ parikalpena prativikalpyamāno na tathā bhaviṣyati yathā parikalpyate? anyadeva bhagavan prativikalpasya lakṣaṇam, anyadeva svabhāvalakṣaṇam / visadṛśahetuke ca bhagavan vikalpasvabhāvalakṣaṇe / te ca parasparaṃ parikalpyamāne bālapṛthagjanairna tathā bhaviṣyataḥ / kiṃ tu sattvānāṃ vikalpavyāvṛttyarthamidamucyate / yathā prativikalpena vikalpyante tathā na vidyante //
body.translated_text: <s>Mahāmati</s> said: If, Blessed One, the own-nature of entities exists as it is ascertained by the Noble Ones through noble knowledge, through noble vision, through the noble eye of wisdom and not through the divine eye or the fleshly eye, and it does not exist as the own-nature of entities is discriminated by childish ordinary beings, then how, Blessed One, will the turning away from <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual discrimination) occur for childish ordinary beings, since they do not understand the reality of noble existence? They, Blessed One, are neither perverted nor unperverted. For what reason? Because they do not understand the own-nature of noble reality, and because they see the operation of characteristics of both existent and non-existent. Even the Noble Ones, Blessed One, do not find that entities exist as they discriminate them, because the domain of own-characteristics is inaccessible. Thus, Blessed One, even for them the own-nature-characteristic of entities appears to be of merely imagined own-nature, because of the designation of causes and non-causes. That is to say, because others have fallen into the view of the own-characteristics of entities, it becomes the domain of others but not as it is for them. Thus an infinite regress follows, Blessed One, due to the non-understanding of the own-nature-characteristic of entities. And, Blessed One, the own-nature-characteristic of entities is not caused by imagined own-nature. How then will it, being counter-discriminated by imagination, not be as it is imagined? The characteristic of counter-discrimination, Blessed One, is one thing, and the own-nature-characteristic is another. And, Blessed One, the own-nature-characteristic of <s>vikalpa</s> has dissimilar causes. When these two are mutually imagined by childish ordinary beings, they will not be as imagined. Rather, this is said for the purpose of turning away the <s>vikalpa</s> of beings: as they are discriminated by counter-discrimination, so they do not exist.

body.text: kimidaṃ bhagavan sattvānāṃ tvayā nāstyastitvadṛṣṭiṃ vinivārya vastusvabhāvābhiniveśena āryajñānagocaraviṣayābhiniveśānnāstitvadṛṣṭiḥ punarnipātyate, viviktadharmopadeśābhāvaśca kriyate āryajñānasvabhāvavastudeśanayā? bhagavānāha - na mayā mahāmate viviktadharmopadeśābhāvaḥ kriyate, na cāstitvadṛṣṭirnipātyate āryavastusvabhāvanirdeśena / kiṃ tu utrāsapadavivarjanārthaṃ sattvānāṃ mahāmate mayā anādikālabhāvasvabhāvalakṣaṇābhiniviṣṭānāmāryajñānavastusvabhāvābhiniveśalakṣaṇadṛṣṭyā viviktadharmopadeśaḥ kriyate / na mayā mahāmate bhāvasvabhāvopadeśaḥ kriyate / kiṃ tu mahāmate svayamevādhigatayāthātathyaviviktadharmavihāriṇo bhaviṣyanti / bhrānternirnimittadarśanāt svacittadṛśyamātramavatīrya bāhyadṛśyabhāvābhāvavinivṛttadṛṣṭayo vimokṣatrayādhigatayāthātathyaviviktadharmavihāriṇo bhaviṣyanti / bhrānternirnimittadṛṣṭayo vimokṣatrayādhigatayāthātathyamudrāsumudritā bhāvasvabhāveṣu pratyātmādhigatayā buddhyā pratyakṣavihāriṇo bhaviṣyanti nāstyastitvavastudṛṣṭivivarjitāḥ //
body.translated_text: Is it, Blessed One, that having turned away the view of non-existence and existence for beings, you, through attachment to the own-nature of reality, through attachment to the domain of <s>āryajñāna</s> (noble knowledge), again cause the view of non-existence to fall, and create the absence of teaching the <s>viviktadharma</s> (solitary dharma) through teaching the own-nature-reality of <s>āryajñāna</s> (noble knowledge)? The Blessed One said: I do not, <s>Mahāmati</s>, create the absence of teaching the <s>viviktadharma</s> (solitary dharma), nor do I cause the view of existence to fall through pointing out the own-nature of noble reality. Rather, <s>Mahāmati</s>, for the sake of removing the ground of terror for beings who from beginningless time have been attached to the own-nature-characteristics of entities, I teach the <s>viviktadharma</s> (solitary dharma) through the view characterized by attachment to the own-nature-reality of <s>āryajñāna</s> (noble knowledge). I do not, <s>Mahāmati</s>, teach the own-nature of entities. Rather, <s>Mahāmati</s>, they will themselves become dwellers in the <s>viviktadharma</s> (solitary dharma) of the truly realized suchness. Through seeing the signless in confusion, having descended into the mere visibility of one's own mind, with views turned away from the existence and non-existence of external appearances, they will become dwellers in the <s>viviktadharma</s> (solitary dharma) of the truly realized <s>vimokṣatraya</s> (three liberations). With views of the signless in confusion, sealed with the seal of the truly realized <s>vimokṣatraya</s> (three liberations), through the personally realized cognition regarding the own-nature of entities, they will become dwellers in direct experience, free from views of the reality of non-existence and existence.

body.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate anutpannāḥ sarvadharmā iti bodhisattvena mahāsattvena pratijñā na karaṇīyā / tatkasya hetoḥ? pratijñāyāḥ sarvasvabhāvabhāvitvāttaddhetupravṛttilakṣaṇatvācca / anutpannān
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Mahāmati</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> should not make the proposition (<s>pratijñā</s>): "All <s>dharmas</s> are unproduced." For what reason? Because the proposition has the nature of every own-nature, and because it has the characteristic of proceeding from that cause. Having proposed that all

body.text: sarvadharmān pratijñāya pratibruvan mahāmate bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ pratijñāyā hīyate / yā pratijñā - anutpannāḥ sarvadharmā iti, sāsya pratijñā hīyate, pratijñāyāstadapekṣotpattitvāt / atha sāpi pratijñā anutpannā sarvadharmābhyantarādanutpannalakṣaṇānutpattitvātpratijñāyāḥ, anutpannāḥ sarvadharmā iti sa vādaḥ prahīyate / pratijñāvayavakāraṇena sadasato 'nutpattiḥ pratijñāyāḥ / sā hi mahāmate pratijñā sarvabhāvābhyantarā sadasatoranutpattilakṣaṇāt / yadi mahāmate tayā pratijñayā anutpannayā anutpannāḥ sarvabhāvā iti pratijñāṃ kurvanti, evamapi pratijñāhāniḥ prasajyate / pratijñāyāḥ sadasatoranutpattibhāvalakṣaṇatvātpratijñā na karaṇīyā / anutpannasvabhāvalakṣaṇā hi mahāmate teṣāṃ pratijñā bhavati / ataste mahāmate pratijñā na karaṇīyā / bahudoṣaduṣṭatvādavayavānāṃ parasparahetuvilakṣaṇakṛtakatvācca avayavānāṃ pratijñā na karaṇīyā - yaduta anutpannāḥ sarvadharmāḥ / evaṃ śūnyā asvabhāvāḥ sarvadharmā iti mahāmate bodhisattvena mahāsattvena pratijñā na karaṇīyā / kiṃ tu mahāmate bodhisattvena mahāsattvena māyāsvapnavatsarvabhāvopadeśaḥ karaṇīyo dṛśyādṛśyalakṣaṇatvāt / dṛṣṭibuddhimohanatvācca sarvadharmāṇāṃ māyāsvapnavadbhāvopadeśaḥ karaṇīyo 'nyatra bālānāmutrāsapadavivarjanatayā / bālāḥ pṛthagjanā hi mahāmate / nāstyastitvadṛṣṭipatitānāṃ teṣāmutrāsaḥ syānmā iti / utrāsyamānā mahāmate dūrībhavanti mahāyānāt //
body.translated_text: <s>dharmas</s> are unproduced and asserting this, <s>Mahāmati</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> is defeated in the proposition. The proposition "all <s>dharmas</s> are unproduced" — that proposition of his is defeated, because the proposition depends on that for its arising. If that proposition too is unproduced, being within the scope of all <s>dharmas</s>, since the proposition does not arise due to having the characteristic of non-arising — then the thesis "all <s>dharmas</s> are unproduced" is abandoned. Through the constituent cause of the proposition, there is non-arising of the proposition as either existent or non-existent. For, <s>Mahāmati</s>, that proposition is within the scope of all entities, due to the characteristic of non-arising of both existent and non-existent. If, <s>Mahāmati</s>, by that unproduced proposition they make the proposition "all entities are unproduced," then too the defeat of the proposition follows. Because the proposition has the nature-characteristic of non-arising of both existent and non-existent, the proposition should not be made. For, <s>Mahāmati</s>, theirs is a proposition with the own-nature-characteristic of being unproduced. Therefore, <s>Mahāmati</s>, the proposition should not be made, because of the many faults corrupting the constituents, and because the constituents are made of mutually dissimilar causes — namely, the proposition "all <s>dharmas</s> are unproduced" should not be made. Likewise, <s>Mahāmati</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> should not make the proposition "all <s>dharmas</s> are empty and without own-nature." Rather, <s>Mahāmati</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> should teach all entities as being like illusion and dream, because they have the characteristic of being both visible and invisible. And because all <s>dharmas</s> delude the intellect of those with views, they should be taught as being like illusion and dream — except for the purpose of removing the ground of terror for the childish. For childish ordinary beings, <s>Mahāmati</s> — for those who have fallen into the view of non-existence and existence, there would be terror, thinking "let it not be so." Being terrified, <s>Mahāmati</s>, they become distant from the <s>Mahāyāna</s>.

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Here it is said:

children.text: na svabhāvo na vijñaptirna vastu na ca ālayaḥ /
children.translated_text: There is no own-nature, no cognition, no reality, and no <s>ālaya</s> (storehouse);
These are imagined by the childish, who are like corpses, poor reasoners. (Laṅk. 3.48)
"All <s>dharmas</s> are unproduced" — this is for the establishment of all <s>tīrthyas</s> (heretics);

children.text: na hi kasyacidutpannā bhāvā vai pratyayānvitāḥ // Lank_3.49 //
children.translated_text: For no entities whatsoever have arisen, though connected with conditions. (Laṅk. 3.49)
"All <s>dharmas</s> are unproduced" — one should not discriminate this through <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom);
Because of that having a cause, and that being established, their understanding is defeated. (Laṅk. 3.50)
Just as a hair-net is falsely grasped by people with cataracts,
So this <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual discrimination) of entities is falsely imagined by the childish. (Laṅk. 3.51)
The three realms of existence are mere designation; they do not exist from the standpoint of the own-nature of reality;
Through designation and the nature of reality, the logicians will construct. (Laṅk. 3.52)

children.text: nimittaṃ vastu vijñaptiṃ manovispanditaṃ ca tat /
children.translated_text: Signs, reality, cognition, and the agitation of mind —

children.text: atikramya tu putrā me nirvikalpāścaranti te // Lank_3.53 //
children.translated_text: Having transcended these, my sons, they move about free from <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual discrimination). (Laṅk. 3.53)

children.text: ajale ca jalagrāho mṛgatṛṣṇā yathā nabhe /
children.translated_text: Just as the grasping of water in a waterless place, like a mirage in the sky,

children.text: dṛśyaṃ tathā hi bālānāmāryāṇāṃ ca viśeṣataḥ // Lank_3.54 //
children.translated_text: So indeed is the visible for the childish, and distinctly so for the Noble Ones. (Laṅk. 3.54)
The vision of the Noble Ones is pure, born from the <s>vimokṣatraya</s> (three liberations),
Free from arising and destruction, moving in <s>nirābhāsa</s> (appearance-free reality). (Laṅk. 3.55)
<s>Nirābhāsa</s> (appearance-free reality) regarding entities — in their non-existence there is nothing for yogins;
Through the equality of existence and non-existence, the fruit of the Noble Ones arises.

children.text: kathaṃ hyabhāvo bhāvānāṃ kurute samatāṃ katham // Lank_3.56 //
children.translated_text: How can there be non-existence of entities? How does one bring about equality? || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.56 ||

children.text: yadā cittaṃ na jānāti bāhyamādhyātmikaṃ calam /
children.translated_text: When the mind does not know [things as] external, internal, or moving,

children.text: tadā tu kurute nāśaṃ samatācittadarśanam // Lank_3.57 //
children.translated_text: then it brings about destruction — the vision of the mind of equality. || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.57 ||

body.text: punarapi mahāmatirāha - yatpunaridamuktaṃ bhagavatā - yadā tvālambyamarthaṃ nopalabhate jñānaṃ tadā vijñaptimātravyavasthānaṃ bhavati / vijñaptergrāhyābhāvādgrāhakasyāpyagrahaṇaṃ bhavati / tadagrahaṇānna pravartate jñānaṃ vikalpasaṃśabditam / tatkiṃ punarbhagavan bhāvānāṃ svasāmānyalakṣaṇānanyavaicitryānavabodhānnopalabhate jñānam? atha svasāmānyalakṣaṇavaicitryabhāvasvabhāvābhibhavānnopalabhate jñānam / atha kuḍyakaṭavapraprākārabhūjalapavanāgnivyavahitātidūrasāmīpyānnopalabhate jñānaṃ jñeyam / atha bālāndhavṛddhayogādindriyāṇāṃ jñeyārthaṃ nopalabhate jñānam / tadyadi bhagavan svasāmānyalakṣaṇānanyavaicitryānavabodhānnopalabhate jñānam, na tarhi bhagavan jñānaṃ vaktavyam / ajñānametadbhagavan yadvidyamānamarthaṃ nopalabhate / atha svasāmānyalakṣaṇavaicitryabhāvasvabhāvābhibhavānnopalabhate jñānam, tadajñānameva bhagavan na jñānam / jñeye sati bhagavan jñānaṃ pravartate nābhāvāt / tadyogācca jñeyasya jñānamityucyate / atha kuḍyakaṭavapraprākārabhūjalapavanāgnivyavahitātidūrasāmīpyānnopalabhate bālavṛddhāndhayogavadvaikalyādindriyāṇāṃ jñānaṃ nopalabhate / tadyadevaṃ nopalabhate, na tadbhagavan jñānam / ajñānameva tadvidyamānamarthaṃ buddhivaikalyāt //
body.translated_text: <s>Mahāmati</s> again asked: As for this that was said by the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'When knowledge does not apprehend an object as something to be grasped, then the establishment of mere cognition (<s>vijñaptimātra</s>) comes about; from the absence of the graspable in cognition, there is also the non-grasping of the grasper; from that non-grasping, the knowledge called conceptual discrimination does not operate' — does, then, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowledge not apprehend because of the non-awakening to the non-otherness of the variety of specific and general characteristics of entities? Or does knowledge not apprehend because of the overpowering of the inherent nature of the variety of specific and general characteristics of entities? Or does knowledge not apprehend what is to be known because [it is] obstructed by walls, screens, curtains, ramparts, earth, water, wind, fire, or because of too great a distance or too close a proximity? Or does knowledge not apprehend what is to be known because of deficient sense-faculties, as in the case of the childish, the blind, or the aged yogin? If, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowledge does not apprehend because of the non-awakening to the non-otherness of the variety of specific and general characteristics, then, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, it should not be called knowledge. This is ignorance, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, which does not apprehend an existing object. If knowledge does not apprehend because of the overpowering of the inherent nature of the variety of specific and general characteristics, then that is just ignorance, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, not knowledge. When there is something to be known, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowledge operates — not from absence. And because of that connection, it is called 'knowledge of the knowable.' If knowledge does not apprehend because [it is] obstructed by walls, screens, curtains, ramparts, earth, water, wind, fire, or too great a distance or proximity, or like the childish, the aged, or the blind, knowledge does not apprehend due to the deficiency of sense-faculties — if it does not apprehend in this way, then that, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, is not knowledge. That is just ignorance, which does not apprehend an existing object due to the deficiency of intellect.

body.text: bhagavānāha - na hi tanmahāmate evamajñānaṃ bhavati / jñānameva tanmahāmate, nājñānam / na caitatsaṃdhāyoktaṃ mayā - yadā tvālambyamarthaṃ nopalabhate jñānaṃ tadā vijñaptimātravyavasthānaṃ bhavatīti / kiṃ tu svacittadṛśyamātrāvabodhātsadasatorbāhyabhāvābhāvājjñānamapyarthaṃ nopalabhate / tadanupalambhājjñānajñeyayorapravṛttiḥ / vimokṣatrayānugamājjñānasyāpyanupalabdhiḥ / na ca tārkikā anādikālabhāvābhāvaprapañcavāsitamataya evaṃ prajānanti / te cāprajānanto bāhyadravyasaṃsthānalakṣaṇabhāvābhāvaṃ kṛtvā vikalpasyāpravṛttiṃ cittamātratāṃ nirdekṣyanti / ātmātmīyalakṣaṇagrāhābhiniveśābhiniviṣṭāḥ svacittadṛśyamātrānavabodhājjñānaṃ jñeyaṃ prativikalpayanti / te ca jñānajñeyaprativikalpanayā bāhyabhāvābhāvapravicayānupalabdherucchedadṛṣṭimāśrayante //
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> replied: No, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, it is not ignorance in that way. That is indeed knowledge, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, not ignorance. And it was not with this intention that I said: 'When knowledge does not apprehend an object as something to be grasped, then the establishment of mere cognition comes about.' Rather, from the awakening to [the truth that all is] merely the appearance of one's own mind, because of the absence of external entities as existent or non-existent, knowledge too does not apprehend an object. From that non-apprehension, there is the non-operation of knowledge and the knowable. From the entry into the three liberations (<s>vimokṣatraya</s>), there is also the non-apprehension of knowledge [itself]. And the logicians (<s>tārkikas</s>), whose minds are perfumed by the impressions of beginningless proliferation of existence and non-existence, do not understand this. And not understanding, they assert the non-operation of conceptual discrimination — [as] mind-only (<s>cittamātra</s>) — based on the existence and non-existence of external objects, shapes, and characteristics. Being attached to the grasping of the characteristics of self and what belongs to self, due to the non-awakening to [the truth of] the mere appearance of one's own mind, they conceptually discriminate knowledge and the knowable. And through that conceptual discrimination of knowledge and knowable, because of the non-apprehension of the investigation of external existence and non-existence, they resort to the view of annihilationism (<s>ucchedadṛṣṭi</s>).

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Therein it is said:

children.text: vidyamānaṃ hi ālambyaṃ yadi jñānaṃ na paśyati /
children.translated_text: If knowledge does not see an existing graspable [object],

children.text: ajñānaṃ taddhi na jñānaṃ tārkikāṇāmayaṃ nayaḥ // Lank_3.58 //
children.translated_text: that is ignorance, not knowledge — this is the method of the logicians. || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.58 ||
If knowledge does not see because of the absence of a different characteristic,
[or because of] obstruction, distance, or proximity — that is called false knowledge. || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.59 ||
And if knowledge does not arise due to the condition of the childish, aged, or blind,

children.text: vidyamānaṃ hi tajjñeyaṃ mithyājñānaṃ taducyate // Lank_3.60 //
children.translated_text: that knowable indeed exists [yet] is unseen — that is called false knowledge. || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.60 ||

body.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate bālapṛthagjanā anādikālaprapañcadauṣṭhulyasvaprativikalpanā nāṭake nṛtyantaḥ svasiddhāntanayadeśanāyāmakuśalāḥ svacittadṛśyabāhyabhāvalakṣaṇābhiniviṣṭā upāyadeśanāpāṭhamabhiniviśante, na svasiddhāntanayaṃ cātuṣkoṭikanayaviśuddhaṃ prativibhāvayanti / mahāmatirāha - evametadbhagavan yathā vadasi / deśayatu me bhagavān deśanāsiddhāntanayalakṣaṇaṃ yena ahaṃ ca anye ca bodhisattvā mahāsattvā anāgate 'dhvani deśanāsiddhāntanayakuśalā na vipralabhyeran kutārkikaistīrthakaraśrāvakapratyekabuddhayānikaiḥ / bhagavānāha - yena hi mahāmate śṛṇu, sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasikuru / bhāṣiṣye 'haṃ te / sādhu bhagavanniti mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavataḥ pratyaśrauṣīt / bhagavāṃstasyaitadavocat - dviprakāro mahāmate atītānāgatapratyutpannānāṃ tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ dharmanayo yaduta deśanānayaśca siddhāntapratyavasthānanayaśca / tatra deśanāpāṭhanayo mahāmate yaduta vicitrasaṃbhārasūtropadeśaḥ / yathācittādhimuktikatayā deśayanti sattvebhyaḥ / tatra siddhāntanayaḥ punarmahāmate katamaḥ? yena yoginaḥ svacittadṛśyavikalpavyāvṛttiṃ kurvanti yaduta ekatvānyatvobhayatvānubhayatvapakṣāpatanatācittamanomanovijñānātītaṃ svapratyātmāryagatigocaraṃ hetuyuktidṛṣṭilakṣaṇavinivṛttamanālīḍhaṃ sarvakutārkikaistīrthakaraśrāvakapratyekabuddhayānikairnāstyastitvāntadvayapatitaiḥ, tamahaṃ siddhānta iti vadāmi / etanmahāmate siddhāntanayadeśanālakṣaṇaṃ yatra tvayā ca anyaiśca bodhisattvairmahāsattvairyogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the foolish ordinary beings, through their own conceptual discriminations of the depravity of beginningless proliferation, dancing on the stage [of existence], unskillful in the teaching of their own doctrinal method, and attached to the characteristics of external entities as appearances of their own mind — cling to the reading of the expedient teaching and do not discern [that] their own doctrinal method is purified by the method of the fourfold [proposition]. <s>Mahāmati</s> asked: Thus it is, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, as you say. May the <s>Bhagavān</s> teach me the characteristic of the method of teaching and doctrine, so that I and other <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas</s>, in the future time, being skillful in the method of teaching and doctrine, may not be deceived by the wrong logicians — non-Buddhist teachers, <s>Śrāvakas</s>, and those of the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> vehicle. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: Then, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, listen, and attend well and thoroughly. I shall teach you. 'Very well, O <s>Bhagavān</s>,' the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s> assented to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said this to him: The <s>Dharma</s>-method of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly awakened ones, of the past, future, and present, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is twofold — namely, the method of teaching (<s>deśanānaya</s>) and the method of the doctrine's establishment (<s>siddhāntapratyavasthānanaya</s>). Therein, the method of teaching-recitation, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the instruction through varied collections of <s>sūtras</s>. According to the faith and disposition of the mind, [the <s>Tathāgatas</s>] teach beings. Therein, what, moreover, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the method of the doctrine? By which <s>yogins</s> turn away from the conceptual discrimination of the appearance of their own mind — namely, not falling into the theses of oneness, otherness, both, or neither, transcending mind, <s>manas</s>, and <s>manovijñāna</s>, having the domain of one's own inner noble course, free from the characteristics of views based on cause and reasoning, untouched by all the wrong logicians — non-Buddhist teachers, <s>Śrāvakas</s>, and those of the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> vehicle who have fallen into the duality of existence and non-existence — that I call the doctrine (<s>siddhānta</s>). This, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the characteristic of the method of doctrine and teaching, in which you and other <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas</s> should practice <s>yoga</s>.

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Therein it is said:

children.text: nayo hi dvividho mahyaṃ siddhānto deśanā ca vai /
children.translated_text: The method for me is twofold — the doctrine and the teaching;

children.text: deśemi yā bālānāṃ siddhāntaṃ yogināmaham // Lank_3.61 //
children.translated_text: I teach for the childish; the doctrine [I give] to the <s>yogins</s>. || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.61 ||

body.text: atha khalu mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ punarapi bhagavantametadavocat - uktametadbhagavaṃstathāgatenārhatā samyaksaṃbuddhena ekasmin kāle ekasmin samaye yathā lokāyatiko vicitramantrapratibhāno na sevitavyo na bhaktavyo na paryupāsitavyaḥ, yaṃ ca sevamānasya lokāmiṣasaṃgraho bhavati na dharmasaṃgraha iti / kiṃ kāraṇaṃ punarbhagavatedamuktaṃ lokāyatiko vicitramantrapratibhānaḥ, yaṃ ca sevamānasya lokāmiṣasaṃgraho bhavati na dharmasaṃgrahaḥ? bhagavānāha - vicitramantrapratibhāno mahāmate lokāyatiko vicitrairhetupadavyañjanairbālān vyāmohayati na yuktiyuktaṃ nārthopasaṃhitam / atha yāvadeva yatkiṃcidbālapralāpaṃ deśayati / etena mahāmate kāraṇena lokāyatiko vicitramantrapratibhāna ityucyate / akṣaravaicitryasauṣṭhavena bālānākarṣati, na tattvanayapraveśena praviśati / svayaṃ sarvadharmānavabodhādantadvayapatitayā dṛṣṭyā bālān vyāmohayati, svātmānaṃ ca kṣiṇoti / gatisaṃdhyapramuktatvātsvacittadṛśyamātrānavabodhādbāhyabhāvasvabhāvābhiniveśādvikalpasya vyāvṛttirna bhavati / ata etasmātkāraṇānmahāmate lokāyatiko
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s> again said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: This has been said by the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, perfectly awakened: 'At one time, at one moment, a <s>Lokāyatika</s> (materialist), with the eloquence of varied spells, should not be served, not honored, not attended upon. And for one who serves him, there is the accumulation of worldly gains, not the accumulation of <s>Dharma</s>.' For what reason, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, was this said — 'the <s>Lokāyatika</s> with the eloquence of varied spells, and for one who serves him there is the accumulation of worldly gains, not the accumulation of <s>Dharma</s>'? The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: The <s>Lokāyatika</s> with the eloquence of varied spells, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, deludes the childish with varied causal words and syllables — [his teachings are] not connected with reason, not related to the subject matter. Rather, he teaches whatever is mere prattle of the childish. For this reason, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the <s>Lokāyatika</s> is called 'one with the eloquence of varied spells.' By the beauty of varied syllables he attracts the childish, but does not enter through the entry into the true method. Because he himself does not awaken to all phenomena, with a view fallen into the duality, he deludes the childish and destroys himself. Because of not being liberated from the connection of existential courses, because of not awakening to [the truth of] the mere appearance of one's own mind, because of attachment to the inherent nature of external entities, the turning away from conceptual discrimination does not occur. For this very reason, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the <s>Lokāyatika</s>

body.text: vicitramantrapratibhāno 'parimukta eva jātijarāvyādhimaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsādibhyo vicitraiḥ padavyañjanairhetudṛṣṭāntopasaṃhārairbālān vyāmohayati //
body.translated_text: with the eloquence of varied spells is indeed not freed from birth, old age, sickness, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, dejection, and distress — and deludes the childish with varied words, syllables, causal arguments, and examples.

body.text: indro 'pi mahāmate anekaśāstravidagdhabuddhiḥ svaśabdaśāstrapraṇetā / tacchiṣyeṇa nāgaveśarūpadhāriṇā svarge indasabhāyāṃ pratijñāṃ kṛtvā tava vā sahasrāro ratho bhajyatāṃ mama vā ekaikanāgabhāvasya phaṇācchedo bhavatviti / sahadharmeṇa ca nāgaveśadhāriṇā lokāyatikaśiṣyeṇa devānāmindraṃ vijitya sahasrāraṃ rathaṃ bhaṅktvā punarapīmaṃ lokamāgataḥ / evamidaṃ mahāmate lokāyatikavicitrahetudṛṣṭāntopanibaddhaṃ yena tiryañco 'pyadhītya devāsuralokaṃ vicitrapadavyañjanairvyāmohayati / āyavyayadṛṣṭābhiniveśenābhiniveśayati kimaṅga punarmānuṣān / ata etasmātkāraṇānmahāmate lokāyatikaḥ parivarjitavyo duḥkhajanmahetuvāhakatvāt, na sevitavyo na bhajitavyo na paryupāsitavyaḥ / śarīrabuddhiviṣayopalabdhimātraṃ hi mahāmate lokāyatikairdeśyate vicitraiḥ padavyañjanaiḥ / śatasahasraṃ mahāmate lokāyatam / kiṃ tu paścime loke paścimāyāṃ pañcāśatyāṃ bhinnasaṃhitaṃ bhaviṣyati kutarkahetudṛṣṭipraṇītatvāt / bhinnasaṃhitaṃ bhaviṣyatyaśiṣyaparigrahāt / evadeva mahāmate lokāyataṃ bhinnasaṃhitaṃ vicitrahetūpanibaddhaṃ tīrthakarairdeśyate svakāraṇābhiniveśābhiniviṣṭaiḥ, na svanayaḥ / na ca mahāmate kasyacittīrthakarasya svaśāstranayaḥ / anyatra lokāyatameva anekairākāraiḥ kāraṇamukhaśatasahasrairdeśayanti / na svanayaṃ ca na prajānanti mohohāllokāyatamidamiti //
body.translated_text: Even <s>Indra</s>, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, an intellect accomplished in many sciences, was a propounder of his own science of grammar. A disciple of his, assuming the form of a <s>Nāga</s> (serpent-being), made a wager in <s>Indra's</s> assembly in heaven: 'Either your thousand-spoked chariot shall be broken, or my heads — one <s>Nāga</s> at a time — shall be severed.' And the disciple of the <s>Lokāyatika</s>, wearing the <s>Nāga</s> form, having defeated <s>Indra</s>, lord of the gods, through legitimate [debate], and having broken the thousand-spoked chariot, came back again to this world. Thus, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the <s>Lokāyata</s> [system], bound together with varied causal arguments and examples, [is such that] even animals, having studied [it], delude the world of gods and <s>asuras</s> with varied words and syllables. They cause attachment through attachment to views of income and expenditure — how much more so for humans! For this very reason, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the <s>Lokāyatika</s> should be avoided, because he carries the cause of the suffering of birth — he should not be served, not honored, not attended upon. For what is taught by the <s>Lokāyatikas</s>, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is merely the apprehension of the objects of the body and intellect, with varied words and syllables. There are a hundred thousand [forms of] <s>Lokāyata</s>, O <s>Mahāmati</s>. But in the final period of the world, in the last fifty [years], the compilation will become fragmented because of being led by wrong reasoning, views, and causes. The compilation will become fragmented because of the acceptance of unworthy disciples. Thus, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the <s>Lokāyata</s>, with its fragmented compilation bound to varied causes, is taught by the non-Buddhist teachers attached to their own causal theories — it is not their own doctrinal method. And no non-Buddhist teacher, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, has his own method of scripture. Rather, in numerous forms, through hundreds of thousands of gates of causation, they teach nothing but <s>Lokāyata</s>. And they do not understand, due to delusion, that this is <s>Lokāyata</s>.

body.text: mahāmatirāha - yadi bhagavan sarvatīrthakarā lokāyatameva vicitraiḥ padavyañjanairdṛṣṭāntopasaṃhārairdeśayanti, na svanayaṃ svakāraṇābhiniveśābhiniviṣṭāḥ, atha kiṃ bhagavānapi lokāyatameva deśayati āgatāgatānāṃ nānādeśasaṃnipatitānāṃ devāsuramanuṣyāṇāṃ vicitraiḥ padavyañjanaiḥ, na svamataṃ sarvatīrthyamatopadeśābhyantaratvāt? bhagavānāha - nāhaṃ mahāmate lokāyataṃ deśayāmi na cāyavyayam / kiṃ tu mahāmate anāyavyayaṃ deśayāmi / tatra āyo nāma mahāmate utpādarāśiḥ samūhāgamādutpadyate / tatra vyayo nāma mahāmate vināśaḥ / anāyavyaya ityanutpādasyaitadadhivacanam / nāhaṃ mahāmate sarvatīrthakaravikalpābhyantaraṃ deśayāmi / tatkasya hetoḥ? yaduta bāhyabhāvābhāvādanabhiniveśātsvacittadṛśyamātrāvasthānāddidhāvṛttino 'pravṛttervikalpasya / nimittagocarābhāvātsvacittadṛśyamātrāvabodhanātsvacittadṛśyavikalpo na pravartate / apravṛttivikalpasyānimittaśūnyatāpraṇihitavimokṣatrayāvatārānmukta ityucyate //
body.translated_text: <s>Mahāmati</s> asked: If, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, all non-Buddhist teachers teach nothing but <s>Lokāyata</s> with varied words, syllables, arguments, and examples, being attached to their own causal theories yet not [teaching] their own method — then does the <s>Bhagavān</s> too teach <s>Lokāyata</s> to the gods, <s>asuras</s>, and humans who have come together from various lands, with varied words and syllables, and not [teach] his own view, since [his teaching] would be included within the views of all non-Buddhist teachers? The <s>Bhagavān</s> replied: I do not, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, teach <s>Lokāyata</s>, nor [the doctrine of] income and expenditure. Rather, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, I teach that which is beyond income and expenditure. Therein, 'income' (<s>āya</s>), O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the heap of arising — arising from the coming together of a mass. Therein, 'expenditure' (<s>vyaya</s>), O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is destruction. 'Beyond income and expenditure' — this is a designation for non-arising (<s>anutpāda</s>). I do not, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, teach what is included within the conceptual discrimination of all non-Buddhist teachers. For what reason? Because, from the non-attachment to external existence and non-existence of entities, from the abiding in the mere appearance of one's own mind, the conceptual discrimination of a person running in two [directions] does not operate. Because of the absence of a domain of signs, from the awakening to [the truth of] the mere appearance of one's own mind, the conceptual discrimination of one's own mind as appearance does not operate. For one whose conceptual discrimination does not operate, from the entry into the three liberations — signless (<s>animitta</s>), emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>), and wishless (<s>apraṇihita</s>) — [such a one] is called liberated.

body.text: abhijānāmyahaṃ mahāmate anyatarasmin pṛthivīpradeśe viharāmi / atha yenāhaṃ tena lokāyatiko brāhmaṇa upasaṃkrāntaḥ / upasaṃkramya akṛtāvakāśa eva māmevamāha - sarvaṃ bho gautama kṛtakam / tasyāhaṃ mahāmate evamāha - sarvaṃ bho brāhmaṇa yadi kṛtakam, idaṃ prathamaṃ lokāyatam / sarvaṃ bho gautama akṛtakam / yadi brāhmaṇa sarvamakṛtakam , idaṃ dvitīyaṃ lokāyatam / evaṃ sarvamanityaṃ sarvaṃ nityaṃ sarvamutpādyaṃ sarvamanutpādyam / idaṃ brāhmaṇa ṣaṣṭhaṃ
body.translated_text: I recall, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, that I was dwelling in a certain region of the earth. Then a <s>Lokāyatika</s> brahmin approached me. Having approached, without being given an opportunity, he said to me thus: 'Everything, O <s>Gautama</s>, is created.' To him, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, I said thus: 'O brahmin, if everything is created, this is the first [proposition of] <s>Lokāyata</s>.' 'Everything, O <s>Gautama</s>, is uncreated.' 'If, O brahmin, everything is uncreated, this is the second <s>Lokāyata</s>.' Likewise: 'Everything is impermanent'; 'everything is permanent'; 'everything is produced'; 'everything is unproduced.' 'This, O brahmin, is the sixth

body.text: lokāyatam / punarapi mahāmate māmevamāha brāhmaṇo lokāyatikaḥ - sarvaṃ bho gautama ekatvaṃ sarvamanyatvaṃ sarvamubhayatvaṃ sarvamanubhayatvaṃ sarvaṃ kāraṇādhīnaṃ vicitrahetūipapattidarśanāt / idamapi brāhmaṇa ekādaśaṃ lokāyatam / punarapi bho gautama sarvamavyākṛtaṃ sarvaṃ vyākṛtam, astyātmā nāstyātmā, astyayaṃ loko nāstyayaṃ lokaḥ,asti paro loko nāsti paro lokaḥ, nāstyasti ca paro lokaḥ, asti mokṣo nāsti mokṣaḥ, sarvaṃ kṣaṇikaṃ sarvamakṣaṇikam, ākāśamapratisaṃkhyānirodho nirvāṇaṃ bho gautama kṛtakamakṛtakam, astyantarābhavo nāstyantarābhava iti / tasyaitaduktaṃ mahāmate mahā - yadi bho brāhmaṇa evam, idamapi brāhmaṇa lokāyatameva bhavatīti, na madīyam / tvadīyametadbrāhmaṇa lokāyatam / ahaṃ bho brāhmaṇa anādikālaprapañcavikalpavāsanādauṣṭhulyahetukaṃ tribhavaṃ varṇayāmi / svacittadṛśyamātrānavabodhādbrāhmaṇa vikalpaḥ pravartate na bāhyabhāvopalambhāt / yathā tīrthakarāṇāmātmendriyārthasaṃnikarṣātrayāṇāṃ na tathā mama / ahaṃ bhe brāhmaṇa na hetuvādī nāhetuvādī anyatra vikalpameva grāhyagrāhakabhāvena prajñāpya pratītyasamutpādaṃ deśayāmi / na ca tvādṛśā anye vā budhyante ātmagrāhapatitayā saṃtatyā / nirvāṇākāśanirodhānāṃ mahāmate tattvameva nopalabhyate saṃkhyāyām, kutaḥ punaḥ kṛtakatvam //
body.translated_text: <s>Lokāyata</s> (worldly philosophy). Again, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the <s>Lokāyatika</s> brahmin said to me thus: "Everything, O <s>Gautama</s>, is oneness; everything is otherness; everything is bothness; everything is non-bothness; everything depends on a cause, because of the perception of diverse causes and rebirths." "This too, O brahmin, is the eleventh [type of] <s>Lokāyata</s>." "Again, O <s>Gautama</s>: everything is undetermined; everything is determined; there is a self; there is no self; this world exists; this world does not exist; the other world exists; the other world does not exist; the other world both exists and does not exist; there is liberation; there is no liberation; everything is momentary; everything is non-momentary; space, the non-analytical cessation, and <s>nirvāṇa</s>, O <s>Gautama</s>, are created or uncreated; there is an intermediate existence; there is no intermediate existence." To that [brahmin] this was said by me, O <s>Mahāmati</s>: "If this is so, O brahmin, this too, O brahmin, is nothing but <s>Lokāyata</s>. It is not mine. This is your <s>Lokāyata</s>, O brahmin. I, O brahmin, describe the three realms of existence as caused by the impressions of the depravity of beginningless proliferative conceptual discrimination. O brahmin, conceptual discrimination proceeds from the non-awakening to [the truth that all is] mere appearance of one's own mind (<s>svacittadṛśyamātra</s>), not from the apprehension of external entities. [It is] not as the heretical teachers [teach] — from the conjunction of the triad of self, sense-faculty, and object. I, O brahmin, am neither a proponent of causation nor a proponent of non-causation; rather, having designated conceptual discrimination itself as the state of grasper and grasped, I teach dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>). But those like you and others do not understand, because [their] mental continuum has fallen into the grasping of self. Of <s>nirvāṇa</s>, space, and cessation, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the reality is indeed not apprehended in enumeration — how much less [their] being created!"

body.text: punarapi mahāmate lokāyatiko brāhmaṇa evamāha - ajñānatṛṣṇākarmahetukamidaṃ bho gautama tribhavam, athāhetukam? dvayamapyetadbrāhmaṇa lokāyatam / svasāmānyalakṣaṇapatitā bho gautama sarvabhāvāḥ / idamapi brāhmaṇa lokāyatameva bhavati / yāvadbrāhmaṇa manovispanditaṃ bāhyārthābhiniveśavikalpasya tāvallokāyatam //
body.translated_text: Again, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the <s>Lokāyatika</s> brahmin said thus: "Is this three-fold existence caused by ignorance, craving, and action, O <s>Gautama</s>, or is it causeless?" "Both of these, O brahmin, are <s>Lokāyata</s>." "O <s>Gautama</s>, all entities fall under specific and general characteristics." "This too, O brahmin, is nothing but <s>Lokāyata</s>. As long as, O brahmin, there is mental agitation — the conceptual discrimination of attachment to external objects — so long is there <s>Lokāyata</s>."

body.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate lokāyatiko brāhmaṇo māmetadavocat - asti bho gautama kiṃcidyanna lokāyatam? madīyameva bho gautama sarvatīrthakaraiḥ prasiddhaṃ vicitraiḥ padavyañjanairhetudṛṣṭāntopasaṃhārairdeśyate / asti bho brāhmaṇa yanna tvadīyaṃ na ca na prasiddhaṃ deśyate na ca na vicitraiḥ padavyañjanairna ca nārthopasaṃhitameva / kiṃ tadalokāyataṃ yanna prasiddhaṃ deśyate ca? asti ca bho brāhmaṇa alokāyataṃ yatra sarvatīrthakarāṇāṃ tava ca buddhirna gāhate bāhyabhāvādasadbhūtavikalpaprapañcābhiniviṣṭānām / yaduta vikalpasyāpravṛttiḥ sadasataḥ svacittadṛśyamātrāvabodhādvikalpo na pravartate / bāhyaviṣayagrahaṇābhāvādvikalpaḥ svasthāne 'vatiṣṭhate dṛśyate / tenedamalokāyataṃ madīyaṃ na ca tvadīyam / svasthāne 'vatiṣṭhata iti na pravartata ityarthaḥ / anutpattivikalpasyāpravṛttirityucyate / evamidaṃ bho brāhmaṇa yanna lokāyatam / saṃkṣepato brāhmaṇa yatra vijñānasyāgatirgatiścyutirupapattiḥ prārthanābhiniveśābhiṣvaṅgo darśanaṃ dṛṣṭiḥ sthānaṃ parāmṛṣṭirvicitralakṣaṇābhiniveśaḥ saṃgatiḥ sattvānāṃ tṛṣṇāyāḥ kāraṇābhiniveśaśca / etadbho brāhmaṇa tvadīyaṃ lokāyataṃ na madīyam / evamahaṃ mahāmate pṛṣṭo lokāyatikena brāhmaṇenāgatya / sa ca mayaivaṃ visarjitastūṣṇībhāvena prakrāntaḥ //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the <s>Lokāyatika</s> brahmin said this to me: "Is there anything, O <s>Gautama</s>, that is not <s>Lokāyata</s>? For what is mine is well-known to all heretical teachers and is taught with diverse words and syllables, reasoning and examples." "There is, O brahmin, that which is not yours and which is not well-known and is taught, and which is not [taught] without diverse words and syllables, and which is not unconnected with meaning." "What is that non-<s>Lokāyata</s> which is not well-known and yet is taught?" "There is, O brahmin, a non-<s>Lokāyata</s> in which the intellect of all heretical teachers, including yours, does not penetrate — [you who are] attached to the proliferation of discriminations of unreal external entities. Namely, the non-operation of conceptual discrimination: from the awakening to [the truth that all is] mere appearance of one's own mind (<s>svacittadṛśyamātra</s>) regarding the existent and non-existent, conceptual discrimination does not operate. From the absence of grasping external objects, conceptual discrimination abides in its own place and is seen [as such]. This is the non-<s>Lokāyata</s> that is mine, not yours. 'Abides in its own place' means 'does not operate.' The non-operation of conceptual discrimination that is non-arising is called [the non-operation]. Thus, O brahmin, this is what is not <s>Lokāyata</s>. In brief, O brahmin, wherever there is the going and coming, falling-away and rebirth, seeking, attachment, clinging, perception, view, establishment, handling, and attachment to diverse characteristics, and the encounter of beings with the attachment to the causation of craving — this, O brahmin, is your <s>Lokāyata</s>, not mine. Thus was I questioned, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, by the <s>Lokāyatika</s> brahmin who came [to me]. And he, dismissed by me thus, departed in silence."

body.text: atha khalu kṛṣṇapakṣiko nāgarājo brāhmaṇarūpeṇāgatya bhagavantametadavocat - tena hi gautama paraloka eva na saṃvidyate / tena hi māṇava kutastvamāgataḥ? ihāhaṃ gautama śvetadvīpādāgataḥ / sa eva brāhmaṇa paro lokaḥ / atha māṇavo niṣpratibhāno nigṛhīto 'ntarhito 'pṛṣṭvaiva māṃ svanayapratyavasthānakathāṃ cintayan śākyaputro mannayabahirdhā varāko 'pravṛttilakṣaṇahetuvādī svavikalpadṛśyalakṣaṇāvabodhādvikalpasyāpravṛttiṃ varṇayati / tvaṃ caitarhi mahāmate māṃ pṛcchasi - kiṃ kāraṇaṃ lokāyatikavicitramantrapratibhānaṃ sevyamānasyāmiṣasaṃgraho bhavati na dharmasaṃgraha iti / mahāmatirāha - atha dharmāmiṣamiti bhagavan kaḥ padārthaḥ? bhagavānāha - sādhu sādhu mahāmate / padārthadvayaṃ prati mīmāṃsā pravṛttā anāgatāṃ janatāṃ samālokya / tena hi mahāmate śṛṇu, sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuru / bhāṣiṣye 'haṃ te / sādhu bhagavanniti mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavataḥ pratyaśrauṣīt //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Nāgarāja</s> (serpent-king) <s>Kṛṣṇapakṣika</s>, having come in the form of a brahmin, said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "Then, <s>Gautama</s>, the other world simply does not exist!" "Then, young man, from where have you come?" "I, O <s>Gautama</s>, have come here from <s>Śvetadvīpa</s> (the White Island)." "That very [place], O brahmin, is the other world." Then the young man, speechless, refuted, [and] having vanished without even asking me, thinking over a response to defend his own doctrine [thought]: "This son of the <s>Śākyas</s>, the wretch, outside of my doctrine, is a proponent of causation through the non-operation-characteristic! From the awakening to the appearance-characteristic of his own conceptual discriminations, he describes the non-operation of conceptual discrimination!" And now, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, you ask me: "For what reason does one who cultivates the varied mantra-eloquence of the <s>Lokāyatikas</s> obtain a gathering of material gain, not a gathering of <s>Dharma</s>?" <s>Mahāmati</s> asked: "Then, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, what is the meaning of ' <s>Dharma</s>' and 'material gain'?"
