The <s>Bhagavān</s> replied: "Excellent, excellent, O <s>Mahāmati</s>! Your inquiry has proceeded regarding these two meanings, looking toward the future generations. Then, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, listen, and attend well and thoroughly. I shall teach you." "Very well, <s>Bhagavān</s>," the <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s> assented to the <s>Bhagavān</s>.

body.text: bhagavāṃstasyaitadavocat - tatra āmiṣaṃ mahāmate katamat? yaduta āmiṣamāmṛśamākarṣaṇaṃ nirmṛṣaṃ parāmṛṣṭiḥ svādo bāhyaviṣayābhiniveśo 'ntadvayapraveśaḥ / kudṛṣṭyā punaḥ skandhaprādurbhāvo jātijarāvyādhimaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsapravṛttistṛṣṇāyāḥ paunarbhavikyā ādiṃ kṛtvā / āmiṣamidamityucyate mayā ca anyaiśca buddhairbhagavadbhiḥ / eṣa mahāmate āmiṣasaṃgraho na dharmasaṃgraho yaṃ lokāyatikaṃ sevamāno labhate lokāyatam //
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said this to him: "Therein, what is material gain (<s>āmiṣa</s>), O <s>Mahāmati</s>? Namely, material gain is touching, seizing, grasping, handling, savoring — the attachment to external objects, the entering into the two extremes. Furthermore, from wrong views, the manifestation of the aggregates (<s>skandha</s>), beginning with craving that leads to renewed existence, the activity of birth, old age, sickness, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, dejection, and disturbance. This is called 'material gain' by me and by other <s>Buddhas</s> <s>Bhagavāns</s>. This, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the gathering of material gain, not the gathering of <s>Dharma</s>, which one obtains by cultivating <s>Lokāyata</s>."

body.text: tatra mahāmate dharmasaṃgrahaḥ katamaḥ? yaduta svacittadharmanairātmyadvayāva - bodhāddharmapudgalanairātmyalakṣaṇadarśanādvikalpasyāpravṛttiḥ, bhūmyuttaroparijñānāccittamanomanovijñānavyāvṛttiḥ, sarvabuddhajñānābhiṣekagatiḥ anadhiṣṭhāpadaparigrahaḥ sarvadharmānābhogavaśavartitā dharma ityucyate, sarvadṛṣṭiprapañcavikalpabhāvāntadvayāpatanatayā / prāyeṇa hi mahāmate tīrthakaravādo bālānantadvaye pātayati na tu viduṣām, yaduta ucchede ca śāśvate ca / ahetuvādaparigrahācchāśvatadṛṣṭirbhavati, kāraṇavināśahetvabhāvāducchedadṛṣṭirbhavati / kiṃ tu utpādasthitibhaṅgadarśanāddharma ityevaṃ vadāmi / eṣa mahāmate dharmāmiṣanirṇayaḥ, yatra tvayā anyaiśca bodhisattvairmahāsattvaiḥ śikṣitavyam //
body.translated_text: "Therein, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, what is the gathering of <s>Dharma</s>? Namely, from the awakening to the twofold [selflessness of] the <s>dharma</s>-nature of one's own mind, from the vision of the characteristics of the selflessness of <s>dharmas</s> and persons, the non-operation of conceptual discrimination; from the knowledge of the progressively higher stages, the turning-away of mind, <s>manas</s>, and <s>manovijñāna</s>; the course of the consecration-knowledge of all <s>Buddhas</s>, the embracing of the stage of non-empowerment, the mastery over all <s>dharmas</s> without effort — [this] is called <s>Dharma</s>, because of the non-falling into the two extremes of the existence of conceptual discrimination, proliferative views, and all views. For, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the doctrine of the heretical teachers mostly causes the foolish to fall into the two extremes — namely, annihilation and eternalism. From the embrace of the doctrine of non-causation, the eternalist view arises; from the absence of a cause for the destruction of the cause, the annihilationist view arises. But [I say] from the vision of arising, abiding, and destruction — [this] I call <s>Dharma</s>. This, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the determination of <s>Dharma</s> and material gain, in which you and other <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas</s> should train."

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Therein this is said:

children.translated_text: By the [four] means of gathering, one should tame beings; by morality (<s>śīla</s>), one should subdue them;
by wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), one should destroy views; by the liberations, one should cause growth. [Laṅk 3.62]
All this is <s>Lokāyata</s>, what is taught falsely by the heretics;
through the view of cause and effect, their own established doctrine is not found. [Laṅk 3.63]
I alone [teach] my own established doctrine, free from cause and effect,
I teach it to the assembly of disciples, free from <s>Lokāyata</s>. [Laṅk 3.64]

children.text: cittamātraṃ na dṛśyo 'sti dvidhā cittaṃ hi dṛśyate /
children.translated_text: Mind-only exists; the visible does not exist. The mind is seen in two ways,
in the form of grasper and grasped — free from eternalism and annihilation. [Laṅk 3.65]
As long as the mind operates, so long does <s>Lokāyata</s> exist;
when conceptual discrimination ceases to operate, one sees one's own mind [as] the world. [Laṅk 3.66]
Income is the accomplishment of the purpose of action; expenditure is the perception of [the results of] action;
from the full comprehension of income and expenditure, conceptual discrimination does not operate. [Laṅk 3.67]
Permanent and impermanent, created and uncreated, higher and lower —
all such [pairs as] these become the doctrine of <s>Lokāyata</s>. [Laṅk 3.68]

body.text: atha khalu mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ punarapi bhagavantametadavocat - nirvāṇaṃ nirvāṇamiti bhagavannucyate / kasyaitadadhivacanaṃ yaduta nirvāṇamiti yatsarvatīrthakarairvikalpyate? bhagavānāha - tena hi mahāmate śṛṇu, sādhu va suṣṭhu ca manasikuru / bhāṣiṣye 'haṃ te / yathā tīrthakarā nirvāṇaṃ vikalpayanti, na ca bhavati teṣāṃ vikalpānurupaṃ nirvāṇam / sādhu bhagavanniti mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavataḥ pratyaśrauṣīt / bhagavāṃstasyaitadavocat - tatra kecittāvanmahāmate tīrthakarāḥ skandhadhātvāyatananirodhādviṣayavairāgyānnivaidharmyādarśanāccittacaittakalāpo na pravartate / atītānāgatapratyutpannaviṣayānanusmaraṇāddīpabījānalavadupādānoparamādapravṛttirvikalpasyeti varṇayanti / atasteṣāṃ tatra nirvāṇabuddhirbhavati / na ca mahāmate vināśadṛṣṭyā nirvāyate //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s> again addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s> thus: "<s>Nirvāṇa</s>, <s>nirvāṇa</s>," it is said, O <s>Bhagavān</s>. Of what is this a designation — namely, "<s>nirvāṇa</s>" — which is conceptually discriminated by all the heretical teachers? The <s>Bhagavān</s> replied: Then, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, listen, and attend well and thoroughly. I shall teach you how the heretical teachers conceive of <s>nirvāṇa</s>, and [why] there is no <s>nirvāṇa</s> corresponding to their conceptions. "Very well, <s>Bhagavān</s>," the <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s> assented to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said this to him: "Therein, certain heretical teachers, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, from the cessation of the aggregates, elements, and sense-bases, from dispassion toward objects, from the vision of the absence of diversity, [maintain that] the aggregate of mind and mental factors does not operate; from the non-recollection of objects past, future, and present — like a lamp, a seed, or a fire, from the cessation of the fuel — [they] describe [this as] the non-operation of conceptual discrimination." Therefore they have the understanding of <s>nirvāṇa</s> therein. But, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, one does not attain <s>nirvāṇa</s> through the view of destruction.

body.text: anye punardeśāntarasthānagamanaṃ mokṣa iti varṇayanti viṣayavikalpoparamādiṣu pavanavat / anye punarvarṇayanti tīrthakarāḥ buddhiboddhavyadarśanavināśānmokṣa iti / anye vikalpasyāpravṛtternityānityadarśanānmokṣaṃ kalpayanti / anye punarvarṇayanti vividhanimittavikalpo duḥkhajanmavāhaka iti svacittadṛśyamātrākuśalāḥ / nimittabhayabhītā nimittadarśanātsukhābhilāṣanimitte nirvāṇabuddhayo bhavanti / anye punaradhyātmabāhyānāṃ sarvadharmāṇāṃ svasāmānyalakṣaṇāvabodhādavināśato 'tītānāgatapratyutpannabhāvāstitayā
body.translated_text: Others describe liberation as the going to another place or state, from the cessation of object-discrimination etc., like wind. Others, the heretical teachers, describe liberation from the destruction of the perception of intellect, the knowable, and the known. Others conceive of liberation from the non-operation of conceptual discrimination, from the vision of the permanent and impermanent. Others describe [it saying that] varied sign-discrimination is the carrier of the birth of suffering — [and those who are] unskilled in [the truth that all is] mere appearance of one's own mind (<s>svacittadṛśyamātra</s>), frightened by fear of signs, from the perception of signs, have the understanding of <s>nirvāṇa</s> through the desire for happiness in [the absence of] signs. Others, from the awakening to the specific and general characteristics of all internal and external <s>dharmas</s>, from indestructibility, from the existence of past, future, and present entities,

body.text: nirvāṇaṃ kalpayanti / anye punarātmasattvajīvapoṣapuruṣapudgalasarvadharmāvināśataśca nirvāṇaṃ kalpayati / anye punarmahāmate tīrthakarā durvidagdhabuddhayaḥ prakṛtipuruṣāntaradarśanādguṇapariṇāmakartṛtvācca nirvāṇaṃ kalpayanti / anye puṇyāpuṇyaparikṣayāt / anye kleśakṣayājjñānena ca / anye īśvarasvatantrakartṛtvadarśanājjagato nirvāṇaṃ kalpayanti / anye anyonyapravṛtto 'yaṃ saṃbhavo jagata iti na kāraṇataḥ / sa ca kāraṇābhiniveśa eva, na cāvabudhyante mohāt, tadanavabodhānnirvāṇaṃ kalpayanti / anye punarmahāmate tīrthakarāḥ satyamārgādhigamānnirvāṇaṃ kalpayanti / anye guṇaguṇinorabhisaṃbaddhādekatvānyatvobhayatvānubhayatvadarśanānnirvāṇabuddhayo bhavanti / anye svabhāvataḥ pravṛttito mayūravaicitryavividharatnākarakaṇṭakataikṣṇyavadbhāvānāṃ svabhāvaṃ dṛṣṭvā nirvāṇaṃ vikalpayanti / anye punarmahāmate pañcaviṃśatitattvāvabodhāt, anye prajāpālena ṣāḍguṇyopadeśagrahaṇānnirvāṇaṃ
body.translated_text: conceive of <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Others conceive of <s>nirvāṇa</s> from the indestructibility of self, being, life, nourisher, person, <s>pudgala</s>, and all <s>dharmas</s>. Others, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, heretical teachers of depraved intellect, from the perception of the difference between <s>Prakṛti</s> (primal nature) and <s>Puruṣa</s> (spirit), and from the agency of the transformation of the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities), conceive of <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Others [conceive it] from the exhaustion of merit and demerit. Others from the destruction of afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>) and through knowledge. Others, from the perception of the agency and independence of <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord), conceive of <s>nirvāṇa</s> for the world. Others [say]: "This arising of the world proceeds from mutual [interaction], not from causation." And that very attachment to causation — they do not understand [it] because of delusion; from that non-understanding, they conceive of <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Others, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, heretical teachers, from the attainment of the path of truth, conceive of <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Others, from the perception of oneness, otherness, bothness, and non-bothness of the connected quality and quality-bearer, have the understanding of <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Others, seeing the inherent nature of entities as proceeding from [their own] inherent nature — like the diversity of a peacock, the sharpness of diverse jewel-mines and thorns — conceive of <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Others, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, from the awakening to the twenty-five principles (<s>tattva</s>); others, from the acceptance of the teaching of the sixfold [quality] by <s>Prajāpāla</s>, [conceive of] <s>nirvāṇa</s>

body.text:
kalpayanti / anye kālakartṛdarśanātkālāyattā lokapravṛttiriti tadavabodhānnirvāṇaṃ kalpayanti / anye punarmahāmate bhavena, anye 'bhavena, anye bhavābhavaparijñayā, anye bhavanirvāṇāviśeṣadarśanena nirvāṇaṃ kalpayanti / anye punarmahāmate varṇayanti sarvajñasiṃhanādanādino yathā svacittadṛśyamātrāvabodhādbāhyabhāvābhāvānabhiniveśāccātuṣkoṭikarahitād yathābhūtāvasthānadarśanātsvacittadṛśyavikalpasyāntadvayāpatanatayā grāhyagrāhakānupalabdheḥ sarvapramāṇāgrahaṇāpravṛttidarśanāttattvasya vyāmohakatvādagrahaṇaṃ tattvasya, tadvyudāsātsvapratyātmāryadharmādhigamānnairātmyadvayāvabodhātkleśadvayavinivṛtterāvaraṇadvayaviśuddhatvādbhūmyuttarottaratathāgatabhūmimāyādiviśvasamādhicittamanomanovijñānavyāvṛtternirvāṇaṃ kalpayanti / evamanyānyapi yāni tārkikaiḥ kutīrthyapraṇītāni tānyayuktiyuktāni vidvadbhiḥ parivarjitāni / sarve 'pyete mahāmate antadvayapatitayā saṃtatyā nirvāṇaṃ kalpayanti / evamādibhirvikalpairmahāmate sarvatīrthakarairnirvāṇaṃ parikalpyate / na cātra kaścitpravartate vā nivartate vā / ekaikasya mahāmate tīrthakarasya
nirvāṇaṃ tatsvaśāstramatibuddhyā parīkṣyamāṇaṃ vyabhicarati / tathā na tiṣṭhate yathā tairvikalpyate / manasa āgatigativispandanānnāsti kasyacinnirvāṇam / atra tvayā mahāmate śikṣitvā anyaiśca bodhisattvairmahāsattvaiḥ sarvatīrthakaranirvāṇadṛṣṭirvyāvartanīyā //
body.translated_text: conceptualize [nirvāṇa]. Others, from seeing time as the agent, conceptualize <s>nirvāṇa</s> [thinking] that worldly activity depends on time, and that liberation comes from understanding that. Others again, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, conceptualize <s>nirvāṇa</s> through becoming, others through non-becoming, others through the full understanding of becoming and non-becoming, others through seeing no difference between becoming and <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Others again, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, declare — those who roar the lion's roar of omniscience — that <s>nirvāṇa</s> is conceptualized thus: through understanding [that all is] merely the appearance of one's own mind, through non-attachment to the existence or non-existence of external entities, free from the fourfold alternative (<s>catuṣkoṭi</s>), through seeing things as they truly are, through the non-falling of the conceptualization of what is seen by one's own mind into either extreme, through the non-apprehension of the grasped and the grasper, through seeing the non-operation of all means of valid knowledge — because truth is bewildering, truth is not grasped — through the removal of that [bewilderment], through the attainment of one's own inner noble <s>dharma</s>, through the understanding of the twofold selflessness (<s>nairātmya</s>), through the cessation of the twofold afflictions, through the purification of the twofold obscurations, through the progressive ascent to the <s>Tathāgata</s>-stages through the stages, [and] through the turning away from the illusion-like universal <s>samādhis</s> of mind, mentation, and consciousness. And whatever other [views] propounded by heretical logicians — those are unjustified and rejected by the wise. All these, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, conceptualize <s>nirvāṇa</s> through a continuity fallen into the two extremes. By such and other conceptualizations, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, <s>nirvāṇa</s> is imagined by all heretical teachers. But nothing here either operates or ceases. For each individual heretic's <s>nirvāṇa</s>, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, when examined by the intellect of his own teacher's doctrine, becomes inconsistent. It does not stand as conceptualized by them. Because of the coming, going, and vibration of the mind, there is no <s>nirvāṇa</s> for anyone. Herein, having trained, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, you and other <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> should turn away from the views of <s>nirvāṇa</s> of all heretical teachers.

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: On this, it is said:

children.translated_text: The heretics conceptualize their views of <s>nirvāṇa</s> variously, each differently;
theirs is mere conceptualization — no means of liberation exists [for them]. || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.69 ||
Freed from barren bondage, and devoid of means —

children.text: tīrthyā mokṣaṃ vikalpenti na ca mokṣo hi vidyate // Lank_3.70 //
children.translated_text: the heretics conceptualize liberation, but no liberation exists [for them]. || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.70 ||
The method of the heretics is seen as divided into many varieties;
therefore there is no liberation for them — why is it conceptualized by the deluded? || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.71 ||
All the heretics are deluded by the wrong view of cause and effect;
therefore there is no liberation for them, the proponents of the positions of existent and non-existent. || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.72 ||

children.text: jalpaprapañcābhiratā hi bālāstattve na kurvanti matiṃ viśālām /
children.translated_text: The childish delight in idle talk and proliferation and do not turn their vast intellect to the truth;

children.text: jalpo hi traidhātukaduḥkhayonistattvaṃ hi duḥkhasya vināśahetuḥ // Lank_3.73 //
children.translated_text: for idle talk is the source of suffering in the three realms, while truth is the cause of the destruction of suffering. || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.73 ||

children.text: yathā hi darpaṇe rūpaṃ dṛśyate na ca vidyate /
children.translated_text: Just as a form is seen in a mirror but does not [truly] exist,

children.text: vāsanādarpaṇe cittaṃ dvidhā dṛśyati bāliśaiḥ // Lank_3.74 //
children.translated_text: so in the mirror of impressions, mind is seen twofold by the childish. || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.74 ||
From not fully understanding what is seen by mind, conceptualization arises twofold;
from fully understanding what is seen by mind, conceptualization does not operate. || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.75 ||
Mind alone is the manifold, free from the characterized and the characteristic;

children.text: dṛśyākāraṃ na dṛśyo 'sti yathā bālairvikalpyate // Lank_3.76 //
children.translated_text: the visible form does not [truly] exist as visible — as conceptualized by the childish. || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.76 ||
The three realms of existence are mere conceptualization; external objects do not exist;

children.text: vikalpaṃ dṛśyate citraṃ na ca bālairvibhāvyate // Lank_3.77 //
children.translated_text: the manifold conceptualization is seen, but this is not understood by the childish. || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.77 ||
In each and every <s>sūtra</s>, conceptualization is spoken of, along with designations and names;
freed from designation, the designated is not perceived. || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.78 ||

body.text: atha khalu mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantametadavocat - deśayatu me bhagavāṃstathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ svabuddhabuddhatām, yena ahaṃ ca anye ca bodhisattvā mahāsattvāstathāgatasvakuśalāḥ svamātmānaṃ parāṃścāvabodhayeyuḥ / bhagavānāha - tena hi mahāmate tvameva paripṛccha / yathā te kṣamate, tathā visarjayiṣyāmi / mahāmatirāha - kiṃ punarbhagavan tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho 'kṛtakaḥ kṛtakaḥ kāryaṃ kāraṇaṃ lakṣyaṃ lakṣaṇamabhidhānamabhidheyaṃ buddhirboddhavyaḥ, evamādyaiḥ padaniruktaiḥ kiṃ bhagavānanyo 'nanyaḥ?
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'May the Blessed One, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, teach me the Buddhahood of the Buddha, so that I and other <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s>, skilled in the <s>Tathāgata's</s> own [nature], may awaken ourselves and others.' The Blessed One said: 'Then, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, you yourself ask. As you see fit, I shall answer.' <s>Mahāmati</s> said: 'Is the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, O Blessed One, uncreated or created? An effect or a cause? The characterized or the characteristic? Designation or designated? Intellect or what is to be known? By such terms and analyses, O Blessed One, is he other or not other?'

body.text: bhagavānāha - na mahāmate tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddha evamādyaiḥ padaniruktairakṛtako na kṛtakaṃ na kāryaṃ na kāraṇam / tatkasya hetoḥ? yaduta ubhayadoṣaprasaṅgāt / yadi hi mahāmate tathāgataḥ kṛtakaḥ syāt, anityatvaṃ syāt / anityatvātsarvaṃ hi kāryaṃ tathāgataḥ syāt / aniṣṭaṃ caitanmama ca anyeṣāṃ ca tathāgatānām / athākṛtakaḥ syāt, alabdhātmakatvātsamudāgatasaṃbhāravaiyarthyaṃ syāt, śaśaviṣāṇavadvandhyāputratulyaśca syādakṛtakatvāt / yacca mahāmate na kāryaṃ na kāraṇaṃ tanna sannāsat / yacca na sannāsat, taccātuṣkoṭikabāhyam / cātuṣkoṭikaṃ ca mahāmate lokavyavahāraḥ / yacca cātuṣkoṭikabāhyaṃ tadvāgmātraṃ prasajyate vandhyāputravat / vandhyāputro hi mahāmate vāgmātraṃ na cātuṣkoṭikapatitaḥ / apatitatvādapramāṇaṃ viduṣām / evaṃ sarvatathāgatapadārthā vidvadbhiḥ pratyavagantavyāḥ / yadapyuktaṃ mayā nirātmānaḥ sarvadharmā iti, tasyāpyarthaṃ niboddhavyaṃ mahāmate / nirātmabhāvo mahāmate nairātmyam / svātmanā sarvadharmā vidyante na parātmanā gośvavat / tadyathā mahāmate na gobhāvo 'śvātmako na cāśvabhāvo gavātmakaḥ, na sannāsat, na ca tau svalakṣaṇato na, vidyete eva tau svalakṣaṇataḥ, evameva mahāmate sarvadharmā na ca svalakṣaṇena na saṃvidyante / vidyanta eva / tena ca bālapṛthagjanairnirātmārthatā avabudhyate vikalpamupādāya, na tvavikalpam / evaṃ śūnyānutpādāsvābhāvyaṃ sarvadharmaṇāṃ pratyavagantavyam / evaṃ skandhebhyo nānyo nānanyastathāgataḥ / yadyananyaḥ skandhebhyaḥ syāt, anityaḥ syāt kṛtatvātskandhānām / athānyaḥ syāt, dvaye satyanyathā bhavati goviṣāṇavat //
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'The <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is not to be [defined] by such terms and analyses as uncreated, nor created, nor effect, nor cause. For what reason? Because of the fault entailed in both [alternatives]. If, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> were created, he would be impermanent. Through impermanence, all effects would be <s>Tathāgatas</s>. And this is undesirable for me and for other <s>Tathāgatas</s>. But if he were uncreated, since he would have no attained selfhood, the accumulation of provisions would be purposeless, and he would be like a hare's horn or a barren woman's son — because of being uncreated. And that which, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is neither effect nor cause, is neither existent nor non-existent. And that which is neither existent nor non-existent is beyond the fourfold alternative. And the fourfold alternative, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is worldly convention. And that which is beyond the fourfold alternative amounts to mere words, like a barren woman's son. For a barren woman's son, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is mere words — not fallen into the fourfold alternative. Being unfallen, it is beyond the means of valid knowledge for the wise. Thus should all the meanings of <s>Tathāgata</s>-terms be understood by the wise. As for what I have also said — "all <s>dharmas</s> are without self" — the meaning of that too should be understood, O <s>Mahāmati</s>. The nature of being without self, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is selflessness. All <s>dharmas</s> exist by their own self, not by another's self — like cows and horses. Just as, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, cow-nature is not horse-self, nor horse-nature cow-self — [each] is neither existent nor non-existent, yet those two are not non-existent by their own characteristic — they do indeed exist by their own characteristic — even so, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, all <s>dharmas</s> are not non-existent by their own characteristic. They do indeed exist. But the meaning of selflessness is understood by childish ordinary persons through grasping at conceptualization, not through non-conceptualization. Thus should the emptiness, non-arising, and essencelessness of all <s>dharmas</s> be understood. Thus the <s>Tathāgata</s> is neither other than nor not other than the aggregates. If he were not other than the aggregates, he would be impermanent, because the aggregates are created. But if he were other, then — both being [separately] real — it would be otherwise, like a cow's horn.'

body.text: tatra sādṛśyadarśanādananyatvaṃ hrasvadīrghadarśanādanyatvaṃ sarvabhāvānām / dakṣiṇaṃ hi mahāmate goviṣāṇaṃ vāmasyānyadbhavati, vāmamapi dakṣiṇasya / evaṃ hrasvadīrghatvayoḥ parasparataḥ /
body.translated_text: Therein, from seeing similarity, the non-otherness [is inferred]; from seeing shortness and length, the otherness of all entities. For the right horn of a cow, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is other than the left, and the left is [other] than the right. Thus with shortness and length — each from the other.

body.text: evaṃ varṇavaicitryataśca / ataścāparasparato 'nyaḥ / na cānyastathāgataḥ skandhadhātvāyanebhyaḥ / evaṃ vimokṣāttathāgato nānyo nānanyaḥ / tathāgata eva mokṣaśabdena deśyate / yadi anyaḥ syānmokṣāttathāgataḥ, rūpalakṣaṇayuktaḥ syāt / rūpalakṣaṇayuktatvādanityaḥ syāt / athānanyaḥ syāt, prāptilakṣaṇavibhāgo na syādyoginām / dṛṣṭaśca mahāmate vibhāgo yogibhiḥ / ato nānyo nānanyaḥ / evaṃ jñānaṃ jñeyānnānyannānanyat / yaddhi mahāmate na nityaṃ nānityaṃ na kāryaṃ na kāraṇaṃ na saṃskṛtaṃ nāsaṃskṛtaṃ na buddhirna boddhavyaṃ na lakṣyaṃ na lakṣaṇaṃ na skandhā na skandhebhyo 'nyat nābhidheyaṃ nābhidhānaṃ naikatvānyatvobhayatvānubhayatvasaṃbaddham, tatsarvapramāṇavinivṛttam / yatsarvapramāṇavinivṛttaṃ tadvāṅbhātraṃ saṃpadyate / yadvāṅbhātraṃ tadanutpannam / yadanutpannaṃ tadaniruddham / yadaniruddhaṃ tadākāśasamam / ākāśaṃ ca mahāmate na kāryaṃ na kāraṇam / yacca na kāryaṃ na kāraṇaṃ tannirālambyam / yannirālambyaṃ tatsarvaprapañcātītam / yatsarvaprapañcātītaṃ sa tathāgataḥ / etaddhi mahāmate samyaksaṃbuddhatvam / eṣā sā buddhabuddhatā sarvapramāṇendriyavinivṛttā //
body.translated_text: Thus also from the variety of color. Therefore, [each] is other from the other's [standpoint]. But the <s>Tathāgata</s> is not other than the aggregates, elements, and sense-bases. Thus the <s>Tathāgata</s> is neither other nor not other than liberation. The <s>Tathāgata</s> himself is taught by the word 'liberation.' If the <s>Tathāgata</s> were other than liberation, he would be endowed with the characteristic of form. Being endowed with the characteristic of form, he would be impermanent. But if he were not other, there would be no distinction of the characteristic of attainment for <s>yogins</s>. Yet the distinction is seen by <s>yogins</s>, O <s>Mahāmati</s>. Therefore he is neither other nor not other. Likewise, knowledge is neither other than nor not other than the knowable. For that which, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is neither permanent nor impermanent, neither effect nor cause, neither conditioned nor unconditioned, neither intellect nor what is to be known, neither characterized nor characteristic, neither aggregates nor other than the aggregates, neither designated nor designation, not connected with oneness, otherness, bothness, or neitherism — that is freed from all means of valid knowledge. That which is freed from all means of valid knowledge amounts to mere words. That which is mere words is unborn. That which is unborn is unceased. That which is unceased is equal to space. And space, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is neither effect nor cause. That which is neither effect nor cause is without support. That which is without support is beyond all proliferation. That which is beyond all proliferation — that is the <s>Tathāgata</s>. This indeed, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is perfect Buddhahood. This is that Buddhahood of the Buddha — freed from all means of valid knowledge and sense-faculties.

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: On this, it is said:

children.translated_text: Freed from means of valid knowledge and sense-faculties, neither effect nor cause,
free from intellect and what is to be known, devoid of the characterized and the characteristic, || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.79 ||

children.text: skandhān pratītya saṃbuddho na dṛṣṭaḥ kenacitkvacit /
children.translated_text: the Awakened One has not been seen anywhere by anyone in dependence on the aggregates;

children.text: yo na dṛṣṭaḥ kvacitkenacitkathaṃ tasya vibhāvanā // Lank_3.80 //
children.translated_text: he who has not been seen anywhere by anyone — how can he be conceived? || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.80 ||

children.text: na kṛtako nākṛtako na kāryaṃ nāpi kāraṇam /
children.translated_text: Neither created nor uncreated, neither effect nor cause,

children.text: na ca skandhā na cāskandhā na cāpyanyatra saṃkarāt // Lank_3.81 //
children.translated_text: neither aggregates nor non-aggregates, nor anything else mixed together, || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.81 ||

children.text: na hi yo yena bhāvena kalpyamāno na dṛśyate /
children.translated_text: for whatever entity, when imagined in whatever way, is not seen —

children.text: na taṃ nāstyeva gantavyaṃ dharmāṇāmeva dharmatā // Lank_3.82 //
children.translated_text: one should not conclude 'it does not exist'; [this is] just the true nature (<s>dharmatā</s>) of <s>dharmas</s>. || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.82 ||
'Does not exist' presupposes existence; 'exists' presupposes non-existence;

children.text: ato nāsti na gantavyamastitvaṃ na ca kalpayet // Lank_3.83 //
children.translated_text: therefore one should not conclude 'does not exist,' nor should one conceptualize 'exists.' || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.83 ||
Confused about self and selflessness, clinging to faults alone,
sunk in both extremes, those ruined ones destroy the childish. || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.84 ||
When they see my doctrine as freed from all faults,

children.text: tadā samyakprapaśyanti na te dūṣenti nāyakān // Lank_3.85 //
children.translated_text: then they see rightly — they do not defame the guides. || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.85 ||

body.text: atha khalu mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ punarapi bhagavantametadavocat - deśayatu me bhagavān, deśayatu sugataḥ, yaddeśanāpāṭhe bhagavatā anirodhānutpādagrahaṇaṃ kṛtam / uktaṃ ca tvayā yathā tathāgatasyaitadadhivacanamanirodhānutpāda iti / tatkimayaṃ bhagavan abhāvo 'nirodhānutpādaḥ, uta tathāgatasyaitatparyāyāntaram? yadbhagavānevamāha - aniruddhā anutpannāśca bhagavatā
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s> again said this to the Blessed One: 'May the Blessed One teach me, may the <s>Sugata</s> teach me — for in the teaching-recitation, the Blessed One has employed the expression 'unceased and unborn.' And you have said that this is a designation of the <s>Tathāgata</s> — namely, 'unceased and unborn.' Is this 'unceased and unborn,' O Blessed One, [the same as] non-existence? Or is it an alternative expression for the <s>Tathāgata</s>? For the Blessed One has said thus: 'Unceased and unborn, the Blessed One

body.text:
sarvadharmā deśyante sadasatpakṣādarśanāt / yadyanutpannāḥ sarvadharmā iti bhagavan dharmagrahaṇaṃ na prāpnoti, ajātatvātsarvadharmāṇām / atha paryāyāntarametatkasyaciddharmasya, taducyatāṃ bhagavan / bhagavānāha - tena hi mahāmate śṛṇu, sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasikuru / bhāṣiṣye 'haṃ te / sādhu bhagavanniti mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavataḥ pratyaśrauṣīt / bhagavāṃstasyaitadavocat - na hi mahāmate abhāvastathāgato na ca sarvadharmāṇāmanirodhānutpādagrahaṇam / na pratyayo 'pekṣitavyo na ca nirarthakamanutpādagrahaṇaṃ kriyate mayā / kiṃ tu mahāmate manomayadharmakāyasya tathāgatasyaitadadhivacanaṃ yatra sarvatīrthakaraśrāvakapratyekabuddhasaptabhūmipratiṣṭhitānāṃ ca bodhisattvānāmaviṣayaḥ / so 'nutpādastathāgatasya / etanmahāmate paryāyavacanam / tadyathā mahāmate indraḥ śakraḥ puraṃdaraḥ, hasyaḥ karaḥ pāṇiḥ, tanurdehaṃ śarīram, pṛthivī bhūmirvasuṃdharā, khamākāśaṃ gaganam / ityevamādyānāṃ bhāvānāmekaikasya bhāvasya bahavaḥ paryāyavācakāḥ śabdā bhavanti vikalpitāḥ / na caiṣāṃ nāmabahutvādbhāvabahutvaṃ vikalpyate / na ca svabhāvo na bhavati / evaṃ mahāmate ahamapi sahāyāṃ lokadhātau tribhirnāmāsaṃkhyeyaśatasahasrairbālānāṃ śravaṇāvabhāsamāgacchāmi / taiścābhilapanti mām, na ca prajānanti tathāgatasyaite nāmaparyāyā iti / tatra kecinmahāmate tathāgatamiti māṃ saṃprajānanti / kecitsvayaṃbhuvamiti / nāyakaṃ vināyakaṃ pariṇāyakaṃ buddhamṛṣiṃ vṛṣabhaṃ brahmāṇaṃ viṣṇumīśvaraṃ pradhānaṃ kapilaṃ bhūtāntamariṣṭaneminaṃ somaṃ bhāskaraṃ rāmaṃ vyāsaṃ śukamindraṃ baliṃ varuṇamiti caike saṃjānanti / apare anirodhānutpādaṃ
śūnyatāṃ tathatāṃ satyatāṃ bhūtatāṃ bhūtakoṭiṃ dharmadhātuṃ nirvāṇaṃ nityaṃ samatāmadvayamanirodhamanimittaṃ pratyayaṃ buddhahetūpadeśaṃ vimokṣaṃ mārgasatyāni sarvajñaṃ jinaṃ manomayamiti caike saṃjānanti / evamādibhirmahāmate paripūrṇaṃ tribhirnāmāsaṃkhyeyaśatasahasrairanūnairanadhikairihānyeṣu ca lokadhātuṣu māṃ janāḥ saṃjānante udakacandra ivāpraviṣṭanirgatam / na ca bālā avabudhyante dvayāntapatitayā saṃtatyā / atha ca satkurvanti gurukurvanti mānayanti pūjayanti ca māṃ padārthaniruktyakuśalā abhinnasaṃjñāḥ, na svanayaṃ prajānantiṃ deśanārutapāṭhābhiniviṣṭāḥ / anirodhānutpādamabhāvaṃ kalpayiṣyanti na ca tathāgatanāmapadaparyāyāntaramindraśakrapuraṃdaraṃ na svanayapratyavasthānapāṭhamadhimokṣanti, yathārutārthapāṭhānusāritvātsarvadharmāṇām / evaṃ ca mahāmate vakṣyanti te mohapuruṣāḥ - yathāruta evārthaḥ, ananyo 'rtho rutāditi / tatkasya hetoḥ? yaduta arthasyāśarīratvādrutādanyo 'rtho na bhavati / kiṃ tu rutamevārtha iti rutasvabhāvāparijñānādavidagdhabuddhayaḥ / na tvevaṃ jñāsyanti mahāmate yathā rutamutpannapradhvaṃsi, artho 'nutpannapradhvaṃsī / rutaṃ mahāmate akṣarapatitam, artho 'nakṣarapatitaḥ / bhāvābhāvavivarjitatvādajanmāśarīram / na ca mahāmate tathāgatā akṣarapatitaṃ dharmaṃ deśayanti / akṣarāṇāṃ sadasato 'nupalabdheḥ / anyatra akṣarapatitāśayaḥ punarmahāmate yo 'kṣarapatitaṃ dharmaṃ deśayati, sa ca pralapati, nirakṣaratvāddharmasya / ata etasmātkāraṇānmahāmate uktaṃ deśanāpāṭhe mayā anyaiśca buddhabodhisattvaiḥ yathaikamapyakṣaraṃ tathāgatā nodāharanti na pratyāharantīti / tatkasya
body.translated_text: All <s>dharmas</s> are taught because of not seeing the theses of existent and non-existent. 'If, Blessed One, all <s>dharmas</s> are unborn, then the grasping of <s>dharma</s> is not obtained, because of the unbornness of all <s>dharmas</s>. Or if this is a synonym for some [particular] <s>dharma</s>, let it be stated, Blessed One.' The Blessed One said: 'Then, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, listen well and thoroughly, and attend. I shall speak to you.' 'Very well, Blessed One,' the <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s> assented to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this to him: 'The <s>Tathāgata</s>, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is not non-existent; nor is there [mere] grasping of the non-ceasing and non-arising of all <s>dharmas</s>. A condition is not to be sought; nor is the grasping of non-arising made by me pointlessly. Rather, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, this is a designation for the <s>Tathāgata</s> who is the mind-made <s>Dharmakāya</s> — [that domain] where [there is] non-domain for all heretical teachers, <s>Śrāvakas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> established on the seventh stage. That non-arising is [a designation for] the <s>Tathāgata</s>. This, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is a synonymous expression. Just as, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Puraṃdara</s> [all denote the same being]; <s>hasta</s>, <s>kara</s>, <s>pāṇi</s> [all mean "hand"]; <s>tanu</s>, <s>deha</s>, <s>śarīra</s> [all mean "body"]; <s>pṛthivī</s>, <s>bhūmi</s>, <s>vasuṃdharā</s> [all mean "earth"]; <s>kha</s>, <s>ākāśa</s>, <s>gagana</s> [all mean "sky"] — thus, for each and every entity, there are many synonym-words that are conceptualized. And from the multiplicity of names, multiplicity of entities is not to be conceptualized; nor does the inherent nature [of the entity] not exist. Even so, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, in this <s>Sahā</s> world-realm, I come within the hearing-perception of the childish by three innumerable hundred-thousands of names. And by those [names] they address me, yet do not understand that these are name-synonyms of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Therein, some, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, know me as <s>Tathāgata</s>; some as Self-existent (<s>Svayaṃbhu</s>); Leader (<s>Nāyaka</s>), Guide (<s>Vināyaka</s>), Conductor (<s>Pariṇāyaka</s>), <s>Buddha</s>, Sage (<s>Ṛṣi</s>), Bull (<s>Vṛṣabha</s>), <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Īśvara</s>, <s>Pradhāna</s> (Primal Matter), <s>Kapila</s>, <s>Bhūtānta</s> (End of Beings), <s>Ariṣṭanemi</s>, <s>Soma</s>, <s>Bhāskara</s> (Sun), <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Vyāsa</s>, <s>Śuka</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Bali</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s> — thus some know [me]. Others [know me as] non-ceasing and non-arising, emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>), suchness (<s>tathatā</s>), truthness (<s>satyatā</s>), realness (<s>bhūtatā</s>), limit of reality (<s>bhūtakoṭi</s>), <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of <s>dharma</s>), <s>nirvāṇa</s>, the permanent, equality (<s>samatā</s>), non-duality, non-ceasing, signless, condition, Buddha-cause-instruction, liberation, path-truths, omniscient (<s>sarvajña</s>), conqueror (<s>jina</s>), mind-made — thus some know [me]. With such [names] as these, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, completely with three innumerable hundred-thousands of names — neither fewer nor more — here and in other world-realms, people know me, like the moon in water, as neither having entered nor departed. And the childish do not understand [me], because of the continuum that has fallen into the two extremes. And yet they revere, esteem, honor, and worship me — unskilled in the etymology of words, with undifferentiated notions; they do not understand their own method, attached to the recitation of the letter of teachings. They will conceptualize non-ceasing and non-arising as non-existence, and will not understand that the name-synonyms <s>Indra</s>-<s>Śakra</s>-<s>Puraṃdara</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s> are the recitation of establishment in one's own method — because of following the recitation of the literal meaning of all <s>dharmas</s>. And thus, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, those deluded persons will declare: "The meaning is just as the letter; the meaning is not other than the letter." For what reason? "Because the meaning is bodiless, and the meaning does not exist apart from the letter; rather, the letter itself is the meaning" — thus, from not fully knowing the inherent nature of the letter, [they are] of unsophisticated intelligence. But they will not know thus, O <s>Mahāmati</s>: the letter arises and perishes; the meaning neither arises nor perishes. The letter, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, falls under syllables; the meaning does not fall under syllables. Because it is free from existence and non-existence, [meaning] is unborn and bodiless. And the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, do not teach <s>dharma</s> falling under syllables — because syllables are not apprehended as existent or non-existent. But otherwise, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, one who, with a disposition falling under syllables, teaches <s>dharma</s> falling under syllables — he is babbling, because of the syllable-free nature of <s>dharma</s>. For this very reason, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, it has been said in the teaching-recitation by me and by other <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> that '<s>Tathāgatas</s> neither utter nor withdraw even a single syllable.' For what reason?

body.text:
hetoḥ? yaduta anakṣaratvāddharmāṇām / na ca nārthopasaṃhitamudāharanti / udāharantyeva vikalpamupādāya / anupādānānmahāmate sarvadharmāṇāṃ śāsanalopaḥ syāt / śāsanānāṃ lopācca buddhapratyekabuddhaśrāvakabodhisattvānāmabhāvaḥ syāt / tadabhāvātkiṃ kasya deśyeta? ata etasmātkāraṇānmahāmate bodhisattvena mahāsattvena deśanāpāṭharutānabhiniviṣṭena bhavitavyam / sa vyabhicārī mahāmate
deśanāpāṭhaḥ / sattvāśayapravṛttatvānnānādhimuktikānāṃ sattvānāṃ dharmadeśanā kriyate cittamanomanovijñānavyāvṛttyarthaṃ mayā anyaiśca tathāgatairarhadbhiḥ samyaksaṃbuddhaiḥ, na svapratyātmāryajñānādhigamapratyavasthānāt sarvadharmanirābhāasasvacittadṛśyamātrāvabodhāddvidhāvikalpasya vyāvṛttitaḥ / arthapratiśaraṇena mahāmate bodhisattvena mahāsattvena bhavitavyaṃ na vyañjanapratiśaraṇena / vyañjanānusārī mahāmate kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā svātmānaṃ ca nāśayati, parārthāṃśca nāvabodhayati / kudṛṣṭipatitayā saṃtatyā svapakṣaṃ vibhrāmyate kutīrthakaiḥ sarvadharmabhūmisvalakṣaṇākuśalaiḥ padaniruktyanabhijñaiḥ //
body.translated_text: Because of the syllable-free nature of <s>dharmas</s>. Yet they do not utter [speech] that is disconnected from meaning; they do utter [speech] — taking hold of discrimination. If there were no grasping of all <s>dharmas</s>, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, there would be the disappearance of the teaching. And from the disappearance of the teachings, there would be the non-existence of <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, <s>Śrāvakas</s>, and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. In that non-existence, what would be taught to whom? For this very reason, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> should be one who is not attached to the recitation of the letter of teaching. That teaching-recitation, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is deviating. Because [teaching] operates in accordance with the dispositions of beings, the <s>Dharma</s>-teaching is given by me and by other <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Enlightened <s>Buddhas</s>, for beings of various inclinations, for the purpose of turning away mind, <s>manas</s>, <s>manovijñāna</s>, and consciousness — not from the establishment of one's own inner noble knowledge-realization, not from the awakening to [the fact that all <s>dharmas</s> are] imageless [and merely] the appearance of one's own mind, [and not from] the turning-away of twofold discrimination. A <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s>, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, should be one who takes refuge in meaning, not one who takes refuge in the letter. One who follows the letter, O <s>Mahāmati</s> — whether a son or daughter of good family — destroys himself and does not awaken others to their welfare. With a continuum fallen into wrong views, he is led astray from his own position by false teachers who are unskilled in the own-characteristics of the stages of all <s>dharmas</s> and unknowing of word-etymology.

body.text: atha sarvadharmabhūmisvalakṣaṇakuśalā bhavanti padaparyāyaniruktigatiṃgatā bhāvārthayuktikuśalāḥ / tataḥ svātmānaṃ ca samyaganimittasukhena prīṇayanti, parāṃśca samyaṅmahāyāne pratiṣṭhāpayanti / mahāyāne ca mahāmate samyakparigṛhyamāṇe buddhaśrāvakapratyekabuddhabodhisattvānāṃ parigrahaḥ kṛto bhavati / buddhabodhisattvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhaparigrahātsarvasattvaparigrahaḥ kṛto bhavati / sarvasattvaparigrahātsaddharmaparigrahaḥ kṛto bhavati / saddharmaparigrahācca mahāmate buddhavaṃśasyānupacchedaḥ kṛto bhavati / buddhavaṃśasyānupacchedādāyatanaviśeṣapratilambhāḥ prajñāyante / atasteṣu viśiṣṭāyatanapratilambheṣu bodhisattvā mahāsattvā upapattiṃ parigṛhya mahāyāne pratiṣṭhāpanatayā daśavaśitāvicitrarūpaveśadhāriṇo bhūtvā sattvaviśeṣānuśayalakṣaṇagatibhūtāstathātvāya dharmaṃ deśayanti //
body.translated_text: But when they become skilled in the own-characteristics of the stages of all <s>dharmas</s>, having entered the course of word-synonym-etymology, skilled in the meaning-reasoning of entities — then they satisfy themselves with the correct signless happiness, and establish others correctly in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. And when the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is correctly upheld, the upholding of <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Śrāvakas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> is accomplished. From the upholding of <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, <s>Śrāvakas</s>, and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, the upholding of all beings is accomplished. From the upholding of all beings, the upholding of the True <s>Dharma</s> (<s>Saddharma</s>) is accomplished. And from the upholding of the True <s>Dharma</s>, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the non-interruption of the <s>Buddha</s>-lineage is accomplished. From the non-interruption of the <s>Buddha</s>-lineage, the attainments of distinguished sense-bases become manifest. Therefore, in those distinguished attainments of sense-bases, <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas</s>, having taken birth, establishing [beings] in the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, bearing diverse forms through the ten masteries (<s>vaśitā</s>), having become [aware of] the characteristics of the dispositions and latent tendencies of the distinctions of beings — they teach the <s>Dharma</s> for the sake of suchness.

body.text: tatra tathātvamananyathātvaṃ tattvam / anāyūhāniryūhalakṣaṇaṃ sarvaprapañcopaśamaṃ tattvamityucyate / tena na mahāmate kulaputreṇa vā kuladuhitrā vā yathārutārthābhiniveśakuśalena bhavitavyam / nirakṣaratvāttattvasya / na cāṅguliprekṣakeṇa bhavitavyam / tadyathā mahāmate aṅgulyā kaścitkasyacitkiṃcidādarśayet / sa cāṅgulyagrameva pratiseradvīkṣitum / evameva mahāmate bālajātīyā iva bālapṛthagjanavargā yathārutāṅgulyagrābhiniveśābhiniviṣṭā eva kālaṃ kariṣyanti, na yathārutāṅgulyagrārthaṃ hitvā paramārthamāgamiṣyanti / tadyathā mahāmate annaṃ bhojyaṃ bālānāṃ ca kaścidanabhisaṃskṛtaṃ paribhoktum / atha kaścidanabhisaṃskṛtaṃ paribhuñjīta, sa unmatta iti vikalpyeta anupūrvasaṃskārānavabodhādannasya, evameva mahāmate anutpādo 'nirodho nānabhisaṃskṛtaḥ śobhate / avaśyamevātrābhisaṃskāreṇa bhavitavyam, na cātmānamaṅgulyagragrahaṇārthadarśanavat / ata etena kāraṇena mahāmate arthābhiyogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ / artho mahāmate vivikto nirvāṇahetuḥ / rutaṃ vikalpasaṃbaddhaṃ saṃsārāvāhakam / arthaśca mahāmate bahuśrutānāṃ
body.translated_text: Therein, suchness (<s>tathātva</s>) is non-otherwise-ness, reality (<s>tattva</s>). What has the characteristic of non-exertion and non-withdrawal, the quiescence of all proliferation — that is called reality. Therefore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, a son or daughter of good family should not be skilled in attachment to the literal meaning. Because reality is syllable-free. And one should not be like one who looks at the finger[-tip]. Just as, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, someone would point out something to someone with a finger, and that [person] would keep looking only at the fingertip; even so, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, those of the class of the childish — the group of foolish ordinary beings — attached to the fingertip of the literal meaning, will die [without attainment], and will not arrive at the supreme truth by abandoning the literal-fingertip-meaning. Just as, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, food is to be eaten by the childish, and if someone were to eat it unprepared, and if someone eats it unprepared, he would be conceptualized as mad — because of not knowing the proper sequential preparation of the food; even so, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, non-arising and non-ceasing do not shine forth unprepared. Here [proper] preparation must certainly be [applied] — not like the seeing of the grasping of the fingertip-meaning. For this very reason, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, application to the meaning should be made. Meaning, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is solitary and the cause of <s>nirvāṇa</s>. The letter is connected with discrimination and carries [one] through <s>saṃsāra</s>. And meaning, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is obtained from the learned —

body.text: sakāśāllabhyate / bāhuśrutyaṃ ca nāma mahāmate yaduta arthakauśalyaṃ na rutakauśalyam / tatrārthakauśalyaṃ yatsarvatīrthakaravādāsaṃsṛṣṭaṃ darśanam / yathā svayaṃ ca na patati parāṃśca na pātayati / evaṃ satyarthe mahāmate bāhuśrutyaṃ bhavati / tasmādarthakāmena te sevanīyāḥ / ato viparītā ye yathārutārthābhiniviṣṭāste varjanīyāstattvānveṣiṇā //
body.translated_text: and 'being learned' (<s>bāhuśrutya</s>), O <s>Mahāmati</s>, means skill in meaning, not skill in the letter. Therein, skill in meaning is the vision that is unmixed with the doctrines of all heretical teachers — by which one neither falls oneself nor causes others to fall. Thus, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, regarding the true meaning, there is learnedness. Therefore those [who are skilled in meaning] are to be attended upon by one who desires meaning. Those opposite — who are attached to the literal meaning — are to be avoided by one who seeks reality.

body.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmatirbuddhādhiṣṭhānādhiṣṭhita evamāha - na bhagavatā anirodhānutpādadarśanena kiṃcidviśiṣyate / tatkasya hetoḥ? sarvatīrthakarāṇāmapi bhagavan kāraṇānyanutpannānyaniruddhāni / tavāpi bhagavan ākāśamapratisaṃkhyānirodho nirvāṇadhātuścānirodho 'nutpannaḥ / tīrthakarā api bhagavan kāraṇapratyayahetukīṃ jagata utpattiṃ varṇayanti / bhagavānapi ajñānatṛṣṇākarmavikalpapratyayebhyo jagata utpattiṃ varṇayati / tasyaiva kāraṇasya saṃjñāntaraviśeṣamutpādya pratyayā iti / evaṃ bāhyaiḥ pratyayairbāhyānām / te ca tvaṃ ca bhāvānāmutpattaye / ato nirviśiṣṭo 'yaṃ bhagavan vādastīrthakaravādena bhavati / aṇupradhāneśvaraprajāpatiprabhṛtayo navadravyasahitā aniruddhā anutpannāḥ / tavāpi bhagavan sarvabhāvā anutpannāniruddhāḥ sadasato 'nupalabdheḥ / bhūtāvināśācca svalakṣaṇaṃ notpadyate, na nirudhyate / yāṃ tāṃ gatiṃ gatvā bhūto bhūtasvabhāvaṃ na vijahāti / bhūtavikalpavikāro 'yaṃ bhagavan sarvatīrthakarairvikalpyate tvayā ca / ata etena kāraṇena aviśiṣṭo 'yaṃ vādaḥ / viśeṣo vātra vaktavyo yena tathāgatavādo viśeṣyate, na sarvatīrthakaravādaḥ / aviśiṣyamāṇe bhagavan svavāde tīrthakarāṇāmapi buddhaprasaṅgaḥ syādanirodhānutpādahetutvāt / asthānamanavakāśaṃ coktaṃ bhagavatā yadekatra lokadhātau bahavastathāgatā utpadyeranniti / prāptaṃ caitattathāgatabahutvaṃ sadasatkāryaparigrahāccāviśiṣyamāṇe svavāde //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, empowered by the <s>Buddhas</s>' empowerment, spoke thus: 'The Blessed One is not distinguished from [the heretics] by the vision of non-ceasing and non-arising. For what reason? All heretical teachers too, Blessed One, [hold that] causes are unborn and unceased. You too, Blessed One — space, <s>apratisaṃkhyānirodha</s> (cessation not through deliberation), and the <s>nirvāṇa</s>-element are unceased and unborn. Heretical teachers too, Blessed One, describe the arising of the world from the cause of causes and conditions. The Blessed One too describes the arising of the world from the conditions of ignorance, craving, and the discrimination of action. Having produced merely a difference of designation for that very same cause, [you call them] "conditions." Thus, external [entities arise] from external conditions. Both they and you [posit causes] for the arising of entities. Therefore, this doctrine of the Blessed One is not distinguished from the doctrine of heretical teachers. Atoms, primal matter (<s>Pradhāna</s>), God (<s>Īśvara</s>), <s>Prajāpati</s>, and others, together with nine substances — [they say these are] unceased and unborn. For you too, Blessed One, all entities are unborn and unceased, because of the non-apprehension of the existent and non-existent. And since an element does not perish, its own-characteristic neither arises nor ceases. Having gone to whatever destiny, an element does not abandon its elemental inherent nature. This, Blessed One, the modification of the discrimination of elements, is conceptualized by all heretical teachers and by you. For this very reason, this doctrine is not distinguished [from theirs]. Or let a distinction be stated here, by which the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s doctrine is distinguished, and not the doctrine of all heretical teachers. If, Blessed One, your own doctrine is not distinguished [from that of] the heretical teachers, then even heretical teachers would be <s>Buddhas</s>, because of having the cause of non-ceasing and non-arising. And it has been said by the Blessed One that it is impossible and without occasion for many <s>Tathāgatas</s> to arise in a single world-realm. Yet this multiplicity of <s>Tathāgatas</s> would be obtained — because of grasping effects as existent and non-existent, and because your own doctrine is not distinguished [from theirs].'

body.text: bhagavānāha - na mama mahāmate anirodhānutpādastīrthakarānutpādānirodhavādena tulyo nāpyutpādānityavādena / tatkasya hetoḥ? tīrthakarāṇāṃ hi mahāmate bhāvasvabhāvo vidyata evānutpannāvikaralakṣaṇaprāptaḥ / na tvevaṃ mama sadasatpakṣapatitaḥ / mama tu mahāmate sadasatpakṣavigata utpādabhaṅgavirahito na bhāvo nābhāavaḥ, māyāsvarūpavaicitryadarśanavannābhāvaḥ / kathaṃ na bhāvaḥ? yaduta rūpasvabhāvalakṣaṇagrahaṇābhāvāddṛśyādṛśyato grahaṇāgrahaṇataḥ / ata etasmātkāraṇātsarvabhāvā na bhāvā nābhāvāḥ / kiṃ tu svacittadṛśyamātrāvabodhādvikalpasyāpravṛtteḥ svastho loko niṣkriyaḥ / bālāḥ kriyāvantaṃ kalpayanti, na tvāryāḥ / abhūtārthavikalpārthavibhram eṣa mahāmate gandharvanagaramāyāpuruṣavat / tadyathā mahāmate kaścidgandharvanagare bālajātīyo māyāpuruṣasattvasārthavaicitryaṃ praviaśantaṃ vā nirgacchantaṃ vā kalpayet - amī praviṣṭā amī nirgatāḥ / na ca tatra kaścitpraviṣṭo vā nirgato vā / atha yāvadeva vikalpavibhramabhāva eṣaḥ, teṣāmevameva mahāmate utpādānutpādavibhrama eṣa bālānām / na cātra kaścitsaṃskṛto 'saṃskṛto vā māyāpuruṣotpattivat / na ca māyāpuruṣa utpadyate vā nirudhyate vā bhāvābhāvākiṃcitkaratvāt / evameva sarvadharmā bhaṅgotpādavarjitāḥ / anyatra vitathapatitayā saṃjñayā bālā utpādanirodhaṃ kalpayanti na tvāryāḥ / tatra vitathamiti mahāmate na tathā yathā bhāvasvabhāvaḥ kalpyate /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: My [doctrine of] non-cessation and non-arising, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is not equal to the non-Buddhist teachers' doctrine of non-arising and non-cessation, nor to their doctrine of arising and impermanence. For what reason? The non-Buddhist teachers, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, hold that the inherent nature of entities indeed exists, having attained the characteristic of being unarisen and unmodified. But this is not so for me — [it is] not fallen into the theses of existent and non-existent. For me, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, [my doctrine is] free from the theses of existent and non-existent, devoid of arising and destruction — neither existent nor non-existent, not non-existent like the vision of the variety of the inherent form of illusion. How is it not existent? Because there is no grasping of the characteristic of the inherent nature of form, from the standpoint of the visible and invisible, grasping and non-grasping. For this very reason, all entities are neither existent nor non-existent. Rather, from the awakening to [the truth that all is] merely the appearance of one's own mind, and from the non-operation of conceptual discrimination, the world is at ease and free from action. The childish construct [things as] having action, but not the noble ones. This, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the confusion over the meaning of conceptual discrimination of unreal objects — like a <s>gandharva</s>-city and an illusory person. Just as, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, a childish person in a <s>gandharva</s>-city might construct [the notion] that the variety of illusory beings and merchants is entering or departing — 'these have entered, these have departed' — yet no one there has entered or departed; rather, this is just the state of confusion of conceptual discrimination. Even so, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, this is the confusion of arising and non-arising for the childish. And here nothing is conditioned or unconditioned, like the arising of an illusory person. And the illusory person neither arises nor ceases, because the states of existence and non-existence accomplish nothing. Even so, all <s>dharmas</s> are free from destruction and arising. Elsewhere, with a perception fallen into falsity, the childish construct arising and cessation, but not the noble ones. Therein, 'falsity,' O <s>Mahāmati</s>, means not as the inherent nature of entities is conceptually constructed,

body.text: nāpyanyathā / anyathā kalpyamāne sarvabhāvasvabhāvābhiniveśa eva syāt / na viviktadarśanāviviktadarśanādvikalpasya vyāvṛttireva na syāt / ata etasmātkāraṇānmahāmate animittadarśanameva śreyo na nimittadarśanam / nimittaṃ punarjanmahetutvādaśreyaḥ / animittamiti mahāmate vikalpasyāpravṛttiranutpādo nirvāṇamiti vadāmi / tatra nirvāṇamiti mahāmate yathābhūtārthasthānadarśanaṃ vikalpacittacaittakalāpasya parāvṛttipūrvakam / tathāgatasvapratyātmāryajñānādhigamaṃ nirvāṇamiti vadāmi //
body.translated_text: and not otherwise either. If conceptually constructed otherwise, there would be nothing but attachment to the inherent nature of all entities. There would be no turning away of conceptual discrimination through the vision of distinction from the non-vision of distinction. For this very reason, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the signless (<s>animitta</s>) vision alone is beneficial, not the vision of signs. The sign is not beneficial because it is a cause of rebirth. 'Signless,' O <s>Mahāmati</s> — the non-operation of conceptual discrimination, non-arising, <s>nirvāṇa</s> — thus I speak. Therein, '<s>nirvāṇa</s>,' O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the vision of the true nature of things, preceded by the turning-back (<s>parāvṛtti</s>) of the aggregate of conceptual mind and mental factors. The attainment of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s own inner noble knowledge — that I call <s>nirvāṇa</s>.

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Therein it is said:

children.translated_text: For the purpose of turning away from arising, establishing non-arising,

children.text: ahetuvādaṃ deśemi na ca bālairvibhāvyate // Lank_3.86 //
children.translated_text: I teach the doctrine of causelessness — but it is not understood by the childish. || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.86 ||

children.text: anutpannamidaṃ sarvaṃ na ca bhāvā na santi ca /
children.translated_text: All this is unborn, and entities do not not-exist;
entities exist as <s>gandharva</s>[-city], dream, and illusion — without cause. || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.87 ||
Of those [entities] that are unborn by inherent nature and empty — by what? Tell me.
Freed from conjunction, an entity is not grasped by the intellect;
therefore I declare [all things] empty, unborn, and without inherent nature. || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.88 ||
Conjunction, as well as each individual thing, does not exist because of the absence of the visible;
conjunction does not exist, not from the dissolution [taught] by the non-Buddhist views. || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.89 ||
Dream, floating hairs, illusion, <s>gandharva</s>[-city], mirage —
without cause these are seen; so too is the variety of the world. || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.90 ||
Having refuted [arising] through the doctrine of causelessness, one should establish non-arising;

children.text: anutpāde prasādhyante mama netrī na naśyati /
children.translated_text: when non-arising is established, my guidance does not perish;

children.text: ahetuvāde deśyante tīrthyānāṃ jāyate bhayam // Lank_3.91 //
children.translated_text: when the doctrine of causelessness is taught, fear arises in the non-Buddhist teachers. || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.91 ||

children.text: kathaṃ kena kutaḥ kutra saṃbhavo 'hetuko bhavet /
children.translated_text: How, by what, from what, where would causeless arising occur?

children.text: nāhetuko na hetubhyo yadā paśyanti saṃskṛtam /
children.translated_text: When they see the conditioned as neither causeless nor from causes,
then the view that speaks of destruction and arising is turned away. || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.92 ||
Is non-arising non-existence, or the investigation of conditions,

children.text: atha bhāvasya nāmedaṃ nirarthaṃ vā bravīhi me // Lank_3.93 //
children.translated_text: or is it a name for an entity, or is it meaningless? Tell me. || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.93 ||

children.text: na cābhāvo hyanutpādo na ca pratyayavīkṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: Non-arising is not non-existence, nor is it the investigation of conditions,

children.text: na ca bhāvasya nāmedaṃ na ca nāma nirarthakam // Lank_3.94 //
children.translated_text: nor is it a name for an entity, nor is the name meaningless. || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.94 ||
Where [it is] beyond the domain of <s>Śrāvakas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and non-Buddhist teachers,
and of those who have reached the seventh stage — that is the characteristic of non-arising. || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.95 ||
The turning away from causes and conditions, the cessation of causation,
the establishment of mind-only (<s>cittamātra</s>) — that I call non-arising. || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.96 ||
The causeless operation of entities, free from the imagined and the imagining,
freed from the theses of existent and non-existent — that I call non-arising. || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.97 ||
Mind freed from the visible, free from the two inherent natures,
the turning-back of the basis (<s>āśraya</s>) — that I call non-arising. || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.98 ||
Neither external existence nor non-existence, nor the grasping of mind;
dream, floating hairs, illusion, <s>gandharva</s>[-city], mirage;
and the abandonment of all views — that is the characteristic of non-arising. || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.99 ||
Thus one should illuminate all terms such as empty and without inherent nature;

children.text: na jātu śūnyayā śūnyā kiṃ tvanutpādaśūnyayā // Lank_3.100 //
children.translated_text: [things are] never empty by [mere] emptiness, but rather by the emptiness of non-arising. || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.100 ||
The aggregate of conditions operates and ceases;

children.text: kalāpācca pṛthagbhūtaṃ na jātaṃ na nirudhyate // Lank_3.101 //
children.translated_text: but that which has become separate from the aggregate is neither born nor ceases. || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.101 ||

children.text: bhāvo na vidyate 'nyo 'nyaḥ kalāpācca pṛthak kvacit /
children.translated_text: An entity does not exist separately from the aggregate anywhere;
as oneness and separateness — so it is conceptually discriminated by the non-Buddhist teachers. || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.102 ||
A non-existent entity is not born, nor a non-existent, nor an existent-and-non-existent anywhere;

children.text: anyatra hi kalāpo 'yaṃ pravartate nivartate // Lank_3.103 //
children.translated_text: apart from this, this aggregate operates and ceases. || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.103 ||
This is merely conventional designation, a chain of mutual dependence;
there is no other object apart from the chain of conditions. || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.104 ||
Due to the non-existence of the producible, I teach non-arising, free from the fault of non-Buddhist teachers,

children.text: deśemi saṃkalāmātraṃ na ca bālairvibhāvyate // Lank_3.105 //
children.translated_text: [as] merely a chain — but it is not understood by the childish. || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.105 ||

children.text: yasya janyo bhavedbhāvaḥ saṃkalāyāḥ pṛthak kvacit /
children.translated_text: For whomever an entity would be producible, separate from the chain somewhere,
he should be known as a proponent of causelessness, a destroyer of the chain. || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.106 ||
A lamp [merely] reveals things and their kinds; the chain would be [like that];

children.text: yasya bhāvo bhavetkaścitsaṃkalāyāḥ pṛthak kvacit // Lank_3.107 //
children.translated_text: for whomever some entity would exist separate from the chain somewhere — || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.107 ||
[<s>dharmas</s>] without inherent nature, unborn, by nature like space —

children.text: saṃkalāyāḥ pṛthagbhūtā ye dharmāḥ kalpitābudhaiḥ // Lank_3.108 //
children.translated_text: those <s>dharmas</s> that have become separate from the chain are constructed by the unwise. || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.108 ||
A different, other non-arising — [this is] the nature of attainment of the noble ones;

children.text: yasya jātinamutpādaṃ tadanutpāde kṣāntiḥ syāt // Lank_3.109 //
children.translated_text: for one whose birth is non-arising — there would be patience (<s>kṣānti</s>) regarding non-arising. || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.109 ||
When one sees all this world as merely a chain,
this is merely a chain — then the mind becomes concentrated. || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.110 ||
Ignorance, craving, <s>karma</s>, and so on — the chain that is internal;
sky-born [things], clay pots, wheel, etc., seed, earth, etc. — [the chain that is] external. || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.111 ||

children.text: parato yasya vai bhāvaḥ pratyayairjāyate kvacit /
children.translated_text: For whomever an entity is born from another, from conditions, somewhere,

children.text: na saṃkalāmātramevedaṃ na te yuktyāgame sthitāḥ // Lank_3.112 //
children.translated_text: this is not merely a chain — they are not established in reason and scripture. || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.112 ||

children.text: yadi janyo na bhāvo 'sti syādbuddhiḥ kasya pratyayāt /
children.translated_text: If there is no producible entity, whose intellect would arise from conditions?

children.text: anyonyajanakā hyete tenaite pratyayāḥ smṛtāḥ // Lank_3.113 //
children.translated_text: These are mutually productive — therefore they are called conditions. || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.113 ||
Hot, fluid, moving, hard — [these] <s>dharmas</s> are conceptually discriminated by the childish;

children.text: kalāpo 'yaṃ na dharmo 'sti ato vai niḥsvabhāvatā // Lank_3.114 //
children.translated_text: this is an aggregate, not a [separate] <s>dharma</s> — hence indeed the absence of inherent nature. || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.114 ||
Just as physicians make different treatments according to the [needs of the] sick,

children.text: na tu śāstrasya bhedo 'sti doṣabhedāttu bhidyate // Lank_3.115 //
children.translated_text: there is no difference in the teaching itself; it is differentiated due to the difference in faults. || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.115 ||
Thus I, [seeing] the continuum of beings always corrupted by the faults of afflictions,

children.text: indriyāṇāṃ balaṃ jñātvā nayaṃ deśemi prāṇinām // Lank_3.116 //
children.translated_text: knowing the strength of the sense-faculties, teach the method to living beings. || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.116 ||
My teaching is not differentiated by the difference of afflictions and faculties;
there would be only one vehicle and the auspicious eightfold noble path. || <s>Laṅk</s> 3.117 ||

body.text: atha khalu mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ punarapi bhagavantametadavocat - anityatā anityateti bhagavan sarvatīrthakarairvikalpyate / tvayā ca sarvadeśanāpāṭhe deśyate - anityā bata saṃskārā utpādavyayadharmiṇa iti / tatkimiyaṃ bhagavaṃstathyā mithyeti? katiprakārā bhagavan anityatā? bhagavānāha - aṣṭaprakārā hi mahāmate sarvatīrthakarairanityatā kalpyate, na tu mayā / katamāṣṭaprakārā? tatra kecittāvanmahāmate āhuḥ - prārambhavinivṛttiranityateti / prārambho nāma mahāmate utpādo 'nutpādo 'nityatā / anye saṃsthānavinivṛttimanityatāṃ varṇayanti / anye rūpamevānityamiti / anye rūpasya vikārāntaramanityatām / nairantaryaprabandhena svarasabhaṅgabhedaṃ sarvadharmāṇāṃ kṣīradadhipariṇāmavikārāntaravadadṛṣṭanaṣṭā sarvabhāveṣu pravartate na nityateti / anye punarbhāvamanityatāṃ kalpayanti / anye bhāvābhāvamanityatāṃ kalpayanti / anye anutpādānityatāṃ sarvadharmāṇāmanityatāyāśca tadantargatatvāt / tatra mahāmate bhāvābhāvānityatā nāma yaduta bhūtabhautikasvalakṣaṇavināśānupalabdhirapravṛttirbhūtasvabhāvasya / tatra anutpādānityatā nāma yaduta nityamanityaṃ sadasatorapravṛttiḥ sarvadharmāṇāmadarśanaṃ paramāṇupravicayādadarśanam / anutpādasyaitadadhivacanaṃ notpādasya / etaddhi mahāmate anutpādānityatāyā lakṣaṇaṃ yasyānavabodhātsarvatīrthakarā utpādānityatāvāde prapatanti //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s> again said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Impermanence, impermanence' — O <s>Bhagavān</s>, it is conceptually discriminated by all non-Buddhist teachers. And you too teach in all the teaching-recitations: 'Impermanent indeed are the formations, having the nature of arising and passing away.' Is this, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, true or false? Of how many kinds, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, is impermanence? The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: Impermanence is conceptually discriminated by all non-Buddhist teachers in eight kinds, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, but not by me. Of which eight kinds? Therein, first, some say, O <s>Mahāmati</s>: 'Impermanence is the cessation of production.' Production, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is arising — non-arising is impermanence. Others describe impermanence as the cessation of shape. Others [say] that form itself is impermanent. Others [describe] impermanence as the transformation of form. [Others say] that with uninterrupted continuum and the disintegration of natural decay, [impermanence] operates in all entities — unseen and undestroyed — like the transformation of milk into curd, and not [as] permanence. Yet others construct the entity [itself] as impermanent. Others construct existence-and-non-existence as impermanent. Others [teach] the impermanence of non-arising for all <s>dharmas</s>, because of the inclusion of impermanence within that [non-arising]. Therein, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, impermanence as existence-and-non-existence means the non-apprehension of the destruction of the own-characteristic of elements and their products, and the non-operation of the inherent nature of elements. Therein, impermanence as non-arising means the non-operation of both permanent and impermanent, existent and non-existent, for all <s>dharmas</s> — the non-seeing, the non-seeing through the investigation of atoms. This is a designation for non-arising, not for arising. This indeed, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the characteristic of the impermanence of non-arising, through the non-awakening to which all non-Buddhist teachers fall into the doctrine of the impermanence of arising.

body.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate yasya bhāvo nityatā, tasya svamativikalpenaiva nityatā nānityatā bhāvaḥ / tatkasya hetoḥ? yaduta svayamavināśitvādanityatāyāḥ / iha mahāmate sarvabhāvānāmabhāvo 'nityatāyāḥ kāryam / na cānityatāmantareṇa sarvabhāvābhāva upalabhyate daṇḍaśilāmudgarānyatarabhedyabhedakavat / anyonyāviśeṣadarśanaṃ dṛṣṭam / ato 'nityatā kāraṇaṃ sarvabhāvābhāvaḥ kāryam / na ca kāryakāraṇayorviśeṣo 'sti iyamanityatā idaṃ kāryamiti / aviśeṣātkāryakāraṇayornityāḥ sarvabhāvā ahetukatvādbhāavasya / sarvabhāvābhāvo hi mahāmate ahetukaḥ / na
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, for one who holds that permanence belongs to an entity — for him, permanence is only by the conceptual discrimination of his own intellect, not impermanence of the entity. For what reason? Because impermanence is itself non-destructible. Here, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the non-existence of all entities is the effect of impermanence. And the non-existence of all entities is not apprehended without impermanence — like a stick, stone, or hammer as breaker and breakable. A mutual non-distinction of view is observed. Therefore impermanence is the cause, and the non-existence of all entities is the effect. And there is no distinction between cause and effect such that 'this is impermanence' and 'this is the effect.' Because of the non-distinction of cause and effect, all entities would be permanent — because of the causelessness of the entity. For the non-existence of all entities, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is without cause.

body.text: ca bālapṛthagjanā avabudhyante / na ca kāraṇaṃ visadṛśaṃ kāryaṃ janayati / atha janayet, teṣāmanityatā sarvabhāvānāṃ visadṛśaṃ kāryaṃ syāt, kāryakāraṇavibhāgo na syāt / dṛṣṭaśca kāryakāraṇavibhāgasteṣām / yadi vā anityatā abhāvaḥ syāt, kriyāhetubhāvalakṣaṇapatitaśca syāt, ekabhāvena vā parisamāptaḥ syātsaervabhāveṣu / kriyāhetubhāvalakṣaṇapatitatvācca svayamevānityatā nityā syāt, anityatvādayaḥ sarvabhāvā nityāḥ syurnityā eva bhaveyuḥ //
body.translated_text: And the foolish ordinary beings do not understand [this]. And a cause does not produce a dissimilar effect. If it did, their impermanence would be a dissimilar effect for all entities, and there would be no distinction of cause and effect. But that distinction of cause and effect is observed for them. Alternatively, if impermanence were non-existence, it would fall into the characteristic of a state having the nature of the cause of action, or it would be completed as a single entity in all entities. And because it falls into the characteristic of a state having the nature of the cause of action, impermanence itself would be permanent, and all entities, being impermanent, would be permanent — they would be permanent indeed.

body.text: atha sarvabhāvāntargatā anityatā, tena tryadhvapatitā syāt / tatra yadatītaṃ rūpaṃ tattena saha vinaṣṭam / anāgatamapi notpannam / rūpānutpattitayā vartamānenāpi rūpeṇa sahābhinnalakṣaṇam / rūpaṃ ca bhūtānāṃ saṃniveśaviśeṣaḥ / bhūtānāṃ bhautikasvabhāvo na vinaśyate anyānanyavivarjitatvāt / sarvatīrthakarāṇāmavināśātsarvabhūtānāṃ sarvaṃ tribhavaṃ bhūtabhautikaṃ yatrotpādasthitivikāraḥ prajñapyate / kimanyadanityaṃ bhūtabhautikavinirmuktaṃ yasyānityatā kalpyate tīrthakaraiḥ? bhūtāni ca na pravartante na nivartante svabhāvalakṣaṇābhiniveśāt //
body.translated_text: If impermanence pervades all entities, then it would fall into the three times. Therein, whatever past form there was — that has perished together with it. The future [form] too has not arisen. Because of the non-arising of form, it has an undifferentiated characteristic even with present form. Form is a particular arrangement of the great elements. The derivative nature of the great elements does not perish, because it is free from both otherness and non-otherness. Since, according to all heretical teachers, all great elements are imperishable, the entire three-fold existence is elemental and derivative, wherein arising, abiding, and transformation are designated. What else is impermanent, apart from the elemental and derivative, the impermanence of which is conceived by the heretical teachers? And the great elements neither proceed nor cease, because of the attachment to their own characteristic-nature.

body.text: tatra prārambhavinivṛttirnāma anityatā - na punarbhūtāni bhūtāntaramārabhante parasparavilakṣaṇasvalakṣaṇānna viśeṣaḥ prārabhyate / tadaviśeṣātteṣāmapunarārambhāddvidhāyogādanārambhasyānityatābuddhayo bhavanti //
body.translated_text: Therein, impermanence as the cessation of origination means: the elements do not originate another element; no distinction is originated [since] the specific characteristics are mutually different. Because of that non-distinction, because of their non-re-origination, because of the impossibility of both, they have the understanding of impermanence as non-origination.

body.text: tatra saṃsthānavinivṛttirnāma anityatā - yaduta na bhūtabhautikaṃ vinaśyati ā pralayāt / pralayo nāma mahāmate ā paramāṇoḥ pravicayaparīkṣā vināśo bhūtabhautikasya saṃsthānasyānyathābhūtadarśanāddīrghahrasvānulabdhiḥ / na paramāṇubhūteṣu vināśādbhūtānāṃ saṃsthānavinivṛttidarśanātsāṃkhyavāde prapatanti //
body.translated_text: Therein, impermanence as the cessation of configuration means: the elemental and derivative does not perish until dissolution (<s>pralaya</s>). Dissolution, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, means the investigation and examination down to the atom — the destruction of the configuration of the elemental and derivative; from the perception of its becoming otherwise, the apprehension of long and short [results]. Because atoms among elements do not perish, from the perception of the cessation of the configuration of elements, they fall into the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> doctrine.

body.text: tatra saṃsthānānityatā nāma - yaduta yasya rūpamevānityaṃ tasya saṃsthānasyānityatā na bhūtānām / atha bhūtānāmanityatā syāt, lokasaṃvyavahārābhāvaḥ syāt / lokasaṃvyavahārābhāvāllokāyatikadṛṣṭipatitaḥ syāt, vāgmātratvātsarvabhāvānām / na punaḥ svalakṣaṇotpattidarśanāt //
body.translated_text: Therein, the impermanence of configuration means: that whose form alone is impermanent — [it is] the impermanence of its configuration, not of the elements. If there were impermanence of the elements, there would be the absence of worldly convention. From the absence of worldly convention, one would fall into the <s>Lokāyatika</s> view, because all entities would be mere words — but [this is not so], because the arising of specific characteristics is perceived.

body.text: tatra vikārānityatā nāma - yaduta rūpasyānyathābhūtadarśanaṃ na bhūtānāṃ suvarṇasaṃsthānabhūṣaṇavikāradarśanavat / na suvarṇaṃ bhāvādvinaśyati kiṃ tu bhūṣaṇasaṃsthānavināśo bhavati //
body.translated_text: Therein, the impermanence of transformation means: the perception of form becoming otherwise, not of the elements — like the perception of the transformation of gold into the configuration of ornaments. Gold does not perish from [its] being, but rather the destruction of the ornament-configuration occurs.

body.text: ye cānye vikārapatitāḥ, evamādyādibhiḥ prakāraistīrthakarairanityatādṛṣṭirvikalpyate / bhūtāni hi dahyamānānyagninā svalakṣaṇatvānna dahyante / anyonyataḥ svalakṣaṇavigamānmahābhūtabhautikabhāvocchedaḥ syāt //
body.translated_text: And others who have fallen into [the doctrine of] transformation — by such and similar methods the view of impermanence is discriminated by the heretical teachers. For the elements, though being burned by fire, are not burned because of their being specific characteristics. From the departure of the specific characteristics from each other, there would be the annihilation of the great elements and their derivatives.

body.text: mama tu mahāmate na nityā nānityā / tatkasya hetoḥ? yaduta bāhyabhāvānabhyupagamātribhavacittamātropadeśādvicitralakṣaṇānupadeśānna pravartate na nivartate mahābhūtasaṃniveśaviśeṣaḥ / na bhūtabhautikatvādvikalpasya dvidhā pravartate grāhyagrāhakālakṣaṇatā / vikalpasya pravṛttidvayaparijñānādbāhyabhāvābhāvadṛṣṭivigamātsvacittamātrāvabodhādvikalpo vikalpābhisaṃskāreṇa pravartate nānabhisaṃskurvataḥ / cittavikalpabhāvābhāvavigamāllaukikalokottaratamānāṃ sarvadharmāṇāṃ
body.translated_text: But for me, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, [things are] neither permanent nor impermanent. For what reason? Because of the non-acceptance of external entities, because of the teaching that the three realms are mind-only (<s>cittamātra</s>), because of the teaching that there are no diverse characteristics — the particular arrangement of the great elements neither proceeds nor ceases. Not because of being elemental and derivative does conceptual discrimination operate in two ways as the characteristic of grasper and grasped. From the full comprehension of the twofold operation of conceptual discrimination, from the departure of the view of the existence and non-existence of external entities, from the awakening to [the truth that all is] one's own mind only — conceptual discrimination operates through the constructions of conceptual discrimination, but not for one who does not construct. From the departure of the existence and non-existence of mind-and-conceptual-discrimination, of all <s>dharmas</s>, mundane and supramundane,

body.text: na nityatā nānityatā / svacittadṛśyamātrānavabodhātkudṛṣṭyāntadvayapatitayā saṃtatyā sarvatīrthakaraiḥ svavikalpānavabodhātkathāpuruṣairasiddhapūrvairanityatā kalpyate / trividhaṃ ca mahāmate sarvatīrthakaralauikikalokottaratamānāṃ sarvadharmāṇāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ vāgvikalpaviniḥsṛtānām / na ca bālapṛthagjanā avabudhyante //
body.translated_text: there is neither permanence nor impermanence. From the non-awakening to [the truth that all is] mere appearance of one's own mind (<s>svacittadṛśyamātra</s>), with a mental continuum fallen into the extremes of wrong views, by all heretical teachers, from the non-awakening to their own conceptual discriminations, impermanence is conceived by figment-persons whose [doctrines are] previously unestablished. And of three kinds, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the characteristic of all <s>dharmas</s> — mundane and supramundane — of all heretical teachers, [insofar as they are] produced from speech-and-conceptual-discrimination. But the foolish ordinary beings do not understand [this].

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Therein this is said:

children.translated_text: The cessation of origination and the becoming-otherwise of configuration,

children.text: bhāvamanityatāṃ rūpaṃ tīrthyāḥ kalpenti mohitāḥ // Lank_3.118 //
children.translated_text: the impermanence of entities and form — the deluded heretics conceive [these]. [Laṅk 3.118]

children.text: bhāvānāṃ nāsti vai nāśaṃ bhūtā bhūtātmanā sthitāḥ /
children.translated_text: There is indeed no destruction of entities; the elements abide in their own elemental nature;
sunk in diverse views, those heretics conceive permanence. [Laṅk 3.119]

children.text: kasyacinna hi tīrthyasya vināśo na ca saṃbhavaḥ /
children.translated_text: For none of the heretics is there either destruction or origination;

children.text: bhūtā bhūtātmanā nityāḥ kasya kalpentyanityatām // Lank_3.120 //
children.translated_text: the elements are permanent in their own elemental nature — of what do they conceive impermanence? [Laṅk 3.120]
All this is mind-only; the mind operates in two ways,
in the form of grasper and grasped — self and what belongs to self do not exist. [Laṅk 3.121]
From <s>Brahmā</s> down to the lowest abodes, I declare [all to be] mind-only;
apart from mind-only, <s>Brahmā</s> and the rest are not apprehended. [Laṅk 3.122]

body.text: iti laṅkāvatāre mahāyānasūtre anityatāparivartastṛtīyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Laṅkāvatāra Mahāyāna Sūtra</s>, [ends] the third chapter called "The Chapter on Impermanence."

body.text: START Parivarta 4
body.translated_text: START Chapter 4

body.text: abhisamayaparivarto nāma caturthaḥ /
body.translated_text: The fourth chapter, called "The Chapter on Realization."
