body.text: atha khalu mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ punarapi bhagavantametadavocat - deśayatu me bhagavān sarvabodhisattvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhanirodhakramānusaṃdhilakṣaṇakauśalyaṃ yena kramānusaṃdhilakṣaṇakauśalyena ahaṃ ca anye ca bodhisattvā mahāsattvā nirodhasukhasamāpattimukhena na pratimuhyema, na ca śrāvakapratyekabuddhatīrthyakaravyāmohe prapatema / bhagavānāha - tena mahāmate śṛṇu, sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasikuru / bhāṣiṣye 'haṃ te / sādhu bhagavanniti mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavataḥ pratyaśrauṣīt //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s> again addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s> thus: May the <s>Bhagavān</s> teach me the skill in the characteristic of the progressive connection of the cessation-[attainment] of all <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, <s>Śrāvakas</s>, and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, so that I and other <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas</s>, by that skill in the characteristic of progressive connection, may not be confused by the cessation-bliss-attainment gateway, and may not fall into the confusion of <s>Śrāvakas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and heretical teachers. The <s>Bhagavān</s> replied: Then, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, listen, and attend well and thoroughly. I shall teach you. "Very well, <s>Bhagavān</s>," the <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s> assented to the <s>Bhagavān</s>.

body.text: bhagavāṃstasyaitadavocat - ṣaṣṭhīṃ mahāmate bhūmimupādāya bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhāśca nirodhaṃ samāpadyante / saptamyāṃ bhūmau punaścittakṣaṇe cittakṣaṇe bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ sarvabhāvasvabhāvalakṣaṇavyudāsātsamāpadyante, na tu śrāvakapratyekabuddhāḥ / teṣāṃ hi śrāvakapratyekabuddhānāmābhisaṃskārikī grāhyagrāhakalakṣaṇapatitā ca nirodhasamāpattiḥ / ataste saptamyāṃ bhūmau cittakṣaṇe cittakṣaṇe samāpadyante - mā sarvadharmāṇāmaviśeṣalakṣaṇaprāptiḥ syāditi / vicitralakṣaṇābhāvaśca / kuśalākuśalasvabhāvalakṣaṇānavabodhātsarvadharmāṇāṃ samāpattirbhavati / ataḥ saptamyāṃ bhūmau cittakṣaṇe cittakṣaṇe samāpattikauśalyaṃ nāsti yena samāpadyeran //
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said this to him: Beginning from the sixth stage (<s>bhūmi</s>), O <s>Mahāmati</s>, <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas</s> and all <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> enter cessation [-attainment]. At the seventh stage, however, at every moment of mind, <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas</s> enter [cessation] through the elimination of the characteristic of the inherent nature of all entities — but not the <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>. For their cessation-attainment, that of the <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, is constructed and fallen into the characteristic of grasper and grasped. Therefore, at the seventh stage, they enter [cessation] at every moment of mind — [thinking] "lest the attainment of the characteristic of non-differentiation of all <s>dharmas</s> should result." And the diversity of characteristics would be absent. From the non-awakening to the characteristic of the inherent nature of wholesome and unwholesome, there is the attainment regarding all <s>dharmas</s>. Therefore, at the seventh stage, there is no skill in attainment at every moment of mind, by which they could enter [cessation].

body.text: aṣṭamyāṃ mahāmate bhūmau bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ śrāvakapratyekabuddhānāṃ ca cittamanomanovijñānavikalpasaṃjñāvyāvṛttirbhavati / prathamaṣaṣṭhyāṃ bhūmau cittamanomanovijñānamātraṃ traidhātukaṃ samanupaśyati ātmātmīyavigataṃ svacittavikalpodbhavam, na ca bāhyabhāvalakṣaṇavaicitryapatitamanyatra svacittameva / dvidhā bālānāṃ grāhyagrāhakabhāvena pariṇāmya svajñānaṃ na cāvabodhyante anādikāladauṣṭhulyavikalpaprapañcavāsanāvāsitāḥ //
body.translated_text: At the eighth stage, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, for <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas</s> and for <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, the turning-away of the discrimination and perception of mind, <s>manas</s>, and <s>manovijñāna</s> occurs. From the first through the sixth stage, one sees the three realms as merely mind, <s>manas</s>, and <s>manovijñāna</s>, devoid of self and what belongs to self, arisen from the conceptual discrimination of one's own mind, and not fallen into the diversity of external entity-characteristics — [it is] nothing other than one's own mind. [Yet their own] knowledge, transforming itself for the foolish in the twofold [mode] of grasper and grasped, they do not awaken [to] — being perfumed by the impressions of the proliferative discrimination of beginningless depravity.

body.text: aṣṭamyāṃ mahāmate nirvāṇaṃ śrāvakapratyekabuddhabodhisattvānām / bodhisattvāśca samādhibuddhairvidhāryante tasmātsamādhisukhād, yena na parinirvānti aparipūrṇatvāttathāgatabhūmeḥ / sarvakāryapratiprasrambhaṇaṃ ca syāt, yadi na saṃghārayet, tathāgatakulavaṃśocchedaśca syāt / acintyabuddhamāhātmyaṃ ca deśayanti te buddhā bhagavantaḥ / ato na parinirvānti / śrāvakapratyekabuddhāstu samādhisukhenāpahriyante / atasteṣāṃ tatra parinirvāṇabuddhirbhavati //
body.translated_text: At the eighth [stage], O <s>Mahāmati</s>, [there is] <s>nirvāṇa</s> for <s>Śrāvakas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. But the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are held back from that <s>samādhi</s>-bliss by the <s>Buddhas</s> through <s>samādhi</s>, so that they do not attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s> — because the <s>Tathāgata</s>-stage has not been fulfilled. There would also be the relaxation of all [beneficial] activities; if [the <s>Buddhas</s>] did not restrain [them], there would be the cutting off of the lineage of the <s>Tathāgata</s> family. And those <s>Buddhas</s> <s>Bhagavāns</s> teach the inconceivable greatness of the <s>Buddha</s>. Therefore they do not attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. But the <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> are carried away by <s>samādhi</s>-bliss. Therefore their understanding of <s>parinirvāṇa</s> arises therein.

body.text: saptasu mahāmate bhūmiṣu cittamanomanovijñānalakṣaṇaparicayakauśalyātmātmīyagrāhyagrāhadharmapudgalanairātmyapravṛttinivṛttisvasāmānya - lakṣaṇaparicayacatuḥpratisaṃvidviniścayakauśalyavaśitāsvādasukhabhūmikramānupraveśabodhipākṣikadharmavibhāgaḥ kriyate mayā - mā bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ svasāmānyalakṣaṇānavabodhādbhūmikramānusaṃdhyakuśalāstīrthakarakudṛṣṭimārge prapateyuḥ, ityato bhūmikramavyavasthā kriyate / na tu mahāmate atra kaścitpravartate vā nivartate vā anyatra svacitadṛśyamātramidaṃ yaduta bhūmikramānusaṃdhistraidhātukavicitropacāraśca / na ca bālā avabudhyante / anavabodhādbālānāṃ bhūmikramānusaṃdhivyapadeśaṃ traidhātukavicitropacāraśca vyavasthāpyate buddhadharmālayā ca //
body.translated_text: In the seven stages, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, I make the differentiation of the factors conducive to enlightenment (<s>bodhipākṣika dharma</s>) — through the skill in the familiarity with the characteristics of mind, <s>manas</s>, and <s>manovijñāna</s>; the operation and cessation of the selflessness of persons and <s>dharmas</s> regarding self, what belongs to self, grasper, and grasped; the familiarity with specific and general characteristics; the skill in the determination of the four analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>); and the progressive entry into the stages of the enjoyment of mastery-bliss — [thinking] "lest the <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas</s>, from the non-awakening to specific and general characteristics, unskilled in the progressive connection of the stages, should fall onto the path of the wrong views of heretical teachers." Therefore the progressive arrangement of the stages is made. But, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, herein nothing whatsoever proceeds or ceases — apart from [the truth that] this is mere appearance of one's own mind, namely, the progressive connection of stages and the diverse operations of the three realms. And the foolish do not understand. Because of the non-understanding of the foolish, the designation of the progressive connection of stages and the diverse operations of the three realms is established, as well as the treasury of <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate śrāvakapratyekabuddhā aṣṭamyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau nirodhasamāpattisukhamadamattāḥ svacittadṛśyamātrākuśalāḥ svasāmānyalakṣaṇāvaraṇavāsanāpudgaladharmanairātmyagrāhakadṛṣṭipatitā vikalpanirvāṇamatibuddhayo bhavanti, na viviktadharmamatibuddhayaḥ / bodhisattvāḥ punarmahāmate nirodhasamādhisukhamukhaṃ dṛṣṭvā pūrvapraṇidhānakṛpākaruṇopetā niṣṭhapadagativibhāgajñā na parinirvānti / parinirvṛtāśca te vikalpasyāpravṛttatvāt / grāhyagrāhakavikalpasteṣāṃ vinivṛttaḥ / svacittadṛśyamātrāvabodhāt sarvadharmāṇāṃ vikalpo na pravartate / cittamanomanovijñānabāhyabhāvasvabhāvalakṣaṇābhiniveśaṃ vikalpayati / tena punarbuddhadharmaheturna pravartate, jñānapūrvakaḥ pravartate tathāgatasvapratyātmabhūmyadhigamanatayā svapnapuruṣaughottaraṇavat //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, at the eighth <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage, intoxicated by the bliss of cessation-attainment, unskilled in [the truth that all is] mere appearance of one's own mind, fallen into the view of the grasper [afflicted by] the obscuration-impressions of specific and general characteristics and the selflessness of persons and <s>dharmas</s> — they have the understanding of discriminative <s>nirvāṇa</s>, not the understanding of the <s>Dharma</s> that is free [from discrimination]. The <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, moreover, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, having seen the gateway of cessation-<s>samādhi</s>-bliss, endowed with former vows, compassion, and <s>karuṇā</s>, knowing the differentiation of the courses of the ultimate stage — do not attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. And those [who have reached cessation] are [already] in <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, because conceptual discrimination does not operate [for them]. The conceptual discrimination of grasper and grasped has ceased for them. From the awakening to [the truth that all is] mere appearance of one's own mind, conceptual discrimination does not operate regarding all <s>dharmas</s>. [Yet others] discriminate the attachment to the characteristic of the inherent nature of external entities through mind, <s>manas</s>, and <s>manovijñāna</s>. Therefore the cause of <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> does not operate [for them]; it operates preceded by knowledge, through the attainment of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s own inner stage — like a man in a dream [who crosses] a flood of water.

body.text: tadyathā punarmahāmate kaścicchayitaḥ svapnāntare mahāvyāyāmautsukyena mahaughādātmānamuttārayet / sa cānuttīrṇa eva pratibudhyeta / pratibuddhaśca sannevamupaparīkṣeta - kimidaṃ satyamuta mithyeti / sa evaṃ samanupaśyet - nedaṃ satyaṃ na mithyā anyatra dṛṣṭaśrutamatavijñātānubhūtavikalpavāsanāvicitrarūpasaṃsthānānādikālavikalpapatitā nāstyastidṛṣṭivikalpaparivarjitā manovijñānānubhūtāḥ svapne dṛśyante / evameva mahāmate bodhisattvā mahāsattvā aṣṭamyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau vikalpasyāpravṛttiṃ dṛṣṭvā prathamasaptamībhūmisaṃcārātsarvadharmābhisamayānmāyādidharmasamatayā sarvadharmautsukyagrāhyagrāhakavikalpoparataṃ cittacaitasikavikalpaprasaraṃ dṛṣṭvā buddhadharmeṣu prayujyante / anadhigatānāmadhigamāya prayoga eṣa mahāmate nirvāṇaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ na vināśaḥ cittamanomanovijñānavikalpasaṃjñāvigamācca anutpattikadharmakṣāntipratilambho bhavati / na cātra mahāmate paramārthe kramo na kramānusaṃdhirnirābhāsavikalpaviviktadharmopadeśāt //
body.translated_text: Just as, moreover, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, someone asleep, in the midst of a dream, with great effort and eagerness, rescues himself from a great flood; and he, not yet having crossed, would awaken. And being awake, he would examine thus: "Is this real or false?" He would perceive thus: "This is neither real nor false — apart from [the fact that] the conceptual discrimination, having fallen into beginningless discriminative impressions of diverse form-configurations of what has been seen, heard, thought, known, and experienced, free from the discrimination of the views of 'it does not exist' and 'it exists,' experienced by <s>manovijñāna</s>, is seen in dreams." Even so, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas</s>, at the eighth <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage, having seen the non-operation of conceptual discrimination, from the course through the first through seventh stages, from the realization of all <s>dharmas</s>, seeing that the activity of mind and mental-factor discrimination has ceased through the equality of all <s>dharmas</s> such as illusion etc., [which are] free from the grasper-grasped discrimination of eagerness regarding all <s>dharmas</s> — they exert themselves in the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>. This effort for the attainment of what has not [yet] been attained, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the <s>nirvāṇa</s> of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, not destruction. And from the departure of the perception of the discrimination of mind, <s>manas</s>, and <s>manovijñāna</s>, the attainment of the <s>anutpattikadharmakṣānti</s> (patient acceptance of the non-arising of <s>dharmas</s>) occurs. And herein, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, in the supreme truth, there is no progression, nor progressive connection — because of the teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> that is free from the appearance-free discrimination.

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Therein this is said:

children.translated_text: In mind-only, the appearance-free, the [<s>Bodhisattva</s>] abodes and the <s>Buddha</s>-stage —

children.text: etaddhi bhāṣitaṃ buddhairbhāṣante bhāṣayanti ca // Lank_4.1 //
children.translated_text: this indeed was taught by the <s>Buddhas</s>, is [being] taught, and will be taught. [Laṅk 4.1]

children.text: cittaṃ hi bhūmayaḥ sapta nirābhāsā tvihāṣṭamī /
children.translated_text: The mind is the seven stages; the appearance-free is the eighth here;

children.text: dve hi bhūmī vihāro 'tra śeṣā bhūmirmamātmikā // Lank_4.2 //
children.translated_text: the two stages are abodes here; the remaining stage belongs to me [the <s>Tathāgata</s>]. [Laṅk 4.2]
Inwardly realized and pure — this stage belongs to me,
the supreme station of <s>Maheśvara</s> (the Great Lord) — <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> shines forth. || <s>Laṅk</s> 4.3 ||
Just as the rays of the sacrificial fire emerge from it,

children.text: citrā manoharāḥ saumyāstribhavaṃ nirmiṇanti te // Lank_4.4 //
children.translated_text: beautiful, captivating, and gentle — they create the three realms of existence. || <s>Laṅk</s> 4.4 ||
Having created part of the three realms, while part was previously created,

children.text: tatra deśemi yānāni eṣā bhūmirmamātmikā // Lank_4.5 //
children.translated_text: therein I teach the vehicles — this stage is my own. || <s>Laṅk</s> 4.5 ||

children.text: daśamī tu bhavetprathamā prathamā cāṣṭamī bhavet /
children.translated_text: The tenth [stage] would be the first, and the first would be the eighth;

children.text: navamī saptamī cāpi saptamī cāṣṭamī bhavet // Lank_4.6 //
children.translated_text: the ninth [would be] the seventh, and the seventh would be the eighth. || <s>Laṅk</s> 4.6 ||

children.text: dvitīyā ca tṛtīyā syāccaturthī pañcamī bhavet /
children.translated_text: The second would be the third, and the fourth would be the fifth;

children.text: tṛtīyā ca bhavetṣaṣṭhī nirābhāse kramaḥ kutaḥ // Lank_4.7 //
children.translated_text: the third would be the sixth — in the imageless, where is there sequence? || <s>Laṅk</s> 4.7 ||

body.text: iti laṅkāvatāre abhisamayaparivartaścaturthaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the fourth chapter, the Chapter on Realization (<s>abhisamaya</s>), in the <s>Laṅkāvatāra</s>.

body.text: START Parivarta 5
body.translated_text: Beginning of Chapter 5.

body.text: tathāgatanityānityaprasaṅgaparivarto nāma pañcamaḥ /
body.translated_text: The fifth [chapter], named the Chapter on the Permanence and Impermanence of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

body.text: atha khalu mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ punarapi bhagavantametadavocat - kiṃ bhagavaṃstathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho nitya utāho 'nityaḥ? bhagavānāha - na mahāmate tathāgato nityo nānityaḥ / tatkasyaḥ hetoḥ? yaduta ubhayadoṣaprasaṅgāt / ubhayathā hi mahāmate doṣaprasaṅgaḥ syāt / nitye sati kāraṇaprasaṅgaḥ syāt / nityāni hi mahāmate sarvatīrthakarāṇāṃ kāraṇānyakṛtakāni ca / ato na nityastathāgato 'kṛtakanityatvāt / anitye sati kṛtakaprasaṅgaḥ syāt / skandhalakṣyalakṣaṇābhāvātskandhavināśāducchedaḥ syāt / na cocchedo bhavati tathāgataḥ / sarvaṃ hi mahāmate kṛtakamanityaṃ ghaṭapaṭatṛṇakāṣṭheṣṭakādi / sarvānityatvaprasaṅgāt sarvajñajñānasaṃbhāravaiyarthyaṃ bhavetkṛtakatvāt / sarvaṃ hi kṛtakaṃ tathāgataḥ syādviśeṣahetvabhāvāt / ata etasmātkāraṇānmahāmate na nityo nānityastathāgataḥ //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s> again said this to the Blessed One: 'Is the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, O Blessed One, permanent or impermanent?' The Blessed One said: 'The <s>Tathāgata</s>, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is neither permanent nor impermanent. For what reason? Because of the fault entailed in both. For in both cases, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, a fault would follow. If permanent, there would be the implication of a [first] cause. For all the causes of the heretical teachers, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, are permanent and uncreated. Therefore the <s>Tathāgata</s> is not permanent, because of the permanence of the uncreated. If impermanent, there would be the implication of being created. Because of the absence of the characterized and the characteristic of the aggregates, and from the destruction of the aggregates, there would be annihilation. But the <s>Tathāgata</s> is not annihilation. For everything created, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is impermanent — like pots, cloth, grass, wood, bricks, and so forth. Since everything would become impermanent, the accumulation of the provisions of omniscient knowledge would be purposeless, because of being created. Everything created would be a <s>Tathāgata</s>, because of the absence of a distinguishing cause. For this reason, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> is neither permanent nor impermanent.'

body.text: punarapi mahāmate na nityastathāgataḥ / kasmāt? ākāśasaṃbhāravaiyarthyaprasaṅgāt / tadyathā mahāmate ākāśaṃ na nityaṃ nānityaṃ nityānityavyudāsādekatvānyatvobhayatvānubhayatvanityānityatvadoṣairavacanīyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> is not permanent. Why? Because of the implication of the purposelessness of the accumulations of space. Just as space, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is neither permanent nor impermanent — through the removal of [the alternatives of] permanence and impermanence — it is inexpressible through the faults of oneness, otherness, both, neither, and permanence-impermanence.

body.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate śaśahayakharoṣṭramaṇḍūkasarpamakṣikāmīnaviṣāṇatulyaḥ syādanutpādanityatvāt / ato 'nutpādanityatvaprasaṅgānna nityastathāgataḥ //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, he would be equal to the horn of a hare, horse, donkey, camel, frog, snake, fly, or fish — because of the permanence of non-arising. Therefore, because of the implication of permanence through non-arising, the <s>Tathāgata</s> is not permanent.

body.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate astyasau paryāyo yena nityastathāgataḥ / tatkasya hetoḥ? yaduta abhisamayādhigamajñānanityatvānnityastathāgataḥ / abhisamayādhigamajñānaṃ hi mahāmate nityaṃ tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānām / utpādādvā tathāgatānāmanutpādādvā sthitaivaiṣā dharmatā dharmaniyāmatā dharmasthititā sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhatīrthakarābhisamayeṣu / na tu gagane dharmasthitirbhavati / na va bālapṛthagjanā avabudhyante / adhigamajñānaṃ ca mahāmate tathāgatānāṃ prajñājñānaprabhāvitam / na mahāmate tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāścittamanomanovijñānaskandhadhātvāyatanāvidyāvāsanāprabhāvitāḥ / sarvaṃ hi mahāmate tribhavamabhūtavikalpaprabhavam / na ca tathāgatā abhūtavikalpaprabhavāḥ / dvaye hi sati mahāmate nityatā cānityatā ca bhavati, nādvayāt / dvayaṃ hi mahāmate viviktamadvayānutpādalakṣaṇātsarvadharmāṇām / ata etasmātkāraṇānmahāmate tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā na nityā nānityāḥ / yāvanmahāmate vāgvikalpaḥ pravartate, tāvannityānityadoṣaḥ prasajyate / vikalpabuddhikṣayānmahāmate nityānityagrāho nivāryate bālānāṃ na tu viviktadṛṣṭibuddhikṣayāt //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, there is a way in which the <s>Tathāgata</s> is permanent. For what reason? Because the <s>Tathāgata</s> is permanent through the permanence of the knowledge of realization-attainment. For the knowledge of realization-attainment, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is permanent for the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones. Whether <s>Tathāgatas</s> arise or do not arise, this <s>dharmatā</s> (nature of <s>dharma</s>), this <s>dharmaniyāmatā</s> (certainty of <s>dharma</s>), this <s>dharmasthititā</s> (stability of <s>dharma</s>) stands established — in the realizations of all <s>Śrāvakas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and heretical teachers. But the stability of <s>dharma</s> does not exist in space. Nor do childish ordinary persons understand it. The knowledge of attainment of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is empowered by wisdom-knowledge. The <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, are not empowered by mind, mentation, consciousness, aggregates, elements, sense-bases, or the impressions of ignorance. For all the three realms of existence, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, arise from unreal imagination. But the <s>Tathāgatas</s> do not arise from unreal imagination. For when there is duality, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, there is permanence and impermanence — not from non-duality. For duality, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is isolated through the characteristic of non-duality and non-arising of all <s>dharmas</s>. For this reason, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones are neither permanent nor impermanent. As long as, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, speech-conceptualization operates, so long does the fault of permanence and impermanence follow. Through the exhaustion of the intellect of conceptualization, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the grasping of permanence and impermanence is warded off for the childish — but not through the exhaustion of the intellect of isolated vision.

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: On this, it is said:

children.translated_text: Those who always see the Buddhas as freed from [both] permanence and impermanence, [yet] manifested through permanence and impermanence —

children.text: ye paśyanti sadā buddhān na te dṛṣṭivaśaṃ gatāḥ // Lank_5.1 //
children.translated_text: they have not fallen under the sway of views. || <s>Laṅk</s> 5.1 ||
The purposelessness of accumulations follows from [attributing] permanence or impermanence;
through the deficiency of the intellect of conceptualization, permanence and impermanence are warded off. || <s>Laṅk</s> 5.2 ||
As long as a thesis is maintained, so long is everything mixed up;

children.text: svacittamātraṃ saṃpaśyan na vivādaṃ samārabhet // Lank_5.3 //
children.translated_text: seeing [all as] one's own mind only, one should not engage in dispute. || <s>Laṅk</s> 5.3 ||

body.text: iti laṅkāvatāre tathāgatanityānityatvaprasaṅgaparivartaḥ pañcamaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the fifth chapter, the Chapter on the Permanence and Impermanence of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, in the <s>Laṅkāvatāra</s>.

body.text: START Parivarta 6
body.translated_text: Beginning of Chapter 6.

body.text: kṣaṇikaparivarto nāma ṣaṣṭhaḥ /
body.translated_text: The sixth [chapter], named the Chapter on Momentariness.

body.text: atha khalu mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ punarapi bhagavantamadhyeṣate sma - deśayatu me bhagavān, deśayatu me sugataḥ skandhadhātvāyatanānāṃ pravṛttinivṛttim / asatyātmani kasya pravṛttirvā nirvṛttirvā? bālāśca pravṛttinivṛttyāśritā duḥkhakṣayānavabodhānnirvāṇaṃ na prajānanti / bhagavānāha - tena hi mahāmate śṛṇu, sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasikuru / bhāṣiṣye 'haṃ te / sādhu bhagavanniti mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavataḥ pratyaśrauṣīt //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s> again entreated the Blessed One: 'May the Blessed One teach me, may the <s>Sugata</s> teach me, the operation and cessation of the aggregates, elements, and sense-bases. When there is no self, whose operation or cessation would there be? The childish, relying on operation and cessation, not understanding the exhaustion of suffering, do not know <s>nirvāṇa</s>.' The Blessed One said: 'Then, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, listen, and attend well and thoroughly. I shall speak to you.' 'Very well, Blessed One!' — the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s> gave assent to the Blessed One.

body.text: bhagavāṃstasyaitadavocat - tathāgatagarbho mahāmate kuśalākuśalahetukaḥ sarvajanmagatikartā pravartate naṭavadgatisaṃkaṭa ātmātmīyavarjitaḥ / tadanavabodhātrisaṃgatipratyayakriyāyogaḥ pravartate / na ca tīrthyā avabudhyante kāraṇābhiniveśābhiniviṣṭāḥ / anādikālavividhaprapañcadauṣṭhulyavāsanāvāsitaḥ ālayavijñānasaṃśabdito 'vidyāvāsanabhūmijaiḥ saptabhirvijñānaiḥ saha mahodadhitaraṃgavannityamavyucchinnaśarīraḥ pravartate anityatādoṣarahita ātmavādavinivṛtto 'tyantaprakṛtipariśuddhaḥ / tadanyāni vijñānānyutpannāpavargāni manomanovijñānaprabhṛtīni kṣaṇikāni, saptāpyabhūtaparikalpahetujanitasaṃsthānākṛtiviśeṣasamavāyāvalambīni nāmanimittābhiniviṣṭāni svacittadṛśyarūpalakṣaṇāavabodhakāni sukhaduḥkhāpratisaṃvedakāni amokṣakāraṇāni nāmanimittaparyutthānarāgajanitajanakataddhetvālambāni / teṣāṃ copāttānāmindriyākhyānāṃ parikṣayanirodhe samantarānutpatteranyeṣāṃ svamativikalpasukhaduḥkhāpratisaṃvedināṃ saṃjñāveditanirodhasamāpattisamāpannānāṃ caturdhyānasatyavimokṣakuśalānāṃ yogināṃ vimokṣabuddhirbhavatyapravṛtteḥ //
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said this to him: 'The <s>Tathāgatagarbha</s> (embryo of the <s>Tathāgata</s>), O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the cause of the wholesome and unwholesome, the maker of all courses of birth. It operates like an actor at a crossroads of destinies, free from self and what belongs to self. Because of not understanding that, the yoga of the activity of conditions of the three types [of beings] operates. But the heretical teachers, who are attached to the notion of a [first] cause, do not understand this. Perfumed by the impressions of the varied depravity of beginningless proliferation, designated as the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> (store-consciousness), together with the seven consciousnesses born from the stages of the impressions of ignorance, it operates with a body that is perpetual and uninterrupted, like the waves of the great ocean — free from the fault of impermanence, freed from the doctrine of self, utterly pure by nature. The other consciousnesses — beginning with <s>manas</s> (mentation) and <s>manovijñāna</s> (mind-consciousness) — arise and perish, are momentary; the seven depend upon configurations, shapes, and distinctive conjunctions produced by the cause of unreal imagination; attached to name and sign; not understanding the characteristics of form that are the appearance of one's own mind; not experiencing pleasure and suffering [directly]; not being causes of liberation — produced and generating through the arising of the agitation of name and sign, having those as their causal supports. When those [consciousnesses] that have been taken up, called sense-faculties, are exhausted and cease — through the non-arising of others immediately after — for those <s>yogins</s> who are skilled in the four <s>dhyānas</s>, the truths, and liberations, who have attained the cessation of perception and feeling, who experience [only] pleasure and suffering through the conceptualization of their own minds, the conviction of liberation arises from non-operation.'

body.text: aparāvṛtte ca tathāgatagarbhaśabdasaṃśabdite ālayavijñāne nāsti saptānāṃ pravṛttivijñānānāṃ nirodhaḥ / tatkasya hetoḥ? taddhetvālambanapravṛttatvādvijñānānām, aviṣayatvācca sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhatīrthyayogayogināṃ svapudgalanairātmyāvabodhātsvasāmānyalakṣaṇaparigrahātskandhadhātvāyatanānāṃ pravartate tathāgatagarbhaḥ / pañcadharmasvabhāvadharmanairātmyadarśanānnivartate bhūmikramānusaṃdhiparāvṛttyā / nānyatīrthyamārgadṛṣṭibhirvicārayituṃ śakyate / tato 'calāyāṃ bhūmau bodhisattvabhūmau pratiṣṭhito daśasamādhisukhamukhamārgān pratilabhate / samādhibuddhaiḥ saṃdhāryamāṇo 'cintyabuddhadharmasvapraṇidhānavyavalokanatayā samādhisukhabhūtakoṭyā vinivārya pratyātmāryagatigamyaiḥ sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhatīrthakarāsādhāraṇairyogamārgairdaśāryagotramārgaṃ pratilabhate, kāyaṃ ca jñānamanomayaṃ samādhyabhisaṃskārarahitam / tasmāttarhi mahāmate tathāgatagarbhaḥ ālayavijñānasaṃśabdito viśodhayitavyo viśeṣārthibhirbodhisattvairmahāsattvaiḥ //
body.translated_text: But when the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> designated as <s>Tathāgatagarbha</s> has not been transformed, there is no cessation of the seven active consciousnesses (<s>pravṛttivijñāna</s>). For what reason? Because the consciousnesses operate having that as their causal support. And because it is beyond the domain of all <s>Śrāvaka</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, and heretical <s>yoga</s>-practitioners — from understanding their own personal selflessness, from grasping at own- and general-characteristics of the aggregates, elements, and sense-bases — the <s>Tathāgatagarbha</s> operates. From seeing the selflessness of <s>dharmas</s> according to the five <s>dharmas</s> and inherent natures, it ceases — through the transformation by the progressive connection of the stages. It cannot be examined by the views of the heretical paths. Then, established on the Immovable (<s>acalā</s>) <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage, one attains the ten gateways of <s>samādhi</s>-bliss. Sustained by the Buddhas of <s>samādhi</s>, contemplating the inconceivable <s>dharma</s> and personal vows of the Buddhas, having been held back by the limit of reality (<s>bhūtakoṭi</s>) of <s>samādhi</s>-bliss, through the paths of <s>yoga</s> reached by one's own inner noble course — uncommon with all <s>Śrāvakas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and heretical teachers — one attains the path of the ten noble lineages, and the body made of knowledge-mind, free from the constructions of <s>samādhi</s>. Therefore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the <s>Tathāgatagarbha</s> designated as <s>ālayavijñāna</s> should be purified by <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> who seek distinction.

body.text: yadi hi mahāmate ālayavijñānasaṃśabditastathāgatagarbho 'tra na syāditi asati mahāmate tathāgatagarbhe ālayavijñānasaṃśabdite na pravṛttirna nivṛttiḥ syāt / bhavati ca mahāmate pravṛttirnivṛttiśca bālāryāṇām / svapratyātmāryagatidṛṣṭadharmasukhavihāreṇa ca viharanti yogino 'nikṣiptadhurā duṣprativedhāśca / mahāmate ayaṃ tathāgatagarbhālayavijñānagocaraḥ sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhatīrthyavitarkadarśanānāṃ
body.translated_text: If, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the <s>Tathāgatagarbha</s> designated as <s>ālayavijñāna</s> did not exist here — in the absence of the <s>Tathāgatagarbha</s> designated as <s>ālayavijñāna</s>, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, there would be neither operation nor cessation. But there is, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, operation and cessation for both the childish and the noble. And <s>yogins</s> who have not set down their burden dwell with the dwelling in the bliss of the visible <s>dharma</s> of one's own inner noble self-realization, which is difficult to penetrate. O <s>Mahāmati</s>, this domain of the <s>Tathāgatagarbha</s>-<s>ālayavijñāna</s> — for all <s>Śrāvakas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and heretical thinkers and seers

body.text: prakṛtipariśuddho 'pi san aśuddha ivāgantukleśopakliṣṭatayā teṣāmābhāti na tu tathāgatānām / tathāgatānāṃ punarmahāmate karatalāmalakavatpratyakṣagocaro bhavati / etadeva mahāmate mayā śrīmālāṃ devīmadhikṛtya deśanāpāṭhe anyāṃśca sūkṣmanipuṇaviśuddhabuddhīn bodhisattvānadhiṣṭhāya tathāgatagarbha ālayavijñānasaṃśabditaḥ saptabhirvijñānaiḥ saha pravṛttyabhiniviṣṭānāṃ śrāvakāṇāṃ dharmanairātmyapradarśanārthaṃ śrīmālāṃ devīmadhiṣṭhāya tathāgataviṣayo deśito na śrāvakapratyekabuddhānyatīrthakaratarkaviṣayo 'nyatra mahāmate tathāgataviṣaya eva tathāgatagarbha ālayavijñānaviṣayastvatsadṛśānāṃ ca sūkṣmanipuṇamatibuddhiprabhedakānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāmarthapratiśaraṇānāṃ no tu yathārutadeśanāpāṭhābhiniviṣṭānāṃ sarvānyatīrthyaśrāvakapratyekabuddhānām / tasmāttarhi mahāmate tvayā anyaiśca bodhisattvairmahāsattvaiḥ sarvatathāgataviṣaye 'smiṃstathāgatagarbhālayavijñānaparijñāne yogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ / na śrutamātrasaṃtuṣṭairbhavitavyam //
body.translated_text: — though pure by nature, appears as if impure because of being defiled by adventitious afflictions (<s>āgantukleśa</s>); but [it does] not [so appear] to the <s>Tathāgatas</s>. For the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, moreover, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, it is the domain of direct perception, like a myrobalan in the palm of the hand. This very [teaching], O <s>Mahāmati</s>, I have taught in the teaching-recitation with reference to Queen <s>Śrīmālā</s>, and having empowered other <s>Bodhisattvas</s> of subtle, refined, and pure intellect — the <s>Tathāgatagarbha</s> designated as <s>ālayavijñāna</s>, together with the seven consciousnesses — for the purpose of demonstrating the selflessness of <s>dharmas</s> to <s>Śrāvakas</s> who are attached to operation. Having empowered Queen <s>Śrīmālā</s>, the domain of the <s>Tathāgata</s> has been taught — not the domain of <s>Śrāvaka</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, or heretical logical speculation. Except, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, it is the domain of the <s>Tathāgata</s> alone — the domain of the <s>Tathāgatagarbha</s>-<s>ālayavijñāna</s> is for <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> of subtle, refined, intellect-discriminating wisdom like yourself, who take refuge in the meaning, not for all heretical teachers, <s>Śrāvakas</s>, and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> who are attached to the teaching-recitation according to the letter. Therefore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, you and other <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> should practice <s>yoga</s> in this domain of all <s>Tathāgatas</s> — in the full understanding of the <s>Tathāgatagarbha</s>-<s>ālayavijñāna</s>. You should not be content with mere hearing.

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: On this, it is said:

children.translated_text: The embryo of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, conjoined with the seven consciousnesses,
operates through the grasping of duality; from full understanding, it ceases. || <s>Laṅk</s> 6.1 ||
Mind is seen like a reflection, cultivated by beginningless mental [impressions];

children.text: arthākāro na cārtho 'sti yathābhūtaṃ vipaśyataḥ // Lank_6.2 //
children.translated_text: the form of objects appears, but objects do not exist — for one who sees as it truly is. || <s>Laṅk</s> 6.2 ||

children.text: aṅgulyagraṃ yathā bālo na gṛhṇāti niśākaram /
children.translated_text: Just as a child does not grasp the moon at the tip of a finger,

children.text: tathā hyakṣarasaṃsaktastattvaṃ vetti na māmakam // Lank_6.3 //
children.translated_text: so one attached to syllables does not know my truth. || <s>Laṅk</s> 6.3 ||
Mind dances like an actor; <s>manas</s> (mentation) resembles a jester;

children.text: vijñānaṃ pañcabhiḥ sārdhaṃ dṛśyaṃ kalpeti raṅgavat // Lank_6.4 //
children.translated_text: consciousness, together with the five [sense-consciousnesses], imagines the visible like a stage. || <s>Laṅk</s> 6.4 ||

body.text: atha khalu mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ punarapi bhagavantamadhyeṣate sma - deśayatu me bhagavān, deśayatu me sugataḥ pañcadharmasvabhāvavijñānanairātmyadvayaprabhedagatilakṣaṇam, yena nairātmyadvayaprabhedagatilakṣaṇena ahaṃ ca anye ca bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ sarvabhūmikramānusaṃdhiṣvetān dharmān vibhāvayema, yathā tairdharmaiḥ sarvabuddhadharmānupraveśo bhavet / sarvabuddhadharmānupraveśācca yāvattathāgatasvapratyayātmabhūmipraveśaḥ syāditi / bhagavānāha - tena hi mahāmate śṛṇu, sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasikuru / bhāṣiṣye 'haṃ te / sādhu bhagavanniti mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavataḥ pratyaśrauṣīt / bhagavāṃstasyaitadavocat - pañcadharmasvabhāvavijñānanairātmyadvayaprabhedagatilakṣaṇaṃ te mahāmate deśayiṣyāmi / yaduta nāma nimittaṃ vikalpaḥ samyagjñānaṃ tathatā ca tathāgatapratyātmāryagatipraveśaḥ śāśvatocchedasadasaddṛṣṭivivarjito dṛṣṭadharmasukhasamāpattisukhavihāra āmukhībhavati yogayoginām / tatra mahāmate pañcadharmasvabhāvavijñānanairātmyadvayasvacittadṛśyabāhyabhāvābhāvānavabodhādvikalpaḥ pravartate bālānāṃ na tvāryāṇām //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s> once again entreated the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "May the <s>Bhagavān</s> teach me, may the <s>Sugata</s> teach me the characteristics of the classification and course of the twofold <s>nairātmya</s> (selflessness) as pertaining to the five <s>dharmas</s>, <s>svabhāvas</s> (inherent natures), <s>vijñānas</s> (consciousnesses), and the twofold <s>nairātmya</s>, so that I and other <s>Bodhisattvas</s> <s>Mahāsattvas</s>, by means of these characteristics of the classification and course of the twofold <s>nairātmya</s>, may clearly discern these <s>dharmas</s> across the successive stages of all the <s>bhūmis</s> (stages), so that through these <s>dharmas</s> there may be entry into all Buddha-<s>dharmas</s>, and through entry into all Buddha-<s>dharmas</s>, there may ultimately be entry into the <s>Tathāgata's</s> own realm of self-realization." The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "Then, <s>Mahāmati</s>, listen and attend well and carefully. I shall speak to you." "Very well, <s>Bhagavān</s>," the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s> assented to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said this to him: "I shall teach you, <s>Mahāmati</s>, the characteristics of the classification and course of the twofold <s>nairātmya</s> as pertaining to the five <s>dharmas</s>, <s>svabhāvas</s>, <s>vijñānas</s>, and the twofold <s>nairātmya</s>. That is to say: <s>nāma</s> (name), <s>nimitta</s> (sign/appearance), <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual discrimination), <s>samyagjñāna</s> (correct knowledge), and <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) — these constitute the entry into the noble realm of the <s>Tathāgata's</s> own self-realization, free from the views of eternalism and annihilationism, existence and non-existence, and become the abode of dwelling in the bliss of meditative attainment in the present life for practitioners of <s>yoga</s>. Therein, <s>Mahāmati</s>, <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual discrimination) arises for the foolish — not for the noble ones — owing to their failure to comprehend the presence or absence of external entities as mere appearances of their own mind, with respect to the five <s>dharmas</s>, <s>svabhāvas</s>, <s>vijñānas</s>, and the twofold <s>nairātmya</s>.

body.text: mahāmatirāha - kathaṃ punarbhagavan bālānāṃ vikalpaḥ pravartate, na tvāryāṇām? bhagavānāha - nāmasaṃjñāsaṃketābhiniveśena mahāmate bālāścittamanusaranti / anusaranto vividhalakṣaṇopacāreṇa ātmātmīyadṛṣṭipatitāśayā varṇapuṣkalatāmabhiniviśante / abhiniviśantaśca ajñānāvṛtāḥ saṃrajyante / saṃraktā rāgadveṣamohajaṃ karmābhisaṃskurvanti / abhisaṃskṛtya punaḥ punaḥ kośakārakīṭakā iva svavikalpapariveṣṭitamatayo gatisamudrakāntāraprapatitā ghaṭiyantravannātipravartante / na ca prajānanti mohānmāyāmarīcyudakacandrasvabhāvakalpanātmātmīyarahitān sarvadharmānabhūtavikalpoditāṃllakṣyalakṣaṇāpagatān bhaṅgotpādasthitigativinivṛttān svacittadṛśyavikalpaprabhavānīśvarakālāṇupradhānaprabhavān / nāmanimittānuplavena mahāmate bālā nimittamanusaranti //
body.translated_text: <s>Mahāmati</s> said: "How, <s>Bhagavān</s>, does <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual discrimination) operate for the foolish but not for the noble ones?" The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "Through attachment to the conventions of <s>nāma</s> (name), designation, and signs, <s>Mahāmati</s>, the foolish follow their minds. Following them, through the employment of various characteristic attributions, with inclinations fallen into the view of self and what belongs to self, they cling to the fullness of verbal expression. Clinging thus, veiled by ignorance, they become impassioned. Impassioned, they produce <s>karma</s> born of desire, aversion, and delusion. Having produced it, again and again, like silkworms in their cocoons, with minds enwrapped by their own <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual discrimination), they fall into the wilderness ocean of the realms of rebirth, and like a water-wheel, they do not cease revolving. Through delusion they do not understand that all <s>dharmas</s> are devoid of self and what belongs to self, being of the nature of illusion, mirage, and the moon reflected in water; that they arise from unreal <s>vikalpa</s>, are devoid of the characteristics of what is characterized, are free from arising, destruction, abiding, and going; that they originate from the <s>vikalpa</s> of what is seen by one's own mind — not from <s>Īśvara</s> (God), <s>kāla</s> (time), <s>aṇu</s> (atoms), or <s>pradhāna</s> (primal matter). By the current of <s>nāma</s> and <s>nimitta</s>, <s>Mahāmati</s>, the foolish follow after appearances.

body.text: tatra nimittaṃ punarmahāmate yaccakṣurvijñānasyābhāsamāgacchati rūpasaṃjñakam / evaṃ śrotraghrāṇajihvākāyamanovijñānānāṃ śabdagandharasaspraṣṭavyadharmasaṃjñakametannimittamiti vadāmi / tatra vikalpaḥ punarmahāmate yena nāma samudīrayati / nimittavyañjakamidam - evamidaṃ nānyatheti hastyaśvarathapadātistrīpuruṣādikasaṃjñakaṃ tadvikalpaḥ pravartate / samyagjñānaṃ punarmahāmate yena nāmanimittayoranupalabdhiḥ / anyonyāgantukatvādapravṛttirvijñānasya anucchedāśāśvatataḥ sarvatīrthakaraśrāvakapratyekabuddhabhūmyapātanatvātsamyagjñānamityucyate / punaraparaṃ mahāmate yena samyagjñānena bodhisattvo mahāsattvo na nāma bhāvīkaroti, na ca nimittamabhāvīkaroti / samāropāpavādāntadvayakudṛṣṭivivarjitaṃ nāmanimittārthayorapravṛttivijñānam / evametāṃ tathatāṃ vadāmi / tathatāvyavasthitaśca mahāmate bodhisattvo mahāsattvo nirābhāsagocarapratilābhitvātpramuditāṃ bodhisattvabhūmiṃ pratilabhate //
body.translated_text: Therein, <s>nimitta</s> (sign/appearance), <s>Mahāmati</s>, is what appears as an object to the eye-consciousness, designated as form. Likewise, what appears to the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousnesses, designated as sound, smell, taste, touch, and mental objects — this I call <s>nimitta</s>. Therein, <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual discrimination), <s>Mahāmati</s>, is that by which <s>nāma</s> (name) is uttered, manifesting the <s>nimitta</s> — 'this is thus, not otherwise' — designated as elephant, horse, chariot, foot-soldier, woman, man, and so forth: that is how <s>vikalpa</s> operates. <s>Samyagjñāna</s> (correct knowledge), <s>Mahāmati</s>, is that by which there is the non-apprehension of <s>nāma</s> and <s>nimitta</s>; because of their being adventitious to one another, the non-operation of <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness), free from annihilationism and eternalism, not causing descent to the stages of all <s>tīrthakara</s> (heterodox teachers), <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers), and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary awakened ones) — this is called <s>samyagjñāna</s>. Furthermore, <s>Mahāmati</s>, that <s>samyagjñāna</s> by which the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> neither reifies <s>nāma</s> nor nihilates <s>nimitta</s>, the consciousness in which there is non-operation with regard to the referents of <s>nāma</s> and <s>nimitta</s>, free from the two extreme wrong views of superimposition and denial — this I call <s>tathatā</s> (suchness). Established in <s>tathatā</s>, <s>Mahāmati</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>, by attaining the domain free from appearances (<s>nirābhāsa</s>), obtains the joyous (<s>Pramuditā</s>) <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage.

body.text: sa pratilabhya pramuditāṃ bodhisattvabhūmiṃ vyāvṛttaḥ sarvatīrthyāpāyagatibhyo bhavati lokottaradharmagatisamavasṛtaḥ lakṣaṇaparicayānmāyādipūrvakāṃ sarvadharmagatiṃ vibhāvayan svapratyātmāryadharmagatilakṣaṇaṃ tarkadṛṣṭivinivṛttakautuko 'nupūrveṇa yāvaddharmameghā bhūmiriti / dharmameghānantaraṃ yāvatsamādhibalavaśitābhijñākusumitāṃ tathāgatabhūmiṃ pratilabhate / sa pratilabhya sattvaparipācanatayā vicitrairnirmāṇakiraṇairvirājate jalacandravat / aṣṭāpadasunibaddhadharmā nānādhimuktikatayā sattvebhyo dharmaṃ deśayati / kāyaṃ manovijñaptirahitam / etanmahāmate tathatāpraveśātpratilabhante bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ //
body.translated_text: Having obtained the joyous (<s>Pramuditā</s>) <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage, he becomes turned away from all heterodox paths of miserable destinies, established in the course of supramundane <s>dharmas</s>. Through familiarity with their characteristics, discerning the course of all <s>dharmas</s> as preceded by illusion and the like, with eagerness turned away from speculative views, following the characteristics of the course of the noble <s>dharma</s> of one's own self-realization, he progresses sequentially up to the <s>Dharmameghā</s> (Cloud of Dharma) stage. After the <s>Dharmameghā</s> stage, he ultimately obtains the <s>Tathāgata</s> stage, blossoming with the powers of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), sovereignty, and <s>abhijñā</s> (superknowledge). Having obtained it, for the sake of maturing beings, he shines forth with various emanation-rays like a moon reflected in water. Established in the eightfold <s>dharma</s> arrangement, he teaches the <s>Dharma</s> to beings according to their various dispositions, with a body free from mental representation. This, <s>Mahāmati</s>, is what <s>Bodhisattvas</s> <s>Mahāsattvas</s> obtain through entry into <s>tathatā</s> (suchness).

body.text: punarapi mahāmatirāha - kiṃ punarbhagavan pañcasu dharmeṣvantargatāstrayaḥ, svabhāvā uta svalakṣaṇasiddhāḥ? bhagavānāha - atraiva mahāmate trayaḥ svabhāvā antargatāḥ, aṣṭau ca vijñānāni, dve ca nairātmye / tatra nāma ca nimittaṃ ca parikalpitaḥ svabhāvo veditavyaḥ / yaḥ punarmahāmate tadāśrayapravṛtto vikalpaścittacaittasaṃśabdito yugapatkālodita āditya iva raśmisahito vicitralakṣaṇasvabhāvo vikalpādhārakaḥ, sa mahāmate svabhāvaḥ paratantra ityucyate / samyagjñānaṃ tathatā ca mahāmate avināśatvātsvabhāvaḥ pariniṣpanno veditavyaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Mahāmati</s> further asked: "<s>Bhagavān</s>, are the three <s>svabhāvas</s> (inherent natures) included within the five <s>dharmas</s>, or are they established through their own characteristics independently?" The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "Right here, <s>Mahāmati</s>, the three <s>svabhāvas</s> are included, as well as the eight <s>vijñānas</s> (consciousnesses) and the two <s>nairātmyas</s> (selflessnesses). Therein, <s>nāma</s> (name) and <s>nimitta</s> (sign/appearance) should be understood as the <s>parikalpita svabhāva</s> (imagined nature). That <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual discrimination), <s>Mahāmati</s>, which operates dependent on those as its basis, designated as <s>citta</s> (mind) and <s>caitta</s> (mental factors), arising simultaneously like the sun together with its rays, of the nature of various characteristics, serving as the support for <s>vikalpa</s> — that, <s>Mahāmati</s>, is called the <s>paratantra svabhāva</s> (dependent nature). <s>Samyagjñāna</s> (correct knowledge) and <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), <s>Mahāmati</s>, should be understood as the <s>pariniṣpanna svabhāva</s> (perfected nature), because of their indestructibility.

body.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate svacittadṛśyamabhiniviśyamānaṃ vikalpo 'ṣṭadhā bhidyate / nimittasyābhūtalakṣaṇaparikalpitatvādātmātmīyagrāhadvayavyupaśamānnairātmyadvayamājāyate / eṣu mahāmate pañcasu dharmeṣu sarvabuddhadharmā antargatāḥ, bhūmivibhāgānusaṃdhiśca śrāvakapratyekabuddhabodhisattvānām, tathāgatānāṃ ca pratyātmāryajñānapraveśaḥ //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Mahāmati</s>, <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual discrimination), when attached to what is seen by one's own mind, divides into eight forms. Because <s>nimitta</s> (sign/appearance) is of the nature of unreal, imagined characteristics, through the cessation of the twofold grasping of self and what belongs to self, the twofold <s>nairātmya</s> (selflessness) arises. Within these five <s>dharmas</s>, <s>Mahāmati</s>, all Buddha-<s>dharmas</s> are included, as well as the classification of stages for <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers), <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary awakened ones), and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, and the entry into the noble knowledge of the <s>Tathāgatas'</s> own self-realization.

body.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate pañcadharmāḥ - nimittaṃ nāma vikalpastathatā samyagjñānaṃ ca / tatra mahāmate nimittaṃ yatsaṃsthānākṛtiviśeṣākārarūpādilakṣaṇaṃ dṛśyate tannimittam / yattasminnimitte ghaṭādisaṃjñākṛtakam - evamidaṃ nānyatheti, tannāma / yena tannāma samudīrayati nimittābhivyañjakaṃ samadharmeti vā, sa mahāmate cittacaittasaṃśabdito vikalpaḥ / yannāmanimittayoratyantānupalabdhitā buddhipralayādanyonyānanubhūtāparikalpitatvādeṣāṃ dharmāṇāṃ sā tathateti / tattvaṃ bhūtaṃ niścato niṣṭhā prakṛtiḥ svabhāvo 'nupalabdhistattathālakṣaṇam / mayā anyaiśca tathāgatairanugamya yathāvaddeśitaṃ prajñaptaṃ vivṛtamuttānīkṛtam, yatrānugamya samyagavabodhānucchedāśāśvatato vikalpasyāpravṛttiḥ svapratyātmāryajñānānukūlaṃ tīrthakarapakṣaparapakṣaśrāvakapratyekabuddhāgatilakṣaṇaṃ tatsamyagjñānam / ete ca mahāmate pañca dharmāḥ / eteṣveva trayaḥ svabhāvāḥ, aṣṭau ca vijñānāni, dve ca nairātmye, sarvabuddhadharmāścāntargatāḥ / atra te mahāmate svamatikauśalaṃ karaṇīyam, anyaiśca kārayitavyam / na parapraṇeyena bhavitavyam //
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Mahāmati</s>, the five <s>dharmas</s> are: <s>nimitta</s> (sign/appearance), <s>nāma</s> (name), <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual discrimination), <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), and <s>samyagjñāna</s> (correct knowledge). Therein, <s>Mahāmati</s>, <s>nimitta</s> is that which is seen as the characteristic of configuration, shape, distinctive form, and so forth — that is <s>nimitta</s>. That which, with respect to that <s>nimitta</s>, produces the designation of pot and so forth — 'this is thus, not otherwise' — that is <s>nāma</s>. That by which one utters that <s>nāma</s>, manifesting the <s>nimitta</s> as 'it is the same thing' or otherwise — that, <s>Mahāmati</s>, designated as <s>citta</s> (mind) and <s>caitta</s> (mental factors), is <s>vikalpa</s>. That which is the utter non-apprehension of <s>nāma</s> and <s>nimitta</s>, because they have not been mutually experienced due to the dissolution of intellection and because they are unimagined — that is <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) of these <s>dharmas</s>. Reality, truth, certainty, finality, intrinsic nature, own-being, non-apprehension — these are the characteristics of that <s>tathatā</s>. This has been taught, designated, elucidated, and made clear by me and by other <s>Tathāgatas</s>, following which, through correct comprehension, free from annihilationism and eternalism, there is the non-operation of <s>vikalpa</s>, conforming to the noble knowledge of one's own self-realization, having the characteristic of not falling into the paths of <s>tīrthakaras</s> (heterodox teachers), opponents, <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers), or <s>pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary awakened ones) — that is <s>samyagjñāna</s> (correct knowledge). These, <s>Mahāmati</s>, are the five <s>dharmas</s>. Within these very five are the three <s>svabhāvas</s> (inherent natures), the eight <s>vijñānas</s> (consciousnesses), the two <s>nairātmyas</s> (selflessnesses), and all Buddha-<s>dharmas</s> included. Herein, <s>Mahāmati</s>, you should exercise skill in your own understanding, and cause others to do the same. One should not be led by others.

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Here it is said:

children.text: pañca dharmāḥ svabhāvaśca vijñānānyaṣṭa eva ca /
children.translated_text: The five <s>dharmas</s>, the <s>svabhāvas</s> (inherent natures), and the eight <s>vijñānas</s> (consciousnesses),
The two <s>nairātmyas</s> (selflessnesses) — these constitute the entire scope of the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle). [Laṅk. 6.5]
<s>Nāma</s> (name), <s>nimitta</s> (sign/appearance), and <s>saṃkalpa</s> (conception) are the characteristics of the two [imagined and dependent] <s>svabhāvas</s>;
<s>Samyagjñāna</s> (correct knowledge) and <s>tathatva</s> (suchness) are the characteristics of the <s>pariniṣpanna</s> (perfected nature). [Laṅk. 6.6]

body.text: atha khalu mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ punarapi bhagavantametadavocat - yatpunaretaduktaṃ bhagavatā deśanāpāṭhe yathā gaṅgānadīvālukāsamāstathāgatā atītā anāgatā vartamānāśca / tatkimidaṃ bhagavan yathārutārthagrahaṇaṃ kartavyam, āhosvidanyaḥ kaścidarthāntaraviśeṣo 'stīti? taducyatāṃ bhagavan / bhagavānāha - na mahāmate yathārutārthagrahaṇaṃ kartavyam / na ca mahāmate gaṅgānadīvālukāpramāṇatayā tryadhvakabuddhapramāṇatā bhavati / tatkasya hetoḥ? yaduta lokātiśayātikrāntatvānmahāmate dṛṣṭānto 'dṛṣṭāntaḥ sadṛśāsadṛśatvāt / na ca mahāmate tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ sadṛśāsadṛśaṃ lokātiśayātikrāntaṃ dṛṣṭāntaṃ prāviṣkurvanti / anyatra upamāmātrametanmahāmate mayopanyastam, taiśca tathāgataiḥ / yathā gaṅgānadīvālukāsamāstathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā iti nityānityābhiniveśābhiniviṣṭānāṃ bālapṛthagjanānāṃ tīrthakarāśayakudṛṣṭiyuktānāṃ saṃsārabhavacakrānusāriṇāmudvejanārtham - kathamete udvignā bhavagaticakrasaṃkaṭādviśeṣārthino viśeṣamārabheranniti sulabhabuddhatvapradarśanārthaṃ na nodumbarapuṣpatulyastathāgatānāmutpāda
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s> once again said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "As for that statement made by the <s>Bhagavān</s> in the course of teaching — '<s>Tathāgatas</s> of the past, future, and present are as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>' — should this, <s>Bhagavān</s>, be taken literally, or is there some other particular meaning? Let the <s>Bhagavān</s> explain this." The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "It should not be taken literally, <s>Mahāmati</s>. Nor, <s>Mahāmati</s>, does the measure of the Buddhas of the three times correspond to the measure of the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>. Why is that? Because, <s>Mahāmati</s>, it surpasses and transcends the world — a simile that is no simile, being both similar and dissimilar. And the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones do not put forth a simile that surpasses and transcends the world as being similar or dissimilar. Rather, this was presented by me and by those <s>Tathāgatas</s> as merely a comparison — that '<s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones are as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>' — for the purpose of alarming the foolish ordinary beings who are attached to views of permanence and impermanence, who are possessed of the wrong views and inclinations of the <s>tīrthakaras</s> (heterodox teachers), who follow the wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s> and becoming — so that, being alarmed, seeking distinction from the straits of the wheel of worldly destinies, they might strive for distinction — and for the purpose of showing that Buddhahood is easily accessible, so that they would not think, 'The arising of <s>Tathāgatas</s> is as rare as the <s>udumbara</s> (fig) flower,'

body.text: iti kṛtvā vīryamārapsyante / deśanāpāṭhe tu mayā vaineyajanatāpekṣayā udumbarapuṣpasudurlabhaprādurbhāvāstathāgatā iti deśitam / na ca mahāmate udumbarapuṣpaṃ kenaciddṛṣṭapūrvaṃ na drakṣyate / tathāgatāḥ punarmahāmate loke dṛṣṭāḥ, dṛśyante caitarhi / na svanayapratyavasthānakathāmadhikṛtya udumbarapuṣpasudurlabhaprādurbhāvāstathāgatā iti / svanayapratyavasthānakathāyāṃ mahāmate nirdiśyamānāyāṃ lokātiśayātikrāntā dṛṣṭāntā yuktāḥ kriyante 'śraddheyatvāt / aśraddheyaṃ syādbālapṛthagjanānāṃ ca / svapratyātmāryajñānagocare na dṛṣṭāntā na pravartante / tattvaṃ ca tathāgatāḥ / atasteṣu dṛṣṭāntā nopanyasyante //
body.translated_text: and so generate effort. However, in the course of teaching, I have taught with regard to beings to be trained that '<s>Tathāgatas</s> are as rare in appearance as the <s>udumbara</s> flower.' But, <s>Mahāmati</s>, no one has ever seen the <s>udumbara</s> flower, nor will anyone see it. <s>Tathāgatas</s>, however, <s>Mahāmati</s>, have been seen in the world and are seen even now. It is not with reference to the teaching of establishing one's own doctrine that '<s>Tathāgatas</s> are as rare in appearance as the <s>udumbara</s> flower.' When the teaching of establishing one's own doctrine is being set forth, <s>Mahāmati</s>, similes that surpass and transcend the world are appropriately employed, because it would be incredible. And it would be incredible to the foolish ordinary beings. In the domain of the noble knowledge of one's own self-realization, similes do not apply. And the <s>Tathāgatas</s> are reality itself. Therefore, similes are not presented with regard to them.

body.text: kiṃ tu upamāmātrametanmahāmate kṛtaṃ yaduta gaṅgānadīvālukāsamāstathāgatāḥ samā na viṣamā akalpāvikalpanataḥ / tadyathā mahāmate gaṅgāyāṃ nadyāṃ vālukā mīnakacchapaśiśumāranakramahiṣasiṃhahastyādibhiḥ saṃkṣobhyamāṇā na kalpayanti na vikalpayanti - saṃkṣobhyāmahe na veti nirvikalpāḥ svacchā malavyapetāḥ / evameva mahāmate tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ svapratyātmāryajñānagaṅgāmahānadībalābhijñāvaśitāvālukāḥ sarvatīrthakarabālamīnaparapravādibhiḥ saṃkṣobhyamāṇā na kalpayanti na vikalpayanti / tathāgatapūrvapraṇihitatvātsarvasukhasamāpattiparipūryā sattvānāṃ na kalpayanti na vikalpayanti / ataste gaṅgānadīvālukāsamāstathāgatā nirviśiṣṭā anunayapratighāpagatatvāt //
body.translated_text: However, this was done merely as a comparison, <s>Mahāmati</s> — namely, '<s>Tathāgatas</s> are as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>' — equal, not unequal, because of being free from conceptualization and discrimination. Just as, <s>Mahāmati</s>, the sands in the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, though churned by fish, turtles, dolphins, crocodiles, buffaloes, lions, elephants, and the like, do not conceptualize or discriminate — 'we are being churned or not' — being free from discrimination, clear, and devoid of impurity; even so, <s>Mahāmati</s>, the sands of the great river <s>Gaṅgā</s> of the <s>Tathāgatas'</s>, <s>Arhats'</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones' own noble self-realized knowledge — the sands of their powers, <s>abhijñā</s> (superknowledge), and sovereign mastery — though churned by all the <s>tīrthakara</s> (heterodox teacher), foolish fish, and proponents of other doctrines, do not conceptualize or discriminate. Because of the prior vows of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, for the fulfillment of all blissful meditative attainments for beings, they do not conceptualize or discriminate. Therefore, the <s>Tathāgatas</s> are as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, without distinction, because of being free from attachment and aversion.

body.text: tadyathā mahāmate gaṅgāyāṃ nadyāṃ vālukā pṛthivīlakṣaṇasvabhāvatvātpṛthivī, kalpoddāhe dahyamānāpi na pṛthivīsvabhāvaṃ vijahāti / na ca mahāmate pṛthivī dahyate tejodhātupratibaddhatvādanyatra bālapṛthagjanā vitathatāpatitayā saṃtatyā dahyamānāṃ kalpayanti, na ca dahyate tadagnihetubhūtatvāt / evameva mahāmate tathāgatānāṃ dharmakāyo gaṅgānadīvālukāsamo 'vināśī / tadyathā mahāmate nadyāṃ gaṅgāyāṃ vālukā apramāṇāḥ, evameva mahāmate tathāgatānāṃ raśmyāloko 'pramāṇaḥ sattvaparipākasaṃcodanamupādāya sarvabuddhaparṣanmaṇḍaleṣu prasarpyate tathāgataiḥ / tadyathā mahāmate gaṅgāyāṃ nadyāṃ vālukā na vālukāsvabhāvāntaramārabhante, vālukāvasthā eva vālukāḥ, evameva mahāmate tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ saṃsāre na pravṛttirna nivṛttiḥ, bhavapravṛttyucchinnahetutvāt / tadyathā mahāmate gaṅgāyāṃ nadyāṃ vālukā apakṛṣṭā api na prajñāyante, prakṣiptā api na prajñāyante, mahāmate evameva tathāgatānāṃ jñānaṃ sattvaparipākayogena na kṣīyate na vardhate, aśarīratvāddharmasya / śarīravatāṃ hi mahāmate nāśo bhavati nāśarīravatām / dharmaścāśarīraḥ / tadyathā mahāmate gaṅgāyāṃ nadyāṃ vālukā niṣpīḍyamānā ghṛtatailārthibhirghṛtatailādivirahitāḥ, evameva mahāmate tathāgatāḥ sattvaduḥkhairniṣpīḍyamānā dharmadhātvīśvarapraṇidhānasukhaṃ na vijahati mahāmate mahākaruṇopetatvāt, yāvatsarvasattvā na nirvāpyante tathāgataiḥ / tadyathā mahāmate gaṅgāyāṃ nadyāṃ vālukāḥ pravāhānukūlāḥ pravahanti nānudake, evameva mahāmate tathāgatānāṃ sarvabuddhadharmadeśanā nirvāṇapravāhānukūlā saṃvartate / tena gaṅgānadīvālukāsamāstathāgatā ityucyante / nāyaṃ mahāmate gatyarthastathāgateṣu pravartate / vināśo
body.translated_text: Just as, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the sand in the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> is earth because of having the inherent nature of the characteristic of earth, and even when being burned in the conflagration at the end of a <s>kalpa</s>, does not abandon the inherent nature of earth — and indeed, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the earth is not burned, because it is bound to the fire-element; only childish ordinary beings, with a continuum fallen into unreality, conceptualize it as being burned, yet it is not burned because it is the causal basis of that fire — even so, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the <s>Dharmakāya</s> of the <s>Tathāgatas</s> is indestructible, equal to the sand of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>. Just as, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the sand in the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> is immeasurable, even so, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the radiant light of the <s>Tathāgatas</s> is immeasurable — it is sent forth by the <s>Tathāgatas</s> into all <s>Buddha</s>-assembly-circles for the purpose of urging the ripening of beings. Just as, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the sand in the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> does not begin another inherent nature of sand — sand remains just in the state of sand — even so, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, for the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, there is neither engagement in nor withdrawal from <s>saṃsāra</s>, because the cause of engagement in existence has been cut off. Just as, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the sand in the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, even when removed, is not perceived [as diminished], and even when added to, is not perceived [as increased] — even so, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the knowledge of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, through the application of ripening beings, neither diminishes nor increases, because <s>dharma</s> is bodiless. For those who have bodies, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, there is destruction, not for those without bodies. And <s>dharma</s> is bodiless. Just as, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the sand in the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, when pressed by those desiring ghee and oil, is devoid of ghee, oil, and such — even so, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, though pressed by the sufferings of beings, do not abandon the happiness of sovereignty over the <s>dharmadhātu</s> and the power of their vow, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, because of being endowed with great compassion, until all beings are led to <s>nirvāṇa</s> by the <s>Tathāgatas</s>. Just as, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the sand in the river <s>Gaṅgā</s> flows along with the current — not against the water — even so, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, all the <s>Dharma</s>-teaching of the <s>Buddhas</s> of the <s>Tathāgatas</s> turns in accordance with the current flowing toward <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Therefore the <s>Tathāgatas</s> are said to be equal to the sand of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>. This term 'going' (<s>gati</s>), O <s>Mahāmati</s>, does not apply to the <s>Tathāgatas</s>. Destruction,

body.text: mahāmate gatyartho bhavati / na ca mahāmate saṃsārasya pūrvā koṭiḥ prajñāyate / aprajñāyamānā kathaṃ gatyarthena nirdekṣyāmi? gatyartho mahāmate ucchedaḥ / na ca bālapṛthagjanāḥ saṃprajānanti //
body.translated_text: O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is the meaning of 'going.' And, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the prior limit of <s>saṃsāra</s> is not perceived. Being unperceived, how shall I indicate it by the meaning of 'going'? The meaning of 'going,' O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is annihilation. But childish ordinary beings do not fully understand this.

body.text: mahāmatirāha - tadyadi bhagavan pūrvā koṭirna prajñāyate sattvānāṃ saṃsaratām, tatkathaṃ mokṣaḥ prajñāyate prāṇinām? bhagavānāha - anādikālaprapañcadauṣṭhulyavikalpavāsanāhetuvinivṛttirmahāmate svacittadṛśyabāhyārthaparijñānādvikalpasyāśrayaparāvṛttirmahāmate mokṣo na nāśaḥ / ato nānantakathā mahāmate kiṃcitkārī bhavati / vikalpasyaiva mahāmate paryāyo 'nantakoṭiriti / na cātra vikalpādanyatkiṃcitsattvāntaramasti, adhyātmaṃ vā bahirdhā vā parīkṣyamāṇaṃ buddhyā / jñānajñeyaviviktā hi mahāmate sarvadharmāḥ / anyatra svacittavikalpāparijñānādvikalpaḥ pravartate, tadavabodhānnivartate //
body.translated_text: <s>Mahāmati</s> said: 'If, Blessed One, the prior limit is not perceived for beings transmigrating, then how is liberation perceived for living beings?' The Blessed One said: 'The cessation of the cause of the latent tendencies of proliferation since beginningless time — from the full understanding of external objects as [merely] the appearance of one's own mind — the turning-about of the support of discrimination, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is liberation, not destruction. Therefore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the talk of infinity accomplishes nothing. The synonym of discrimination itself, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is "infinite limit" (<s>anantakoṭi</s>). And there is nothing here other than discrimination — whether a being examined internally or externally by the intellect. For all <s>dharmas</s>, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, are free from knowledge and the knowable. Discrimination operates only from not fully understanding the appearance of one's own mind as conceptualization; from understanding that, it ceases.'

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Therein this is said:

children.translated_text: Those who see the Guides (<s>Vināyakas</s>) as equal to the sand of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>,

children.text: anāśagatiniṣṭhān vai te paśyanti tathāgatān // Lank_6.7 //
children.translated_text: whose end is non-destruction and non-going — they see the <s>Tathāgatas</s>. || <s>Laṅk</s> 6.7 ||
Just as the sand in the <s>Gaṅgā</s> is free from all faults,

children.text: vāhānukūlā nityāśca tathā buddhasya buddhatā // Lank_6.8 //
children.translated_text: flowing with the current and eternal — so too is the Buddhahood of the <s>Buddha</s>. || <s>Laṅk</s> 6.8 ||

body.text: atha khalu mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ punarapi bhagavantametadavocat - deśayatu bhagavān, deśayatu me sugatastathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ sarvadharmāṇāṃ kṣaṇabhaṅgaṃ bhedalakṣaṇaṃ caiṣām / tatkathaṃ bhagavan sarvadharmāḥ kṣaṇikāḥ? bhagavānāha - tena hi mahāmate śṛṇu, sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasikuru / bhāṣiṣye 'haṃ te / sādhu bhagavanniti mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavataḥ pratyaśrauṣīt / bhagavāṃstasyaitadavocat - sarvadharmāḥ sarvadharmā iti mahāmate yaduta kuśalākuśalāḥ saṃskṛtāsaṃskṛtā laukikalokottarāḥ sāvadyānavadyāḥ sāsravānāsravā upāttānupāttāḥ / saṃkṣepeṇa mahāmate pañcopādānaskandhāścittamanomanovijñānavāsanāhetukāścittamanomanovijñānavāsanāpuṣṭairbālapṛthagjanaiḥ kuśalākuśalena parikalpyante / samādhisukhasamāpattayo mahāmate dṛṣṭadharmasukhavihārabhāvena āryāṇāṃ kuśalānāsravā ityucyante / kuśalākuśalāḥ punarmahāmate yaduta aṣṭau vijñānāni / katamānyaṣṭau? yaduta tathāgatagarbha ālayavijñānasaṃśabdito mano manovijñānaṃ ca pañca ca vijñānakāyāstīrthyānuvarṇitāḥ / tatra mahāmate pañca vijñānakāyā manovijñānasahitā kuśalākuśalakṣaṇaparaṃparābhedabhinnāḥ saṃtatiprabandhanābhinnaśarīrāḥ pravartamānāḥ pravartante / pravṛtya ca vinaśyanti / svacittadṛśyānavabodhātsamanantaranirodhe 'nyadvijñānaṃ pravartate / saṃsthānākṛtiviśeṣagrāhakaṃ manovijñānaṃ pañcabhirvijñānakāyaiḥ saha saṃprayuktaṃ pravartate kṣaṇakālānavasthāyi / tatkṣaṇikamiti vadāmi / kṣaṇikaṃ punarmahāmate ālayavijñānaṃ tathāgatagarbhasaṃśabditaṃ manaḥsahitaṃ pravṛttivijñānavāsanābhiḥ kṣaṇikamanāsravavāsanābhirakṣaṇikam / na ca bālapṛthagjanā avabudhyante kṣaṇikavādābhiniviṣṭā kṣaṇikākṣaṇikatāmimāṃ sarvadharmāṇām / tadanavabodhāducchedadṛṣṭyā asaṃskṛtānapi dharmānnāśayiṣyanti /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s> again said this to the Blessed One: 'May the Blessed One teach, may the <s>Sugata</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened <s>Buddha</s>, teach me the momentary destruction (<s>kṣaṇabhaṅga</s>) of all <s>dharmas</s> and their characteristic of disintegration. How, Blessed One, are all <s>dharmas</s> momentary?' The Blessed One said: 'Then, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, listen well and attend. I shall speak to you.' 'Very well, Blessed One,' the <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s> assented to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this to him: 'All <s>dharmas</s>, all <s>dharmas</s>, O <s>Mahāmati</s> — namely, wholesome and unwholesome, conditioned and unconditioned, worldly and supramundane, blameworthy and blameless, defiled and undefiled, appropriated and unappropriated. In brief, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the five aggregates of clinging (<s>upādānaskandha</s>), caused by the impressions of mind, <s>manas</s>, <s>manovijñāna</s>, and consciousness, are conceptualized by childish ordinary beings — nourished by the impressions of mind, <s>manas</s>, <s>manovijñāna</s>, and consciousness — as wholesome and unwholesome. The meditative absorptions and attainments of bliss, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, are called wholesome and undefiled for the noble ones, because of the cultivation of the happiness of abiding in the present life. Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the wholesome and unwholesome are the eight consciousnesses (<s>vijñāna</s>). Which eight? Namely, the <s>Tathāgatagarbha</s> designated as <s>ālayavijñāna</s>, <s>manas</s>, <s>manovijñāna</s>, and the five consciousness-bodies — described also by heretical teachers. Therein, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the five consciousness-bodies, together with <s>manovijñāna</s>, being divided by the successive differentiation of the characteristics of wholesome and unwholesome, operate with undivided bodies through the continuum of the stream. Having operated, they perish. From not understanding that what is seen by one's own mind [is unreal], at the moment immediately following cessation, another consciousness operates. <s>Manovijñāna</s>, grasping the distinctions of configuration and form, operates together with the five consciousness-bodies, not enduring for even a moment. That I call momentary. Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, <s>ālayavijñāna</s>, designated as <s>Tathāgatagarbha</s>, together with <s>manas</s>, is momentary through the impressions of the operating consciousnesses, and non-momentary through undefiled impressions. Yet childish ordinary beings, attached to the doctrine of momentariness, do not understand this momentary and non-momentary nature of all <s>dharmas</s>. From not understanding that, they will destroy even unconditioned <s>dharmas</s> through the annihilationist view.

body.text:
asaṃsāriṇo mahāmate pañca vijñānakāyā ananubhūtasukhaduḥkhā anirvāṇahetavaḥ / tathāgatagarbhaḥ punarmahāmate anubhūtasukhaduḥkhahetusahitaḥ
pravartate nivartate ca catasṛbhirvāsanābhiḥ saṃmūrcchitaḥ / na ca bālā avabudhyante kṣaṇikadṛṣṭivikalpavāsitamatayaḥ //
body.translated_text: The five consciousness-bodies, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, do not transmigrate — having not experienced pleasure and pain, they are not causes of <s>nirvāṇa</s>. But the <s>Tathāgatagarbha</s>, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, together with the cause of experienced pleasure and pain, operates and ceases, conjoined with four kinds of impressions. Yet the childish do not understand, their minds being colored by the latent tendencies of the view of momentariness.

body.text: punaraparaṃ mahāmate samadhāraṇaṃ kalpasthitāḥ suvarṇavajrajinadhātuprāptiviśeṣā abhaṅginaḥ / yadi punarmahāmate abhisamayaprāptiḥ kṣaṇikā syāt, anāryatvamāryāṇāṃ syāt / na ca anāryatvamāryāṇāṃ bhavati / suvarṇaṃ vajraṃ ca mahāmate samadhāraṇaṃ kalpasthitā api tulyamānā na hīyante na vardhante / tatkathaṃ bālaiḥ kṣaṇikārthe vikalpyate ādhyātmikabāhyānāṃ sarvadharmāṇāmasaṃdhābhāṣyakuśalaiḥ?
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, gold, <s>vajra</s> (diamond), and <s>Jina</s>-relics — being of equal stability — endure for a <s>kalpa</s> and are unbreakable. If, moreover, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the attainment of realization were momentary, there would be non-nobility of the noble ones. But there is no non-nobility of the noble ones. Gold and <s>vajra</s>, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, being of equal stability and enduring for a <s>kalpa</s>, are not diminished or increased even when weighed. Then how is momentariness conceptualized by the childish regarding all inner and outer <s>dharmas</s> — [they who are] unskilled in speaking with intended purport (<s>saṃdhi</s>)?

body.text: punarapi mahāmatirāha - yatpunaretaduktaṃ bhagavatā - ṣaṭpāramitāṃ paripūrya buddhatvamavāpyata iti / tatkatamāstāḥ ṣaṭpāramitāḥ? kathaṃ ca paripūriṃ gacchanti? bhagavānāha - traya ete mahāmate pāramitābhedāḥ / katame trayaḥ? yaduta laukikalokottaralokottaratamāḥ / tatra mahāmate laukikyaḥ pāramitā ātmātmīyagrāhābhiniveśābhiniviṣṭāḥ / antadvayagrāhiṇo vicitrabhavopapattyāyatanārthaṃ rūpādiviṣayābhilāṣiṇo dānapāramitāṃ paripūrayanti / evaṃ śīlakṣāntivīryadhyānaprajñāpāramitāṃ mahāmate paripūrayanti bālāḥ / abhijñāścābhinirharanti brahmatvāya / tatra lokottarābhiḥ pāramitābhiḥ śrāvakapratyekabuddhā nirvāṇagrāhapatitāśayā dānādiṣu prayujyante yathaiva bālā ātmasukhanirvāṇābhilāṣiṇaḥ / lokottaratamāḥ punarmahāmate svacittadṛśyavikalpamātragrahaṇātsvacittadvayāvabodhādapravṛttervikalpasya upādānagrahaṇābhāvātsvacittarūpalakṣaṇānabhiniveśāddānapāramitā sarvasattvahitasukhārthamājāyate bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ paramayogayoginām / yattatraivālambane vikalpasyāpravṛttiṃ śīlayanti, tacchīlaṃ pāramitā ca sā / yā tasyaiva vikalpasyāpravṛttikṣamaṇatā grāhyagrāhakaparijñayā, sā kṣāntipāramitā / yena vīryeṇa pūrvarātrāpararātraṃ ghaṭate yogānukūladarśanādvikalpasya vyāvṛtteḥ, sā vīryapāramitā / yadvikalpanivṛttestīrthyanirvāṇagrāhāpatanaṃ sā dhyānapāramitā / tatra prajñāpāramitā yadā svacittavikalpābhāvādābuddhipravicayātprativicinvan antadvaye na patati āśrayaparāvṛttipūrvakarmavināśataḥ, svapratyātmāryagatipratilambhāya prayujyate, sā prajñāpāramitā / etā mahāmate pāramitāḥ / eṣa pāramitārthaḥ / tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Mahāmati</s> said: 'Regarding what was further said by the Blessed One — "Having fulfilled the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), Buddhahood is attained" — which are those six <s>pāramitās</s>? And how are they fulfilled?' The Blessed One said: 'There are, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, three divisions of the <s>pāramitās</s>. Which three? Namely, worldly, supramundane, and most supramundane. Therein, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the worldly <s>pāramitās</s> are attached to the clinging to self and what belongs to self. Those who grasp both extremes, desiring the sense-objects of form and so forth for the purpose of various existences and rebirths, fulfill the perfection of giving (<s>dānapāramitā</s>). Likewise, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the childish fulfill the perfections of discipline (<s>śīla</s>), patience (<s>kṣānti</s>), vigor (<s>vīrya</s>), meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>), and wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>). And they produce superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>) for the sake of [attaining] <s>Brahma</s>-hood. Therein, with the supramundane <s>pāramitās</s>, <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, with dispositions fallen into the grasping of <s>nirvāṇa</s>, apply themselves to giving and the rest — just like the childish who desire the happiness of <s>nirvāṇa</s> for their own self. But the most supramundane, O <s>Mahāmati</s> — from the understanding that what is seen by one's own mind is mere conceptual grasping, from the understanding of the duality of one's own mind, from the non-operation of discrimination because of the absence of grasping at appropriation, from non-attachment to the characteristics of the form of one's own mind — the perfection of giving arises for <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas</s> who are supreme practitioners of yoga, for the welfare and happiness of all beings. That in which they train the non-operation of discrimination with respect to that very same support — that is the perfection of discipline. That which is the capacity to endure the non-operation of that very discrimination, through the full understanding of what is grasped and the grasper — that is the perfection of patience. The vigor by which one strives in the earlier and later watches of the night, from seeing the favorableness of the turning-away of discrimination through yoga — that is the perfection of vigor. That which is the non-falling into the grasping of <s>nirvāṇa</s> of the heretics from the cessation of discrimination — that is the perfection of meditation. Therein, the perfection of wisdom — when, from the non-existence of the conceptualization of one's own mind, from the investigation up to awakening, one does not fall into both extremes through the prior destruction of <s>karma</s> [by means of] the turning-about of the support, [and] applies oneself to the attainment of one's own inner noble realization — that is the perfection of wisdom. These, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, are the <s>pāramitās</s>. This is the meaning of the <s>pāramitās</s>. Therein this is said:

children.translated_text: The childish conceptualize the conditioned as empty, impermanent, and momentary;
by the analogies of the river, lamp, and seed, the meaning of momentariness is conceptualized. || <s>Laṅk</s> 6.9 ||
Inactive, momentary, free from [elaboration], devoid of destruction —
and the non-arising of <s>dharmas</s> — [this] meaning of momentariness I declare. || <s>Laṅk</s> 6.10 ||

children.text: utpattyanantaraṃ bhaṅgaṃ na vai deśemi bāliśān /
children.translated_text: I do not teach the childish that destruction [occurs] immediately upon arising;

children.text: nairantaryeṇa bhāvānāṃ vikalpaḥ spandate gatau // Lank_6.11 //
children.translated_text: without interruption, for entities, discrimination vibrates in [their] course. || <s>Laṅk</s> 6.11 ||

children.text: sā vidyā kāraṇaṃ teṣāṃ cittānāṃ saṃpravartikam /
children.translated_text: That knowledge is the cause for the operation of those minds;

children.text: antarā kimavasthāsau yāvadrūpaṃ na jāyate // Lank_6.12 //
children.translated_text: what intermediate state is there until form arises? || <s>Laṅk</s> 6.12 ||
Immediately [upon] the destruction [of one], another mind operates;

children.text: rūpaṃ na tiṣṭhate kāle kimālambya pravartsyate // Lank_6.13 //
children.translated_text: form does not remain in time — depending on what will [the next mind] operate? || <s>Laṅk</s> 6.13 ||
Since wherever mind operates it has an unreal cause,

children.text: na prasiddhaṃ kathaṃ tasya kṣaṇabhaṅgo 'vadhāryate // Lank_6.14 //
children.translated_text: it is not established — how can momentary destruction be ascertained for it? || <s>Laṅk</s> 6.14 ||
The attainments of yogins, gold, <s>Jina</s>-relics,
and the luminous mansions — are unbreakable because of worldly causation. || <s>Laṅk</s> 6.15 ||
Enduring states, dharmas of attainment, and the wisdom-perfections of <s>Buddhas</s>,

children.text: bhikṣutvaṃ samayaprāptirdṛṣṭā vai kṣaṇikāḥ katham // Lank_6.16 //
children.translated_text: monkhood, and the attainment of [spiritual] stages — how are these seen as momentary? || <s>Laṅk</s> 6.16 ||

children.text: gandharvapuramāyādyā rūpā vai kṣaṇikā na kim /
children.translated_text: Are not the <s>Gandharva</s>-city, illusion, and other forms indeed momentary?
Both unreal and real — some real [things] are [as if] in hand. || <s>Laṅk</s> 6.17 ||

body.text: iti laṅkāvatāre kṣaṇikaparivartaḥ ṣaṣṭhaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the chapter on momentariness (<s>kṣaṇikaparivarta</s>), the sixth, in the <s>Laṅkāvatāra</s>.

body.text: START Parivarta 7
body.translated_text: START <s>Parivarta</s> 7

body.text: nairmāṇikaparivarto nāma saptamaḥ /
body.translated_text: The seventh chapter, named the chapter on emanation (<s>nairmāṇikaparivarta</s>).

body.text:
