atha khalu mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ punarapi bhagavantametadavocat - arhantaḥ punarbhagavatā vyākṛtā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau / aparinirvāṇadharmakāśca sattvāstathāgatatve / yasyāṃ ca rātrau tathāgato 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddho yasyāṃ ca rātrau parinirvṛtaḥ, etasminnantare bhagavatā ekamapyakṣaraṃ nodāhṛtaṃ na pravyāhṛtam / sadā samāhitāśca tathāgatā na vitarkayanti na vyavacārayanti / nirmāṇāni ca nirmāya taistathāgatakṛtyaṃ kurvanti / kiṃ kāraṇaṃ ca vijñānānāṃ kṣaṇaparaṃparābhedalakṣaṇaṃ nirdiśyate? vajrapāṇiśca satatasamitaṃ nityānubaddhaḥ / pūrvā ca koṭirna prajñāyate / nirvṛtiśca prajñāpyate / mārāśca mārakarmāṇi ca karmaplotayaśca / cañcāmāṇavikā sundarikā pravrājikā yathā dhautapātrādīni ca bhagavan karmāvaraṇāni dṛśyante / tatkathaṃ bhagavatā sarvākārajñatā prāptā aprahīṇairdoṣaiḥ? bhagavānāha - tena hi mahāmate śṛṇu, sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasikuru / bhāṣiṣye 'haṃ te / sādhu bhagavanniti mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavataḥ pratyaśrauṣīt / bhagavāṃstasyaitadavocat - nirupadhiśeṣaṃ nirvāṇadhātuṃ saṃdhāya bodhisattvacaryāṃ ca caritavatāṃ protsāhanārtham / santi hi mahāmate bodhisattvacaryācāriṇaḥ iha anyeṣu ca buddhakṣetreṣu / yeṣāṃ śrāvakayānanirvāṇābhilāṣasteṣāṃ śrāvakayānarucivyāvartanārthaṃ mahāyānagatiprotsāhanārthaṃ ca tannirmitaśrāvakānnirmāṇakāyairvyākaroti, na ca dharmatābuddhaiḥ / etatsaṃdhāya mahāmate śrāvakavyākaraṇaṃ nirdiṣṭam / na hi mahāmate śrāvakapratyekabuddhānāṃ kleśāvaraṇaprahāṇaviśeṣo vimuktyekarasatayā / nātra jñeyāvaraṇaprahāṇam / jñeyāvaraṇaṃ punarmahāmate dharmanairātmyadarśanaviśeṣādviśudhyate / kleśāvaraṇaṃ tu pudgalanairātmyadarśanābhyāsapūrvakaṃ prahīyate, manovijñānanivṛtteḥ / dharmāvaraṇavinirmuktiḥ punarālayavijñānavāsanāvinivṛtterviśudhyati / pūrvadharmasthititāṃ saṃdhāya apūrvacaramasya cābhāvātpūrvaprahiṇairevākṣaraistathāgato na vitarkya na vicārya dharmaṃ deśayati / saṃprajānakāritvādamuṣitasmṛtitvācca
na vitarkayati na vicārayati, caturvāsanābhūmiprahīṇatvāccyutidvayavigamātkleśajñeyāvaraṇadvayaprahāṇācca //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s> again said this to the Blessed One: '<s>Arhats</s> have been given prophecy by the Blessed One for unsurpassed perfect awakening. And beings whose nature is not to enter <s>parinirvāṇa</s> [have been prophesied] for <s>Tathāgata</s>-hood. And in the night when the <s>Tathāgata</s> attained unsurpassed perfect awakening and in the night when he entered <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, in this interval the Blessed One did not utter even a single syllable, nor did he speak. And <s>Tathāgatas</s> are always in <s>samādhi</s> — they do not engage in discursive thought or deliberation. And having created emanations, they perform the work of the <s>Tathāgata</s> through those. And for what reason is the characteristic of the moment-succession-differentiation of consciousnesses taught? And <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> constantly and perpetually follows [the Buddha]. And the prior limit is not perceived. And cessation is proclaimed. And there are <s>Māras</s> and <s>Māra</s>-deeds and intrigues of <s>karma</s>. And the deceitful youth, <s>Sundarikā</s> the wanderer, and the washing of bowls and other obstructions of <s>karma</s>, O Blessed One, are observed. How then has the Blessed One attained omniscient knowledge with faults unabandonned?' The Blessed One said: 'Then, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, listen, and attend well and thoroughly. I shall speak to you.' 'Very well, Blessed One!' — the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s> gave assent to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this to him: 'With reference to the <s>nirvāṇa</s>-element without remainder, and for the purpose of encouraging those who have practiced the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-course. For there are, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, those who practice the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-course here and in other Buddha-fields. For those who have desire for <s>nirvāṇa</s> of the <s>Śrāvaka</s> vehicle, in order to turn them away from their inclination toward the <s>Śrāvaka</s> vehicle and to encourage them toward the <s>Mahāyāna</s> path, he gives prophecy to those emanated <s>Śrāvakas</s> through emanation-bodies, but not through <s>Dharmatā</s>-Buddhas. With reference to this, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the prophecy for <s>Śrāvakas</s> has been taught. For, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, there is no distinction in the abandonment of the affliction-obstruction for <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, because liberation has a single taste. Therein there is no abandonment of the knowledge-obstruction. The knowledge-obstruction, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is purified through the distinction of seeing the selflessness of <s>dharmas</s>. The affliction-obstruction, however, is abandoned through the prior practice of seeing the selflessness of persons, from the cessation of <s>manovijñāna</s> (mind-consciousness). The liberation from the <s>dharma</s>-obstruction, moreover, is purified from the cessation of the impressions of the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> (store-consciousness). With reference to the prior stability of <s>dharma</s>, and because of the absence of a first or a last, the <s>Tathāgata</s> teaches the <s>Dharma</s> without discursive thought or deliberation, through the very syllables previously abandoned. Because of acting with full awareness and because of being one whose mindfulness is unimpaired, he does not engage in discursive thought or deliberation — because of the abandonment of the four impressions on all grounds, because of the removal of both types of falling, and because of the abandonment of both the affliction-obstruction and the knowledge-obstruction.'

body.text: sapta mahāmate manomanovijñānacakṣurvijñānādayaḥ kṣaṇikāḥ vāsanāhetutvātkuśalānāsravapakṣarahitāḥ na saṃsāriṇaḥ / tathāgatagarbhaḥ punarmahāmate saṃsarati nirvāṇasukhaduḥkhahetukaḥ / na ca bālapṛthagjanā avabudhyante śūnyatāvikṣiptamatayaḥ / nirmitanairmāṇikānāṃ mahāmate tathāgatānāṃ vajrapāṇiḥ pārśvānugato na maulānāṃ tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānām / maulo hi mahāmate tathāgataḥ sarvapramāṇendriyavinivṛttaḥ sarvabālaśrāvakapratyekabuddhatīrthyānām / dṛṣṭadharmasukhavihāriṇastamāgacchantyabhisamayadharmajñānakṣāntyā / ato vajrapāṇistānnānubadhnāti / sarve hi nirmitabuddhā na karmaprabhavāḥ / na teṣu tathāgato na cānyatra tebhyastathāgataḥ / kumbhakārālambanādiprayogeṇeva sattvakṛtyāni karoti, lakṣaṇopetaṃ ca deśayati, na tu svanayapratyavasthānakathāṃ svapratyātmāryagatigocaram / punaraparaṃ mahāmate ṣaṇṇāṃ vijñānakāyānāṃ nirodhāducchedadṛṣṭimāśrayanti
body.translated_text: 'The seven — <s>manas</s> (mentation), <s>manovijñāna</s> (mind-consciousness), and the eye-consciousness and others, O <s>Mahāmati</s> — are momentary, because they are causes of impressions, devoid of the wholesome and the undefiled class, and are not the transmigrators. The <s>Tathāgatagarbha</s>, moreover, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, transmigrates, being the cause of <s>nirvāṇa</s>, pleasure, and suffering. But the childish ordinary persons do not understand, their minds being distracted by emptiness. <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, follows alongside the emanated <s>Tathāgatas</s>, not the original <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones. For the original <s>Tathāgata</s>, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is free from all measure-faculties, [beyond] all childish <s>Śrāvakas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and heretical teachers. Those who dwell in the bliss of the visible <s>dharma</s> approach him through the realization-<s>dharma</s>-knowledge-patience. Therefore <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> does not follow them. For all emanated Buddhas are not born from <s>karma</s>. The <s>Tathāgata</s> is not in them, nor is the <s>Tathāgata</s> elsewhere than them. Like the contrivance of a potter's wheel or a loom, he performs the works for beings, and teaches with the marks — but does not discourse on his own method of personal realization, the domain of one's own inner noble course. Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, from the cessation of the six consciousness-groups, the childish ordinary persons

body.text: bālapṛthagjanāḥ, ālayānavabodhācchāśvatadṛṣṭayo bhavanti / svamativikalpasya mahāmate pūrvā koṭirna prajñāyate / svamativikalpasyaiva vinivṛttermokṣaḥ prajñāyate / caturvāsanāprahāṇātsarvadoṣaprahāṇam //
body.translated_text: resort to the annihilationist view, and because of not understanding the <s>ālaya</s> (store-consciousness), they hold the eternalist view. The prior limit of one's own mental conceptualization, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is not perceived. From the very cessation of one's own mental conceptualization, liberation is perceived. From the abandonment of the four impressions, there is the abandonment of all faults.'

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: On this, it is said:

children.text: trīṇi yānānyayānaṃ ca buddhānāṃ nāsti nirvṛtiḥ /
children.translated_text: Three vehicles, a non-vehicle — for the Buddhas there is no cessation;

children.text: buddhatve vyākṛtāḥ sarve vītadeṣāśca deśitāḥ // Lank_7.1 //
children.translated_text: all are prophesied for Buddhahood and are taught as freed from faults. || <s>Laṅk</s> 7.1 ||
The knowledge near realization, and likewise the attainment without remainder,
and the encouragement of the disheartened — this has been taught for the assembly. || <s>Laṅk</s> 7.2 ||
The knowledge produced by the Buddhas — the path has been taught by them alone;

children.text: yānti tenaiva nānyena atasteṣāṃ na nirvṛtiḥ // Lank_7.3 //
children.translated_text: they go by that [path] and not by another — therefore for them there is no cessation. || <s>Laṅk</s> 7.3 ||
The impressions of [the three] existences — desire, form, and views — are fourfold,
born from <s>manovijñāna</s> (mind-consciousness), and established in the <s>ālaya</s> (store-consciousness) and <s>manas</s> (mentation). || <s>Laṅk</s> 7.4 ||
Through <s>manovijñāna</s>, the eye-consciousness, and the others, there is both annihilation and impermanence;
and permanence through the beginningless — this is the <s>nirvāṇa</s> of those with excessive views. || <s>Laṅk</s> 7.5 ||

body.text: iti laṅkāvatārasūtre nairmāṇikaparivartaḥ saptamaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the seventh chapter, the Chapter on Emanation (<s>nairmāṇika</s>), in the <s>Laṅkāvatāra Sūtra</s>.

body.text: START Parivarta 8
body.translated_text: Beginning of Chapter 8.

body.text: māṃsabhakṣaṇaparivarto nāmāṣṭamaḥ /
body.translated_text: The eighth [chapter], named the Chapter on Meat-Eating.

body.text: atha khalu mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantaṃ gāthābhiḥ paripṛcchaya punarapyadhyeṣate sma - deśayatu me bhagavāṃstathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho māṃsabhakṣaṇe guṇadoṣam, yena ahaṃ ca anye ca bodhisattvā mahāsattvā anāgatapratyutpannakāle sattvānāṃ kravyādasattvagativāsanāvāsitānāṃ māṃsabhojagṛddhāṇāṃ rasatṛṣṇāprahāṇāya dharmaṃ deśayāma, yathā ca te kravyādabhojinaḥ sattvā virāgya rasatṛṣṇāṃ dharmarasāhārakāṅkṣayā sarvasattvaikaputrakapremānugatāḥ parasparaṃ mahāmaitrīṃ pratilabheran / pratilabhya sarvabodhisattvabhūmiṣu kṛtayogyāḥ kṣipramanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeran / śrāvakapratyekabuddhabhūmyā vā viśramya anuttarāṃ tāthāgatīṃ bhūmimupasarpayeyuḥ / durākhyātadharmairapi tāvadbhagavannanyatīrthikairlokāyatadṛṣṭyabhiniviṣṭaiḥ sadasatpakṣocchedaśāśvatavādibhirmāsaṃ nivāryate bhakṣyamāṇam / svayaṃ ca na bhakṣyate, prāgeva kṛpaikarase samyaksaṃbuddhe praṇīte lokanāthe / tava śāsane māṃsaṃ svayaṃ ca bhakṣyate, bhakṣyamāṇaṃ ca na nivāryate / tatsādhu bhagavān sarvalokānukampakaḥ sarvasattvaiputrakasamadarśī mahākāruṇiko 'nukampāmupādāya māṃsabhakṣaṇe guṇadeṣān deśayatu me, yathā ahaṃ ca anye ca bodhisattvāstathatvāya sattvebhyo dharmaṃ deśayema / bhagavānāha - tena hi mahāmate śṛṇu, sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasikuru / bhāṣiṣye 'haṃ te / sādhu bhagavanniti mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavataḥ pratyaśrauṣīt //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s>, having questioned the Blessed One with verses, further entreated him: 'May the Blessed One, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, teach me the merits and faults in meat-eating, so that I and other <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> may teach the <s>Dharma</s> to beings in the future and present ages — those perfumed by the impressions of the destiny of flesh-eating beings, those who are greedy for meat-eating — for the abandonment of their craving for taste, and so that those flesh-eating beings, having become dispassionate toward taste-craving, with longing for the nourishment of the taste of <s>Dharma</s>, endowed with the love of an only child toward all beings, having cultivated great <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) toward one another, may obtain [it]. Having obtained it, with accomplished skill on all <s>Bodhisattva</s> stages, they would quickly attain unsurpassed perfect awakening. Or having rested on the <s>Śrāvaka</s>-<s>Pratyekabuddha</s> stage, they would approach the unsurpassed stage of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. O Blessed One, even by those whose teachings are poorly proclaimed — the other heretical teachers devoted to <s>Lokāyata</s> views, who hold both existence-and-nonexistence, annihilationism and eternalism — meat being eaten is not prohibited. How much less so in the case of the well-proclaimed Perfectly Awakened One who has the sole taste of compassion, the Lord of the World! In your teaching, meat is both eaten by oneself and eating by others is not prohibited. Therefore, O Blessed One, you who have compassion for the whole world, who see all beings as an only child, who are the great compassionate one — out of consideration, please teach me the merits and faults in meat-eating, so that I and other <s>Bodhisattvas</s> may teach the <s>Dharma</s> to beings for their suchness.' The Blessed One said: 'Then, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, listen, and attend well and thoroughly. I shall speak to you.' 'Very well, Blessed One!' — the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s> gave assent to the Blessed One.

body.text: bhagavāṃstasyaitadavocat - aparimitairmahāmate kāraṇairmāṃsaṃ sarvamabhakṣyaṃ kṛpātmano bodhisattvasya / tebhyastūpadeśamātraṃ vakṣyāmi / iha mahāmate anena dīrgheṇādhvanā saṃsaratāṃ prāṇināṃ nāstyasau kaścitsattvaḥ sulabharūpo yo na mātābhūtpitā vā bhrātā vā bhaginī vā putro vā duhitā vā anyatarānyataro vā svajanabandhubandhūbhūto vā / tasya anyajanmaparivṛttāśrayasya mṛgapaśupakṣiyonyantarbhūtasya bandhorbandhubhūtasya vā sarvabhūtātmabhūtānupāgantukāmena sarvajantuprāṇibhūtasaṃbhūtaṃ māṃsaṃ kathamiva bhakṣyaṃ syādbuddhadharmakāmena bodhisattvena mahāsattvena? rākṣasasyāpi mahāmate tathāgatānāmimāṃ dharmasudharmatāmupaśrutya upagatarakṣabhāvāḥ kṛpālavā bhavanti māṃsabhakṣaṇavinivṛttāḥ, kimuta dharmakāmā janāḥ / evaṃ tāvanmahāmate teṣu teṣu jātiparivarteṣu sarvasattvāḥ svajanabandhubhāvasaṃjñāḥ sarvasattvaikaputrakasaṃjñābhāvanārthaṃ māṃsaṃ sarvamabhakṣyam / kṛpātmano bodhisattvasyābhakṣyaṃ māṃsam / vyabhicārādapi mahāmate māṃsaṃ sarvamabhakṣyaṃ cāritravato bodhisattvasya / śvakharoṣṭrāśvabalīvardamānuṣamāṃsādīni hi mahāmate lokasyābhakṣyāṇi māṃsāni / tāni ca mahāmate vīthyantareṣvaurabhrikā bhakṣyāṇīti kṛtvā mūlyahetorvikrīyante yataḥ, tato 'pi mahāmate māṃsamabhakṣyaṃ bodhisattvasya //
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said this to him: 'For innumerable reasons, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, all meat is not to be eaten by a <s>Bodhisattva</s> whose nature is compassion. From those [reasons] I shall give merely an indication. Here, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, for beings who have transmigrated through this long course, there is no being, hard to find, who has not been one's mother or father, brother or sister, son or daughter, or one or another relative or family-connection. For that being, having changed its support in another birth, having entered the womb of a deer, domestic animal, or bird — as a relative of one's relative, and as one who is in essence all beings — wishing to approach, how could meat produced from all creatures, living beings, and existents be edible for a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> who desires the Buddha-<s>Dharma</s>? Even a <s>Rākṣasa</s>, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, having heard this excellent <s>Dharma</s> of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, having attained the state of a guardian, becomes compassionate and refrains from meat-eating — how much more so those who desire the <s>Dharma</s>! Thus, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, in all those various cycles of birth, all beings are to be regarded with the perception of being one's own kin and relatives, and for the purpose of cultivating the perception of an only child toward all beings, all meat is not to be eaten. For a <s>Bodhisattva</s> whose nature is compassion, meat is not to be eaten. Even from transgression, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, all meat is not to be eaten by a <s>Bodhisattva</s> of good conduct. For dog, camel, donkey, horse, ox, and human meats, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, are meats not to be eaten by people in the world. But, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, butchers in the alleyways sell them as edible for the sake of profit — therefore too, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, meat is not to be eaten by a <s>Bodhisattva</s>.'

body.text: śukraśoṇitasaṃbhavādapi mahāmate śucikāmatāmupādāya bodhisattvasya māṃsamabhakṣyam / udvejanakaratvādapi mahāmate bhūtānāṃ maitrīmicchato yogino māṃsaṃ sarvamabhakṣyaṃ bodhisattvasya /
body.translated_text: 'Even because of being born from blood and semen, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, out of desire for purity, meat is not to be eaten by a <s>Bodhisattva</s>. Even because of causing alarm to beings, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, for a <s>yogin</s> who desires <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), all meat is not to be eaten by a <s>Bodhisattva</s>.

body.text: tadyathāpi mahāmate ḍombacāṇḍālakaivartādīn piśitāśinaḥ sattvān dūrata eva dṛṣṭvā śvānaḥ prabhayanti bhayena, maraṇaprāptāścaike bhavanti - asmānapi mārayiṣyantīti / evameva mahāmate anye 'pi khabhūjalasaṃniśritān sūkṣmajantavo ye māṃsāśino darśanāddūrādeva paṭunā ghrāṇenāghrāya gandhaṃ rākṣasasyeva mānuṣā drutamapasarpanti, maraṇasaṃdehāścaike bhavanti / tasmādapi ca mahāmate udvejanakaratvānmahāmaitrīvihāriṇo yogino māṃsamabhakṣyaṃ bodhisattvasya anāryajanajuṣṭaṃ durgandham / akīrtikaratvādapi mahāmate āryajanavivarjitatvācca māṃsamabhakṣyaṃ bodhisattvasya / ṛṣibhojanāhāro hi mahāmate āryajano na māṃsarudhirāhāraḥ, ityato 'pi bodhisattvasya māṃsamabhakṣyam //
body.translated_text: Just as, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, dogs tremble with fear from a distance upon seeing flesh-eating beings such as <s>Ḍombas</s>, <s>Caṇḍālas</s>, fishermen, and the like, and some even reach the point of death [thinking] "they will kill us too" — in the same way, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, even other minute creatures dwelling in sky, ground, and water, smelling the odor of meat-eaters from afar with their keen sense of smell, flee quickly like humans [fleeing] from a <s>Rākṣasa</s>, and some become doubtful of death. Therefore too, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, because of causing alarm, for a <s>yogin</s> dwelling in great <s>maitrī</s>, meat is not to be eaten by a <s>Bodhisattva</s> — being frequented by ignoble persons. Even because of causing ill-repute, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, and because of being avoided by noble persons, meat is not to be eaten by a <s>Bodhisattva</s>. For the food and nourishment of noble persons, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is that of <s>ṛṣis</s> (sages) — not the nourishment of meat and blood; therefore too, meat is not to be eaten by a <s>Bodhisattva</s>.'

body.text: bahujanacittānurakṣaṇatayāpi apavādaparihāraṃ cecchataḥ śāsanasya mahāmate māṃsamabhakṣyaṃ kṛpātmano bodhisattvasya / tadyathā mahāmate bhavanti loke śāsanāpavādavaktāraḥ / kiṃcitteṣāṃ śrāmaṇyam, kuto vā brāhmaṇyam? yannāmaite pūrvarṣibhojanānyapāsya kravyādā ivāmiṣāhārāḥ paripūrṇakukṣayaḥ khabhūmijalasaṃniśritān sūkṣmāṃstrāsayanto jantūn samutrāsayanta imaṃ lokaṃ samantataḥ paryaṭanti / nihatameṣāṃ śrāmaṇyam, dhvastameṣāṃ brāhmaṇyam, nāstyeṣāṃ dharmo na vinayaḥ, ityanekaprakārapratihatacetasaḥ śāsanamevāpavadanti / tasmādbahujanacittānurakṣaṇatayāpi apavādaparihāraṃ cecchataḥ śāsanasya mahāmate māṃsaṃṃ sarvamabhakṣyaṃ kṛpātmano bodhisattvasya //
body.translated_text: 'Even for the purpose of guarding the minds of many people and wishing to avoid reproach against the teaching, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, meat is not to be eaten by a <s>Bodhisattva</s> whose nature is compassion. Consider, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, there are in the world those who speak reproach against the teaching: "What kind of asceticism is theirs, and where is their brahminhood? — these who, having set aside the foods of the ancient <s>ṛṣis</s> (sages), like flesh-eaters, nourished on meat, with full bellies, terrifying the minute creatures dwelling in sky, ground, and water, causing them fear, roam throughout this world on all sides. Their asceticism is slain, their brahminhood is destroyed — they have no <s>Dharma</s>, no <s>Vinaya</s>." With minds obstructed in many such ways, they reproach the very teaching. Therefore, even for the purpose of guarding the minds of many people and wishing to avoid reproach against the teaching, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, all meat is not to be eaten by a <s>Bodhisattva</s> whose nature is compassion.'

body.text: mṛtaśavadurgandhapratikūlasāmānyādapi mahāmate māṃsamabhakṣyaṃ bodhisattvasya / mṛtasyāpi hi mahāmate manuṣyasya māṃse dahyamāne tadanyaprāṇimāṃse ca, na kaścidgandhaviśeṣaḥ / samamubhayamāṃsayordahyamānayordaurgandhyam / ato 'pi mahāmate śucikāmasya yoginaḥ sarvaṃ māṃsamabhakṣyaṃ bodhisattvasya //
body.translated_text: Also because of the general similarity [of its] offensive odor to that of a dead corpse, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, meat is not to be eaten by a <s>Bodhisattva</s>. For even when a dead human's flesh, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, is being burned, and the flesh of other living creatures [is being burned], there is no difference in smell. The foul smell of both kinds of flesh when burning is the same. Therefore too, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, for a <s>yogin</s> who desires purity, all meat is not to be eaten by a <s>Bodhisattva</s>.

body.text: śmaśānikānāṃ ca mahāmate araṇyavanaprasthānyamanuṣyāvacarāṇi prāntāni śayanāsanānyadhyāvasatāṃ yogināṃ yogācārāṇāṃ maitrīvihāriṇāṃ vidyādharāṇāṃ vidyāṃ sādhayitukāmānāṃ vidyāsādhanamokṣavighnakaratvānmahāyānasaṃprasthitānāṃ kulaputrāṇāṃ kuladuhitṝṇāṃ ca sarvayogasādhanāntarāyakaramityapi samanupaśyatāṃ mahāmate svaparātmahitakāmasya māṃsaṃ sarvamabhakṣyaṃ bodhisattvasya / rūpālambanavijñānapratyayāsvādajanakatvādapi sarvabhūtātmabhūtasya kṛpātmanaḥ sarvaṃ māṃsamabhakṣyaṃ bodhisattvasya / devatā api cainaṃ parivarjayantīti kṛtvā mahāmate kṛpātmanaḥ sarvaṃ māṃsamabhakṣyaṃ bodhisattvasya / mukhaṃ cāsya paramadurgandhi ihaiva tāvajjanmani, ityapi kṛtvā mahāmate kṛpātmanaḥ sarvaṃ māṃsamabhakṣyaṃ bodhisattvasya / duḥkhaṃ svapiti, duḥkhaṃ pratibudhyate / pāpakāṃśca romaharṣaṇān svapnān paśyanti / śūnyāgārasthitasya caikākino rahogatasya viharato 'syāmanuṣyāstejo haranti / utrasyantyapi, kadācitsaṃtrasyantyapi, saṃtrāsamakasmāccāpadyante, āhāre ca mātrāṃ na jānāti nāpyaśitapītakhāditākhāditasya samyagrasapariṇāmapuṣṭyādi samāsādayati, krimijantupracurakuṣṭhanidānakoṣṭhaśca bhavati vyādhibahulam, na ca pratikūlasaṃjñāṃ pratilabhate /
body.translated_text: For <s>yogins</s> dwelling in cremation grounds, O <s>Mahāmati</s> — those practicing <s>yoga</s> in remote, solitary resting places in forests and wilderness areas frequented by non-human beings, dwelling in loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>), practitioners of <s>vidyā</s> (sacred knowledge), wishing to accomplish their <s>vidyā</s> practice — because [meat-eating] obstructs the accomplishment of <s>vidyā</s> and liberation; for sons and daughters of good families who have set forth in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> — seeing that it causes obstacles to all <s>yoga</s>-practices, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, for one who desires the welfare of self and others — all meat is not to be eaten by a <s>Bodhisattva</s>. Because [meat-eating] produces relish for consciousness conditioned by form-object, for one who is the self of all beings, who has compassion as his nature — all meat is not to be eaten by a <s>Bodhisattva</s>. Because even the deities shun him, O <s>Mahāmati</s> — for one of compassionate nature, all meat is not to be eaten by a <s>Bodhisattva</s>. Because his mouth becomes extremely foul-smelling even in this very birth, O <s>Mahāmati</s> — for one of compassionate nature, all meat is not to be eaten by a <s>Bodhisattva</s>. He sleeps in suffering, awakens in suffering. He sees evil and hair-raising dreams. When dwelling alone in an empty dwelling in solitude, non-human beings steal his vitality. He is also frightened, sometimes terrified, and suddenly experiences terror. He does not know measure in food, nor does one who has eaten, drunk, chewed, and tasted properly obtain nourishment from the full transformation of flavor, and so forth. His bowels become full of worms and parasites, the source of leprosy, and full of diseases. And he does not attain the perception of what is repulsive.

body.text: putramāṃsabhaiṣajyavadāhāraṃ deśayaṃścāhaṃ mahāmate kathamiva anāryajanasevitamāryajanavivarjitamevamanekadoṣāvahamanekaguṇavivarjitamanṛṣibhojanapraṇītamakalpyaṃ māṃsarudhirāhāraṃ śiṣyebhyo 'nujñāpyāmi?
body.translated_text: Teaching food as [something to be viewed] like medicine or the flesh of one's own child, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, how could I approve for my disciples the eating of meat and blood — improper food, consumed by ignoble people, shunned by noble people, bringing many faults, devoid of many virtues, and not proclaimed by the sages?

body.text: anujñātavān punarahaṃ mahāmate sarvāryajanasevitamanāryajanavivarjitamanekaguṇavāhakamanekadoṣavivarjitaṃ sarvapūrvarṣipraṇītaṃ bhojanam, yaduta śāliyavagodhūmamudgamāṣamasūrādisarpistailamadhuphāṇitaguḍakhaṇḍamatsyaṇḍikādiṣu samupapadyamānaṃ bhojanaṃ kalpyamiti kṛtvā / na ca mahāmate anāgate 'dhvani ekeṣāṃ mohapuruṣāṇāṃ vividhavinayavikalpavādināṃ kravyādakulavāsitāvāsitānāṃ rasatṛṣṇāvyavasitānāmidaṃ praṇītaṃ bhojanaṃ pratibhāṣyate / na tu mahāmate pūrvajinakṛtādhikārāṇāmavaropitakuśalamūlānāṃ śrāddhānāmavikalpānāṃ bahulānāṃ śākyakulakulīnānāṃ kulaputrāṇāṃ kuladuhitṝṇāṃ kāyajīvitabhogānadhyavasitānāmarasagṛdhrāṇāmalolupānāṃ kṛpālūnāṃ sarvabhūtātmabhūtatāmupagantukāmānāṃ sarvasattvaikaputrakapriyadarśināṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānamiti vadāmi //
body.translated_text: Rather, I have approved food that is consumed by all noble people, shunned by ignoble people, bringing many virtues, free from many faults, and proclaimed by all former sages — food that comes from rice, barley, wheat, green gram, black gram, lentils, and the like, and from ghee, oil, honey, sugar, jaggery, sugar candy, treacle, and so forth — as proper food. And, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, in the future time, this wholesome food will not be acceptable to certain deluded persons who propound various interpretations of the <s>Vinaya</s>, who are perfumed by the habits of meat-eating families, who are addicted to the craving for taste. But I say this, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, not for such [people], but for <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> — sons and daughters of good families of the <s>Śākya</s> lineage who have performed obligations to former <s>Jinas</s>, who have planted roots of merit, who are faithful, non-discriminating, abundant, who are not addicted to body, life, and enjoyment, who are not greedy for flavor, who are not covetous, who are compassionate, who wish to become the self of all beings, who see all beings as [their] only child, [seeing each one as] dear.

body.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ mahāmate atīte 'dhvani rājābhūtsiṃhasaudāso nāma / sa māṃsabhojanāhārātiprasaṅgena pratisevamāno rasatṛṣṇādhyavasānaparamatayā māṃsāni mānuṣyāṇyapi bhakṣitavān / tannidānaṃ ca mitrāmātyajñātibandhuvargeṇāpi parityaktaḥ, prāgeva paurajānapadaiḥ / svarājyaviṣayaparityāgācca mahadvayasanamāsāditavān māṃsahetoḥ //
body.translated_text: Once upon a time, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, in a past era, there was a king named <s>Siṃhasaudāsa</s>. Through excessive addiction to the eating of meat, being driven by the addiction to taste-craving, he even ate human flesh. Because of that, he was abandoned even by his circle of friends, ministers, relatives, and kinsmen — let alone the townspeople and countryfolk. And from the loss of his kingdom and territory, he suffered great distress because of meat.

body.text: indreṇāpi ca mahāmate devādhipatyaṃ prāptena (pūrvābhūtvā) pūrvajanmamāṃsādavāsanādoṣācchyenarūpamāsthāya kapotaveṣarūpadhārī viśvakarmā samabhidruto 'bhūt / tulāyāṃ cātmānamāropita āsīt / yasmādrājā anaparādhibhūtānukampakaḥ śibī duḥkhena mahatā lambhitaḥ / tadevamanekajanmābhyastamapi mahāmate devendrabhūtasya śakrasyāpi sataḥ svaparadoṣāvahanamabhūt, prāgeva tadanyeṣām //
body.translated_text: Even <s>Indra</s>, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, having attained lordship over the gods — (having previously been [in another form]) — through the fault of the impressions of meat-eating in a former birth, assuming the form of a hawk, pursued <s>Viśvakarman</s> who had assumed the form of a pigeon. And he placed himself on a scale. Because king <s>Śibi</s>, who was compassionate toward the innocent, was made to suffer greatly. Thus even for <s>Śakra</s>, who had become lord of the gods, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, though [the habit] had been practiced in many births, it brought harm to self and others — how much more so for others.

body.text: anyeṣāṃ ca mahāmate narendrabhūtānāṃ satāmaśvenāpahṛtānāmaṭavyāṃ paryaṭamānānāṃ siṃhyā saha maithunaṃ gatavatāṃ jīvitabhayādapatyāni cotpāditavantaḥ siṃhasaṃvāsānvayātkalmāṣapādaprabhṛtayo nṛpaputrāḥ pūrvajanmamāṃsādadoṣavāsanatayā manuṣyendrabhūtā api santo māṃsādā abhūvan / ihaiva ca mahāmate janmani saptakuṭīrake 'pi grāme pracuramāṃsalaulyādatiprasaṅgena niṣevamānā mānuṣamāṃsādā ghorā ḍākā vā ḍākinyaśca saṃjāyante / jātiparivarte ca mahāmate tathaiva māṃsarasādhyavasānatayā siṃhavyāghradvīpivṛkatarakṣumārjārajambukolūkādipracuramāṃsādayoniṣu pracuratarapiśitāśanā rākṣasādighoratarayoniṣu vinipātyante / yatra vinipatitānāṃ duḥkhena mānuṣyayonirapi samāpadyate, prāgave nirvṛtiḥ / ityevamādayo mahāmate māṃsādadoṣāḥ prāgeva niṣevamānānāṃ samupajāyante, viparyayācca bhūyāṃso guṇāḥ / na ca mahāmate bālapṛthagjanā
body.translated_text: Other [princes], O <s>Mahāmati</s>, who had been kings, having been carried off by a horse, wandering in the wilderness, having mated with a lioness out of fear for their lives, and having produced offspring — princes such as <s>Kalmāṣapāda</s> and others, from the lineage of cohabitation with a lioness — through the impressions of the fault of meat-eating in former births, even though they had become lords of men, they became meat-eaters. Even here in this birth, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, in the village of the seven huts, through excessive indulgence in abundant meat-craving, they become terrible cannibals — <s>ḍākas</s> (male demons) or <s>ḍākinīs</s> (female demons). And in the turning of births, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, likewise through addiction to the taste of meat, they fall into the wombs of abundant meat-eaters — lions, tigers, leopards, wolves, hyenas, cats, owls, and the like — and into even more terrible wombs such as <s>Rākṣasas</s> and others, consuming excessive amounts of flesh. Having fallen there, even a human birth is [attained only] with difficulty, let alone liberation. Such and more, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, are the faults of meat-eating that arise [even] before one actually indulges; and from the opposite, the virtues are greater. But childish ordinary persons, O <s>Mahāmati</s>,

body.text: etāṃścānyāṃśca guṇadoṣānavabudhyante / evamādiguṇadoṣadarśanānmahāmate māṃsaṃ sarvamabhakṣyaṃ kṛpātmano bodhisattvasyeti vadāmi //
body.translated_text: do not understand these and other virtues and faults. From seeing such virtues and faults, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, I say that all meat is not to be eaten by a <s>Bodhisattva</s> of compassionate nature.

body.text: yadi ca mahāmate māṃsaṃ na kathaṃcana kecana bhakṣayeyuḥ, na tannidānaṃ ghāteran / mūlyahetorhi mahāmate prāyaḥ prāṇino niraparādhino vadhyante svalpādanyahetoḥ / kaṣṭaṃ mahāmate rasatṛṣṇāyāmatisevatāṃ māṃsāni mānuṣānyapi mānuṣairbhakṣyante, kiṃ punaritaramṛgapakṣiprāṇisaṃbhūtamāṃsāni / prāyo mahāmate māṃsarasatṛṣṇārtairidaṃ tathā tathā jālayantramāviddhaṃ mohapuruṣaiḥ, yacchākunikaurabhrakakaivartādayaḥ khecarabhūcarajalacarān prāṇino 'naparādhino 'nekaprakāraṃ mūlyahetorviśasanti / na caiṣāṃ mahāmate kiṃkanīkṛtarūkṣacetasāṃ rākṣasānāmiva gataghṛṇānāṃ kadācidapi prāṇiṣu prāṇisaṃjñayā ghātayatāṃ bhakṣayatāṃ na ghṛṇotpadyate //
body.translated_text: If, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, no one whatsoever were to eat meat, they would not kill for that reason. For the most part, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, innocent living beings are killed for the sake of their price — rarely for any other reason. Alas, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, for those addicted to the craving for the taste [of meat], even human flesh is eaten by humans — how much more the flesh produced from deer, birds, and [other] living creatures. For the most part, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, this [situation] — in which fowlers, sheep-dealers, fishermen, and others slaughter innocent creatures of sky, land, and water in various ways for the sake of their price — is thus trapped and pierced by deluded persons craving the taste of meat. And for these people, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, who are as harsh and pitiless as <s>Rākṣasas</s>, who have lost all compassion, killing and eating living beings with the perception of them as living beings — no compassion ever arises.

body.text: na ca mahāmate akṛtakamakāritamasaṃkalpitaṃ nāma māṃsaṃ kalpyamasti yadupādāya anujānīyāṃ śrāvakebhyaḥ / bhaviṣyanti tu punarmahāmate anāgate 'dhvani mamaiva śāsane pravrajitvā śākyaputrīyatvaṃ pratijānānāḥ kāṣāyadhvajadhāriṇo mohapuruṣā mithyāvitarkopahatacetaso vividhavinayavikalpavādinaḥ satkāyadṛṣṭiyuktā rasatṛṣṇādhyavasitāstāṃ tāṃ māṃsabhakṣaṇahetvābhāsāṃ granthayiṣyanti / mama cābhūtābhyākhyānaṃ dātavyaṃ maṃsyante / tattadarthotpattinidānaṃ kalpayitvā vakṣyanti - iyamarthotpattirasminnidāne, bhagavatā māṃsabhojanamanujñātaṃ kalpyamiti / praṇītabhojaneṣu coktam, svayaṃ ca kila tathāgatena paribhuktamiti / na ca mahāmate kutracitsūtre pratisevitavyamityanujñātam, praṇītabhojaneṣu vā deśitaṃ kalpyamiti //
body.translated_text: There is no such thing, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, as meat that is 'not killed, not caused to be killed, and not intended' — proper [meat] on account of which I would approve [it] for <s>Śrāvakas</s>. But there will be, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, in the future time, deluded persons who, having gone forth in my very teaching, claiming to be sons of <s>Śākya</s>, bearing the banner of the saffron robe, whose minds are corrupted by false reasoning, who propound various interpretations of the <s>Vinaya</s>, who hold the view of the self-existing body, who are addicted to taste-craving — they will compose those various pretexts for meat-eating. And they will think they should create a false account about me. Having fabricated the occasion and context of various meanings, they will say: 'In this context, for this occasion, meat-eating was approved by the Blessed One as proper.' And [they will say it is] included among wholesome foods, and that the <s>Tathāgata</s> himself ate [meat]. But nowhere, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, in any <s>sūtra</s>, has it been approved as 'to be consumed,' nor has it been taught among wholesome foods as 'proper.'

body.text: yadi tu mahāmate anujñātukāmatā me syāt, kalpyaṃ vā me śrāvakāṇāṃ pratisevituṃ syāt, nāhaṃ maitrīvihāriṇāṃ yogināṃ yogācārāṇāṃ śmaśānikānāṃ mahāyānasaṃprasthitānāṃ kulaputrāṇāṃ kuladuhitṝṇāṃ ca sarvasattvaikaputrakasaṃjñābhāvanārthaṃ sarvāmāṃsabhakṣaṇapratiṣedhaṃ kuryām, kṛtavāṃśca / asmin mahāmate dharmakāmānāṃ kulaputrāṇāṃ kuladuhitṝṇāṃ ca sarvayānasaṃprasthitānāṃ śmaśānikānāṃ maitrīvihāriṇāmāraṇyakānāṃ yogināṃ yogācārāṇāṃ sarvayogasādhanāya sarvasattvaikaputrakasaṃjñābhāvanārthaṃ sarvamāṃsapratiṣedham //
body.translated_text: If, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, it were my wish to approve [meat], or if it were proper for my <s>Śrāvakas</s> to consume it, I would not have made a prohibition of all meat-eating for the sake of cultivating the perception of all beings as one's only child — for <s>yogins</s> and <s>yoga</s>-practitioners dwelling in loving-kindness, for cremation-ground [dwellers], for sons and daughters of good families who have set forth in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> — yet I have done so. In this [teaching], O <s>Mahāmati</s>, for the sake of accomplishing all <s>yoga</s>-practices and for cultivating the perception of all beings as one's only child — for sons and daughters of good families who love the <s>Dharma</s>, who have set forth in all vehicles, who dwell in cremation grounds, who dwell in loving-kindness, who are forest-dwellers, who are <s>yogins</s> and <s>yoga</s>-practitioners — I [make] the prohibition of all meat.

body.text: tatra tatra deśanāpāṭhe śikṣāpadānāmanupūrvībandhaṃ niḥśreṇīpadavinyāsayogena trikoṭiṃ baddhvā na taduddiśya kṛtāni pratiṣiddhāni / tato daśaprakṛtimṛtānyapi māṃsāni pratiṣiddhāni / iha tu sūtre sarveṇa sarvaṃ sarvathā sarvaṃ nirupāyena sarvaṃ pratiṣiddham / yato 'haṃ mahāmate māṃsabhojanaṃ na kasyacidanujñātavān, nānujānāmi, nānujñāsyāmi / akalpyaṃ mahāmate pravrajitānāṃ māṃsabhojanamiti vadāmi / yadapi ca mahāmate mamābhyākhyānaṃ dātavyaṃ maṃsyante tathāgatenāpi paribhuktamiti, tadanyeṣāṃ mahāmate mohapuruṣāṇāṃ svakarmadoṣāvaraṇāvṛtānāṃ dīrgharātramanarthāyāhitāya saṃvartakaṃ bhaviṣyati / na hi mahāmate āryaśrāvakāḥ prākṛtamanuṣyāhāramāharanti,
body.translated_text: In various teaching-recitations, through the progressive binding of training rules, by the method of step-by-step ladder placement, having set the three-pointed boundary, those [meats] were prohibited with reference to that. Therefore even the ten kinds of naturally dead [animals'] meat were prohibited. But in this <s>sūtra</s>, all meat in every way, all meat entirely, all meat without exception, is prohibited. Since I, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, have not approved meat-eating for anyone, do not approve it, and will not approve it — I say that meat-eating is improper for renunciants, O <s>Mahāmati</s>. And as for those who, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, will think they should create a false account that the <s>Tathāgata</s> himself ate [meat] — for those other deluded persons, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, whose [vision] is obstructed by the veil of their own <s>karmic</s> faults, it will be conducive to harm and detriment for a long night. For noble <s>Śrāvakas</s>, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, do not consume ordinary human food —

body.text: kuta eva māṃsarudhirāhāramakalpyam / dharmāhārā hi mahāmate mama śrāvakāḥ pratyekabuddhā bodhisattvāśca nāmiṣāhārāḥ, prāgeva tathāgatāḥ / dharmakāyā hi mahāmate tathāgatā dharmāhārasthitayo nāmiṣakāyā na sarvāmiṣāhārasthitayo vāntasarvabhavopakaraṇatṛṣṇaiṣaṇāvāsanāḥ sarvakleśadoṣavāsanāpagatāḥ suvimuktacittaprajñāḥ sarvajñāḥ sarvadarśinaḥ sarvasattvaikaputrakasamadarśino mahākāruṇikāḥ / so 'haṃ mahāmate sarvasattvaikaputrakasaṃjñī san kathamiva svaputramāṃsamanujñāsyāmi paribhoktuṃ śrāvakebhyaḥ, kuta eva svayaṃ paribhoktum? anujñātavānasmi śrāvakebhyaḥ svayaṃ vā paribhuktavāniti mahāmate nedaṃ sthānaṃ vidyate //
body.translated_text: how much less the improper food of meat and blood! For my <s>Śrāvakas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, are nourished by <s>Dharma</s>-food, not by material food — how much more so the <s>Tathāgatas</s>! For the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, have the <s>Dharmakāya</s> (Dharma-body), abide in <s>Dharma</s>-food, not in the body of material [food], not in abiding on any material food — they have vomited up the impressions of craving and seeking for all the provisions of existence, they are free from the impressions of all affliction-faults, their minds and wisdom are well-liberated, they are omniscient, all-seeing, seeing all beings equally as [their] only child, greatly compassionate. How could I, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, who have the perception of all beings as my only child, approve the eating of my own child's flesh to <s>Śrāvakas</s>, let alone eat it myself? That I have approved it to <s>Śrāvakas</s> or have myself eaten [meat], O <s>Mahāmati</s> — this possibility does not exist.

body.text: tatredamucyate -
body.translated_text: On this, it is said:

children.text: madyaṃ māṃsaṃ palāṇḍuṃ na bhakṣayeyaṃ mahāmune /
children.translated_text: Liquor, meat, and onion I would not eat, O great sage —
thus have the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s>, the chief <s>Jinas</s>, declared. || <s>Laṅk</s> 8.1 ||
Consumed by ignoble [people], foul-smelling, and indeed producing ill-repute —
meat is the food of flesh-eaters; proclaim it as not to be eaten, O great sage. || <s>Laṅk</s> 8.2 ||

children.text: bhakṣyamāṇe ca ye deṣā abhakṣye tu guṇāśca ye /
children.translated_text: The faults in eating [meat], and the virtues in not eating it —

children.text: mahāmate nibodha tvaṃ ye doṣā māṃsabhakṣaṇe // Lank_8.3 //
children.translated_text: understand, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the faults of meat-eating. || <s>Laṅk</s> 8.3 ||
Because of being born from one's own kind, because of deviation [from purity], because of being produced from semen and blood —

children.text: udvejanīyaṃ bhūtānāṃ yogī māṃsaṃ vivarjayet // Lank_8.4 //
children.translated_text: the <s>yogin</s> should abstain from meat, [which is] repulsive to beings. || <s>Laṅk</s> 8.4 ||

children.text: māṃsāni ca palāṇḍūṃśca madyāni vividhāni ca /
children.translated_text: Meats, onions, and various kinds of liquor,

children.text: gṛñjanaṃ laśunaṃ caiva yogī nityaṃ vivarjayet // Lank_8.5 //
children.translated_text: ginger-root and garlic — the <s>yogin</s> should always abstain [from these]. || <s>Laṅk</s> 8.5 ||
One should avoid oil as an ointment; one should not sleep in places infested with insects;

children.text: chidrācchidreṣu sattvānāṃ yacca sthānaṃ mahadbhayam // Lank_8.6 //
children.translated_text: in the holes and crevices of beings — and [in] any place of great fear. || <s>Laṅk</s> 8.6 ||
From food arises pride; from pride arises intention;
from intention is born passion — therefore one should not eat [meat]. || <s>Laṅk</s> 8.7 ||
From intention arises desire; the mind is deluded by desire.

children.text: mūḍhasya saṃgatirbhavati jāyate na ca mucyate // Lank_8.8 //
children.translated_text: For the deluded one there is attachment; he is born and is not liberated. [Laṅk 8.8]

children.text: lābhārthaṃ hanyate sattvo māṃsārthaṃ dīyate dhanam /
children.translated_text: For the sake of gain, a being is killed; for the sake of meat, wealth is given.

children.text: ubhau tau pāpakarmāṇau pacyete rauravādiṣu // Lank_8.9 //
children.translated_text: Both of those evil-doers are cooked in the <s>Raurava</s> and other [hells]. [Laṅk 8.9]
He who, transgressing the words of the <s>Muni</s>, eats meat, the evil-minded one,
is consecrated for the destruction of both worlds in the <s>Śākya</s> dispensation. [Laṅk 8.10]

children.text: te yānti paramaṃ ghoraṃ narakaṃ pāpakarmiṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Those sinful ones go to the most terrible hell;
the meat-eaters are cooked in the dreadful <s>Raurava</s> and other [hells]. [Laṅk 8.11]
Truly, the threefold-pure meat — unsolicited, uninvited,

children.text: acoditaṃ ca naivāsti tasmānmāṃsaṃ na bhakṣayet // Lank_8.12 //
children.translated_text: and unprompted — does not exist at all; therefore one should not eat meat. [Laṅk 8.12]

children.text: māṃsaṃ na bhakṣayedyogī mayā buddhaiśca garhitam /
children.translated_text: A <s>yogin</s> should not eat meat — it is condemned by me and by the <s>Buddhas</s>;
beings who devour one another are born in families of flesh-eaters. [Laṅk 8.13]
One becomes foul-smelling, contemptible, and also mad,

children.text: caṇḍālapukkasakule ḍombeṣu ca punaḥ punaḥ // Lank_8.14 //
children.translated_text: born again and again in the families of <s>Caṇḍālas</s>, <s>Pukkasas</s>, and <s>Ḍombas</s>. [Laṅk 8.14]
One is born in the wombs of <s>Ḍākinī</s>-races and in the family of meat-eaters;
that lowest of men is born in the wombs of <s>Rākṣasīs</s> and cats. [Laṅk 8.15]
In the <s>Hastikakṣya</s>, the <s>Mahāmegha</s>, the <s>Nirvāṇāṅgulimālika</s>,

children.text: laṅkāvatārasūtre ca mayā māṃsaṃ vivarjitam // Lank_8.16 //
children.translated_text: and in the <s>Laṅkāvatāra Sūtra</s> — meat has been prohibited by me. [Laṅk 8.16]
It is condemned by <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, and <s>Śrāvakas</s>;

children.text: khādate yadi nairlajjyādunmatto jāyate sadā // Lank_8.17 //
children.translated_text: if one eats shamelessly, one is always born mad. [Laṅk 8.17]

children.text: brāhmaṇeṣu ca jāyeta atha vā yogināṃ kule /
children.translated_text: One would be born among <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> or in the family of <s>yogins</s>,
becoming wise and wealthy — from the renunciation of meat-eating and the like. [Laṅk 8.18]
One should renounce all meat through the suspicions of what is seen and heard;
the logicians do not understand, being born in families of flesh-eaters. [Laṅk 8.19]
Just as desire becomes an obstacle to liberation,
so too do meat, liquor, and the like become obstacles [to liberation]. [Laṅk 8.20]
In the future time, meat-eaters who are preachers of delusion will say:

children.text: kalpikaṃ niravadyaṃ ca māṃsaṃ buddhānuvarṇitam // Lank_8.21 //
children.translated_text: "Meat is proper, blameless, and described by the <s>Buddha</s>." [Laṅk 8.21]
Meat as food is [like] medicine, and again, like the flesh of one's own child;

children.text: mātrayā pratikūlaṃ ca yogī piṇḍaṃ samācaret // Lank_8.22 //
children.translated_text: a <s>yogin</s> should take his alms-food with moderation and with aversion. [Laṅk 8.22]
It has been always and in every way condemned by me for those who dwell in <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness);
one would be co-dwelling with lions, tigers, wolves, and the like. [Laṅk 8.23]
Therefore one should not eat meat, which causes distress to people;
because it is contrary to the <s>dharma</s> of liberation — this is the banner of the noble ones. [Laṅk 8.24]

body.text: iti laṅkāvatārātsarvabuddhapravacanahṛdayānmāṃsabhakṣaṇaparivarto 'ṣṭamaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the eighth chapter, the Chapter on Meat-Eating, in the <s>Laṅkāvatāra</s>, the heart of all <s>Buddha</s>-discourses.

body.text: START Parivarta 9
body.translated_text: Beginning of Chapter 9.

body.text: dhāraṇīparivarto nāma navamaḥ /
body.translated_text: The ninth [chapter], named the Chapter on <s>Dhāraṇī</s>.

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān mahāmatiṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvamāmantrayate sma - udgṛhṇa tvaṃ mahāmate laṅkāvatāre mantrapadāni yānyatītānāgatapratyutpannairbuddhairbhagavadbhirbhāṣitāni, bhāṣante, bhāṣiṣyante ca / ahamapyetarhi bhāṣiṣye dharmabhāṇakānāṃ parigrahārtham / tadyathā / tuṭṭe 2 / vuṭṭe 2 / paṭṭe 2 / kaṭṭe 2 / amale 2 / vimale 2 / nime 2 / hime 2 / vame 2 / kale 2 / kale 2 / aṭṭe maṭṭe / vaṭṭe tuṭṭe / jñeṭṭe spuṭṭe / kaṭṭe 2 / laṭṭe paṭṭe / dime 2 / cale 2 / pace pace / bandhe 2 / añce mañce / dutāre 2 / patāre 2 / akke 2 / sarkke 2 / cakre 2 / dime 2 / hime 2 / ṭu ṭu ṭu ṭu / 4 / ḍu ḍu ḍu ḍu / 4 / ru ru ru ru / 4 / phu phu phu phu / 4 / svāhā //
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One addressed the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s>: "Take up, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, the <s>mantra</s>-words in the <s>Laṅkāvatāra</s> which have been spoken, are being spoken, and will be spoken by the Blessed <s>Buddhas</s> of the past, future, and present. I too shall now speak [them] for the protection of the <s>Dharma</s>-preachers. That is: <s>tuṭṭe tuṭṭe</s> / <s>vuṭṭe vuṭṭe</s> / <s>paṭṭe paṭṭe</s> / <s>kaṭṭe kaṭṭe</s> / <s>amale amale</s> / <s>vimale vimale</s> / <s>nime nime</s> / <s>hime hime</s> / <s>vame vame</s> / <s>kale kale</s> / <s>kale kale</s> / <s>aṭṭe maṭṭe</s> / <s>vaṭṭe tuṭṭe</s> / <s>jñeṭṭe spuṭṭe</s> / <s>kaṭṭe kaṭṭe</s> / <s>laṭṭe paṭṭe</s> / <s>dime dime</s> / <s>cale cale</s> / <s>pace pace</s> / <s>bandhe bandhe</s> / <s>añce mañce</s> / <s>dutāre dutāre</s> / <s>patāre patāre</s> / <s>akke akke</s> / <s>sarkke sarkke</s> / <s>cakre cakre</s> / <s>dime dime</s> / <s>hime hime</s> / <s>ṭu ṭu ṭu ṭu</s> / [×4] / <s>ḍu ḍu ḍu ḍu</s> / [×4] / <s>ru ru ru ru</s> / [×4] / <s>phu phu phu phu</s> / [×4] / <s>svāhā</s>."

body.text: imāni mahāmate mantrapadāni laṅkāvatāre mahāyānasūtre / yaḥ kaścinmahāmate kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā imāni mantrapadānyudgrahīṣyati dhārayiṣyati vācayiṣyati paryavāpsyati, na tasya kaścidavatāraṃ lapsyate devo vā devī vā nāgo vā nāgī vā yakṣo vā yakṣī vā asuro vā asurī vā garuḍo vā garuḍī vā kinnaro vā kinnarī vā mahorago vā mahoragī vā gandharvo vā gandharvī vā bhūto vā bhūtī vā kumbhāṇḍo vā kumbhāṇḍī vā piśāco vā piśācī vā ostārako vā austārakī vā apasmāro vā apasmārī vā rākṣaso vā rākṣasī vā ḍāko vā ḍākinī vā ojohāro vā ojohārī vā kaṭapūtano vā kaṭapūtanī vā amanuṣyo vā amanuṣyī vā, sarve te 'vatāraṃ na lapsyate / sa cedviṣamagraho bhaviṣyati, so 'syāṣṭottaraśatābhimantritena rodan krandanto kaṃ diśaṃ dṛṣṭvā yāsyati //
body.translated_text: "These, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, are the <s>mantra</s>-words in the <s>Laṅkāvatāra</s>, the <s>Mahāyāna</s> sūtra. Whoever, O <s>Mahāmati</s> — whether a son of good family or a daughter of good family — takes up, retains, recites, and masters these <s>mantra</s>-words, no one will gain access to them — neither a <s>deva</s> nor a <s>devī</s>, a <s>nāga</s> nor a <s>nāgī</s>, a <s>yakṣa</s> nor a <s>yakṣī</s>, an <s>asura</s> nor an <s>asurī</s>, a <s>garuḍa</s> nor a <s>garuḍī</s>, a <s>kinnara</s> nor a <s>kinnarī</s>, a <s>mahoraga</s> nor a <s>mahoragī</s>, a <s>gandharva</s> nor a <s>gandharvī</s>, a <s>bhūta</s> nor a <s>bhūtī</s>, a <s>kumbhāṇḍa</s> nor a <s>kumbhāṇḍī</s>, a <s>piśāca</s> nor a <s>piśācī</s>, an <s>ostāraka</s> nor an <s>ostārakī</s>, an <s>apasmāra</s> nor an <s>apasmārī</s>, a <s>rākṣasa</s> nor a <s>rākṣasī</s>, a <s>ḍāka</s> nor a <s>ḍākinī</s>, an <s>ojohāra</s> nor an <s>ojohārī</s>, a <s>kaṭapūtana</s> nor a <s>kaṭapūtanī</s>, a non-human male nor a non-human female — none of them will gain access. And if an adverse seizure should occur, that [being], consecrated with the 108-fold recitation [of this <s>mantra</s>], will flee weeping and wailing, looking in which direction to go."

body.text: punaraparāṇi mahāmate mantrapadāni bhāṣiṣye / tadyathā - padme padmadeve / hine hini hine / cu cule culu cule / phale phula phule / yule ghule yula yule / ghule ghula ghule / pale pala pale / muñce 3 / chinde bhinde bhañje marde pramarde dinakare svāhā //
body.translated_text: "Furthermore, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, I shall speak other <s>mantra</s>-words. That is: <s>padme padmadeve</s> / <s>hine hini hine</s> / <s>cu cule culu cule</s> / <s>phale phula phule</s> / <s>yule ghule yula yule</s> / <s>ghule ghula ghule</s> / <s>pale pala pale</s> / <s>muñce muñce muñce</s> / <s>chinde bhinde bhañje marde pramarde dinakare svāhā</s>."

body.text: imāni mahāmate mantrapadāni yaḥ kaścitkulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā udgrahīṣyati dhārayiṣyati vācayiṣyati paryavāpsyati, tasya na kaścidavatāraṃ lapsyate devo vā devī vā nāgo vā nāgī vā yakṣo vā yakṣī vā asuro vā asurī vā garuḍo vā garuḍī vā kinnaro vā kinnarī vā mahorago vā mahoragī vā gandharvo vā gandharvī vā bhūto vā bhūtī vā kumbhāṇḍo vā kumbhāṇḍī vā piśāco vā piśācī vā ostārako vā ostārakī vā, apasmāro vā apasmārī vā, rākṣaso vā rākṣasī vā, ḍāko vā ḍākinī vā, ojoharo vā ojoharī vā, kaṭapūtano vā kaṭapūtanī vā, manuṣyo vā manuṣyī vā, sarve te 'vatāraṃ na lapsyate / ya imāni mantrapadāni paṭhiṣyati, tena laṅkāvatārasūtraṃ paṭhitaṃ bhaviṣyati / imāni bhagavatā mantrapadāni bhāṣitāni rākṣasānāṃ nivāraṇārtham //
body.translated_text: "These, O <s>Mahāmati</s>, are the <s>mantra</s>-words. Whoever — whether a son of good family or a daughter of good family — takes up, retains, recites, and masters these <s>mantra</s>-words, no one will gain access to them — neither a <s>deva</s> nor a <s>devī</s>, a <s>nāga</s> nor a <s>nāgī</s>, a <s>yakṣa</s> nor a <s>yakṣī</s>, an <s>asura</s> nor an <s>asurī</s>, a <s>garuḍa</s> nor a <s>garuḍī</s>, a <s>kinnara</s> nor a <s>kinnarī</s>, a <s>mahoraga</s> nor a <s>mahoragī</s>, a <s>gandharva</s> nor a <s>gandharvī</s>, a <s>bhūta</s> nor a <s>bhūtī</s>, a <s>kumbhāṇḍa</s> nor a <s>kumbhāṇḍī</s>, a <s>piśāca</s> nor a <s>piśācī</s>, an <s>ostāraka</s> nor an <s>ostārakī</s>, an <s>apasmāra</s> nor an <s>apasmārī</s>, a <s>rākṣasa</s> nor a <s>rākṣasī</s>, a <s>ḍāka</s> nor a <s>ḍākinī</s>, an <s>ojohara</s> nor an <s>ojoharī</s>, a <s>kaṭapūtana</s> nor a <s>kaṭapūtanī</s>, a human male nor a human female — none of them will gain access. Whoever recites these <s>mantra</s>-words, for them it will be as though the <s>Laṅkāvatāra Sūtra</s> has been recited. These <s>mantra</s>-words were spoken by the Blessed One for the purpose of warding off <s>rākṣasas</s>."

body.text: iti laṅkāvatāre dhāraṇīparivarto nāma navamaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the ninth chapter, named the Chapter on <s>Dhāraṇī</s>, in the <s>Laṅkāvatāra</s>.

body.text: START Parivarta 10
body.translated_text: Beginning of Chapter 10.

body.text: sagāthakam /
body.translated_text: With verses.

body.text: atha khalu mahāmatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantametadavocat -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāmati</s> said this to the Blessed One:

children.translated_text: The world is free from arising and destruction, resembling a flower in the sky;

children.text: sadasannopalabdho 'yaṃ prajñayā kṛpayā ca te // Lank_10.1 //
children.translated_text: it is apprehended as neither existent nor non-existent — by your wisdom and compassion. [Laṅk 10.1]
The world, free from eternalism and annihilationism, is always like a dream;

children.text: sadasannopalabdho 'yaṃ prajñayā kṛpayā ca te // Lank_10.2 //
children.translated_text: it is apprehended as neither existent nor non-existent — by your wisdom and compassion. [Laṅk 10.2]
All <s>dharmas</s> are like illusion, free from mind and consciousness;

children.text: sadasannopalabdhāste prajñayā kṛpayā ca te // Lank_10.3 //
children.translated_text: they are apprehended as neither existent nor non-existent — by your wisdom and compassion. [Laṅk 10.3]
The selflessness of <s>dharmas</s> and persons, the afflictive and the knowable [obscurations] — always for you

children.text: viśuddhamanimittena prajñayā kṛpayā ca te // Lank_10.4 //
children.translated_text: are purified by the signless — by your wisdom and compassion. [Laṅk 10.4]

children.text: na nirvāsi na nirvāṇe na nirvāṇaṃ tvayi sthitam /
children.translated_text: You have not passed into <s>nirvāṇa</s>, nor is there <s>nirvāṇa</s>, nor does <s>nirvāṇa</s> abide in you;
it is free from intellect and what is to be understood, free from the sides of existence and non-existence. [Laṅk 10.5]
Those who see the <s>Muni</s> as peaceful, thus free from arising,
they become free from clinging, unstained in this world and the next. [Laṅk 10.6]
Just as a mirage in summer shimmers, deluding the mind,

children.text: mṛgā gṛhṇanti pānīyaṃ vastu tasya na vidyate // Lank_10.7 //
children.translated_text: deer grasp at water, but there is no substance in it. [Laṅk 10.7]
So this seed of consciousness shimmers in the domain of views;

children.text: bālā gṛhṇanti jāyantaṃ timiraṃ taimirā yathā // Lank_10.8 //
children.translated_text: the childish grasp at it as arising, as those with cataracts [see] floaters. [Laṅk 10.8]

children.text: dhyātā dhyānaṃ ca dhyeyaṃ ca prahāṇaṃ satyadarśanam /
children.translated_text: The meditator, the meditation, and what is to be meditated upon; abandonment and the seeing of truth —

children.text: kalpanāmātramevedaṃ yo budhyati sa mucyati // Lank_10.9 //
children.translated_text: all this is merely conceptualization; whoever understands this is liberated. [Laṅk 10.9]
These <s>dharmas</s> are without essence, arisen from false imagination;

children.text: sāpyatra manyanā śūnyā yayā śūnyeti manyate // Lank_10.10 //
children.translated_text: and that very imagination is also empty, by which one imagines "empty." [Laṅk 10.10]
The aggregates, with consciousness as the fifth, are like reflections in water and shadows of trees;

children.text: māyāsvapnopamaṃ dṛśyaṃ vijñaptyā na vikalpayet // Lank_10.11 //
children.translated_text: the visible is like illusion and dreams — one should not discriminate through mere representation. [Laṅk 10.11]
Like illusion, a <s>vetāla</s>-device, a dream, lightning, and clouds — always,
the world, cut off by the three continuities, is seen — and one who sees thus is liberated. [Laṅk 10.12]
Through improper conceptualization, consciousness operates

children.text: aṣṭaghā navadhā citraṃ taraṃgāṇi mahodadhau // Lank_10.13 //
children.translated_text: in eight and nine [forms], variegated, like waves in the great ocean. [Laṅk 10.13]
Always augmented by impressions, with intellect as the root and a stable basis,
the mind wanders in its domain, like iron [drawn] to a magnet. [Laṅk 10.14]
Inherent in all beings, the <s>gotra</s> (spiritual lineage), free from logic,
turns back, freed from action, free from knower and the knowable. [Laṅk 10.15]
Behold the illusion-like <s>samādhi</s>, gone beyond the ten stages —
the king of mind, free from perception and consciousness. [Laṅk 10.16]

children.text: parāvṛttaṃ yadā cittaṃ tadā tiṣṭhati śāśvatam /
children.translated_text: When the mind is turned around, then it abides eternally
in a palace resembling a lotus, arisen from the domain of illusion. [Laṅk 10.17]
Established therein, having entered effortless conduct,
one accomplishes the welfare of beings, like a wish-fulfilling jewel of manifold forms. [Laṅk 10.18]
There is neither conditioned nor unconditioned, apart from conceptualization;

children.text: bālā gṛhṇanti dhiṅbhūḍhā vandhyāḥ svapne yathā sutam // Lank_10.19 //
children.translated_text: the childish grasp — alas, the fools! — like a barren woman's son in a dream. [Laṅk 10.19]
Essencelessness, non-arising, person, aggregates, continuity,

children.text: pratyayā dhātavo jñeyā śūnyatā ca bhavābhavam // Lank_10.20 //
children.translated_text: conditions, elements, and the knowable — <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) and existence and non-existence [should be known]. [Laṅk 10.20]
My teaching is by skillful means; I do not teach characteristics.

children.text: bālā gṛhṇanti bhāvena lakṣaṇaṃ lakṣyameva ca // Lank_10.21 //
children.translated_text: The childish grasp as real both the characteristic and what is characterized. [Laṅk 10.21]

children.text: sarvasya vettā na ca sarvavettā sarvasya madhye na ca sarvamasti /
children.translated_text: The knower of all, yet not the knower of all; in the midst of everything, yet everything does not exist.

children.text: bālā vikalpenti budhaśca loko na cāpi budhyāmi na ca bodhayāmi // Lank_10.22 //
children.translated_text: The childish and the wise discriminate, but the world — I neither understand nor cause to understand. [Laṅk 10.22]
This designation is mere name; it does not exist through characteristics.
The aggregates are like the form of a ball of hair, about which the childish discriminate. [Laṅk 10.23]
Nothing arises without having previously existed; nothing perishes through conditions.
When one sees the conditioned as a barren woman's son or a sky-flower,

children.text: tadā grāhaśca grāhyaṃ ca bhrāntiṃ dṛṣṭvā nivartate // Lank_10.24 //
children.translated_text: then the grasper and the grasped, having seen the error, turn back. [Laṅk 10.24]

children.text: nāhaṃ nirvāmi bhāvena kriyayā lakṣaṇena ca /
children.translated_text: I do not pass into <s>nirvāṇa</s> through [mere] existence, action, or characteristics;
I am at peace through the cessation of consciousness [that is] the cause of conceptual discrimination.
(Characteristics do not perish — about which the childish discriminate.) [Laṅk 10.25]
Just as when a great flood subsides, waves cannot arise,

children.text: tathā vijñānavaicitryaṃ niruddhaṃ na pravartate // Lank_10.26 //
children.translated_text: so too the diversity of consciousness, having ceased, does not operate. [Laṅk 10.26]
Empty, without inherent nature, illusion-like, unborn —

children.text: sadasanto na vidyante bhāvāḥ svapnopamā ime // Lank_10.27 //
children.translated_text: these entities are not found as existent or non-existent; they are like dreams. [Laṅk 10.27]
I teach a single inherent nature, free from logic and representation,
the divine domain of the noble ones, free from the duality of inherent natures. [Laṅk 10.28]

children.text: khadyotā iva mattasya yathā citrā na santi ca /
children.translated_text: Just as for one intoxicated, fireflies [appear] diverse yet do not [truly] exist,
they are seen due to the disturbance of elements — so is the world by its inherent nature. [Laṅk 10.29]
Just as illusion manifests in grass, wood, and splinters,

children.text: na cāsau vidyate māyā evaṃ dharmāḥ svabhāvataḥ // Lank_10.30 //
children.translated_text: yet that illusion does not [truly] exist — so are <s>dharmas</s> by their inherent nature. [Laṅk 10.30]

children.text: na grāhako na ca grāhyaṃ na bandhyo na ca bandhanam /
children.translated_text: There is no grasper and no grasped, no bondage and no binding;
like illusion and mirage, like a dream, like a cataract. [Laṅk 10.31]
When one who seeks the truth sees, free from conceptualization and unstained,

children.text: tadā yogaṃ samāpanno drakṣyate māṃ na saṃśayaḥ // Lank_10.32 //
children.translated_text: then, having attained <s>yoga</s>, one shall see me — there is no doubt. [Laṅk 10.32]
For there is no cognition here whatsoever — like mirages in the sky;

children.text: evaṃ dharmān vijānanto na kiṃcitpratijānati // Lank_10.33 //
children.translated_text: thus knowing <s>dharmas</s>, one asserts nothing at all. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.33 ||
From conditions of existent and non-existent, there is no arising of <s>dharmas</s>;

children.text: bhrāntaṃ traidhātuke cittaṃ vicitraṃ khyāyate yataḥ // Lank_10.34 //
children.translated_text: the mind, deluded in the three realms, appears in manifold ways. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.34 ||

children.text: svapnaṃ ca lokaṃ ca samasvabhāvaṃ rūpāṇi citrāṇi hi tatra cāpi /
children.translated_text: Dream and world are of the same inherent nature — forms, variegated, appear therein too,

children.text: dṛśyanti bhogaṃ spariśaṃ samānaṃ dehāntagaṃ lokaguruṃ kriyāṃ ca // Lank_10.35 //
children.translated_text: enjoyment and touch are seen as the same — [all] within the body, the world-teacher, and action. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.35 ||

children.text: cittaṃ hi traidhātukayoniretadbhrāntaṃ hi cittamihamutra dṛśyate /
children.translated_text: Mind indeed is the womb of the three realms — this deluded mind is seen here and there;

children.text: na kalpayellokamasatta eṣāmetādṛśīṃ lokagatiṃ viditvā // Lank_10.36 //
children.translated_text: one should not conceptualize the world as non-existent — having known this such course of the world. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.36 ||
The childish see arising and destruction through delusion;

children.text: na saṃbhavaṃ na vibhavaṃ prajñāyukto vipaśyati // Lank_10.37 //
children.translated_text: one endowed with wisdom sees neither arising nor destruction. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.37 ||
In the divine <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> mansion, free from all evil,
always absorbed, free from conceptualization, devoid of mind and mental factors, || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.38 ||
having attained the powers, superknowledges, and mastery, gone to the course of that <s>samādhi</s> —

children.text: tatra budhyanti saṃbuddhā nirmitastviha budhyate // Lank_10.39 //
children.translated_text: therein the fully awakened Buddhas awaken; but here [in this world] an emanation awakens. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.39 ||
Immeasurable millions of emanations of the Buddhas go forth,

children.text: sarvatra bālāḥ śṛṇvanti dharmaṃ tebhyaḥ pratiśrutvā (?) // Lank_10.40 //
children.translated_text: and everywhere the childish hear the <s>Dharma</s>, having responded to them. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.40 ||
Free from beginning, middle, and end, devoid of existence and non-existence,
pervading, immovable, pure, without variety yet the source of variety, || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.41 ||
covered by the lineage of cognition, not dissolved in all embodied beings —

children.text: bhrānteśca vidyate māyā na māyā bhrāntikāraṇam // Lank_10.42 //
children.translated_text: for the deluded, illusion exists; but illusion is not the cause of delusion. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.42 ||
Through the delusion of mind, whatever exists does indeed exist,
bound by the duality of inherent natures, produced by <s>ālayavijñāna</s> (store-consciousness) —

children.text: lokaṃ vijñaptimātraṃ ca dṛṣṭyaughaṃ dharmapudgalam // Lank_10.43 //
children.translated_text: the world is mere cognition, and the flood of views is [about] <s>dharma</s> and person. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.43 ||

children.text: vibhāvya lokamevaṃ tu parāvṛtto yadā bhavet /
children.translated_text: Having discerned the world in this way, when one becomes transformed (<s>parāvṛtta</s>),
then one becomes my child, a turner of the perfected <s>Dharma</s>. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.44 ||
Hot, fluid, moving, and hard — these <s>dharmas</s> are conceptualized by the childish;

children.text: asadbhūtasamāropo nāsti lakṣyaṃ na lakṣaṇam // Lank_10.45 //
children.translated_text: it is a superimposition upon what is unreal — there is neither the characterized nor the characteristic. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.45 ||
This body with its eight substances, its configuration, and its faculties —

children.text: rūpaṃ kalpanti vai bālā bhrāntāḥ saṃsārapañjare // Lank_10.46 //
children.translated_text: the childish conceptualize [it as] form, deluded in the cage of <s>saṃsāra</s>. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.46 ||
Through the assemblage of causes and conditions, the childish conceptualize arising,
not knowing this method, they wander in the abode of the three existences. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.47 ||
All entities are without inherent nature, and even the speech of men [is so];
from conceptualization, too, is emanation — existence is empty, like a dream;
examining, one does not transmigrate, nor does one attain <s>nirvāṇa</s>. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.48 ||
Mind, variegated, called 'seed,' appears as the domain of mind;

children.text: khyātau kalpanti utpattiṃ bālāḥ kalpadvaye ratāḥ // Lank_10.49 //
children.translated_text: the childish, delighting in the two types of conceptualization, conceptualize arising in what appears. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.49 ||

children.text: ajñāna tṛṣṇā karmaṃ ca cittacaittā na mārakam /
children.translated_text: Ignorance, craving, and <s>karma</s>, and mind and mental factors — are not <s>Māra</s>;

children.text: pravartati tato yasmātpāratantryaṃ hi tanmatam // Lank_10.50 //
children.translated_text: since it operates from that, dependent-nature (<s>pāratantrya</s>) is indeed that [very thing] considered. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.50 ||
They conceptualize that entity which is the delusion of the domain of mind;
in conceptualization it is unperfected — falsely discriminated through erroneous delusion. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.51 ||
Mind, connected with conditions, operates in embodied beings;

children.text: pratyayebhyo vinirmuktaṃ na paśyāmi vadāmyaham // Lank_10.52 //
children.translated_text: freed from conditions, I do not see [it] — thus I declare. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.52 ||
Freed from conditions, devoid of own-characteristics,

children.text: na tiṣṭhati yadā dehe tena mahyamagocaram // Lank_10.53 //
children.translated_text: when it does not abide in the body, therefore it is beyond my domain. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.53 ||
Just as a king or a merchant, with variegated deer-like [toys],

children.text: pralobhya krīḍati gṛhe vane mṛgasamāgamam // Lank_10.54 //
children.translated_text: having enticed [his] sons, plays in the house [as if with] a gathering of deer in the forest — || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.54 ||
so I, with variegated characteristics that are reflections of <s>dharmas</s>,

children.text: pratyātmavedyāṃ hi sutāṃ bhūtakoṭiṃ vadāmyaham // Lank_10.55 //
children.translated_text: speak of the limit of reality (<s>bhūtakoṭi</s>) as the child [to be realized] through one's own inner realization. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.55 ||
Just as waves of the ocean, arisen from the condition of wind,

children.text: nṛtyamānāḥ pravartante vyucchedaścaḥ na vidyate // Lank_10.56 //
children.translated_text: dance forth and operate — and there is no interruption — || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.56 ||
so the ocean of the <s>ālaya</s> (store-consciousness), always stirred by the wind of objects,
dances forth and operates with the variegated consciousness-waves. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.57 ||
Through the mode of grasped and grasper, mind bends in embodied beings;

children.text: dṛśyasya lakṣaṇaṃ nāsti yathā bālairvikalpyate // Lank_10.58 //
children.translated_text: but the characteristic of what is seen does not exist as conceptualized by the childish. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.58 ||
The supreme <s>ālayavijñāna</s> (store-consciousness) — and cognition is [merely] the <s>ālaya</s> again;
from the removal of grasped and grasper, I teach <s>tathatā</s> (suchness). || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.59 ||

children.text: nāsti skandheṣvātmā na sattvo na ca pudgalaḥ /
children.translated_text: There is no self in the aggregates, no being, and no person;

children.text: utpadyate ca vijñānaṃ vijñānaṃ ca nirudhyate // Lank_10.60 //
children.translated_text: consciousness arises and consciousness ceases. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.60 ||

children.text: nimnonnataṃ yathā citre dṛśyate na ca vidyate /
children.translated_text: Just as high and low are seen in a painting but do not exist [in reality],

children.text: tathā bhāveṣu bhāvatvaṃ dṛśyate na ca vidyate // Lank_10.61 //
children.translated_text: so entity-ness in entities is seen but does not exist. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.61 ||
Like a <s>gandharva</s>-city and like a mirage,

children.text: dṛśyaṃ khyāti tathā nityaṃ prajñayā ca na vidyate // Lank_10.62 //
children.translated_text: the visible always appears thus, but through wisdom it is not found. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.62 ||
Free from means of knowledge and faculties, neither effect nor cause,
devoid of intellect and what is to be known, free from the characterized and the characteristic — || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.63 ||

children.text: skandhān pratītya saṃbuddho na dṛṣṭaḥ kenacitkvacit /
children.translated_text: a <s>Saṃbuddha</s> (fully awakened one) dependent on the aggregates has not been seen by anyone anywhere;

children.text: yo na dṛṣṭaḥ kvacitkena kutastasya vibhāvanā // Lank_10.64 //
children.translated_text: that which has not been seen anywhere by anyone — how can it be examined? || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.64 ||
Through conditions, reasons, examples, thesis, and cause,
and through the wheel of dream, <s>gandharva</s>-[city], mirages, moon, and sun — || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.65 ||
by the examples of the unseen, family, and so forth, I proclaim arising;

children.text: svapnavibhramamāyākhyaṃ śūnyaṃ vai kalpitaṃ jagat // Lank_10.66 //
children.translated_text: the world, called dream-delusion-illusion, is indeed empty and imagined. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.66 ||
Unsupported in the three worlds, both internally and externally,

children.text: anutpannaṃ bhavaṃ dṛṣṭvā kṣāntyanutpatti jāyate // Lank_10.67 //
children.translated_text: having seen existence as non-arisen, the patience of non-arising (<s>anutpattikṣānti</s>) is born. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.67 ||
And the illusion-like <s>samādhi</s>, and the mind-made body again,

children.text: abhijñā vaśitā tasya balā cittasya citritā // Lank_10.68 //
children.translated_text: superknowledges, mastery, powers of that [yogin] — the variegation of mind. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.68 ||

children.text: bhāvā yeṣāṃ hyanutpannāḥ śūnyā vai asvabhāvakāḥ /
children.translated_text: For those whose entities are non-arisen, empty, and without inherent nature —
for them delusion arises and by conditions it ceases. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.69 ||

children.text: cittaṃ hi khyāti cittasya bahirdhā khyāti rūpiṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Mind indeed appears to the mind; externally it appears as having form;

children.text: anyanna vidyate dṛśyaṃ yathā bālairvikalpyate // Lank_10.70 //
children.translated_text: there is no other visible [reality] — as is conceptualized by the childish. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.70 ||

children.text: saṃkalā buddhabimbaṃ ca bhūtānāṃ ca vidāraṇam /
children.translated_text: The chain [of dependent origination], Buddha-images, and the splitting open of beings —

children.text: adhiṣṭhanti jagaccitraṃ prajñaptyā vai suśikṣitāḥ // Lank_10.71 //
children.translated_text: they empower the variegated world, well-trained through designation. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.71 ||
Body, support, and enjoyment — these three are the grasped cognitions;
<s>manas</s> (mentation), grasping-cognition, and conceptualization — [these] three are the graspers. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.72 ||
Conceptualization and what is conceptualized — as long as [one remains] within the domain of syllables,
so long the logicians do not see reality, from the confusion of logic. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.73 ||

children.text: naiḥsvabhāvyaṃ hi bhāvānāṃ yadā budhyanti prajñayā /
children.translated_text: When through wisdom they awaken to the non-inherent-nature of entities,
then the <s>yogin</s> comes to rest, established in the signless (<s>ānimitta</s>). || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.74 ||
Just as a chicken smeared with ink is taken up by the ignorant,
so too, not knowing [the truth], the childish [regard] the three vehicles in the same way. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.75 ||
For there are no <s>Śrāvakas</s> here, nor are there <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>-vehicle practitioners;
and that form which is seen as belonging to a <s>Śrāvaka</s> and a <s>Jina</s> —
these compassionate <s>Bodhisattvas</s> teach [it] as an emanation. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.76 ||
The three existences are mere cognition (<s>vijñaptimātra</s>), imagined by the duality of inherent natures;
but when transformed (<s>parāvṛtta</s>), that is <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) — from departing from <s>dharma</s> and person. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.77 ||
Moon, sun, lamp-flames, beings, and gems likewise —

children.text: nirvikalpāḥ pravartante tathā buddhasya buddhatā // Lank_10.78 //
children.translated_text: they operate without conceptualization; so too is the Buddhahood of the <s>Buddha</s>. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.78 ||
Just as a hair-net is falsely grasped by people with cataracts,
so this conceptualization of entities is falsely conceptualized by the childish. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.79 ||
Without abiding, destruction, or arising, devoid of permanence and impermanence,
called defilement and purification — entities are like a hair-net. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.80 ||
Just as someone sees the world as a golden doll,

children.text: na hyasti kanakaṃ tatra bhūmiśca kanakāyate // Lank_10.81 //
children.translated_text: there is no gold therein, yet the ground appears golden. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.81 ||
Thus indeed the childish are corrupted by beginningless mind and mental factors;
they grasp as real the existence produced from illusion and mirage. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.82 ||
One seed and seedless, and the ocean as one seed,
and all-seeded too — behold this mind, the variegated! || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.83 ||
When the one seed is pure, transformed, and seedless,
it is equal through being free from conceptualization; from excess arises the mixture of births —
the seed carries the variegated; it is called 'all-seeded.' || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.84 ||
Nothing whatsoever arises here from conditions, nor does it cease;

children.text: utpadyante nirudhyante pratyayā eva kalpitāḥ // Lank_10.85 //
children.translated_text: conditions themselves, as conceptualized, arise and cease. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.85 ||
The three existences are mere designation; there is no entity by its own nature;
the logicians will conceptualize entity-ness through the existence of what is designated. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.86 ||
The desire to know the inherent nature of entities — delusion is not thereby warded off;
having seen thus the non-arising of the inherent nature of entities, one is liberated. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.87 ||
Illusion is not [like non-existence] — from the similarity with non-existence, the existence of entities is not stated;
they are like the false, the swift, and lightning — therefore they are remembered as illusion-like. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.88 ||

children.text: na cotpadyā na cotpannāḥ pratyayo 'pi na kecana /
children.translated_text: They are neither to be produced nor are they produced; conditions too are not any at all;

children.text: saṃvidyante kvacittena vyavahāraṃ tu kathyate // Lank_10.89 //
children.translated_text: they are found nowhere — therefore conventional usage alone is spoken. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.89 ||
The defilement of destruction, arising, and affliction of conditions is not warded off;

children.text: yattu bālā vikalpenti pratyayaiḥ saṃnivāryate // Lank_10.90 //
children.translated_text: but what the childish conceptualize is warded off by conditions. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.90 ||

children.text: na svabhāvo na vijñaptirna vastu na ca ālayaḥ /
children.translated_text: There is no inherent nature, no cognition, no entity, and no <s>ālaya</s> (store);
these are conceptualized by the childish who are under the sway of bad logic. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.91 ||
When the sons of the <s>Jinas</s> see the world as mind-only,
then they obtain the <s>nirvāṇa</s>-body, free from the constructions of action,

children.text: labhante te balābhijñāvaśitaiḥ saha saṃyutam // Lank_10.92 //
children.translated_text: endowed with the powers, superknowledges, and masteries. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.92 ||
When mind operates manifesting all forms,

children.text: nātra cittaṃ na rūpāṇi bhrāntaṃ cittamanādikam // Lank_10.93 //
children.translated_text: therein there is neither mind nor forms — mind is deluded from beginningless [time]. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.93 ||

children.text: tadā yogī hyanābhāsaṃ prajñayā paśyate jagat /
children.translated_text: Then the <s>yogin</s> sees the world as non-appearing through wisdom;
sign, entity-cognition, and the vibration of <s>manas</s> —

children.text: atikramya tu putrā me nirvikalpāścaranti te // Lank_10.94 //
children.translated_text: having transcended these, my children wander free from conceptualization. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.94 ||
<s>Gandharva</s>-city, illusion, hair-net, mirage —

children.text: asatyāḥ satyataḥ khyānti tathā bhāveṣu bhāvanā // Lank_10.95 //
children.translated_text: these unreal [things] appear as real; so too is the cultivation regarding entities. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.95 ||
All entities are non-arisen — only delusion is seen;

children.text: bhrāntiṃ kalpenti utpannāṃ bālāṃ kalpadvaye ratāḥ // Lank_10.96 //
children.translated_text: the childish, delighting in the two types of conceptualization, conceptualize delusion as arisen. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.96 ||
Mind, which is limb-like in spontaneous arising, variegated, born from impressions,
operates as a flood of waves — and from its cutting, it does not operate. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.97 ||
As the variegated, with variegated support, manifests in mind,

children.text: tathākāśe ca kuḍye ca kasmānnābhipravartate // Lank_10.98 //
children.translated_text: so [why does it not manifest] in space and on a wall — why does it not operate [there]? || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.98 ||
If mind operates by grasping some sign [as its support],

children.text: pratyayairjanitaṃ cittaṃ cittamātraṃ na yujyate // Lank_10.99 //
children.translated_text: then mind produced by conditions — mind-only would not be tenable. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.99 ||
Mind is grasped by mind; there is nothing whatsoever with cause;

children.text: cittasya dharmatā śuddhā gagane nāsti vāsanā // Lank_10.100 //
children.translated_text: the <s>dharmatā</s> (nature) of mind is pure — in space there are no impressions. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.100 ||
Through the fixation on one's own mind, mind indeed operates;

children.text: bahirdhā nāsti vai dṛśyamato vai cittamātrakam // Lank_10.101 //
children.translated_text: externally there is no visible [reality] — therefore it is mind-only. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.101 ||
