Mind is <s>ālayavijñāna</s> (store-consciousness); <s>manas</s> is that which has the nature of thinking;

children.text: gṛhṇāti viṣayān yena vijñānaṃ hi taducyate // Lank_10.102 //
children.translated_text: that by which it grasps objects — that is called consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>). || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.102 ||
Mind is always indeterminate; <s>manas</s> moves in both [ways];

children.text: vartamānaṃ hi vijñānaṃ kuśalākuśalaṃ hi tat // Lank_10.103 //
children.translated_text: For consciousness that is operating is indeed wholesome and unwholesome. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.103 ||
The gate of the supreme meaning is free from the duality of representation;
how can the establishment of three vehicles be situated in the imageless? || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.104 ||
Mind-only, imageless, the abodes and the <s>Buddha</s>-stage —

children.text: etaddhi bhāṣitaṃ buddhairbhāṣante bhāṣayanti ca // Lank_10.105 //
children.translated_text: this has been spoken by <s>Buddhas</s>, they speak it and cause it to be spoken. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.105 ||

children.text: cittaṃ hi bhūmayaḥ sapta nirābhāsā ca aṣṭamī /
children.translated_text: Mind is the seven stages; the imageless is the eighth;

children.text: dve bhūmayo vihāraśca śeṣā bhūmirmamātmikā // Lank_10.106 //
children.translated_text: two stages are the abode, and the remaining stage is my own. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.106 ||
Self-realized and pure, that stage too is my own;
the supreme abode of <s>Maheśvara</s>, it shines in <s>Akaniṣṭha</s>. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.107 ||
Just as from fire itself its rays emerge —

children.text: citrā manoharāḥ saumyāstribhavaṃ nirmiṇanti ye // Lank_10.108 //
children.translated_text: variegated, captivating, and gentle — those that emanate the three realms of existence. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.108 ||
Having emanated the three realms in part, and in part what was previously emanated,

children.text: tatra deśanti yānāni eṣā bhūmirmamātmikā // Lank_10.109 //
children.translated_text: there they teach the vehicles — this is my own stage. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.109 ||
There is no time indeed in the realization of the stages or in the transition across fields;
having transcended mind-only, the fruit is established in the imageless. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.110 ||

children.text: asattā caiva sattā ca dṛśyate ca vicitratā /
children.translated_text: Non-existence and existence — and diversity is seen;

children.text: bālā grāhaviparyastā viparyāso hi citratā // Lank_10.111 //
children.translated_text: the childish are confused by wrong grasping, for confusion is indeed diversity. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.111 ||

children.text: nirvikalpaṃ yadi jñānaṃ vastvastīti na yujyate /
children.translated_text: If knowledge is non-discriminative, it is not correct to say a thing exists;

children.text: yasmāccittaṃ na rūpāṇi nirvikalpaṃ hi tena tat // Lank_10.112 //
children.translated_text: since mind is not [the same as] forms, therefore it is non-discriminative. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.112 ||
The sense-faculties are called illusion; the objects resemble dreams;

children.text: kartā karma kriyā caiva sarvathāpi na vidyate // Lank_10.113 //
children.translated_text: agent, action, and activity — in every way they do not exist. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.113 ||
The <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations) and the immeasurables, the formless attainments and <s>samādhis</s>,
and the cessation of perception in its entirety — do not exist in mind-only. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.114 ||
The fruit of stream-entry, and likewise the fruit of once-returning,
and the fruit of non-returning, and <s>arhat</s>-ship — [all these are] the confusion of mind. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.115 ||
The childish conceptualize the conditioned as empty, impermanent, and momentary;
by analogies of the river, lamp, and the like, the meaning of momentariness is conceptualized. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.116 ||
Inactive, momentary, free [from elaboration], devoid of activity —

children.text: anutpattiṃ ca dharmāṇāṃ kṣaṇikārthaṃ vadāmyahyam // Lank_10.117 //
children.translated_text: and the non-arising of <s>dharmas</s> — [this] meaning of momentariness I declare. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.117 ||
Non-arising from the existent and non-existent is asserted by the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s> and <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s>;

children.text: avyākṛtāni sarvāṇi taireva hi prakāśitam // Lank_10.118 //
children.translated_text: all [questions] are undetermined — this has been made clear by them alone. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.118 ||
There are four kinds of answers: the categorical response to a question,
the analytical, the setting aside — and the refutation of heretical doctrines. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.119 ||

children.text: sarvaṃ vidyati saṃvṛtyāṃ paramārthe na vidyate /
children.translated_text: Everything exists in conventional [truth]; in the ultimate it does not exist;
the essencelessness of <s>dharmas</s> is seen even in the ultimate;
since apprehension is essenceless, therefore it is called conventional. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.120 ||
If an entity exists whose inherent nature is caused by verbal expression,

children.text: abhilāpasaṃbhavo bhāvo nāstīti ca na vidyate // Lank_10.121 //
children.translated_text: then an entity arising from verbal expression would not be non-existent. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.121 ||
But verbal expression is without substance — therefore even conventionally it does not exist;
because error has substantiality, apprehension does not exist. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.122 ||
If error exists, then essencelessness does not exist;
because error has substantiality, whatever is apprehended

children.text: niḥsvabhāvaṃ bhavettaddhi sarvathāpi na vidyate // Lank_10.123 //
children.translated_text: would be essenceless — thus in every way it does not exist. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.123 ||
This diversity that is seen — mind perfumed by depravity —
the grasping of the appearance of form is the external confusion of mind. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.124 ||
Through discrimination, by non-discrimination, discrimination is indeed abandoned;
through discrimination, by non-discrimination — the seeing of the reality of emptiness. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.125 ||

children.text: māyāhastī yathā citraṃ patrāṇi kanakā yathā /
children.translated_text: Like an illusory elephant, like a painting, like leaves [that appear as] gold —

children.text: tathā dṛśyaṃ nṛṇāṃ khyāti citte ajñānavāsite // Lank_10.126 //
children.translated_text: so the visible appears to humans, in a mind perfumed by ignorance. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.126 ||

children.text: āryo na paśyate bhrāntiṃ nāpi tattvaṃ tadantare /
children.translated_text: The noble one sees neither error nor reality therein;
error itself would be reality, since reality is therein. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.127 ||

children.text: bhrāntiṃ vidhūya sarvāṃ tu nimittaṃ yadi jāyate /
children.translated_text: If, having dispelled all error, a sign arises —

children.text: saiva cāsya bhavedbhrāntiraśuddhaṃ timiraṃ yathā // Lank_10.128 //
children.translated_text: that itself would be error for him, like impure cataract-vision. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.128 ||
Just as one with cataract grasps a hair-net through confusion,
so for the childish, grasping operates with respect to objects. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.129 ||
This [world] resembles a hair-net, the confusion of a mirage-water;
the three realms resemble a dream and illusion — one who discerns [this] is liberated. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.130 ||
Discrimination and what is discriminated, and the operation of discrimination,

children.text: bandho bandhyaśca baddhaśca ṣaḍete mokṣahetavaḥ // Lank_10.131 //
children.translated_text: bondage, what is to be bound, and the bound — these six are the causes of liberation. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.131 ||

children.text: na bhūmayo na satyāni na kṣetrā na ca nirmitāḥ /
children.translated_text: There are no stages, no truths, no fields, and no emanations;
<s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and <s>Śrāvakas</s> too are conceptualized. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.132 ||
Person, continuum, aggregates, conditions, and atoms likewise,
<s>Pradhāna</s> (Primal Matter), <s>Īśvara</s> (God), the agent — [all these are] conceptualized in mind-only. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.133 ||

children.text: cittaṃ hi sarvaṃ sarvatra sarvadeheṣu vartate /
children.translated_text: Mind is indeed everything, everywhere, operating in all bodies;
diversity is grasped by the unwise, but mind-only is without characteristics. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.134 ||

children.text: na hyātmā vidyate skandhe skandhāścaiva hi nātmani /
children.translated_text: The self does not exist in the aggregates, nor are the aggregates in the self;

children.text: na te yathā vikalpyante na ca te vai na santi ca // Lank_10.135 //
children.translated_text: they do not exist as they are conceptualized, yet they are not non-existent either. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.135 ||
The existence of all entities, as conceptualized by the childish —

children.text: yadi te bhavedyathādṛṣṭāḥ sarve syustattvadarśinaḥ // Lank_10.136 //
children.translated_text: if they existed as seen, all would be seers of truth. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.136 ||
Because of the non-existence of all <s>dharmas</s>, there is neither defilement nor purification;

children.text: na ca te tathā yathādṛṣṭā na ca te vai na santi ca // Lank_10.137 //
children.translated_text: they do not exist as they are seen, yet they are not non-existent either. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.137 ||
Error, sign, and conceptualization — [these are] the characteristic of the other-dependent (<s>paratantra</s>);
in that sign, whatever is a name — that is the characteristic of the imagined (<s>parikalpita</s>). || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.138 ||
When the conceptualization of name and sign does not arise for that [mind],
the signification of conditions and non-substance — [that is] the characteristic of the perfected (<s>pariniṣpanna</s>). || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.139 ||

children.text: vaipākikāśca ye buddhā jinā nairmāṇikāśca ye /
children.translated_text: Those <s>Buddhas</s> who are fruition-bodies (<s>vaipākika</s>), and those <s>Jinas</s> who are emanations (<s>nairmāṇika</s>),

children.text: sattvāśca bodhisattvāśca kṣetrāṇi ca diśe diśe // Lank_10.140 //
children.translated_text: and beings and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, and fields in every direction — || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.140 ||
The outflow-<s>dharma</s>-emanations and those <s>Jinas</s> who are emanations —

children.text: sarve te hyamitābhasya sukhāvatyā vinirgatāḥ // Lank_10.141 //
children.translated_text: all of them have gone forth from <s>Amitābha</s>'s <s>Sukhāvatī</s>. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.141 ||
What has been spoken by the emanation[-bodies] and what has been spoken by the fruition[-bodies] —
know the intended purport (<s>saṃdhi</s>) of the method of <s>sūtrānta</s> and <s>vaipulya</s>. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.142 ||
What has been spoken by the sons of the <s>Jina</s>, and what the guides speak,

children.text: yaddhi nairmāṇikābhāṣṭaṃ na tu vaipākikairjinaiḥ // Lank_10.143 //
children.translated_text: what indeed was spoken by the emanation[-bodies] — but not by the fruition-<s>Jinas</s>. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.143 ||

children.text: anutpannā hyamī dharmā na caivaite na santi ca /
children.translated_text: These <s>dharmas</s> are indeed unborn, and they are not non-existent either;
they resemble a <s>Gandharva</s>-city, a dream, illusion, and emanation. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.144 ||
Mind operates, mind — and by mind alone one is liberated;

children.text: cittaṃ hi jāyate nānyaccittameva nirudhyate // Lank_10.145 //
children.translated_text: mind indeed arises, not another — mind alone ceases. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.145 ||

children.text: arthābhāsaṃ nṛṇāṃ cittaṃ cittaṃ vai khyāti kalpitam /
children.translated_text: The mind of humans has the appearance of objects; mind appears as the imagined;
there is no [external] object — this is mind-only; the non-discriminative one is liberated. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.146 ||
The depravity of proliferation since beginningless time is indeed accumulated;
discrimination, having been cultivated by that, operates as false appearance. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.147 ||
In the consciousness that has the appearance of objects, knowledge has suchness as its domain;
turned about, imageless — it is in the domain of the noble ones. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.148 ||
Meditation on the investigation of meaning, meditation for the practice of the childish,

children.text: tathatārambaṇaṃ dhyānaṃ dhyānaṃ tāthāgataṃ śubham // Lank_10.149 //
children.translated_text: meditation with suchness as its object, the auspicious <s>Tathāgata</s>-meditation. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.149 ||
By the imagined inherent nature, all <s>dharmas</s> are unknowing;

children.text: paratantraṃ samāśritya vikalpo bhramate nṛṇām // Lank_10.150 //
children.translated_text: depending on the other-dependent, discrimination confuses humans. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.150 ||
When the other-dependent is purified, dissociated from discrimination,

children.text: parāvṛttaṃ hi tathatā vihāraḥ kalpavarjitaḥ // Lank_10.151 //
children.translated_text: turned about, it is suchness — the abode free from conceptualization. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.151 ||

children.text: mā vikalpaṃ vikalpetha vikalpo nāsti satyataḥ /
children.translated_text: Do not conceptualize discrimination! Discrimination does not exist in truth;
for one who conceptualizes error regarding the grasped and the grasper, there is not [liberation];
the seeing of external objects is conceptualization — the inherent nature is imagined. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.152 ||
By whichever conceptualization they conceptualize — the inherent nature arises from conditions;

children.text: bāhyārthadarśanaṃ mithyā nāstyarthaṃ cittameva tu // Lank_10.153 //
children.translated_text: the seeing of external objects is false — there is no [external] object, but mind alone. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.153 ||
For those who investigate with reasoning, the grasped and the grasper cease;

children.text: bāhyo na vidyate hyartho yathā bālairvikalpyate // Lank_10.154 //
children.translated_text: external objects do not exist, as conceptualized by the childish. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.154 ||
Mind, disturbed by impressions, operates as the appearance of objects;
by the cessation of twofold conceptualization, knowledge has suchness as its domain. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.155 ||
It arises as imageless, inconceivable, in the domain of the noble ones;
the conceptualization of name and sign — [that is] the characteristic of the two inherent natures;
correct knowledge, which is suchness — [that is] the characteristic of the perfected. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.156 ||
From the union of mother and father, conjoined with <s>ālaya</s> and <s>manas</s>,

children.text: ghṛtakumbhe mūṣikā yadvatsaha śukreṇa vardhate // Lank_10.157 //
children.translated_text: like a mouse in a ghee-pot, it grows together with the semen. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.157 ||
The fleshy embryo, the lump, the swelling (<s>piṭaka</s>) — foul, variegated by <s>karma</s> —
through the great elements [driven by] the wind of <s>karma</s>, it develops like a fruit. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.158 ||
Five and five and five, and nine openings,
covered with nails, teeth, and hair — [the being] is born, quivering. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.159 ||
As soon as born, like a worm in excrement, like a man asleep-then-awake,

children.text: cakṣuṣā sphurate rūpaṃ vivṛddhiṃ yāti kalpanāt // Lank_10.160 //
children.translated_text: with the eye form flickers forth — and it grows through conceptualization. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.160 ||
Through the conjunction of palate, lips, and cheeks, and grasped by discrimination,

children.text: vācā pravartate nṝṇāṃ śukasyeva vikalpanā // Lank_10.161 //
children.translated_text: speech operates for humans — [mere] conceptualization, like that of a parrot. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.161 ||
The doctrines of heretical teachers are certain; the <s>Mahāyāna</s> is uncertain [to them];
this [teaching] operates based on the support of beings — for those with wrong views it is no foundation. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.162 ||
My vehicle of self-realization is beyond the domain of logicians;

children.text: paścātkāle gate nāthe brūhi ko 'yaṃ dhariṣyati // Lank_10.163 //
children.translated_text: when the Master has departed in the future time, tell me — who will uphold it? || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.163 ||
After the <s>Sugata</s> has entered <s>nirvāṇa</s>, a time will come in the future;

children.text: mahāmate nibodha tvaṃ yo netrīṃ dhārayiṣyati // Lank_10.164 //
children.translated_text: understand, O <s>Mahāmati</s> — who will uphold the guidance. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.164 ||
In <s>Vedalī</s> of the southern region, a monk, glorious and of great fame,

children.text: nāgāhvayaḥ sa nāmnā tu sadasatpakṣadārakaḥ // Lank_10.165 //
children.translated_text: named <s>Nāga</s> by name — he who destroys the positions of existence and non-existence. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.165 ||
Having illuminated my vehicle in the world, the supreme <s>Mahāyāna</s>,

children.text: āsādya bhūmiṃ muditāṃ yāsyate 'sau sukhāvatīm // Lank_10.166 //
children.translated_text: having attained the Joyous Stage (<s>Muditā bhūmi</s>), he will go to <s>Sukhāvatī</s>. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.166 ||
For those who investigate by intellect, the inherent nature is not ascertained;
since that [reality] is inexpressible, [<s>dharmas</s>] have been taught as essenceless. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.167 ||
In an entity produced by conditions, neither 'exists' nor 'does not exist' is found;

children.text: pratyayāntargataṃ bhāvaṃ ye kalpentyasti nāsti ca /
children.translated_text: those who conceptualize an entity contained within conditions as existing or not existing —
they, I think, have strayed far from the teaching, [holding] heretical views. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.168 ||
The designation of all entities, through hundreds of births always
practiced and being practiced — through mutual conceptualization. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.169 ||
When [names] are not spoken, the whole world falls into delusion;
therefore names are made, for the purpose of dispelling delusion. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.170 ||
By threefold discrimination, entities are conceptualized by the childish;
error is [produced] by name-discrimination, and by that which is born from conditions. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.171 ||
Unceased and unborn, by nature resembling space,

children.text: abhāvasvabhāvā ye tu te vikalpitalakṣaṇāḥ // Lank_10.172 //
children.translated_text: those whose inherent nature is non-existence — they have the characteristic of the imagined. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.172 ||
Resembling a reflection, an image, illusion, a mirage, and a dream,
of the same origin as a whirling firebrand, a <s>Gandharva</s>[-city], and an echo — || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.173 ||
Non-dual, suchness, emptiness, the limit of reality (<s>bhūtakoṭi</s>), and the nature of <s>dharma</s> (<s>dharmatā</s>) —

children.text: nirvikalpaśca deśemi ye te niṣpannalakṣaṇāḥ // Lank_10.174 //
children.translated_text: And I teach the non-discriminative — those that have the perfected characteristic. [Laṅk 10.174]
The domain of speech and mind is false; truly, wisdom is conceptualized.

children.text: dvayāntapatitaṃ cittaṃ tasmātprajñā na kalpitā // Lank_10.175 //
children.translated_text: The mind falls into the two extremes; therefore wisdom is not conceptualized. [Laṅk 10.175]

children.text: asti nāsti ca dvāvantau yāvaccittasya gocaraḥ /
children.translated_text: "It exists" and "it does not exist" — two extremes — so long as there is a domain of the mind;
when the domain is swept away, the mind is properly ceased. [Laṅk 10.176]
From the absence of grasping at objects, and through cessation, [the world] does not exist;

children.text: vidyate tathatāvasthā āryāṇāṃ gocaro yathā // Lank_10.177 //
children.translated_text: the state of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) exists, as the domain of the noble ones. [Laṅk 10.177]

children.text: bālānāṃ na tathā khyāti yathā khyāti manīṣiṇām /
children.translated_text: For the childish, things do not appear as they appear to the wise;

children.text: manīṣiṇāṃ tathā khyāti sarvadharmā alakṣaṇāḥ // Lank_10.178 //
children.translated_text: for the wise, all <s>dharmas</s> appear thus — without characteristics. [Laṅk 10.178]
Just as brass is imagined by the childish to be gold,

children.text: asuvarṇaṃ suvarṇābhaṃ tathā dharmāḥ kutārkikaiḥ // Lank_10.179 //
children.translated_text: not-gold appearing like gold — so are <s>dharmas</s> [viewed] by the wrong logicians. [Laṅk 10.179]

children.text: abhūtvā yasya cotpādo bhūtvā cāpi vinaśyati /
children.translated_text: That which, not having existed, arises, and having existed, perishes,

children.text: pratyayaiḥ sadasaccāpi na te me śāsane sthitāḥ // Lank_10.180 //
children.translated_text: being both existent and non-existent through conditions — those do not stand in my teaching. [Laṅk 10.180]
Established in the characteristics of reality, without beginning and without end,

children.text: kāraṇakaravalloke na ca budhyanti tārkikāḥ // Lank_10.181 //
children.translated_text: like cause and effect in the world — the logicians do not understand. [Laṅk 10.181]

children.text: atīto vidyate bhāvo vidyate ca anāgataḥ /
children.translated_text: The past entity exists, and the future also exists;
since the present exists — therefore, entities are unborn. [Laṅk 10.182]
Those who conceive of transformation, time, and configuration in elements, entities, and sense-faculties,

children.text: antarābhavasaṃgrāhaṃ ye kalpanti na te budhāḥ // Lank_10.183 //
children.translated_text: and the intermediate state — they are not the wise. [Laṅk 10.183]

children.text: na pratītyasamutpannaṃ lokaṃ varṇanti vai jināḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>Jinas</s> (Victorious Ones) do not describe the world as arisen from dependent origination;

children.text: kiṃ tu pratyayamevāyaṃ loko gandharvasaṃnibhaḥ // Lank_10.184 //
children.translated_text: but this world, merely conditioned, is like a <s>gandharva</s> [city]. [Laṅk 10.184]
This is merely a conventional designation of <s>dharma</s> — in it, "this depends on that" is said;

children.text: saṃketācca pṛthagbhūto na jāto na nirudhyate // Lank_10.185 //
children.translated_text: and being separate from convention, it neither arises nor ceases. [Laṅk 10.185]

children.text: darpaṇe udake netre bhāṇḍeṣu ca maṇīṣu ca /
children.translated_text: In a mirror, in water, in the eye, in vessels, and in jewels,

children.text: bimbaṃ hi dṛśyate teṣu na ca bimbo 'sti kutracit // Lank_10.186 //
children.translated_text: a reflection is seen in them, but the reflection does not exist anywhere. [Laṅk 10.186]

children.text: bhāvābhāsaṃ tathā cittaṃ mṛgatṛṣṇā yathā nabhe /
children.translated_text: The mind likewise [produces] the appearance of entities, like a mirage in the sky;

children.text: dṛśyate citrarūpeṇa svapne vandhyauraso yathā // Lank_10.187 //
children.translated_text: it is seen with diverse forms, like a barren woman's son in a dream. [Laṅk 10.187]

children.text: na me yānaṃ mahāyānaṃ na ghoṣo na ca akṣarāḥ /
children.translated_text: I have no vehicle, no <s>Mahāyāna</s>, no sound, and no syllables,

children.text: na satyā na vimokṣā vai na nirābhāsagocaram // Lank_10.188 //
children.translated_text: no truths, no liberations — no domain of imagelessness. [Laṅk 10.188]
But the vehicle, the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, operates through the power of <s>samādhi</s>,
the variegated body made of mind, adorned with the flowers of mastery. [Laṅk 10.189]

children.text: ekatvena pṛthaktvena bhāvo vai pratyaye na tu /
children.translated_text: An entity is not [produced] by oneness or separateness in a condition;

children.text: janma samāsamevoktaṃ nirodho nāśa eva hi // Lank_10.190 //
children.translated_text: birth is declared to be equal and unequal; cessation is indeed destruction. [Laṅk 10.190]
The emptiness of the unborn is one; the emptiness in what has arisen is one [too].
The emptiness of the unborn is supreme; the emptiness of what has arisen perishes. [Laṅk 10.191]
<s>Tathatā</s> (suchness), <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), the limit [of reality], <s>nirvāṇa</s>, like the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of <s>dharma</s>),

children.text: kāyo manomayaṃ citraṃ paryāyairdeśitaṃ mayā // Lank_10.192 //
children.translated_text: the variegated body made of mind — [all] have been taught by me in synonyms. [Laṅk 10.192]
Those who conceive of purification through <s>sūtra</s>, <s>vinaya</s>, and <s>abhidharma</s>

children.text: granthato na tu arthena na te nairātmyamāśritāḥ // Lank_10.193 //
children.translated_text: by the letter, not by the meaning — they have not taken refuge in selflessness. [Laṅk 10.193]

children.text: na tīrthikairna buddhaiśca na mayā na ca kenacit /
children.translated_text: Neither by the heretical teachers, nor by the <s>Buddhas</s>, nor by me, nor by anyone
has existence been established through conditions — how then could non-existence be? [Laṅk 10.194]
By whom has existence been established? — for which there is non-existence through conditions;
through the wrong view of the doctrine of arising, one discriminates "it does not exist" and "it exists." [Laṅk 10.195]
For one for whom nothing arises and nothing ceases,

children.text: tasyāstināsti nopaiti viviktaṃ paśyato jagat // Lank_10.196 //
children.translated_text: "it exists" and "it does not exist" do not apply — for one who sees the world as isolated. [Laṅk 10.196]
What is called a hare's horn is perceived; discrimination exists among people.

children.text: ye tu kalpenti te bhrāntā mṛgatṛṣṇāṃ yathā mṛgāḥ // Lank_10.197 //
children.translated_text: But those who conceptualize are deluded, like deer [chasing] a mirage. [Laṅk 10.197]
Through attachment to conceptualization, conceptualization operates;

children.text: nirhetukaṃ vikalpaṃ hi vikalpo 'pi na yujyate // Lank_10.198 //
children.translated_text: but since conceptualization is without cause, conceptualization too is not tenable. [Laṅk 10.198]

children.text: ajale ca jalagrāho mṛgatṛṣṇā yathā nabhe /
children.translated_text: Just as the grasping of water where there is no water, like a mirage in the sky —

children.text: dṛśyate 'rtho hi bālānāmāryāṇāṃ na viśeṣataḥ // Lank_10.199 //
children.translated_text: objects are seen by the childish, but not distinctly by the noble ones. [Laṅk 10.199]
The vision of the noble ones is pure, arisen from the three liberations,
freed from arising and destruction, moving in the imageless. [Laṅk 10.200]
The depth, nobility, and breadth [of teaching]; knowledge, fields, and powers —
I teach to the sons of the <s>Jinas</s>; impermanence to the <s>Śrāvakas</s>. [Laṅk 10.201]
The three realms are impermanent, empty, free from self and what belongs to self;

children.text: śrāvakāṇāṃ ca deśemi tathā sāmānyalakṣaṇam // Lank_10.202 //
children.translated_text: and likewise I teach the general characteristic to the <s>Śrāvakas</s>. [Laṅk 10.202]
Non-attachment to all <s>dharmas</s>, detachment, and solitary wandering —
the fruit for the sons of the <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> I teach, beyond logic. [Laṅk 10.203]
External [objects are] conceptualized by inherent nature, and dependent for embodied beings;
not seeing the confusion of self, consciousness then operates. [Laṅk 10.204]

children.text: daśamī tu bhavetprathamī prathamī cāṣṭamī bhavet /
children.translated_text: The tenth [stage] would be the first, and the first would be the eighth;

children.text: navamī saptamī cāpi saptamī cāṣṭamī bhavet // Lank_10.205 //
children.translated_text: the ninth [would be] the seventh, and the seventh would be the eighth. [Laṅk 10.205]

children.text: dvitīyā tu tṛtīyā syāccaturthī pañcamī bhavet /
children.translated_text: The second would be the third, and the fourth would be the fifth;

children.text: tṛtīyā tu bhavetṣaṣṭhī nirābhāse kramaḥ kutaḥ // Lank_10.206 //
children.translated_text: the third would be the sixth — in the imageless, where is there sequence? [Laṅk 10.206]
The imageless of entities — non-existence does not exist for <s>yogins</s>;
through the equality of existence and non-existence, the fruit arises for the noble ones. [Laṅk 10.207]

children.text: kathaṃ hyabhāvo bhāvānāṃ kurute samatāṃ katham /
children.translated_text: How indeed could there be non-existence of entities? How could there be equality?

children.text: yadā cittaṃ na jānāti bāhyamadhyātmikaṃ calam /
children.translated_text: When the mind does not know external or internal movement,

children.text: tadā tu kurute nāśaṃ samatācittadarśanāt // Lank_10.208 //
children.translated_text: then it makes cessation, from the vision of the mind of equality. [Laṅk 10.208]
In beginningless <s>saṃsāra</s>, embraced by the grasping of entities,

children.text: bālaiḥ kīla yathā kīlaṃ pralobhya vinivartate // Lank_10.209 //
children.translated_text: for the childish, like a peg by a peg, one is enticed and turns back. [Laṅk 10.209]
Having that as cause, having that as object, relying on the movement of <s>manas</s> (mentation),

children.text: hetuṃ dadāti cittasya vijñānaṃ ca samāśritam // Lank_10.210 //
children.translated_text: consciousness, relying [on it], gives rise to the cause of the mind. [Laṅk 10.210]
From the basis of the matured [consciousness], from the arising of the courses of existence,

children.text: labhyante yena vai svapne abhijñāśca caturvidhāḥ // Lank_10.211 //
children.translated_text: the fourfold <s>abhijñā</s> (superknowledges) are obtained in dreams. [Laṅk 10.211]

children.text: svapne ca labhyate yacca yacca buddhaprasādataḥ /
children.translated_text: What is obtained in dreams and what [is obtained] through the grace of the <s>Buddhas</s> —
the lineages of the courses of existence are born from the maturation of consciousness. [Laṅk 10.212]
The mind, cultivated by impressions, operates with the appearance of entities;

children.text: bālā yadā na budhyante utpādaṃ deśayettadā // Lank_10.213 //
children.translated_text: when the childish do not understand, then I teach arising. [Laṅk 10.213]
So long as one conceptualizes speech, and entities endowed with characteristics,
so long does the mind operate without understanding, not seeing its own error. [Laṅk 10.214]
Why is arising described? Why is the visible not described?

children.text: adṛśyaṃ dṛśyamānaṃ hi kasya kiṃ varṇyate kutaḥ // Lank_10.215 //
children.translated_text: For the invisible is [what is] being seen — whose what is described and from where? [Laṅk 10.215]
The mind is pure by its own nature; <s>manas</s> (mentation) is the defiler.
<s>Manas</s>, together with the [five] consciousnesses, always projects impressions. [Laṅk 10.216]

children.text: ālayo muñcate kāyaṃ manaḥ prārthayate gatim /
children.translated_text: The <s>ālaya</s> (store-consciousness) releases the body; <s>manas</s> seeks a [new] course [of rebirth];

children.text: vijñānaṃ viṣayābhāsaṃ bhrāntiṃ dṛṣṭvā pralabhyate // Lank_10.217 //
children.translated_text: consciousness, [producing] the appearance of objects, is obtained — having seen the error. [Laṅk 10.217]

children.text: madīyaṃ dṛśyate cittaṃ bāhyamarthaṃ na vidyate /
children.translated_text: What is seen is my mind; external objects do not exist.
Thus one should discern the error and also recollect <s>tathatā</s> (suchness). [Laṅk 10.218]
The domain of meditators, <s>karma</s> (action), and the greatness of the <s>Buddhas</s> —
these three are inconceivable; inconceivable is the domain of consciousness. [Laṅk 10.219]
The future, the past, <s>nirvāṇa</s>, the person, and speech —
I teach these through conventional [truth]; but the ultimate truth is without syllables. [Laṅk 10.220]
The sectarians and the heretical teachers, attached to one-sided views,

children.text: cittamātre visaṃmūḍhā bhāvaṃ kalpenti bāhiram // Lank_10.221 //
children.translated_text: confused about mind-only, conceptualize external entities. [Laṅk 10.221]
<s>Pratyekabuddha</s>-enlightenment, <s>Buddhahood</s>, <s>Arhatship</s>, and seeing the <s>Buddha</s> —

children.text: gūḍhabījaṃ bhavedbodhau svapne vai sidhyate tu yaḥ // Lank_10.222 //
children.translated_text: the seed is hidden in enlightenment; it is accomplished in dreams. [Laṅk 10.222]

children.text: kutra keṣāṃ kathaṃ kasmātkimarthaṃ ca vadāhi me /
children.translated_text: Where, for whom, how, why, and for what purpose — tell me
about my mind, supremely peaceful, [and] the teaching of the sides of existent and non-existent. [Laṅk 10.223]
For those confused about mind-only — the illusory teaching of "does not exist" and "exists,"
conjoined with arising and destruction, free from the characterized and the characteristic. [Laṅk 10.224]

children.text: vikalpo mano nāma vijñānaiḥ pañcabhiḥ saha /
children.translated_text: Conceptualization is called <s>manas</s> (mentation), together with the five consciousnesses;
the seed of consciousness operates in what resembles reflections, floods, and water. [Laṅk 10.225]

children.text: yadā cittaṃ manaścāpi vijñānaṃ na pravartate /
children.translated_text: When mind, <s>manas</s>, and consciousness do not operate,

children.text: tadā manomayaṃ kāyaṃ labhate buddhabhūmi ca // Lank_10.226 //
children.translated_text: then one obtains the body made of mind and the <s>Buddha</s>-stage. [Laṅk 10.226]

children.text: pratyayā dhātavaḥ skandhā dharmāṇāṃ ca svalakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: Conditions, elements, aggregates, and the specific characteristics of <s>dharmas</s>,
designation, person, and mind — are like dreams and hair-balls. [Laṅk 10.227]
Having seen the world as like illusion and dreams, one should take refuge in the truth;
for truth is free from characteristics, devoid of reasoning and causes. [Laṅk 10.228]
One should always remember the abode of the noble ones, realized by oneself,
and establish the world, confused by reasoning and causes, in the truth. [Laṅk 10.229]
Through the subsiding of all conceptual proliferation, error does not operate;
as long as wisdom discriminates, so long does error operate. [Laṅk 10.230]

children.text: naiḥsvabhāvyaṃ ca bhāvaṃ ca śūnyā vai nityānityatā /
children.translated_text: Essencelessness and entity, emptiness, and permanence and impermanence —
this is the view of those who hold the doctrine of arising, not of those who hold the doctrine of non-arising. [Laṅk 10.231]
Through oneness, otherness, both, through <s>Īśvara</s>, through chance,
through time, <s>pradhāna</s> (primal matter), and other conditions — the world is conceptualized. [Laṅk 10.232]
Consciousness is the seed of <s>saṃsāra</s>; it operates when the visible exists.

children.text: kuḍye sati yathā citraṃ parijñānānnirudhyate // Lank_10.233 //
children.translated_text: Like a painting on a wall — it ceases through complete understanding. [Laṅk 10.233]
Like an illusory person, death and birth operate for people;
likewise, through delusion, bondage and liberation operate for the childish. [Laṅk 10.234]
Internal and external are twofold — <s>dharmas</s> and conditions;
the <s>yogin</s> who discerns this is established in the imageless. [Laṅk 10.235]

children.text: na vāsanairbhidyate cittaṃ na cittaṃ vāsanaiḥ saha /
children.translated_text: The mind is not divided by impressions, nor does the mind [exist] with impressions;
the mind, with undivided characteristics, is enveloped by impressions. [Laṅk 10.236]
For one whose impressions, arising from <s>manas</s> and consciousness, are like impurities,
the mind, like white cloth, does not shine due to the impressions. [Laṅk 10.237]

children.text: yathā na bhāvo nābhāvo gaganaṃ kathyate mayā /
children.translated_text: Just as space is described by me as neither existent nor non-existent,

children.text: ālayaṃ hi tathā kāye bhāvābhāvavivarjitam // Lank_10.238 //
children.translated_text: so is the <s>ālaya</s> (store-consciousness) in the body — free from existence and non-existence. [Laṅk 10.238]
The mind, turned away from <s>manas</s> and consciousness, is free from defilement.
Through the awakening to all <s>dharmas</s>, I declare the mind to be <s>Buddha</s>. [Laṅk 10.239]
Cut off by the three continuities, free from existence and non-existence,

children.text: cātuṣkoṭikayā muktaṃ bhavaṃ māyopamaṃ sadā // Lank_10.240 //
children.translated_text: freed from the fourfold [logical] alternative — existence is always like illusion. [Laṅk 10.240]
Two inherent natures and seven stages arise from the mind;

children.text: śeṣā bhaveyurniṣpannā bhūmayo buddhabhūmi ca // Lank_10.241 //
children.translated_text: the remaining stages and the <s>Buddha</s>-stage would be perfected. [Laṅk 10.241]
The form-realm, the formless realm, the desire-realm, and cessation —

children.text: asmin kalevare sarvaṃ kathitaṃ cittagocaram // Lank_10.242 //
children.translated_text: all this in this body has been described as the domain of mind. [Laṅk 10.242]
So long as something is apprehended, so long does error operate;

children.text: bhrāntiḥ svacittasaṃbodhānna pravartate na nivartate // Lank_10.243 //
children.translated_text: error, through the awakening to one's own mind, neither operates nor turns back. [Laṅk 10.243]
In non-arising, there is the absence of cause; in existence, there is the collection of <s>saṃsāra</s>.

children.text: māyādisadṛśaṃ paśyan lakṣaṇaṃ na vikalpayet // Lank_10.244 //
children.translated_text: Seeing [all] as resembling illusion and the like, one should not discriminate characteristics. [Laṅk 10.244]
Three vehicles, one vehicle, and no vehicle — I teach
for the childish of dull intellect, and the isolation of the noble ones. [Laṅk 10.245]
Arising is twofold for me — that of characteristics and of realization;
the method of reasoning is fourfold: the <s>siddhānta</s> (established conclusion) and the demonstration of logic. [Laṅk 10.246]
Through the distinctions of configuration and form, seeing error, one discriminates;
free from name and configuration — the inherent nature [is] the domain of the noble ones. [Laṅk 10.247]
So long as one conceptualizes through <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual discrimination), so long does the characteristic of the conceptualized [persist];
through the absence of conceptual construction, [reality's] inherent nature is the domain of the noble ones. [Laṅk 10.248]

children.text: nityaṃ ca śāśvataṃ tattvaṃ gotraṃ vastusvabhāvakam /
children.translated_text: The eternal and permanent reality, the <s>gotra</s> (lineage), the inherent nature of things —
<s>tathatā</s> (suchness), freed from mind and devoid of conceptual constructions. [Laṅk 10.249]

children.text: yadyadvastu na śuddhiḥ syātsaṃkleśo nāpi kasyacit /
children.translated_text: If there were no purification of any entity whatsoever, there would be no defilement of anyone either;
but since the mind is indeed purified, and defilement is also seen,
therefore reality must be an entity — pure, the domain of the noble ones. [Laṅk 10.250]
The world, arisen from conditions and devoid of conceptual constructions,
resembling illusion, dreams, and the like — those who see thus are liberated. [Laṅk 10.251]
The variegated impressions of <s>dauṣṭhulya</s> (psychic heaviness), conjoined with the mind,

children.text: bahirdhā dṛśyate nṝṇāṃ na hi cittasya dharmatā // Lank_10.252 //
children.translated_text: appear externally to people — but this is not the <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature) of mind. [Laṅk 10.252]

children.text: cittasya dharmatā śuddhā na cittaṃ bhrāntisaṃbhavam /
children.translated_text: The <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature) of mind is pure; mind is not born from error.

children.text: bhrāntiśca dauṣṭhulyamayī tena cittaṃ na dṛśyate // Lank_10.253 //
children.translated_text: Error consists of <s>dauṣṭhulya</s> (psychic heaviness); therefore mind is not seen [as it truly is]. [Laṅk 10.253]
Reality would be mere error; reality is not found elsewhere —

children.text: na saṃskāre na cānyatra kiṃ tu saṃskāradarśanāt // Lank_10.254 //
children.translated_text: not in the conditioned nor anywhere else — but because of seeing the conditioned [as real, error arises]. [Laṅk 10.254]
When one sees the conditioned as freed from the characterized and characteristics,

children.text: vidhūtaṃ hi bhavettena svacittaṃ paśyato jagat // Lank_10.255 //
children.translated_text: then, for one who sees the world as one's own mind, it is thoroughly purified. [Laṅk 10.255]
Having ascended to <s>cittamātra</s> (mind-only), one should not conceptualize external objects;
abiding in the support of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), one should transcend <s>cittamātra</s> (mind-only). [Laṅk 10.256]
Having transcended <s>cittamātra</s> (mind-only), one should transcend the imageless;

children.text: nirābhāsasthito yogī mahāyānaṃ sa paśyati // Lank_10.257 //
children.translated_text: the <s>yogī</s> established in the imageless sees the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. [Laṅk 10.257]
The effortless course is peaceful, purified by <s>praṇidhāna</s> (vows);

children.text: jñānamanātmakaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ nirābhāse na paśyati // Lank_10.258 //
children.translated_text: the supreme selfless knowledge — in the imageless one does not see [even that]. [Laṅk 10.258]
One should see the domain of mind, one should see the domain of knowledge,

children.text: prajñāyā gocaraṃ paśyellakṣaṇe na pramuhyate // Lank_10.259 //
children.translated_text: one should see the domain of wisdom — and one is not confused regarding characteristics. [Laṅk 10.259]
The truth of suffering belongs to the domain of mind; origination is the domain of knowledge;

children.text: dve satye buddhabhūmiśca prajñā yatra pravartate // Lank_10.260 //
children.translated_text: the two truths [cessation and path] are the <s>buddhabhūmi</s> (buddha-stage), where wisdom operates. [Laṅk 10.260]
The attainment of the fruit and <s>nirvāṇa</s>, and likewise the eightfold path —
through the awakening to all <s>dharmas</s>, the <s>buddhajñāna</s> (buddha-knowledge) is purified. [Laṅk 10.261]
The eye, form, light, space, and mind —
from these arises for people <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness), born from the <s>ālaya</s> (store-consciousness). [Laṅk 10.262]

children.text: grāhyaṃ grāho grahītā ca nāsti nāma hyavastukam /
children.translated_text: The graspable, grasping, and the grasper do not exist — name is without substance;

children.text: nirhetukaṃ vikalpaṃ ye manyanti hi na te budhāḥ // Lank_10.263 //
children.translated_text: those who consider conceptualization to be without cause are not the wise. [Laṅk 10.263]

children.text: arthe nāma hyasaṃbhūtamartho nāmni tathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: Name does not arise in the object, nor does the object [arise] in name;
one should not conceptualize conceptualization as arisen from cause and non-cause. [Laṅk 10.264]
The inherent nature of all entities is non-existent, and speech is likewise unreal;

children.text: śūnyatāṃ śūnyatārthaṃ vā bālo 'paśyan vidhāvati // Lank_10.265 //
children.translated_text: the fool, not seeing <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) or the meaning of emptiness, runs about [in confusion]. [Laṅk 10.265]
Having seen the establishment of truth through this method, the teaching is by designation;
unity established as fivefold — this truth is abandoned [by the wise]. [Laṅk 10.266]
Invulnerable to the <s>Māra</s> of proliferation, one should transcend existence and non-existence;
there is no desire for becoming — a false perception, from seeing selflessness. [Laṅk 10.267]
Eternalism with an agent is set in motion by mere argument;

children.text: satyaṃ paraṃ hyavaktavyaṃ nirodhe dharmadarśanam // Lank_10.268 //
children.translated_text: the supreme truth is inexpressible — in cessation is the seeing of <s>dharma</s>. [Laṅk 10.268]

children.text: ālayaṃ hi samāśritya mano vai saṃpravartate /
children.translated_text: Depending on the <s>ālaya</s> (store-consciousness), <s>manas</s> (mind) indeed operates;

children.text: cittaṃ manaśca saṃśritya vijñānaṃ saṃpravartate // Lank_10.269 //
children.translated_text: depending on <s>citta</s> (mind) and <s>manas</s>, <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) operates. [Laṅk 10.269]
Having superimposed superimposition, <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) is the <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature) of mind;
the <s>yogī</s> who discerns this attains the understanding of <s>cittamātra</s> (mind-only). [Laṅk 10.270]

children.text: manaśca lakṣaṇaṃ vastu nityānitye na manyate /
children.translated_text: <s>Manas</s> (mind), characteristics, and objects — one does not regard as permanent or impermanent;

children.text: utpādaṃ cāpyanutpādaṃ yogī yoge na manyate // Lank_10.271 //
children.translated_text: the <s>yogī</s> in <s>yoga</s> does not regard either arising or non-arising. [Laṅk 10.271]
They do not conceptualize a duality of objects — <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) is born from the <s>ālaya</s>;

children.text: ekamarthaṃ dvicittena na jānīte tadudbhavam // Lank_10.272 //
children.translated_text: one does not know a single object through a dual mind — that arises from it. [Laṅk 10.272]

children.text: na vaktā na ca vācyo 'sti na śūnyaṃ cittadarśanāt /
children.translated_text: There is neither a speaker nor what is spoken; nor is [mind] empty, because of the seeing of mind;
from the non-seeing of one's own mind, the net of views operates. [Laṅk 10.273]
There is no coming of conditions; the sense faculties are nothing at all;

children.text: na dhātavo na ca skandhā na rāgo na ca saṃskṛtam // Lank_10.274 //
children.translated_text: there are no elements and no aggregates, no passion and nothing conditioned. [Laṅk 10.274]

children.text: karmaṇo 'gniṃ na vai pūrvaṃ na kṛtaṃ na ca saṃskṛtam /
children.translated_text: There is no fire prior to action, nothing done and nothing conditioned;

children.text: na koṭi na ca vai śaktirna mokṣo na ca bandhanam // Lank_10.275 //
children.translated_text: there is no limit and no power, no liberation and no bondage. [Laṅk 10.275]

children.text: avyākṛto na bhāvo 'sti dharmādharmaṃ na caiva hi /
children.translated_text: There is no undeclared entity, and neither merit nor demerit;

children.text: na kālaṃ na ca nirvāṇaṃ dharmatāpi na vidyate // Lank_10.276 //
children.translated_text: there is no time and no <s>nirvāṇa</s>, and <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature) too is not found. [Laṅk 10.276]

children.text: na ca buddho na satyāni na phalaṃ na ca hetavaḥ /
children.translated_text: There is no <s>Buddha</s> and no truths, no fruit and no causes;

children.text: viparyayo na nirvāṇaṃ vibhavo nāsti saṃbhavaḥ // Lank_10.277 //
children.translated_text: error is not <s>nirvāṇa</s>, there is no dissolution and no arising. [Laṅk 10.277]

children.text: dvādaśāṅgaṃ na caivāsti antānantaṃ na caiva hi /
children.translated_text: There is no twelvefold [dependent origination], and no finitude or infinitude either;
for the abandonment of all views, I teach <s>cittamātra</s> (mind-only). [Laṅk 10.278]

children.text: kleśāḥ karmapathā dehaḥ kartāraśca phalaṃ ca vai /
children.translated_text: <s>Kleśas</s> (afflictions), paths of action, bodies, agents, and fruits —
are like mirages and dreams, comparable to a <s>gandharva</s>-city. [Laṅk 10.279]
Through the establishment of <s>cittamātra</s> (mind-only), the characteristic of entities is turned away from duality;
through the establishment of <s>cittamātra</s> (mind-only), the views of eternalism and annihilationism [are overcome]. [Laṅk 10.280]

children.text: skandhā na santi nirvāṇe na caivātmā na lakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: The aggregates do not exist in <s>nirvāṇa</s>, and neither self nor characteristics;
through the descent into <s>cittamātra</s> (mind-only), one turns back from the grasping of liberation. [Laṅk 10.281]
The fault of the cause of appearance of an existent world appears externally to people;

children.text: cittaṃ hyadṛśyasaṃbhūtaṃ tena cittaṃ na dṛśyate // Lank_10.282 //
children.translated_text: mind is born from the invisible — therefore mind is not seen. [Laṅk 10.282]
The impressions, established in body and enjoyment, appear to people;

children.text: cittaṃ na bhāvo nābhāvo vāsane na virājate // Lank_10.283 //
children.translated_text: mind is neither entity nor non-entity — impressions do not shine [in it]. [Laṅk 10.283]

children.text: malo vai khyāyate śukle na śukle khyāyate malaḥ /
children.translated_text: Impurity appears in the pure; impurity does not appear in the pure [itself];

children.text: ghane hi gaganaṃ yadvattathā cittaṃ na dṛśyate // Lank_10.284 //
children.translated_text: just as the sky [is not seen] in dense [clouds], so mind is not seen. [Laṅk 10.284]

children.text: cittena cīyate karma jñānena ca vicīyate /
children.translated_text: <s>Karma</s> (action) is accumulated by mind, and by knowledge it is dispersed;

children.text: prajñayā ca nirābhāsaṃ prabhāvaṃ cādhigacchati // Lank_10.285 //
children.translated_text: through wisdom, the imageless, one attains sovereignty. [Laṅk 10.285]
Mind is bound to objects; knowledge operates in reasoning;

children.text: nirābhāse viśeṣe ca jñānaṃ vai saṃpravartate // Lank_10.286 //
children.translated_text: in the imageless and in distinction, knowledge indeed operates. [Laṅk 10.286]

children.text: cittaṃ manaśca vijñānaṃ saṃjñā vai kalpavarjitā /
children.translated_text: Mind, <s>manas</s>, <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness), and perception — devoid of conceptualization;

children.text: avikalpadharmatāṃ prāptāḥ śrāvakā na jinātmajāḥ // Lank_10.287 //
children.translated_text: those who have attained the <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature) of non-conceptualization are <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers), not sons of the Conqueror. [Laṅk 10.287]

children.text: kṣānte kṣānte viśeṣe vai jñānaṃ tāthāgataṃ śubham /
children.translated_text: In patience upon patience, in distinction, the auspicious <s>tathāgata</s>-knowledge
arises for the purpose of distinction, free from occurrence. [Laṅk 10.288]
The imagined nature exists; the dependent does not exist;

children.text: kalpitaṃ gṛhyate bhrāntyā paratantraṃ na kalpyate // Lank_10.289 //
children.translated_text: the imagined is grasped through error; the dependent is not conceptualized. [Laṅk 10.289]

children.text: cittaṃ hyabhūtasaṃbhūtaṃ na cittaṃ dṛśyate kvacit /
children.translated_text: Mind is born from the unreal; mind is not seen anywhere;
the impressions, established in body and enjoyment, appear to people. [Laṅk 10.290]
Not all form is material; there is immaterial form —
what is like <s>gandharva</s>-[cities], dreams, and illusions, and mirages — that is immaterial. [Laṅk 10.291]

children.text: prajñā hi trividhā mahyamāryaṃ yena prabhāvitam /
children.translated_text: Wisdom is threefold for me, by which the noble [state] is manifested;

children.text: cittaṃ hyadṛśyasaṃbhūtaṃ tena cittaṃ na dṛśyate // Lank_10.292 //
children.translated_text: mind is born from the invisible — therefore mind is not seen. [Laṅk 10.292]
The impressions, established in body and enjoyment, appear to people;

children.text: lakṣaṇaṃ kalpate yena yaḥ svabhāvān vṛṇoti ca // Lank_10.293 //
children.translated_text: by which one conceptualizes characteristics and covers over inherent natures. [Laṅk 10.293]
Wisdom, disjoined from the two vehicles, free from appearances,
operates for <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers) through attachment to arising;
through descent into <s>cittamātra</s> (mind-only), the <s>tathāgata</s>-wisdom is stainless. [Laṅk 10.294]
If from the existent and the non-existent something arises through conditions,
then the views of unity and otherness are necessarily resorted to by them. [Laṅk 10.295]

children.text: vividhāgatirhi nirvṛttā yathā māyā na sidhyati /
children.translated_text: The manifold course has ceased — like illusion, it is not established;

children.text: nimittaṃ hi tathā citraṃ kalpyamānaṃ na sidhyati // Lank_10.296 //
children.translated_text: likewise the sign, however variegated, when conceptualized, is not established. [Laṅk 10.296]
The bondage born from the mind, consisting of signs and <s>dauṣṭhulya</s> (psychic heaviness) —
the imagined, not understood by the ignorant, is conceptualized as the dependent. [Laṅk 10.297]

children.text: ya eva kalpito bhāvaḥ paratantraṃ tadeva hi /
children.translated_text: That very entity which is imagined — that itself is the dependent;

children.text: kalpitaṃ hi vicitrābhaṃ paratantraṃ vikalpyate // Lank_10.298 //
children.translated_text: the imagined, of variegated appearance, is conceptualized as the dependent. [Laṅk 10.298]
<s>Saṃvṛti</s> (conventional truth) and <s>paramārtha</s> (ultimate truth) — there is no third cause;
the imagined is called <s>saṃvṛti</s> (conventional); through its cutting off, [one enters] the domain of the noble ones. [Laṅk 10.299]

children.text: yathā hi yogināṃ vastu citramekaṃ virājate /
children.translated_text: Just as for <s>yogīs</s>, a single object appears as variegated,

children.text: na hyasti citratā tatra tathā kalpitalakṣaṇam // Lank_10.300 //
children.translated_text: yet there is no real variegation therein — so is the characteristic of the imagined. [Laṅk 10.300]
Just as through eye-disease, a variegated form-perception is conceptualized,

children.text: timiraṃ na rūpaṃ nārūpaṃ paratantraṃ tathā budhaiḥ // Lank_10.301 //
children.translated_text: the eye-disease is neither form nor non-form — so is the dependent [understood] by the wise. [Laṅk 10.301]

children.text: hemaṃ syāttu yathā śuddhaṃ jalaṃ kaluṣavarjitam /
children.translated_text: Just as gold may be pure, and water free from turbidity,

children.text: gaganaṃ hi ghanābhāvāttathā śuddhaṃ vikalpitam // Lank_10.302 //
children.translated_text: and the sky [seen] in the absence of clouds — so is the pure [nature], though conceptualized. [Laṅk 10.302]
<s>Śrāvakas</s> (hearers) are threefold for me: created, born from vows,
and the <s>śrāvaka</s> free from passion and aversion, arisen from the <s>Dharma</s>. [Laṅk 10.303]
<s>Bodhisattvas</s> are also threefold; the <s>Buddhas</s> have no characteristics —

children.text: citte citte tu sattvānāṃ buddhabimbaṃ vidṛśyate // Lank_10.304 //
children.translated_text: yet in the mind of each being, the image of the <s>Buddha</s> is seen. [Laṅk 10.304]

children.text: nāsti vai kalpito bhāvaḥ paratantraṃ ca vidyate /
children.translated_text: The imagined entity does not exist; the dependent exists;

children.text: samāropāpavādaṃ ca vikalpaṃ no vinaśyati // Lank_10.305 //
children.translated_text: through superimposition and denial, conceptualization does not perish. [Laṅk 10.305]
If the imagined were non-existent by the inherent nature of the dependent,
then existence without non-existence, and existence born from non-existence [would follow]. [Laṅk 10.306]
Depending on the imagined, the dependent is obtained;
the imagined arises from the connection of signs and names. [Laṅk 10.307]
Absolutely and also the unconsummated [nature], the other arisen from the imagined —

children.text: tadā prajñāyate śuddhaḥ svabhāavaḥ pāramārthikaḥ // Lank_10.308 //
children.translated_text: then the pure inherent nature, the ultimate, becomes manifest. [Laṅk 10.308]
The imagined is tenfold, and the dependent is sixfold;

children.text: tathatā ca pratyātmagatimato nāsti viśeṣaṇam // Lank_10.309 //
children.translated_text: <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) — for one who has attained inner realization, there is no distinction. [Laṅk 10.309]

children.text: pañca dharmā bhavettatvaṃ svabhāvā hi trayastathā /
children.translated_text: The five <s>dharmas</s> constitute reality, and likewise the three inherent natures;
the <s>yogī</s> who discerns this does not deviate from <s>tathatā</s> (suchness). [Laṅk 10.310]
Like the configuration of stars and clouds, resembling the moon and sun,

children.text: cittaṃ saṃdṛśyate nṝṇāṃ dṛśyābhaṃ vāsanoditam // Lank_10.311 //
children.translated_text: the mind is seen by people — appearing as the visible, arisen from impressions. [Laṅk 10.311]

children.text: bhūtālabdhātmakā hyete na lakṣyaṃ na ca lakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: These [things], without real self-nature attained from the elements — neither what is characterized nor characteristics;

children.text: sarve bhūtamayā bhūtā yadi rūpaṃ hi bhautikam // Lank_10.312 //
children.translated_text: all are made of elements, arising from elements, if form is indeed elemental. [Laṅk 10.312]
The great elements are unborn; there is nothing elemental in the elements;

children.text: kāraṇaṃ hi mahābhūtāḥ kāryaṃ bhūsalilādayaḥ // Lank_10.313 //
children.translated_text: the great elements are the cause; the effects are earth, water, and so forth. [Laṅk 10.313]
Form [consisting of] substance and designation, likewise produced by the species of illusion,

children.text: svapnagandharvarūpaṃ ca mṛgatṛṣṇā ca pañcamam // Lank_10.314 //
children.translated_text: and dream- and <s>gandharva</s>-form, and mirage as the fifth. [Laṅk 10.314]

children.text: icchantikaṃ pañcavidhaṃ gotrāḥ pañca tathā bhavet /
children.translated_text: <s>Icchantikas</s> are fivefold, and the <s>gotras</s> (lineages) are likewise five;

children.text: pañca yānānyayānaṃ ca nirvāṇaṃ ṣaḍvidhaṃ bhavet // Lank_10.315 //
children.translated_text: the vehicles are five and a non-vehicle, and <s>nirvāṇa</s> is sixfold. [Laṅk 10.315]
The divisions of the aggregates are twenty-four, and form is eightfold;
<s>Buddhas</s> are twenty-four, and the sons of the Conqueror are twofold. [Laṅk 10.316]
There are one hundred and eight approaches, and <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers) are threefold;

children.text: kṣetramekaṃ hi buddhānāṃ buddhaścaikastathā bhavet // Lank_10.317 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Buddha</s>-field is one, and the <s>Buddha</s> is likewise one. [Laṅk 10.317]
The liberations are likewise three, and the streams of mind are fourfold;

children.text: nairātmyaṃ ṣaḍvidhaṃ mahyaṃ jñeyaṃ cāpi caturvidham // Lank_10.318 //
children.translated_text: <s>nairātmya</s> (selflessness) is sixfold for me, and the knowable is also fourfold. [Laṅk 10.318]
Disjoined from causes, free from the faults of views —
self-realized, immovable, the unsurpassed <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle). // Laṅk 10.319 //
Arising and non-arising may be eightfold or ninefold,
in a single gradual sequence, yet the established conclusion is one alone. // Laṅk 10.320 //
The formless realm (<s>ārūpyadhātu</s>) is eightfold, and the divisions of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) are sixfold;
the exits of the sons of the <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary awakened ones) are sevenfold. // Laṅk 10.321 //

children.text: adhvatrayaṃ na caivāsti nityānityaṃ ca nāsti vai /
children.translated_text: The three times do not truly exist, and neither permanence nor impermanence exists;

children.text: kriyā karma phalaṃ caiva svapnakāryaṃ tathā bhavet // Lank_10.322 //
children.translated_text: action, <s>karma</s>, and its fruit — all become like the work of a dream. // Laṅk 10.322 //
The <s>Buddhas</s>, who are without beginning or end in their arising, and the <s>Śrāvakas</s> (hearers) who are true sons of the <s>Jina</s> (Victor) —
mind (<s>citta</s>) is always disjoined from the visible, resembling the <s>dharma</s> of illusion (<s>māyā</s>). // Laṅk 10.323 //
The womb, the wheel, likewise birth, renunciation, and the abode of <s>Tuṣita</s> —

children.text: sarvakṣetragatāścāpi dṛśyante na ca yonijāḥ // Lank_10.324 //
children.translated_text: they are seen going to all fields, yet they are not womb-born. // Laṅk 10.324 //
Transmigration, movement, sentient beings, teaching, and cessation likewise,
truth, awakening in the fields — all are set in motion by conditions. // Laṅk 10.325 //
Worlds, forests, islands, the passage through the ford of <s>nairātmya</s> (selflessness),
<s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), attainment of the vehicle's foundation — the domain of inconceivable fruit. // Laṅk 10.326 //
The lineages of moon and stars, the lineages of kings, the abode of the gods,
the lineages of <s>Yakṣas</s> and <s>Gandharvas</s> — all are born from <s>karma</s>, arisen from craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>). // Laṅk 10.327 //
There is inconceivable transformation, and decease (<s>cyuti</s>) is conjoined with impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>);
by the absence of decease through complete severance, the net of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) is extinguished. // Laṅk 10.328 //
Wealth, grain, gold, fields, and property are conceptually elaborated;

children.text: gavaiḍakāśca dāsā vai tathā hayagajādayaḥ // Lank_10.329 //
children.translated_text: cattle, sheep, servants, and likewise horses, elephants, and so forth. // Laṅk 10.329 //

children.text: talpaviddhe na svaptavyaṃ bhūmiścāpi na lepayet /
children.translated_text: One should not sleep on a pierced bed, nor should one smear the ground;

children.text: sauvarṇarājataṃ pātraṃ kāṃsaṃ tāmraṃ na kārayet // Lank_10.330 //
children.translated_text: one should not make vessels of gold, silver, bronze, or copper. // Laṅk 10.330 //
Blankets, whether blue or red, and the <s>kāṣāya</s> (ochre robe) — with cow-dung,

children.text: kardamaiḥ phalapatraiśca śuklān yogī rajetsadā // Lank_10.331 //
children.translated_text: with mud, with fruits and leaves, the <s>yogī</s> should always dye white cloth. // Laṅk 10.331 //

children.text: śailīkaṃ mṛnmayaṃ lohaṃ śāṅkhaṃ vai sphaṭikamayam /
children.translated_text: Of stone, of clay, of iron, of conch-shell, or of crystal —

children.text: pātrārthaṃ dhārayedyogī paripūrṇaṃ ca māgadham // Lank_10.332 //
children.translated_text: the <s>yogī</s> should hold a bowl for alms, full and of the <s>Māgadha</s> measure. // Laṅk 10.332 //
The blade should be four finger-breadths, curved, for cutting cloth;

children.text: śilpavidyāṃ na śikṣeta yogī yogaparāyaṇaḥ // Lank_10.333 //
children.translated_text: the <s>yogī</s> devoted to <s>yoga</s> should not study craft-sciences (<s>śilpavidyā</s>). // Laṅk 10.333 //
Buying and selling should not be done by the <s>yogī</s> who carries the practice of <s>yoga</s>;
this should be done by monastery attendants (<s>ārāmikas</s>) — this is the <s>dharma</s> I declare. // Laṅk 10.334 //
With senses guarded, knowing the meaning, in <s>sūtra</s> and <s>vinaya</s> alike,

children.text: gṛhasthairna ca saṃsṛṣṭaṃ yoginaṃ taṃ vadāmyaham // Lank_10.335 //
children.translated_text: not mingling with householders — such a one I call a <s>yogī</s>. // Laṅk 10.335 //

children.text: śūnyāgāre śmaśāne vā vṛkṣamūle guhāsu vā /
children.translated_text: In an empty house, in a cremation ground, at the root of a tree, or in caves,

children.text: palāle 'bhyavakāśe ca yogī vāsaṃ prakalpayet // Lank_10.336 //
children.translated_text: on straw, or in the open air — the <s>yogī</s> should arrange a dwelling. // Laṅk 10.336 //
Always covered with three garments, whether from cremation grounds or anywhere else,
cloth should be obtained, and whatever is given freely. // Laṅk 10.337 //
One should follow only for a yoke's length, intent on eating alms-food;

children.text: kusumebhyo yathā bhramarāstathā piṇḍaṃ samācaret // Lank_10.338 //
children.translated_text: just as bees approach flowers, so should one collect alms. // Laṅk 10.338 //

children.text: gaṇe ca gaṇasaṃsṛṣṭe bhikṣuṇīṣu ca yadbhavet /
children.translated_text: Whatever exists in a group, in gatherings of <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> (nuns),

children.text: taddhi ājīvasaṃsṛṣṭaṃ na tatkalpati yoginām // Lank_10.339 //
children.translated_text: that is mingled with livelihood concerns — it is not suitable for <s>yogīs</s>. // Laṅk 10.339 //
Kings, princes, ministers, and merchants —
the <s>yogī</s> devoted to <s>yoga</s> should not teach for the sake of alms. // Laṅk 10.340 //
Food from the family of one recently deceased, food connected with friendly affection,
mingled with <s>bhikṣus</s> and <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s> — that is not suitable for <s>yogīs</s>. // Laṅk 10.341 //

children.text: vihāre yatra vai dhūmaḥ pacyate vidhivatsadā /
children.translated_text: In a monastery where there is smoke, where food is cooked according to ritual always,

children.text: uddiśya yatkṛtaṃ cāpi na tatkalpati yoginām // Lank_10.342 //
children.translated_text: and what is prepared with dedication to a specific person — that is not suitable for <s>yogīs</s>. // Laṅk 10.342 //
Free from arising and destruction, abandoning the positions of being and non-being,
endowed with the mark and the marked — the <s>yogī</s> should contemplate the world thus. // Laṅk 10.343 //
Endowed with the power of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), with <s>abhijñā</s> (superknowledges) and <s>vaśitā</s> (masteries),

children.text: nacirāttu bhavedyogī yadyutpādaṃ na kalpayet // Lank_10.344 //
children.translated_text: before long one becomes a <s>yogī</s>, if one does not construct arising. // Laṅk 10.344 //
From atoms, time, or <s>pradhāna</s> (primal matter) — from such causes one should not construct;

children.text: hetupratyayasaṃbhūtaṃ yogī lokaṃ na kalpayet // Lank_10.345 //
children.translated_text: the <s>yogī</s> should not construct the world as born from causes and conditions. // Laṅk 10.345 //
The world, constructed by one's own conceptualization, variegated and arisen from impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) —
the <s>yogī</s> should always perceive existence as like illusion (<s>māyā</s>) and dream (<s>svapna</s>). // Laṅk 10.346 //
A view always free from repudiation (<s>apavāda</s>) and superimposition (<s>samāropa</s>),
appearing as body, enjoyment, and abode — one should not conceptualize the three realms of existence. // Laṅk 10.347 //
Having eaten the alms-food, having firmly set the body upright,

children.text: buddhāṃśca bodhisattvāṃśca namaskṛtya punaḥ punaḥ // Lank_10.348 //
children.translated_text: paying homage again and again to the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, // Laṅk 10.348 //
the knower of <s>yoga</s>, having gathered reality from <s>Vinaya</s>, <s>Sūtra</s>, and reasoning,

children.text: pañcadharmasvacittaṃ ca nairātmyaṃ ca vibhāvayet // Lank_10.349 //
children.translated_text: should contemplate the five <s>dharmas</s>, one's own mind (<s>svacitta</s>), and <s>nairātmya</s> (selflessness). // Laṅk 10.349 //
The purity of one's own inner <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature of things), the stages (<s>bhūmis</s>), and the <s>Buddha</s>-stage —
the <s>yogī</s> should contemplate this and be anointed upon the great lotus. // Laṅk 10.350 //
All destinies (<s>gatis</s>) being delusion, with a mind of revulsion from existence,

children.text: yogānārabhate citrāṃ gatvā śivapathīṃ śubhām // Lank_10.351 //
children.translated_text: one undertakes the variegated <s>yogas</s>, having gone to the auspicious path of peace (<s>śiva</s>). // Laṅk 10.351 //
Appearances resembling the moon and sun, radiant like lotus petals and rays,
resembling variegated patterns of fire in the sky — the <s>yogī</s> perceives these luminous masses. // Laṅk 10.352 //

children.text: nimittāni ca citrāṇi tīrthyamārgaṃ nayanti te /
children.translated_text: These variegated signs (<s>nimittas</s>) lead one to the path of the <s>tīrthikas</s> (heterodox teachers);
they cause one to fall into <s>Śrāvakahood</s> (the state of a hearer) or the domain of <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>. // Laṅk 10.353 //
Having dispelled all of these, when one becomes free from appearances (<s>nirābhāsa</s>),
then the sun-like <s>Buddhas</s>, having come together from all fields,

children.text: śiro hi tasya mārjanti nimittaṃ tathatānugāḥ // Lank_10.354 //
children.translated_text: anoint one's head — those who accord with <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) mark the sign. // Laṅk 10.354 //
Existence arises without form, free from eternalism and annihilationism;
departed from the positions of being and non-being, they will construct the middle way (<s>madhyama</s>). // Laṅk 10.355 //
In the doctrine of no-cause they construct, in causelessness, the view of annihilation;
through not fully knowing external entities, they will not attain the middle way (<s>madhyamā</s>). // Laṅk 10.356 //
They will not be released from grasping at entities — lest there be the view of annihilation;
through superimposition and repudiation they will teach the middle way (<s>madhyamā</s>). // Laṅk 10.357 //
Through the realization of <s>cittamātra</s> (mind-only), external entities are without basis;
the cessation of conceptualization — that itself is the middle way (<s>madhyamā pratipad</s>). // Laṅk 10.358 //
<s>Cittamātra</s> (mind-only) is not seen, and from the absence of the seen, nothing arises;

children.text: pratipanmadhyamā caiṣā mayā cānyaiśca deśitā // Lank_10.359 //
children.translated_text: this is the middle way (<s>madhyamā pratipad</s>) taught by me and by others. // Laṅk 10.359 //
Arising and non-arising, being and non-being, and emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>),

children.text: naiḥsvabhāvyaṃ ca bhāvānāṃ dvayametanna kalpayet // Lank_10.360 //
children.translated_text: and the essencelessness (<s>naiḥsvābhāvya</s>) of entities — this duality one should not construct. // Laṅk 10.360 //

children.text: vikalpavṛttyā bhāvo na mokṣaṃ kalpenti bāliśāḥ /
children.translated_text: Through the operation of conceptualization, entities do not exist — the foolish construct liberation;
without the awakening to the operations of mind, the grasping at duality is not abandoned. // Laṅk 10.361 //
Through the awakening to what is seen by one's own mind, the grasping at duality is abandoned;
for abandonment is full knowledge, which does not destroy what is conceptualized. // Laṅk 10.362 //
Through full knowledge that the seen is mind, conceptualization does not operate;
the non-operation of conceptualization is <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), free from mind. // Laṅk 10.363 //
If activity is seen that is free from the faults of the <s>tīrthikas</s> (heterodox teachers),
that should be affirmed by the wise — and cessation is without destruction. // Laṅk 10.364 //
Through the realization of this, <s>Buddhahood</s> — this has been taught by me and by the <s>Buddhas</s>;

children.text: anyathā kalpyamānaṃ hi tīrthyavādaḥ prasajyate // Lank_10.365 //
children.translated_text: for if construed otherwise, the doctrine of the <s>tīrthikas</s> follows as a consequence. // Laṅk 10.365 //

children.text: ajāḥ prasūtajanmā vai acyutāśca cyavanti ca /
children.translated_text: The unborn indeed give birth, and the unfallen indeed fall;
simultaneously, like reflections of the moon in water, they are seen in billions of fields. // Laṅk 10.366 //

children.text: ekadhā bahudhā bhūtvā varṣanti ca jvalanti vai /
children.translated_text: Becoming one and many, they rain down and blaze forth;

children.text: citte cintamayā bhūtvā cittamātraṃ vadanti te // Lank_10.367 //
children.translated_text: becoming mind-made (<s>cintamaya</s>) in the mind, they declare <s>cittamātra</s> (mind-only). // Laṅk 10.367 //
In minds there is <s>cittamātra</s> (mind-only), and the mindless arise from mind;
those of variegated forms and appearances have reached their course in <s>cittamātra</s> (mind-only). // Laṅk 10.368 //
In forms resembling the lords of sages (<s>Maunīndras</s>), <s>Śrāvakas</s>, and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>,

children.text: anyaiśca vividhai rūpaiścittamātraṃ vadanti te // Lank_10.369 //
children.translated_text: and in various other forms — they declare <s>cittamātra</s> (mind-only). // Laṅk 10.369 //
The formless form for those in the formless realm, and the hellish form for hell-beings —

children.text: rūpaṃ darśyanti sattvānāṃ cittamātrasya kāraṇam // Lank_10.370 //
children.translated_text: they display forms to beings, due to <s>cittamātra</s> (mind-only) as the cause. // Laṅk 10.370 //

children.text: māyopamaṃ samādhiṃ ca kāyaṃ cāpi manomayam /
children.translated_text: Illusion-like <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), and also the mind-made body (<s>manomayakāya</s>),

children.text: daśa bhūmīśca vaśitāḥ parāvṛttā labhanti te // Lank_10.371 //
children.translated_text: the ten stages (<s>bhūmis</s>) and the masteries (<s>vaśitās</s>) — through transformation (<s>parāvṛtti</s>) they obtain these. // Laṅk 10.371 //
Through the distortions of their own conceptualizations, through the vibrations of <s>prapañca</s> (proliferation),
the foolish are bound by perception in what is seen, heard, thought, and known. // Laṅk 10.372 //

children.text: nimittaṃ paratantraṃ hi yannāma tatra kalpitam /
children.translated_text: The sign (<s>nimitta</s>) is the dependent (<s>paratantra</s>), and what is named there is the imagined (<s>kalpita</s>);
the imagined sign operates from the dependent (<s>pāratantrya</s>). // Laṅk 10.373 //

children.text: buddhyā vivecyamānaṃ hi na tantraṃ nāpi kalpitam /
children.translated_text: When analyzed by wisdom, it is neither the dependent nor the imagined;

children.text: niṣpanno nāsti vai bhāvaḥ kathaṃ buddhyā prakalpyate // Lank_10.374 //
children.translated_text: there is no perfected (<s>niṣpanna</s>) entity — how then is it constructed by wisdom? // Laṅk 10.374 //
The perfected (<s>niṣpanna</s>) entity does exist, free from both being and non-being;

children.text: bhāvābhāvavinirmuktau dvau svabhāvau kathaṃ bhavet // Lank_10.375 //
children.translated_text: when freed from being and non-being, how can the two natures (<s>svabhāvas</s>) exist? // Laṅk 10.375 //

children.text: parikalpite svabhāve ca svabhāvau dvau pratiṣṭhitau /
children.translated_text: In the imagined nature (<s>parikalpita svabhāva</s>), the two natures are established;
the imagined is seen as variegated, while the purified is the domain of the noble ones (<s>āryas</s>). // Laṅk 10.376 //
The imagined, of variegated appearance, is conceptualized in the dependent (<s>paratantra</s>);

children.text: anyathā kalpyamānaṃ hi tīrthyavādaṃ samāśrayet // Lank_10.377 //
children.translated_text: if construed otherwise, one would resort to the doctrine of the <s>tīrthikas</s> (heterodox teachers). // Laṅk 10.377 //
It is said 'conceptualization is conceptualization' from seeing its causal arising;
that which is free from the duality of conceptualization — that indeed is the perfected (<s>niṣpanna</s>). // Laṅk 10.378 //

children.text: kṣetraṃ buddhāśca nirmāṇā ekaṃ yānaṃ trayaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: Fields, <s>Buddhas</s>, and emanations (<s>nirmāṇas</s>), one vehicle and three likewise,

children.text: na nirvāṇamahaṃ sarve śūnyā utpattivarjitāḥ // Lank_10.379 //
children.translated_text: no <s>nirvāṇa</s>, no self — all are empty, devoid of arising. // Laṅk 10.379 //
Thirty-six divisions of <s>Buddhas</s>, and ten divisions separately,
these are the mind-streams (<s>cittasaṃtāna</s>) of beings — these are the fields as receptacle-worlds. // Laṅk 10.380 //

children.text: yathā hi kalpitaṃ bhāvaṃ khyāyate citradarśanam /
children.translated_text: Just as an imagined entity appears as a variegated perception,

children.text: na hyasti citratā tatra buddhadharmaṃ tathā jagat // Lank_10.381 //
children.translated_text: yet there is no real variegation there — so too is the world with respect to <s>Buddhadharma</s>. // Laṅk 10.381 //

children.text: dharmabuddho bhavedbuddhaḥ śeṣā vai tasya nirmitāḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>Dharmakāya Buddha</s> (Buddha of the Dharma-body) is the true <s>Buddha</s>; the rest are indeed his emanations;
beings see their own seed-continuity through the visions of the <s>Buddha</s>. // Laṅk 10.382 //
From the connection with signs of delusion, conceptualization operates;

children.text: vikalpā tathatā nānyā na nimittā vikalpanā // Lank_10.383 //
children.translated_text: conceptualization is not other than <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), nor is the sign other than conceptualization. // Laṅk 10.383 //
The <s>Svābhāvika</s> (essential body), the <s>Saṃbhoga</s> (enjoyment body), the emanated (<s>nirmita</s>), and the five emanations —

children.text: ṣaṭtriṃśakaṃ buddhagaṇaṃ buddhaḥ svābhāviko bhavet // Lank_10.384 //
children.translated_text: the assembly of thirty-six <s>Buddhas</s>; the <s>Svābhāvika</s> (essential) <s>Buddha</s> is the true one. // Laṅk 10.384 //

children.text: nīle rakte 'tha lavaṇe śaṅkhe kṣīre ca śārkare /
children.translated_text: In blue, in red, in salt, in conch-shell, in milk, and in sugar —

children.text: kaṣāyaiḥ phalapuṣpādyaiḥ kiraṇā yatha bhāskare // Lank_10.385 //
children.translated_text: through astringent fruits, flowers, and the like — as rays are in the sun, // Laṅk 10.385 //

children.text: na cānye na ca nānanye taraṃgā hyudadhāviva /
children.translated_text: they are neither different nor not different, like waves in the ocean;

children.text: vijñānāni tathā sapta cittena saha saṃyutā // Lank_10.386 //
children.translated_text: likewise the seven <s>vijñānas</s> (consciousnesses) are conjoined with <s>citta</s> (mind). // Laṅk 10.386 //
That is the transformation of the ocean, and the variegation of the waves;

children.text: ālayaṃ hi tathā citraṃ vijñānākhyaṃ pravartate // Lank_10.387 //
children.translated_text: likewise the <s>ālaya</s> (store-consciousness), being variegated, operates under the name of <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness). // Laṅk 10.387 //
<s>Citta</s> (mind), <s>manas</s> (mentation), and <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) are constructed for the purpose of defining characteristics;

children.text: abhinnalakṣaṇānyaṣṭau na ca lakṣyaṃ na lakṣaṇam // Lank_10.388 //
children.translated_text: the eight have undifferentiated characteristics — there is neither the characterized nor the characteristic. // Laṅk 10.388 //
Just as there is no real distinction between the ocean and its waves,

children.text: vijñānānāṃ tathā citte pariṇāmo na labhyate // Lank_10.389 //
children.translated_text: likewise no transformation of the <s>vijñānas</s> (consciousnesses) is found apart from <s>citta</s> (mind). // Laṅk 10.389 //

children.text: cittena cīyate karma manasā ca vicīyate /
children.translated_text: By <s>citta</s> (mind), <s>karma</s> is accumulated; by <s>manas</s> (mentation), it is discriminated;

children.text: vijñānena vijānāti dṛśyaṃ kalpeti pañcabhiḥ // Lank_10.390 //
children.translated_text: by <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness), one cognizes; by the five, one constructs the visible. // Laṅk 10.390 //
Blue, red, and other modes — <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) appears thus to people;
speak — why is there this similarity of waves and mind, O great sage? // Laṅk 10.391 //
Blue, red, and other modes are indeed not found in the waves;

children.text: vṛttiśca varṇyate citte lakṣaṇārthaṃ hi bāliśāḥ // Lank_10.392 //
children.translated_text: and operation is described in mind — for the childish [mistake it] for the meaning of characteristics. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.392 ||

children.text: na tasya vidyate vṛttiḥ svacittaṃ grāhyavarjitam /
children.translated_text: There is no operation of that [mind] — one's own mind is free from what is grasped;

children.text: grāhye sati hi vai grāhastaraṃgaiḥ saha sādhyate // Lank_10.393 //
children.translated_text: when the grasped exists, indeed grasping is established together with the waves. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.393 ||
As the support of body and enjoyment, consciousness appears to people;
thereby its operation is seen, resembling [the ocean] together with waves. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.394 ||
It is perceived as dancing in the mode of ocean-and-waves;

children.text: ālayasya tathā vṛttiḥ kasmādbuddhyā na gṛhyate // Lank_10.395 //
children.translated_text: the operation of the <s>ālaya</s> (store-consciousness) is likewise — why is it not grasped by the intellect? || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.395 ||
Because of the deficiency of intellect of the childish, the <s>ālaya</s>, like the ocean,
is conveyed through the analogy of resemblance to the operation of waves. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.396 ||
Just as the sun rises equally upon the low and the high,

children.text: tathā tvaṃ lokapradyota tattvaṃ deśesi bāliśān // Lank_10.397 //
children.translated_text: so you, the illuminator of the world, teach reality to the childish. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.397 ||
Having established a position in <s>dharmas</s>, why do you not speak reality?

children.text: bhāṣase yadi tattvaṃ vai tattvaṃ citte na vidyate // Lank_10.398 //
children.translated_text: If you speak reality, [then know that] reality is not found in mind. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.398 ||
Just as waves of the ocean, just as in a mirror, just as in a dream,
are seen at one and the same time — so too mind [operates] in its own domain;
but because of the deficiency of sense-objects, it operates in sequential operation. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.399 ||
