By consciousness one cognizes, by <s>manas</s> one thinks;

children.text: pañcānāṃ khyāyate dṛśyaṃ kramo nāsti samāhite // Lank_10.400 //
children.translated_text: for the five [sense-consciousnesses] the visible appears — there is no sequence for one in <s>samādhi</s>. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.400 ||
Just as a master painter or a painter's apprentice

children.text: citrārthe nāmayedraṅgaṃ deśanāpi tathā mama // Lank_10.401 //
children.translated_text: applies pigment for the purpose of a painting — so too is my teaching. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.401 ||

children.text: raṅge na vidyate citraṃ na kuḍye na ca bhājane /
children.translated_text: The painting is not found in the pigment, nor on the wall, nor in the vessel;
for the purpose of attracting beings, the painting is conceptualized through pigments. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.402 ||
Teaching is invariable, and reality is devoid of syllables;

children.text: kṛtvā dharme vyavasthānaṃ tattvaṃ deśemi yoginām // Lank_10.403 //
children.translated_text: having established a position in <s>dharma</s>, I teach reality to <s>yogins</s>. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.403 ||
Reality is the domain of one's own inner realization, free from what is to be conceptualized and conceptualization;
I teach [it] to the sons of the <s>Jinas</s> — for the childish, the teaching is otherwise. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.404 ||

children.text: vicitrā hi yathā māyā dṛśyate na ca vidyate /
children.translated_text: Just as variegated illusion is seen but does not exist,

children.text: deśanā hi tathā citrā dṛśyate 'vyabhicāriṇī // Lank_10.405 //
children.translated_text: so too the variegated teaching is seen, [yet] invariable. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.405 ||
What is a teaching for one is a non-teaching for another;
just as a physician administers medicine according to each patient,

children.text: buddhā hi tadvatsattvānāṃ cittamātraṃ vadanti te // Lank_10.406 //
children.translated_text: so too the Buddhas speak mind-only to beings. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.406 ||
Discrimination operates by the seed of external impressions;

children.text: tantraṃ hi yena gṛhṇāti yadgṛhṇāti sa kalpitam // Lank_10.407 //
children.translated_text: that by which one grasps the system — what one grasps is the imagined. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.407 ||
The external support is the grasped, and mind, depending [on it], arises;

children.text: dvidhā pravartate bhrāntistṛtīyaṃ nāsti kāraṇam // Lank_10.408 //
children.translated_text: delusion operates in two ways — there is no third cause. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.408 ||
From that which delusion arises, and depending on which it arises —
the six, twelve, and eighteen — I declare [them all to be] mind alone. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.409 ||
Through the connection of own-seed and grasped, the grasping of self is abandoned;
through the descent into the mind-<s>kalpa</s> (mind-age), the grasping of <s>dharmas</s> is abandoned. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.410 ||
That which is the <s>ālayavijñāna</s> (store-consciousness) — that consciousness operates;
the internal sense-base would be [the object]; the external, when there is fearlessness. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.411 ||
Just as the grasping of stars, hair-nets [is] by the ignorant — [so too] dream-forms;

children.text: saṃskṛtāsaṃskṛtaṃ nityaṃ kalpyate na ca vidyate // Lank_10.412 //
children.translated_text: the conditioned and unconditioned are perpetually conceptualized but do not exist. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.412 ||
<s>Gandharva</s>-city, illusion, and the waters of a mirage —

children.text: asanto vā vidṛśyante paratantraṃ tathā bhavet // Lank_10.413 //
children.translated_text: they are non-existent yet appear; so too is the dependent-nature (<s>paratantra</s>). || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.413 ||
Through the metaphor of self and faculties, I teach the threefold mind:
mind, <s>manas</s>, and consciousness — disjoined from their own-characteristics. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.414 ||

children.text: cittaṃ manaśca vijñānaṃ nairātmyaṃ syāddvayaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: Mind, <s>manas</s>, and consciousness, the twofold selflessness likewise,

children.text: pañca dharmāḥ svabhāvā hi buddhānāṃ gocaro hyayam // Lank_10.415 //
children.translated_text: the five <s>dharmas</s> and inherent natures — this indeed is the domain of the Buddhas. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.415 ||
By characteristic they would be three, [but] one as the cause of impressions;

children.text: raṅgaṃ hi yathāpyekaṃ kuḍye citraṃ vidṛśyate // Lank_10.416 //
children.translated_text: just as pigment is one, [yet] a painting is seen on a wall. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.416 ||
Selflessness, non-duality, mind, and <s>manovijñāna</s> (mind-consciousness) as well,

children.text: pañca dharmāḥ svabhāvā hi mama gotre na santi te // Lank_10.417 //
children.translated_text: the five <s>dharmas</s> and inherent natures — these do not exist in my lineage (<s>gotra</s>). || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.417 ||
Free from the characteristic of mind, devoid of consciousness and <s>manas</s>,
free from <s>dharma</s>-inherent-nature — one would attain the <s>Tathāgata</s>-lineage. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.418 ||

children.text: kāyena vācā manasā na tatra kriyate śubham /
children.translated_text: By body, speech, or mind, no wholesome [action] is performed therein;
the <s>Tathāgata</s>-lineage is pure, free from active conduct. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.419 ||
Purified by superknowledges and masteries, adorned with the power of <s>samādhi</s>,

children.text: kāyaṃ manomayaṃ cittaṃ gotraṃ tāthāgataṃ śubham // Lank_10.420 //
children.translated_text: the mind-made body — the <s>Tathāgata</s>-lineage is auspicious. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.420 ||
Stainless, to be known through one's own inner realization, devoid of the characteristic of cause,

children.text: aṣṭamī buddhabhūmiśca gotraṃ tāthāgataṃ bhavet // Lank_10.421 //
children.translated_text: the eighth, the Buddha-stage — this would be the <s>Tathāgata</s>-lineage. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.421 ||
<s>Dūraṃgamā</s> (Far-Going), <s>Sādhumatī</s> (Good Intelligence), <s>Dharmameghā</s> (Dharma-Cloud), and the <s>Tathāgatī</s> (Tathāgata-stage) —

children.text: etaddhi gotraṃ buddhānāṃ śeṣā yānadvayāvahā // Lank_10.422 //
children.translated_text: this indeed is the lineage of the Buddhas; the rest convey the two vehicles. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.422 ||
According to the differentiation of the continuum of beings, and for the sake of the meaning of characteristics for the childish,

children.text: deśyante bhūmayaḥ sapta buddhaiścittavaśaṃ gatāḥ // Lank_10.423 //
children.translated_text: the seven stages are taught by the Buddhas who have gone to the mastery of mind. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.423 ||
The rigidity of speech, body, and mind does not operate on the seventh [stage];
on the eighth, the support of that [yogin] resembles dream and flood. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.424 ||
On the eighth and fifth stages, the sons of the <s>Jinas</s> engage in

children.text: kurvanti jinaputrā vai nṛpatvaṃ ca bhavālaye // Lank_10.425 //
children.translated_text: crafts, sciences, and arts — and also kingship in the abode of existence. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.425 ||
One should not conceptualize arising or non-arising, empty or non-empty,
inherent nature or non-inherent-nature — in mind-only these do not exist. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.426 ||
'This is true, this is true, this is false' — one should conceptualize [thus];

children.text: pratyekaśrāvakāṇāṃ ca deśanā na jinaurasām // Lank_10.427 //
children.translated_text: this is the teaching for <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> and <s>Śrāvakas</s>, not for the true sons of the <s>Jinas</s>. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.427 ||

children.text: saccāsacca sato naiva kṣaṇikaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ na vai /
children.translated_text: Real-and-unreal, of the existent — not [that]; momentary, characteristic — not [that] indeed;
designation and substance — not [that] either; in mind-only these do not exist. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.428 ||

children.text: bhāvā vidyanti saṃvṛtyā paramārthe na bhāvakāḥ /
children.translated_text: Entities exist conventionally; in the ultimate sense, entities do not exist;
the delusion regarding those without inherent nature — that truth would be conventional truth (<s>saṃvṛti</s>). || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.429 ||
Regarding all <s>dharmas</s> that are non-existent, designation is made by me;
speech and conventional usage of the childish are devoid of reality. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.430 ||
An entity born from speech exists as the domain of meaning;

children.text: abhilāpasaṃbhavo bhāvo dṛṣṭvā vai nāsti vidyate // Lank_10.431 //
children.translated_text: having seen that an entity born from speech does not exist — [then] it is non-existent. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.431 ||
Just as a painting in the absence of a wall, or a shadow without a post,

children.text: ālayaṃ tu tathā śuddhaṃ taraṃge na virājate // Lank_10.432 //
children.translated_text: so too the <s>ālaya</s> (store), when pure, does not shine forth in waves. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.432 ||
Mind stands like an actor; <s>manas</s> resembles a jester;

children.text: vijñānapañcakaiḥ sārdhaṃ dṛśyaṃ kalpati raṅgavat // Lank_10.433 //
children.translated_text: together with the five consciousnesses, it conceptualizes the visible like a stage. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.433 ||
The outflow of the teaching-<s>dharma</s>, and that which is an outflow-emanation —

children.text: buddhā hyete bhavetpaurāḥ śeṣā nirmāṇavigrahāḥ // Lank_10.434 //
children.translated_text: these Buddhas would be the original ones; the rest are emanation-bodies. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.434 ||

children.text: dṛśyaṃ na vidyate cittaṃ cittaṃ dṛśyātpramuhyate /
children.translated_text: The visible does not exist [as] mind; mind is deluded by the visible;
as the support of body and enjoyment, the <s>ālaya</s> appears to people. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.435 ||
Mind, <s>manas</s>, and consciousness, inherent nature, and the fivefold <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: nairātmyaṃ dvitayaṃ śuddhaṃ prabhāṣante vināyakāḥ // Lank_10.436 //
children.translated_text: the twofold selflessness, pure — the Guides (<s>Vināyakas</s>) proclaim [these]. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.436 ||
Beyond the domain of logicians, and not indeed of <s>Śrāvakas</s> —

children.text: yaṃ deśayanti vai nāthā pratyātmagatigocaram // Lank_10.437 //
children.translated_text: that which the Protectors teach: the domain of one's own inner realization. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.437 ||
Connected with long, short, and so forth, it operates from one another;
there are no provers of existence — existence and non-existence have no prover. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.438 ||

children.text: aṇuśo vibhajya dravyaṃ na vai rūpaṃ vikalpayet /
children.translated_text: Dividing substance atom by atom, one should not conceptualize form;
the establishment of mind-only does not find acceptance through wrong views. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.439 ||

children.text: mā śūnyatāṃ vikalpetha māśūnyamiti vā punaḥ /
children.translated_text: Do not conceptualize emptiness, nor again [conceptualize] 'non-empty';

children.text: nāstyasti kalpanaiveyaṃ kalpyamarthaṃ na vidyate // Lank_10.440 //
children.translated_text: this very [talk of] 'exists' and 'does not exist' is conceptualization — the object to be conceptualized does not exist. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.440 ||
Form is conceptualized by the childish through aggregations of qualities, atoms, and substances;

children.text: ekaikamaṇuśo nāsti ato 'pyarthaṃ na vidyate // Lank_10.441 //
children.translated_text: atom by atom, each one does not exist — therefore the object too does not exist. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.441 ||
One's own mind, having the configuration of the visible, appears externally to people;

children.text: bāhyaṃ na vidyate dṛśyamato 'pyarthaṃ na vidyate // Lank_10.442 //
children.translated_text: the external visible does not exist — therefore the object too does not exist. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.442 ||

children.text: citraṃ keśoṇḍukaṃ māyāṃ svapna gandharvameva ca /
children.translated_text: A painting, a hair-net, illusion, a dream, a <s>gandharva</s>-[city],

children.text: alātaṃ mṛgatṛṣṇā ca asantaṃ khyāyate nṛṇām // Lank_10.443 //
children.translated_text: a fire-brand, a mirage — these non-existent [things] appear to people. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.443 ||
Permanent and impermanent, likewise oneness, both and neither —
the childish, connected with beginningless faults, conceptualize [these], deluded. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.444 ||
The establishment of vehicles does not exist; I speak of one vehicle;
for the purpose of attracting the childish, I speak of the differentiation of vehicles. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.445 ||
Likewise the three liberations, and the selflessness of <s>dharmas</s>;
equanimity, knowledge, and afflictions — through liberation they are removed. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.446 ||
Just as a piece of wood in the ocean is carried off by waves,

children.text: tathā ca śrāvako mūḍho lakṣaṇena pravāhyate // Lank_10.447 //
children.translated_text: so too the deluded <s>Śrāvaka</s> is carried off by [the mark of] characteristics. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.447 ||

children.text: niṣṭhāgatirna tattasyā na ca bhūyo nivartate /
children.translated_text: The final destination is not truly theirs, nor do they return again;

children.text: samādhikāyaṃ saṃprāpya ā kalpānna prabudhyate // Lank_10.448 //
children.translated_text: having attained the body of <s>samādhi</s>, they do not awaken until [the end of] the <s>kalpa</s>. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.448 ||
Connected with the impressions of afflictions, disjoined from active eruptions,
intoxicated by the intoxication of <s>samādhi</s>, they abide in the undefiled element. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.449 ||
Just as an intoxicated man awakens from the absence of liquor,

children.text: tathā te buddhadharmākhyaṃ kāyaṃ prāpsyanti māmakam // Lank_10.450 //
children.translated_text: so too they will attain my body, called the Buddha-<s>dharma</s>. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.450 ||

children.text: paṅkamagno yathā hastī itastato na dhāvati /
children.translated_text: Just as an elephant sunk in mud does not run here and there,

children.text: samādhimadamagnā vai tathā tiṣṭhanti śrāvakāḥ // Lank_10.451 //
children.translated_text: so too <s>Śrāvakas</s>, sunk in the intoxication of <s>samādhi</s>, abide [immobile]. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.451 ||
The empowerment of the lords of men, purified by vows,

children.text: abhiṣekasamādhyādyaṃ prathamā daśamī ca vai // Lank_10.452 //
children.translated_text: the consecration-<s>samādhi</s> and the rest — the first and the tenth [stages] indeed. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.452 ||

children.text: ākāśaṃ śaśaśṛṅgaṃ ca vandhyāyāḥ putra eva ca /
children.translated_text: Space, a hare's horn, and indeed the son of a barren woman —
non-existent [things] are spoken of; so too is conceptualization regarding entities. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.453 ||
The world, caused by impressions, is neither non-existent nor anywhere existent-and-non-existent;
those who see thus are liberated — those skilled in the selflessness of <s>dharmas</s>. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.454 ||
The imagined (<s>svabhāvakalpita</s>) is [mere] name; the dependent (<s>parabhāva</s>) arises from the system (<s>tantra</s>);

children.text: niṣpannaṃ tathatetyuktaṃ sūtre sūtre sadā mayā // Lank_10.455 //
children.translated_text: the perfected (<s>niṣpanna</s>) is called suchness (<s>tathatā</s>) — [thus] always by me in sūtra after sūtra. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.455 ||

children.text: vyañjanaṃ padakāyaṃ ca nāma cāpi viśeṣataḥ /
children.translated_text: To syllables, word-bodies, and names especially,

children.text: bālāḥ sajanti durmedhā yathā paṅke mahāgajāḥ // Lank_10.456 //
children.translated_text: the childish of poor intellect are attached — like great elephants in mud. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.456 ||
The <s>deva</s>-vehicle, the <s>Brahma</s>-vehicle, and the <s>Śrāvaka</s>-vehicle likewise,

children.text: tāthāgataṃ ca pratyekaṃ yānānyetān vadāmyaham // Lank_10.457 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Tathāgata</s> and the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> — I speak of these vehicles. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.457 ||

children.text: yānānāṃ nāsti vai niṣṭhā yāvaccittaṃ pravartate /
children.translated_text: There is no final destination for the vehicles as long as mind operates;

children.text: citte tu vai parāvṛtte na yānaṃ na ca yāyinaḥ // Lank_10.458 //
children.translated_text: but when mind is transformed (<s>parāvṛtta</s>), there is no vehicle and no travelers. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.458 ||
Mind, discrimination, cognition, <s>manas</s>, and consciousness,

children.text: ālayaṃ tribhavaśceṣṭā ete cittasya paryayāḥ // Lank_10.459 //
children.translated_text: the <s>ālaya</s>, the activity of the three existences — these are synonyms of mind. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.459 ||
Life-force (<s>āyus</s>), warmth, and consciousness, the <s>ālaya</s>, the life-faculty,
<s>manas</s>, and <s>manovijñāna</s> — [these are] qualifications of discrimination. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.460 ||

children.text: cittena dhāryate kāyo mano manyati vai sadā /
children.translated_text: By mind the body is sustained; <s>manas</s> always thinks;

children.text: vijñānaṃ cittaviṣayaṃ vijñānaiḥ saha chindati // Lank_10.461 //
children.translated_text: consciousness, the domain of mind, cuts [experience] together with the [five] consciousnesses. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.461 ||

children.text: tṛṣṇā hi mātā ityuktā avidyā ca tathā pitā /
children.translated_text: Craving is said to be the mother, and ignorance likewise the father;
from the awakening to the object of consciousness, one is taught [to be] a 'Buddha.' || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.462 ||
<s>Arhats</s> indeed [have] latent tendencies; the aggregates are the <s>Saṅgha</s> — the fivefold group of aggregates;
from the cutting of the uninterrupted continuity, <s>karma</s> becomes uninterrupted (<s>ānantarya</s>). || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.463 ||
Selflessness is twofold; afflictions and likewise the twofold obstruction —
<s>Tathāgatas</s> [arise] from the gain of inconceivable transformation and transmigration. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.464 ||

children.text: siddhāntaśca nayaścāpi pratyātmaṃ śāsanaṃ ca vai /
children.translated_text: The established conclusion (<s>siddhānta</s>), the method, and the teaching of self-realization —

children.text: ye paśyanti vibhāgajñā na te tarkavaśaṃ gatāḥ // Lank_10.465 //
children.translated_text: those who see these, knowing distinctions, have not fallen under the power of logic. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.465 ||

children.text: na bhāvo vidyate satyaṃ yathā bālairvikalpyate /
children.translated_text: An entity does not truly exist as conceptualized by the childish;

children.text: abhāvena tu vai mokṣaṃ kathaṃ necchanti tārkikāḥ // Lank_10.466 //
children.translated_text: yet through non-existence, liberation — why do the logicians not desire it? || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.466 ||
For one who sees the conditioned as connected with arising and destruction,

children.text: dṛṣṭidvayaṃ prapuṣṇanti na ca jānanti pratyayān // Lank_10.467 //
children.translated_text: the two views are nourished — and they do not know conditions. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.467 ||
One alone would be the truth — <s>nirvāṇa</s>, free from <s>manas</s>;
one should see the world as conceptualized, resembling a plantain tree, a dream, and illusion. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.468 ||

children.text: rāgo na vidyate dveṣo mohaścāpi na pudgalaḥ /
children.translated_text: Passion does not exist, hatred, and delusion too — nor the person;

children.text: tṛṣṇāyā hyuditāḥ skandhā vidyante svapnasādṛśāḥ // Lank_10.469 //
children.translated_text: the aggregates, arisen from craving, exist resembling a dream. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.469 ||

children.text: yasyāṃ ca rātryāṃ dhigamo yasyāṃ ca parinirvṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: In whichever night [there was] realization, and in whichever [night there was] <s>parinirvāṇa</s> —
in this interval, nothing has been illuminated by me. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.470 ||
With reference to the stability of <s>dharma</s> realized by oneself, it has been spoken by me;

children.text: taiśca buddhairmayā caiva na ca kiṃcidviśeṣitam // Lank_10.471 //
children.translated_text: and by those <s>Buddhas</s> and by me — nothing whatsoever has been differentiated. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.471 ||
The self exists like a substance; the aggregates are devoid of characteristics;

children.text: skandhā vidyanti bhāvena ātmā teṣu na vidyate // Lank_10.472 //
children.translated_text: the aggregates exist as entities — the self does not exist in them. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.472 ||
Understanding the practice, through afflictions and human associations,

children.text: mucyate sarvaduḥkhebhyaḥ svacittaṃ paśyato jagat // Lank_10.473 //
children.translated_text: one is freed from all sufferings — for one who sees the world as one's own mind. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.473 ||
Those for whom the world proceeds by causes and conditions,

children.text: cātuṣkoṭikayā yukto na te mannayakovidāḥ // Lank_10.474 //
children.translated_text: connected with the fourfold [proposition] — they are not skilled in my method. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.474 ||
The world does not arise from the existent, nor from the non-existent, nor from the existent-and-non-existent, ever;
yet by conditions and causes — how is it conceptualized by the childish? || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.475 ||
When one sees the world as neither existent, nor non-existent, nor both,

children.text: tadā vyāvartate cittaṃ nairātmyaṃ cādhigacchati // Lank_10.476 //
children.translated_text: then the mind turns away and realizes selflessness (<s>nairātmya</s>). || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.476 ||
All entities are unborn, since they arise from conditions;

children.text: kāryaṃ hi pratyayāḥ sarve na kāryājjāyate bhavaḥ // Lank_10.477 //
children.translated_text: conditions are all effects — existence does not arise from an effect. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.477 ||

children.text: kāryaṃ na jāyate kāryaṃ dvitvaṃ kārye prasajyate /
children.translated_text: An effect does not arise from an effect; duality in the effect would follow;
and by the implication of duality, non-existence of effect is apprehended. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.478 ||
When one sees the conditioned as free from object and subject,

children.text: nimittaṃ cittamātraṃ hi cittamātraṃ vadāmyaham // Lank_10.479 //
children.translated_text: the sign is mind-only indeed — I declare mind-only. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.479 ||
The 'only' (<s>mātrā</s>) is the establishment of inherent nature, free from entities [produced] by conditions;

children.text: niṣṭhābhāvaparaṃ brahma etāṃ mātrāṃ vadāmyaham // Lank_10.480 //
children.translated_text: the ultimate non-existence, the supreme <s>Brahman</s> — this 'only' I declare. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.480 ||

children.text: prajñaptisatyato hyātmā dravyaḥ sa hi na vidyate /
children.translated_text: The self exists by the truth of designation (<s>prajñapti</s>); it does not exist as substance;

children.text: skandhānāṃ skandhatā tadvatprajñaptyā na tu dravyataḥ // Lank_10.481 //
children.translated_text: the aggregate-nature of the aggregates is likewise by designation, not by substance. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.481 ||
Equality (<s>samatā</s>) is fourfold: [that] of characteristics, cause, and recipient,
and the equality of selflessness — the fourth is that of the <s>yogins</s> of yoga. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.482 ||
The turning-away from all views, free from the imagined and imagining,
non-apprehension and non-arising — I declare mind-only. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.483 ||
Neither entity nor non-entity, free from entity and non-entity,
suchness, freed from mind — I declare mind-only. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.484 ||
Suchness, emptiness, the limit (<s>koṭi</s>), <s>nirvāṇa</s>, the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of <s>dharma</s>),

children.text: kāyaṃ manomayaṃ cittaṃ cittamātraṃ vadāmyaham // Lank_10.485 //
children.translated_text: the mind-made body, mind — I declare mind-only. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.485 ||
Bound by the impressions of discrimination, diverse, arisen from mind,

children.text: bahirdhā jāyate nṝṇāṃ cittamātraṃ hi laukikam // Lank_10.486 //
children.translated_text: it is proclaimed externally for humans — worldly mind-only indeed. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.486 ||

children.text: dṛśyaṃ na vidyate bāhyaṃ cittacitraṃ vidṛśyate /
children.translated_text: The external perceived does not exist; mind is seen diversely;
appearing as body, enjoyment, and abode — I declare mind-only. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.487 ||
The destruction-knowledge of <s>Śrāvakas</s>, the birth-production of <s>Buddhas</s>,
and that of the sons of the Solitary Victors — operates from non-defilement. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.488 ||

children.text: bahirdhā nāsti vai rūpaṃ svacittaṃ dṛśyate bahiḥ /
children.translated_text: External form does not exist; one's own mind is seen as external;
from not understanding one's own mind, the childish conceptualize the conditioned. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.489 ||
By the deluded who do not know external objects [as] the seeing of the variegation of one's own mind,
it is obstructed by causes, [they being] connected with the fourfold [proposition]. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.490 ||

children.text: na hetavo na koṭyo vai dṛṣṭāntāvayavāni ca /
children.translated_text: There are no causes, no logical alternatives, no examples and their parts,

children.text: svacittaṃ hyarthasaṃkrāntaṃ yadi jānanti paṇḍitāḥ // Lank_10.491 //
children.translated_text: if the wise know that one's own mind has migrated into objects. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.491 ||
One should not conceptualize by discriminations that which has the characteristic of the imagined;

children.text: kalpitaṃ ca samāśritya vikalpaḥ saṃpravartate // Lank_10.492 //
children.translated_text: depending on the imagined, discrimination operates. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.492 ||
Mutually related with an undivided connection, caused by a single impression,
because of the adventitious nature of that duality, mind does not arise for humans. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.493 ||
Those who desire the object of discrimination, mind, and mental factors, established in the three realms —

children.text: yadarthābhāḥ pravartante svabhāvakalpito hi saḥ // Lank_10.494 //
children.translated_text: that which operates as the appearance of objects — that inherent nature is indeed imagined. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.494 ||
From the conjunction of appearance and seed, the twelve sense-bases [arise];
from the conjunction of support and supported, the procedure is described by me. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.495 ||

children.text: yathā hi darpaṇe bimbaṃ keśoṇḍustimirasya vā /
children.translated_text: Just as an image in a mirror, or a hair-net [seen due to] cataract,

children.text: tathā hi vāsanaiśchannaṃ cittaṃ paśyanti bāliśāḥ // Lank_10.496 //
children.translated_text: so the childish see the mind covered by impressions. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.496 ||
In an object imagined by one's own discrimination, discrimination operates;

children.text: artho na vidyate bāhyo yathā tīrthyairvikalpyate // Lank_10.497 //
children.translated_text: the object does not exist externally, as conceptualized by the heretics. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.497 ||

children.text: rajjuṃ yathā hyajānānāḥ sarpaṃ gṛhṇanti bāliśāḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as the childish, not knowing a rope, grasp it as a snake,
not knowing the object of one's own mind, they conceptualize an external object. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.498 ||
As a rope in its rope-ness is free from oneness and otherness —

children.text: kiṃ tu svacittadoṣo 'yaṃ yena rajjurvikalpyate // Lank_10.499 //
children.translated_text: this is merely the fault of one's own mind, by which the rope is conceptualized. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.499 ||

children.text: na hi yo yena bhāvena kalpyamāno na lakṣyate /
children.translated_text: For whatever entity, when imagined in whatever way, is not perceived —
one should not conclude it does not exist; this is the true nature (<s>dharmatā</s>) of <s>dharmas</s>. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.500 ||
'Does not exist' presupposes existence; 'exists' presupposes non-existence;

children.text: ato nāsti na gantavyaṃ astitvaṃ na ca kalpayet // Lank_10.501 //
children.translated_text: therefore one should not conclude 'does not exist,' nor should one conceptualize 'exists.' || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.501 ||

children.text: kalpitaṃ kalpyamānaṃ hi yadidaṃ na tadātmakam /
children.translated_text: That which is imagined and being imagined — this is not of that nature;

children.text: anātmakaṃ kathaṃ dṛṣṭvā vikalpaḥ saṃpravartate // Lank_10.502 //
children.translated_text: seeing it as without self, how does discrimination operate? || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.502 ||
Form does not exist by its own form-nature; likewise pots, cloths, and the like;

children.text: avidyamāne dṛśye tu vikalpastena jāyate // Lank_10.503 //
children.translated_text: when the perceived does not exist, discrimination arises thereby. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.503 ||
If those discriminations [operate] in error, in the conditioned that has no beginning,

children.text: bhāvānāṃ bhāvatā kena bhrāmitā brūhi me mune // Lank_10.504 //
children.translated_text: by whom has the entity-hood of entities been made to err? Tell me, O sage! || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.504 ||

children.text: bhāvānāṃ bhāvatā nāsti cittamātraṃ ca dṛśyate /
children.translated_text: The entity-hood of entities does not exist; only mind-only is seen;
not seeing one's own mind, discrimination operates. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.505 ||

children.text: kalpitaṃ yadi vai nāsti yathā kalpati bāliśaḥ /
children.translated_text: If the imagined does not exist, as the childish imagines,

children.text: anyathā vidyate cāsau na ca buddhyāvagamyate // Lank_10.506 //
children.translated_text: and it exists otherwise — yet it is not understood by the intellect. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.506 ||

children.text: āryāṇāṃ yadi vā so 'sti nāsau bālairvikalpitaḥ /
children.translated_text: If it exists for the noble ones — then it is not conceptualized by the childish;

children.text: āryāṇāmatha mithyāsau āryā bālaiḥ samaṃ gatāḥ // Lank_10.507 //
children.translated_text: but if it is false for the noble ones, then the noble ones would be equal to the childish. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.507 ||
For the noble ones there is no error, since the mind has been purified;
the childish, with impure mental continuums, conceptualize the imagined. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.508 ||
Just as a mother would bring fruit from space for her son —

children.text: etaddhi putra mā kranda gṛhṇa citramidaṃ phalam // Lank_10.509 //
children.translated_text: 'Here, son, do not cry — take this variegated fruit!' || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.509 ||
So I, for all beings, with various imagined fruits,
enticing them, teach the method free from the sides of existent and non-existent. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.510 ||

children.text: abhūtvā yasya vai bhāvaḥ pratyayairna ca saṃkulaḥ /
children.translated_text: For that which, having not existed, comes into being — not crowded by conditions —
that is born without having been born before, and has indeed an unobtained self. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.511 ||

children.text: alabdhātmakaṃ hyajātaṃ ca pratyayairna vinā kvacit /
children.translated_text: Having an unobtained self and unborn, never without conditions —

children.text: utpannamapi te bhāvo pratyayairna vinā kvacit // Lank_10.512 //
children.translated_text: even arisen, that entity [is] never without conditions. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.512 ||
Thus seeing in brief — neither non-existent, nor existent-and-non-existent, ever —
the real arises from conditions; it is not to be conceptualized by the wise. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.513 ||
Bad heretics and the childish make talk of oneness and otherness;

children.text: pratyayairna ca jānanti māyāsvapnopamaṃ jagat // Lank_10.514 //
children.translated_text: they do not know through conditions that the world resembles illusion and dream. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.514 ||
The vehicle that is the domain of verbal expression — the supreme <s>Mahāyāna</s>;

children.text: arthaṃ sunītaṃ hi mayā na ca budhyanti bāliśāḥ // Lank_10.515 //
children.translated_text: the meaning well-conveyed by me — yet the childish do not understand. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.515 ||
Those produced by the stinginess of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and heretics —

children.text: vyabhicaranti te hyarthaṃ yasmāttarkeṇa deśitāḥ // Lank_10.516 //
children.translated_text: they deviate from the meaning, since they teach by logic. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.516 ||

children.text: lakṣaṇaṃ bhāva saṃsthānaṃ nāma caiva caturvidham /
children.translated_text: Characteristic, entity, configuration, and name — these are fourfold;
having made these the object of support, conceptualization operates. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.517 ||
Those who, in oneness and multiplicity, have gone under the power of the <s>Brahmā</s>-body,

children.text: somabhāskarayorbhāvā ye nāśenti na te sutāḥ // Lank_10.518 //
children.translated_text: those whose entities of <s>Soma</s> and <s>Bhāskara</s> (sun and moon) they destroy — they are not [my] sons. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.518 ||
Endowed with the noble vision, having gone the course of things as they are,
skilled in the turning-about of perception, and having gone beyond in consciousness — || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.519 ||

children.text: eṣā hi mudrā muktānāṃ putrāṇāṃ mama śāsane /
children.translated_text: This indeed is the seal of those liberated sons in my teaching —
freed from existence and non-existence, devoid of going and coming. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.520 ||
When form-consciousness is turned about, if <s>karma</s> is destroyed,

children.text: nityānityaṃ na prāpnoti saṃsāraśca na vidyate // Lank_10.521 //
children.translated_text: it attains neither permanence nor impermanence, and <s>saṃsāra</s> does not exist. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.521 ||
At the time of cessation, form, having been destroyed, turns away from [its] place;
freed from the faults of 'does not exist' and 'exists,' <s>karma</s> remains in the <s>ālaya</s> (store). || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.522 ||

children.text: pradhvaṃsi patitaṃ rūpaṃ vijñānaṃ ca bhavālaye /
children.translated_text: Form has fallen into destruction, and consciousness [resides] in the <s>ālaya</s> of existence;

children.text: rūpavijñānasaṃbaddhaṃ na ca karma vinaśyati // Lank_10.523 //
children.translated_text: connected with form and consciousness, <s>karma</s> is not destroyed. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.523 ||

children.text: atha taiḥ saha saṃbaddhaṃ karma vai dhvasyate nṛṇām /
children.translated_text: But if <s>karma</s>, connected with them, is destroyed for humans,

children.text: dhvaste tu karmasaṃbandhe na saṃsṛtirna nirvṛtiḥ // Lank_10.524 //
children.translated_text: when the connection of <s>karma</s> is destroyed, there is neither <s>saṃsāra</s> nor cessation. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.524 ||

children.text: atha dhvastamapi taiḥ sārdhaṃ saṃsāre yadi jāyate /
children.translated_text: But if, though destroyed, together with them it is born in <s>saṃsāra</s>,
then form, connected with it, would exist, because of non-difference. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.525 ||

children.text: nābhinnaṃ na ca vai bhinnaṃ cittaṃ rūpaṃ vikalpanāt /
children.translated_text: Mind and form — neither undivided nor divided — [arise] from conceptualization;
there is no destruction of entities, because of the avoidance of the sides of existent and non-existent. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.526 ||
The imagined and the other-dependent — because of their mutually undivided characteristic;
just as impermanence in form — they are indeed mutually productive. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.527 ||
Freed from other and non-other, the imagined is not ascertained;

children.text: nāstyasti kathaṃ bhavati rūpe cānityatā yathā // Lank_10.528 //
children.translated_text: how does 'does not exist' and 'exists' come about? — just as impermanence in form. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.528 ||
By the imagined, when well-seen, the other-dependent does not arise;
by the other-dependent, when seen, the imagined becomes suchness. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.529 ||

children.text: kalpitaṃ hi vināśete mama netrī vinaśyate /
children.translated_text: If the imagined is destroyed, my guidance is destroyed;

children.text: samāropāpavādaṃ ca kurvate mama śāsane // Lank_10.530 //
children.translated_text: they perform superimposition and denial in my teaching. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.530 ||
When at whatever time there are such corrupters of the <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: sarve ca te hyasaṃkathyā mama netrīvināśakāḥ // Lank_10.531 //
children.translated_text: all of them are not to be conversed with — they are destroyers of my guidance. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.531 ||
They are not to be spoken to by the wise, and monastic duties should be avoided [with them] —
those who destroy the imagined, the proponents of superimposition and denial. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.532 ||
Resembling a hair-net, illusion, a dream, a <s>Gandharva</s>[-city],
resembling a mirage — conceptualization for those [free] from the vision of 'does not exist' and 'exists.' || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.533 ||

children.text: nāsau śikṣati buddhānāṃ yasteṣāṃ saṃgrahe caret /
children.translated_text: One who associates with those does not train in [the way of] the <s>Buddhas</s>;

children.text: dvayāntapatitā hyete anyeṣāṃ ca vināśakāḥ // Lank_10.534 //
children.translated_text: these have fallen into both extremes and are destroyers of others. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.534 ||

children.text: viviktaṃ kalpitaṃ bhāvaṃ ye tu paśyanti yoginaḥ /
children.translated_text: Those <s>yogins</s> who see the imagined entity as isolated,

children.text: bhāvābhāvavinirmuktaṃ teṣāṃ vai saṃgrahe caret // Lank_10.535 //
children.translated_text: freed from existence and non-existence — one should associate with them. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.535 ||
Just as in the world, mines produce gold, gems, and pearls,
variegated, not caused by action, and sustaining the childish — || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.536 ||

children.text: tathā hi sattvagotrāṇi citrā vai karmavarjitā /
children.translated_text: So too the lineages of beings are variegated and devoid of [deliberate] action —

children.text: dṛśyābhāvānna karmāsti na ca vai karmajā gatiḥ // Lank_10.537 //
children.translated_text: From the absence of the visible, there is no <s>karma</s> (action), nor is there a course born from <s>karma</s>. [Laṅk 10.537]
The entity-ness of entities does not exist, as the noble ones discern;

children.text: kiṃ tu vidyanti vai bhāvā yathā bālairvikalpitāḥ // Lank_10.538 //
children.translated_text: but entities exist as conceptualized by the childish. [Laṅk 10.538]

children.text: yadi bhāvā va vidyante yathā bālairvikalpitāḥ /
children.translated_text: If entities existed as conceptualized by the childish,

children.text: asatsu sattvabhāveṣu saṃkleśo nāsti kasyacit // Lank_10.539 //
children.translated_text: then in the absence of real sentient-entity-ness, there would be no affliction for anyone. [Laṅk 10.539]
Through the affliction of the diversity of entities, <s>saṃsāra</s>, attended by the sense-faculties,
bound by ignorance and craving, operates for embodied beings. [Laṅk 10.540]

children.text: yeṣāṃ tu bhāvo vai nāsti yathā bālairvikalpitaḥ /
children.translated_text: For those for whom entities do not exist as conceptualized by the childish,

children.text: teṣāṃ na vidyate vṛttirindriyāṇāṃ na yoginaḥ // Lank_10.541 //
children.translated_text: the operation of the sense-faculties does not exist for the <s>yogin</s>. [Laṅk 10.541]
If entities do not exist — entities that are the causes of <s>saṃsāra</s> —

children.text: ayaṃ tena bhavenmokṣo bālānāṃ kriyavarjitaḥ // Lank_10.542 //
children.translated_text: this then would be liberation for the childish, free from action. [Laṅk 10.542]
The distinction between the childish and the noble — how would it come from the existence or non-existence of entities?

children.text: āryāṇāṃ nāsti vai bhāvo vimokṣatrayacāriṇām // Lank_10.543 //
children.translated_text: For the noble ones, entities do not exist — for those who move in the three liberations. [Laṅk 10.543]
Aggregates, persons, <s>dharmas</s>, specific and general [characteristics], characteristicless,
conditions, and sense-faculties — I teach to the <s>Śrāvakas</s>. [Laṅk 10.544]
But mind-only without cause, powers, and stages —
I teach the pure <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) realized by oneself to the true sons of the <s>Jinas</s>. [Laṅk 10.545]
In the future time there will be corrupters of my teaching,
wearing ochre robes, proponents of the doctrine of existent and non-existent effects. [Laṅk 10.546]
Non-existent entities exist through conditions — [this is] the domain of the noble;

children.text: kalpito nāsti vai bhāvaḥ kalpayiṣyanti tārkikāḥ // Lank_10.547 //
children.translated_text: the conceptualized entity does not exist — [yet] the logicians will conceptualize [it]. [Laṅk 10.547]
In the future time there will arise those of the childish race of <s>Kaṇabhuj</s> (<s>Kaṇāda</s>),
who, through the wrong view of the doctrine of non-existent effects, will destroy the people. [Laṅk 10.548]
The world has arisen from atoms, and atoms are without cause;

children.text: nava dravyāṇi nityāni kudṛṣṭyā deśayiṣyati // Lank_10.549 //
children.translated_text: nine substances are eternal — [thus] they will teach through wrong views. [Laṅk 10.549]
Substance is produced from substances, and qualities from qualities likewise;

children.text: bhāvānāṃ bhāvatāmanyāṃ satīṃ vai nāśayiṣyati // Lank_10.550 //
children.translated_text: they will destroy another entity-ness of entities that is real. [Laṅk 10.550]
The world would have a beginning if it operates without having previously existed;

children.text: pūrvā ca koṭirnaivāsti saṃsārasya vadāmyaham // Lank_10.551 //
children.translated_text: but there is no prior limit of <s>saṃsāra</s> — [this] I teach. [Laṅk 10.551]
If the three realms and all that is enumerated operate without having previously existed,
then there would be the arising of horns of dogs, camels, and donkeys — without doubt. [Laṅk 10.552]
If the eye, form, and consciousness come into being without having previously existed,
then mats, crowns, cloths, and the like would arise from a lump of clay. [Laṅk 10.553]

children.text: paṭaiśca vai kaṭo nāsti paṭo vai vīraṇaistathā /
children.translated_text: A mat does not come from cloths, nor cloth from <s>vīraṇa</s> grass;

children.text: eka ekatrā saṃbhūtaḥ pratyayaiḥ kiṃ na jāyate // Lank_10.554 //
children.translated_text: if one [thing] arises from one [other], why is not [everything] born from conditions? [Laṅk 10.554]
"The soul is the same as the body" and "what operates without having previously existed" —

children.text: paravādā hyamī sarve mayā ca samudāhṛtāḥ // Lank_10.555 //
children.translated_text: all these are doctrines of others, and they have been stated by me [for refutation]. [Laṅk 10.555]
Having stated the opponent's position, their view is refuted;

children.text: nivārya tu matisteṣāṃ svapakṣaṃ deśayāmyaham // Lank_10.556 //
children.translated_text: and having refuted their view, I teach my own position. [Laṅk 10.556]
Thus the articulation of the heretical doctrines has been made by me for this purpose:

children.text: mā me śiṣyagaṇo mūḍhaḥ sadasatpakṣamāśrayet // Lank_10.557 //
children.translated_text: lest my community of disciples, confused, should take refuge in the side of existent and non-existent. [Laṅk 10.557]
<s>Kapila</s> too, the evil-minded, with tawny limbs,

children.text: śiṣyebhyaḥ saṃprakāśeti guṇānāṃ ca vikāritā // Lank_10.558 //
children.translated_text: teaches his disciples the transformations of the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities). [Laṅk 10.558]

children.text: na bhūtaṃ nāpi cābhūtaṃ pratyayairna ca pratyayāḥ /
children.translated_text: Neither existent nor non-existent, not through conditions, nor are there conditions;
since conditions are non-existent, the non-existent does not operate. [Laṅk 10.559]
Free from the sides of existent and non-existent, devoid of causes and conditions,
free from arising and destruction — my own position is devoid of the characterized. [Laṅk 10.560]
The world is like illusion and dreams, devoid of causes and conditions;

children.text: ahetukaṃ sadā paśyan vikalpo na pravartate // Lank_10.561 //
children.translated_text: always seeing it as causeless, conceptualization does not operate. [Laṅk 10.561]
Like a <s>gandharva</s>-[city] and a mirage, like a hair-ball — always
free from the sides of existent and non-existent, devoid of causes and conditions,
seeing existence as causeless — the stream of mind is purified. [Laṅk 10.562]

children.text: vastu na vidyate paśyaṃścittamātraṃ na vidyate /
children.translated_text: Seeing that substance does not exist, mind-only [also] does not exist;

children.text: avastukaṃ kathaṃ cittaṃ cittamātraṃ na yujyate // Lank_10.563 //
children.translated_text: how can the mind be substanceless? Mind-only is not tenable. [Laṅk 10.563]
Having made substance its support, the mind arises for people;

children.text: ahetukaṃ kathaṃ cittaṃ cittamātraṃ na yujyate // Lank_10.564 //
children.translated_text: how can the mind be causeless? Mind-only is not tenable. [Laṅk 10.564]
<s>Tathatā</s> (suchness) and mind-only, and the method of the noble substance —

children.text: vidyante na ca vidyante na te mannayakovidāḥ // Lank_10.565 //
children.translated_text: they exist and do not exist — those who [hold thus] are not skilled in my method. [Laṅk 10.565]
If the mind operates with the nature of grasped and grasper,

children.text: etaddhi laukikaṃ cittaṃ cittamātraṃ na yujyate // Lank_10.566 //
children.translated_text: this indeed is a worldly mind — mind-only is not tenable. [Laṅk 10.566]
If it arises like a dream with the appearance of body, enjoyment, and abode,

children.text: dvicittatā prasajyeta na ca cittaṃ dvilakṣaṇam // Lank_10.567 //
children.translated_text: there would be the consequence of two minds — but the mind does not have two characteristics. [Laṅk 10.567]

children.text: svadhāraṃ hi yathā khaḍgaṃ svāgraṃ vai aṅguliryathā /
children.translated_text: Just as a sword [cannot cut] its own edge, and a finger [cannot touch] its own tip,

children.text: na chindate na spṛśate tathā cittaṃ svadarśane // Lank_10.568 //
children.translated_text: so the mind [cannot see] its own vision. [Laṅk 10.568]

children.text: na paraṃ na ca vai tantraṃ kalpitaṃ vastumeva ca /
children.translated_text: Neither other-dependent nor the system, neither the conceptualized nor substance itself —

children.text: pañca dharmā dvicittaṃ ca nirābhāse na santi vai // Lank_10.569 //
children.translated_text: the five <s>dharmas</s> and the two minds do not exist in the imageless. [Laṅk 10.569]
The producer and the produced — twofold is the characteristic of entities;

children.text: utpādakaṃ hi saṃdhāya naiḥsvabhāvyaṃ vadāmyaham // Lank_10.570 //
children.translated_text: with reference to the producer, I teach essencelessness. [Laṅk 10.570]

children.text: atha vaicitryasaṃsthāne kalpā ca yadi jāyate /
children.translated_text: If conceptualization arises in the diversity of configurations,

children.text: ākāśe śaśaśṛṅge ca arthābhāsaṃ bhaviṣyati // Lank_10.571 //
children.translated_text: then there would be the appearance of objects in space and in a hare's horn. [Laṅk 10.571]
The mind would be an appearance of objects, and that object would be unconceptualized;

children.text: na ca vai kalpito hyarthaścittādanyo 'bhilapyate // Lank_10.572 //
children.translated_text: but the conceptualized object is not spoken of as other than mind. [Laṅk 10.572]

children.text: anādimati saṃsāre artho vai nāsti kutracit /
children.translated_text: In beginningless <s>saṃsāra</s>, the object does not exist anywhere;

children.text: apuṣṭaṃ hi kathaṃ cittamarthābhāsaṃ pravartate // Lank_10.573 //
children.translated_text: how then does the mind, not nourished, operate with the appearance of objects? [Laṅk 10.573]
If there were nourishment by non-existence, that would apply to a hare's horn too;

children.text: na cābhāvena vai puṣṭo vikalpaḥ saṃpravartate // Lank_10.574 //
children.translated_text: but conceptualization does not operate nourished by non-existence. [Laṅk 10.574]

children.text: yathāpi dānīṃ naivāsti tathā pūrve 'pi nāstyasau /
children.translated_text: Just as it does not exist now, so too it did not exist before;

children.text: anarthe arthasaṃbaddhaṃ kathaṃ cittaṃ pravartate // Lank_10.575 //
children.translated_text: how does the mind, connected with objects in what is objectless, operate? [Laṅk 10.575]
<s>Tathatā</s> (suchness), <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), the limit [of reality], <s>nirvāṇa</s>, the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of <s>dharma</s>),
and the non-arising of <s>dharmas</s> — the inherent nature is ultimate. [Laṅk 10.576]
The childish, fallen into "does not exist" and "exists," through conceptualizations of causes and conditions,
do not understand that existence is causeless and unborn. [Laṅk 10.577]
The mind appears, but the visible does not exist; the distinction is beginninglessly caused.

children.text: anādāvapi nāstyartho viśeṣaḥ kena jāyate // Lank_10.578 //
children.translated_text: Even in the beginningless, no object exists — by what does the distinction arise? [Laṅk 10.578]
If there were nourishment by non-existence, a poor man would become wealthy;

children.text: arthābhāve kathaṃ cittaṃ jāyate brūhi me mune // Lank_10.579 //
children.translated_text: in the absence of objects, how does the mind arise? Tell me, O <s>Muni</s>. [Laṅk 10.579]

children.text: ahetukamidaṃ sarvaṃ na cittaṃ na ca gocaraḥ /
children.translated_text: All this is causeless — there is no mind and no domain;

children.text: na ca vai puṣyate cittaṃ tribhavaṃ kriyavarjitam // Lank_10.580 //
children.translated_text: the mind is not nourished — the three realms are free from action. [Laṅk 10.580]
For the purpose of the cessation of arising, for the establishment of non-arising,
I teach the doctrine of causelessness — but the childish do not discern it.

children.text: anutpannamidaṃ sarvaṃ na ca bhāvā na santi ca // Lank_10.581 //
children.translated_text: All this is unborn, and entities neither exist nor do not exist. [Laṅk 10.581]
Entities called <s>gandharva</s>-[city], dream, and illusion exist without cause;

children.text: anutpannān svabhāvāṃśca śūnyāḥ kena vadāsi me // Lank_10.582 //
children.translated_text: being unborn and without inherent nature — why do you call them empty? Tell me. [Laṅk 10.582]
When an entity is not seen apart from aggregation (<s>samavāya</s>),
then I call it empty, unborn, and without inherent nature. [Laṅk 10.583]
Dreams, hair-balls, illusion, a <s>gandharva</s>-[city], and a mirage —

children.text: ahetukā pi dṛśyante tathā lokavicitratā // Lank_10.584 //
children.translated_text: though causeless, they are seen — so too is the diversity of the world. [Laṅk 10.584]
Aggregation too is a single [concept]; from the absence of the visible, it does not exist.

children.text: na tu tīrthyadṛṣṭyā pralayo samavāyo na vidyate // Lank_10.585 //
children.translated_text: But not through the heretical view of annihilation — aggregation does not exist. [Laṅk 10.585]
Having taken up the doctrine of causelessness, one should establish non-arising;

children.text: anutpādaiḥ prasādhyante mama netrī na naśyati // Lank_10.586 //
children.translated_text: through non-arisings is [the teaching] established — my guidance does not perish. [Laṅk 10.586]
Through the doctrines of causelessness, fear arises in the heretical teachers:

children.text: kathaṃ kena kutaḥ kutra saṃbhavo 'hetuko bhavet // Lank_10.587 //
children.translated_text: "How, by what, from where, and where could there be a causeless arising?" [Laṅk 10.587]
When the wise see that causelessness is not without cause,
then the view that follows arising and destruction turns back. [Laṅk 10.588]
Is non-arising non-existence? Is arising the characteristic of arising?

children.text: atha bhāvasya nāmedaṃ nirarthaṃ vā bravīhi me // Lank_10.589 //
children.translated_text: Or is this a name for an entity? Or is it meaningless? — tell me. [Laṅk 10.589]

children.text: na ca bhāvo hyanutpādo na ca pratyayalakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: Non-arising is not an entity, nor is it the characteristic of conditions;

children.text: na ca bhāvasya nāmedaṃ na ca nāma nirarthakam // Lank_10.590 //
children.translated_text: this is not a name for an entity, nor is the name meaningless. [Laṅk 10.590]
Where [this is] beyond the domain of <s>Śrāvaka-Buddhas</s>,
heretical teachers, and those who have reached the seventh stage — that is the characteristic of non-arising. [Laṅk 10.591]
The turning away from causes and conditions, the negation of causation,
the establishment in mind-only — I call [this] non-arising. [Laṅk 10.592]
The causeless operation of entities, free from what conceptualizes and what is conceptualized,
freed from the sides of existent and non-existent — I call [this] non-arising. [Laṅk 10.593]
Freed from what is seen by the mind, devoid of the duality of inherent natures,
the turning-around of the basis (<s>āśrayaparāvṛtti</s>) — I call [this] non-arising. [Laṅk 10.594]

children.text: na bāhyabhāvaṃ bhāvānāṃ na ca cittaparigraham /
children.translated_text: Neither external entity-ness of entities, nor the grasping of mind —
the abandonment of all views — that is the characteristic of non-arising. [Laṅk 10.595]
Thus one should discern all <s>dharmas</s> as empty, without inherent nature, and so forth;

children.text: na jātu śūnyayā śūnyā kiṃ tvanutpādaśūnyayā // Lank_10.596 //
children.translated_text: [<s>dharmas</s> are] never empty by [mere] emptiness, but by the emptiness of non-arising. [Laṅk 10.596]
The aggregate of conditions operates and ceases;

children.text: kalapācca pṛthagbhūtaṃ na jātaṃ na nirudhyate // Lank_10.597 //
children.translated_text: but what is separate from the aggregate is neither born nor ceases. [Laṅk 10.597]

children.text: bhāvo na vidyate hyanyaḥ kalāpācca pṛthak kvacit /
children.translated_text: No other entity exists anywhere separate from the aggregate,
as is conceptualized by the heretical teachers through oneness and separateness. [Laṅk 10.598]
An entity is not born from the existent, the non-existent, nor from both existent and non-existent;

children.text: anyatra hi kalāpo 'yaṃ pravartate nivartate // Lank_10.599 //
children.translated_text: apart [from these], this aggregate operates and ceases. [Laṅk 10.599]
This is merely a convention, from the assemblage of mutual dependence;
the produced object does not exist, separate from the assemblage of conditions. [Laṅk 10.600]
The absence of the produced is non-arising, free from the fault of heretical [views];

children.text: deśemi saṃkalāmātraṃ na ca bālairvibhāvyate // Lank_10.601 //
children.translated_text: I teach [it as] mere assemblage — but the childish do not discern it. [Laṅk 10.601]

children.text: yasya janyo hi bhāvo 'sti saṃkalāyāḥ pṛthak kvacit /
children.translated_text: For one who holds that an entity produced exists somewhere separate from the assemblage,
he should be known as a proponent of causelessness, a destroyer of the assemblage. [Laṅk 10.602]
For lamps, substances, and birth-classes, the assemblage would be the manifester;

children.text: yasya bhāvo bhavetkaścitsaṃkalāyāḥ pṛthak kvacit // Lank_10.603 //
children.translated_text: for one who holds that any entity exists somewhere separate from the assemblage, [Laṅk 10.603]
without inherent nature, unborn, by nature like space —

children.text: saṃkalāyāḥ pṛthagbhūto yo dharmaḥ kalpito 'budhaiḥ // Lank_10.604 //
children.translated_text: that <s>dharma</s> conceived by the unwise as separate from the assemblage. [Laṅk 10.604]
This [realization of] another's non-arising is the nature of attainment for the noble ones;

children.text: yaśca tasya anutpādaṃ tadanutpādakṣāntiḥ syāt // Lank_10.605 //
children.translated_text: and whoever [realizes] the non-arising of that — that would be the <s>anutpādakṣānti</s> (patient acceptance of non-arising). [Laṅk 10.605]
When one sees all this world as merely an assemblage,
and [sees that] this is merely an assemblage — then the mind is concentrated. [Laṅk 10.606]
Ignorance, craving, <s>karma</s>, and the like constitute the internal assemblage;
the potter's wheel, stick, wheel, and the like, and seed and earth and the like, are external. [Laṅk 10.607]

children.text: parato yasya vai bhāvaḥ pratyayairjāyate kvacit /
children.translated_text: For one whose entity is born from another through conditions somewhere,

children.text: na saṃkalāmātramevedaṃ na te yuktyāgame sthitāḥ // Lank_10.608 //
children.translated_text: this is not merely an assemblage — they do not stand in reasoning and scripture. [Laṅk 10.608]

children.text: yadi janyo na bhāvo 'sti syādbuddhiḥ kasya pratyayāt /
children.translated_text: If no entity is produced, whose understanding would come from conditions?

children.text: anyonyapratyayā hyete te tena pratyayāḥ smṛtāḥ // Lank_10.609 //
children.translated_text: These are mutually conditioned — therefore they are called conditions. [Laṅk 10.609]
Hot, fluid, moving, and hard — <s>dharmas</s> conceptualized by the childish.

children.text: kalāpo 'yaṃ na dharmo 'sti ato vai niḥsvabhāvatā // Lank_10.610 //
children.translated_text: this is [merely] a collection — there is no [independent] <s>dharma</s>; therefore indeed [all things are] without inherent nature. [Laṅk 10.610]
Just as physicians perform different treatments according to the patient's condition,

children.text: na tu śāstrasya bhedo 'sti doṣabhedastu vidyate // Lank_10.611 //
children.translated_text: yet there is no difference in the science [of medicine] — it is the difference in ailments that exists. [Laṅk 10.611]
So too I, knowing the strengths of the faculties

children.text: indriyāṇāṃ balaṃ jñātvā nayaṃ deśemi bāliśān // Lank_10.612 //
children.translated_text: in the continua of beings thoroughly defiled by the afflictions, teach the method to the childish. [Laṅk 10.612]
My teaching is not divided by the difference of afflictions and faculties;
the vehicle is indeed one — the auspicious eightfold path. [Laṅk 10.613]
A pot, a cloth, a crown, a horn — from these causes, the non-existence of a hare's horn [is established];

children.text: yaddhetusamutpannaṃ sa ca nāsti te 'vagantavyam // Lank_10.614 //
children.translated_text: whatever has arisen from causes — that too does not [truly] exist; this you should understand. [Laṅk 10.614]

children.text: astitvasādhakaṃ nāsti nāsti nāsti na yujyate /
children.translated_text: That which establishes existence does not exist; non-existence of non-existence is not tenable;
existence depends on non-existence — [they are] mutually dependent causes. [Laṅk 10.615]

children.text: kiṃcidāśritya punaḥ kiṃcitkhyāyate yasya vai matam /
children.translated_text: If one holds the view that something appears depending on something else,

children.text: ahetukaṃ yadāśritya kiṃciccāhetukaṃ na tu // Lank_10.616 //
children.translated_text: and that which is depended upon is without cause — then that something too is not without cause. [Laṅk 10.616]
But if, depending on yet another, that too appears for another,

children.text: anavasthā prasajyeta kiṃcicca kiṃ ca no bhavet // Lank_10.617 //
children.translated_text: an infinite regress would follow — and there would be neither something nor nothing. [Laṅk 10.617]
Just as illusion occurs depending on leaves, wood, and the like,

children.text: vastu tadvatsamāśritya vaicitryaṃ khyāyate nṛṇām // Lank_10.618 //
children.translated_text: similarly, depending on a [seemingly real] object, variegation appears to people. [Laṅk 10.618]

children.text: māyājālaṃ na parṇāni na kāṣṭhaṃ na ca śarkarā /
children.translated_text: The illusion-net is not the leaves, not the wood, not the pebbles;
it is only the illusion that is seen by the childish — the support through the form of illusion. [Laṅk 10.619]
Similarly, if something perishes depending on an object,

children.text: dṛśyakāle dvayaṃ nāsti kathaṃ kiṃcidvikalpyate // Lank_10.620 //
children.translated_text: at the time of seeing, the duality does not exist — how then can anything be conceptualized? [Laṅk 10.620]
What is conceptualized by conceptualizations does not exist, and conceptualization itself is not found;

children.text: vikalpe hyavidyamāne tu na saṃsṛtirna nirvṛtiḥ // Lank_10.621 //
children.translated_text: when conceptualization does not exist, there is neither <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence) nor cessation. [Laṅk 10.621]

children.text: vikalpe hyavidyamāne tu vikalpo na pravartate /
children.translated_text: When conceptualization does not exist, conceptualization does not operate;

children.text: apravṛttiṃ kathaṃ cittaṃ cittamātraṃ na yujyate // Lank_10.622 //
children.translated_text: how [can there be] non-operation of mind? <s>Cittamātra</s> (mind-only) is not tenable. [Laṅk 10.622]
Due to the multiplicity of differing views, there is no essence in the teaching;

children.text: sārābhāvānna mokṣo 'sti na ca lokavicitratā // Lank_10.623 //
children.translated_text: due to the absence of essence, there is no liberation, and there is no variegation of the world. [Laṅk 10.623]

children.text: bāhyaṃ na vidyate dṛśyaṃ yathā bālairvikalpyate /
children.translated_text: The external visible does not exist as the childish conceptualize it;
the mind appears like a reflection, made to wander by impressions. [Laṅk 10.624]
All entities are indeed unborn, arising from neither the real nor the unreal;
all this is <s>cittamātra</s> (mind-only), and devoid of conceptual constructions. [Laṅk 10.625]
Entities are declared [to arise] from conditions by the childish, not by the wise;
the mind freed from inherent nature — <s>cittamātra</s> is the auspicious domain of the noble ones. [Laṅk 10.626]
<s>Sāṃkhyas</s>, <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s>, <s>Jainas</s> (the naked ones), <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, and <s>Pāśupatas</s> —
fallen into views of existence and non-existence, devoid of the meaning of solitude. [Laṅk 10.627]
Without inherent nature, unborn, empty, like illusion, stainless —

children.text: kasyaite deśitā buddhaistvayā ca prativarṇitāḥ // Lank_10.628 //
children.translated_text: for whom were these taught by the <s>Buddhas</s>, and by you described? [Laṅk 10.628]
For <s>yogīs</s> of pure mind, free from the views and logic —

children.text: buddhā deśenti vai yogaṃ mayā ca prativarṇitāḥ // Lank_10.629 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Buddhas</s> teach <s>yoga</s>, and I have [so] described it. [Laṅk 10.629]
If all this is mind, in what is the world established?

children.text: gamanāgamanaṃ kena dṛśyate bhūtale nṛṇām // Lank_10.630 //
children.translated_text: By what are coming and going seen by people on the ground? [Laṅk 10.630]
Just as a bird in the sky, impelled by conceptualization,
without support and without grasping, moves about on the ground, as it were — [Laṅk 10.631]

children.text: tathā hi dehinaḥ sarve vikalpena samīritāḥ /
children.translated_text: so too all embodied beings, impelled by conceptualization,

children.text: svacitte caṃkramante te gagane śukaniryathā // Lank_10.632 //
children.translated_text: wander in their own minds, like parrots in the sky. [Laṅk 10.632]
Tell [me] — mind operates with the appearance of body, enjoyment, and establishment;

children.text: ābhā vṛttiḥ kathaṃ kena cittamātraṃ vadāhi me // Lank_10.633 //
children.translated_text: what is this appearance and operation, and by what? Tell me about <s>cittamātra</s> (mind-only). [Laṅk 10.633]
Body, enjoyment, and establishment, and the appearance and operation —
arise through impressions for the unenlightened; the appearance and operation are through conceptualizations. [Laṅk 10.634]
The object is an entity conceptualized; mind arises from objects;
through the thorough understanding of the visible and mind, conceptualization does not operate. [Laṅk 10.635]

children.text: nāma nāmni visaṃyuktaṃ yadā paśyati kalpitam /
children.translated_text: When one sees name as disjoined from [what is] named, as conceptualized,
free from intellect and the knowable, then one is liberated from the conditioned. [Laṅk 10.636]
This intellect would be the knowable — the discernment of name in the named;

children.text: ye tvanyathāvabudhyante na te buddhā na bodhakāḥ // Lank_10.637 //
children.translated_text: those who understand otherwise are neither <s>Buddhas</s> nor awakeners. [Laṅk 10.637]

children.text: pañca dharmāḥ svabhāvāśca vijñānānyaṣṭa eva ca /
children.translated_text: The five <s>dharmas</s> and the inherent natures, and the eight <s>vijñānas</s> (consciousnesses),
and the two <s>nairātmyas</s> (selflessnesses) — this constitutes the entire <s>Mahāyāna</s>. [Laṅk 10.638]

children.text: yadā buddhiśca boddhavyaṃ viviktaṃ paśyate jagat /
children.translated_text: When one sees the world with intellect and the knowable as solitary,

children.text: nāsti nāma vikalpaśca tadā nābhipravartate // Lank_10.639 //
children.translated_text: then name and conceptualization do not operate. [Laṅk 10.639]
The cessation of conceptualization of action, syllable, and [linguistic] concepts [comes] from seeing the mind;
from the non-seeing of one's own mind, conceptualization operates. [Laṅk 10.640]

children.text: catvāro 'rūpiṇaḥ skandhāḥ saṃkhyā teṣāṃ na vidyate /
children.translated_text: The four formless aggregates — their enumeration is not found;
form, with characteristics different from the elements — how [can there be] multiplicity of form? [Laṅk 10.641]

children.text: lakṣaṇasya parityāgānna bhūtaṃ na ca bhautikam /
children.translated_text: Through the abandonment of characteristics, there is neither element nor elemental;
but if form has other characteristics, why is it not born from the aggregates? [Laṅk 10.642]
When one sees the aggregates, sense-bases, and elements as free from characteristics and liberated,
then the mind turns back from seeing <s>dharma-nairātmya</s> (selflessness of phenomena). [Laṅk 10.643]
Through the differentiation of objects and sense faculties, <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) arises in eight forms;
by characteristics they are three; in the imageless, [they] cease. [Laṅk 10.644]

children.text: ālayaṃ hi manasyātmā ātmīyaṃ jñānameva ca /
children.translated_text: In the <s>ālaya</s> (store-consciousness), <s>manas</s> [cognizes] self and what belongs to self, and knowledge itself;
it operates through the grasping of duality; through thorough understanding, it ceases. [Laṅk 10.645]
When one sees [reality as] free from other and non-other, without movement,

children.text: tadā dvayaṃ na kalpanti ātmā cātmīyameva ca // Lank_10.646 //
children.translated_text: then one does not conceptualize the duality — self and what belongs to self. [Laṅk 10.646]

children.text: apravṛttaṃ na puṣṇāti na ca vijñānakāraṇam /
children.translated_text: What has not operated does not nourish, nor is it a cause of consciousness;
freed from effect and cause, what has ceased does not operate. [Laṅk 10.647]

children.text: vikalpaṃ cittamātraṃ ca lokaṃ kena vadāhi me /
children.translated_text: Tell me by what [you teach] conceptualization, <s>cittamātra</s> (mind-only), and the world —
disjoined from causes, free from the characterized and characteristics. [Laṅk 10.648]
One's own mind is seen as variegated, conceptualized in the form of the visible;
through not thoroughly understanding the visible [as] mind, [one grasps at] another through the collection of mind and objects. [Laṅk 10.649]
The view of non-existence arises when one does not see with wisdom;

children.text: astitvaṃ hi kathaṃ tasya cittagrāhānna jāyate // Lank_10.650 //
children.translated_text: how can existence arise for one who does not grasp at mind? [Laṅk 10.650]

children.text: vikalpo na bhāvo nābhāvo ato 'stitvaṃ na jāyate /
children.translated_text: Conceptualization is neither entity nor non-entity; therefore existence does not arise;
through thorough understanding of the visible [as] mind, conceptualization does not operate. [Laṅk 10.651]
The non-operation of conceptualization is the turning-around, without support;

children.text: nivārya pakṣāṃścatvāro yadi bhāvā sahetukāḥ // Lank_10.652 //
children.translated_text: having rejected the four alternatives — if entities have causes — [Laṅk 10.652]
this is a distinction of designation — how is it established and by whom?
Implication would follow for them, or it operates from a cause. [Laṅk 10.653]
Through the conjunction of cause and condition, from the negation of the cause,

children.text: nityadoṣo nivāryate anityā yadi pratyayāḥ // Lank_10.654 //
children.translated_text: the fault of permanence is averted, if the conditions are impermanent. [Laṅk 10.654]

children.text: na saṃbhavo na vibhavo anityatvāddhi bāliśām /
children.translated_text: There is neither arising nor dissolution, due to the impermanence of the childish;

children.text: na hi naśyamānaṃ kiṃcidvai kāraṇatvena dṛśyate // Lank_10.655 //
children.translated_text: nothing whatsoever that is perishing is seen as a cause. [Laṅk 10.655]

children.text: adṛṣṭaṃ hi kathaṃ kena nānityo jāyate bhavaḥ /
children.translated_text: What is unseen — how and by whom? The impermanent does not arise as becoming;

children.text: saṃgrahaiśca dametsattvān śīlena ca vaśīkaret // Lank_10.656 //
children.translated_text: one should tame beings through generosity and bring them under control through moral discipline. [Laṅk 10.656]
Through wisdom one should destroy views, and through liberations one should increase [realization];
all this <s>lokāyata</s> (materialism) is what the heretics teach falsely. [Laṅk 10.657]
Through the view of cause and effect as real, their own established doctrine is not found;
I [teach] one established doctrine, free from cause and effect. [Laṅk 10.658]
I teach my assembly of disciples, free from <s>lokāyata</s> (materialism);

children.text: cittamātraṃ na dṛśyo 'sti dvidhā cittaṃ vidṛśyate /
children.translated_text: <s>cittamātra</s> (mind-only) — the visible does not exist; the mind is seen as twofold —
through the [false] appearance of graspable and grasper — free from eternalism and annihilationism. [Laṅk 10.659]
So long as the mind operates, so long will there be <s>lokāyata</s> (materialism);
the non-operation of conceptualization [comes from] seeing one's own mind as the world. [Laṅk 10.660]
Income is the production of effects; expenditure is the perception of effects;
through the thorough understanding of income and expenditure, conceptualization does not operate. [Laṅk 10.661]
Permanent and impermanent, made and unmade, prior and subsequent —
all such [dualities] would be <s>lokāyata</s> (materialism). [Laṅk 10.662]
<s>Devas</s> (gods), <s>asuras</s> (demons), humans, animals, hungry ghosts, and hell-dwellers —

children.text: gatayaḥ ṣaṭ samākhyātā yatra jāyanti dehinaḥ // Lank_10.663 //
children.translated_text: these six destinies are declared, where embodied beings are born. [Laṅk 10.663]
Through inferior, superior, and middling <s>karma</s> (action), one is born in those [destinies];

children.text: saraṃkṣya kuśalān sarvān viśeṣo mokṣa eva vā // Lank_10.664 //
children.translated_text: preserving all wholesome [actions], [one attains] distinction or liberation itself. [Laṅk 10.664]

children.text: kṣaṇe kṣaṇe tvayā yanmaraṇaṃ upapattiṃ ca /
children.translated_text: That moment-by-moment death and rebirth which you

children.text: deśyate bhikṣuvargasya abhiprāyaṃ vadāhi me // Lank_10.665 //
children.translated_text: teach to the assembly of monks — tell me the intention. [Laṅk 10.665]
Just as mind, having come together from form to [another] form, is broken apart,
therefore I teach my disciples the succession of momentary births. [Laṅk 10.666]
In each form, there is the arising and dissolution of conceptualization;

children.text: vikalpo hi bhavejjanturvikalpo 'nyo na vidyate // Lank_10.667 //
children.translated_text: for conceptualization is indeed the being — another conceptualization is not found. [Laṅk 10.667]
The moment-by-moment [arising] is not tenable — this is spoken with reference to conditions;

children.text: rūpagrāhavinirmuktaṃ na janma na ca bhajyate // Lank_10.668 //
children.translated_text: freed from the grasping of form, there is neither birth nor dissolution. [Laṅk 10.668]
Conditions arisen from conditions — ignorance, <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), and so forth —

children.text: dharmadvayena vartante advayā tathatā bhavet // Lank_10.669 //
children.translated_text: operate through a duality of <s>dharmas</s>; <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) would be non-dual. [Laṅk 10.669]
If conditions arisen from conditions are <s>dharmas</s> that are differentiated,

children.text: nityādayo bhavetkāryaṃ kāraṇaṃ pratyayo bhavet // Lank_10.670 //
children.translated_text: permanence and the like would be the effect, and the condition would be the cause. [Laṅk 10.670]
The teaching would be undifferentiated from the heretics through the collection of cause and effect —

children.text: vādastava ca buddhānāṃ tasmānnāryo mahāmune // Lank_10.671 //
children.translated_text: your teaching and that of the <s>Buddhas</s> — therefore, [this is] not noble, O great sage. [Laṅk 10.671]

children.text: śarīre vyāmamātre ca lokaṃ vai lokasamudayam /
children.translated_text: In this body measuring a fathom, [I teach] the world and the origination of the world,
and the path leading to cessation — I teach the sons of the Conqueror. [Laṅk 10.672]
Through the grasping of the three natures, with views of graspable and grasper,
ordinary people conceptualize worldly and supramundane <s>dharmas</s>. [Laṅk 10.673]
Therefore, the grasping of inherent natures is undertaken as a preliminary objection;

children.text: nivārārthaṃ tu dṛṣṭīnāṃ svabhāvaṃ na vikalpayet // Lank_10.674 //
children.translated_text: but for the purpose of averting views, one should not conceptualize inherent nature. [Laṅk 10.674]

children.text: chidradoṣānna niyamo na vā cittaṃ pravartate /
children.translated_text: Due to the fault of gaps, there is no regularity, nor does mind operate;
through the grasping of the duality of operation, <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) would be non-dual. [Laṅk 10.675]

children.text: ajñāna tṛṣṇā karma ca vijñānādyā ayonijāḥ /
children.translated_text: Ignorance, craving, action, and consciousness and the rest are born from improper [attention];

children.text: anavasthākṛtakatvaṃ ca na kṛtvā jāyate bhavaḥ // Lank_10.676 //
children.translated_text: through the absence of infinite regress and being made, becoming does not arise without being produced. [Laṅk 10.676]
The fourfold destruction of entities is spoken of by the unwise;
through the twofold turning of conceptualization, entity and non-entity are not found —
free from the <s>catuṣkoṭi</s> (four alternatives), devoid of the two views. [Laṅk 10.677]
The twofold turning of conceptualization — having seen [it], one does not operate;
when entities are unborn, through the nature of the <s>Buddha's</s> rising [from meditation]. [Laṅk 10.678]
Even when entities have arisen, one should not conceptualize them as being of that moment;

children.text: yuktiṃ vadāhi me nātha dvidhādṛṣṭinivāraṇāt // Lank_10.679 //
children.translated_text: tell me the reasoning, O Lord, for averting the twofold view. [Laṅk 10.679]

children.text: yathāhamanye ca sadā nāstyasti na visaṃkaret /
children.translated_text: Just as I and others always [teach] — one should not doubt existence and non-existence;
unmixed with heretical doctrines, free from <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers) and Conquerors,
and the practice of the <s>Jina's</s> (Conqueror's) realization — the sons of the <s>Jina</s> are imperishable. [Laṅk 10.680]
Whether with or without cause for liberation, having the single characteristic of non-arising —
by synonyms they confuse this [teaching], which should always be avoided by the wise. [Laṅk 10.681]
Shining like clouds, mists, mountain peaks, and rainbows — comparable to mirages, hair-nets, round balls, and illusions —

children.text: bhāvā hi sarve svavikalpasaṃbhavāstīrthyā vikalpenti jagatsvakāraṇaiḥ // Lank_10.682 //
children.translated_text: for all entities arise from one's own conceptualization — heretics conceptualize the world through their own causes. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.682 ||
Non-arising, suchness, the limit of reality, and emptiness —

children.text: rūpasya nāmānyetāni abhāvaṃ na vikalpayet // Lank_10.683 //
children.translated_text: these are names of form; one should not conceptualize non-existence. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.683 ||

children.text: hastaḥ karo yathā loke indraḥ śakraḥ puraṃdaraḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as in the world, 'hand' and 'palm,' '<s>Indra</s>' and '<s>Śakra</s>' and '<s>Puraṃdara</s>' [are synonyms] —

children.text: tathā hi sarvabhāvānāmabhāvaṃ na vikalpayet // Lank_10.684 //
children.translated_text: so too for all entities, one should not conceptualize non-existence. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.684 ||

children.text: rūpācca śūnyatā nānyā anutpādaṃ tathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: Emptiness is not other than form, and likewise non-arising;
one should not conceptualize non-otherness — the fault of views would follow. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.685 ||
Thought (<s>saṃkalpa</s>) and conceptualization (<s>vikalpa</s>) [arise] from the grasping of the characteristics of entities;
long, short, and round, and so forth — from the grasping of the imagined. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.686 ||
Thought (<s>saṃkalpa</s>) would be mind (<s>citta</s>); imagination (<s>parikalpa</s>) is <s>manas</s> likewise;
conceptualization (<s>vikalpa</s>) is <s>manovijñāna</s> — devoid of the characterized and the characteristic. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.687 ||
That non-arising [declared] by heretics and that [declared] by those of my doctrinal views —
this one is conceptualized as undifferentiated — the fault of views would follow. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.688 ||
The purpose of non-arising, and the meaning of non-arising itself —

children.text: ye vai jānanti yuktijñāste 'bhibudhyanti mannayam // Lank_10.689 //
children.translated_text: those who know through reasoning and know [both] — they understand my doctrine. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.689 ||
The purpose is the contraction of views; non-arising is without support (<s>anālaya</s>);
from the full understanding of both meanings, I speak of non-arising. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.690 ||

children.text: bhāvā vidyantyanutpannā na vā brūhi mahāmune /
children.translated_text: 'Do entities exist as non-arisen, or not?' — tell [me], O Great Sage;
'Non-arising is the doctrine of no-cause; operation is the heretical view.' || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.691 ||
'Non-arising is the doctrine of no-cause; it is the unequal heretical view.'
Freed from 'exists' and 'does not exist,' I speak of mind-only. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.692 ||
One should avoid arising and non-arising that are caused by views;
in the doctrine of no-cause and non-arising, and in arising, there is reliance on cause. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.693 ||
Without effort, action does not exist; and if there is action, there is a mixture of views;
through skillful means, vows, and the rest, tell me about views alone —
since all <s>dharmas</s> are non-existent, how does the circle [of existence] arise? || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.694 ||
From the disjunction of grasped and grasper, there is no operation and no cessation;

children.text: bhāvādbhāvāntaraṃ dṛṣṭiṃ cittaṃ vai tatsamutthitam // Lank_10.695 //
children.translated_text: the view of one entity from another — mind is indeed arisen from that. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.695 ||
'And the non-arising of <s>dharmas</s> — tell me, how is this?'
'If beings do not understand, therefore this is illuminated.' || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.696 ||
'Speak all the contradictions of earlier and later, O Great Sage,
freed from the faults of heretics, and free from the unequal without cause.' || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.697 ||
'Non-operation and cessation — tell me, O best of speakers,
freed from 'exists' and 'does not exist,' without destruction of cause and effect.' || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.698 ||
'The connection and sequence of stages — tell me the characteristic of <s>Dharma</s>;
the world has fallen into both extremes, confused by views.' || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.699 ||
'Non-arising, through arising and the rest, the cause of quiescence is not understood;

children.text: maṇḍalaṃ hi na me kiṃcinna ca deśemi dharmatām // Lank_10.700 //
children.translated_text: for I have no circle [of doctrine] at all, nor do I teach <s>dharmatā</s> (the nature of dharma).' || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.700 ||
