children.text: dvaye sati hi doṣaḥ syāddvayaṃ buddhairviśodhitam /
children.translated_text: 'When duality exists, there would be a fault; duality is purified by the Buddhas;

children.text: śūnyāśca kṣaṇikā bhāvā niḥsvabhāvā hyajātikāḥ // Lank_10.701 //
children.translated_text: entities are empty, momentary, without inherent nature, and birthless.' || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.701 ||
'These are conceptualized by those covered by wrong views — not by <s>Tathāgatas</s>.'

children.text: pravṛttiṃ ca nivṛttiṃ ca vikalpasya vadāhi me // Lank_10.702 //
children.translated_text: 'The operation and cessation of conceptualization — tell me [about them].' || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.702 ||

children.text: yathā yena prakāreṇa jāyate viṣayo mukham /
children.translated_text: 'In whatever way and by whatever manner the object-face arises,
from the conjunction of fullness and color, it is brought forth by proliferations.' || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.703 ||

children.text: rūpaṃ dṛṣṭvā bahirdhā vai vikalpaḥ saṃpravartate /
children.translated_text: 'Having seen form externally, conceptualization operates;
from the full understanding of that very [form], from seeing things as they truly are,
mind does not operate in conformity with the noble lineage.' || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.704 ||
Having rejected the elements, the arising of entities is not found;
one should discern that mind, having the form of elements, is always non-arisen. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.705 ||

children.text: mā vikalpaṃ vikalpetha nirvikalpā hi paṇḍitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Do not conceptualize conceptualization — for the wise are free from conceptualization;

children.text: vikalpaṃ vikalpayaṃstasya dvayameva na nirvṛtiḥ // Lank_10.706 //
children.translated_text: for one who conceptualizes conceptualization, there is only duality, not cessation. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.706 ||
For one who maintains the thesis of non-arising, illusion is seen as the method;
illusion, arising without cause — this has the characteristic of defeating [one's own] thesis. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.707 ||
Mind appears like a reflection, cultivated by beginningless intellect;

children.text: arthākāraṃ na cārtho 'sti yathābhūtaṃ vibhāvayet // Lank_10.708 //
children.translated_text: it has the form of objects, but objects do not exist — one should discern this as it truly is. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.708 ||
Just as form in a mirror, free from oneness and otherness,

children.text: dṛśyate na ca tannāsti tathā cotpādalakṣaṇam // Lank_10.709 //
children.translated_text: is seen yet does not [truly] exist — so too is the characteristic of arising. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.709 ||
Just as <s>gandharva</s>-[city], illusion, and the rest have the characteristics of causes and conditions,

children.text: tathā hi sarvabhāvānāṃ saṃbhavo na hyasaṃbhavaḥ // Lank_10.710 //
children.translated_text: so too for all entities there is arising, but not non-arising. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.710 ||
Conceptualization, having the form of a person, operates in a twofold operation:
through the metaphors of self and <s>dharma</s> — but this is not discerned by the childish. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.711 ||
Dependent on abundant conditions, even the <s>Śrāvaka</s> becomes an <s>Arhat</s>;

children.text: svabalādhīnaṃ jinādhīnaṃ pañcamaṃ śrāvakaṃ nayet // Lank_10.712 //
children.translated_text: dependent on one's own power and the <s>Jina</s>'s [power], the fifth [stage] would lead the <s>Śrāvaka</s>. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.712 ||
Time-interval, destruction, the ultimate, and mutual [dependence] —
the childish, unskilled, conceptualize the fourfold impermanence. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.713 ||
The childish, fallen into both extremes, through qualities, atoms, and the causes of <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature),
do not know the means of liberation, from grasping the sides of existent and non-existent. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.714 ||
Just as the childish of poor intellect grasp the moon at the tip of a finger,
so too those attached to syllables do not know my truth. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.715 ||
The elements are of different characteristics, operating in the form of entities;

children.text: bhūtānāṃ saṃniveśo 'yaṃ na bhūtairbhautikaṃ kṛtam // Lank_10.716 //
children.translated_text: this is the arrangement of elements — the elemental product is not made by elements. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.716 ||
By fire, form is burned; the water-element has the nature of moistening;

children.text: vāyunā kīryate rūpaṃ kathaṃ bhūtaiḥ pravartate // Lank_10.717 //
children.translated_text: by wind, form is scattered — how does [form] operate through elements? || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.717 ||
Form and aggregates and consciousness — these are two, not five;
I teach the differentiation of the aggregates by synonyms in a hundredfold [way]. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.718 ||
Through the differentiation of mind and mental factors, the present operates;

children.text: vyatibhinnāni rūpāṇi cittaṃ rūpaṃ na bhautikam // Lank_10.719 //
children.translated_text: forms are differentiated — mind is form, not elemental product. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.719 ||
Blue and the rest depend on white; white depends on blue;

children.text: kāryakāraṇamutpādya śūnyatā asti nāsti ca // Lank_10.720 //
children.translated_text: having produced cause and effect, emptiness both exists and does not exist. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.720 ||
The means, the prover, and what is to be proved, cold and hot, the characterized and the characteristic —
all these and the rest are not established by logicians. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.721 ||
Mind, <s>manas</s>, and the other six consciousnesses, conjoined with self —
devoid of oneness and otherness, this <s>ālaya</s> (store-consciousness) operates. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.722 ||
<s>Sāṃkhyas</s>, <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s>, <s>Nirgranthas</s> (Jains), logicians, and those who proclaim <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord) —
fallen into the sides of existent and non-existent, they are devoid of the isolated meaning. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.723 ||
The distinction of configuration and shape of elements — there is no elemental product;

children.text: tīrthyā vadanti janma bhūtānāṃ bhautikasya ca // Lank_10.724 //
children.translated_text: the heretics speak of the birth of elements and of the elemental product. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.724 ||

children.text: anutpannā yato ye 'nye tīrthyāḥ kalpanti kāraṇaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Those that are non-arisen — other heretics conceptualize [them] through causes;

children.text: na ca budhyanti mohena sadasatpakṣamāśritāḥ // Lank_10.725 //
children.translated_text: but they do not understand, through delusion, having resorted to the sides of existent and non-existent. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.725 ||
Conjoined with mind, disjoined from <s>manas</s> and the rest,

children.text: viśuddhalakṣaṇaṃ sattvaṃ jñānena saha tiṣṭhati // Lank_10.726 //
children.translated_text: the being with the characteristic of purity abides together with knowledge. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.726 ||
<s>Karma</s>, which would be form, is caused by aggregates and sense-objects;
beings without appropriation do not abide in the formless [realm]. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.727 ||
Selflessness, being a speaker of beings — from the non-existence of beings, this follows;
the proponent of selflessness [holds] annihilation, and even the non-arising of consciousness. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.728 ||
Four [elements] abide in that — from the non-existence of form, how would [the formless realm] exist?
From the non-existence of internal and external, consciousness does not operate. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.729 ||
The aggregates of the intermediate state — just as the logicians wish;

children.text: tathārūpyopapannasya bhavo 'rūpo na cāsti kim // Lank_10.730 //
children.translated_text: for one born in the formless realm likewise — is there not a formless existence? || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.730 ||
Without effort, liberation would occur — without being or consciousness;

children.text: tīrthyavādo na saṃdeho na ca budhyanti tārkikāḥ // Lank_10.731 //
children.translated_text: this is heretical doctrine, no doubt — and the logicians do not understand. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.731 ||

children.text: rūpaṃ ca vidyate tatra ārūpye nāsti darśanam /
children.translated_text: Form exists therein — in the formless there is no seeing;

children.text: tadabhāvo na siddhānto na yānaṃ na ca yāyinam // Lank_10.732 //
children.translated_text: the non-existence of that is not the doctrine — there is no vehicle and no traveler. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.732 ||
Consciousness, conjoined with the faculties, arises from impressions;

children.text: aṣṭavidhaikadeśaṃ hi kṣaṇe kāle na gṛhṇanti // Lank_10.733 //
children.translated_text: as a portion of the eightfold [vijñāna], they do not grasp [objects] in a moment of time. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.733 ||

children.text: na pravartati yadā rūpaṃ indriyā na ca indriyaiḥ /
children.translated_text: When form does not operate, and the faculties [do not operate] through the faculties —

children.text: ato hi deśeti bhagavān kṣaṇikā indriyādayaḥ // Lank_10.734 //
children.translated_text: therefore the Blessed One teaches: the faculties and the rest are momentary. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.734 ||
Without ascertaining form, how will consciousness operate?

children.text: apravṛttaṃ kathaṃ jñānaṃ saṃsāraṃ janayiṣyati // Lank_10.735 //
children.translated_text: Without operating, how will knowledge generate <s>saṃsāra</s>? || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.735 ||
The Guides do not teach destruction immediately upon arising;

children.text: nairantaryaṃ na bhāvānāṃ vikalpaspandite gatau // Lank_10.736 //
children.translated_text: there is no uninterrupted [continuity] for entities — in the course [where] conceptualization vibrates. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.736 ||

children.text: indriyā indriyārthāśca mūḍhānāṃ na tu paṇḍitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Faculties and faculty-objects — for the deluded, not for the wise;

children.text: bālā gṛhṇanti nāmena āryā vai arthakovidāḥ // Lank_10.737 //
children.translated_text: the childish grasp by name, while the noble are skilled in meaning. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.737 ||

children.text: ṣaṣṭhaṃ hi nirupādānaḥ sopādāno na gṛhyate /
children.translated_text: The sixth [consciousness] is without appropriation; [the mind] with appropriation is not grasped;
the noble declare it indeterminate, free from the faults of 'exists.' || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.738 ||
Fearing eternalism and annihilationism, the logicians, devoid of knowledge,
the childish do not distinguish the self as conditioned or unconditioned. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.739 ||
In oneness, giving exists; in otherness too, giving exists;

children.text: cittena saha caikatvamanyatvaṃ vai manādibhiḥ // Lank_10.740 //
children.translated_text: oneness with mind, and otherness with <s>manas</s> and the rest. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.740 ||
When giving is ascertained, mind is said to be 'mental factor' (<s>caitta</s>);
through appropriation, how is it determined therein as oneness? || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.741 ||
The apprehension of [mind] with appropriation — through <s>karma</s>, birth, action, and the rest —
they will establish [it] by similar and dissimilar methods, like fire. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.742 ||
Just as fire simultaneously burns — both the burnt and the burner —

children.text: sopādānastathā hyātmā tārkikaiḥ kiṃ na gṛhyate // Lank_10.743 //
children.translated_text: so too the self with appropriation — why is it not grasped by logicians? || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.743 ||
Whether from arising or non-arising, mind is always luminous;

children.text: dṛṣṭāntaṃ kiṃ na kurvanti tārkikā ātmasādhakāḥ // Lank_10.744 //
children.translated_text: why do the logicians, proponents of self, not make [this] an example? || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.744 ||
The logicians, deluded in the thicket of consciousness, devoid of method,
run here and there, wishing to make the doctrine of self. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.745 ||
To be reached through one's own inner realization, the self has the characteristic of purity;
that is the embryo of the <s>Tathāgata</s> — beyond the domain of logicians. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.746 ||
Of the appropriated and the appropriator, and the division of aggregates likewise —

children.text: lakṣaṇaṃ yadi jānāti jñānaṃ saṃjāyate nayam // Lank_10.747 //
children.translated_text: if one knows the characteristic, the knowledge-method arises. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.747 ||
The <s>ālaya</s> (store), the configuration of the embryo, is described similarly to [what is] held by heretics;

children.text: ātmanā saha saṃyuktaṃ na ca dharmāḥ prakīrtitāḥ // Lank_10.748 //
children.translated_text: conjoined with self — but <s>dharmas</s> are not proclaimed [therein]. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.748 ||
Through the differentiation of these, liberation is the seeing of truth;
there would be the purification of afflictions — of entities to be seen and abandoned. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.749 ||
Mind is luminous by nature (<s>prakṛtiprabhāsvara</s>); the auspicious embryo of the <s>Tathāgata</s>;
the appropriation of the being is devoid of end and endlessness. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.750 ||
Just as the luster of gold — the raw gold and the [gold in] gravel —
through refinement they see the being; so too through aggregates and <s>ālaya</s>. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.751 ||

children.text: na pudgalo na ca skandhā buddho jñānamanāsravam /
children.translated_text: Neither person nor aggregates — the <s>Buddha</s> is undefiled knowledge;

children.text: sadāśāntiṃ vibhāvitvā gacchāmi śaraṇaṃ hyaham // Lank_10.752 //
children.translated_text: having discerned eternal peace, I go for refuge. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.752 ||
Mind is luminous by nature; through the adventitious defilements of <s>manas</s> and the rest,

children.text: ātmanā saha saṃyuktaṃ deśeti vadatāṃvaraḥ // Lank_10.753 //
children.translated_text: conjoined with self — the best of speakers teaches [this]. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.753 ||
Mind is luminous by nature; <s>manas</s> and the rest are other to it;

children.text: tairācitāni karmāṇi yataḥ kliśyanti tāvubhau // Lank_10.754 //
children.translated_text: by those, <s>karmas</s> are accumulated — from which both [mind and manas] are afflicted. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.754 ||
Through adventitious and beginningless afflictions, the self is luminous;
it is defiled and, when approached [by purification], is purified like a garment. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.755 ||
Just as a garment, when free from stain, or gold when free from faults,

children.text: tiṣṭhanti na ca naśyante ātmā doṣaistathā vinā // Lank_10.756 //
children.translated_text: endures and does not perish — so the self, when free from faults. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.756 ||
In a <s>vīṇā</s>, conch, or drum, [one might search for] the richness of sweet sound;
someone unskilled might search — so for the person (<s>pudgala</s>) in the aggregates. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.757 ||
Treasures and gems in the earth, and water likewise,

children.text: vidyamānā na dṛśyanti tathā skandheṣu pudgalam // Lank_10.758 //
children.translated_text: are present yet not seen — so the person in the aggregates. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.758 ||
The collection of mind and mental factors, [each] with its own qualities, conjoined with the aggregates —

children.text: akovidā na gṛhṇanti tathā skandheṣu pudgalam // Lank_10.759 //
children.translated_text: the unskilled do not grasp [them], so [they do not grasp] the person in the aggregates. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.759 ||

children.text: yathā hi garbho garbhiṇyāṃ vidyate na ca dṛśyate /
children.translated_text: Just as an embryo in a pregnant woman is present yet not seen,

children.text: ātmā hi tadvatskandheṣu ayuktijño na paśyati // Lank_10.760 //
children.translated_text: so the self in the aggregates — one who does not know reasoning does not see it. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.760 ||
Just as the essence of medicinal herbs, or fire within fuel —

children.text: na paśyanti ayuktijñāstathā skandheṣu pudgalam // Lank_10.761 //
children.translated_text: those who do not know reasoning do not see the person in the aggregates. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.761 ||
Just as the undiscerning do not see the impermanence and emptiness present in all entities,

children.text: vidyamānāṃ na paśyanti tathā skandheṣu pudgalam // Lank_10.762 //
children.translated_text: so [they do not see] the person in the aggregates. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.762 ||
The stages, masteries, superknowledges, and the supreme consecration,

children.text: samādhayo viśeṣāśca asatyātmani nāsti vai // Lank_10.763 //
children.translated_text: <s>samādhis</s> and distinctions — do not exist when the self is unreal. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.763 ||
When an annihilationist, having come, would say: 'If [the self] exists, let it be shown!' —

children.text: sa vaktavyo bhavedvijñaḥ svavikalpaṃ pradarśaya // Lank_10.764 //
children.translated_text: he should be told: 'Be wise — show your own discrimination!' || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.764 ||
Proponents of selflessness are not to be conversed with; monastic duties should be avoided [with them];
harmful to the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> are those who hold views of the sides of existent and non-existent. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.765 ||
Freed from the faults of heretical teachers, burning the forest of selflessness,
this doctrine of the self blazes forth like the fire at the end of an age, risen up. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.766 ||
In pieces of sugarcane, in sugar, honey, and the like, in curds, sesame, ghee, and the like,

children.text: svarasaṃ vidyate teṣu anāsvādyaṃ na gṛhyate // Lank_10.767 //
children.translated_text: the natural flavor exists in them — [but if] not tasted, it is not grasped. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.767 ||
Grasped in fivefold manner, the self in the aggregate-collection —

children.text: na ca paśyantyavidvāṃso vidvān dṛṣṭvā vimucyate // Lank_10.768 //
children.translated_text: the unlearned do not see [it]; the learned one, having seen, is liberated. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.768 ||
By analogies of knowledge and the like, mind is not ascertained;

children.text: yatra yasmādyadarthaṃ ca samūhaṃ nāvadhāryate // Lank_10.769 //
children.translated_text: where, from where, for what purpose — the aggregate is not ascertained. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.769 ||

children.text: vilakṣaṇā hi vai dharmāścittamekaṃ na gṛhyate /
children.translated_text: For <s>dharmas</s> are indeed of diverse characteristics; one mind is not grasped;
causelessness and non-operation would follow for the logicians. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.770 ||

children.text: cittānupaśyī ca yogī cittaṃ citte na paśyati /
children.translated_text: The <s>yogin</s> who contemplates mind does not see mind in mind;

children.text: paśyako dṛśyanirjāto dṛśyaṃ kiṃ hetusaṃbhavam // Lank_10.771 //
children.translated_text: the seer is produced from the seen — the seen, how is it produced from a cause? || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.771 ||
I am of the <s>Kātyāyana</s> lineage, gone forth from the <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> (Pure Abodes);
I teach the <s>Dharma</s> to beings, leading toward the city of <s>nirvāṇa</s>. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.772 ||

children.text: paurāṇikamidaṃ vartma ahaṃ te ca tathāgatāḥ /
children.translated_text: This is the ancient path — I and those <s>Tathāgatas</s>,
with three thousand <s>sūtras</s>, taught <s>nirvāṇa</s> exceedingly. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.773 ||

children.text: kāmadhātau tathārūpye na vai buddho vibudhyate /
children.translated_text: In the desire-realm or in the formless, a <s>Buddha</s> does not indeed awaken;
in the form-realm, in <s>Akaniṣṭha</s>, among those free from passion, one awakens. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.774 ||
Sense-objects are not the cause of bondage; the cause of bondage to objects [is within];
by knowledge the afflictions are bound — this is the vow of the razor's edge. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.775 ||

children.text: asatyātmani māyādyā dharmā nāstyasti vai katham /
children.translated_text: When the self is unreal, how can <s>dharmas</s> such as illusion [have] 'does not exist' and 'exists'?

children.text: bālānāṃ khyāti tathatā kathaṃ nāsti nirātmikā // Lank_10.776 //
children.translated_text: How does suchness appear to the childish — does it not exist, being selfless? || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.776 ||
Because of being both created and uncreated, there is no operative cause;

children.text: anutpannamidaṃ sarvaṃ na ca bālairvibhāvyate // Lank_10.777 //
children.translated_text: all this is unborn — but the childish do not discern [this]. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.777 ||
Causes are unborn and conditions are created;

children.text: dvāvapyetau na janakau kāraṇaiḥ kalpyate katham // Lank_10.778 //
children.translated_text: both of these are not producers — how is it conceptualized through causes? || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.778 ||
Before, after, and simultaneously — the logicians describe causes;
by [analogies of] light, pot, pupil, and the like, the birth of entities is proclaimed. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.779 ||
<s>Buddhas</s> are not endowed with marks that are created through preparation;
these are the qualities of a wheel-turning [monarch] — they are not proclaimed by the <s>Buddha</s>. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.780 ||
The mark of the <s>Buddhas</s> is knowledge, free from the faults of [wrong] views,
having the course of self-realized vision, destroying all faults. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.781 ||
For the deaf, blind, one-eyed, mute, the aged, those of hostile conduct,

children.text: bālānāṃ ca viśeṣeṇa brahmacaryaṃ na vidyate // Lank_10.782 //
children.translated_text: and the childish in particular — the holy life does not exist. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.782 ||
By the concealed divine marks and signs of a wheel-turner,

children.text: vyañjitaiḥ pravrajantyeke na cānye ca pravādinaḥ // Lank_10.783 //
children.translated_text: some go forth by disclosed [marks] — and others are speakers [without them]. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.783 ||
<s>Vyāsa</s>, <s>Kaṇāda</s>, <s>Ṛṣabha</s>, <s>Kapila</s>, and the <s>Śākya</s> leader —
after my <s>nirvāṇa</s>, such ones will arise. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.784 ||

children.text: mayi nirvṛte varṣaśate vyāso vai bhāratastathā /
children.translated_text: A hundred years after my <s>nirvāṇa</s>, <s>Vyāsa</s> and the <s>Bhārata</s> [epic],

children.text: pāṇḍavāḥ kauravā rāmaḥ paścānmaurī bhaviṣyati // Lank_10.785 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>, <s>Kauravas</s>, <s>Rāma</s> — and afterward the <s>Maurya</s> [dynasty] will be. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.785 ||

children.text: mauryā nandāśca guptāśca tato mlecchā nṛpādhamāḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>Mauryas</s>, <s>Nandas</s>, and <s>Guptas</s> — then <s>Mlecchas</s>, the lowest kings;
at the end of the <s>Mlecchas</s>, upheaval of weapons; at the end of weapons, the <s>Kali</s> age;

children.text: kaliyugānte lokaiśca saddharmo hi na bhāvitaḥ // Lank_10.786 //
children.translated_text: at the end of the <s>Kali</s> age, the True <s>Dharma</s> is not cultivated by the world. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.786 ||
Such past [events] — the world revolves like a wheel;
from the conjunction of fire and sun, the desire-realm is shattered. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.787 ||
Again the divine [world] will be established, and the world will proceed in it —

children.text: cātuṃ rvarṇā nṛpendrāśca ṛṣayo dharmameva ca // Lank_10.788 //
children.translated_text: the four castes, the kings, the sages, and the <s>Dharma</s> itself. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.788 ||

children.text: vedāśca yajñaṃ dānaṃ ca dharmasthā vartsyate punaḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>Vedas</s>, sacrifice, giving — and [the world] will proceed established in <s>Dharma</s>;
with narratives, histories, and the like, prose, verse-commentaries —

children.text: evaṃ mayā śrutādibhyo loko vai vibhramiṣyati // Lank_10.789 //
children.translated_text: thus from what I have heard and the like, the world will indeed be confused. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.789 ||
Having made the top well-dyed in red, one should color [the garment] above;
with blue mud and cow-dung, one should variegate the cloth;
with all kinds of dress, variegated in limb, devoid of heretical emblems — || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.790 ||
the <s>yogin</s> should teach the teaching — this indeed is the banner of the <s>Buddhas</s>;

children.text: vastrapūtaṃ jalaṃ peyaṃ kaṭisūtraṃ ca dhārayet /
children.translated_text: cloth-filtered water should be drunk, and a waist-cord should be worn;

children.text: upapadyamānaṃ kālena bhaikṣyaṃ vā nīcavarjitam // Lank_10.791 //
children.translated_text: alms-food obtained when available, in due time, avoiding what is lowly. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.791 ||
A divine [being] is born from heaven, and two others are of human origin;
endowed with the marks of jewels, of divine birth, the lord of the world. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.792 ||
He who teaches the <s>Dharma</s> enjoys heaven and the four continents;

children.text: bhuktvā tu suciraṃ dvīpāṃstṛṣṇayā vipraṇaśyati // Lank_10.793 //
children.translated_text: having enjoyed the continents for a long time, he perishes through craving. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.793 ||
The <s>Kṛta</s> age, the <s>Tretā</s>, and <s>Dvāpara</s>, and the <s>Kali</s> likewise —

children.text: ahaṃ cānye kṛtayuge śākyasiṃhaḥ kalau yuge // Lank_10.794 //
children.translated_text: I and others [appear] in the <s>Kṛta</s> age; <s>Śākyasiṃha</s> in the <s>Kali</s> age. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.794 ||
<s>Siddhārtha</s>, son of the <s>Śākyas</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Vyāsa</s>, <s>Maheśvara</s> —

children.text: evamādyāni tīrthyāni nirvṛte me bhaviṣyati // Lank_10.795 //
children.translated_text: such heretical [teachers] will arise after my <s>nirvāṇa</s>. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.795 ||
Thus from what I have heard and the like — the teaching of <s>Śākyasiṃha</s>,
the history and ancient account — this will be <s>Vyāsa</s>'s [compilation]. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.796 ||
<s>Viṣṇu</s> and <s>Maheśvara</s> too will teach creatorship;

children.text: evaṃ me nirvṛte paścādevamādyaṃ bhaviṣyati // Lank_10.797 //
children.translated_text: thus after my <s>nirvāṇa</s>, such and more will come to be. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.797 ||

children.text: mātā ca me vasumatiḥ pitā vipraḥ prajāpatiḥ /
children.translated_text: My mother is <s>Vasumatī</s>, my father a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>Prajāpati</s>;

children.text: kātyāyanasagotro 'haṃ nāmnā vai virajo jinaḥ // Lank_10.798 //
children.translated_text: I am of the <s>Kātyāyana</s> lineage, named <s>Viraja</s> the <s>Jina</s>. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.798 ||

children.text: campāyāṃ haṃ samutpannaḥ pitāpi ca pitāmahaḥ /
children.translated_text: I am born in <s>Campā</s>, and my father and grandfather too;
named <s>Somagupta</s>, of the <s>Soma</s> lineage. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.799 ||
Having fulfilled my vows, I go forth; I teach a thousand methods;
having given prophecy, I shall enter <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, having consecrated <s>Mahāmati</s>. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.800 ||
<s>Mati</s> will give [the teaching] to <s>Dharma</s>; <s>Dharma</s> will give to <s>Mekhala</s>;
<s>Mekhala</s>'s disciple, through weakness, will destroy [the teaching] at the end of the age. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.801 ||
<s>Kāśyapa</s>, <s>Krakucchanda</s>, and <s>Kanaka</s> the guide,

children.text: ahaṃ ca virajo 'nye vai sarve te kṛtino jināḥ // Lank_10.802 //
children.translated_text: and I, <s>Viraja</s>, and others — all these are accomplished <s>Jinas</s>. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.802 ||
In the <s>Kṛta</s> age, after that, the guide named <s>Mati</s>
will be a great hero, awakening to the five objects of knowledge. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.803 ||

children.text: na dvāpare na tretāyāṃ na paścācca kalau yuge /
children.translated_text: Not in the <s>Dvāpara</s>, nor in the <s>Tretā</s>, nor afterward in the <s>Kali</s> age —

children.text: saṃbhavo lokanāthānāṃ saṃbudhyante kṛte yuge // Lank_10.804 //
children.translated_text: the world-protectors do not arise [then]; they awaken in the <s>Kṛta</s> age. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.804 ||
Inalienable from the marks, together with the unbroken tens,
with moons like peacock[-eye] moons, one should variegate the upper garment. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.805 ||

children.text: dvayaṅgulaṃ tryaṅgulaṃ vāpi candraṃ candrāntaraṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: Two finger[-widths] or three finger[-widths] — the moon and the space between moons should be;

children.text: anyathā citryamānaṃ hi lobhanīyaṃ hi bāliśān // Lank_10.806 //
children.translated_text: otherwise being decorated would indeed be enticing to the childish. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.806 ||
One should always quench the fire of passion; one should bathe in the water of knowledge;
the triple refuge at the three junctures — the <s>yogin</s> should perform diligently. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.807 ||
Arrows, pebbles, sticks, and the like, set in motion by throwing and such —
one [that is] thrown falls — likewise the wholesome and unwholesome. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.808 ||

children.text: ekaṃ ca bahudhā nāsti vailakṣaṇyānna kutracit /
children.translated_text: The one does not exist as many, because of difference of characteristics — nowhere;

children.text: vāyubhā grāhakāḥ sarve kṣetravaddāyakā bhavet // Lank_10.809 //
children.translated_text: all the graspers are like wind — they would be givers like a field. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.809 ||

children.text: yadyekaṃ bahudhā vai syātsarve hyakṛtakā bhavet /
children.translated_text: If the one were indeed many, all would be uncreated;
for the created there would be destruction — this is the method of the logicians. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.810 ||
It would be like a lamp or a seed — from similarity, how [could there be] multiplicity?

children.text: ekaṃ hi bahudhā bhavati tārkikāṇāmayaṃ nayaḥ // Lank_10.811 //
children.translated_text: The one becomes many — this is the method of the logicians. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.811 ||
A <s>muṅga</s>-bean is not born from sesame, nor rice from a barley-cause;

children.text: godhūmadhānyajātāni ekaṃ hi bahudhā katham // Lank_10.812 //
children.translated_text: wheat and grain[-species] — how can the one be many? || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.812 ||
<s>Pāṇini</s>, the leader of grammar, <s>Akṣapāda</s>, <s>Bṛhaspati</s>,
founders of <s>Lokāyata</s> — <s>Brahmā</s> will be born [as them]. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.813 ||
<s>Kātyāyana</s> the <s>sūtra</s>-maker, and <s>Yājñavalkya</s> likewise,
<s>Bhuḍhuka</s>, astrology, and the like will arise in the <s>Kali</s> age. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.814 ||
<s>Bali</s>, from the meritorious world, due to the fortune of beings, will arise —

children.text: rakṣakaḥ sarvadharmāṇāṃ rājā balī mahīpatiḥ // Lank_10.815 //
children.translated_text: protector of all <s>dharmas</s>, king <s>Bali</s>, lord of the earth. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.815 ||
<s>Vālmīki</s>, <s>Masurākṣa</s>, <s>Kauṭilya</s>, <s>Āśvalāyana</s> —
these great fortunate sages will arise in the future. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.816 ||
<s>Siddhārtha</s>, son of the <s>Śākyas</s>, <s>Bhūtānta</s>, <s>Pañcacūḍaka</s>,
<s>Vāgbali</s>, and <s>Medhāvī</s> — they will be in the future time. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.817 ||
An antelope-skin, a staff of wood, a girdle and a circle-<s>maṇḍala</s> —

children.text: dadāti brahmā maheśvaro vanabhūmau vyavasthite // Lank_10.818 //
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Maheśvara</s> give [these] to one established in the forest-ground. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.818 ||

children.text: bhaviṣyati mahāyogī nāmnā vai virajo muniḥ /
children.translated_text: There will be a great <s>yogin</s>, the sage named <s>Viraja</s>,

children.text: mokṣasya deśakaḥ śāstā munīnāmeṣa vai dhvajaḥ // Lank_10.819 //
children.translated_text: a teacher proclaiming liberation — this indeed is the banner of sages. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.819 ||
<s>Brahmā</s>, together with a hundred <s>Brahmās</s> and many gods, before me,
having cast down an antelope-skin from the sky — there the master disappeared. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.820 ||
All variegated garments, the alms-bowl, together with the gods —

children.text: indro virūḍhakādyāśca vanabhūmau dadanti me // Lank_10.821 //
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s>, <s>Virūḍhaka</s>, and others give [these] to me in the forest-ground. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.821 ||
One who holds the cause of the doctrine of non-arising — is [he] unborn, or is he born again?

children.text: sādhayiṣyatyanutpādaṃ vāṅbhātraṃ kīrtyate tu vai // Lank_10.822 //
children.translated_text: He will establish non-arising — [this] is proclaimed as a kinship of speech indeed. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.822 ||
That ignorance is the cause, the set-in-motion of those minds;

children.text: antarā kimavasthāsau yāvadrūpaṃ na jānati // Lank_10.823 //
children.translated_text: what intermediate state is there until form is not known? || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.823 ||
Immediately upon destruction, another mind operates;

children.text: rūpaṃ na tiṣṭhate kiṃcitkimālambya pravartsyate // Lank_10.824 //
children.translated_text: form does not remain at all — depending on what will [the next mind] operate? || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.824 ||
Since wherever mind would operate it has an unreal cause,

children.text: na prasiddhaṃ kathaṃ tasya kṣaṇabhaṅgo 'vadhāryate // Lank_10.825 //
children.translated_text: it is not established — how can momentary destruction be ascertained for it? || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.825 ||
The attainments of <s>yogins</s>, gold, and <s>Jina</s>-relics,
the luminous mansions — are unbreakable because of worldly causation. || <s>Laṅk</s> 10.826 ||
Enduring states, <s>dharmas</s> of attainment, and the wisdom-perfections of the <s>Buddhas</s> —

children.text: bhikṣutvaṃ samayaprāptirdṛṣṭā vai kṣaṇikā katham // Lank_10.827 //
children.translated_text: Monkhood and the attainment of the precepts — how are they seen as momentary? [Laṅk 10.827]
<s>Gandharva</s>-city, illusion, and the like — how are forms momentary?

children.text: abhūtikā ca bhūtāni bhūtāḥ kiṃcitkva cāgatau // Lank_10.828 //
children.translated_text: Non-real and yet real — whence and where have real [things] come? [Laṅk 10.828]
The mind, caused by ignorance, accumulated from beginningless time,
is conceived by the logicians as connected with arising and destruction. [Laṅk 10.829]
The <s>Sāṃkhya</s> doctrine is twofold: transformation from <s>pradhāna</s> (primal matter);

children.text: pradhāne vidyate kāryaṃ kāryaṃ svātmaprasādhitam // Lank_10.830 //
children.translated_text: the effect exists in <s>pradhāna</s>, and the effect is established by its own self. [Laṅk 10.830]
<s>Pradhāna</s> together with [its] entity — the differentiation of <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) is proclaimed;
the diversity of cause and effect does not exist in transformation. [Laṅk 10.831]

children.text: yathā hi pāradaḥ śuddha upakleśairna lipyate /
children.translated_text: Just as mercury is pure and is not tainted by impurities,

children.text: ālayaṃ hi tathā śuddhamāśrayaḥ sarvadehinām // Lank_10.832 //
children.translated_text: so is the <s>ālaya</s> (store-consciousness) pure — the basis of all embodied beings. [Laṅk 10.832]
The scent of <s>hiṅgu</s> (asafoetida) and onion, the seeing of the embryo by a pregnant woman,

children.text: lavaṇādibhiśca lāvaṇyaṃ bījavatkiṃ na vartate // Lank_10.833 //
children.translated_text: saltiness through salt and the like — does it not operate like a seed? [Laṅk 10.833]

children.text: anyatve ca tadanyatve ubhayaṃ nobhaye tathā /
children.translated_text: In otherness and non-otherness, neither both nor both likewise;

children.text: astitvaṃ nirupādānaṃ na ca nāsti na saṃskṛtam // Lank_10.834 //
children.translated_text: existence without substratum — and it is not non-existent, nor conditioned. [Laṅk 10.834]
The self exists like a horse [in aggregates], free from the nature of a cow, [among] the aggregates;
the conditioned and unconditioned are expressible, but the inherent nature is inexpressible. [Laṅk 10.835]
Through reasoning and scripture, through wrong views, defiled by the view of logic,

children.text: anirdhāryaṃ vadantyātmā nopādāne na cānyataḥ // Lank_10.836 //
children.translated_text: they say the self is undeterminable — not in the substratum, nor from anything else. [Laṅk 10.836]
Through the determination of faults, the self is discerned in the aggregates by them;

children.text: ekatvena tadanyatvena na ca budhyanti tārkikāḥ // Lank_10.837 //
children.translated_text: but the logicians do not understand [it] through oneness or otherness [with them]. [Laṅk 10.837]

children.text: darpaṇe udake netre yatha bimbaṃ pradṛśyate /
children.translated_text: Just as a reflection is seen in a mirror, in water, and in the eye,
free from oneness and otherness — so is the person in the aggregates. [Laṅk 10.838]

children.text: bhāvyaṃ vibhāvanādhyātā mārgaḥ satyā ca darśanam /
children.translated_text: What is to be contemplated, the contemplation-master, the path, the truths, and seeing —

children.text: etatrayaṃ vibhāvento mucyante hi kudarśanaiḥ // Lank_10.839 //
children.translated_text: those who discern these three are liberated from wrong views. [Laṅk 10.839]

children.text: dṛṣṭaṃ naṣṭaṃ yathā vidyuccakraṃ chidragṛhe yathā /
children.translated_text: What is seen perishes like lightning, like a wheel [seen through] a hole;

children.text: pariṇāmaḥ sarvadharmāṇāṃ bālairiva na kalpayet // Lank_10.840 //
children.translated_text: one should not conceive of the transformation of all <s>dharmas</s> like the childish. [Laṅk 10.840]
<s>Nirvāṇa</s> through existence and non-existence deludes the minds of the childish;
from the reality of the noble vision, from the seeing of things as they are. [Laṅk 10.841]
Free from arising and destruction, devoid of existence and non-existence,
freed from the characterized and the characteristic — one should discern transformation. [Laṅk 10.842]
Free from the doctrine of heretical teachers, devoid of name and configuration,
with its abode in the inner vision — one should discern transformation. [Laṅk 10.843]
Through contact and affliction, the [realms] of <s>devas</s> and of hell-beings,
and intermediate-state [beings] do not exist — [they are] set in motion by consciousness. [Laṅk 10.844]
Born from aging, from eggs, from moisture, and so forth — those born from the intermediate state,

children.text: sattvakāyā yathā citrā gatyāgatyāṃ vibhāvayet // Lank_10.845 //
children.translated_text: the bodies of beings are variegated — one should discern [them] in terms of going and coming. [Laṅk 10.845]
Devoid of reasoning and scripture, bringing the destruction of the side of affliction-freedom,
the ramblings of heretical views — the wise one should not practice [them]. [Laṅk 10.846]
First the self is determined, and then distinguished from the substratum;
those who distinguish the undeterminable [self] distinguish a barren woman's son. [Laṅk 10.847]
I see beings with the divine [eye], free from the fleshly [eye] and wisdom [eye],
freed from the aggregates of <s>saṃsāra</s>, embodied among all embodied beings. [Laṅk 10.848]
Gone to ugly and beautiful [forms], with the distinction of liberated and unliberated,
divine and free from <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations) — [yet] one sees [them as] situated in <s>saṃskāras</s>. [Laṅk 10.849]
Embodied at the junction of [rebirth-]courses, beyond the domain of the logicians,
transcending the human course — I [see thus], not other wrong logicians. [Laṅk 10.850]
The self does not exist; the mind arises — from what does it operate?

children.text: nadīdīpabījavattasya nirgamaḥ kiṃ na kathyate // Lank_10.851 //
children.translated_text: Like a river, a lamp, and a seed — why is its going-forth not spoken of? [Laṅk 10.851]

children.text: anutpanne ca vijñāne ajñānādi na vidyate /
children.translated_text: When consciousness has not arisen, ignorance and the like do not exist;

children.text: tadabhāve na vijñānaṃ saṃtatyā jāyate katham // Lank_10.852 //
children.translated_text: in the absence of those, how is consciousness born in a [causal] series? [Laṅk 10.852]
The three time-periods, the timeless, and the inexpressible as the fifth —
this should be known as belonging to the <s>Buddhas</s>, [yet] it is proclaimed by the logicians. [Laṅk 10.853]
The inexpressible [is related] to formations; knowledge is caused by formations;
knowledge grasps what belongs to formations — knowledge is designated [by] formations. [Laṅk 10.854]
"When this exists, that arises" — and conditions too are causeless.
They are indicated by the manifester — from the absence of that, there is no agent. [Laṅk 10.855]

children.text: pavanaṃ hi vahnerdahanaṃ preraṇe na tu saṃbhave /
children.translated_text: Wind is the burning of fire, the impelling — not the arising;

children.text: prerya nirvāyate tena kathaṃ sattvaprasādhakāḥ // Lank_10.856 //
children.translated_text: being impelled, it is extinguished by that — how then do they establish beings? [Laṅk 10.856]
The conditioned and unconditioned are expressible, devoid of substratum;
how then is fire conceived by the childish as its establisher? [Laṅk 10.857]
From the mutual imparting of strength, fire arises for people;

children.text: sattvaḥ pravartitaḥ kena vahnivatkalpyate yataḥ // Lank_10.858 //
children.translated_text: by what is a being set in motion? — since it is conceptualized like fire. [Laṅk 10.858]
Of the mass of aggregates and sense-bases, <s>manas</s> (mentation) and the like are not the cause;

children.text: nairātmā sārthavannityaṃ cittena saha vartate // Lank_10.859 //
children.translated_text: the selfless one, like a caravan, always operates together with the mind. [Laṅk 10.859]
These two are always luminous, free from cause and effect;

children.text: agnirhyasādhakasteṣāṃ na ca budhyanti tārkikāḥ // Lank_10.860 //
children.translated_text: fire is not [their] establisher — the logicians do not understand [this]. [Laṅk 10.860]

children.text: cittaṃ sattvāśca nirvāṇaṃ prakṛtyā bhāsurā nu vai /
children.translated_text: The mind, beings, and <s>nirvāṇa</s> — by nature they are luminous;
afflicted by beginningless defilements, [yet] undivided, like space. [Laṅk 10.861]
Like the shadow of an elephant's couch and the like(?), defiled by heretical views,
covered by <s>manas</s> and consciousness — purified by fire and the like. [Laṅk 10.862]

children.text: dṛṣṭāśca te yathābhūtaṃ dṛṣṭvā kleśā vidāritāḥ /
children.translated_text: And they are seen as they truly are; having seen, the afflictions are torn asunder;
having abandoned the thicket of [wrong] examples, they have gone to the domain of the noble ones. [Laṅk 10.863]
Through the division of knower and knowable, otherness is conceptualized;

children.text: na ca budhyanti durmedhā avaktavyaśca kathyate // Lank_10.864 //
children.translated_text: the dull-witted do not understand, and the inexpressible is spoken of. [Laṅk 10.864]

children.text: bherī yathā candanajā bālaiḥ kurvanti nānyathā /
children.translated_text: Just as a drum made of sandalwood — the childish do not make [it] otherwise;
resembling sandal and aloe — so is knowledge [treated] by the wrong logicians. [Laṅk 10.865]
One who has risen and eaten, merely relying on a vessel —
despite faults such as the impurity of the mouth and the like, one should take the pure food. [Laṅk 10.866]

children.text: imaṃ nayaṃ yo 'numinoti yuktitaḥ prasādavān yogaparo hyakalpanaḥ /
children.translated_text: Whoever infers this method through reasoning, faithful, devoted to <s>yoga</s>, free from conceptualization,

children.text: anāśrito hyarthaparo bhavedasau hiraṇmayīṃ dharmagatiṃ pradīpayet // Lank_10.867 //
children.translated_text: not dependent, and intent on the meaning — he would illuminate the golden path of <s>Dharma</s>. [Laṅk 10.867]

children.text: bhāvābhāvapratyayamohakalpanā kudṛṣṭijālaṃ samalaṃ hi tasya tu /
children.translated_text: The conceptualization of the delusion of conditions, of existence and non-existence — the net of wrong views and defilement — for him

children.text: sarāgadoṣapratighaṃ nivartate nirañjano buddhakaraiśca sicyate // Lank_10.868 //
children.translated_text: desire, fault, and hostility turn back; unstained, he is anointed with the deeds of a <s>Buddha</s>. [Laṅk 10.868]
The heretical teachers are confused about the direction of cause; others are bewildered by conditions;
others, from the existence of causelessness, hold to annihilationism as [if it were] the noble [teaching]. [Laṅk 10.869]
Maturation and transformation — of consciousness and of <s>manas</s>;

children.text: mano hyālayasaṃbhūtaṃ vijñānaṃ ca manobhavam // Lank_10.870 //
children.translated_text: <s>manas</s> is born from the <s>ālaya</s>, and consciousness is born from <s>manas</s>. [Laṅk 10.870]
All minds proceed from the <s>ālaya</s>, like waves;
all are caused by impressions, arising according to their conditions. [Laṅk 10.871]
Bound by the assemblage of momentary differences, grasping the objects of one's own mind,
with the form of configurations and characteristics — arising from <s>manas</s>, the eye, and the like. [Laṅk 10.872]
Connected with beginningless faults, arisen from the impressions of the appearance of objects,
the mind is seen externally — [this is taught] for the warding off of heretical views. [Laṅk 10.873]
Having that as cause, and having that as object, another operates;

children.text: yadā saṃjāyate dṛṣṭiḥ saṃsāraśca pravartate // Lank_10.874 //
children.translated_text: when views arise, <s>saṃsāra</s> operates. [Laṅk 10.874]
Entities are like illusion and dreams, resembling a <s>gandharva</s>-city,
like a mirage, water, and the moon — one should discern one's own conceptualization. [Laṅk 10.875]
Through the differentiation of operations, <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) [arises]; right knowledge takes that as its basis;
illusion-like, the <s>Śūraṅgama</s> and other supreme <s>samādhis</s>. [Laṅk 10.876]
Through entry into the stages, one obtains the <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges) and the masteries,
the illusion-like body of knowledge, and the consecration of the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One). [Laṅk 10.877]

children.text: nivartate yadā cittaṃ nivṛttaṃ paśyato jagat /
children.translated_text: When the mind turns back, and seeing the world as turned back,

children.text: muditāṃ labhate bhūmiṃ buddhabhūmiṃ labhanti ca // Lank_10.878 //
children.translated_text: one attains the stage of Joy (<s>Muditā</s>) and attains the <s>Buddha</s>-stage. [Laṅk 10.878]
With the basis turned around, like a wish-fulfilling jewel of manifold forms,

children.text: karoti sattvakṛtyāni pratibimbaṃ yathā jale // Lank_10.879 //
children.translated_text: one accomplishes the welfare of beings, like a reflection in water. [Laṅk 10.879]
Freed from the sides of existent and non-existent — neither both nor not-both;
having gone beyond both the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> and <s>Śrāvaka</s> [vehicles], the seventh [stage] would be. [Laṅk 10.880]
For those whose <s>dharmas</s> are seen by their own inner [realization], purified by the stage of reality,
freed from heretical external teachers — one should proclaim the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. [Laṅk 10.881]
The turning-around of conceptualization, free from falling and destruction —
resembling the wool of a hare and a jewel — one should teach this method to the liberated. [Laṅk 10.882]

children.text: yathā hi grantho granthena yuktyā yuktistathā yadi /
children.translated_text: Just as a knot [is loosened] by a knot, and reasoning by reasoning —

children.text: ato yuktirbhavedyuktimanyathā tu na kalpayet // Lank_10.883 //
children.translated_text: if so, reasoning would be [valid] reasoning; otherwise, one should not conceive [thus]. [Laṅk 10.883]

children.text: cakṣuḥ karma ca tṛṣṇā ca avidyāyoniśastathā /
children.translated_text: The eye, <s>karma</s>, craving, ignorance, and improper [attention],
the eye and forms, <s>manas</s>, and the <s>manas</s> of the turbid [mind]. [Laṅk 10.884]

body.text: ityāryasaddharmalaṅkāvatāro nāma mahāyānasūtraṃ sagāthakaṃ samāptamiti //
body.translated_text: Thus [is completed] the <s>Mahāyāna</s> sūtra called the Noble <s>Saddharmalaṅkāvatāra</s>, with verses.

children.text: ye dharmā hetuprabhavā hetuṃ teṣāṃ tathāgato hyavadat /
children.translated_text: Those <s>dharmas</s> that arise from causes — the <s>Tathāgata</s> has declared their cause,

children.text: teṣāṃ ca yo nirodho evaṃ vādī mahāśramaṇaḥ //
children.translated_text: and that which is their cessation — thus speaks the Great <s>Śramaṇa</s>.
